**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> विश्वानि भद्रा मरुतो रथेषु वो मिथस्पृध्येव तविषाण्याहिता ।
> अंसेष्वा वः प्रपथेषु खादयोऽक्षो वश्चक्रा समया वि वावृते ॥ ९ ॥

> *viśvāni bhadrā maruto ratheṣu vo mithaspṛdhyeva taviṣāṇyāhitā |*
> *aṃseṣvā vaḥ prapatheṣu khādayo 'kṣo vaścakrā samayā vi vāvṛte ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> विश्वानि । भद्रा । मरुतः । रथेषु । वः । मिथःस्पृध्याऽइव । तविषाणि । आऽहिता ।
> अंसेषु । आ । वः । प्रऽपथेषु । खादयः । अक्षः । वः । चक्रा । समया । वि । ववृते ॥ ९ ॥

> *viśvāni | bhadrā | marutaḥ | ratheṣu | vaḥ | mithaḥspṛdhyā 'iva | taviṣāṇi | ā 'hitā |*
> *aṃseṣu | ā | vaḥ | pra 'patheṣu | khādayaḥ | akṣaḥ | vaḥ | cakrā | samayā | vi | vavṛte ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः वो रथेषु युष्मत्संबन्धिरथेषु रंहणसाधनेषु विश्वानि भद्रा सर्वाणि कल्याणानि भोगयोग्यानि द्रव्याण्यस्मभ्यं प्रदेयानि फलानि वाहितानि । तथा वोऽसेष्वा [?] तदुसलक्षितभुजेष्वपि । आकारोऽस्यर्थे । मिथस्पृध्येव बलाधिक्यात्परस्परस्पर्धाविषयाणि तविषाणि बलानि अंसेषूक्तलक्षणान्यायुधानि वाहितानि । किञ्च वः प्रपथेषु । प्रगताः पन्थानो येषु विश्रामस्थानेषु तानि प्रपथानि । तेषु खादयः खाद्यानि भक्ष्याण्याहितानि । यद्वा । प्रगतः पन्था यैस्तेषु पादाग्रेषु खादयः स्थिरा आभरणविशेषा आहिताः । किञ्चाक्षो वो युष्मत्संबन्धी रथ्योऽक्षः [?] चक्रा तेक्रोपनिबद्धानि [?] चक्राणि समया समीपे तेषां परिसरे वि ववृते । विशेषेण वर्तते । न कदाचिदपि चक्रेषु संलग्नो भवतीत्यर्थः । यस्मादेवं देवयजनगमनसाधनानि सन्ति तस्माच्छीघ्रमागच्छतेत्यभिप्रायः ॥

*Gist:* O Maruts, in your chariots all enjoyable good things are laid, ready to be given to us; on your shoulders are weapons of rival strength; in your resting-places are food, or firm ornaments on your feet; and the axle turns evenly in the wheels — everything is ready for the journey to the sacrifice, so come quickly.

**Pratipadārtha.** (*he*) *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *vaḥ* — your; *ratheṣu* — in the chariots; *viśvāni bhadrā* — all the means of enjoyment, or the things to be given to us; *ā hitā* — are set; *aṃseṣu ā* — on your shoulders too; *mithaspṛdhyā iva* — as if in rivalry with one another; *taviṣāṇi* — strengths (weapons that display strength); (*ā hitā* — are set); (and) *vaḥ* — your; *prapatheṣu* — at the resting-places on the road; *khādayaḥ* — edible things *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 42  (PDF 62)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* …are set; [or, *prapatheṣu* — at the ends of the feet; *khādayaḥ* — firm special ornaments are set]; (*kiṃce* — and further) *vaḥ akṣaḥ* — the axle (of your chariot); *cakrā* — (of the wheels fixed to it); *samayā* — near; *vi vāvṛte* — turns specially.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Maruts, in your chariots all the means of enjoyment, and things to be given to us, are ready; your protecting weapons are borne on your arms; at your resting-places on the road, eatables are ready (or special ornaments are put on the ends of your feet); the wheels of your chariot are fitted properly to the axle; (so, since everything is ready for your journey, set out quickly for our sacrificial hall).

**English Translation (as printed):** Maruts, all good things are in your cars: on your shoulders abides emulous strength: at your resting-places on the road refreshments (are ready): the axle of your (chariot) wheels holds them firmly together.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***viśvāni bhadrā maruto ratheṣu vaḥ*** — in this ṛk the ṛṣi, wishing the Maruts' coming, describes everything as ready for their coming. O Maruts, in your chariots everything excellent and choice is laid ready; those things are fit for enjoyment; they have been laid in your chariots in order to be given to us, who praise these [gods]: this is the main purport of this sentence.

***ratheṣu*** — for the word *ratha*, Yāska in his Nirukta says:

> रथो रंहतेर्गतिकर्मणः । स्थिरतेर्वा स्याद्विपरीतस्य । रमतेर्वा स्याद्विपरीतस्य । रममाणोऽस्मिंस्तिष्ठतीति वा । रसतेर्वा [?]

> *ratho raṃhater gatikarmaṇaḥ | sthiratervā syādviparītasya | ramatervā syādviparītasya | ramamāṇo 'smiṃstiṣṭhatīti vā | rasatervā [?]*

(Ni. 9-11 [?]) That is: the word may be formed from the root *raṃh*, which indicates motion, or from the root *sthira* in the opposite sense. Because this always goes about (travels), it is called *ratha*. Or the warrior (*yodha*) who sits in it becomes steady: when one sits on horses and other vehicles the body shakes about; when one sits in a chariot it does not shake about, one can sit steady; therefore it is called *ratha*. Or, since the one who sits in it enjoys himself while he sits there, it is called *ratha*: thus he has explained the literal sense.

***mithaspṛdhyeva*** — *balādhikyātparasparaspardhāviṣayāṇi*: "through the abundance of strength, things about which they compete with one another"; rubbing against each other (taking spar), "clashing against each other" (English in the source). Iron and the like *[continues on the next page]*

---

### Printed p. 43  (PDF 63)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 2".)* …made of iron and the like — many kinds of weapons are joined together and set in one place in the chariots; with the motion of the chariot those weapons rub against one another and make a noise: this is the purport.

***taviṣāṇi*** — the word *taviṣa* is read among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]); but here this word is in the neuter plural, so the explanation of the word *taviṣāṇi* in the first ṛk of this Sūkta as *sāmarthyāni* — "capabilities, valorous deeds, deeds of daring" — does not fit well; for neither capabilities nor deeds of daring are things that are laid in chariots — they are only names of acts; and if *taviṣāṇi* is explained as "armies" (*sainya*), it is not possible to lay armies (however large) in chariots. Therefore the sense "weapons that give strength" for the word *taviṣāṇi* is the one that fits. Hence:

***mithaspṛdhyeva taviṣāṇy āhitā*** — in this sentence the meaning is: "many excellent weapons, rubbing against each other through the movement of the chariots, are laid in your chariots".

***aṃseṣv ā vaḥ*** — besides the weapons in the chariots described above, you have also kept some weapons on your arms.

***prapatheṣu khādayaḥ*** — 

> वः प्रपथेषु । प्रगताः पन्थानो येषु विश्रामस्थानेषु तानि प्रपथानि । तेषु खादयः खाद्यानि भक्ष्याण्याहितानि । यद्वा । प्रगतः पन्था यैस्तेषु पादाग्रेषु खादयः स्थिरा आभरणविशेषा आहिताः ॥

> *vaḥ prapatheṣu | pragatāḥ panthāno yeṣu viśrāmasthāneṣu tāni prapathāni | teṣu khādayaḥ khādyāni bhakṣyāṇyāhitāni | yadvā | pragataḥ panthā yaisteṣu pādāgreṣu khādayaḥ sthirā ābharaṇaviśeṣā āhitāḥ ‖*

The Bhāṣyakāra has given two kinds of meaning for this sentence. *Prapatha* are the places where, at the time of journeys, one sits for some time to rest from the fatigue of the road; it is natural to eat, while sitting at such places, the food one has brought with one; this very matter is indicated here. Or *prapatha* means the feet that serve for going along the paths (for walking), and *khādayaḥ* is the name of the foot-ornaments worn on them — he gives this other meaning too.

Max Müller, a German scholar, takes the two phrases *aṃseṣv ā vaḥ prapatheṣu khādayaḥ* as one sentence and translates it: "When you are on your journeys, you carry rings on your shoulders." (English in the source; with the Kannada: "when you journey you wear ornaments (weapons?) on your arms"). To support this, in explaining the word *vṛṣakhādayaḥ* in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-10 [?] he has made the following discussion about the word *khādi* (English):

"In वृषखादयः (*vṛṣakhādayaḥ*) the meaning of खादि (*khādi*) is by no means clear. Sayana evidently guesses and proposes two meanings–weapon or food. In several *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 44  (PDF 64)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* "passages where खादि occurs, it seems to be an ornament rather than a weapon, yet if derived from khad to bite, it may originally have signified some kind of weapon. Roth tranlates [sic] it by ring, and it is certain that these khadis were to be seen not only on the arms and shoulders, but likewise on the feet of the Maruts. There is a famous weapon in India, the चक्र (*cakra*) or quoit, a ring with sharp edges (चक्रायुध) which is thrown from a great distance with fatal effect. Bollensen (Orient and Occident Vol. II. p. 46) suggests for वृषन् (*vṛṣan*) the meanig [sic] of hole in the ear, and then translates the compound as having earrings in the hole of the ear. But वृषन् does not mean the hole in the lap of the ear, nor has वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*) that meaning either in the Veda or elsewhere. Wilson gives for वृषभ, not for वृषन्, the meaning of orifice of the ear, but this is very different from the hole in the lap of the ear. Benfey suggests that the khadis were made of the teeth of wild animals and hence their name of biters. वृषन् conveys the meanig [sic] of strong, though possibly with the implied idea of rain-producing, fertlising [sic]. In वृषन् we have one of those words which it is almost impossible to translate accurately. It occurs over and over again in the Vedic Hymns, and if we once know the various ideas which it either expreesss [sic] or implies, we have little difficulty in understanding its import in a vague and genaral [sic] way, though we look in vain for corresponding terms in any modern language. In the Veda, and in ancient languages generally, one and the same word is frequently made to do service for many. Words retain their general meaning, though at the same time they are evidently used with a definite purpose. This is not only a peculiar phase of language, but a peculiar phase of thought, and as to us this phase hase [sic] become strange and unreal, it is very difficult to transport ourselves back into it, still more to translate the pregnant terms of the Vedic poets into the definite languages which we have to use."

(Kannada:) There is another mantra which says that the Marut-gods wear on their arms ornaments called *khādi*, or special weapons — *[continues on the next page]*

> अंसेष्वा मरुतः खादयो वो वक्षःसु रुक्मा उपशिश्रियाणाः । वि विद्युतो न वृष्टिभी रुचानाः अनु स्वधामायुधैर्यच्छमानाः ॥

> *aṃseṣvā marutaḥ khādayo vo vakṣaḥsu rukmā upaśiśriyāṇāḥ | vi vidyuto na vṛṣṭibhī rucānāḥ anu svadhāmāyudhairyacchamānāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-13 [?]) — in this ṛk there is the description: "O Maruts, on your arms there are weapons called *khādi*; on your chests golden ornaments are fastened."

> एषामंसेषु रम्भिणीव रारभे हस्तेषु खादिश्च कृतिश्च सं दधे ।

> *eṣāmaṃseṣu rambhiṇīva rārabhe hasteṣu khādiśca kṛtiśca saṃ dadhe |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168-3)

> त्वेषं गणं तवसं खादिहस्तं धुनिव्रतं मायिनं दातिवारम् ।

> *tveṣaṃ gaṇaṃ tavasaṃ khādihastaṃ dhunivrataṃ māyinaṃ dātivāram |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-58-2 [?]) — in these ṛks the weapon called *khādi* is described as held in the hands. The places where the Maruts bear special weapons and ornaments —

> अंसेषु व ऋष्टयः पत्सु खादयो वक्षःसु रुक्मा मरुतो रथे शुभः ।

> *aṃseṣu va ṛṣṭayaḥ patsu khādayo vakṣaḥsu rukmā maruto rathe śubhaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-54-11) — in explaining this ṛk it is said that they bear the weapons called *khādi* (or ornaments) on the feet ("The khadis are on your forefeet" — English in the source). It is not possible to bear weapons on the feet, so here the word *khādi* must be taken in the sense of a special ornament. The shape and form of the *khādi* are not known to us now, but it is a point established that it is a special weapon resembling a *cakra*. Since it is circular (round, ring-shaped), it may be inferred that these ankle-rings (rounded like a *cakra*) worn on the feet were described in many places by the name *khādi*. Whether worn on the feet, or on the arms or hands, or on other limbs, when fighting they would have to be held in the hands. Hence the ṛṣis have described this matter in different ways. The weapon called *cakra* in the hand of Viṣṇu also may have come into usage on the basis of this weapon *khādi*.

The Bhāṣyakāra gives for the word *khādi* the sense "*khādyāni bhakṣyāṇi*" — "edibles, things fit for eating". Many Western scholars do not accept that this is fitting. Max Müller, on this matter (English):

"What however is quite certain is this, that खादि in the Veda never means food, as Sayana opt'onally [sic] interprets it. This interpretation is accepted by Wilson, who translates–at your resting places on the road *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 46  (PDF 66)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* "refreshments (are ready). Nay, he goes on in a note to use this passage as a proof of the advanced civilisation of India at the time of the Vedic Rishis. "The expression" he says "is worthy of note as indicating the existence of accomodations [sic] for the use of travellers: the प्रपथ is the choltri (छत्र) of the south of India, the Sarai of Mohammadans, a place by the roadside whare [sic] the travellers may find shelter and provisions.""

In the matter of the meaning of the word *prapatha* too, the Bhāṣyakāra has explained in this ṛk: *prapatheṣu panthāno viśrāmasthāneṣu* — "in the resting places found on the road"; but in

> आयुर्विश्वायुः परि पासति त्वा पूषा त्वा पातु प्रपथे पुरस्तात् ।

> *āyurviśvāyuḥ pari pāsati tvā pūṣā tvā pātu prapathe purastāt |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-4)

> प्रपथे पथामजनिष्ट पूषा प्रपथे दिवः प्रपथे पृथिव्याः ।

> *prapathe pathāmajaniṣṭa pūṣā prapathe divaḥ prapathe pṛthivyāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-6)

> स्वस्तिरिद्धि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्णस्वत्यभि या वाममेति ।

> *svastiriddhi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṇasvatyabhi yā vāmameti |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-63-15 [?]) — in ṛks like these, the word *prapathe* is said to mean "*prakṛṣṭe mārge*", "in an excellent road". Therefore, for the words *prapatheṣu khādayaḥ* in this ṛk, the meaning "when the Maruts journey along excellent roads they wear the special weapons called *khādi*" fits well.

***akṣo vaścakrā samayā vi vāvṛte*** — the Bhāṣyakāra: "*akṣo vo yuṣmatsaṃbandhī rathyo 'kṣaś cakrā tetropanibaddhāni cakrāṇi samayā samīpe teṣāṃ parisare vi vavṛte viśeṣeṇa vartate na kadācidapi cakreṣu saṃlagno bhavatīty arthaḥ*" [as read, doubtful]. O Maruts, the axle of your chariot makes the wheels at its two sides turn round simultaneously. They are firmly fastened; there is no falling off from the axle. The same sense is said in

> सत्रा ते अनु कृष्टयो विश्वा चक्रेण नावृतुः ।

> *satrā te anu kṛṣṭayo viśvā cakreṇa nāvṛtuḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-2 [?]) — that is: your chariot moves smoothly, without any hindrance: this is the main purport. To say here that the axle makes the wheel turn is not correct. As the horses pull the chariot the wheels turn; but still, in the neighbourhood of the axle, to that *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 47  (PDF 67)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 2".)* …in the same way as the wheels are connected — thus the ṛṣi may have described it. The word *samayā* in the Veda means "together" or "at the same time".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *bhadrā* (root *bhadi kalyāṇe sukhe ca*; *oṇādika* suffix *rak*; in the neuter plural *śi* is dropped by *śeśchandasi bahulam* Pā. 6-1-70). *āhitā* (prefix *ā*; root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *kta* in the passive by *niṣṭhā*; *dadhāter hiḥ* Pā. 7-4-42 gives *hi* for the root; *gatir anantaraḥ* Pā. 6-2-49 gives the acute to the *gati* (*ā*); *śi* dropped in the neuter plural as before). *mithaspṛdhyā* (root *spardha saṅgharṣe*; *kvip* is given; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *saṃprasāraṇa* to the *r* of the root and drops the *ā*; *spṛdhaḥ* "that which is rivalled"; then *yat* in the sense of the action; *yato 'nāvaḥ* Pā. 6-1-213 gives initial acute; in the compound the *kṛdutta* member keeps its accent; *śi* dropped as before). *prapatheṣu* (*pragatāḥ panthāno yeṣu tāni prapathāni*; *ṛkpūrabdhūḥpathām ānakṣe* Pā. 5-4-74 gives the suffix *a* as a compound-final; *ṭi* dropped; in the *bahuvrīhi* the first member keeps its accent). *cakrā* (*cakrāṇi*; *śeśchandasi bahulam* drops *śi*). *samayā* (since it is connected with *samayā*, *abhitaḥ paritaḥ samayā…* gives the second case as an exception to the sixth). *vavṛte* (root *vṛtu vartane*; *liṭ* 3rd singular, Vedic; *nighāta* after a *tiṅanta*). ‖ 9 ‖

#### Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> भूरीणि भद्रा नर्येषु बाहुषु वक्षःसु रुक्मा रभसासो अञ्जयः ।
> अंसेष्वेताः पविषु क्षुरा अधि वयो न पक्षान्व्यनु श्रियो धिरे ॥ १० ॥

> *bhūrīṇi bhadrā naryeṣu bāhuṣu vakṣaḥsu rukmā rabhasāso añjayaḥ |*
> *aṃseṣvetāḥ paviṣu kṣurā adhi vayo na pakṣānvyanu śriyo dhire ‖ 10 ‖*

### Printed p. 48  (PDF 68)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> भूरीणि । भद्रा । नर्येषु । बाहुषु । वक्षःऽसु । रुक्माः । रभसासः । अञ्जयः ।
> अंसेषु । एताः । पविषु । क्षुराः । अधि । वयः । न । पक्षान् । वि । अनु । श्रियः । धिरे ॥ १० ॥

> *bhūrīṇi | bhadrā | naryeṣu | bāhuṣu | vakṣaḥ 'su | rukmāḥ | rabhasāsaḥ | añjayaḥ |*
> *aṃseṣu | etāḥ | paviṣu | kṣurāḥ | adhi | vayaḥ | na | pakṣān | vi | anu | śriyaḥ | dhire ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> ते मरुतो नर्येषु नरेभ्यो हितेषु बाहुषु भुजेषु भूरीणि प्रभूतानि भद्रा भद्राणि कल्याणानि धनानि स्तोतृभ्यो दातुं धिरे । दधिरे । धारयन्ति । तथा वक्षःसूरःस्थलेषु रुक्माः सुवर्णरत्नादिनिर्मितान्याभरणानि धारयन्ति । कीदृशानि । रभसासो राभस्ययुक्तानि कान्तिमन्ति वा तथाञ्जयो व्यक्तानि । अंसेषु भुजमूलेषु एताः शुक्लवर्णा मालाः । पविषु वज्रसदृशेष्वायुधेषु क्षुराः क्षुरधाराः । अधि सप्तम्यर्थानुवादी । एवमेते मरुतः सर्वाङ्गेषु श्रियो लक्ष्मीरनुक्रमेण वि धिरे । विविधं धारयन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वयो न पक्षान् पक्षिणः पक्षानिव ॥

*Gist:* The Maruts bear much auspicious wealth to give to the singers on their arms that benefit men, golden ornaments on their chests, white garlands on their shoulders, razor-edges on their thunderbolt-like weapons — they carry adornments on all limbs, as birds carry wings.

**Pratipadārtha.** (*te marutaḥ* — those Marut-gods); *naryeṣu* — for the good of men; *bāhuṣu* — on the arms; *bhūrīṇi* — abundant; *bhadrā* — auspicious (wealth to be given to those who praise); *dhire* — they bear; *vakṣaḥsu* — on the chests; *rabhasāsaḥ* — splendid; *añjayaḥ* — clear (to be seen); *rukmāḥ* — ornaments made of gold and the like; (*dhire* — they bear); *aṃseṣu* — on the roots of the arms; *etāḥ* — white garlands; *paviṣu* — on the weapons resembling the thunderbolt; *kṣurāḥ* — keen edges; *adhi* (*dhire*) — they bear; (thus the Marut-gods) *śriyaḥ* — (various) adornments; *anu* — in the said order; *vayaḥ* — birds; *pakṣān na* — as (various-coloured) wings; *vi* (*dhire*) — bear variously.

**Bhāvārtha.** On the arms of the Marut-gods, who do good to men, are many auspicious things to be given to men; on their chests glitter and are plainly seen golden ornaments; on their shoulders are white garlands, and on their (hands) green [?] weapons resembling the thunderbolt are keen edges. As birds have wings of many kinds, the Marut-gods are adorned in many ways (or: they scatter their splendour all round).

### Printed p. 49  (PDF 69)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 2".)*

**English Translation (as printed):** Maruts, in your arms, propitious to man, are many good things: on your breasts are golden (ornaments), brilliant and conspicuous: white garlands (hang) on your shoulders: sharp are (the edges of) your weapons: the Maruts have various decorations, as birds have (many coloured) wings.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** In this ṛk the ornaments the Marut-gods wear on their various limbs for adornment, and their weapons, are described.

***bhūrīṇi bhadrā naryeṣu bāhuṣu*** — the Marut-gods bear in their strong arms (hands) excellent things in order to give to the sacrificers; that is, they hold in their hands many auspicious excellent things to be given to the sacrificers who praise them. Here for the word *naryeṣu* the Bhāṣyakāra explains *narebhyo hiteṣu*, "beneficial to men", that is, "desired by men". The scholar Max Müller translates it as "manly" — "strong (arms) such as men ought to have" (English: manly).

***vakṣassu rukmā*** — *urasthaleṣu rukmāḥ suvarṇaratnādinirmitānyābharaṇāni dhārayanti*: they wear on the chest ornaments such as necklaces made of gold and jewels. This matter is described also in the ṛk *vakṣaḥsu rukmā* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-4). The word *rukmā*, in the plural, is used to denote the necklaces and similar ornaments of gold that the Maruts wear on their breasts. For this very reason, in ṛks 2-34-2 [?]; 5-55-1 [?]; 5-52-5 [?] and others, the Marut-gods are called *rukmavakṣasaḥ* ("with golden ornaments on the chest" — "gold-breasted", English). In the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. Śrau. Sū. 9-4 [?]) and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 1-8-13-1 [?]) the *rukmaṃ hotre* — the gold ornament given to the *hotṛ* priest in a sacrifice, at the end of the performance [?] — is described. It is said that this ornament is round in shape; it may be an ornament like what is called a necklace (*hāra*).

***rabhasāsaḥ*** — *rābhasyayuktāni kāntimanti vā*: glittering, shining. This word is formed from the root *rabh*, meaning "to rush in, to fall upon". This word shows strength accompanied by speed. The word *rabhasa* is found used not only of the Maruts but also of Agni and Indra. *(Printer's signature at the foot: "XIII 4".)*

### Printed p. 50  (PDF 70)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)*

> पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासो रभिष्ठाः स्वया मत्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः ।

> *pṛśneḥ putrā upamāso rabhiṣṭhāḥ svayā matyā marutaḥ saṃ mimikṣuḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-52-16 [?]) — in this ṛk the word *rabhiṣṭhāḥ* (very forceful ones) is used as an epithet of the Maruts.

> पृथुं तिरश्चा वयसा बृहन्तं व्यचिष्ठमन्नै रभसं दृशानम् । [?]

> *pṛthuṃ tiraścā vayasā bṛhantaṃ vyaciṣṭhamannai rabhasaṃ dṛśānam | [?]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-10-4 [?]) — here the word *rabhasam* is used as an epithet of Agni.

> विष्कभ्नन्तः स्कम्भनेना जनित्री आसीना ऊर्ध्वं रभसं वि मिन्वन् ।

> *viṣkabhnantaḥ skambhanenā janitrī āsīnā ūrdhvaṃ rabhasaṃ vi minvan |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-13 [?]) — in this ṛk the word *rabhasam* is used as an epithet of Indra. And in some places this word is found used in the senses of cruel, terrible, falling suddenly with speed, and so on:

> अधा शयीत निर्ऋतेरुपस्थेऽधैनं वृका रभसासो अद्युः ।

> *adhā śayīta nirṛterupasthe 'dhainaṃ vṛkā rabhasāso adyuḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-14 [?]) — in this ṛk the word *rabhasāsaḥ* is used as an epithet of *vṛkāḥ* (wolves), in the sense "rushing in front with speed, terrible". In the ṛk in question here (the present ṛk) the word *rabhasa* has been used in the sense "shining, luminous".

> भद्रान्कृण्वन्निन्द्रहवान्त्सखिभ्य आ सोमो वस्त्रा रभसानि दत्ते ।

> *bhadrānkṛṇvannindrahavāntsakhibhya ā somo vastrā rabhasāni datte |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-96-1 [?]) — in this ṛk too, the word is used in the same sense, as an epithet of *vastrā* (garments).

The ornaments and weapons of the Maruts are described in detail in the ṛks:

> चित्रैरञ्जिभिर्वपुषे व्यञ्जते वक्षःसु रुक्माँ अधि येतिरे शुभे । अंसेष्वेषां नि मिम्रक्षुर्ऋष्टयः साकं जज्ञिरे स्वधया दिवो नरः ॥

> *citrairañjibhirvapuṣe vyañjate vakṣaḥsu rukmā~ adhi yetire śubhe | aṃseṣveṣāṃ ni mimrakṣurṛṣṭayaḥ sākaṃ jajñire svadhayā divo naraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-4)

> अंसेषु व ऋष्टयः पत्सु खादयो वक्षःसु रुक्मा मरुतो रथे शुभः । अग्निभ्राजसो विद्युतो गभस्त्योः शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययीः ॥

> *aṃseṣu va ṛṣṭayaḥ patsu khādayo vakṣaḥsu rukmā maruto rathe śubhaḥ | agnibhrājaso vidyuto gabhastyoḥ śiprāḥ śīrṣasu vitatā hiraṇyayīḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-54-11)

***etāḥ*** — *śuklavarṇā mālāḥ*: "white garlands or necklaces", is the Bhāṣyakāra's explanation. The word *etāḥ* suggests the sense "a spotted deer". For this very reason *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 51  (PDF 71)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 2".)* …Western scholars are of opinion that the sense indicated here is that the Marut-gods wear (have thrown over) on their shoulders the skin of a spotted deer, [spotted] with marks. For in the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra, and in other Gṛhya-sūtras too, there is the rule that a brāhmaṇa should wear a deer-skin as a garment (in place of a garment). After the *upanayana*, a *brahmacārin* who is a brāhmaṇa should, while studying the Veda, wear the *aiṇeya* (antelope) skin, a kṣatriya the skin of the *raurava* (the deer called *ruru*), and a vaiśya the skin of a goat (*aja*); and when they wear garments, the brāhmaṇa should wear a garment of *kāṣāya* (dark red colour — English), the kṣatriya of *mañjiṣṭha* (bright red colour — English), and the vaiśya of *hāridra* (yellow — English). Hence it may be said that the use of deer-skin in place of cloth was the custom. For this reason it may be that in the present ṛk the ṛṣis and Marut-gods are described as wearing deer-skins on their shoulders. The prepared hide of a deer used as cloth is called *ajina*; it is also called *kṛṣṇājina* (black-deer skin). The use of the word *ajina*, though not in the Ṛgveda, is especially common in the Yajurveda and in the other Vedas.

***kṣurāḥ*** — weapons with greenish edges. *Kṣura* is the name also of the knife that shaves (Razor — English); for a razor must be very green [dark] in colour. It is the custom, when speaking of greenish weapons, to give the example of the razor (*kṣura*). In the Ṛgveda period, and earlier too, shaving with a knife is seen to have been the custom. In this matter:

> यदा ते वातो अनुवाति शोचिर्वप्तेव श्मश्रु वपसि प्र भूम ।

> *yadā te vāto anuvāti śocirvapteva śmaśru vapasi pra bhūma |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-142-4)

> केशश्मश्रु वपते नखानि निकृन्तते मृता वा एषा त्वगमेध्या यत्केशश्मश्रु मृतामेव त्वचममेध्यामपहत्य यज्ञियो भूत्वा मेधमुपैति । [?]

> *keśaśmaśru vapate nakhāni nikṛntate mṛtā vā eṣā tvagamedhyā yatkeśaśmaśru mṛtāmeva tvacamamedhyāmapahatya yajñiyo bhūtvā medhamupaiti | [?]*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-1-2 [?]) — mantras such as these support the fact that shaving with a razor was customary.

***vayo na pakṣān vi anu śriyo dhire*** — here *śriyaḥ* means beauty, splendour ("Splendour", English). As birds spread out their wings when they fly, when the Marut-gods journey their splendour spreads all round, or in all directions: this is the purport.

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* **॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *naryeṣu* (*narāya hitāḥ naryāḥ*; *yat*; *yasyeti ca* drops *a*; *yato 'nāvaḥ* gives the initial acute). *rukmāḥ* (root *ruca dīptau*; suffix *mak* by *yuji rucitijāṃ kuś ca* Uṇ. 1-[?]; *ku* for the root's final by its association; *kit*, so no *laghūpadha-guṇa*; final acute by the suffix). *rabhasāsaḥ* (root *rabha rābhasye*; *asac* suffix by *atyavipracitam…* [as read] Uṇ. 3-[?]; *ciṭaḥ* Pā. 6-1-163 gives the final acute; *jas* with *asuk* by *ājjaser asuk*). *añjayaḥ* (root *añjū vyaktimrakṣaṇagatiṣu*; suffix *i* by *khanikaṣyañji…* Uṇ. 4-[?]; final acute by the suffix; nominative plural). *etāḥ* (root *iṇ gatau*; suffix *tan* by *hasimṛgrinvā…* Uṇ. 3-[?]; guṇa of the *ik* because of it; initial acute as *nit*). *paviṣu* (root *pūñ pavane*; suffix *i* by *āc ca iḥ* Uṇ. 4-[?]; guṇa and *av*-substitution; final acute by the suffix). *kṣurāḥ* (root *kṣura vilekhane*; *ran* by *ṛjrendrāgra…* Uṇ. 2-[?] given by *nipātana*; final acute by *vyatyaya*). *dhire* (root *dhṛñ dhāraṇe*; Vedic *liṭ*; by *vyatyaya* the *ṛ*-part is dropped; no doubling since in the Veda it is optional; *nighāta* since it follows a non-*tiṅanta* [?]). ‖ 10 ‖

### Printed p. 53  (PDF 73)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 3".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> महान्तः । मह्ना । विऽभ्वः । विऽभूतयः । दूरेऽदृशः । ये । दिव्याःऽइव । स्तृऽभिः ।
> मन्द्राः । सुऽजिह्वाः । स्वरितारः । आसऽभिः । संऽमिश्लाः । इन्द्रे । मरुतः । परिऽस्तुभः ॥ ११ ॥

> *mahāntaḥ | mahnā | vi 'bhvaḥ | vi 'bhūtayaḥ | dūre 'dṛśaḥ | ye | divyāḥ 'iva | stṛ 'bhiḥ |*
> *mandrāḥ | su 'jihvāḥ | svaritāraḥ | āsa 'bhiḥ | saṃ 'miślāḥ | indre | marutaḥ | pari 'stubhaḥ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> ये मरुतो महान्तो महाप्रभावोपेताः । केन । मह्ना महत्त्वेन प्रभावातिशयेन । तथा विभ्वो विभवो व्याप्ताः तथा विभूतयो विविधैश्वर्यवन्तः । दूरेदृशो दूरे दृश्यमानाः प्रकाशमानाः । दूरदर्शने दृष्टान्तः । दिव्याः स्तृभिरिव । स्तृ इति नक्षत्रनाम ऋक्षाः स्तृभिरिति नक्षत्राणाम् । नि. ३-२० । इति निरुक्तात् । दिवि भवा देवाः स्तृभिः स्वपुष्पकभूतैस्तेजःपुञ्जैर्नक्षत्रैर्यथा दूरे दृश्यमाना भवन्ति तद्वत् । किञ्च मन्द्रा मादनाः सुजिह्वाः शोभनजिह्वाः आसभिराश्यैः स्वरितारः शब्दयितारः । प्रियवचना इत्यर्थः । अत एव सुजिह्वा इत्युक्तम् । किञ्च इन्द्रे संमिश्लाः सम्यग्मिश्रयितारः । इन्द्रसहायिन इत्यर्थः । मरुतो ह्येनं नाजहुरिति श्रुतेः । तथा परिष्टुभः परिस्तोभयुक्ताः स्तुतिभिर्युक्ताः । एवं महाभागा ये मरुतः सन्ति तेऽस्मद्यज्ञमागच्छन्तीति शेषः ॥

*Gist:* The Maruts, great in glory, all-pervading, many-powered, seen from afar as the star-gods are, joyous, sweet-tongued, speaking pleasantly, Indra's associates, praised on all sides — may such Maruts come to our sacrifice. (Ni. 3-20 [?] is cited for *stṛ* = star.)

**Pratipadārtha.** (*ye marutaḥ* — which Marut-gods); *mahnā* — by the abundance of power; *mahāntaḥ* — endowed with greatness; *vibhvaḥ* — all-pervading; *vibhūtayaḥ* — possessed of manifold glories; *stṛbhiḥ* — by the stars (by their light); *divyāḥ iva* — like those dwelling in the heavenly world, the gods (who are seen from afar); *dūredṛśaḥ* — seen even from afar; *mandrāḥ* — gladdening; *āsabhiḥ* — with mouths; *svaritāraḥ* — sounders (of pleasant speech); *sujihvāḥ* — with excellent tongues (therefore); (*kiṃca* — and further) *indre* — in Indra (with Indra); *saṃmiślāḥ* — well mingled (helpers of Indra); (*tathā* — likewise) *pariṣṭubhaḥ* — endowed with praise (let them come to our sacrificial hall).

**Bhāvārtha.** These Marut-gods are by nature endowed with greatness, are all-pervading, possessed of manifold powers, are seen from afar as the gods are by the brilliance of the stars; they are bestowers of contentment, speakers of pleasant words from their mouths, of good tongues, helpers of Indra and praised everywhere: such as they are, they come to our sacrificial hall.

### Printed p. 54  (PDF 74)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)*

**English Translation (as printed):** Maruts, mighty with mighty power, all-pervading, manifest afar off, as the gods (are made manifest) by the constellations; exhilarating, soft-tongued, speaking gently with your mouths, associated with Indra, glorified by praise; (come to our sacrifice).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***vibhūtayaḥ*** — *vividhaiśvaryavantaḥ*: having manifold glories. In some contexts this word means "powers and capabilities". Though this word is ordinarily used in the nominative (as a subject), in many contexts it is used as an adjective.

> एवा हि ते विभूतय ऊतय इन्द्र मावते ।

> *evā hi te vibhūtaya ūtaya indra māvate |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-8-9 [?]) — here, "O Indra, your powers and capabilities produce protection for a sacrificer such as I": used as a noun (as the thing described).

> स्तोत्रं राधानां पते गिर्वाहो वीर यस्य ते । विभूतिरस्तु सूनृता ॥

> *stotraṃ rādhānāṃ pate girvāho vīra yasya te | vibhūtirastu sūnṛtā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-30-5 [?]) — here, "O Indra, may the praise we make to you be of great power": *vibhūti* is an adjective of the word *sūnṛtā*.

> महामनूनं तवसं विभूतिं मत्सरासो जर्हृषन्त प्रसाहम् ।

> *mahāmanūnaṃ tavasaṃ vibhūtiṃ matsarāso jarhṛṣanta prasāham |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-18-4 [?]) — here, "the sweet Soma juices gladdened Indra, who is great-souled, complete, strong, capable and unconquerable": the word *vibhūti* is used as an epithet of Indra.

> उग्रं न वीरं नमसोप सेदिमा विभूतिमक्षितावसुम् ।

> *ugraṃ na vīraṃ namasopa sedimā vibhūtimakṣitāvasum |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-49-6 [?])

> प्र वीरमुग्रं विविचिं धनस्पृतं विभूतिं राधसो महः ।

> *pra vīramugraṃ viviciṃ dhanaspṛtaṃ vibhūtiṃ rādhaso mahaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-50-6 [?]) — in these ṛks too the word *vibhūti* has been used as an adjective meaning "powerful".

### Printed p. 55  (PDF 75)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 3".)* **Special Topics (continued).**

***stṛbhiḥ*** — *stṛ iti nakṣatranāma | ṛkṣāḥ stṛbhiriti nakṣatrāṇām* (Ni. 3-20 [?]): Yāska says that *stṛbhiḥ* means "stars". Therefore the sentence *dūredṛśo ye divyā iva stṛbhiḥ* means: like the stars shining in the sky, visible from regions very far away; though the stars in the sky are exceedingly far, they appear to us; in the same way the Maruts, though very far off, are visible to us: this is the purport.

***saṃmiślāḥ indre marutaḥ*** — "those who are mixed in Indra", that is, who are in Indra's company, helpers of Indra: this is the purport. That the Marut-gods are Indra's friends is described in ṛks such as:

> अयमिन्द्रो मरुत्सखा वि वृत्रस्याभिनच्छिरः ।

> *ayamindro marutsakhā vi vṛtrasyābhinacchiraḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-76-2 [?])

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *mahnā* (formed as *mahimnā*, with the loss of a letter by Vedic usage; or from the root *mahū pūjāyām* with the *oṇādika* suffix *kasi*; final acute by the suffix; in the instrumental singular the *a* is dropped by *allopo 'naḥ* Pā. 6-4-134; the case-ending gets the acute by *anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ* Pā. 6-1-158). *vibhvaḥ* (*vibhu* + *jas*; by *jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam* there is no guṇa; *yaṇ*-substitution; *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ* Pā. 8-2-4 gives *svarita* to the case-ending). *vibhūtayaḥ* (root *bhū sattāyām*; *ktin*; *tādau ca niti kṛty atiḥ* Pā. 6-2-50 keeps the *gati* (*vi*) accent). *dūredṛśaḥ* (root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; *kvip*; in the *tatpuruṣa* with a *kṛt*, *taṭpuruṣe kṛti bahulam* Pā. 6-3-14 gives *aluk* of the locative; nominative plural). *divyāḥ* (*divi bhavāḥ*; *bhave chandasi* Pā. 4-4-110 [?] gives suffix *ya*; final acute by the suffix). *mandrāḥ* (root *madi stutau*; *rak* by *sphāyitañcivañci…* Uṇ. 2-[?]; *num* by *idito num dhātoḥ* Pā. 7-1-58; final acute by the suffix). *sujihvāḥ* (*śobhanā jihvā yeṣāṃ te*; *nañsubhyām* Pā. 6-2-172 gives the later member the final acute).

### Printed p. 56  (PDF 76)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* **Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (continued).** *svaritāraḥ* (root *svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ*; *tṛc* in the agent sense; *svarati sūti…* Pā. 7-2-44 gives optional *iṭ*; the *iṭ* augment is prescribed; guṇa; *ra*-ending; initial/final accent as the suffix; nominative plural). *āsabhiḥ* (the word *āsya* with *bhis* following; *pad-dan-no-māsa…* Pā. 6-1-63 gives *āsan* in its place; it has the *pada*-designation, so *nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya* Pā. 8-2-7 drops the *n*). ‖ 11 ‖

#### Ṛk 12

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तद्वः सुजाता मरुतो महित्वनं दीर्घं वो दात्रमदितेरिव व्रतम् ।
> इन्द्रश्चन त्यजसा वि ह्रुणाति तज्जनाय यस्मै सुकृते अराध्वम् ॥ १२ ॥

> *tadvaḥ sujātā maruto mahitvanaṃ dīrghaṃ vo dātramaditeriva vratam |*
> *indraścana tyajasā vi hruṇāti tajjanāya yasmai sukṛte arādhvam ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तत् । वः । सुऽजाताः । मरुतः । महित्वनम् । दीर्घम् । वः । दात्रम् । अदितेःऽइव । व्रतम् ।
> इन्द्रः । चन । त्यजसा । वि । ह्रुणाति । तत् । जनाय । यस्मै । सुऽकृते । अराध्वम् ॥ १२ ॥

> *tat | vaḥ | su 'jātāḥ | marutaḥ | mahitvanam | dīrgham | vaḥ | dātram | aditeḥ 'iva | vratam |*
> *indraḥ | cana | tyajasā | vi | hruṇāti | tat | janāya | yasmai | su 'kṛte | arādhvam ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे सुजाताः शोभनजनना हे मरुतः वो युष्मदीयं महित्वनं महत्त्वं तत् ताद्दृक् खलु । तदित्युक्तं किमित्याह । वो युष्माकं दात्रं दानं वृष्ट्यादिरूपं दीर्घमत्यायतमविच्छिन्नं । प्रकृष्टोपकारीत्यर्थः । दीर्घत्वे दृष्टान्तः । अदितेर्व्रतमिव । अदीनाया [?] देवमातुर्भूम्या वा । व्रतमिति कर्मनाम । तद्यथा दीर्घमतिविस्तृतं तद्वत् । अदितिर्द्यौरदितिरन्तरिक्षम् । ऋ. १-८९-१० । इत्यादिमन्त्रवर्णात् । किञ्च हे मरुतः यूयं यस्मै सुकृते शोभनयागादिकर्त्रे यजमानाय यदभिमतं धनमराध्वं तदिन्द्रश्चेन्द्रोऽपि त्यजसा त्यागेन न वि ह्रुणाति ।

> *he sujātāḥ śobhanajananā he marutaḥ vo yuṣmadīyaṃ mahitvanaṃ mahattvaṃ tat tāddṛk khalu | tadityuktaṃ kimityāha | vo yuṣmākaṃ dātraṃ dānaṃ vṛṣṭyādirūpaṃ dīrghamatyāyatamavicchinnaṃ | prakṛṣṭopakārītyarthaḥ | dīrghatve dṛṣṭāntaḥ | aditervratamiva | adīnāyā [?] devamāturbhūmyā vā | vratamiti karmanāma | tadyathā dīrghamativistṛtaṃ tadvat | aditirdyauraditirantarikṣam | ṛ. 1-89-10 | ityādimantravarṇāt | kiñca he marutaḥ yūyaṃ yasmai sukṛte śobhanayāgādikartre yajamānāya yadabhimataṃ dhanamarādhvaṃ tadindraścendro 'pi tyajasā tyāgena na vi hruṇāti |*

### Printed p. 57  (PDF 77)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 3".)* **Bhāṣya (end of Ṛk 12; from the top of the page):**

> न विह्वरति [?] । कौटिल्यं न करोति ॥ चनेत्येयं यद्यपि निपातत्वेऽपि समुदायरूप एको निपातः तथाप्यवयवनिष्ठाभागेन चेशब्दः समुच्चये नशब्दो निषेधेऽधिगन्तव्यः [?] ॥ युष्मद्दत्तनादित्यागमिन्द्रत्यागोऽपि [?] नातिक्रामतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । यस्मै तद्धनमराध्वं तमिन्द्रोऽपि न कुटिलयति । न निषेधयति किन्त्वनुमोदयतीत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* The Maruts' gift of wealth to the sacrificer is as long-lasting as Aditi's rite; even Indra, with his own gift, does not exceed it, nor does he thwart it — he rather approves it.

**Pratipadārtha.** (*he*) *sujātāḥ marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods of fine birth; *vaḥ* — your; *mahitvanam* — greatness; *tat* — such (as described); *vaḥ* — your; *dātram* — gift (in the form of rain and the like); *aditeḥ* — of Aditi, the mother of the gods, or of Earth; *vratam iva* — like the act [of that]; *dīrgham* — very extended (unbroken); (*kiṃca* — and further) *yasmai* — to which; *sukṛte janāya* — to the sacrificer who does auspicious acts such as sacrifice; *arādhvam* — [the desired wealth] you give; *tat* — that giving; *indraḥ ca* — even Indra; *tyajasā* — by his own gift; *na vi hruṇāti* — does not make crooked (does not transgress); *tat* — that [giving]; *indraḥ ca* — even Indra; *na vi hruṇāti* — does not make crooked (does not forbid; he rather approves).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, of excellent birth: your gift in the form of rain and the like is as unbroken as the act of Earth, the goddess [Aditi]; the wealth you give to the sacrificer who performs sacrifices and the like cannot be exceeded even by Indra; (it is approved even by Indra). O Marut-gods, such is your greatness.

**English Translation (as printed):** Such, well-born Maruts, is your greatness, that your munificence is as long (continued) as the function of Aditi; and Indra does not exceed by his own liberality, (the value of) that which you have bestowed upon the devout man (who worships you).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***vrataṃ*** — the word *vrata* is stated among the names of action (*karmanāma*) (Ni. 2-1 [?]). Yāska, explaining the meaning of this word in detail, says:

> व्रतमिति कर्मनाम वृणोतीति सतः । इदमपीतरद्व्रतमेतस्मादेव निवृत्तिकर्म वारयतीति सतः । अन्नमपि व्रतमुच्यते यदावृणोति शरीरम् ।

> *vratamiti karmanāma vṛṇotīti sataḥ | idamapītaradvratametasmādeva nivṛttikarma vārayatīti sataḥ | annamapi vratamucyate yadāvṛṇoti śarīram |*

(Ni. 2-13 [?]) *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 58  (PDF 78)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* Thus he states three kinds of meaning of the word *vrata*: that the action a man does, whether auspicious or inauspicious, pervades him, so action is called *vrata*; or this action may also be *nivṛtti*-action: since it prevents (turns aside) an action that is not desired or not enjoined by the śāstra, it is called *vrata*; and since food pervades the body, food too is called *vrata*.

(1) The word *vrata* is used in the sense of "restrain, hinder, protect" —

> याः पार्थिवासो या अपामसि व्रते ता नो देवीः सुहवाः शर्म यच्छत ।

> *yāḥ pārthivāso yā apāmasi vrate tā no devīḥ suhavāḥ śarma yacchata |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-46-7 [?]) — the word *vrate* in this ṛk gives the sense "hindrance", that is, "protection" which prevents evil: "may the goddesses who are on earth and those who are in water, giving us protection from distress, bestow happiness on us". Here *vrate* means protection that frees from distress.

> तासां नि चिक्युः कवयो निवानं परेषु या गुह्येषु व्रतेषु ।

> *tāsāṃ ni cikyuḥ kavayo nivānaṃ pareṣu yā guhyeṣu vrateṣu |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-109-3 [?]) — the poets (*nirṛti*s?) [as read] discovered what had been enclosed in caves, where no one sees it: here *vrateṣu* with the sense "that which is enclosed" is used as an epithet of the word *guhyeṣu*.

> दद्दृश्र एषामवमा सदांसि परेषु या गुह्येषु व्रतेषु ।

> *daddṛśra eṣāmavamā sadāṃsi pareṣu yā guhyeṣu vrateṣu |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-3 [?])

> असि यमो अस्यादित्यो अर्वन्नसि त्रितो गुह्येन व्रतेन ।

> *asi yamo asyādityo arvannasi trito guhyena vratena |*


(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-163-3) — here too the word *vratena* is used in the sense "enclosed, concealed".

(2) *Vrata* means a prohibitory ordinance, "such work must not be done", or a rule that "such work only must be done" — *dharma-niyama* ("law or ordinance" — English):

> यच्चिद्धि ते विशो यथा प्र देव वरुण व्रतम् । मिनीमसि द्यविद्यवि ॥

> *yaccid dhi te viśo yathā pra deva varuṇa vratam | minīmasi dyavidyavi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-1) — "O Varuṇa, whatever rules of yours we, as men, transgress by negligence (not noticing, doing the act through want of attention) ... *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 59  (PDF 79)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 3".)* **Special Topics (continued: *vrata* as "rule").**

> य उ श्रियो दमेष्वा दोषोषसि प्रशस्यते । यस्य व्रतं न मीयते ॥

> *ya u śriyo dameṣvā doṣoṣasi praśasyate | yasya vrataṃ na mīyate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-8-3 [?]) — "he (Agni) whose rule is not transgressed…" [the print has an ellipsis here].

> इन्द्रस्य कर्म सुकृता पुरूणि व्रतानि देवा न मिनन्ति विश्वे ।

> *indrasya karma sukṛtā purūṇi vratāni devā na minanti viśve |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-32-8) — Indra's deeds of valour are many and well performed; the gods do not break (do not transgress) such rules of Indra.

> विश्वं सत्यं मघवाना युवोरिदापश्चन प्र मिनन्ति व्रतं वाम् ।

> *viśvaṃ satyaṃ maghavānā yuvoridāpaścana pra minanti vrataṃ vām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-84-2 [?]) — "O mighty gods, all that is yours is true; even the waters do not violate your rules."

> वनानि विभ्यो नकिरस्य तानि व्रता देवस्य सवितुर्मिनन्ति ।

> *vanāni vibhyo nakirasya tāni vratā devasya savitur minanti |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-2) — no one transgresses these rules of the god Savitṛ.

> अमिनती दैव्यानि व्रतानि सूर्यस्य चेति रश्मिभिर्दृशाना ।

> *aminatī daivyāni vratāni sūryasya ceti raśmibhirdṛśānā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-12)

> अमिनती दैव्यानि व्रतानि प्रमिनती मनुष्या युगानि ।

> *aminatī daivyāni vratāni praminatī manuṣyā yugāni |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-124-2) — this goddess Uṣas does not transgress the rules of the gods.

> किं स्विन्नो राजा जगृहे कदस्याति व्रतं चकृमा को वि वेद ।

> *kiṃ svinno rājā jagṛhe kadasyāti vrataṃ cakṛmā ko vi veda |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-12-5) — "which of the rules of (this Agni) have we transgressed?"

> अयमेक इत्था पुरूरु चष्टे वि विश्पतिः । तस्य व्रतान्यनु वश्चरामसि ॥

> *ayameka itthā purūru caṣṭe vi viśpatiḥ | tasya vratānyanu vaścarāmasi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-23-16 [?])

### Printed p. 60  (PDF 80)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* …"we shall follow his rules (observe them)". In ṛks like these, and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-37-8 [?]; 2-5-4 [?]; 2-28-6 [?]; 3-38-6 [?] and others, the word *vrata* suggests the meaning "rules, ordinances"; and the word *anuvrata*, found in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-3 [?]; 3-38-6 [?]; 8-40-8 [?]; 1-136-5 [?]; 3-61-1 [?]; 4-13-2 [?]; 5-69-1 [?] and others, suggests the meaning "in accordance with the rules".

(3) In some contexts the rules of the gods are explained as *yajña*, or as the acts of sacrifice, and the word *vrata* has been used for them; for by performing sacrifices and the like, the wish of the gods or their rules are, so to say, observed; thus it is said:

> यो अग्नीषोमा हविषा सपर्याद्देवद्रीचा मनसा यो घृतेन । तस्य व्रतं रक्षतं पातमंहसो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतम् ॥

> *yo agnīṣomā haviṣā saparyāddevadrīcā manasā yo ghṛtena | tasya vrataṃ rakṣataṃ pātamaṃhaso viśe janāya mahi śarma yacchatam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-93-8) — "O Agni and Soma, protect the sacrifice of the man (the sacrificer) who honours you with his mind full of devotion, with oblations and ghee; guard him, so that no harm may happen to him."

> त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरास्तमः कविर्देवानां परि भूषसि व्रतम् ।

> *tvamagne prathamo aṅgirāstamaḥ kavirdevānāṃ pari bhūṣasi vratam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-2) — "O Agni, you are the foremost of the Aṅgirasas, and a seer; you carry out the sacrifice of the gods."

> तस्य व्रतानि भूरिपोषिणो वयमुप भूषेम दम आ सुवृक्तिभिः ।

> *tasya vratāni bhūripoṣiṇo vayamupa bhūṣema dama ā suvṛktibhiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-9 [?]) — "we, rich in wealth and the like, shall perform Agni's sacrificial acts in our house with hymns of praise." In ṛks like these, and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-9 [?]; 8-43-1 [?]; 6-14-3 [?]; 1-24-13 [?]; 6-34-5 [?]; 10-34-13 [?] and others the word *vrata* is used in some one sense: sacrifice, sacrificial act, or act (*karma*). When the meanings are to be made to fit the mantras, of the three kinds of meaning that Yāska has given, whichever fits according to the context is to be stated. This is the main sense and use of the word *vrata*.

***dātram*** — *dānam*: giving, that is, "the act of giving". From the root *dā dāne* are formed *dātā*, *dātram* and the like; the meaning is "one who gives, giving".

***aditeriva*** — the word *aditi* is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 1-1 [?]), among the names of speech (Ni. 1-11 [?]), among the names of the cow (Ni. 4-9 [?]), and among the names of heaven and earth (in the dual) (Ni. 4-22 [?]). Besides this Yāska has said "*aditir adīnā devamātā*" (Ni. 4-22 [?]) ["Aditi, the not-poor, the mother of the gods"]. The derivation and the like and the explanation of the meaning of this word we have already given at length earlier.

***cana*** — *caneti ayaṃ yadyapi nipātatve 'pi samudāyarūpa eko nipātaḥ tathāpy avayavavibhāgena caśabdaḥ samuccaye naśabdo niṣedhe 'dhigantavyaḥ*: although the word *cana* is regarded as one word made up of two particles, if its parts are divided the particle *ca* indicates conjunction and the particle *na* indicates negation. The use of this word to emphasize negation ("not even") is found in many ṛks:

> यस्मादृते न सिध्यति यज्ञो विपश्चितश्चन । स धीनां योगमिन्वति ॥

> *yasmādṛte na sidhyati yajño vipaścitaścana | sa dhīnāṃ yogaminvati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-18-7)

> न पञ्चभिर्दशभिर्वष्ट्यारभं नासुन्वता सचते पुष्यता चन ।

> *na pañcabhirdaśabhirvaṣṭyārabhaṃ nāsunvatā sacate puṣyatā cana |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-34-3)

> नहि ते क्षत्रं न सहो न मन्युं वयश्चनामी पतयन्त आपुः ।

> *nahi te kṣatraṃ na saho na manyuṃ vayaścanāmī patayanta āpuḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-6)

> तृतीयमस्य नकिरा दधर्षति वयश्चन पतयन्तः पतत्रिणः ॥

> *tṛtīyamasya nakirā dadharṣati vayaścana patayantaḥ patatriṇaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-155-5)

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *sujātāḥ* (*śobhanaṃ jātaṃ yeṣāṃ te*; *āmantritasya ca* Pā. 8-1-19 gives *nighāta*). *mahitvanam* (suffix *tva* in the sense of state by *tasya bhāvas tvatalau*; *avan* follows and by Vedic usage a *n* comes to the base). *dātram* (root *ḍudāñ dāne*; *tra* in the sense of the action by *dādibhyaś chandasi* Uṇ. 4-[?]; final acute by the suffix). *cana* (although regarded as one word in the *pada* text, here by dividing its parts it is to be understood that *ca* is used in the sense of conjunction and *na* in negation). *tyajasā* (root *tyaja hānau*; suffix *asun*, which attaches to all roots; initial acute by *ñit*-rule [?]; instrumental singular). *hruṇāti* (a *sautra* root, used in the sense of crookedness; by *vyatyaya* the *śnā* vikaraṇa; *laṭ* 3rd singular; *nighāta* after a *tiṅanta*).

#### Ṛk 13

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तद्वो जामित्वं मरुतः परे युगे पुरू यच्छंसममृतास आवत ।
> अया धिया मनवे श्रुष्टिमाव्या साकं नरो दंसनैरा चिकित्रिरे ॥ १३ ॥

> *tadvo jāmitvaṃ marutaḥ pare yuge purū yacchaṃsamamṛtāsa āvata |*
> *ayā dhiyā manave śruṣṭimāvyā sākaṃ naro daṃsanairā cikitrire ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तत् । वः । जामिऽत्वम् । मरुतः । परे । युगे । पुरु । यत् । शंसम् । अमृतासः । आवत ।
> अया । धिया । मनवे । श्रुष्टिम् । आव्य । साकम् । नरः । दंसनैः । आ । चिकित्रिरे ॥ १३ ॥

> *tat | vaḥ | jāmi 'tvam | marutaḥ | pare | yuge | puru | yat | śaṃsam | amṛtāsaḥ | āvata |*
> *ayā | dhiyā | manave | śruṣṭim | āvya | sākam | naraḥ | daṃsanaiḥ | ā | cikitrire ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः वो जामित्वं बन्धुत्वमस्मद्विषयप्रेमाधिक्यं तत् खलु प्रसिद्धमित्यर्थः । कियत्पर्यन्तमिति तदुच्यते । परे युगे । युगशब्दः कालोपलक्षकः । उत्कृष्टे महति कालेऽतीतेऽपि वर्तत इति शेषः । तत्कथमवगतमित्यत आह । अमृतासोऽमरणधर्माणो हे मरुतः यूयं यद्यस्माच्छंसमस्माभिः क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं पुरु प्रभूतं यथा भवति तथावत रक्षथ । तस्माद्युष्मत्कृतं जामित्वमविनाशीत्यर्थः । किञ्च यूयमया धियानयानुग्रहात्मिकया बुद्ध्या मनवे मनुष्याय स्तोत्रे यष्ट्रेऽस्मदादये श्रुष्टिमाव्य कीर्तिं स्तुतिं वा रक्षित्वा साकं सम्भूय नरो नेतारः सन्तो दंसनैः कर्मभिरित्थंभूता आ चिकित्रिरे । सर्वतो जानीथ ॥ [?]

*Gist:* The Maruts' kinship with us, felt for long ages, shows in their having protected our praises abundantly; with this gracious intent, protecting the fame of the praising man, they act as leaders and come to know all through their deeds.

### Printed p. 64  (PDF 84)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)*

**Pratipadārtha.** (*he*) *amṛtāsaḥ* — O immortal Marut-gods (you); *yat* — for which reason; *śaṃsam* — praise offered by us; *puru* — abundantly; *āvata* — you protect; *ayā dhiyā* — by this intelligence (of grace); *manave* — to men who praise, to us; *śruṣṭim āvya* — protecting fame (praise); *sākam* — (all) together; *naraḥ* — (for us) as leaders; *daṃsanaiḥ* — by acts which; *ā cikitrire* — you know all around (or: you are satisfied); (*he marutaḥ* — O Maruts); *tat* — that; *vaḥ* — your; *jāmitvam* — kinship; *pare yuge* — for a very long time (will remain).

**Bhāvārtha.** O immortal Marut-gods, you consider with great pleasure the praises that we offer, and with a gracious mind you produce renown for us, men who praise you, and become our leaders and perform acts, and are satisfied with them; such is your kinship with us, which is everlasting.

**English Translation (as printed):** Your alliance with us, Maruts, is of a long duration: on which account, immortals, accept our ample praise; and, having accepted our laudation, be gratified, leaders (of sacrifice), by our holy acts, through this (your) favourable disposition towards mankind.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***jāmitvam*** — the word *jāmi* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-12 [?]); but here, for the word *jāmitvam*, the Bhāṣyakāra explains "kinship" (*bandhutva*). Yāska, in his Nirukta, says:

> न जामये भगिन्यै । जामिरन्येऽस्यां जनयन्ति जामुपत्यम् । जमतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मणो निर्गमनप्रायो भवति ॥

> *na jāmaye bhaginyai | jāmiranye 'syāṃ janayanti jāmupatyam | jamatervā syādgatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyo bhavati ‖*

(Ni. 3-6 [?]) — that is, *jāmi* means a sister (*bhaginī*): since in this woman others, that is, the husband and so on, beget offspring, she is called *jāmi*; or, since the word *jāmi* has the sense of motion (*gamana*): since the woman born in a house leaves the house after her marriage and goes to her husband's house, the sister is called *jāmi*: such is the derivation he gives. The general meaning "kinship" which has been given in this ṛk is appropriate.

### Printed p. 65  (PDF 85)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 3".)* **Special Topics (continued).**

***yuge*** — *yugaśabdaḥ kālopalakṣakaḥ | utkṛṣṭe mahati kāle 'tīte 'pi*: the word *yuga* indicates time. Here *pare yuge* means "even after a very long time has passed". The relation between the sacrificer, that is, us, and the Marut-gods is not one that lasts only a short time; it is for a long time: this is the purport.

***śaṃsam*** — *asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇāṃ stutim*: the praise being made by us. The root *śaṃs* means "to say", so *śaṃsa* means "saying". According to the context, in many ṛks the meaning is given as praise (*stotra*) or curse (*śāpa*).

> यजाम देवान्यदि शक्नवाम मा ज्यायसः शंसमा वृक्षि देवाः ।

> *yajāma devānyadi śaknavāma mā jyāyasaḥ śaṃsamā vṛkṣi devāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-42-13 [?])

> अवादेहो दिव आ दस्युमुच्चा प्र सुन्वतः स्तुवतः शंसमावः ॥

> *avādeho diva ā dasyumuccā pra sunvataḥ stuvataḥ śaṃsamāvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-33-6 [?])

> आ वो रुवण्युमौशिजो हुवध्यै घोषेव शंसमर्जुनस्य नंशे ।

> *ā vo ruvaṇyumauśijo huvadhyai ghoṣeva śaṃsamarjunasya naṃśe |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-5 [?]) — in these ṛks the word *śaṃsa* has the senses praise, eulogy, extolling; and in

> मा नः शंसो अररुषो धूर्तिः प्रणङ्मर्त्यस्य ।

> *mā naḥ śaṃso araruṣo dhūrtiḥ praṇaṅmartyasya |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-18-3) and ṛks like it the word *śaṃsa* is used in the senses of defamation, evil speech, and curse.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *jāmitvam* (*jāmeḥ bhāvaḥ*; the suffix *tva* by *tasya bhāvas tvatalau*). *yuge* (root *yujir yoge*; *ghañ*; *cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ* Pā. 7-3-52 turns *j* of the root into *g*; in the sense of a particular time it is in the *uṅbādi* class, so *uṅbādīnāṃ ca* Pā. 6-1-160 gives the final acute; by the force of the text the *laghūpadha-guṇa* that the suffix would bring does not apply). *amṛtāsaḥ* (*na vidyate mṛtaṃ maraṇaṃ yeṣāṃ te*; *ājjaser asuk* Pā. 7-1-50 gives *asuk* to *jas*; *āmantritasya ca* Pā. 8-1-19 gives *nighāta*). *(Printer's signature at the foot: "XIII 5".)*

### Printed p. 66  (PDF 86)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* **Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (continued).** *āvata* (root *ava rakṣaṇe*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* Pā. 3-4-6 gives *laṅ* in the sense of the imperative; 2nd plural; no *nighāta* by the connection with *yad*; the *āṭ* augment being acute gives the initial acute). *ayā* (*anayā*; by *vyatyaya*, in the Veda the *n* is dropped). *dhiyā* (instrumental singular; *sānekācaś ca tṛtīyādiḥ* Pā. 6-1-168 gives the acute to the case-ending). *āvya* (prefix *ā*; root *ava rakṣaṇe*; *ktvā*; *samāse 'napūrve ktvo lyap* Pā. 7-1-37 gives *lyap*; as it has *p* it is *anudātta*). *naraḥ* (root *nṛ nayane*; *kvip*; *jas* following, *ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ* Pā. 7-3-110 gives guṇa; *ra*-ending). *cikitrire* (root *kita jñāne*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* gives *liṭ* in the sense of the present; by *vyatyaya* the third plural suffix comes in place of the second plural; *liṭas tajhayor eśirec* Pā. 3-4-81 gives *ire* for it; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *ruk*; as it is *ṭit* the initial acute; *kuhoś cuḥ* gives *cu* to the reduplicate; *nighāta* after a non-*tiṅanta*). ‖ 13 ‖

#### Ṛk 14

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> येन दीर्घं मरुतः शूशवाम युष्माकेन परीणसा तुरासः ।
> आ यत्ततनन्वृजने जनास एभिर्यज्ञेभिस्तदभीष्टिमश्याम् ॥ १४ ॥

> *yena dīrghaṃ marutaḥ śūśavāma yuṣmākena parīṇasā turāsaḥ |*
> *ā yattatananvṛjane janāsa ebhiryajñebhistadabhīṣṭimaśyām ‖ 14 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> येन । दीर्घम् । मरुतः । शूशवाम । युष्माकेन । परीणसा । तुरासः ।
> आ । यत् । ततनन् । वृजने । जनासः । एभिः । यज्ञेभिः । तत् । अभि । इष्टिम् । अश्याम् ॥ १४ ॥

> *yena | dīrgham | marutaḥ | śūśavāma | yuṣmākena | parīṇasā | turāsaḥ |*
> *ā | yat | tatanan | vṛjane | janāsaḥ | ebhiḥ | yajñebhiḥ | tat | abhi | iṣṭim | aśyām ‖ 14 ‖*

### Printed p. 67  (PDF 87)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 3".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे तुरासो वेगवन्तो मरुतः युष्माकेन युष्मत्सम्बन्धिना येन परीणसा । यद्यप्येतद्बहुनामसु पठितं तथापि यद्बहु तन्महदसि भवतीत्यत्र महदित्यर्थे गृह्यते । महता युष्मदभिगमनेनैषणेन वा दीर्घमायतं सत्रादिरूपं कर्म शूशवाम प्रवर्धयामः । किञ्च यद्येन चाभिगमनेनैषणेन वा जनासो जना अस्मदीया वृजने सङ्ग्रामे आ ततेनन् [?] सर्वतो विस्तारयन्ति । स्वसामर्थ्यैः सङ्ग्रामं जयन्तीत्यर्थः । तदिष्टिमेषणं गमनमेभिर्यज्ञेभिरिदानीं क्रियमाणैः स्तोत्रादिरूपैः पूजनैरभ्याभिमुख्येनाश्याम् । व्याप्नुयाम् ॥

*Gist:* O swift Maruts, by your mighty approach we extend the long, sattra-type rite; by the same approach our men spread out in battle and win; may we gain your coming through these sacrifices, with hymns and worship.

**Pratipadārtha.** *turāsaḥ* — those who are swift; (*he*) *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *yuṣmākena* — connected with you; *yena pariṇasā* — by which great and splendid (approach); *dīrgham* — extended (sacrificial acts in the form of *sattra* and the like); *śūśavāma* — we increase; (and) *yat* — which, by your coming or desire; *janāsaḥ* — (our) men; *vṛjane* — in battle; *ā tatenan* — spread out in all directions (are victorious); *tat* — such; *iṣṭim* — your (wished-for) arrival; *ebhiḥ yajñebhiḥ* — by these sacrifices; *abhi aśyām* — may we obtain, facing it.

**Bhāvārtha.** O swift-going Maruts, by your coming, full of greatness, we increase the long acts such as *sattra*, which we perform; and by your coming men become victorious in battle. Such a coming of yours we desire through these sacrifices.

**English Translation (as printed):** Quick-moving Maruts, we augment the long (offered ceremony) upon your mighty (approach), whereby men triumph in war.—May we obtain, by these our sacrifices, your wished-for (presence).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***dīrgham*** — of sacrifices, some are to be done in a few days, and some are of long duration, that is, to be done over a period of up to a year (*saṃvatsara*); there are two kinds. Sacrifices such as the *darśapūrṇamāsa*, the Soma sacrifices, the *paśubandha*, the *vājapeya*, the *abhiplavaṣaḍaha*, the *agniṣṭoma* are to be done in a few days *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 68  (PDF 88)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* (that is, within a fixed number of days) and finished. The *sattra* sacrifice may be one that is to be done for a year or longer: a long period. Here *dīrgham* means: the Bhāṣyakāra's explanation is that the *sattra* sacrifice to be performed over a long time is intended.

***pariṇasā*** — this word is read among the twelve names of "much", beginning with *uru*, *tuvi*, so it means "abundantly" (Ni. 3-13 [?]). Here the Bhāṣyakāra, in "*yadyapyetadbahunāmasu paṭhitaṃ tathāpi yadbahu tanmahadasi bhavatītyatra mahadityarthe gṛhyate | mahatā yuṣmadabhigamanenaiṣaṇena*", has said: although *pariṇasā* is read among the names of multiplicity, since what is much is great, here it is taken in the sense of "great". Therefore here this word must be rendered "mahatā", that is, "with your coming, full of greatness".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *śūśavāma* (root *ṭuośvi gativṛddhyoḥ*, with the sense of a causal included; 1st plural *mas*; by *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* the *s* of *mas* drops; by *vyatyaya* *śap* → *ślu*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *saṃprasāraṇa* to the root; or by *vibhāṣā śveḥ* [Pā. 6-1-30] *saṃprasāraṇa* after the manner of the *yajus*; doubling; *āḍutta* … [Pā. 6-4-9? [?]] gives the *ā* augment to the suffix; guṇa after the *ik* by the *nimitta*; *av*-substitution; as it is *yad*-connected no *nighāta*; the root accent remains). *yuṣmākena* (*yuṣmākam ayam*; suffix *aṇ* in the sense of relation; *tasminn aṇi ca yuṣmākāsmākau* Pā. 4-3-2 gives *yuṣmāka* to the stem; *saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ* [Pā.] so no *vṛddhi* because of the suffix; by *vyatyaya* the acute falls on the syllable before the suffix). *turāsaḥ* (*matup* dropped in the Veda; *jas* with *asuk*; *āmantrita-nighāta*). *tatenan* [?] (root *tanu vistāre*; *leṭ* 3rd plural, *jhi* suffix; *jho 'ntaḥ* gives *ant*; *itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* Pā. 3-4-97 drops the *i*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *ślu* in place of the vikaraṇa; the root is doubled because of it; no *nighāta* because of *yad*; the root accent remains). *vṛjane* (root *vṛjī varjane*; suffix *kyu* by *kvaipy avṛji…* [Uṇ. 2-[?]]; *yuvor anākau* Pā. 7-1-1 gives *ana* for *yu*; as it is *kit* no *laghūpadha-guṇa*; initial acute by the suffix; locative singular).

#### Ṛk 15

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> एष वः स्तोमो मरुत इयं गीर्मान्दार्यस्य मान्यस्य कारोः ।
> एषा यासीष्ट तन्वे वयां विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ १५ ॥

> *eṣa vaḥ stomo maruta iyaṃ gīrmāndāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ |*
> *eṣā yāsīṣṭa tanve vayāṃ vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ‖ 15 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एषः । वः । स्तोमः । मरुतः । इयम् । गीः । मान्दार्यस्य । मान्यस्य । कारोः ।
> आ । इषा । यासीष्ट । तन्वे । वयाम् । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥ १५ ॥

> *eṣaḥ | vaḥ | stomaḥ | marutaḥ | iyam | gīḥ | māndāryasya | mānyasya | kāroḥ |*
> *ā | iṣā | yāsīṣṭa | tanve | vayām | vidyāma | iṣam | vṛjanam | jīra 'dānum ‖ 15 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अयं मन्त्रस्तृतीयाध्यायान्ते व्याख्यातः । सूक्तोपक्रमप्रभृति क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं मरुद्भ्यः समर्प्य स्वाभीष्टमाशास्ते । हे मरुतः एष स्तोम इदानीं कृतं स्तोत्रं वो युष्माकं युष्मदर्थमित्यर्थः । तथेयं गीः स्तुतिरूपा वागपि वो युष्माकम् । कस्य सम्बन्धीदमिति तदुच्यते । मान्दार्यस्य । मन्दतेरीयतेश्च मान्दार्यः । स्तुतिं प्रेरयतो मान्यस्य माननार्हस्य कारोः स्तोत्रकर्तुः । स्तोत्रैनान्येतत् [?] । स्तोतुः सम्बन्धि । यद्वा । एतत्पदत्रयमुत्तरत्र सम्बध्यते ।

> *ayaṃ mantrastṛtīyādhyāyānte vyākhyātaḥ | sūktopakramaprabhṛti kriyamāṇāṃ stutiṃ marudbhyaḥ samarpya svābhīṣṭamāśāste | he marutaḥ eṣa stoma idānīṃ kṛtaṃ stotraṃ vo yuṣmākaṃ yuṣmadarthamityarthaḥ | tatheyaṃ gīḥ stutirūpā vāgapi vo yuṣmākam | kasya sambandhīdamiti taducyate | māndāryasya | mandaterīyateśca māndāryaḥ | stutiṃ prerayato mānyasya mānanārhasya kāroḥ stotrakartuḥ | stotrainānyetat [?] | stotuḥ sambandhi | yadvā | etatpadatrayamuttaratra sambadhyate |*

### Printed p. 70  (PDF 90)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* **Bhāṣya (continued from p. 69):**

> उक्तलक्षणस्तोतुरिष्टेच्छया कामनया तन्वे युष्मच्छरीरवृद्ध्यै । स्तुत्या हि शरीरं वर्धते । आ यासीष्ट । अभिगच्छतु स्तुतिः । वयां वयं चेषमन्नं वृजनं बलं जीरदानुं चिरकालजीवनं च विद्याम । लभेमहि ॥

*Gist:* This ṛk was explained at the end of the third adhyāya. Presenting the praise made since the beginning of the Sūkta to the Maruts, the poet asks for his wish: may the praise of the honoured praiser, who is a delight-giver by his praise, reach you for your bodily growth, and may we obtain food, strength and long life.

**Pratipadārtha.** (*he*) *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *eṣaḥ* — this (what has been made so far); *stomaḥ* — praise; *vaḥ* — to you (to please you); *iyaṃ gīḥ* — this speech of praise; *vaḥ* — to you (therefore); *māndāryasya* — who gives you delight by praise; *mānyasya* — worshipful (by giving boons, by [your] honouring); *kāroḥ* — of the praiser; *iṣā* — with desire; *tanve* — for the body (for its nourishment); *ā yāsīṣṭa* — may it come; *vayām* — we; *iṣam* — food; *vṛjanam* — strength; *jīradānum* — long life; *vidyāma* — may we obtain.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, may the praise made so far, and this speech [being uttered] now, give you satisfaction; and, by the wish of the praiser, who delights you with praise and who is worshipful, may it come to you for the nourishing of your bodies; (and having come) may you grant us food, strength and a long life.

**English Translation (as printed):** This praise, Maruts, is for you: this hymn is for you; (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring delight (by his laudationi [sic]): may the praise reach you (for the good of your) persons, so that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** In this last ṛk of the Sūkta the ṛṣi offers the praise to the deities and prays for their grace in the form of food, strength, long life, and — beginning with victory — the like; this prayer is made. This ṛk is read again at the end of the previous Sūkta, that is, in 1-165 [?], and in the Sūktas 1-166 [?]; 1-167 [?]; 1-168 [?]. Besides this, the sentence of the last pāda of this ṛk, *vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum*, is read again in many of the following Sūktas seen by this ṛṣi.

***māndāryasya*** — *mandater īyateś ca māndāryaḥ*: "the praiser of you who impels you with hymns", is the meaning.

---

### Printed p. 71  (PDF 91)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 3".)* **Special Topics (continued).**

***mānyasya*** — *varapradānādibhiḥ* (by you) honourable: since you favour those who praise, with the granting of boons and the like — this is the purport.

***kāroḥ*** — since the word *kāru* is read among the thirteen names of the praiser, *rebhaḥ*, *jaritā* and the rest (Ni. 3-16 [?]), *kāroḥ* means "of the praiser". And for the word *kāru* he has also given the derivation "*yajñasya kartārau* (*ṛtvijau*)" — "the priests who take part in a sacrifice" (Ni. 9-13 [?]).

***tanve*** — *yuṣmacchararīravṛddhyai*: for the increase of your (bodies); it is well known that deities who are praised, grow. In many ṛks, in place of words meaning "to praise", the word *vṛddhi* ("growth") is used. For example:

> त्वां स्तोमा अवीवृधन् त्वामुक्था शतक्रतो । त्वां वर्धन्तु नो गिरः ॥

> *tvāṃ stomā avīvṛdhan tvāmukthā śatakrato | tvāṃ vardhantu no giraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-5-8)

> इमा उ त्वा पुरूवसो गिरो वर्धन्तु या मम ।

> *imā u tvā purūvaso giro vardhantu yā mama |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-3 [?])

> अग्निं वर्धन्तु नो गिरो यतो जायत उक्थ्यः ।

> *agniṃ vardhantu no giro yato jāyata ukthyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-10-6 [?])

> वर्धन्तु त्वा सुष्टुतयो गिरो मे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ।

> *vardhantu tvā suṣṭutayo giro me yūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-99-7 [?]) — in ṛks like these it is said that deities grow by the praises made by the priests.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *māndāryasya* (from the root *madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu*, and from the root *īra gatau preraṇe ca*; from these it is obtained by *pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam*). *kāroḥ* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *karotīti kāruḥ*; suffix *uṇ* by *kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhya uṇ* Uṇ. 1-1; being *ṇit*, *vṛddhi* by *aco 'ñṇiti*; final acute by the suffix). *iṣā* (root *iṣu icchāyām*; *kvip* by *kvip ca*; instrumental singular; *sānekācaś ca tṛtīyādiḥ* Pā. 6-1-168 gives the acute to the case-ending).

### Printed p. 72  (PDF 92)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 166".)* **Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (continued).** *yāsīṣṭa* (root *yā prāpaṇe*; by *vyatyayo bahulam* ātmanepada; *liṅ* 3rd singular *ta*; *suṭ tithoḥ* Pā. 3-4-107 gives *suṭ*; *liṅaḥ sīyuṭ* Pā. 3-4-102 gives *sīyuṭ*; *y* dropped; *nighāta* after a non-*tiṅanta*). *tanve* (the word *tanū*, dative singular; *tanādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam* gives *yaṇ*-substitution; *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ* Pā. 8-2-4 gives *svarita* to the case-ending). *vayām* (*asmad* + *jas*; *jasaḥ śī* … *prathamayor am* Pā. 7-1-28 gives *am* for the suffix; *yūyavayau jasi* Pā. 7-2-93 gives *vaya* for the base; *ā* by *vyatyaya*). *vidyāma* (root *vida lābhe*; *liṅ* 1st plural; since it is at the start of the pāda no *nighāta*; the suffix gets the initial acute). *jīradānum* (*jīraḥ dānur yasya saḥ jīradānuḥ taṃ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* gives the first member's accent). ‖ 15 ‖

## Sūkta 167 — *sahasraṃ te svapivāta* (Anuvāka 23, third Sūkta; 11 ṛks)

*(Heading, p. 72: "The hundred and sixty-seventh Sūkta" — ನೂರ ಅರವತ್ತೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> सहस्रं ते इत्येकादशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभम् । आद्येन्द्री शिष्टा मरुद्देवताकाः पूर्वत्र हिशब्दात् । सहस्रमेकादशाद्यैन्द्रीत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ विशेषविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

*Gist:* The third sūkta (*sahasraṃ te*), of eleven ṛks, seen by Agastya, in triṣṭubh; the first ṛk is addressed to Indra, the rest to the Maruts (because of *hi* in the preceding sūkta); the Anukramaṇikā: "*sahasram ekādaśādyaindrī*". Special application by indication.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This Sūkta beginning *sahasraṃ te* is the third Sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has eleven ṛks. Agastya is the ṛṣi of this Sūkta. The metre is *triṣṭubh*. The first ṛk has Indra as its deity; the remaining ṛks are addressed to the Maruts. The Anukramaṇikā says: "*sahasram ekādaśādyaindrī*". The special application (*viniyoga*) is by indication.

> *sahasraṃ ta indrotayo naḥ sahasramiṣo harivo gūrtatamāḥ |*
> *sahasraṃ rāyo mādayadhyai sahasriṇa upa no yantu vājāḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सहस्रम् । ते । इन्द्र । ऊतयः । नः । सहस्रम् । इषः । हरिऽवः । गूर्तऽतमाः ।
> सहस्रम् । रायः । मादयध्यै । सहस्रिणः । उप । नः । यन्तु । वाजाः ॥ १ ॥

> *sahasram | te | indra | ūtayaḥ | naḥ | sahasram | iṣaḥ | hari 'vaḥ | gūrta 'tamāḥ |*
> *sahasram | rāyaḥ | mādayadhyai | sahasriṇaḥ | upa | naḥ | yantu | vājāḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र ते तवोतयो रक्षाप्रकाराः सहस्रम् । अपरिमिता इत्यर्थः । नोऽस्मभ्यमुप यन्त्विति सर्वत्र योज्यम् । तथा हे हरिवः । हरी इन्द्रस्याश्वौ । ताभ्यां तद्वन्निन्द्र गूर्ततमा अत्यन्तं गूर्णानि [?] एषणीयानि [?] अन्नानि सहस्रं बहूनि त्वदीयानि । तथा सहस्रं रायोऽपरिमितानि धनानि मणिमुक्तादीनि मादयध्यै अस्मान्मादयितुं यानि सन्ति तान्यस्मानुप यन्तु । तथा सहस्रिणो वाजा गमनवन्तश्चतुष्पादपशवोऽपि नोऽस्मानुप यन्तु । समीपं प्राप्नुवन्तु ॥

*Gist:* O Indra, may your thousand (countless) protections, thousands of coveted foods, countless gems and pearls to gladden us, and thousands of moving animals, come near to us.

**Pratipadārtha.** (*he*) *indra* — O Indra; *te* — your; *ūtayaḥ* — acts of protection; *sahasram* — a thousand; *naḥ* — for us; *upa yantu* — may they come near; (*he*) *harivaḥ* — O Indra with the horses called Hari; *gūrtatamāḥ* — (exceedingly strong =) most excellent; *sahasram* — countless; *iṣaḥ* — (various) foods; (*naḥ upa yantu* — may they come near us); (*tathā* — likewise) *sahasram rāyaḥ* — countless wealth of jewels and the like; *mādayadhyai* — to gladden us; (*naḥ upa yantu*); (*tathā* — likewise) *sahasriṇaḥ* — in thousands; *vājāḥ* — moving beings, animals and the like; *naḥ* — to us; (*upa yantu* — may they come near).

### Printed p. 74  (PDF 94)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* **Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, protect us in a thousand ways; O Indra, with the horses called Hari, grant us, for our delight, most excellent foods of many kinds, in countless numbers, unlimited wealth of jewels and the like, and thousands of animals.

**English Translation (as printed):** May your thousand benefits, Indra, come to us: may a thousand kinds of abundant food come to us, lord of horses: may a thousand (sorts of) wealth come to exhilarate us: may thousands of horses be ours.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***sahasraṃ ūtayaḥ*** — here, in addressing Indra, the word *sahasra* is explained as *aparimitāḥ* ("immeasurable"), that is, "so many that it is impossible to count". The prayer is made that Indra, as many as there are acts of protection, may protect us, the sacrificers, by his many kinds of protection.

***harivaḥ*** — Yāska says "*harī indrasya*" (Ni. 1-[?]); the horses of Indra are known as *harī*. Because Indra has these horses he is addressed by the word *harivaḥ*.

***gūrtatamāḥ iṣaḥ*** — *atyantaṃ gūrṇāni eṣaṇīyāni annāni*: "very greatly desirable foods, to be sought". Because living beings seek them, the word *iṣaḥ* is explained as "food". *Iṣam* is stated among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?]). The prayer is made: "O Indra, grant us countless foods."

***sahasraṃ rāyaḥ mādayadhyai upayantu*** — *aparimitāni dhanāni maṇimuktādīni asmān mādayituṃ yāni santi tāni asmān upayantu*: "may all the countless riches, jewels, pearls and the like that exist for gladdening us come to us". The word *rāyaḥ* is read among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]). The prayer is made that all the wealth, that is, countless jewels and pearls and other things such as we desire in order to be glad and gladdened, may come to us by Indra's grace.

### Printed p. 75  (PDF 95)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 4".)* **Special Topics (continued).**

***sahasriṇaḥ vājāḥ*** — *gamanavantaś catuṣpādādipaśavaḥ*: animals such as quadrupeds that move. The word *vāja* is read among the names of food (Ni. 2-7 [?]).

> पावका नः सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती । यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुः ॥

> *pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī vājebhirvājinīvatī | yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-10) — here, for the word *vājinīvatī* Sāyaṇa explains *annena haviṣā udakena vā tadvatī* ("possessed of food, the oblation, or of water"); since he has explained "possessed of food in the form of oblation, or of water", the word *vāja* indicates several meanings. But here the meaning "*vājāḥ gamanavantaḥ*" — creatures that move, that go about — is given. The prayer is made that cattle and other creatures with two feet and four feet, may, by Indra's grace, come to us without number.

Yāska (Ni. 10-8 [?]) has explained the meaning of the word *indra* by derivations: [as read]

> इरां दृणाति । इरां ददाति । इरां दधाति । इरां दारयति । इन्दवे द्रवतीति वा । इन्दौ रमत इति वा । इन्धे भूतानीति वा । इदं करणादित्याग्रायणः । इदं दर्शनादित्यौपमन्यवः । इन्देरैश्वर्यकर्मणः । इन्द्रो दृशत्रूणां [?] दारयिता वा द्रावयिता वा आदरयिता च यज्वनाम् ।

> *irāṃ dṛṇāti | irāṃ dadāti | irāṃ dadhāti | irāṃ dārayati | indave dravatīti vā | indau ramata iti vā | indhe bhūtānīti vā | idaṃ karaṇādityāgrāyaṇaḥ | idaṃ darśanādityaupamanyavaḥ | inderaiśvaryakarmaṇaḥ | indro dṛśatrūṇāṃ [?] dārayitā vā drāvayitā vā ādarayitā ca yajvanām |*

That is: "he who splits (*dṛṇāti*) the *irā* — he who makes the shoots spring up from seeds moistened by the rain-water"; "he who gives *irā* (food) — who, making food spring up by the rain, gives it to the world"; "he who holds *irā* — who bears food for the good of the world"; "he who impels (*dārayati*) *irā* — who impels the seeds to grow, in the form of sprouts"; or "he who runs to Indu (Soma)" — who comes to the sacrificial hall for drinking Soma; or "he who rejoices in Indu" — who is delighted in the drinking of Soma; or "he who kindles beings" — who favours beings with food and the like and makes them prosper. And, according to the Āgrāyaṇa school, "because he does *idam*" — Indra himself does all the acts in the world; according to the disciples of Aupamanyu, "because he sees *idam*" — Indra sees directly all the affairs of the world; "from the root *ind*, of the sense of lordship" — he who has excess of lordship; "Indra is one who splits (destroys) enemies, or makes them flee, or destroys the lordship of the enemies and himself becomes lord, and who shows respect for the sacrificers": in many ways has he explained.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *ūtayaḥ* (formed by *ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca* Pā. 3-3-97 [?] as a *kin*-ending word, which has the *udātta*, by *nipātana*; nominative plural). *harivaḥ* (*harī asya staḥ iti harivān*; *matup*; *chandasīraḥ* Pā. 8-2-15 turns the *m* of *matup* into *v*; in the vocative *ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ* Pā. 7-1-70 gives *num*; *saṃyogāntalopa* drops the final… *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 76  (PDF 96)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* …*matuvasoḥ ru sambuddhau chandasi* Pā. 8-3-1 gives *ru* in the vocative; *āmantritasya ca* gives *nighāta*). *gūrtatamāḥ* (*atyantaṃ gūrtāḥ gūrtatamāḥ*; *atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau* Pā. 5-3-55 gives *tamap*; as it has *p*, the suffix is *anudātta*). *mādayadhyai* (root *mada tṛptiyoge*; *hetumati ca* Pā. 3-1-26 gives *ṇic*; after the *ṇijanta*, wishing for *tumun*, *tumarthe sesenasase…* Pā. 3-4-9 gives *adhyai*; since it ends in *ej* it is called an indeclinable by *kṛnmejantaḥ* Pā. 1-1-39; initial acute of the suffix). *sahasriṇaḥ* (*sahasram eṣām asti iti*; *ata iniṭhanau* Pā. 5-2-115 gives *ini* in the sense of possession; initial acute by the suffix's accent). *yantu* (root *iṇ gatau*; *loṭ* 3rd plural; *nighāta* after a non-*tiṅanta*). *vājāḥ* (belongs to the *vṛṣādi* class, so *vṛṣādīnāṃ ca* Pā. 6-1-203 gives the initial acute; nominative plural). ‖ 1 ‖

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आ नोऽवोभिर्मरुतो यान्त्वच्छा ज्येष्ठेभिर्वा बृहद्दिवैः सुमायाः ।
> अध यदेषां नियुतः परमाः समुद्रस्य चिद्धनयन्त पारे ॥ २ ॥

> *ā no 'vobhirmaruto yāntvacchā jyeṣṭhebhirvā bṛhaddivaiḥ sumāyāḥ |*
> *adha yadeṣāṃ niyutaḥ paramāḥ samudrasya ciddhanayanta pāre ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । नः । अवःऽभिः । मरुतः । यान्तु । अच्छ । ज्येष्ठेभिः । वा । बृहत्ऽदिवैः । सुऽमायाः ।
> अध । यत् । एषाम् । निऽयुतः । परमाः । समुद्रस्य । चित् । धनयन्त । पारे ॥ २ ॥

> *ā | naḥ | avaḥ 'bhiḥ | marutaḥ | yāntu | accha | jyeṣṭhebhiḥ | vā | bṛhat 'divaiḥ | su 'māyāḥ |*
> *adha | yat | eṣām | ni 'yutaḥ | paramāḥ | samudrasya | cit | dhanayanta | pāre ‖ 2 ‖*
