### Printed p. 77  (PDF 97)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 4".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> ते मरुतोऽवोभी रक्षणैः सहिता नोऽस्मानच्छाभिमुख्येन यान्तु । आगच्छन्तु । सुमायाः । मायेति प्रज्ञानाम । शोभनप्रज्ञा एव मरुतो ज्येष्ठेभिर्बृहद्दिवैर्वा ज्येष्ठैः प्रशस्यतमैर्बृहद्दिवैः [?] मणिमुक्तादिधनैश्च सहिता आ यान्तु । वाशब्दः समुच्चये । आगमने कथमेषां सामर्थ्यमिति अत आह । अध यद्यस्मादेषां मरुतां नियुत एतन्नामकाः परमा उत्कृष्टा अश्वाः समुद्रस्य चित् चिच्छब्दोऽप्यर्थे । समुद्रस्यापि पारे परस्मिंस्तीरे धनयन्ते धनधारणं वहनं कुर्वन्ति । तस्माज्ज्येष्ठैर्धनैश्चायान्त्वित्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* May the Maruts, of good wisdom, come to us with their protections and with their choice treasures (jewels, pearls), since their excellent horses called Niyut carry wealth even from beyond the sea.

**Pratipadārtha.** *adha* — afterwards; *yat* — for what reason; *eṣām* — of these Marut-gods; *paramāḥ* — most excellent; *niyutaḥ* — horses named Niyut; *samudrasya* — of the ocean; *pāre cit* — even on the farther side; *dhanayante* — bear wealth; (*tat* — therefore); (*te*) *marutaḥ* — those Marut-gods; *avobhiḥ* — with (our) acts of protection; *naḥ* — to us; *acchā* — towards; *ā yāntu* — may they come; *sumāyāḥ* — wise Marut-gods; *jyeṣṭhebhiḥ* — most excellent; (and) *bṛhaddivaiḥ vā* — greatly praiseworthy jewels and pearls, riches [with them]; (*ā yāntu* — may they come).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, of excellent wisdom: your best horses called Niyut are able to carry wealth from even beyond the ocean; therefore, with the highest and most praiseworthy wealth of jewels and the like, and with acts of protection, come toward us.

**English Translation (as printed):** May the Maruts come to our presence with benefactions: may they who are possessed of knowledge (come) with most excellent and brilliant (treasures), since their glorious horses, the Niyutas, gather wealth even on the farther shore of the sea.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***marutaḥ avobhiḥ naḥ ā yāntu*** — *rakṣaṇaiḥ sahitāḥ asmān āgacchantu*: "may they come to us together with protections". The word *marutaḥ* is read among the names of priests (Ni. 3-19 [?]) and also among the names of gold (Ni. 1-10 [?]). *Marutaḥ* — "*mitarāviṇo vā mitarociṇo vā mahad dravantīti vā*" [as read] is the derivation given by Yāska *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 78  (PDF 98)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* …the explained word *marut* is read by Yāska among the groups of gods in the middle region. Explaining the word as "those who make a sound in proportion to their strength", as "those who shine with brilliance", and as "those who give rain", and thus giving the meaning in many ways, the prayer is made that these Maruts may come to our sacrifice together with the means of protecting us.

***sumāyāḥ*** — *śobhanaprajñāḥ*: the word *māyā* is stated among the names of intelligence (Ni. 3-13 [?]). The Marut-gods are described as having extraordinary wisdom.

***jyeṣṭhebhiḥ bṛhaddivaiḥ ā yāntu*** — the word *jyeṣṭhebhiḥ* may mean "with abundant brilliance"; or *praśasyaiḥ maṇimuktādidhanaiś ca sahitāḥ*: giving two kinds of meaning, "jewels (*ratna*)", "pearls (*muktā*)" and such wealth, the prayer is made that the Maruts come with these.

***niyutaḥ paramāḥ samudrasya cit pāre dhanayante*** — *etannāmakāḥ utkṛṣṭāḥ aśvāḥ samudrasyāpi pare 'smiṃstīre…* [as read]: "excellent horses named Niyut carry wealth even on the farther shore of the ocean"; so, describing that the Marut-gods have such horses, called Niyut, and bring wealth even from the farther shore of the sea, the prayer is made that they come to our sacrifice with such abundant wealth. The word *samudra* is read among the names of the middle region (Ni. 2-10 [?]); and since the word *samudra* indicates both the earthly ocean, filled with well-known water, and the middle region, in order to clear the doubt Yāska says:

> तत्र समुद्र इत्येतत् पार्थिवेन समुद्रेण संदिह्यते । समुद्रः कस्मात् । समुद्द्रवन्त्यस्मादापः । समभिद्रवन्त्येनमापः । संमोदन्तेऽस्मिन्भूतानि । समुदको भवति । समुनत्तीति वा ।

> *tatra samudra ityetat pārthivena samudreṇa saṃdihyate | samudraḥ kasmāt | samuddravantyasmādāpaḥ | samabhidravantyenamāpaḥ | saṃmodante 'smin bhūtāni | samudako bhavati | samunattīti vā |*

(Ni. 2-10 [?]) — [meaning]: because the waters in it, in the form of waves and ripples, move in many ways; because very abundant waters collect in your region, the waters flow in with speed; because creatures living in water are made happy by the abundance of water; and because it makes everything wet with water — for these reasons the name *samudra* has come about: thus Yāska has explained; and he has also established that *samudra* means the *antarikṣa* (middle region). That the Maruts have horses is well known in the Yajurveda.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *avobhiḥ* (root *ava rakṣaṇe*; *asun* by *sarvadhātubhya asun* Uṇ. 4-[?]; as it is *nit*, the initial acute; instrumental plural). *yāntu* (root *yā prāpaṇe*; *loṭ* 3rd plural; *nighāta* after a *tiṅanta*).

### Printed p. 79  (PDF 99)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 4".)* **Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (continued, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *acchā* (*nipātasya ca* Pā. 6-3-136 [?] gives lengthening in the Saṃhitā). *jyeṣṭhebhiḥ* (*atiśayena praśasyaḥ*; suffix *iṣṭhan*; *jyā ca* Pā. 5-3-61 gives *jya* for *praśasya*; *prakṛtyaikāc* Pā. 6-4-163 [?] — by the preservation of the base the *al*-drop does not occur; guṇa; *bhis*: *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives no *ais*; *bahuvacane jhaly et* gives *e*). *bṛhaddivaiḥ* (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* gives the accent of the first member). *sumāyāḥ* (*śobhanā māyā yeṣāṃ te*; *nañsubhyām* Pā. 6-2-172 gives the final acute of the later member). *adha* (the Vedic change in the word *atha*). *niyutaḥ* (root *yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ*; *kvip ca*; *hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk* gives *tuk*; the *kṛdutta* member keeps its own accent; nominative plural). *dhanayante* (from the word *dhana*; *tatkaroti tadācaṣṭe* gives *ṇic*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* gives *laṭ* in the present sense; 3rd plural, *jha* → *anta*; *śap*; guṇa and *ay*-substitution after *ṇic*; *ṭi* dropped; *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi* gives no *aṭ*). ‖ 2 ‖

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> मिम्यक्ष येषु सुधिता घृताची हिरण्यनिर्णिगुपरा न ऋष्टिः ।
> गुहा चरन्ती मनुषो न योषा सभावती विदथ्येव सं वाक् ॥ ३ ॥

> *mimyakṣa yeṣu sudhitā ghṛtācī hiraṇyanirṇiguparā na ṛṣṭiḥ |*
> *guhā carantī manuṣo na yoṣā sabhāvatī vidathyeva saṃ vāk ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 80  (PDF 100)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> मिम्यक्ष । येषु । सुऽधिता । घृताची । हिरण्यऽनिर्निक् । उपरा । न । ऋष्टिः ।
> गुहा । चरन्ती । मनुषः । न । योषा । सभाऽवती । विदथ्याऽइव । सम् । वाक् ॥ ३ ॥

> *mimyakṣa | yeṣu | su 'dhitā | ghṛtācī | hiraṇya 'nirnik | uparā | na | ṛṣṭiḥ |*
> *guhā | carantī | manuṣaḥ | na | yoṣā | sabhā 'vatī | vidathyā 'iva | sam | vāk ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> सुधिता सुष्ठु निहिता सुष्ठु हिता वा लोके घृताची घृतं क्षरणशीलमुदकमञ्चन्ती हिरण्यनिर्णिक् तरमणीयरूपा [?] । निर्णिगिति रूपनाम । एवंरूपा ऋष्टिर्विद्युदाख्यायुधविशेषो वा उपरा न मेघमालेव येषु मरुत्सु सं मिम्यक्ष संगतभूत् । मेघपङ्क्तिर्विद्युताविनो [?] अपि संगते इत्यर्थः । मेघपङ्क्तिर्विद्युच्छोभे दृष्टान्तेन विशेष्येते [?] । गुहा निगूढा गुहायां वान्तरिक्षे चरन्ती । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । मनुषो न योषा मनुष्यस्य परिव्यूढादेर्महिषीव [?] । सा यथा सुवेषान्तःपुर इव मध्ये चरति तद्वत् । किं सर्वदैवमिति नेत्याह । सभावती । सभा जनसंघः । तद्वती । वर्षकाल आविर्भवन्तीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । विदथ्येव वाक् । विदथो यज्ञः । तदर्हतीति विदथ्या प्रैषस्तोत्रादिरूपा वाक् । सा यथा यज्ञसभां प्राप्याविर्भवति तद्वत् । यद्वा । विदथ्या वेदनार्हा विविदमानयोर्वाक् । सा यथा सभा भवति तद्वत् । एवंरूपा येषु मिम्यक्ष ते मरुतो देवयजनमागच्छन्त्वित्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* In whichever Maruts the lightning, well-set, water-pouring, golden-shaped, is joined, like a cloud-line; moving hidden in the sky as a woman of a man, appearing in the rainy season as in an assembly, as sacrificial speech appears at the sacrifice — may those Maruts come to our sacrifice.

**Pratipadārtha.** *yeṣu* — in which Marut-gods; *sudhitā* — well fixed; *ghṛtācī* — water-pouring; *hiraṇyanirnik* — of a lovely, golden form; *ṛṣṭiḥ* — the lightning-weapon; *manuṣaḥ* — of a man (an excellent man); *yoṣā* — an adorned woman; (*guhā carantī iva* — as if moving concealed in the inner apartments); *guhā* — in the hidden place; *carantī* — moving; *vidathyā* — fit for sacrifice; *vāk* — speech in the form of praise (*sabhāvatī iva* — as if appearing in the sacrificial assembly); *vidathyā* — of those who discuss; *vāk* — speech; (*sabhāvatī iva* — as if appearing in an assembly); *sabhāvatī* — appearing in the rainy season; *upara na* — like a garland of clouds (as it is joined with the Maruts); *saṃ mimyakṣa* — is well joined (may those Marut-gods come to our sacrificial hall).

### Printed p. 81  (PDF 101)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 4".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** As the adorned wife of an excellent man moves about in the inner apartments, so the garland of clouds — moving in the sky, appearing in the rainy season like speech (the praises and the rest) fit for sacrifice, which comes out only in assemblies — is joined with the Marut-gods; and lightning, golden-coloured and the cause of rain, is joined with them in a fitting manner. May such Marut-gods come to our sacrificial hall.

**English Translation (as printed):** In whom the water-shedding, golden-coloured lightning, is fitly deposited like a chaplet (of clouds) moving in the firmament like the (splendidly-attired) wife of a man (of rank), and distinguished in assemblies like a sacrificial hymn.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***sudhitā*** — *suṣṭhu nihitā suṣṭhu hitā vā*: "well placed" or "very beneficial". Two kinds of meaning are given: that which does good to the world, or that which is known as lovely to all in the world.

***ghṛtācī hiraṇyanirṇik ṛṣṭiḥ*** — *ghṛtaṃ kṣaraṇaśīlam udakam añcati hitaramaṇīyarūpā vidyudākhyāyudhaviśeṣo vā*: [Sāyaṇa]. The word *nirṇik* is read among the names of form (Ni. 2-13 [?]); the word *ghṛta* is also read among the names of water (Ni. 1-12 [?]). The meaning given is: the Marut-gods produce a weapon, lightning (*vidyut*), which has a form beneficial to the people of the world, joined with water that flows in liquid form. By the special action of their motion the Marut-gods produce the weapon, lightning (*aśani*), in the waters.

***upara na saṃ mimyakṣa*** — *meghapaṅktir vidyutā … ime api saṃgate ity arthaḥ*: the word *upara* is stated among the names of the cloud (Ni. 1-[?]). The Marut-gods, by making in the waters two kinds of change, the fluid nature and the dense (thickening) nature, in that, the line of clouds and the lightning join together; and in their body of this form is borne the weapon known as *ṛṣṭi*, the *aśani*, and they are seen in the world with lightning as with a garland of clouds — thus the form of the Maruts' special weapon is compared with the form together with cloud and lightning. Yāska — *(Printer's signature at the foot: "XIII 6".)* *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 82  (PDF 102)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)*

> आ विद्युन्मद्भिर्मरुतः स्वर्कै रथेभिर्यात ऋष्टिमद्भिरश्वपर्णैः । आ वर्षिष्ठया न इषा वयो न पप्तता सुमायाः ॥

> *ā vidyunmadbhirmarutaḥ svarkai rathebhiryāta ṛṣṭimadbhiraśvaparṇaiḥ | ā varṣiṣṭhayā na iṣā vayo na paptatā sumāyāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-88-1) — in the ṛk that teaches this same idea, the Maruts' coming, with their weapons, riding in chariots, is described. About the moving of the line of clouds together with lightning, the sentence *guhā carantī manuṣo na yoṣā* has been said in the form of an illustration. In the cloud the lightning (*vidyut*) is hidden; and because it moves in the middle region, for the word *guhā* two meanings, "secret place" and "the middle region", are explained. The particle *na* is explained by Yāska: "*neti pratiṣedhārthīyo bhāṣāyām ubhayam anvadhyāyam*" (Ni. 1-4 [?]) [as read]; the particle *na*, as a word of ordinary usage, conveys the sense of negation. In the Veda it is used in two kinds of sense, negation and comparison (*upamā*). For example:

> नेन्द्रं देवममंसत ।

> *nendraṃ devamamaṃsata |*

— here the word *na* is used in the sense of negation.

> हृत्सु पीतासो युध्यन्ते दुर्मदासो न सुरायाम् । ऊधर्न नग्ना जरन्ते ॥

> *hṛtsu pītāso yudhyante durmadāso na surāyām | ūdharna nagnā jarante ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-2-12 [?]) — here, to say "those who have drunk spirits fight like those who are in mutual rivalry", the sense of comparison is given to the word *na*, and its usage in the sense of comparison is shown. Likewise in *ūdhar na nagnā* it is used in the comparative sense. Following this, for the sentence *manuṣo na yoṣā* the meaning is given: "*manuṣyasya parivyūḍhādeḥ mahiṣīvat*" — as the wife of a hero or of an excellent man is; "*sā yathā suveṣā antaḥpura iva madhye carati*" — as that well-dressed woman moves within the inner apartments; so the line of clouds, likened to a woman of a hero, who, adorned with ornaments and the like, moves hidden in the inner apartments, and the movement of the lightning, have been described.

***sabhāvatī vidathyā vāg iva*** — *sabhā janasaṅghaḥ | tadvatī | varṣākāle āvirbhavanti | vidatho yajñaḥ | tadarhatīti vidathyā praiṣastotrādirūpā vāk | sā yathā yajñasabhāṃ prāpyāvirbhavati tadvat | yadvā | vedanārhā vividamānayor vāk | sā yathā sabhā bhavati tadvat*: the line of clouds, which is not visible at all seasons, is likened to the speech (*vāk*) of *praiṣa* and praise, which is read at sacrifices; the sacrificial words, *praiṣa* and praise, that are parts of the sacrifice, are recited only at that time in the midst of the multitude gathered in the sacrificial assembly. In the same way, in the middle region, the lightning and the garland of clouds *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 83  (PDF 103)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 4".)* …is perceptible only in the rainy season: thus one kind of meaning is explained. In the second meaning, for the words *vidathyā vāk* the Bhāṣyakāra says "*vedanārhā vivadamānayor vāk*" — the speech of those who dispute, which is worth knowing, with a view to deciding the meaning by argument, with the *pūrvapakṣa* and the *siddhānta*; this speech is perceptible only at that time in the gathering of people in the midst of the assembly: so the line of clouds and lightning are perceptible only in the rainy season — thus it is described. By this the word *sabhāvatī* is explained here. The Maruts move with such lines of clouds and, bearing their weapons, may come to the sacrificial hall for the sacrifice: this is explained by the sentence "*evaṃrūpā yeṣu mimyakṣa te maruto devayajanam āgacchantv*". The word *vidatha* is stated among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-17 [?]); *vidathāni vedanāni* (Ni. 6-[?]) — it is also a word conveying the meaning "knowledge" (*vijñāna*).

> होता देवो अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादेति मायया । विदथानि प्रचोदयन् ॥

> *hotā devo amartyaḥ purastādeti māyayā | vidathāni pracodayan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-27-7 [?]) — in this example the word *vidathāni* is explained in the sense "knowledge".

> मा नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुरिन्द्र ऋभुक्षा मरुतः परि ख्यन् । यद्वाजिनो देवजातस्य सप्तेः प्रवक्ष्यामो विदथे वीर्याणि ॥

> *mā no mitro varuṇo aryamāyurindra ṛbhukṣā marutaḥ pari khyan | yadvājino devajātasya sapteḥ pravakṣyāmo vidathe vīryāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-1) — here the word *vidatha* is used in the sense "sacrifice". Sāyaṇa has explained both these kinds of meaning for the word *vidathyā* here. (See pp. 9–13.)

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *mimyakṣa* (root *myakṣa gatau*; *liṭ* 3rd singular; *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…* Pā. 3-4-82 gives *ṇal*; the root is doubled; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *saṃprasāraṇa* to the reduplicate; *pūrvarūpa*; pāda-initial, so no *nighāta*; *liti* Pā. 6-1-193 [?] gives the acute to the syllable before the suffix). *sudhitā* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *kta* in the passive; by *vyatyaya* *dhi* in place of the root's *hi*; *gatir anantaraḥ* gives the *gati* accent; *ṭāp* in the feminine). *hiraṇyanirṇik* (*hiraṇyam iva nirṇik yasyāḥ sā*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* gives the accent of the first member).

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> परा शुभ्रा अयासो यव्या साधारण्येव मरुतो मिमिक्षुः ।
> न रोदसी अप नुदन्त घोरा जुषन्त वृधं सख्याय देवाः ॥ ४ ॥

> *parā śubhrā ayāso yavyā sādhāraṇyeva maruto mimikṣuḥ |*
> *na rodasī apa nudanta ghorā juṣanta vṛdhaṃ sakhyāya devāḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> परा । शुभ्राः । अयासः । यव्या । साधारण्याऽइव । मरुतः । मिमिक्षुः ।
> न । रोदसी इति । अप । नुदन्त । घोराः । जुषन्त । वृधम् । सख्याय । देवाः ॥ ४ ॥

> *parā | śubhrāḥ | ayāsaḥ | yavyā | sādhāraṇyā 'iva | marutaḥ | mimikṣuḥ |*
> *na | rodasī iti | apa | nudanta | ghorāḥ | juṣanta | vṛdham | sakhyāya | devāḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(begins at the foot of p. 84)*

> शुभ्राः शोभनालंकारा अयासोऽभिगन्तारो मरुतो यव्या मिश्रणशीलया विद्युता परा मिमिक्षुः । प्रकर्षेण सिञ्चन्त्युदकसंस्थाप्यम् [?] । साधारण्येव । यथा लोके साधारण्या स्त्रिया सङ्गता युवानो रेतो मुञ्चन्ति तद्वत् । एवं *[continues on the next page]*

> *śubhrāḥ śobhanālaṃkārā ayāso 'bhigantāro maruto yavyā miśraṇaśīlayā vidyutā parā mimikṣuḥ | prakarṣeṇa siñcantyudakasaṃsthāpyam [?] | sādhāraṇyeva | yathā loke sādhāraṇyā striyā saṅgatā yuvāno reto muñcanti tadvat | evaṃ *[continues on the next page]**

### Printed p. 85  (PDF 105)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 4".)* **Bhāṣya (continued from p. 84):**

> एवं कुर्वन्तो घोरा अतिवृष्टिप्रदानेन भयंकरास्ते रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ नापनुदन्त । अपनोदनं वर्षणरूपं तिरस्कारं न कुर्वन्ति । द्यावापृथिवीवचनो रोदसीशब्दः सर्वत्राद्युदात्तः । अत्र तु व्यत्ययेनान्तोदात्तत्वमिति द्रष्टव्यम् । यद्वा । रोदसा शब्देन रोदनस्वभावो रुद्रः । तस्य स्त्री रोदसीति केचिदाहुः । अपरे तु मरुतां स्त्रियो रोदसीति नामधेयमित्याहुः । अयमेव पक्षो युक्तः । उत्तरत्रैवं व्यवहारात् । तत्पक्षे रोदसी रोदस्याम् [?] ॥ जोषन्तात्स्तं स्तम्याः [?] ईकारो लुग्णाः [?] । ईदूतौ च सप्तम्यर्थ इति प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा ॥ तस्यां प्रियं धनं मुञ्चन्ति । किन्तु देवा मोदयितारो मादयितारो वा मरुतः सख्याय वृधं वृद्धिं जुषन्ते । सेवन्ते द्यावापृथिवीपक्षे सख्याय जगतां सखिभावाय तयोर्वृद्धिं कुर्वन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* The Maruts, adorned and moving, mix with the lightning, their companion, and send down rain, as young men with a woman of the common sort; terrible by giving abundant rain, they do not drive away heaven and earth (do not insult them by the form of rain), but, gladdening gods, they enjoy and promote the growth of the worlds, for friendship.

**Pratipadārtha.** *śubhrāḥ* — the beautifully adorned; *ayāsaḥ* — those that move; *marutaḥ* — the Marut-gods; *yavyā* — with the mixing, [the lightning] (those who are united with the lightning); *sādhāraṇyā iva* — like a common woman (as youths sprinkle their seed upon her); *parā mimikṣuḥ* — they pour water abundantly (as they do thus); *ghorāḥ* — the fearful Marut-gods (who give excess of rain); *rodasī* — heaven and earth; *na apa nudante* — do not reject (but); *devāḥ* — the Marut-gods, givers of delight (gladness); *sakhyāya* — for friendship (of the worlds); *vṛdham* — their growth; *juṣanta* — they serve.

**Bhāvārtha.** The splendid and moving Marut-gods, as young men in the world join a common woman and discharge their seed, join with their companion, the lightning, and bring about rain. These terrible ones, though they send excessive rain, do not make heaven and earth tremble. But, wishing for the friendship of the worlds, they desire their prosperity.

**English Translation (as printed):** The radiant, ever-moving Maruts, have mingled with (their) associate, (lightning), like (youths) with common women; the formidable divinities do not overwhelm heaven and earth (with rain), but promote their prosperity through (friendly) regard.

### Printed p. 86  (PDF 106)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* **Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***marutaḥ yavyā sādhāraṇyeva parā mimikṣuḥ*** — *miśraṇaśīlayā vidyutā prakarṣeṇa siñcanty udakasaṃsthāpyam* [as read] *| yathā loke sādhāraṇyā striyā saṅgatā yuvāno reto muñcanti tadvat*: "with the lightning, which is of a mixing nature, they sprinkle abundantly [water]; as young men in the world, united with a common woman, let go their seed, so". Lightning (*miñcu*) is of a nature that is always to join with a cloud other than itself. By a cloud together with lightning, rain is naturally produced; the raindrops fall to the ground through contact with the wind. This matter is described here in the style of poetry (*kāvya*). Since the word *vidyut* is feminine it indicates a woman, and since the word *marut* is masculine it indicates a man, and the relationship between the two is described here. The Marut-gods are *śubhrāḥ* — *śobhanālaṅkārāḥ*, "possessed of excellent, auspicious ornaments and other adornments"; *ayāsaḥ* — *abhigantāraḥ*, "moving about" is the meaning given. As in the world men in youth, adorned with ornaments and the like, move about with a woman, wandering, and enjoy her, so it is described that the Marut-gods let fall raindrops in company with the lightning, in the form of the cloud.

***ghorāḥ rodasī na apanudante*** — *atiṛṣṭipradānena bhayaṅkarāḥ dyāvāpṛthivyau apanodanaṃ varṣaṇarūpaṃ tiraskāraṃ na kurvanti | yadvā rodasā śabdena rodanasvabhāvo rudraḥ | tasya strī rodasīti kecid āhuḥ | apare tu marutāṃ striyo rodasīti nāmadheyam ityāhuḥ | ayam eva pakṣo yuktaḥ | uttaratraivaṃ vyavahārāt | tatpakṣe rodasī rodasyām* [as read]: "terrible by giving excess of rain, they do not insult (repel) heaven and earth in the form of rain-driving". The word *rodasī* is stated among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-30 [?]).

> उताभये पुरुहूत श्रवोभिरेको दृळ्हमवदो वृत्रहा सन् । इमे चिदिन्द्र रोदसी अपारे यत्संगृभ्णा मघवन्काशिरित्ते ॥ [?]

> *utābhaye puruhūta śravobhireko dṛḷhamavado vṛtrahā san | ime cidindra rodasī apāre yatsaṃgṛbhṇā maghavankāśirit te ‖ [?]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-5 [?]) — here *rodasī*: "*rodhasī dyāvāpṛthivyau | vividhāni hi bhūtāni ete rundhaḥ virodhanāt*" — since these two obstruct and shut in many kinds of beings, heaven and earth are intended by the word *rodasī*: this meaning is explained (Ni. 6-1 [?]). The meaning is given in one way: the Marut-gods, by their fierce form and abundant rain, do not at all offer to heaven and earth the insult of non-rain (*anāvṛṣṭi*). In the second meaning the word *rodasī* is used in the sense "the wife of Rudra, the manifestation of Rudra" (Ni. 11-30 [?]); having said so, *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 87  (PDF 107)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 4".)* **Special Topics (continued: *rodasī*).**

> उत ग्ना व्यन्तु देवपत्नीरिन्द्राण्यग्नाय्यश्विनी राट् । आ रोदसी वरुणानी शृणोतु व्यन्तु देवीर्य ऋतुर्जनीनाम् ॥

> *uta gnā vyantu devapatnīrindrāṇyagnāyyaśvinī rāṭ | ā rodasī varuṇānī śṛṇotu vyantu devīrya ṛturjanīnām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-46-8) — for the word *rodasī* used in this ṛk the meaning *rudrasya patnī*, "Rudra's wife", is given (Ni. 11-[?]). Sāyaṇa, too, explains the word *rodas* as indicating Rudra, who has the nature of weeping (*rodana*), and so shows another view — that the denoted one of the word *rodasī* is the wife of Rudra, Rudra's wife. And by the sentence *apare tu* he points out the other view that, since the wives of the Marut-gods are mentioned [with this word], the name *rodasī* is for the wives of the Marut-gods; and he explains that this interpretation will be suited, in accordance with the meaning, in what follows; in this explanation, the form *rodasī* ends in the seventh case, and "*tasyāṃ priyaṃ dhanaṃ muñcanti*" — "in that woman they let fall their beloved wealth" he explains. Yāska —

> रथं नु मारुतं वयं श्रवस्युमा हवामहे । आ यस्मिन्तस्थौ सुरणानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ॥

> *rathaṃ nu mārutaṃ vayaṃ śravasyumā havāmahe | ā yasmintasthau suraṇāni bibhratī sacā marutsu rodasī ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-56-8) — quoting this ṛk, he explains: "we call here the chariot of the Maruts, desiring fame, in which Rodasī, bearing pleasing [riches], stands with the Maruts" (Ni. 11-30 [?]).

***devāḥ*** — *modayitāro mādayitāro vā marutaḥ*: Yāska says "*devo dānād vā dīpanād vā dyotanād vā dyusthāno bhavatīti vā*" (Ni. 7-15 [?]) — [the deity is so called] because he gives to the sacrificers abundantly with favour, or because he makes the sacrificers radiant, or because he himself shines with his own splendour, or because he dwells in the excellent heaven: thus he gives the meaning of the word *deva*. Here the Marut-gods are called *devāḥ*; the purport is that these Marut-gods keep the sacrificers happy, or make them intoxicated with joy.

***sakhyāya vṛdhaṃ juṣante*** — by this sentence it is described that the Maruts increase in order that their friendship may reach others; and that heaven and earth gain prosperity for the good of the world: that is, "for the friendship of heaven and earth" — in order to be always together with heaven and earth — thus the meaning "they increase" is explained: they promote the growth of heaven and earth by their friendship.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> जोषद्यदीमसुर्या सचध्यै विषितस्तुका रोदसी नृमणाः ।
> आ सूर्येव विधतो रथं गात्त्वेषप्रतीका नभसो नेत्या ॥ ५ ॥

> *joṣadyadīmasuryā sacadhyai viṣitastukā rodasī nṛmaṇāḥ |*
> *ā sūryeva vidhato rathaṃ gāttveṣapratīkā nabhaso netyā ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> जोषत् । यत् । ईम् । असुर्या । सचध्यै । विषितऽस्तुका । रोदसी । नृऽमनाः ।
> आ । सूर्याऽइव । विधतः । रथम् । गात् । त्वेषऽप्रतीका । नभसः । न । इत्या ॥ ५ ॥

*(The Saṃhitā has* nṛmaṇāḥ*, the Pada* nṛ-manāḥ *as printed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> रोदसी मरुत्पत्नी विद्युद्वा एतन्नामिकेयमीमेनं मरुत्संघं जोषत् सेवते ॥ जुषेर्लेट्यडागमः ॥ किमर्थम् । सचध्यै सङ्गमनार्थम् । कीदृशी सा । असुर्या । असुराः क्षेप्तारो मरुतः । तेषां स्वभूता विषितस्तुका विशिथिलकेशसंघा विप्रकीर्णकेशसंघा वा सम्भोगवशेन तथा नृमणा नृषु नेतृषु मरुत्सु मननवती मनुष्येषु वा वृष्टिप्रदानमनोयुक्ता त्वेषप्रतीका दीप्तोपक्रमा दीप्तावयवा वा । ईदृशी देवी विधतः परिचरतो मरुत्संघस्य रथमा गात् । आगच्छति । व्याप्नोति । यागदेशं गन्तुं रथमारुह्य वा यज्ञमागच्छति । केव । विधतः सूर्यस्य रथं त्वेषप्रतीका सूर्येव सूर्यपत्नीव । यद्वा । सूर्यस्य दुहिताश्विनो रथमिव सा यथारोहति तद्वत् । आगमने दृष्टान्तः । नभस इत्या न । अन्तरिक्षादित्ययोः साधारणोऽयं नभःशब्दः नभ इति षट् साधारणानि । नै. १-४ । इत्युक्तत्वात् । अत्रादित्यवचनः । तस्य गतिरिव । सा यथा शीघ्रं तद्वत् ॥ [?]

*Gist:* Rodasī, the Maruts' wife (lightning), with scattered locks and her mind on the Marut-leaders, comes to join the Marut band; radiant, she mounts the chariot of the busy Maruts, as Sūryā mounts the Aśvins' chariot, and comes as swift as the sun's course.

**Pratipadārtha.** *asuryā* — (agitating the clouds) belonging to the Maruts; *viṣitastukā* — with dishevelled locks; (and) *nṛmaṇāḥ* — whose mind is firmly on the leaders, the Marut-gods; *rodasī* — the Maruts' wife called Rodasī (lightning); *sacadhyai* — for union; *īm* — this Marut-host; *yat* — when; *joṣat* — she serves (desires); *tat* — for that reason; *tveṣapratīkā* — Rodasī of shining limbs; *sūryā iva* — as the wife of Sūrya [mounts Sūrya's chariot], or as Sūrya's daughter Sūryā mounts the Aśvins' chariot; *nabhasaḥ* — of the sun; *itvā na* — as with speed; *vidhataḥ* — of the restless Maruts; *ratham* — the chariot; *ā gāt* — she reaches.

### Printed p. 90  (PDF 110)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* **Bhāvārtha.** The consort of the cloud-agitating Marut-gods, with fluttering locks and with her mind fixed on the Marut-gods, the Marut-wife Rodasī (lightning), desires the Marut-host for the sake of union; therefore, she, of radiant limbs, ascends the chariot of the Marut-gods, as the wife of Sūrya ascends the chariot of Sūrya, or as Sūryā, the daughter of Sūrya, ascends the chariot of the Aśvins, with the speed of the sun.

**English Translation (as printed):** Rodasi, the associate of the scatterers (of the clouds), with dishevelled tresses, and mind devoted to her lords, wooes them to associate (with her): Radiant in form, she has ascended the car of the restless (Maruts) as Surya (ascended the car of the Ashwins), and comes hither (with the celerity) of the sun.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***rodasī īṃ joṣat*** — *marutpatnī vidyut vā etannāmikā iyam īm enaṃ marutsaṅghaṃ sevate*: the wife of the Marut-gods, lightning (*miñcu*), serves the host of the Maruts. In poetic style the husband-and-wife relation between the Maruts and lightning is described. That the Maruts are of seven kinds (*avaha*, *uvaha*, *saṃvaha*, *pravaha*, *parivaha* and so on, names of the seven Maruts) is well known in the Purāṇas. Following this, "host of Maruts" is said here. This is one kind of meaning. Another implied meaning, as of a woman who, desiring pleasure, sees men going about here and there and becomes attached to their companies, also appears here from the sentence "*etannāmikā marutsaṅghaṃ sevate*".

The particle *īm* is explained by Yāska:

> अथ ये प्रवृत्तीर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रन्थेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छन्ति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिदित्येते [?]

> *atha ye pravṛttīrthe 'mitākṣareṣu grantheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchanti padapūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmidityete [?]*

— the particles in the form of sentence-fillers (indeclinables) are used in the Vedic texts for completing the sentence; in the metrical texts, in the form of padding (*padapūraṇa*) they are used in an expletive sense. These particles are *kam*, *īm*, *it*, *u*. Of these, the particle *īm* is used here; Sāyaṇa has explained its meaning as "*enaṃ marutsaṅgham*".

### Printed p. 91  (PDF 111)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 4".)* **Special Topics (continued).**

***asuryā*** — *asurāḥ kṣeptāro marutaḥ teṣāṃ svabhūtā*: the Marut-gods move in accordance with their speed. "Belonging to them" means: in the form of the wife of these deities, she who is under their control.

***viṣitastukā*** — *viśithilakeśasaṅghā viprakīrṇakeśasaṅghā vā saṃbhogena tathā*: the wife of the Marut-gods, who has gathered up her hair and adorned herself, or who, since she has experienced union with her husband, has dishevelled hair.

***nṛmaṇāḥ*** — *nṛṣu netṛṣu marutsu mananavatī vṛṣṭipradānamanoyuktā vā manuṣyeṣu*: she who is always meditating on the welfare of her husband, the Maruts; or one who, in regard to men, has a mind to give rain, that is, to favour with water: this is the meaning explained.

***tveṣapratīkā*** — *dīptopakramā dīptāvayavā vā*: one whose enterprise begins with brilliance, or whose limbs shine with brilliance: the wife of the Marut-gods, who thus has work starting radiantly and limbs shining with brilliance, is eager to come to the place where the sacrifice is going on, pervading the chariot of the Marut-gods who go all round. For this the illustration is given by the sentence *vidhataḥ rathaṃ sūryeva*. Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning for this sentence. In the first meaning the comparison is made with the wife of Sūrya mounting the chariot of Sūrya.

In the second meaning — "*yadvā sūryasya duhitāśvino rathamiva sā yathārohati tadvat*" — it is said as an illustration: as the daughter of Sūrya, at her *svayaṃvara* (choice of a husband), mounts the chariot of the Aśvins. This matter [is stated] in

> आ वां रथं दुहिता सूर्यस्य काष्ठेवातिष्ठदर्वता जयन्ती । विश्वे देवा अन्वमन्यन्त हृद्भिः सं उ श्रिया नासत्या सचेथे ॥

> *ā vāṃ rathaṃ duhitā sūryasya kāṣṭhevātiṣṭhadarvatā jayantī | viśve devā anvamanyanta hṛdbhiḥ saṃ u śriyā nāsatyā sacethe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-17 [?]) — it is expounded in this ṛk; and in

> आ वां रथं युवतिस्तिष्ठदत्र जुष्ट्वी नरा दुहिता सूर्यस्य ॥

> *ā vāṃ rathaṃ yuvatistiṣṭhadatra juṣṭvī narā duhitā sūryasya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-5 [?]) — in this ṛk also it is stated.

***nabhasaḥ itvā na*** — *antarikṣādityayoḥ sādhāraṇaḥ nabhaḥśabdaḥ | atrādityavacanaḥ | tasya gatiriva | sā yathā śīghraṃ tadvat*: the word *nabhas*, common to the middle region and to the sun, here means the sun; "like his course; as swiftly as he". The word *nabhaḥ* is stated in the middle of the six common names beginning with *svaḥ*, *pṛśniḥ* (Ni. 2-[?]); "*sādhāraṇānyatra ṣaṭ divaś cādityasya ca*" *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 92  (PDF 112)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* — these six common names are explained by Yāska as synonymous words that denote the middle region and the sun: "*nabha ādityo bhavati netā bhāsāṃ jyotiṣāṃ praṇayo 'pi vā bhana iva syād vyaparītaḥ na na bhātīti*" (Ni. 2-[?]) [as read] — "he is the leader of the lustres in all directions"; hence the name *nabha* has come for the sun. Or, *bhana* is the word of the opposite order [with the letters transposed], *nabha*; or, *bhanaḥ* [with the letters] is also *nabhaḥ*. Or "*na na bhāti*" — he who does not not shine, that is, "who always shines" — by this derivation the word *nabhas* is explained here to mean the sun.

The sun's course is swift; so the wife of the Marut-gods mounts the swiftly moving chariot of the Maruts and comes to the sacrificial hall with the Marut-gods: thus the speed of the coming is compared with the swiftness of the sun.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *joṣat* (root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*, of the *tudādi* class; *leṭ* 3rd singular; *iteś ca parasmaipadeṣu* [?] drops the *i*; by *vyatyaya* the suffix *tip*; *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* Pā. 3-4-94 gives the *aḍ* augment; in the Veda the *vikaraṇa* is dropped; *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* Pā. 7-3-86 gives guṇa to the light penultimate of the root; since it stands at the beginning of the pāda no *nighāta*; the root-accent remains). *sacadhyai* (root *saca samavāye*; in the sense of *tumun*, *tumarthe sesenase…* Pā. 3-4-9 gives the suffix *adhyai*; *kṛnmejantaḥ* gives the name indeclinable; the initial acute by the suffix, so middle acute). *asuryā* (*asurāṇāṃ sambandhinī*; *yat* in the sense of relation; *tit svaritam* Pā. 6-1-185 gives *svarita*; *ṭāp* in the feminine). *viṣitastukā* (*viṣitāḥ viprakīrṇāḥ stukāḥ keśasaṅghāḥ yasyāḥ sā*; in the *bahuvrīhi* the first member keeps its accent). *nṛmanāḥ* (*nṛṣu manaḥ yasyāḥ sā*; *parādiś chandasi bahulam* Pā. 6-2-199 gives the initial acute of the latter member). *sūryā* (*sūryasya strī devatā*; *sūryād devatāyāṃ cāp vācyaḥ* Pā. 4-1-48 [?] gives the suffix *cāp*).

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आस्थापयन्त युवतिं युवानः शुभे निमिश्लां विदथेषु पज्राम् ।
> अर्को यद्वो मरुतो हविष्मान्गायद्गाथं सुतसोमो दुवस्यन् ॥ ६ ॥

> *āsthāpayanta yuvatiṃ yuvānaḥ śubhe nimiślāṃ vidatheṣu pajrām |*
> *arko yadvo maruto haviṣmāngāyadgāthaṃ sutasomo duvasyan ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । अस्थापयन्त । युवतिम् । युवानः । शुभे । निऽमिश्लाम् । विदथेषु । पज्राम् ।
> अर्कः । यत् । वः । मरुतः । हविष्मान् । गायत् । गाथम् । सुतऽसोमः । दुवस्यन् ॥ ६ ॥

> *ā | asthāpayanta | yuvatim | yuvānaḥ | śubhe | ni 'miślām | vidatheṣu | pajrām |*
> *arkaḥ | yat | vaḥ | marutaḥ | haviṣmān | gāyat | gātham | suta 'somaḥ | duvasyan ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> युवानो मिश्रयन्तो नित्यतरुणा वा मरुतो युवतिं मिश्रयन्तीं नित्यतरुणीं वा विद्युद्रूपां रोदस्यां स्त्रियमास्थापयन्त । आस्थापयन्ति । देवतात्वेन रथे धारयन्ति ।

> *yuvāno miśrayanto nityataruṇā vā maruto yuvatiṃ miśrayantīṃ nityataruṇīṃ vā vidyudrūpāṃ rodasyāṃ striyamāsthāpayanta | āsthāpayanti | devatātvena rathe dhārayanti |*

### Printed p. 94  (PDF 114)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* **Bhāṣya (continued from p. 93):**

> कीदृशीं तां । निमिश्लां नियमेन मिश्रयन्तीं पज्रां पज्रो बलं तद्वतीम् । शुभे । शोभते दीप्यत इति शुभुदकं वृष्ट्युदकार्थम् । शुभे रथे इति वा योज्यम् । किं निमित्तम् । विदथेषु योगेषु निमित्तभूतेषु । कदा । यद्यदा हे मरुतः वो युष्माकमर्कः । मत्वर्थीयो लुप्तः [?] । अर्चनसाधनमन्त्रोपेतः स्तोता वा हविष्मान् प्रदेयाज्यादिहविर्युक्तः सुतसोमो होमायाभिषुतसोमोऽयं यजमानो दुवस्यन् । परिचरन् गाथं गातव्यं स्तोत्रं गायत् गायति । तदेत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* The ever-young Maruts seat in their chariot the young, mixing, lightning-woman, strong, for the sake of rain at the sacrifices, whenever the sacrificer, with oblations and pressed Soma, serves them and sings the hymn.

**Pratipadārtha.** (*he*) *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *yat* — when; *haviṣmān* — one with oblations such as *ājya* to be offered; *sutasomaḥ* — one who has pressed Soma for the *homa*; *arkaḥ* — the worshipper, the sacrificer, possessed of hymns as means of worship; *vaḥ* — you; *duvasyan* — serving; *gātham* — the hymn to be sung; *gāyat* — sings; (*tadā* — then); *yuvānaḥ* — you who are ever young; *nimiślām* — who is closely mingled with [you]; *pajrām* — strong; *yuvatim* — the ever-young woman in the form of lightning (of mixing nature); *śubhe* — for the sake of rain (in your auspicious chariot); *vidatheṣu* — for the sacrifices (setting out with a view to them); *ā asthāpayanta* — you seat together (with you).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, when your worshipper (the sacrificer) offers *ājya* and other oblations and prepares the Soma juice and praises you with hymns, then, ever-young, you set out in your chariot for the sacrifices, with the ever-young woman in the form of lightning, well mingled with you and endowed with great vigour (calling her again [and again]).

**English Translation (as printed):** The youthful (Maruts) have placed the young (lightning) in (their) brilliant (car), commingling (with them), and vigorous (in yielding rain) on sacrifices (being solemnized); when, Maruts, your worshipper, presenting oblations, pouring out the Soma juice, and offering adoration, chants the sacred song.

### Printed p. 95  (PDF 115)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 5".)* **Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***yuvānaḥ*** — *miśrayanto nityatarunā vā*: [Sāyaṇa: "mixing, or ever young"]. Yāska —

> युवं च्यवानं सनयं यथा रथं पुनर्युवानं चरथाय तक्षथुः । निष्टौग्र्यमूहथुरद्भ्यस्परि विश्वेत्ता वां सवनेषु प्रवाच्या ॥

> *yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ sanayaṃ yathā rathaṃ punaryuvānaṃ carathāya takṣathuḥ | niṣṭaugryamūhathuradbhyaspari viśvettā vāṃ savaneṣu pravācyā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-4) — here, for the word *yuvānam*, *yuvā prayoyati karmāṇi miśrayati*: "one who joins together, mixes". Sāyaṇa has explained that the Marut-gods are those who are always in youthful strength, and are united [with the other one].

***yuvatīm āsthāpayanta*** — *miśrayantīṃ nityatarūṇīṃ vā vidyudrūpāṃ rodasyāṃ striyam āsthāpayanta devatātvena rathe dhārayanti*: she of the nature of being united at all times in her youth with the men (desirous), shining like the lightning, or the woman called Rodasī, in the form of lightning: they have her seated in their chariot. The meaning is: they bear Rodasī in their chariot so that those who worship their chariots and themselves may have the knowledge that Rodasī is of the nature of a goddess.

***śubhe*** — *śobhate dīpyate iti śubhudakaṃ vṛṣṭyudakārthaṃ | śubhe rathe iti vā yojyam*: by the derivation "that which shines", water is named *śubh*, [meaning "for the sake of the water of rain", that is,] for giving water in the form of rain; or, as another meaning, "in your auspicious chariot".

***arkaḥ*** — *arcanasādhanamantropetaḥ stotā vā*: "the praiser, endowed with a mantra as the means of worship". The word *arka* is stated among the names of food (Ni. 2-7 [?]) and among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 2-11 [?]).

> अर्कः । अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चन्ति । अर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदनेनार्चन्ति । अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चन्ति भूतानि । अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्ना ॥

> *arkaḥ | arko devo bhavati yadenamarcanti | arko mantro bhavati yadanenārcanti | arkamannaṃ bhavatyarcanti bhūtāni | arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimnā ‖*

From the root *arc* (to worship, to honour) the word *arka* has been formed; by the derivation "*arcatīty arkaḥ*" it is explained that the word is used in the senses of "means of worship" and "worthy of worship"; and since the deity must be worshipped with praises, the deity is the meaning of the word *arka*: one kind of meaning. As the mantra is the means of worship, it is *arka*; and since beings worship [food] and honour it by preparing it, food too is the meaning of the word *arka*. Because it is joined with bitterness (*kaṭuka*), the word *arka* indicates the tree. Here, since the suffix *matup* has been dropped after the word *arka*, the word *arka* is used for one who has a mantra serving as the means of worship. By this it is explained that the sacrificers, who know the mantras by which they worship, or who recite the praises, with the oblations offered to Agni, and having prepared the Soma juice for the *homa* in the fire, serve the fire and recite the stotras. *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 96  (PDF 116)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* ***duvasyan*** — *paricaran*: *duvasyati* is stated among the names of acts of service (Ni. 3-[?]). And

> परेयिवांसं प्रवतो महीरनु बहुभ्यः पन्थामनुपस्पशानम् । वैवस्वतं सङ्गमनं जनानां यमं राजानं हविषा दुवस्य ॥

> *pareyivāṃsaṃ pravato mahīranu bahubhyaḥ panthāmanupaspaśānam | vaivasvataṃ saṅgamanaṃ janānāṃ yamaṃ rājānaṃ haviṣā duvasya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-1) — here the word *duvasya* is explained as *rādhnuhi*; Durgācārya explains the word *rādhnuhi* as *paricarasva* ("serve").

***gātham*** — *gātavyaṃ stotram*: "a hymn to be sung". The word *gāthā* is read among the names of speech (Ni. 1-[?]). Here the word *gātham* is used; the meaning given for it is "stotra".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *āsthāpayanta* (root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *ṇic* by *hetumati ca*; *puk* by *arti-hrī-vlī-rī-knūyī-kṣmāyy-ātāṃ puk ṇau* Pā. 7-3-36 since the root ends in *ā*; Vedic *laṅ* [?] in the present sense after the *ṇijanta*; 3rd plural; *nighāta* after a *tiṅanta*). *yuvatim* (the word *yuvan*; in the feminine *yūnas tiḥ* Pā. 4-1-77 gives *ti*; *nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya* drops the *n*; final acute by the suffix). *śubhe* (*śobhata iti śubh*; root *śubha dīptau*; *kvip*; dative singular; *sānekācaś ca tṛtīyādiḥ* Pā. 6-1-168 gives the acute to the case-ending). *vidatheṣu* (root *vida jñāne*; *athac* by *rudhividibhyāṃ jit* Uṇ. 3-[?]; as it is *jit*, no *laghūpadha-guṇa*; initial acute by the suffix). *arkaḥ* (root *arca pūjāyām*; *ka* by *kṛdādhārārciśubhyaḥ kaḥ* [?] Uṇ. 3-[?]; *arka* is a mantra; since it is "that which has it", in the Veda the possessive suffix is dropped; or, as it belongs to the *arśa-ādi* class, *ac* in the sense of possession).

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्र तं विवक्मि वक्म्यो य एषां मरुतां महिमा सत्यो अस्ति ।
> सचा यदीं वृषमना अहंयुः स्थिरा चिज्जनीर्वहते सुभागाः ॥ ७ ॥

> *pra taṃ vivakmi vakmyo ya eṣāṃ marutāṃ mahimā satyo asti |*
> *sacā yadīṃ vṛṣamanā ahaṃyuḥ sthirā cijjanīrvahate subhāgāḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्र । तम् । विवक्मि । वक्म्यः । यः । एषाम् । मरुताम् । महिमा । सत्यः । अस्ति ।
> सचा । यत् । ईम् । वृषऽमनाः । अहंऽयुः । स्थिरा । चित् । जनीः । वहते । सुऽभागाः ॥ ७ ॥

> *pra | tam | vivakmi | vakmyaḥ | yaḥ | eṣām | marutām | mahimā | satyaḥ | asti |*
> *sacā | yat | īm | vṛṣa 'manāḥ | ahaṃ 'yuḥ | sthirā | cit | janīḥ | vahate | su 'bhāgāḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> एषां मरुतां यो महिमा महत्त्वातिशयो वक्म्यः सर्वैः स्तुत्यः सत्योऽबाध्योऽमोघोऽस्ति तं प्र विवक्मि प्रवच्मि । वर्णयामि । कथमेषां महिमा प्राप्त इति उच्यते । यद्यस्मादीमेतेषां सम्बन्धिनी रोदसी वृषमना वृष्ट्यादिवर्षणमनस्का अहंयुरहंकारवती । जगदुपकारकर्त्र्या न कदाचिदस्तीत्यहंकारः । स्थिरा । चित् । चिदिति पूजायाम् । अत्यन्तमविनश्वरा ईदृशी देवी सुभागाः शोभनभाग्योपेताः सुजनीर्जननशीलाः प्रजा वृष्ट्युत्पत्त्रीर्वा वहते धारयति । वृष्ट्या सत्यां सर्वे प्राणिन उत्पद्यन्ते । यस्मादेवं तस्मान्महिमास्ति । तं महिमानं स्तौमीत्यर्थः ॥ [?]

> *eṣāṃ marutāṃ yo mahimā mahattvātiśayo vakmyaḥ sarvaiḥ stutyaḥ satyo 'bādhyo 'mogho 'sti taṃ pra vivakmi pravacmi | varṇayāmi | kathameṣāṃ mahimā prāpta iti ucyate | yadyasmādīmeteṣāṃ sambandhinī rodasī vṛṣamanā vṛṣṭyādivarṣaṇamanaskā ahaṃyurahaṃkāravatī | jagadupakārakartryā na kadācidastītyahaṃkāraḥ | sthirā | cit | ciditi pūjāyām | atyantamavinaśvarā īdṛśī devī subhāgāḥ śobhanabhāgyopetāḥ sujanīrjananaśīlāḥ prajā vṛṣṭyutpattrīrvā vahate dhārayati | vṛṣṭyā satyāṃ sarve prāṇina utpadyante | yasmādevaṃ tasmānmahimāsti | taṃ mahimānaṃ staumītyarthaḥ ‖ [?]*

### Printed p. 98  (PDF 118)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)*

*Gist:* I proclaim the great and unobstructed glory of the Maruts, which all praise, because their companion Rodasī, whose mind is on rain, proud and ever-lasting, bears fortunate, productive creatures; for all beings arise from rain.

**Pratipadārtha.** *yat* — by whose (the Marut-gods') greatness; *vṛṣamanāḥ* — she whose mind is set on raining; *ahaṃyuḥ* — endowed with pride; *sthirā cit* — also eternal; *īm* — this goddess Rodasī, the lightning-deity who is the Maruts' own; *subhāgāḥ* — fortunate ones, endowed with auspicious fortune; *janīḥ* — creatures who produce [others] (or: *subhāgāḥ* — as the cause of auspicious fortune; *janīḥ* — the rain that generates); *sacā vahate* — she supports completely; *eṣām* — of such; *marutām* — Marut-gods; *yaḥ* — which; *mahimā* — greatness; *vakmyaḥ* — praised by all; *satyaḥ* — unobstructible (not in vain); *asti* — is; *tam* — that greatness; *pra vivakmi* — I describe well.

**Bhāvārtha.** I describe well the great glory of the Marut-gods, true and praiseworthy: their wife called Rodasī (the lightning-deity), whose mind is on bringing rain, proud (the one who is the cause of all benefit to the world), and everlasting, by this very glory of theirs supports and protects fortunate and fertile creatures, bringing rain.

**English Translation (as printed):** I celebrate that greatness of the Maruts, which is true, and worthy of celebration, inasmuch as their highminded, haughty, and ever-enduring (bride), supports a flourishing progeny.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***mahimā vakmyaḥ*** — *mahatvātiśayaḥ sarvaiḥ stutyaḥ*: the abundant greatness of these Marut-gods is worthy of being praised by all. And ***satyaḥ*** — *abādhyaḥ amoghaḥ*: since it is such that none can obstruct it and it is not in vain, "I describe this glory" — thus the seer of the mantra describes.

***īṃ vṛṣamanāḥ ahaṃyuḥ janīḥ vahate*** — *etesāṃ sambandhinī rodasī vṛṣṭyādivarṣaṇamanaskā ahaṃkāravatī jagadupakārakartrī ye janaśīlāḥ prajāḥ vṛṣṭyutpattrī vā dhārayati*: the goddess connected with these Maruts (the goddess known by the name Rodasī) *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 99  (PDF 119)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 5".)* …with a mind eager to pour rain, taking pride in her function of benefiting the world, always honourable, and with a nature of ever arising, she bears the creatures that are by nature productive. Or, since all beings come to be when rain falls, she causes rain to arise and sustains all. Therefore, because the greatness of the Marut-gods is manifest through this goddess, it is said here, "I praise the greatness of these Marut-gods."

***sthirā cit*** — *cid iti pūjāyām | atyantam avinaśvarā*: ["*cit*" is in the sense of honour]: extremely imperishable. Yāska says that the particle *cit* is used in many different meanings:

> चिदित्येषोऽनेककर्मा । आचार्यश्चिदिदं ब्रूयादिति पूजायाम् । दधिचित्क्षुपमार्थे [?] । कुल्माषांश्चिदाहरेत्यकुत्सिते [?]

> *cidityeṣo 'nekakarmā | ācāryaścididaṃ brūyāditi pūjāyām | dadhicitkṣupamārthe [?] | kulmāṣāṃścidāharetyakutsite [?]*

(Ni. 1-[?]) — in the sentence "*ācāryaś cid*" it is used for reverence; in the sentence "*dadhicit*" in the sense of comparison (*upamā*); in "*kulmāṣāṃś cit*" in censure: thus he explains with examples. Here Sāyaṇa explains it as used in the sense of honour: "that goddess is worthy of honour and imperishable"; by describing the greatness of that goddess he has described the great glory of the Maruts.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *vivakmi* (root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *laṭ* 1st singular, *mip*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *ślu* for the vikaraṇa; the root is doubled; *bahulaṃ chandasi* Pā. 2-4-73 gives *i* to the reduplicate; the Vedic [?] gives *ku*-substitution for the *c* of the root; *nighāta* after a *tiṅanta*). *mahimā* (after the word *mahat*, *imanic* in the sense of excess; *ciṭaḥ* Pā. 6-1-163 gives the final acute). *asti* (by connection with *yad*, no *nighāta*; *tip* being *pit*, the root-accent remains). *vṛṣamanāḥ* (*bahuvrīhi*; the accent of the first member remains). *ahaṃyuḥ* (*aham* is an indeclinable ending in *m*, used in the sense of pride; *ahaṃśubhamor yus* Pā. 5-2-140 gives *yus* in the possessive sense; final acute by the suffix). *sthirā* (root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *kirac* by *ajiraśiśira…* Uṇ. 1-53 given by *nipātana*; in the feminine, being *a*-ending, *ṭāp*; as it is *cit* the final acute).

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* **Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (continued).** *janīḥ* (*janyante āsu iti janayaḥ*; the root *jani prādurbhāve*; suffix *iṇ* by *iṇ sarvadhātubhyaḥ* Uṇ. 4-[?]; *jñityādir nityam* Pā. 6-1-197 gives the initial acute; accusative plural). *vahate* (root *vaha prāpaṇe*; *laṭ* 3rd singular; by connection with *yad*, no *nighāta*; by *tāsyanudāttet* the root-accent remains). *subhāgāḥ* (*śobhano bhāgo yāsāṃ tāḥ*; *nañsubhyām* Pā. 6-2-172 gives the final acute). ‖ 7 ‖

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पान्ति मित्रावरुणाववद्याच्चयत ईमर्यमो अप्रशस्तान् ।
> उत च्यवन्ते अच्युता ध्रुवाणि वावृध ईं मरुतो दातिवारः ॥ ८ ॥

> *pānti mitrāvaruṇāvavadyāccayata īmaryamo apraśastān |*
> *uta cyavante acyutā dhruvāṇi vāvṛdha īṃ maruto dātivāraḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पान्ति । मित्रावरुणौ । अवद्यात् । चयते । ईम् । आर्यमः । इति । अप्रऽशस्तान् ।
> उत । च्यवन्ते । अच्युता । ध्रुवाणि । ववृधे । ईम् । मरुतः । दातिऽवारः ॥ ८ ॥

*(The Saṃhitā word "*cayata*" and the Pada "*cayate*" are as printed [?]; the reading of the Saṃhitā is doubtful.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(begins)*

> हे मरुतः युष्मत्सम्बन्धिनो देवा मित्रावरुणावहोरात्राभिमानिदेवावर्यमा । अर्यमा उ इति निपातेसमुदायात्कमेकं पदम् । उशब्दोऽपि शब्दार्थः । अर्यमापि । एते त्रयोऽपीमममुं लोकं यज्ञं वावद्याद्गर्ह्यादयथानुष्ठानात् । जगत्पक्षे व्यवहारप्रतिबन्धरूपात् पान्ति । रक्षन्ति । तथैतेषामप्रशस्तान् श्रेणानामपि पदार्थाश्च यते । चातयन्ति । नाशयन्ति । उतापि चैत्यैः [?] प्रेरितान्यच्युतान्यच्युतानि ध्रुवाणि विशक्तध्रुवाणि विचलानि मेघस्फोदकानि च्यवन्ते । च्यावयन्ति वैते । अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणावहोरात्राभ्यां खलु वै पर्जन्यो वर्षतीति श्रुतेः । यद्वा । अच्युतानि ध्रुवाणि धनानि च्यवन्ते । कदेति उच्यते । *[continues on the next page — the whole of this Ṛk 8 bhāṣya is doubtful in several words]*

> *he marutaḥ yuṣmatsambandhino devā mitrāvaruṇāvahorātrābhimānidevāvaryamā | aryamā u iti nipātesamudāyātkamekaṃ padam | uśabdo 'pi śabdārthaḥ | aryamāpi | ete trayo 'pīmamamuṃ lokaṃ yajñaṃ vāvadyādgarhyādayathānuṣṭhānāt | jagatpakṣe vyavahārapratibandharūpāt pānti | rakṣanti | tathaiteṣāmapraśastān śreṇānāmapi padārthāśca yate | cātayanti | nāśayanti | utāpi caityaiḥ [?] preritānyacyutānyacyutāni dhruvāṇi viśaktadhruvāṇi vicalāni meghasphodakāni cyavante | cyāvayanti vaite | ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇāvahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vai parjanyo varṣatīti śruteḥ | yadvā | acyutāni dhruvāṇi dhanāni cyavante | kadeti ucyate | *[continues on the next page — the whole of this Ṛk 8 bhāṣya is doubtful in several words]**

### Printed p. 101  (PDF 121)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 5".)* **Bhāṣya (continued from p. 100):**

> हे मरुतः युष्मदीय ईमयं कालो दातिवारः प्रदेयजलः खण्डितमेघो वा यदा वावृधे वर्धते । तदा मित्रादयो देवा युष्मदनुकूलप्यासारेण [?] जगद्रक्षन्तीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । दातिवारो दत्त्वरणीयोपहविर्लक्षणधनो यजमानो हे मरुतः ईमेनास्यु ष्मान् [?] ववृधे वर्धयति यदा तदेत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* The Maruts' time of water-giving rain strengthens [the world]; then Mitra and the others, in agreement with you, protect the world; or the sacrificer who offers oblations for the gods increases you; then they act.

**Pratipadārtha.** (*he*) *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; (*yadā* — when); *īm* — this time; *dātivāraḥ* — [the time] with the rain divided, for the clouds that are broken up and ready to give water; *vavṛdhe* — grows (increases); [or: *dātivāraḥ* — (to you) the sacrificer who gives desirable wealth in the form of oblation; *īm* — he, you; *vavṛdhe* — causes to prosper]; (*tadā* — then); *mitrāvaruṇau* — Mitra and Varuṇa; *aryamaḥ* — and Aryaman; *īm* — this world or sacrifice; *avadyāt* — from the reprehensible [from every fault]; *pānti* — protect; (*tathā* — likewise); *apraśastān* — all things unworthy of praise; *cayate* — they destroy; *uta* — and; *acyutā* — the one that is never falling [water]; (*adaḥ* — therefore); *dhruvāṇi* — the stable, unmoving water in the clouds; *cyavante* — make fall; [or: *acyutā* — what is without decay; *dhruvāṇi* — firm riches; *cyavante* — they bestow].

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, when the sacrificer increases you by offering oblations and the like, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman protect our sacrifice from all faults; destroy everything unworthy of praise; and cause the waters in the clouds that do not fall of themselves to fall, and bestow unfailing, stable wealth. (In this world: they destroy all things that are perishable, and make the water in the unmoving clouds fall, and bestow it.)

**English Translation (as printed):** Mitra, and Varuna, and Aryaman, defend (this) sacrifice from (all that is) reprehensible, and destroy (all that are) unworthy. They cause the yet unfallen and showering (rains) to descend, when, Maruts, the water-yielding (season) gives increase to this (world).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***mitrāvaruṇau aryamaḥ īm avadyāt pānti*** — *ahorātrābhimānidevau aryamā api ete trayaḥ amuṃ lokaṃ yajñaṃ vā ayathānuṣṭhānāt jagatpakṣe* *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 102  (PDF 122)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* *vyavahāraprativandharūpāt rakṣanti*: "these three, the presiding deities of day and night and Aryaman too, protect this world, or the sacrifice, from wrong performance; and, on the side of the world, from obstruction in the form of [hindrance to] worldly dealings." Yāska says of Mitra and Varuṇa: "*sahaiva saṃstavaḥ*" — in the same sentence the praise of both is made. Here Mitra and Varuṇa are described as the deities connected with the Maruts. These Mitra and Varuṇa, and the god called Aryaman, three gods, protect this world and the sacrifice. Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning thus: they protect so that in the sacrifice there be no negligence of duty or error in performing it, and in the world's affairs no obstruction of any kind arises. And they, these two, are also said to be the presiding deities of day and night.

***apraśastān cayate*** — *śreṇānapi padārthān cātayanti nāśayanti*: [Sāyaṇa as read] "they cause even the *śreṇa* things to perish". These Mitra and Varuṇa, presiding deities of day and night, in the course of time cause a change of form in those things (the changes of the same things), and bring about their destruction: this is the meaning given. By this the capacity of the acts of creation and dissolution is established for Mitra and Varuṇa, the presiding deities of day and night.

***acyutā dhruvāṇi cyavante*** — by this sentence maintenance (*sthiti*) too is said to be done by them. ***acyutāni*** — *āsrāviṇi*: in the first kind of meaning, "the waters in the cloud, which are fixed (*dhruva*) because the cloud, being in a dense state, does not move, and are in a liquid form (*āsrāviṇi*), these [two] cause to fall (*cyāvayanti*) as rain to the earth"; in the other: *yadvā acyutāni dhruvāṇi dhanāni cyavante* — "they bestow imperishable wealth upon the earth and cause the affairs of the world to be fulfilled" — thus the agency of creation, maintenance and dissolution is said to belong to Mitra and Varuṇa, the presiding deities of day and night. Mitra and Varuṇa are by form the day and night. To show that rain arises from day and night, the Vedic sentence is cited:

> अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणावहोरात्राभ्यां खलु वै पर्जन्यो वर्षति ।

> *ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇāvahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vai parjanyo varṣati |*

Addressing the Marut-gods, the time when the Mitra deities and the rest perform the acts of creation of the world is shown. By the sentence *īṃ dātivāraḥ vavṛdhe* the time of the favour of Mitra and the others is shown; the word *īm* is explained here as meaning "this time". *Dātivāraḥ* — "*khaṇḍitameghaḥ pradeyajalaḥ*": of the clouds broken up, with the water to give: the water is brought to increase in the form of rain; and ***dattvaraṇīyahavirlakṣaṇadhano yajamānaḥ*** — "the sacrificer, whose wealth, in the form of oblations, is to be accepted by the gods who accept [the oblations]" — the sacrificer, having offered oblations to the gods, pours out wealth in the form of the oblation desired by the deities; and in accordance with the time offered with the gods in view, Mitra and the other gods, the Marut-gods, perform the acts needed for the world's good and complete and protect the affairs of the world: thus it is described.

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> नही नु वो मरुतो अन्त्यस्मे आरात्ताच्चिच्छवसो अन्तमापुः ।
> ते धृष्णुना शवसा शूशुवांसोऽर्णो न द्वेषो धृषता परि ष्ठुः ॥ ९ ॥

> *nahī nu vo maruto antyasme ārāttāccicchavaso antamāpuḥ |*
> *te dhṛṣṇunā śavasā śūśuvāṃso 'rṇo na dveṣo dhṛṣatā pari ṣṭhuḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

### Printed p. 104  (PDF 124)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> नहि । नु । वः । मरुतः । अन्ति । अस्मे इति । आरात्तात् । चित् । शवसः । अन्तम् । आपुः ।
> ते । धृष्णुना । शवसा । शूशुवांसः । अर्णः । न । द्वेषः । धृषता । परि । स्थुः ॥ ९ ॥

> *nahi | nu | vaḥ | marutaḥ | anti | asme iti | ārāttāt | cit | śavasaḥ | antam | āpuḥ |*
> *te | dhṛṣṇunā | śavasā | śūśuvāṃsaḥ | arṇaḥ | na | dveṣaḥ | dhṛṣatā | pari | sthuḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः वः शवसो युष्मत्सम्बन्धिनो बलस्यान्तमवसानमन्त्यैकान्तिके [?] आरात्ताच्चिद्दूरादपि । यद्वा । चिदिति कुत्सायाम् । अत्यन्तदूरात् । अस्मे अस्मासु मध्य एकेऽपि नु क्षिप्रं नह्याप्नुवन्ति । नैव खलु प्राप्नुवन्ति । संनिधानासंनिधौ च न प्राप्नुवन्तीत्यर्थः । अथ परोक्षे [?] प्राप्तबलवत्त्वमाह । ते खलु मरुतो धृष्णुना धर्षकेण शवसा बलेन शूशुवांसो वर्धमानाः अत एव धृषता पराभिभावकेन सामर्थ्येन द्विषो द्वेष्टॄन् परि ष्ठुः । परिभवन्ति । वशीकुर्वन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अर्णो न । उदकमिव । यथोदकं स्वनिरोधि रजआदिकमभिभवति तद्वत् । यस्मादेवं तस्मात्तव शवसोऽन्तं नापुः ॥

*Gist:* None among us has reached, near or far, the limit of your strength; for you, grown in bold strength, overcome your enemies, as water overwhelms dust and the like.

**Pratipadārtha.** *te* — those Marut-gods; *dhṛṣṇunā* — overpowering; *śavasā* — with their own strength; *śūśuvāṃsaḥ* — increasing; *dhṛṣatā* — (therefore) by their capacity for overcoming; *dviṣaḥ* — the haters; *arṇaḥ na* — as the water of the sea covers dust and the like; *pari ṣṭhuḥ* — they surround (they overcome); (therefore) (*he*) *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *vaḥ* — your; *śavasaḥ* — of strength; *antam* — the end; *anti* — near; (or) *ārāttāt cit* — from afar; *asme* — (anyone in the midst of) us; *nu* — quickly; *nahi āpuḥ* — do not reach at all.

**Bhāvārtha.** The Marut-gods, increasing with their own strength, overwhelming the haters, bring all of them into their power, as the water of the sea brings dust and such things into its own power; therefore no one can know the end (the limit) of their strength, either near or from afar.

**English Translation (as printed):** None of us, Maruts, have attained, either nearly or remotely the limit of your strength: those (Maruts), increasing in energy and vigour, overwhelm their enemies like an ocean.

### Printed p. 105  (PDF 125)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 5".)* **Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***śavasaḥ antam asme nu nahi āpuḥ*** — *yuṣmākaṃ sambandhino balasya avasānam asmākaṃ madhye 'py eko 'pi kṣipraṃ naiva khalu prāpnuvanti | sannidhāvasannidhau ca na prāpnuvanti*. The word *śavas* is stated among the names of water (Ni. 1-12 [?]) and read among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]). The seers of the mantra, in order to praise the greatness of the Maruts, say that not even one of us, whether near you or far, has the capacity to know by knowledge the measure of your strength; thus, since it is boundless, the Maruts' greatness is praised.

The word *asme*, though having the same form in all the seven cases, conveys the sense of the respective case; thus the Nirukta-writers have given explanations and examples. *Asme te bandhuḥ* — in this sentence the word *asme* has the sense of the nominative case, "we". *Asme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ* — here the sense of the accusative, *asmān* ("us"). *Asme samānebhir vṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ* — here the sense of the instrumental, *asmābhiḥ* ("by us"). *Asme priyendhi maghavann ṛjīṣin* — the sense of the dative, *asmabhyam* ("to us"). *Asme ārāc cid dveṣaḥ sanutar yuyotu* — the sense of the ablative, *asmat* ("from us"). *Ūrvo iva paprathe kāmo asme* — the use of the genitive, *asmākam* ("our"). *Asme dhatta vasavo vasūni* — the sense of the locative, *asmāsu* ("in us") is given here (Ni. 6-[?]).

***ārāccit*** — *dūrādapi | yadvā cideti kutsāyāṃ atyantadūrāt*: "even from afar"; or the particle *cit* is in the sense of scorn: "from very far". The Nirukta-writer has explained that the particle *cit* is used in many senses. Here, for the word *cit*, the sense *api* ("even"), which is of the nature of conjunction, and a sense of disparagement are given. He explains the sense as "whether far, or from very far".

***śavasā śūśuvāṃsaḥ*** — the Marut-gods, who grow in strength by a power that overbears others, *dveṣaḥ pari ṣṭhuḥ* by their own strength — it is described that they keep enemies under their own control. In this matter the simile *arṇaḥ na* is stated: *yathā udakaṃ rajaḥ ādikam abhibhavati tadvat* — "as water overwhelms the dust and the like". It is explained that, as water, by its own capacity, draws into itself the dust, its enemy, so these keep their enemies in subjection to themselves. From this it is described that they are of immeasurable strength.

### Printed p. 106  (PDF 126)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* **॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *nahi* (*nipātasya ca* Pā. 6-3-136 gives lengthening in the Saṃhitā). *anti* (the word *antika*; by the statement *kādilopaḥ… bahulam iti vaktavyam* the *k* of it is dropped). *asme* (locative plural; *supāṃ sulug…* Pā. 7-1-39 gives *śe* in its place). *ārāttāt* (*ārāt* is an indeclinable that gives the senses "far" and "near"; the suffix *tātil* in its own sense; being *lit*, the preceding syllable gets the acute). *āpuḥ* (root *āpḷ vyāptau*; Vedic *liṭ* in the present sense; 3rd plural; by connection with *nahi*, no *nighāta*; final acute by the suffix). *dhṛṣṇunā* (root *ḍhṛṣā prāgalbhye*; *knu* by *trasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ* Pā. 3-2-140; as it is *kit* no *laghūpadha-guṇa*; instrumental singular). *śūśuvāṃsaḥ* (root *ṭuośvi gativṛddhyoḥ*; *kvasu* in place of *liṭ*; *vibhāṣā śveḥ* Pā. 6-1-30 gives *saṃprasāraṇa* to the root; *pūrvarūpa*; *vasvekājāddhasām* Pā. 7-2-67 prevents *iṭ* for the suffix; the root being doubled, *tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya* Pā. 6-1-7 gives the reduplicate its lengthening; accent by the suffix). *dveṣaḥ* (root *dviṣa aprītau*; *vic* by *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante*; *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* gives guṇa; the suffix is wholly dropped; accusative plural). *ṣṭhuḥ* (root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; Vedic *luṅ* in the present sense by *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*; 3rd plural, *jhi*; *cli* → *sic*; *āteḥ* Pā. 3-4-110 gives *jus* for *jhi*; *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* gives *luk* of *sic*; *uṣyapadāntāt* gives *pararūpa*; by *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi* no *aṭ*; *nighāta* follows; *upasargāt sunoti…* Pā. 8-3-65 gives *ṣatva*). ‖ 9 ‖

> *vayamadyetyetāsāṃ daśamīmastamita āditye japet | tathā ca sūtram | vayamadyendrasya preṣṭhā ityastaṃ yātyādye | ā. gṛ. 3-6-14 | iti ‖*
>
> अद्यास्मिन्निने [?] दिने वयं यष्टारः इन्द्रस्य देवस्य प्रेष्ठाः प्रियतमा भवेम । यद्वा । प्रियतमा वयमिन्द्रस्य महत्त्वं वोचेमहि । स्तोतुं समर्था भूयास्म । किञ्च वयं श्वः परस्मिन्नपि दिने समर्ये । सह मर्यैर्मर्त्यैऋत्विग्भिर्यस्मिन् स समर्यो यज्ञस्तस्मिन् । संग्रामे वा । इन्द्रस्य महत्त्वं वोचेमहि । किञ्च वयं पुरा पूर्वस्मिन्नतीतेऽपि काले मही महद्बलं नोऽस्मदर्थं वोचेमहि । तथा द्यून् दिवसाननु । प्रतिदिवसमित्यर्थः । अतीते आगामिनि च दिवसे सर्वदा वोचेमहि । तत्स्मद्भ्यामिभक्षाः [?] । महन्नामैतत् ऋभुक्षा उक्षा इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । महानिन्द्रो नरां मनुष्याणां मध्ये नोऽस्मानन्वनु स्यात् । अनुभवतु । अनुकूलमभिमतप्रदो वा भवतु ॥

*Gist:* The tenth ṛk is to be recited when the sun has set (Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra). May we be dearest to Indra today; may we tell his greatness tomorrow too, at the sacrifice or in battle, and in the past and every day; may great Indra be favourable to us among men.

**Pratipadārtha.** *adya* — this day; *indrasya* — to Indra; *preṣṭhāḥ* — the dearest; *vayam* — we (the sacrificers); *vocemahi* — [may we be] capable of praising (Indra's greatness); [or: *vayam* — we; *indrasya* — of Indra; *preṣṭhāḥ* — his dearest (we become); *adya* — this day; *vocemahi* — (his greatness) may we declare;] *vayam* — we; *śvaḥ* — tomorrow's *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 108  (PDF 128)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* *samarye* — at a sacrifice with priests and so on, or in a battle (*vocemahi* — may we praise his greatness); and *vayam* — we; *purā* — in the past also; (*vocemahi* — we have declared his greatness); *dyūn anu* — now, every day; *mahi* — his great strength; *naḥ* — for us (as the giver of strength); (*vocemahi* — we praise); *tat* — therefore; *ṛbhukṣāḥ* — the great Indra; *narām* — among men; *naḥ* — to us (praisers); *anu syāt* — may he be favourable (the giver of the desired).

**Bhāvārtha.** We who are dear to Indra will praise him today; tomorrow too, at the time of the sacrifice, we shall praise him; as in the past, so also every day, we shall praise him for our benefit. Thereby may Indra, pleased, favour us among men, the praisers.

**English Translation (as printed):** Let us, who are beloved of Indra, glorify him to-day; let us glorify him tomorrow, at the sacred rite; let us glorify him for our gret [sic] (good), in future days as of old, so that Ribhukshin may ever be favourable to us amongst men.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** This ṛk is said, in the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 3-6-14 [?]), to be recited after sunset.

***vayam adya indrasya preṣṭhāḥ*** — *yaṣṭāraḥ asmin dine devasya priyatamā bhavema*: "we, the sacrificers, on this day may be most dear to the god": the wish, made by the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice that on this day they become objects of affection to the deities, is stated as the first meaning of this sentence. *Yadvā vayam indrasya mahatvaṃ stotuṃ samarthā bhūyāsma*: or, as the second meaning, "we, as sacrificers, may become able to praise Indra's greatness" is explained.

***śvaḥ samarye vocemahi*** — "tomorrow, after the sacrifice has been performed, we praise Indra's greatness". The word *samarya* here: *saha maryāḥ martyāḥ ṛtvijaḥ yasmin sa samaryo yajñaḥ tasmin | saṃgrāme vā* — "the sacrifice in which are men, mortals, that is, priests", or "in a battle". The word *marya* is stated among the names of men (Ni. 3-[?]); the meaning of the word *samarya* is *yajña*, the sacrifice with the priests who gather with men at the place of the sacrifice to perform the necessary rites, or *yuddha* (war), a battle with the intent of men to carry out their purposes; it is explained: we praise Indra's greatness both in sacrifices and in battles.

### Printed p. 109  (PDF 129)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 5".)* **Special Topics (continued).**

***purā mahi naḥ*** — *pūrvasmin atīte 'pi kāle mahadbalam asmadartham vocemahi*: "even in the past too we shall declare his great strength for our sake". In the preceding days of the sacrifice too we have been praising the greatness of the mighty Indra who favours us; and ***naḥ ṛbhukṣāḥ anu syāt*** — the wish is made that Indra, as to us who live among ordinary men, as sacrificers, may fulfil our desires. The word *ṛbhukṣāḥ* is stated among the names of "great" (Ni. 3-13 [?]). And —

> मा नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुरिन्द्र ऋभुक्षा मरुतः परि ख्यन् । यद्वाजिनो देवजातस्य सप्तेः प्रवक्ष्यामो विदथे वीर्याणि ॥

> *mā no mitro varuṇo aryamāyurindra ṛbhukṣā marutaḥ pari khyan | yadvājino devajātasya sapteḥ pravakṣyāmo vidathe vīryāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-1) — for the word *ṛbhukṣāḥ* in this ṛk the explanation is given: *urāv antarikṣe kṣiyati nivasati* ("who dwells in the great middle region") [as read], or *athavā kṣayatir aiśvaryakarmā ṛbhūṇāṃ devānāṃ rājā* ("[the root] *kṣi* has the sense of lordship: who is king of the Ṛbhu deities"): thus the abundant greatness of Indra is established.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *preṣṭhāḥ* (*atiśayena priyāḥ preṣṭhāḥ*; *atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau* Pā. 5-3-55 gives *iṣṭhan*; following it, *priyasthirasphirorubahulagurvavṛddhatvadīrghavṛndārakāṇāṃ prasthasphavabahaguravarddhatrapadīrghavṛndāḥ* Pā. 6-4-157 gives *pra* for *priya*; *prakṛtyaikāc* Pā. 6-4-163 prevents the loss; guṇa; as the suffix is *nit*, initial acute). *vocemahi* (root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *liṅ* 1st plural; by *vyatyaya* *mahiṅ* [ātmanepada]; *vyatyayo bahulam* gives *aj*; *sīyuṭ* comes to the *liṅ* and, with *s*-loss, guṇa; *vaco 'ruṃ* [Pā. 7-4-20 [?]] gives *uṃ* to the root; at the start of the pāda no *nighāta*). *samarye* (*saha maryāḥ yasmin tasmin samarye*; *samāsasya* Pā. 6-1-223 gives final acute). *ṛbhukṣāḥ* (with *uru* or *ṛtu* as *upapada*; root *bhā dīptau* or *bhū sattāyām*; suffix *ku* by *mṛgayopadeyaś ca* Uṇ. 1-38; the *ṛ* of the prior member is established by *nipātana*; with *ṛbhu* as *upapada*, the root *kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ*; the suffix *ini* by *pathe iṣṭa* … by *bahula*; the *i* of the root dropped; a following *su* … *pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt* Pā. 7-1-85 gives *ā*; the *ā* gets the acute by the suffix's accent).

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> एष वः स्तोमो मरुत इयं गीर्मान्दार्यस्य मान्यस्य कारोः ।
> एषा यासीष्ट तन्वे वयां विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ ११ ॥

> *eṣa vaḥ stomo maruta iyaṃ gīrmāndāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ |*
> *eṣā yāsīṣṭa tanve vayāṃ vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एषः । वः । स्तोमः । मरुतः । इयम् । गीः । मान्दार्यस्य । मान्यस्य । कारोः ।
> आ । इषा । यासीष्ट । तन्वे । वयाम् । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥ ११ ॥

> *eṣaḥ | vaḥ | stomaḥ | marutaḥ | iyam | gīḥ | māndāryasya | mānyasya | kāroḥ |*
> *ā | iṣā | yāsīṣṭa | tanve | vayām | vidyāma | iṣam | vṛjanam | jīra 'dānum ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> एष इत्येकादशे [?] व्याख्याता ॥ *(printed note: "See p. 69")*

**Pratipadārtha.** (*he*) *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *māndāryasya* — who gladdens you with praises; *mānyasya* — worshipful; *kāroḥ* — of the praiser; *eṣaḥ stomaḥ* — this praise (made so far); (*thā* — likewise); *iyaṃ gīḥ* — this (praise-form) speech; (*vaḥ* — for you); *vaḥ* — may it be pleasing to you; [*māndāryasya* — of him who gladdens you by praises; *mānyasya* — and therefore of the man who is honourable; *kāroḥ* — of this praiser]; *iṣā* — with desire; *tanve* — for the body (for its growth); *ā yāsīṣṭa* — (the praise) may it reach you; *vayam* — we; *iṣam* — food; *vṛjanam* — strength; *jīradānum* — long life; *vidyāma* — may we obtain.

### Printed p. 111  (PDF 131)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 5".)* **Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, may the praise made so far and this praise-speech [being made now] give you satisfaction; and, from the wish of the praiser, who is a giver of delight to you by his praises and the like, and is honourable, may it come to you for the nourishment of your bodies; and for us too grant food, strength and long life.

**English Translation (as printed):** This praise, Maruts, is for you; this hymn is for you, (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring delight (by his laudations): may the praise reach you for (the good of your) persons, so that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***eṣaḥ stomaḥ vaḥ*** — by this sentence, addressing the Maruts: *idānīṃ kriyamāṇa prakāraṃ stotraṃ yuṣmat prīṇanāya bhavatu* — "let the praise, in the manner now being made by us, the sacrificers, be glorious and give you pleasure" — thus it is explained.

***iyaṃ gīḥ*** — *stutirūpā vāk api yuṣmadarthāya*: even this speech in the form of praise, may it be for your delight: thus a wish is expressed.

***māndāryasya*** — this word is used as an adjective of the word *kāroḥ*. The word *kāru* is read among the names of the praiser (Ni. 3-19 [?]). By the word *māndārya* is explained "he who, by his praises, makes manifest, or increases, the greatness of his praised deity"; and by the word *mānyasya*, "the praiser who, by his praise, through the favour of the satisfied deities, has obtained boons and is worthy of honour" — by the explanation *stotṛviśeṣaiḥ mandayituḥ stutibhiḥ madasya preraṇayituḥ nārā varapradānādinā mānanīyasya* [as read].

***vayāṃ tanve iṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānuṃ vidyāma*** — *vayaṃ śarīrāya tejobalāya annaṃ balaṃ jayaśīlatānaṃ yuṣmat-prāgateṣu yajñasaṃpūrtyai* [?]: "we, because the sacrifice is performed without obstruction through the coming of the deities, have our desires granted by the deities *[continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 112  (PDF 132)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 167".)* …and, being favoured, for the growth of our body we pray the deities that we may have food and strength, and be victorious, and be of a nature to do abundant giving."

The word *iṣa* is stated among the names of food (Ni. 2-7 [?]); the word *vṛjana* is also read among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]). Here the meaning "strength" is given. The Nirukta-writer has also illustrated the use of this word in another sense:

> महां अमत्रो वृजने विरप्शी उग्रं शवः पत्यते धृष्ण्वोजः । नाह विव्याच पृथिवी चनैनं यत्सोमासो हर्यश्वममन्दन् ॥

> *mahāṃ amatro vṛjane virapśī ugraṃ śavaḥ patyate dhṛṣṇvojaḥ | nāha vivyāca pṛthivī canainaṃ yatsomāso haryaśvamamandan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-36-4 [?]) — here *vṛjane* is explained as "in battle" (*saṃgrāme*).

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥** This has been explained earlier, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-166-15 [?].

## Sūkta 168 — *yajñāyajñā vaḥ* (Anuvāka 23, fourth Sūkta; 10 ṛks)

*(Heading, p. 112: "The hundred and sixty-eighth Sūkta" — ನೂರ ಅರವತ್ತೆಂಟನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> यज्ञायज्ञेति दशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तमागस्त्यं मारुतम् । अन्त्यास्तिस्रस्त्रिष्टुभः । शिष्टाः सप्त तिसृष्टुबन्तपरिभाषया जगत्यः [?] । यज्ञायज्ञा दश त्रिष्टुबन्तमित्यनुक्रान्तम् ॥ विशेषविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

*Gist:* The fourth sūkta (*yajñāyajñā*), of ten ṛks, by Agastya, to the Maruts; the last three ṛks are triṣṭubh, the other seven jagatī (by the rule "up to the triṣṭubh ones"); the Anukramaṇikā: "*yajñāyajñā daśa triṣṭubantam*"; the special application is by indication.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This Sūkta beginning *yajñāyajñā* is the fourth Sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has ten ṛks. Agastya is the ṛṣi of this Sūkta; the Maruts are the deities. The last three ṛks are in *jagatī* metre [*as printed*; the bhāṣya says the last three are *triṣṭubh*]. The Anukramaṇikā says: "*yajñāyajñā daśa triṣṭubantam*". The special application (*viniyoga*) is by indication.
