### Printed p. 113  (PDF 133)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6".)*

**॥ ॐ ॥** Sūkta—168
Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 23 ‖ Sūkta 168 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 6, 7 ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 10 · Ṛṣi: Agastya · Devatā: the Maruts · Chandas: ṛks 1–8 *jagatī*, 9–10 *triṣṭubh* (as read in the heading block [?]).

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यज्ञायज्ञा वः समना तुतुर्वणिर्धियंधियं वो देवया उ दधिध्वे ।
> आ वोऽर्वाचः सुविताय रोदस्योर्महे ववृत्यामवसे सुवृक्तिभिः ॥ १ ॥

> *yajñāyajñā vaḥ samanā tuturvaṇirdhiyaṃdhiyaṃ vo devayā u dadhidhve |*
> *ā vo 'rvācaḥ suvitāya rodasyormahe vavṛtyāmavase suvṛktibhiḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यज्ञाऽयज्ञा । वः । समना । तुतुर्वणिः । धियम्ऽधियम् । वः । देवऽयाः । ऊँ इति । दधिध्वे ।
> आ । वः । अर्वाचः । सुविताय । रोदस्योः । महे । ववृत्याम् । अवसे । सुवृक्तिऽभिः ॥ १ ॥

> *yajñā 'yajñā | vaḥ | samanā | tuturvaṇiḥ | dhiyam 'dhiyam | vaḥ | deva 'yāḥ | ū~ iti | dadhidhve |*
> *ā | vaḥ | arvācaḥ | suvitāya | rodasyoḥ | mahe | vavṛtyām | avase | suvṛkti 'bhiḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः वः समना समाकृतिर्न्यूनाधिकाभावलक्षणा यज्ञा यज्ञा सर्वेष्वपि यज्ञेषु तुतुर्वणिस्तूर्णवनिस्त्वरमाणा संभजमाना भवति । तुतुर्वणिस्तूर्णवनिरिति यास्कः ॥ नि. ६-१४ । तत्र त्यागावसर आगत्य हविः स्वीकृत्य वैकल्यपरिहारेण सफलं कुरुथेत्यर्थः । किञ्च वो यूयं धियं धियं युष्मत्सम्बन्धिवृष्टिप्रदानादिरूपं सर्वं कर्म देवयाः देवानात्मन इच्छन्तः [?] पूजयितार इव सन्तो दधिध्वे । धारयथ धारयध्वे वा । देवार्थहविराद्युत्पादनाय वृष्टिं कुरुथेत्यर्थः । यस्मादेवं कुरथ तस्माद्वो युष्मानर्वाचोऽभिमुखानहं ववृत्याम् । आवर्तयामि । किमर्थम् । रोदस्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योर्महते [?] ऽवसे रक्षणाय प्रीणनाय वा । तदपि किमर्थमिति । सुविताय सुष्ठु व्याप्ताय । कैः साधनैः । सुवृक्तिभिः शोभनावर्जनैः स्तोत्रैः ॥

*Gist:* O Maruts, in every sacrifice your balanced hastening is felt; you come at the time of oblation, accept it and make it fruitful; you carry out every act (rain-giving and the like) as if you desired the gods; therefore, with good praises I turn you towards us, for the great protection of heaven and earth.

### Printed p. 114  (PDF 134)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

**Pratipadārtha.** (*he marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods); *vaḥ* — your; *samanā* — an even mind (free from the feeling of "more" or "less"); *yajñāyajñā* — in every sacrifice too; *tuturvaṇiḥ* — hastening, pervading with speed; (*kiṃca* — and further); *vaḥ* — you; *dhiyaṃdhiyam* — every act of yours (of the form of giving rain and so on); *devayā u* — those serving the gods; *dadhidhve* — you bear (you carry out); (therefore) *vaḥ* — you; *rodasyoḥ* — of heaven and earth; *suvitāya* — well pervaded; *mahe avase* — for the great protection (for satisfaction); *suvṛktibhiḥ* — by auspicious praises; *arvācaḥ* — (towards us) facing us; *ā vavṛtyām* — I turn.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, your equable mind (without more or less) pervades all sacrifices; and all your acts (the giving of rain and so on) you carry out as helpers of the gods (as if as bringers of the oblations and the like to the gods). Therefore, for our satisfaction and for the protection of heaven and earth and the sky, I face you towards us with beneficial praises.

**English Translation (as printed):** Maruts, at every sacrifice your alacrity is uniform: you, verily, discharge your every function for the benefit of the gods: therefore, do I invite you to come hither, by sacred hymns, for (the sake of) your powerful protection of heaven and earth, and your beneficent praise.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***vaḥ samanā yajñāyajñā tuturvaṇiḥ*** — addressing the Marut-gods: "in all sacrifices, that is, at the times when the sacrifices are performed by the sacrificer, you favour with your presence for the acceptance of the oblation, and you are capable of being at hand in the sacrifice, without deficiency or excess" *[continues on the next page]*

---

### Printed p. 115  (PDF 135)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6".)* …"removing the faults, they perform the sacrifice so that it is completed in the manner enjoined by the rule": thus their greatness, and the excess of haste of the Marut-gods in regard to the sacrifice, is described. By the word *samanā* the *samākṛti*, "equality of intent", which consists in the absence of deficiency or excess in regard to every sacrifice, is explained for the Marut-gods. For the word *tuturvaṇiḥ* used here, the text has explained "*turvaṇiḥ*". The word *turvaṇi* is [stated] by Yāska —

> सतुर्वणिर्मह्ना अरेणु पौंस्ये गिरेर्भृष्टिर्न भ्राजते तुजा शवः । येन शुष्णं मायिनमायसो मदे दुध्र आभूषु रामयन्नि दामनि ॥ [?]

> *saturvaṇirmahnā areṇu pauṃsye girerbhṛṣṭirna bhrājate tujā śavaḥ | yena śuṣṇaṃ māyinamāyaso made dudhra ābhūṣu rāmayanni dāmani ‖ [?]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-3) — in the cited ṛk *turvaṇiḥ* (Ni. 6-14 [?]) is explained as "*stotāraṃ tūrṇaṃ bhajate*" — "he who comes quickly near the praiser": the meaning "one who has haste" is given.

***dhiyaṃ dhiyam*** — for these words: *yuṣmatsambandhivṛṣṭipradānādikaṃ sarvaṃ karma* — "all the acts of yours, giving rain and the rest": the grace of giving rain by the Maruts is explained as the first of the later acts; and the meaning that these acts, too, are such as give satisfaction to the gods, "like those who serve the gods" (*devān prāpayitāra iva*, [as read]), is explained for the word *devayāḥ*: "*devārthaṃ havirādyutpādanāya vṛṣṭiṃ kurutha*" — the Marut-gods cause rain, for the very sake of the production, in the form of grain and the like, of the oblations offered to the gods.

***rodasyoḥ mahe avase suvitāya*** — *dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ mahate rakṣaṇāya prīṇanāya vā suṣṭhu vyāptāya*: "for the great protection of heaven and earth, or for their satisfaction; for the sake of your pervading all places and times, which is [equable]": with *suvṛktibhiḥ* — "excellent praises" — we call you towards us who sacrifice: this prayer of the seer of the mantra is described here. The Nirukta-writer has quoted an example of the use of the word *suvṛktibhiḥ* in this same sense:

> इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः । पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेम धीतिभिः ॥

> *iyaṃ śuṣmebhirbisakhā ivārujatsānu girīṇāṃ taviṣebhirūrmibhiḥ | pārāvataghnīmavase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīmā vivāsema dhītibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-61-2) — here *suvṛktibhiḥ* means *supravṛttābhiḥ svaraṣoṣmādiyuktābhiḥ* [as read]: "praises endowed with such sounds as *udātta* and the rest, with soft words, and with words that convey the right meaning".

### Printed p. 116  (PDF 136)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)* **॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numbers [?]).** *yajñāyajñā* (*nityavīpsayoḥ* Pā. 8-1-4 gives doubling; *anudāttaṃ ca* Pā. 8-1-3 [?] makes the latter reduplicated member wholly unaccented; *supāṃ sulug…* gives *ā* to the case-ending). *samanā* (*samyag ānayitrī samanā*; root *ana prāṇane*; *ac* since the root belongs to the *pacādi* class; final acute; *ṭāp* in the feminine; in the *prādisamāsa* the *kṛdutta* member keeps its own accent). *devayāḥ* (root *yā prāpaṇe*; *devān yāpayantīti devayāḥ*; after a *ṇijanta* *kvip*; *ṇeraniṭi* Pā. 6-4-51 drops *ṇi*; the *kṛdutta* member keeps its accent). *dadhidhve* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; Vedic *liṭ*; 2nd plural; *nighāta* after a *tiṅanta*). *suvitāya* (*suṣṭhu itāya*; root *iṇ gatau*; *kta*; *tanādīnāṃ chandasi bahulam upasaṃkhyānam* gives *uvaṅ*; final acute by the suffix; dative singular). *mahe* (root *maha pūjāyām*; *kvip*; dative; *sānekācaś ca* Pā. 6-1-168 gives the acute to the case-ending). *vavṛtyām* (root *vṛtu vartane*; *liṅ* 1st singular; by *vyatyaya* *mip* → *am*; *ślu* for *śap*; the root doubled; *yāsuṭ*; *nighāta* after a *tiṅanta*). *suvṛktibhiḥ* (*śobhanā vṛktiḥ yeṣāṃ taiḥ*; *nañsubhyām* gives final acute to the later member). ‖ 1 ‖

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वव्रासो न ये स्वजाः स्वतवस इषं स्वरभिजायन्त धूतयः ।
> सहस्रियासो अपां नोर्मय आसा गावो वन्द्यासो नोक्षणः ॥ २ ॥

> *vavrāso na ye svajāḥ svatavasa iṣaṃ svarabhijāyanta dhūtayaḥ |*
> *sahasriyāso apāṃ normaya āsā gāvo vandyāso nokṣaṇaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

---

### Printed p. 117  (PDF 137)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वव्रासः । न । ये । स्वऽजाः । स्वऽतवसः । इषम् । स्वः । अभिऽजायन्ते । धूतयः ।
> सहस्रियासः । अपाम् । न । ऊर्मयः । आसा । गावः । वन्द्यासः । न । उक्षणः ॥ २ ॥

> *vavrāsaḥ | na | ye | sva 'jāḥ | sva 'tavasaḥ | iṣam | svaḥ | abhi 'jāyante | dhūtayaḥ |*
> *sahasriyāsaḥ | apām | na | ūrmayaḥ | āsā | gāvaḥ | vandyāsaḥ | na | ukṣaṇaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> ये मरुतो वव्रासो न । वव्रिरिति रूपनाम । रूपवन्त इव । ते यथा प्रकृष्टा लक्ष्यन्ते तद्वत् । यद्वा । अरूपा अपि सरूपा इव । स्वजाः स्वयमेव स्वस्माद्वा जायमानाः । अनन्यहेतुका इत्यर्थः । धूतयः कम्पनशीलाः सन्ति ते इषमन्नं हविर्लक्षणमन्नसाधनं सस्यादिकं वा स्वः स्वर्गं चाभिजायन्ते । अभिलक्ष्य प्रादुर्भवन्ति । ते दृष्टान्तमुखेन श्रूयन्ते । अपां नोर्मयः उदकानामूर्मय इव सहस्रियासः सहस्रसंमिताः । तथा वन्द्यासो बहुक्षीरादिप्रदेशेन [?] स्तुत्या गावो न गाव इवासा समीपापि [?] उक्षणो वृष्ट्युदकस्य सेक्तारः । ताद्दृशा मरुतः प्रादुर्भवन्तीत्यन्वयः ॥

*Gist:* The self-born, self-powered, quivering Maruts, as if embodied, appear for the sake of food and heaven, numerous as the waves of the waters, praise-worthy like cows, sprinklers of the rain.

**Pratipadārtha.** *ye marutaḥ* — which Marut-gods; *vavrāsaḥ na* — (though formless) like those who have a form; *svajāḥ* — self-born (not born of anything else); *svatavasaḥ* — endowed with innate strength; *dhūtayaḥ* — of trembling nature (those who shake); *te* — those; *apām* — of waters; *ūrmayaḥ na* — like the waves; *sahasriyāsaḥ* — countless; (*tathā* — likewise) *vandyāsaḥ* — (as givers of milk and the like) deserving praise; *gāvaḥ na* — like cows; *āsā* — being near; *ukṣaṇaḥ* — sprinklers of water; (*vandyāsaḥ* — praise-worthy) *te* — those Marut-gods; *iṣam* — (what we desire) food; *svaḥ* — heaven too (to give them); *abhi jāyante* — appear.

**Bhāvārtha.** The Marut-gods, as though having form though formless, self-born, powerful by nature, of trembling nature, numerous like the waves of water, and worthy of praise like cows that give milk and the like, appear sprinkling water, in order to bestow on us the food and heavenly worlds that we wish for.

### Printed p. 118  (PDF 138)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

**English Translation (as printed):** They who are as if embodied, self-born, self-invigorated, and (ever) tremulous (in movement), are generated (to confer) abundant food and heaven: they are numerous as the undulations of the waters; they are to be praised when present, shedding water, like cows (yielding milk).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***marutaḥ vavrāso na*** — *vavririti rūpanāma rūpavanta iva te yathā prakṛṣṭā lakṣyante tadvat | yadvā arūpā api sarūpā iva*: here the particle *na* is used in the sense of comparison. The word *vavri* is read among the names of form (Ni. 3-7 [?]) and

> अयं स शिङ्क्ते येन गौरभीवृता मिमाति मायुं ध्वसनावधि श्रिता । सा चित्तिभिर्नि हि चकार मर्त्यं विद्युद्भवन्ती प्रति वव्रिमौहत ॥

> *ayaṃ sa śiṅkte yena gaurabhīvṛtā mimāti māyuṃ dhvasanāvadhi śritā | sā cittibhirni hi cakāra martyaṃ vidyudbhavantī prati vavrimauhata ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-29) — for the word *vavri* in this ṛk, "*vavririti rūpanāma vṛṇotīti sataḥ*" [as read] (from the root *vṛñ*): the word *vavri* is explained as conveying the sense of form (*rūpa*). Following the sense of the Vedic statement that the Maruts are of various forms, Sāyaṇa, in the ṛk

> वायवा याहि दर्शतेमे सोमा अरंकृताः ।

> *vāyavā yāhi darśateme somā araṃkṛtāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-1 [?]) explains *darśate* as *darśanīya* ("O beautiful Vāyu, to be seen"), taking the sense of "*rūpavantaḥ iva*" ("as having form"), and explains "*te yathā prakṛṣṭā lakṣyante*" — "they are seen as splendid ones" — as "beautiful": thus the Maruts, having bodies, are of changeable forms; he establishes the meaning by comparing them to those of different forms. Based on another Vedic statement, that the deity Vāyu has no form but his activity alone is perceptible, he gives the second meaning "*arūpā api sarūpā iva*": though the Marut-gods have no form, they perform acts as if they were of changed form.

***svajāḥ*** — *svayam eva svasmād vā jāyamānāḥ | ananyahetukāḥ*: "born of themselves, from themselves; without any other cause": the Marut-gods do not come to birth in the world as beings do, taking birth by a cause in accordance with their own meritorious and unmeritorious acts, to experience the fruits that depend on acts. They are said to have arisen of themselves to manifest their own glory to the world and to bring about the increase of the happiness of the world.

### Printed p. 119  (PDF 139)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6"; the page continues the Special Topics of Ṛk 2.)*

***dhūtayaḥ, iṣaṃ svaḥ abhijāyante*** — *kampanaśīlāḥ santi | annaṃ haviḥ-lakṣaṇam anna-sādhanaṃ sasyādikaṃ vā svargaṃ ca abhilakṣya prādurbhavanti*: the Marut-gods, being always of a moving (shaking) nature, set other things (trees and the like) in motion; and, for the production of the grain that is the means of the food in the form of the oblation, they themselves become eager in their work; and, for the sacrificers who offer oblations in the name of the gods, they engage in bringing about heaven and the other excellent states that begin with heaven. This is what is described.

***apāṃ ūrmayo na*** — as the waves in the ocean are without number, so the number of the Marut-gods is endless; or, they are those who do endless benefits. This is what is said.

***sahasriyāsaḥ vandyāsaḥ gāvo na*** — *sahasrasaṃmitāḥ bahukṣīrādi pradeśena stutyāḥ gāva iva*: being of countless number, not to be encompassed by counting; and, as cows, because they give much milk and the like, are benefactors to others and so become objects of praise, in the same way, since the action of the Marut-gods is of indirect benefit (*paropakāra*), the Marut-gods are described as worthy of praise. And

***āsā ukṣaṇaḥ*** — *samīpā iva vṛṣṭyudakasya sektāraḥ*: the word *āsāt* [as read; the ṛk has *āsā*] is read among the names of "near" (Ni. 3-[?]). As the Marut-gods bestow rain-water directly upon the world, and as cows give milk and the like directly, it is said here by way of the relation of comparison (*upamānopameyabhāva*).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *vavrāsaḥ* (*vavriḥ yeṣām asti*; affix *ac* by "*arśa ādibhyo'c*", Pā. Sū. 5-2-127 [?]; elision of the *i* by "*yasyeti ca*"; the augment *asuk* before *jas* by "*ājjaserasuk*", Pā. Sū. 7-1-50 [?]); *svajāḥ* (*svayameva jāyante*; affix *ḍa* by "*anyeṣvapi dṛśyate*", Pā. Sū. 3-2-101); *svatavasaḥ* (*svaṃ tavaḥ yeṣāṃ te*; a *bahuvrīhi*, the first member keeping its own accent by "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*", Pā. Sū. 6-2-1).

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सोमासः । न । ये । सुताः । तृप्त्यऽअंशवः [?] । हृत्ऽसु । पीतासः । दुवसः । न । आसते ।
> आ । एषाम् । अंसेषु । रम्भिणीऽइव । ररभे [?] । हस्तेषु । खादिः । च । कृतिः । च ।
> सम् । दधे ॥ ३ ॥

*(Pada as printed; the word *rārabhe* of the Saṃhitā is read in the Pada as *ra-rabhe*, doubtful — see the doubts log.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> ये मरुतः सुता अभिषुतास्तृप्त्यांशवस्तर्पितावयवाः सोमासो न सोमा इव । यथा वल्लीरूपाः सोमा अभिषवात्पूर्वमाप्यायनेन तृप्त्यावयवाः सन्तः पश्चात्सुता अभिषुता रसभूताः पीतासः पीताः सन्तो हृत्सु पातॄणां [?] हृदयेषु दुवसो नासते परिचरन्त इवासते तद्वत् । ये मरुतो यज्ञे आहूतास्तृप्त्यावयवा भवन्ति ध्यायमानाः सन्तो हृत्सु हृदयेषु दुवसो न परिचरन्त इवासते । यद्वा । प्राणादिरूपेण शरीरे स्थिता दुवसः परिचरन्त इव गमनादिचेष्टाः कुर्वन्त आसते । ऐषामंसेषु रम्भिणीव युवतेर्वनांसालम्बिनी [?] योषिदिवा रारभे । आरेभे । आश्लिष्यति । अवलम्बने सामर्थ्याच्छक्त्यायुधविशेषो भुजलक्ष्मीर्वा [?] । किंच हस्तेषु खादिर्हस्तत्राणकश्च [?] कृतिः कर्तनी च खड्गलताष्टिश्च [?] सं दधे । संधीयते । सम्यग्धृता भवति । परस्परसमुच्चयार्थाश्चकाराः । ये मरुत उक्तरूपास्त आविर्भवन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* The Maruts, well-nourished like soma plants, once drunk dwell in the hearts of worshippers like attendants; on their shoulders a spear is held like a clinging young woman, and in their hands a hand-guard and a sword.

**Pratipadārtha.** *ye* — which Marut-gods; *tṛptyāṃśavaḥ* — those whose limbs are full (satisfied) with juice; *somāsaḥ* — like soma-creepers; *sutāḥ* — pressed (in the form of juice); *pītāsaḥ* — having been drunk; *hṛtsu* — (of those who drink) in the hearts; *duvasaḥ na* — like those who serve (they produce delight); *āsate* — (as) they remain (those invoked in sacrifices). Or: *tṛptyāṃśavaḥ* — (those who are, meditated upon) whose limbs are full (satisfied); *hṛtsu* — (of those who meditate) in the hearts; *duvasaḥ na* — like those who serve; *āsate* — they remain. Or: [*tṛptyāṃśavaḥ* — (by the form of the vital airs and the like) abiding in the body]; *duvasaḥ na* — like servants (through the activities of movement and the like); *āsate* — they remain. *eṣām* — of these Maruts; *aṃseṣu* — on the shoulders; *ā-bhujeṣu* [as printed] — on the arms; *rambhiṇī iva* — like a young woman (clinging to the arm of a youth, taking refuge); *rārabhe* — (the lance of power) is held up; (*kiṃca* — and further) *hasteṣu* — in the hands; *khādiḥ ca* — a guard (a hand-guard) too; *kṛtiḥ ca* — a sword too; *saṃ dadhe* — is held fast (such Marut-gods appear).

### Printed p. 122  (PDF 142)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** (Even before being pressed) full of limbs (rich in juice), and after being pressed, like soma-creepers which delight the minds of those who have drunk the soma juice that has the form of the sap, the Marut-gods, invoked in the sacrifices, delight the hearts of those who are satiated with fullness of limbs (those who meditate on them) (as established in the body, as the cause of movement and other activities, they produce contentment); as a young woman clings to the arm of a youth, a lance of power clings to their arms. That is: these hold the lance of power; and these also hold in their hands a sword and a guard (such Marut-gods appear for us).

**English Translation (as printed):** They, who are like the Soma plants, with well-nourished branches, and then poured out (in libations), are imbibed; they abide, like devoted adherents, in the hearts (of men); upon their shoulders hangs (a lance), like a youthful female, and in their hands a guard and sword are wielded.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***sutāḥ tṛptyāṃśavaḥ somāso na*** — the sentence *somāso na* and the sentence *hṛtsu pītāsaḥ duvaso na* are both *upamāna*-sentences. Soma-creepers are *sutāḥ* — those from which the juice has been pressed; *tṛptyāṃśavaḥ* — the pressed soma juice, for those who drink it, becomes a cause of satisfaction; or, before that, the soma-creepers are made full. This is the meaning. *yathā vallīrūpāḥ somāḥ abhiṣavāt pūrvam āpyāyanena tṛptyāvayavāḥ santaḥ paścāt sutāḥ abhiṣutāḥ rasabhūtāḥ* — the soma-creepers are brought and made to swell (like an offering, as one does); afterwards they are pressed and the juice is taken. The Marut-gods too, invoked for the soma-drinking in the sacrifice like soma, are *sutāḥ* — those who have been called; *tṛptyāṃśavaḥ* — those who have been satisfied (*tarpitāḥ santaḥ*); *vayovāḥ* [as printed; *vayo-avāḥ*?] — those of limbs satisfied with joy. By this, the two qualities *sutāḥ* and *tṛptyāṃśavaḥ* are described as belonging (to the Maruts) in both the *upamāna* and the *upameya*.

***hṛtsu pītāsaḥ duvaso na āsate*** — *pītāsaḥ santaḥ pātṝṇāṃ hṛdayeṣu paricaranta ivāsate*: after the soma juice has been drunk, it acts in the hearts of those who have drunk it, as if performing service. So also the Marut-gods appear as if performing acts in the hearts of those who meditate on them. This sense is explained by the sentence "*yajñe āhūtāḥ tṛptyāvayavāḥ bhavanti marutaḥ dhyāyamānāḥ santaḥ hṛtsu hṛdayeṣu paricaranta ivāsate*". This is one kind of meaning.

***yadvā prāṇādirūpeṇa śarīre sthitāḥ gamanādicēṣṭāḥ kurvaṃta āsate*** — in this second meaning the Marut-gods, abiding in the body in the forms of the vital airs and the like, are explained as being of the nature of actions such as moving; this is another meaning.

***eṣām aṃseṣu rambhiṇīva ā rārabhe*** — *yuvatervanāṃsālambinī yoṣiditva āśliṣyati | avalambane sāmarthyāt śaktyāyudhaviśeṣo bhujalakṣmīrvā*: the Marut-gods hold on their arms the weapon called *śakti*; as a young woman, or a special beauty, clings to the arms, so the holding of the weapon is described.

***hasteṣu khādiḥ kṛtiśca saṃdadhe*** — *hastatrāṇakaḥ kartanī khaḍgalatā ca samyak dhṛtā*: the Marut-gods hold in their hands a hand-guard and also a sword; thus their form is described, and it is explained that Marut-gods of such shape appear in the sacrifice.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *tṛptyāṃśavaḥ* (*tṛptāḥ aṃśavaḥ yeṣāṃ te*, a *bahuvrīhi*; the first member keeps its own accent) [the printed analysis reads as *tṛptāḥ*]; *hṛtsu* (*hṛdaya* before the locative plural; *hṛd* substituted by "*padannomāsṛn…*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-63 [?]; accent on the ending by "*ūḍidaṃpadādi…*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 [?]); *pītāsaḥ* (root *pā pāne*; *kta* in the passive; *ī* for the root by "*ghumāsthāgāpā…*", Pā. Sū. 6-4-66 [?]; *asuk* before *jas*); *duvasaḥ* (root *duvas* in the sense of serving; affix *kvip*; accent on the last syllable of the root); *āsate* (root *āsa upaveśane*, *adādi*; *laṭ*, 3rd person plural, *jha* → *ata*; the loss of the *nighāta* accent by "*yadvṛttānnityam*", Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 [?]; since the root is *anudāttet*, the root keeps its accent as the personal ending is unaccented); *rārabhe* (root *rabha rābhasye*; *liṭ*; the Vedic option "*sarve vidhayaḥ chandasi vikalpyante*" means the *itva* and the loss of the reduplicative syllable do not occur; lengthening of the reduplicative syllable in the Veda; accent of the verb after a non-verb (*nighāta*) because a word with the ending stands before it).

### Printed p. 124  (PDF 144)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

*khādiḥ* (root *khāda bhakṣaṇe*; by "*bahulagrahaṇa*", the Uṇādi affix *i* applies, as with *auṇādika* forms; the affix's accent makes the word *antodātta*); *dadhe* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *liṭ*, 3rd person singular, the middle form; *nighāta* accent on the verb). ‖ 3 ‖

*(ornamental rule)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अव स्वयुक्ता दिव आ वृथा ययुरमर्त्याः कशया चोदत त्मना ।
> अरेणवस्तुविजाता अचुच्यवुर्दृळ्हानि चिन्मरुतो भ्राजदृष्टयः ॥ ४ ॥

> *ava svayuktā diva ā vṛthā yayuramartyāḥ kaśayā codata tmanā |*
> *areṇavastuvijātā acucyavurdṛḷhāni cinmaruto bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अव । स्वऽयुक्ताः । दिवः । आ । वृथा । ययुः । अमर्त्याः । कशया । चोदत । त्मना ।
> अरेणवः । तुविऽजाताः । अचुच्यवुः । दृळ्हानि । चित् । मरुतः । भ्राजत्ऽऋष्टयः ॥ ४ ॥

> *ava | sva 'yuktāḥ | divaḥ | ā | vṛthā | yayuḥ | amartyāḥ | kaśayā | codata | tmanā |*
> *areṇavaḥ | tuvi 'jātāḥ | acucyavuḥ | dṛḷhāni | cit | marutaḥ | bhrājat 'ṛṣṭayaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> एते मरुतः स्वयुक्ताः स्वैर्योक्तृभिः परस्परं संयुक्ताः स्वेन धनेन वा युक्ताः सन्तो दिवो द्युलोकात् वृथानायासेन वा [?] ययुः । अवाङ्मुखा गच्छन्ति । हे अमर्त्या मरुतः यूयं त्मना आत्मना स्वयमेव कशया [?] वाङ्मा [?] स्मैतत् [?] । वाचा स्तुतिरूपया चोदत । प्रेरयत । स्तोतृभिरिति शेषः । ते च मरुतोऽरेणवोऽपांसवः [?] तुविजाता बहुयज्ञेषु प्रादुर्भूता भ्राजदृष्टयो दीप्ता एवंभूताः सन्तो दृळ्हानि चिद्दृढान्यपि पर्वतादीनि अचुच्यवुः । च्यावयन्ति । चालयन्ति ॥

*Gist:* The Maruts, self-yoked, come down from heaven without effort; with the word of praise they urge us; dustless, born in many sacrifices, bright-speared, they shake even firm mountains.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(ete* — these Marut-gods); *svayuktāḥ* — joined to one another (each with his own wealth); *divaḥ* — from the heaven-world; *vṛthā* — without effort; *ava* — downward-faced; *ā yayuḥ* — they come. *(he)* *amartyāḥ* — O immortal Marut-gods (you); *tmanā* — of your own accord; *kaśayā* — (the praise in form of) with the word; *codata* — (like praise) urge us on. *(te)* *marutaḥ* —

### Printed p. 125  (PDF 145)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6".)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 4, continued)* — those Marut-gods: *arenavaḥ* — free of dust; *tuvijātāḥ* — (in many sacrifices) those who appear; *bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ* — brilliant ones (being); *dṛḷhāni cit* — even exceedingly firm mountains and the like — *acucyavuḥ* — they shake.

**Bhāvārtha.** The Marut-gods, joined to one another, come without effort from the heaven-world to this world; O immortal Marut-gods, urge us (as if to praise) by your own speech; the Marut-gods, free from dust, appearing in many sacrifices, brilliant, make even exceedingly firm mountains and the like tremble.

**English Translation (as printed):** Mutually supported, they descend readily form [sic] the sky: immortal Maruts, animate us by your own words (to praise you): exempt from toil, present at many (sacrifices) brilliant-eyed, the Maruts have shaken the firmest mountains.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***svayuktāḥ*** — the Marut-gods are *ekonapañcāśat* in number ("forty-nine persons"). They are described as mutually in friendship, or, taking the word *sva* in the sense of wealth, as joined with wealth: the two senses are given.

***vṛthā ava ā yayuḥ*** — it describes the way they come: from heaven, without effort, face downward, they descend to the sacrificial hall (*yāgaśāle* [?]).

***tmanā kaśayā codata*** — *ātmanā stutirūpayā vācā stotuṃ prerayata*: the word *tmanā* is used in the sense of *ātmanā*, as shown by the example

> तन्नस्तुरीपमद्भुतं पुरु वारं पुरु त्मना । त्वष्टा पोषाय वि ष्यतु रायो नाभा नो अस्मयुः ॥

> *tannasturīpam adbhutaṃ puru vāraṃ puru tmanā | tvaṣṭā poṣāya vi ṣyatu rāyo nābhā no asmayuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142-10 [?]). Here the sense of *tmanā* is *ātmanā*, as explained. The word *kaśā* is read among the names of speech (Ni. 1-11 [?]). The Marut-gods are besought to favour, with words of praise, that they may inspire the order of praising in those who praise them.

### Printed p. 126  (PDF 146)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

***arenavaḥ tuvijātāḥ bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ*** — these words are adjectives of the word *marutaḥ*: the Marut-gods are free of dust, those who appear (in many sacrifices) abundantly, of exceeding brilliance — thus their greatness is described. And that they shake even firm mountains — thus their strength is described.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numerals small, not read)*: *svayuktāḥ* (root *yuj yoge*; *kta* in the passive; *svaiḥ yuktāḥ*, a *tṛtīyā* compound; the first member keeps its accent by "*tṛtīyā karmaṇi*"); *yayuḥ* (root *yā prāpaṇe*; Vedic *liṭ* with present sense, 3rd plural; *nighāta* accent); *codata* (root *cud preraṇe*, *curādi*; *loṭ* 2nd plural, *ta*-substitute; *śap* by *vyatyaya*; *guṇa* of the light penultimate by "*pugantalaghūpadhasya ca*"; *nighāta*); *tmanā* (by "*mantreṣvāṅyādeḥ ātmanaḥ*" the *ā* of *ātman* is dropped after the *tṛtīyā* ending); *arenavaḥ* (*na vidyate reṇuḥ yeṣāṃ te*; accent on the last syllable of the latter member by "*nañsubhyām*"); *acucyavuḥ* (root *cyu gatau*; the causal sense included in the root; Vedic *luṅ*; *parasmaipada* by *vyatyaya*; *śap* replaced; reduplication of the root; *jher jus* by "*sijabhyastavidibhyaśca*"; *guṇa* by "*jusi ca*"; *av* substitution; augment *aṭ*; *nighāta*); *dṛḷhāni* (root *vṛha vṛddhau*; *kta*; *ha* → *ḍha* by "*hoḍhaḥ*"; *ta* → *dha* by "*jhaṣastathordho'dhaḥ*"; *ṣṭutva*; "*ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ*" drops the former *ḍha*; the accent falls on the last syllable by the affix).

### Printed p. 127  (PDF 147)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6". The scan of this page is smudged; the readings below are therefore marked [?] more often.)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 4, concluded; noted briefly)*: *bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ* (root *bhrāja dīptau*; *śatṛ* in place of *laṭ* by *vyatyaya*; the accent of the root stays since the *lasārvadhātuka* ending is unaccented; *ṛṣṭi* from root *ṛṣī gatau*, with the affix *kric* [as read], which yields the form *ṛṣṭi*; in the *bahuvrīhi* the first member keeps its own accent). ‖ 4 ‖

*(ornamental rule)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> को वोऽन्तर्मरुत ऋष्टिविद्युतो रेजति त्मना हन्वेव जिह्वया ।
> धन्वच्युत इषां न यामनि पुरुप्रैषा अहन्यो नैतशः ॥ ५ ॥

> *ko vo 'ntarmaruta ṛṣṭividyuto rejati tmanā hanveva jihvayā |*
> *dhanvacyuta iṣāṃ na yāmani purupraiṣā ahanyo naitaśaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> कः । वः । अन्तः । मरुतः । ऋष्टिऽविद्युतः । रेजति । त्मना । हन्वाऽइव । जिह्वया ।
> धन्वऽच्युतः । इषाम् । न । यामनि । पुरुऽप्रैषाः । अहन्यः । न । एतशः ॥ ५ ॥

> *kaḥ | vaḥ | antaḥ | marutaḥ | ṛṣṭi 'vidyutaḥ | rejati | tmanā | hanvā 'iva | jihvayā |*
> *dhanva 'cyutaḥ | iṣām | na | yāmani | puru 'praiṣāḥ | ahanyaḥ | na | etaśaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः ऋष्टिविद्युतः मेघभेदनायुधविशेषेण विद्योतमानाः युष्माकमन्तर्युष्मासु मध्ये स्थितः कः पुमान् रेजति । चालयति । प्रेरयति । तर्हि कथं चालनमित्युच्यते । त्मना आत्मनैव । चालने दृष्टान्तः । जिह्वया हन्वेव । द्विवचनस्याकारः [?] । हनू इव । तौ यथा जिह्वया चाल्येते तद्वत् । यद्यप्येवं तथापीषामन्नानां तत्साधनानां सस्यानां यामनि प्राप्तौ सम्यक्सिद्ध्यर्थं धन्वच्युतो न [?] । धन्वन्नन्तरिक्षं [?] वचनः [?] । तेन तत्स्थमुदकं लक्ष्यते । उदकेन आविर्भूतो मेघा [?] इव । तेन यथाकाङ्क्षन्ते [?] तथा युष्मानन्नादिप्राप्तये पुरुप्रैषा बहुविधं फलमिच्छन् यजमानः स्तोत्रैर्बहुप्रकारमाकारयतीत्यर्थः [?] । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अहन्योऽश्वो भवत्येतशो नाश्व इव । स यथा शिक्षकेण नानाप्रकारं प्राप्यते तद्वत् [?] ।

*Gist:* Who among you, lightning-armed Maruts, moves you? You move of yourselves, like the jaws moved by the tongue; for food and crops, the sacrificer, as one trains a horse daily, urges you in many ways with praise.

**Pratipadārtha.** *ṛṣṭividyutaḥ* — the ones shining as if with a special weapon that splits clouds; *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *vaḥ* — your; *antaḥ* — among (you) (standing); *kaḥ* — who; *hanvā* — the two jaws

### Printed p. 128  (PDF 148)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

— *jihvayā iva* — as the tongue moves (them); *tmanā* — by yourselves; *rejati* — makes (you) move? — *(tathāpi* — nevertheless*)* *iṣām* — of foods (of crops, the means of food); *yāmani* — for attainment (prosperity); *dhanvacyutaḥ na* — like clouds that pour out the water present in the sky [?]; *(vaḥ* — you*)*; *ahanyaḥ* — on every day too; *etaśaḥ na* — like a horse made to move in many ways by a trainer; *puruprraiṣāḥ* — (the sacrificer, desiring many fruits) by praises urges you in many ways.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, shining as if with a weapon that splits clouds — who is it that would make you move, as the tongue makes the two jaws move, when you are yourselves in your midst? Even so, as a trainer, at the time of exercise, turns a horse about in many ways, and as clouds are needed by crops, so the sacrificer makes you, who are needed for the many kinds of fruits of the sacrifice, favourable to himself with his hymns of praise.

**English Translation (as printed):** Maruts, lightning-armed, who, (standing) amongst you, sets you of yourselves in motion, as the jaws are (set in motion) by the tongue: as falling rains (are essential) for the obtaining of food, so (those, desirous of sustenance), excite you in various ways, like a horse in (his) daily (training).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***ṛṣṭi vidyutaḥ*** — *meghabhedanāyudhaviśeṣeṇa vidyotamānāḥ*: the word *ṛṣṭi* conveys a special weapon. By this weapon the Marut-gods shine. The question, "who sets them in motion in the work of splitting the cloud?", is asked by the sentence *ko rejati*; and to answer it, and to remove the impossibility of a motion-action, the reply *tmanā* ("of themselves") is given. Rain does not result merely from the Marut-gods' wearing the weapon and shining; as the action of splitting the cloud is brought about, there is no one else to urge them, so the meaning is described that they themselves split the cloud with their weapon.

***jihvayā hanveva*** — as the tongue (*jihvā*) moves the two jaws. It is compared thus: as, when the Marut-gods, set in motion by themselves, split the cloud, the movement-action arises, the impelling cause is born from the Marut-gods themselves; in this matter, as the movement of the jaws arises of itself from the movement-action of the tongue, it is said by way of a further illustration (*dṛṣṭāntara*).

### Printed p. 129  (PDF 149)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 5 continue. A stray "XIII 9" is printed at the foot, a signature mark.)*

***iṣāṃ yāmani dhanvacyuto na*** — *annānāṃ tatsādhanānāṃ sasyānāṃ prāptau samṛddhyarthaṃ udakasrāviṇo meghā iva*: the word *dhanvan* is read among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 1-10 [?]), and in Yāska's text:

> यः परस्याः परावतस्तिरो धन्वाति रोचते । स नः पर्षदति द्विषः ॥

> *yaḥ parasyāḥ parāvatas tiro dhanvāti rocate | sa naḥ parṣad ati dviṣaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-187-2 [?]). In this ṛk the word *dhanvan* is explained by Yāska as "*dhanvāntarikṣaṃ dhanvanty asmād āpaḥ*" [as read]. Sāyaṇa says, "*dhanvan śabdo'ntarikṣavacanaḥ | tena tatsthamudakaṃ lakṣyate*": the word *dhanvan* denotes the atmosphere, but here, by the word, the sense "the water that is in the atmosphere" is stated. As people desire the necessity of clouds that pour water for the production of the crops that are the cause of food and the like, so the sacrificer, with abundant praise, desires the coming of the Marut-gods. This is described.

***ahanyaḥ etaśo na*** — by this sentence, as a horse every day comes under the trainer's command and learns many kinds of gaits, so the comings of the Marut-gods too are of many kinds: this is the sense illustrated by the comparison.

***etaśaḥ*** — this word is read among the names of the horse (Ni. 1-[?]).

***puruprraiṣāḥ — bahuvidhaṃ phalamicchan*** — the sacrificer who desires many kinds of benefits: this sense is explained for the word. The analysis of the compound is given: *puruprraiṣaḥ stotraṃ yasya* (he whose praise is of many kinds). The sacrificer, praising with many kinds of hymns, desires food and the like through the various comings of the Marut-gods.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *ṛṣṭividyutaḥ* (*ṛṣṭyā vidyotante*; vocative plural form; accent of a vocative-governed word by "*ānantritasya ca*" [as read]); *rejati* (root *reja kampane*, causal sense included; *laṭ* 3rd singular; not accentless at the start of a *pāda*; the root accent remains because *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented); *hanvā* (stem *hanu*, dual; before *jas* the dual ending is replaced by *ā* by "*supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇa…*", Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]; *yaṇ* substitution); *dhanvacyutaḥ* (root *cyutir kṣaraṇe*; *kvip*; *dhanvānaṃ cyotayanti*; the latter member keeps its accent as a *kṛdutara-pada*).

*(ornamental rule)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> क्व स्विदस्य रजसो महस्परं क्वावरं मरुतो यस्मिन्नाययु ।
> यच्च्यावयथ विथुरेव संहितं व्यद्रिणा पतथ त्वेषमर्णवम् ॥ ६ ॥

> *kva svidasya rajaso mahasparaṃ kvāvaraṃ maruto yasminnāyayu |*
> *yaccyāvayatha vithureva saṃhitaṃ vyadriṇā patatha tveṣamarṇavam ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> क्व । स्वित् । अस्य । रजसः । महः । परम् । क्व । अवरम् । मरुतः । यस्मिन् । आऽययु [?] ।
> यत् । च्यावयथ । विथुराऽइव । सम्ऽहितम् । वि । अद्रिणा । पतथ । त्वेषम् । अर्णवम् ॥ ६ ॥

> *kva | svit | asya | rajasaḥ | mahaḥ | param | kva | avaram | marutaḥ | yasmin | ā 'yayu [?] |*
> *yat | cyāvayatha | vithurā 'iva | sam 'hitam | vi | adriṇā | patatha | tveṣam | arṇavam ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः यूयं यस्मिन्नुदकनिमित्तभूते सत्यायुधे [?] आगच्छत अस्य रजसो वृष्ट्युदकस्य लोकस्य वा महो महतः परं पारमन्तं क्व स्वित् । कुत्रास्तीति । नास्तीत्यर्थः । तथावरमवाञ्चागादिश्च [?] क्व स्वित् । कुत्रास्ति । आद्यन्तं न कोऽपि जानातीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । यूयं विथुरेव विथुराणि शिथिलानि तृणानीव संहितमेकीभूतमुदकं च्यावयथ स्वस्थानाच्चालयथ तदा [?] अद्रिणा वज्रेण त्वेषं दीप्तमर्णवमुदकवन्तं मेघं वि पतथ । विशीर्णं पातयथ ॥

*Gist:* Where is the farther end, where the nearer, of this great region (of waters) to which you come? When you shake loose the gathered water like scattered straws, you split the bright cloud with the thunderbolt.

### Printed p. 131  (PDF 151)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6".)*

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods (you); *yasmin* — for what water-purpose; *āyayu* [as printed] — you come; *asya* — of this; *mahaḥ* — immense (boundless); *rajasaḥ* — of the water (of the world); *param* — the end; *kva svit* — where is it?; *(tathā* — likewise*)* *avaram* — (its) beginning; *kva* — where?; *yat* — when (you); *saṃhitam* — the water gathered together into one; *vithurā iva* — like loose (scattering) grass (as one disperses it); *cyāvayatha* — you shake; *(tat* — then*)* *adriṇā* — with the thunderbolt-weapon; *tveṣam* — brilliant; *arṇavam* — the water-possessing cloud; *vi patatha* — you cause to fall down.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, for the sake of what water do you come? What are its beginning and end? You make the water collected in one place, and the water-bearing clouds, burst with the thunderbolt-weapon and cause them to fall down.

**English Translation (as printed):** Where, Maruts, is the limit of the vast region (whence you come [the scan reads "whenee … eome"]): where is the beginning of that to which you proceed: when you scatter the dense vapour like light grass, and hurl down the brilliant rain-cloud by the thunderbolt.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***asya rajasaḥ mahaḥ paraṃ kva svit*** — *vṛṣṭyudakasya lokasya vā mahataḥ pāraṃ antaṃ kutrāsti*: the word *rajas* is read among the names of night (Ni. 1-[?]). Yāska, explaining that the word *rajas* is formed from the root *raj* (*rañj*) with the sense of colouring, explains it as "*rajo rajateḥ jyotiḥ rajaḥ ucyate*" [as read]: since light pervades all things with its own radiance, light is called *rajas*; and "*udakaṃ rajaḥ ucyate; lokāḥ rajāṃsi ucyante*": water and the worlds are also called *rajas*, since the word is meaningful for them (Ni. 4-[?]); he cites usages that convey this sense, as in

> अब्जामुक्थैरहिं गृणीषे बुध्ने नदीनां रजस्सु सीदन् ॥

> *abjām ukthair ahiṃ gṛṇīṣe budhne nadīnāṃ rajassu sīdan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?]). Here the word *rajassu* is explained as meaning *udake* ("in the waters").

### Printed p. 132  (PDF 152)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

> एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमञ्जते ॥

> *etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketum akrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānum añjate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1 [?]). Here *rajasaḥ* is said to mean *antarikṣalokasya* ("of the world of the atmosphere"). Sāyaṇa, addressing the Marut-gods, explains that they come to bestow the waters on the world. Having asked where is the end of the greatness (the limit) of the waters and the worlds, he explains that, since that is not directly perceived, it is boundless [reading of the Kannada partly doubtful]. In the same way, asking by means of a question, "where is *avaram avāg bhāgaḥ ādiśca kva svit*, the beginning, the lower part?" of the waters, he explains "*na ko'pi jānāti*": no one knows the beginning and end of the waters.

***vithureva saṃhitaṃ cyāvayatha*** — *śithilāni tṛṇānīva ekībhūtam udakaṃ svasthānāt cālayatha*: as one makes loose grass move, the Marut-gods make the condensed waters move from their place; *arṇavaṃ vi patetha udakavantaṃ meghaṃ viśīrṇaṃ pātayatha*: splitting the cloud that holds the water with the thunderbolt-weapon, you make the rain fall. Thus the extraordinary power of the Marut-gods is described here.

***adriṇā*** — the word *adri* is read among the names of *vajra* (Ni. 2-[?]); the meaning "thunderbolt-weapon" is explained.

***tveṣam — dīptam*** — this word is explained as used by Yāska in the sense of "radiant":

> त्वेषमित्था समरणं शिमीवतोरिन्द्राविष्णू सुतपा वामुरुष्यति ।

> *tveṣam itthā samaraṇaṃ śimīvator indrāviṣṇū sutapā vām uruṣyati |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-155-2 [?]). Here the word *tveṣam* is explained as meaning "possessing brilliance".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly; sūtra numerals small, not read)*: *āyayu* (root *yā prāpaṇe*; Vedic *liṭ*; the substitute *a* for the 2nd-person plural ending [as printed]; reduplication; the affix is *kit* by "*asaṃyogāl liṭ kit*"; the root-final *ā* dropped by "*ātolopa iṭi ca*"; because of *yat* (*yadyoga*) there is no *nighāta* accent; the affix accent makes it final-acuted; the preverb *ā* loses its accent by "*tiṅ codāttavati*" [as read]); *cyāvayatha* (root *cyu(j?) gatau* [as printed]; *ṇic* by "*hetumati ca*"; *vṛddhi* by "*aco ñṇiti*"; *āv* substitution; *laṭ* 2nd plural; because of *yat* no *nighāta*; the accent of *ṇic* remains).

*(ornamental rule)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सातिर्न वोऽमवती स्वर्वती त्वेषा विपाका मरुतः पिपिष्वती ।
> भद्रा वो रातिः पृणतो न दक्षिणा पृथुज्रया [?] असुर्येव जञ्जती ॥ ७ ॥

> *sātirna vo 'mavatī svarvatī tveṣā vipākā marutaḥ pipiṣvatī |*
> *bhadrā vo rātiḥ pṛṇato na dakṣiṇā pṛthujrayā [?] asuryeva jañjatī ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सातिः । न । वः । अमऽवती । स्वःऽवती । त्वेषा । विऽपाका । मरुतः । पिपिष्वती ।
> भद्रा । वः । रातिः । पृणतः । न । दक्षिणा । पृथुऽज्रयी [?] । असुर्याऽइव । जंजती ॥ ७ ॥

> *sātiḥ | na | vaḥ | ama 'vatī | svaḥ 'vatī | tveṣā | vi 'pākā | marutaḥ | pipiṣvatī |*
> *bhadrā | vaḥ | rātiḥ | pṛṇataḥ | na | dakṣiṇā | pṛthu 'jrayī [?] | asuryā 'iva | jaṃjatī ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः वो युष्माकं सम्बन्धिनी सातिर्न सम्भक्तिरिव युष्मत्संभजनं यथा प्रशस्तगुणं तद्वत् । वो रात्रिवृष्ट्याख्या दिविषयोमवत्कमात्यवतीन्द्रातिसहायवती [?] । यथा राजेवामवान् । ऋ. ४-४-१ [?] । इत्यत्र त्रामश्चब्दोऽमात्यवचनः [?] तद्वत् । यद्वा । वः सातिः सम्भक्तिरमवती । रोगवती न भवति । किंतु स्वर्वती सुखवती त्वेषा दीप्ता विपाका परिपक्वफला पिपिष्वती प्रेषणवती कृषीवलैः कर्षणवती । वृष्टौ सत्यां कर्षन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् । स्वविरोधिपेषणवती वा । भद्रा भन्दनीया सुत्या [?] । किंच पृणतो धातुर्धनिकस्य दक्षिणा न दक्षिणेव तद्वत् स्वर्वती [?] पृथुज्रयी पृथुजवा शीघ्रगामिनी । किंचासुर्येवासुरस्य स्वभूता जंजती सर्वानभिभवन्ती शक्तिरिव । सा यथान्येभ्योऽपहृत्यान्यस्मै दातुं समर्था तद्वदियमपि मेघस्थमुदकमपहृत्य जगतो दातुं शक्तेत्यर्थः । ईदृशी रातिरस्मभ्यमस्त्विति भावः ॥

*Gist:* Your giving (of rain) is like a splendid gift: mighty, heaven-bringing, bright, ripening, bountiful like a rich man's fee, swift, and like the all-overcoming Asura power.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *vaḥ* — your; *sātiḥ na* — like (your) coming (as if praised); *rātiḥ* — (your) gift of rain and the like; *amavatī* — accompanied by Indra and others as companions, praised; *vaḥ* — your; *sātiḥ* — coming; *na amavatī* — not diseased (not afflicted); *(kiṃtu* — but*)* *svarvatī* — endowed with happiness (heaven); *tveṣā* — brilliant; *vipākā* — bearing ripened fruit; *pipiṣvatī* — favourable to farmers; *bhadrā* — auspicious; *pṛṇataḥ* — of a giver, a wealthy man; *dakṣiṇā na* — like a *dakṣiṇā* (bringing prosperity); *pṛthujrayī* — swift-moving (giving fruit quickly); *(ca)* *asuryā* [as printed: *asuryor*] — related to the Asuras; *jaṃjatī* — like a power overcoming all, being otherwise too; *rātiḥ* — (such) giving (be obtained by us).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, the rain that you shower with the help of Indra is, like your coming, a means of the happiness of heaven, brilliant, bearing ripened fruit, favourable to farmers, auspicious, prosperity-giving like the *dakṣiṇā* of a wealthy man, bearing fruit in very short time, and, like the Asuri power, overcoming everything (so that it can be given by one, quickly). May such a gift of yours be ours.

**English Translation (as printed):** Like your possession of treasure, Maruts, is your liberality: ministeral [sic] (of Indra's bounty), heaven-bestowing, brilliant, fruitful, favowable [sic] to the husbandman, propitions [sic]: it is like the donation of a wealthy (donor), prompt (of distribution), and like the all-subduing force of the Asuras.

### Printed p. 135  (PDF 155)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6".)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***vaḥ sātirna vaḥ rātiḥ amavatī*** — *yuṣmākaṃ sambandhinī sambhaktiriva yuṣmatsaṃbhajanaṃ yathā prasastaguṇaṃ tadvat vṛṣṭyādiviṣayā amātyavatī indrādisahāyavatī | yadvā vaḥ sātiḥ saṃvibhaktiḥ na amavatī rogavatī na bhavati*: the word *sāti* is explained as meaning "service"; the word *rāti* is said to mean "gift". The word *amavatī* is explained by the Nirukta-writers as meaning *āmātya* ("a minister").

> कृणुष्व पाजः प्रसितिं न पृथ्वीं याहि राजेवामवाँ इभेन ।
> तृष्वीमनु प्रसितिं द्रूणानोऽस्तासि विध्य रक्षसस्तपिष्ठैः ॥

> *kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ prasitiṃ na pṛthvīṃ yāhi rājevāmavāṃ ibhena |*
> *tṛṣvīm anu prasitiṃ drūṇāno'stāsi vidhya rakṣasas tapiṣṭhaiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4-1). In this ṛk, for the word *amavān* (*rājeva*), the sense "*āmātyavān abhyamanavān*" is stated [as read]. Durgācārya explains it as: the king who sets out to win victory together with a minister who knows policy (*nīti*); or, alternatively, "*abhyamanavān — rogabhūtaḥ parebhyo bhayadātā*": as a disease causes fear to others, one who causes fear to enemies. In this passage Sāyaṇa supports both senses.

The coming of the Marut-gods is like their abundant and excellent qualities; the rain-giving that the Marut-gods perform is, he says, with the help of Indra, and so the king is compared: as the king goes, together with a minister who knows policy, and with strength gathered by his helpers, to conquer his enemies, so the Marut-gods, when they give rain, keep Indra himself as their *amātya* (helper). This is one kind of meaning.

In the second meaning, the giving of rain by the Marut-gods, like a disease to a king's enemies, is fear-causing, and it is described as not causing fear to others. Of the two meanings of the word *amavatī*, one agrees with the comparison to the king and the other does not.

Sāyaṇa also gives here another kind of meaning: among these there is implied a *vyatireka* (contrast) concerning the king. The king's coming is full of fear; in the coming of the Marut-gods there is never any occasion for the fear of disease. Though this contrast is indicated, the superiority over the king's coming is stated by the other epithets.

### Printed p. 136  (PDF 156)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

***svarvatī*** — the coming of the Marut-gods, which always produces happiness; ***tveṣā*** — which is brilliant; ***vipākā*** — which produces excellent fruits; ***pipiṣvatī*** — which, by farmers, ploughs the earth for the increase of the crops and destroys enemies; ***bhadrā*** — which is worthy of praise: thus it is described.

***pṛṇataḥ dakṣiṇā na*** — *dātur dhanikasya dakṣiṇeva samṛddhikarī*: the word *pṛṇataḥ* is explained, following the Nirukta, in the sense of "filling", as in

> तमूर्मिरं न पृणता यवेन [?]

> *tam ūrmiraṃ na pṛṇatā yavena [?]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-11 [?]), where *yavena pūrayati* is taken in the sense of filling. Here it is explained as "wealthy, filled with wealth". As the wealth given by a rich man as *dakṣiṇā* produces prosperity, so the prosperity brought about by the coming of the Marut-gods is shown by this comparison.

***asuryeva jañjatī*** — *asurasya svabhūtā sarvānabhibhavantī śaktiriva*: for the word *asuryā* the sense "related to the Asuras" is explained. The word *asura* is read among the names of cloud (Ni. 2-[?]) and, as "*asorasurānām asṛjata tad asurāṇām asuratvam iti vijñāyate*" [as read] (Ni. 3-[?]), it is explained. Durgācārya says: "*asuraḥ asuratāḥ sthāneṣu*" — those not firmly settled in their own places are *asuras*; or "*āsyāḥ sthānebhyaḥ*" — those driven by the gods from their places.

The power of these Asuras is all-overcoming. And "*anyebhyo apahṛtya anyasmai dātuṃ samarthā*" — to take another's property or wealth from him and to be able to give it to somebody else: thus Sāyaṇa explains the nature of the Asura power. In the same way, the power of the Marut-gods, "*meghasthamudakam apahṛtya jagataḥ dātuṃ samarthā*" — taking the water that is in the clouds, being able to give it to the world — it is described that they are ready to give it as rain.

Here, "*yuṣmākaṃ sambandhinī sātiḥ yathā prasastaguṇaṃ tadvat vaḥ rātiḥ*" — in addressing the Marut-gods, it is said as a comparison that "as your coming has praiseworthy qualities, so your gift is of the nature of rain, which you grant"; by this it is indicated that all the other epithets about *sāti* are related to *rāti* as well. And "*īdṛśī rātiḥ asmabhyam astu*" — "may such a gift of yours be for us who perform sacrifices": thus the prayer is made.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *sātiḥ* (by "*ūtiyūtijūti…*", Pā. Sū. 3-3-97 [?], the affix *ktin* is given as irregular, with the acute accent).

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6"; grammar of Ṛk 7 concluded.)*

*(Grammar, noted briefly)*: *amavatī* (*amaḥ asyā asti*; affix *matup*; *m* → *v* by "*mādupadhāyāśca…*" [as read]; *ṅīp* in the feminine because of the *u* marker); *svarvatī* (as before, *matup*, *va*, *ṅīp*; the affix being *pit* it is unaccented; *svar* becomes *svarita* by the Phiṭ-sūtra "*nyaṅ svarau svaritau*", [number printed, read as 65 [?]]); *rātiḥ* (root *rā ādāne*; affix *ktin*; the affix takes the acute by "*mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanaviḍāvanarakṣaśāḥ…*" [as read; Pā. Sū. 3-3-96 [?]]); *pṛṇataḥ* (root *pṛṇa prīṇane*; *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; the genitive ending after *śatṛ* without *num* takes the acute by "*śatuḥ anumo nadyajādī*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-173 [?]); *asuryā* (*asurasya iyam*; affix *yat* in the sense of relation; loss of *a* by "*yasyeti ca*"; *svarita* by "*tit svaritam*"; *ṭāp* in the feminine). ‖ 7 ‖

*(ornamental rule)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्रति ष्टोभन्ति सिन्धवः पविभ्यो यदभ्रियां वाचमुदीरयन्ति ।
> अव स्मयन्त विद्युतः पृथिव्यां यदी घृतं मरुतः प्रुष्ण्वन्ति ॥ ८ ॥

> *prati ṣṭobhanti sindhavaḥ pavibhyo yadabhriyāṃ vācamudīrayanti |*
> *ava smayanta vidyutaḥ pṛthivyāṃ yadī ghṛtaṃ marutaḥ pruṣṇvanti ‖ 8 ‖*

*(The Saṃhitā reads *ṣṭobhanti* and *pruṣṇvanti* as printed; the second is split across the line as "प्रुष्ण्-वन्ति".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्रति । ष्टोभन्ति । सिन्धवः । पविऽभ्यः । यत् । अभ्रियाम् । वाचम् । उत्ऽईरयन्ति ।
> अव । स्मयन्त । विऽद्युतः । पृथिव्याम् । यदि । घृतम् । मरुतः । प्रुष्ण्वन्ति ॥ ८ ॥

> *prati | ṣṭobhanti | sindhavaḥ | pavi 'bhyaḥ | yat | abhriyām | vācam | ut 'īrayanti |*
> *ava | smayanta | vi 'dyutaḥ | pṛthivyām | yadi | ghṛtam | marutaḥ | pruṣṇvanti ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> पविभ्यो मरुत्संबन्धिवज्रेभ्यः सिन्धवः स्यन्दनशीला आपः प्रति ष्टोभन्ति । प्रतिचलन्ति । कदा । यद्यदाभ्रियां मेघभवां वाचं शब्दं स्तनितलक्षणमुदीरयन्ति उच्चारयन्ति वज्राणि । किंच विद्युतो विद्योतमानास्तडितः पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे । पृथिवीत्यन्तरिक्षनाम । पृथिवी भूरिति तन्नामसूक्तत्वात् [?] । तत्रावस्मयन्ते । स्मयन्ते । अवाङ्मुखं प्रकाशन्ते । पृथिव्यामित्येतदुत्तरत्र वा योज्यम् । यदि यदा पृथिव्यां भूम्यां घृतं क्षरदुदकं मरुतः प्रुष्णवन्ति [?] प्रुष्णन्ति सिञ्चन्ति । प्रुषेः क्र्यादिकस्य व्यत्ययेन श्नुः । यद्येवं तदेत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* When the Marut-thunderbolts utter the cloud's voice, the waters rush forth; the lightnings smile downward in the sky when the Maruts sprinkle rain on the earth.

### Printed p. 138  (PDF 158)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168". The bhāṣya of Ṛk 8 ends at the top.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** *yat* — when; *(vajrāṇi* — the thunderbolt-weapons*)* *abhriyām* — that is in the clouds; *vācam* — (the sound in the form of a thunder-rumble) voice; *ut īrayanti* — they send forth; *(tat* — then*)* *sindhavaḥ* — waters of flowing nature; *pavibhyaḥ* — by the thunderbolt-weapons of the Maruts; *prati ṣṭobhanti* — they start forth; *(kiṃca* — and*)* *yadi* — when; *pṛthivyām* — on the earth; *ghṛtam* — water; *marutaḥ* — the Marut-gods; *pruṣṇvanti* — are those who sprinkle; *(tadā* — then*)* *vidyutaḥ* — flashing lightnings; *(pṛthivyām* — in the atmosphere*)* *ava smayante* — they smile downward (shine).

**Bhāvārtha.** While the clouds are thundering, the waters are sent forth by the thunderbolt-weapons (belonging to the Maruts); thus, while the Marut-gods sprinkle water on the earth, lightning shines in the sky.

**English Translation (as printed):** The rivers are arrested by the thunderbolts when they utter the voice of the clouds; but the lightnings smile in the firmament when the Maruts sprinkle water on the earth.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***abhriyāṃ vācaṃ udīrayanti*** — *abhrabhavāṃ stanitalakṣaṇāṃ vācaṃ śabdam uccārayanti*: the thunderbolt-weapons, in the clouds, produce the sound of thunder; the lightnings, as they shine downward in the sky, are as if the Marut-gods drew forth the waters in the earth. Then ***sindhavaḥ prati ṣṭobhanti*** — *syandanaśīlāḥ āpaḥ praticalanti*: the waters, of flowing nature, flow over the earth and in the atmosphere as well: this is the meaning explained — that is, the rain-water fallen in the form of a downpour falls on the earth and flows.

### Printed p. 139  (PDF 159)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 8 continue.)*

***pavibhyaḥ*** — *marutsaṃbandhi vajrebhyaḥ*: the word *pavi* is read among the names of speech (Ni. 1-[?]) and also among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 2-[?]). Yāska explains it as "*pavī rathanemirbhavati yadvipunāti bhūmim*": the sound produced by the rim of a chariot wheel as it cleaves (*vipunāti*) the earth is well known as *pavi*; and he gives as example the ṛk

> उत स्मा ते परुष्ण्यामूर्णा वसते शुन्ध्यवः । उत पव्या रथानामद्रिं [?] भिन्दन्त्योजसा ॥

> *uta smā te paruṣṇyām ūrṇā vasate śundhyavaḥ | uta pavyā rathānām adriṃ [?] bhindanty ojasā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-52-9 [?]). In this ṛk they explain *pavi* as "the rim of a chariot wheel". Durgācārya says: "*devā vai vṛtrasya marmaṇi nāvindan taṃ marutaḥ kṣuradhārapavinā vyayuḥ*" [as read] — when the gods did not find Vṛtra's vital spot, the Marut-gods cut him open with the razor-edged rims of their wheels, which are the colour of the tawny (*haritavarṇa*) edges, like thunderbolt-weapons; that is, the Maruts split the cloud with the sharp edges (*pavi*) of their chariots. Sāyaṇa adopts this meaning in his commentary and, in the sentence *pavibhyaḥ sindhavaḥ prati ṣṭobhanti*, explains "*marutsaṃbandhi vajrebhyaḥ*" as meaning the rims of the chariot wheels belonging to the Marut-gods (the streams of rain).

***sindhavaḥ*** — *syandanaśīlāḥ āpaḥ*: the word *sindhu* is read among the names of rivers (Ni. 1-[?]); and

> सुदेवो असि वरुण यस्य ते सप्त सिन्धवः । अनुक्षरन्ति काकुदं सूर्म्यं सुषिरामिव ॥

> *sudevo asi varuṇa yasya te sapta sindhavaḥ | anukṣaranti kākudaṃ sūrmyaṃ suṣirām iva ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-41-2 [?]). In this ṛk it is explained that, since the water flows (*sravaṇāt*), *sindhu* is well known as the name of water.

***pṛthivyām*** — *antarikṣe, bhūmyām*: the word *pṛthivī* is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 1-[?]) and among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 1-[?]). Here the two senses (atmosphere, earth) are explained.

***ghṛtam*** — *kṣaradudakam*: the word *ghṛta* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]), and

> कृष्णं नियानं हरयः सुपर्णा अपो वसाना दिवमुत्पतन्ति ।
> त आववृत्रन्त्सदनादृतस्यादिद्घृतेन पृथिवी व्युद्यते ॥

> *kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ harayaḥ suparṇā apo vasānā divam utpatanti |*
> *ta āvavṛtrant sadanād ṛtasyād id ghṛtena pṛthivī vy udyate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-47).

### Printed p. 140  (PDF 160)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

In this ṛk the word *ghṛtena* is given the sense "by water". "*ghṛtam ity udakanāma jigharteḥ secanakarmaṇaḥ*": the word *ghṛta*, formed from the root *ghṛ* with the sense of sprinkling, is described by Yāska as meaning water.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *ṣṭobhanti* (root *ṣṭubhu stambhe*; the *parasmaipada* by *vyatyaya*; *laṭ* 3rd person plural form; since the preverb *prati* stands before it, the root-initial *s* becomes *ṣ* by "*upasargāt sunoti…*", Pā. Sū. 8-3-65 [?]; *nighāta* accent of the verb); *pavibhyaḥ* (root *pūñ pavane*; affix *i* by an Uṇādi sūtra, "*aci iḥ*" [as read]; *guṇa* and *av* before it; accent by the affix); *abhriyām* (*abhre bhavā abhriyā*; affix *gha* by "*samudrābhrād ghaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 4-4-118 [?]; the *iya* substitute by "*āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ…*"; loss of *a* by "*yasyeti ca*"; the affix takes the acute on the first syllable; *ṭāp* in the feminine, the stem ending in *a*); *udīrayanti* (root *īra gatau preraṇe ca*; *ṇic* by "*hetumati ca*"; *laṭ* 3rd plural after the *ṇijanta*; because of *yat* no *nighāta*; the accent of *ṇic* remains; the preverb *ut* takes *nighāta* by "*tiṅ codāttavati*"); *smayante* (root *ṣmiṅ īṣaddhasane*; Vedic *laṅ* in the sense of present time [as read]; 3rd plural middle; the augment *aṭ* does not occur by "*bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyogepi*"; *nighāta* accent); *yadi* (long vowel in the Saṃhitā by "*nipātasya ca*", Pā. Sū. 6-3-136 [?], hence *yadī*); *pruṣṇvanti* (root *pruṣa snehanasevanapūraṇeṣu*, *kryādi*; *laṭ* 3rd plural, *jhi* → *anta*; *śnu* by "*vyatyayo bahulam*"; *guṇa* does not occur because the affixes are *jit*-type; *uvaṅ* substitute by "*aci śnudhātu…*"; since *yadi* is connected, no *nighāta* by "*nipātair yadyadihantakuvinnetracetcaṇkaccid yatra yuktam*", Pā. Sū. 8-1-30 [?]; accent on the first syllable of the affix). ‖ 8 ‖

### Printed p. 141  (PDF 161)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> असूत पृश्निर्महते रणाय त्वेषमयासां मरुतामनीकम् ।
> ते सप्सरासोऽजनयन्ताभ्वमादित्स्वधामिषिरां पर्यपश्यन् ॥ ९ ॥

> *asūta pṛśnirmahate raṇāya tveṣamayāsāṃ marutāmanīkam |*
> *te sapsarāso 'janayantābhvamāditsvadhāmiṣirāṃ paryapaśyan ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> असूत । पृश्निः । महते । रणाय । त्वेषम् । अयासाम् । मरुताम् । अनीकम् ।
> ते । सप्सरासः । अजनयन्त । अभ्वम् । आत् । इत् । स्वधाम् । इषिराम् । परि । अपश्यन् ॥ ९ ॥

> *asūta | pṛśniḥ | mahate | raṇāya | tveṣam | ayāsām | marutām | anīkam |*
> *te | sapsarāsaḥ | ajanayanta | abhvam | āt | it | svadhām | iṣirām | pari | apaśyan ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> पृश्निर्मरुन्माता नानावर्णा । पृश्न्यै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः । तै. सं. २-२-११-४ [?] । पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासः । ऋ. ५-५२-१६ [?] । इत्यादिश्रुतेः । तामेवान्तरिक्षदेवतां केचिदाहुः । सा देवी त्वेषं दीप्तमयासां गन्तॄणां मरुतामनीकं समूहमेकोनपञ्चाशत्संख्याकमसूत । उत्पादितवती । किमर्थम् । महते रणाय संग्रामाय । मेघजयायेत्यर्थः । ते च मरुतः सप्सरासः समानरूपा हिंसका वा मेघानामभ्वं मेघं जनयन्ति । उत्पादितवन्तः । आदिदनन्तरमेवेषिरां सर्वैरेष्टव्यां स्वधामन्नं सस्यादिसमृद्धिलक्षणं पर्यपश्यन् । परिपश्यन्ति सर्वे जनाः ॥

*Gist:* Pṛśni bore the brilliant host of the swift Maruts for the great fight with the cloud; they brought forth the cloud, and at once all people saw the longed-for food.

**Pratipadārtha.** *pṛśniḥ* — the many-coloured sky (the deity named Pṛśni); *tveṣam* — brilliant; *ayāsām* — of those who are of moving nature; *marutām* — of the Marut-gods; *anīkam* — the host; *mahate raṇāya* — (in the form of victory over the clouds) for a great battle; *asūta* — gave birth to; *sapsarāsaḥ* — of equal form, or the destroyers of the clouds; *te* — those Marut-gods; *abhvam* — the cloud; *ajanayanta* — created; *āt it* — immediately after; *iṣirām* — desired by all; *svadhām* — (in the form of crops and the like) food; *pari apaśyan* — (people) saw.

**Bhāvārtha.** After the many-coloured sky (or the deity named Pṛśni) had given birth to the brilliant host of the Marut-gods for a great battle, in the form of victory over the clouds, the cloud was created by those Marut-gods. Immediately after, (people) saw the prosperity of crops and the like.

### Printed p. 142  (PDF 162)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

**English Translation (as printed):** Prishni bore the brilliant troop of the quick-moving Maruts for the great combat (with the clouds), whercupon [sic] (mankind) immediately beheld the desiderated food.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***pṛśniḥ*** — *marunmātā nānāvarṇā | tām evāntarikṣadevatāṃ kecid āhuḥ*: the word *pṛśni* is read among the names "*svaḥ, nākaḥ*" of the atmosphere and among the common names of the Āditya (Ni. 2-[?]), and "*pṛśnirādityo bhavati prāśnute enaṃ varṇa iti nairuktāḥ*" (Ni. 2-[?]) — "abundant colour spreads over him exceedingly, thus the Āditya is *Pṛśni*", so Yāska explains. The deity *Pṛśni* is, in one explanation, the mother of the Marut-gods, one of many colours; some say that she is the very deity of the atmosphere. On the point of *Pṛśni* being the mother of the Marut-gods, Sāyaṇa cites the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence "*pṛśnyai vai payaso maruto jātāḥ*" (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-4 [?]) and the Ṛk Saṃhitā sentence "*pṛśneḥ putrāḥ upamāsaḥ*" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-52-16 [?]).

***sā devī tveṣam ayāsām marutām anīkam asūta*** — it is explained that the goddess *Pṛśni*, brilliant and of moving nature, gave birth to the host of the Marut-gods, forty-nine in number (49 persons); *mahate raṇāya saṃgrāmāya meghajayāya* — it is described that these Marut-gods, fighting with the clouds, should be victorious.

***sapsarāsaḥ abhvam*** — *samānarūpā hiṃsakā vā meghānām | meghaṃ janayanti utpādayantaḥ*: all the Marut-gods have an identical form, and they harm the clouds: thus the meaning of the word *sapsarāsaḥ* is explained. The word *abhva* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]) and among the names of great things (Ni. 3-[?]). Here, the meaning "cloud" is given to this word, and it is said that the Marut-gods produce the cloud.

***ādit iṣirāṃ svadhāṃ paryapaśyan*** — *anantarameva sarvairaṣṭavyāṃ annaṃ sasyādisamṛddhilakṣaṇaṃ paripaśyanti sarve janāḥ*: immediately after the Marut-gods have produced the cloud, all the people of the world know that the desired food, in the form of the growth of crops and the like, is going to arise.

### Printed p. 143  (PDF 163)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 9 conclude.)*

***svadhā*** — the word *svadhā* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]) and among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?]); and *svadhe* is stated among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-[?]). Here it is used in the sense of food that arises from crops and the like (in forms).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *asūta* (root *sūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane*; *laṅ* 3rd singular; no *nighāta* since it stands at the beginning of a *pāda*; the augment *aṭ* being acute, the word is accented on the first syllable); *ayāsām* (root *aya gatau*; *ayante iti ayāḥ teṣām*; since it is included among the *pacādi* roots, the affix *ac* by "*nandigrahipacādibhyaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 3-1-134 [?]; the augment *suṭ* before the genitive plural ending by *vyatyaya*); *anīkam* (root *ana prāṇane*; affix *īkan* by an Uṇādi sūtra, "*anihṛṣibhyāṃ …*" [as read]; first-syllable acute by "*ñityādirnityam*"); *sapsarāsaḥ* (root *psā bhakṣaṇe*; *psāti bhakṣayati iti psaraḥ*, form; Uṇādi affix *ḍara*; because of the *ḍ* marker the final (*ā*) of the root is dropped; *samānaḥ psaraḥ yeṣāṃ te*; the substitute *sa* for *samāna* by "*samānasya chandasi…*", Pā. Sū. 6-3-84 [?]; *asuk* before *jas* by "*ājjaserasuk*"); *ajanayanta* (root *janī prādurbhāve*; *laṅ* in the present sense by "*chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 3-4-6 [?]; *ṇic* by "*hetumati ca*"; when the penultimate lengthening has come, as it is *mit*-marked, shortening by "*mitāṃ hrasvaḥ*"; 3rd plural middle; *nighāta* accent); *iṣirām* (root *iṣu icchāyām*; affix *kirac* by "*iṣimadimudikhidichidibhyaḥ kirac*" [as read]; because it is *kit* there is no *guṇa* of the light penultimate; accent on the last syllable by "*citaḥ*"; *ṭāp* in the feminine because it ends in *a*); *apaśyan* (root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; Vedic *laṅ* in the present sense; 3rd plural; *nighāta* because it stands after a word ending in a verb). ‖ 9 ‖

*(ornamental rule)*

### Printed p. 144  (PDF 164)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 168".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> एष वः स्तोमो मरुत इयं गीर्मांदार्यस्य मान्यस्य कारोः ।
> एषा यासीष्ट तन्वे वयां विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ १० ॥

> *eṣa vaḥ stomo maruta iyaṃ gīrmāṃdāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ |*
> *eṣā yāsīṣṭa tanve vayāṃ vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एषः । वः । स्तोमः । मरुतः । इयम् । गीः । मांदार्यस्य । मान्यस्य । कारोः ।
> आ । इषा । यासीष्ट । तन्वे । वयाम् । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥ १० ॥

> *eṣaḥ | vaḥ | stomaḥ | marutaḥ | iyam | gīḥ | māṃdāryasya | mānyasya | kāroḥ |*
> *ā | iṣā | yāsīṣṭa | tanve | vayām | vidyāma | iṣam | vṛjanam | jīra 'dānum ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अथ पञ्चदश्यां [?] सूक्तोपक्रममारभ्य कृतां स्तुतिं मरुद्भ्यो निवेद्याभिमतमाशास्ते ॥ हे मरुतः एष स्तोम इदानीं क्रियमाणप्रकारं स्तोत्रं वो युष्मदर्थम् । युष्मत्प्रीणनाय भवत्वित्यर्थः । तथेयं गीः स्तुतिरूपा वागपि वो युष्मदर्थाय । यस्मादेवं तस्मान्मांदार्यस्य स्तुतिविशेषैर्मन्दयितुः स्तुतिभिर्मदस्य प्रेरयितुर्वा मान्यस्य वरप्रदानादिना माननीयस्य कारोः स्तोतुर्विशेषेच्छया यासीष्ट । आगच्छत [?] । किमर्थम् । तन्वे शरीराय । तत्पोषायेत्यर्थः । वयां वयमपीषमन्नं वृजनं बलं जीरदानुं जयशीलदानमेतत्सर्वं विद्याम । युष्मास्वागतेषु यज्ञसंपूर्त्येष्ट्यादिद्वारा लभेमहि ॥

*Gist:* Beginning at the opening of the sūkta, the praise made is offered to the Maruts and the desired boon is asked: may they come for the sake of the praiser's body, and may we obtain food, strength and victorious gifts.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *māndāryasya* — of one who gives delight by praises; *mānyasya* — worthy of honour; *kāroḥ* — of the praise-composer; *eṣaḥ stomaḥ* — this praise, made for (you); *vaḥ* — be for you; *(tathā* — likewise*)* *iyaṃ gīḥ* — this speech (in the form of praise); *(vaḥ* — be for you*)*; [*māndāryasya* — of one who satisfies you with praises; *mānyasya* — therefore worthy of worship; *kāroḥ* — of this praise-composer] —

### Printed p. 145  (PDF 165)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6"; a signature mark "XIII 10" is printed at the foot.)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 10, continued)* — *iṣā* — by the wish; *tanve* — for the increase of (your) body; *ā yāsīṣṭa* — (may the praise) go, having you as its object; *vayām* — we; *iṣam* — food too; *vṛjanam* — strength too; *jīradānum* — long life too; *vidyāma* — may we obtain.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, may this praise of ours, the praise-composers who satisfy you with praises and are worthy of worship, be delightful to you; by our wish, may this praise be a cause of the increase of your body; and may we too be favoured with food, strength and long life.

**English Translation (as printed):** This praise, Maruts, is for you: this hymn is for you, (the work) of a venerable author, capable of conferring delight (by his laudations): may the praise reach you for (the good of your) persons, so that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***māndāryasya mānyasya*** — in explaining the component parts of these words, Sāyaṇa takes *māndārya* to mean "one who produces delight" and *mānya* to mean "worthy of worship"; both are epithets of Agastya. Both are also used as *aṅkita-nāma* (signature names). In telling of Agastya's birth, the Bṛhaddevatā says:

> मानेन संमितो यस्मात्तस्मान्मान्य इहोच्यते । यद्वा कुम्भादृषिर्जातः कुम्भेनापि मिमायते ॥

> *mānena saṃmito yasmāt tasmān mānya ihocyate | yadvā kumbhād ṛṣir jātaḥ kumbhenāpi mimāyate ‖*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-153 [?]) — it is explained that the name *mānya* is well known for Agastya either because he is worthy of worship, or because he is born from a pot (*kumbha*) that gives the measure (*māna*), that is, born from the pot as a measure. In the same order the words *māndāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ* occur also in the last ṛks of the Sūktas 165, 166 and 167 [numerals as read].

***stomaḥ, gīḥ*** — these are two words for praise, which indicate different kinds of praise. The matter of the greatness of *stoma* is explained in detail in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, Part 11, pp. 50–52.

## Sūkta 169 — *mahaścittvam* (Anuvāka 23, fifth Sūkta; 8 ṛks)

*(Heading, p. 146: "The hundred and sixty-ninth Sūkta" — ನೂರ ಅರವತ್ತೊಂಭತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> महश्चित्त्वमित्यष्टर्चं पञ्चमं सूक्तमैन्द्रमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभम् । द्वितीया चतुष्पदा विराट् । अथ चतुष्पदा विराड्दशकैरित्युक्तत्वात् विराजो दिशः । पिं. ३-५ [?] । इति पिङ्गलनागेन सूत्रितत्वाच्च । महोऽष्टौ द्वितीया विराडित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ समूळ्हे दशरात्रे द्वितीयेऽहनि मरुत्वतीये इदं विश्वजिकोऽग्निं नर इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । द्वितीयस्य शंसा महाँ महश्चित्त्वमिन्द्र । आ. ८-६ [?] । इति ॥

*Gist:* The fifth sūkta (*mahaścit tvam*), of eight ṛks, by Agastya, to Indra, in triṣṭubh; the second ṛk is a four-pāda *virāṭ*; used in the Samūḍha ten-day rite on the second day, in the Marutvatīya litany.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This Sūkta beginning *mahaścittvam* is the fifth Sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. Agastya is the ṛṣi of this Sūkta; Indra is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. *Virāṭ daśakaiḥ* — since Piṅgalanāga, in the Chandonukramaṇikā, has said that a ṛk of four pādas of ten syllables is called *virāṭ* metre (Piṅ. 3-5 [?]), the second ṛk is of the *virāṭ* metre. In the Anukramaṇikā, too, it is said "*maho'ṣṭau dvitīyā virāṭ*". In the sacrifice called *samūḍha*, to be performed over ten days, its use in the Marutvatīya-śastra mantras at the time of the recitation of the mantras of the second metre on the second day is stated by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section beginning *viśvajiko'gniṃ nara*, by the sūtra "*dvitīyasya śaṃsā mahāṃ mahaścittvam indra*" (Āś. 8-6 [?]).

**॥ ॐ ॥** Sūkta—169
Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 23 ‖ Sūkta 169 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 8, 9 ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 8 · Ṛṣi: Agastya · Devatā: Indra · Chandas: ṛks 1, 3–8 *triṣṭubh*; ṛk 2 *catuṣpadā virāṭ*.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> महश्चित्त्वमिन्द्र यत एतान्महश्चिदसि त्यजसो वरूता ।
> स नो वेधो मरुतां चिकित्वान्त्सुम्ना वनुष्व तव हि प्रेष्ठा ॥ १ ॥

> *mahaścittvamindra yata etānmahaścidasi tyajaso varūtā |*
> *sa no vedho marutāṃ cikitvāntsumnā vanuṣva tava hi preṣṭhā ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> महः । चित् । त्वम् । इन्द्र । यतः । एतान् । महः । चित् । असि । त्यजसः । वरूता ।
> सः । नः । वेधः । मरुताम् । चिकित्वान् । सुम्ना । वनुष्व । तव । हि । प्रेष्ठा ॥ १ ॥

> *mahaḥ | cit | tvam | indra | yataḥ | etān | mahaḥ | cit | asi | tyajasaḥ | varūtā |*
> *saḥ | naḥ | vedhaḥ | marutām | cikitvān | sumnā | vanuṣva | tava | hi | preṣṭhā ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र त्वं यतः कारणादेतान्मरुतो महश्चिन्महतोऽपि सामर्थ्यातिशयवत्त्वात् त्वं निरपेक्षेणापि स्नेहान्न त्यजसीति शेषः । अतः कारणान्महश्चिदसि । चिदिति पादपूरणः । महतोऽपि त्यजसस्त्यागात् [?] । यद्वा । एतेः क्रोधनाम [?] । क्रोधाद्वा । वरूता वरिता रक्षितासि । भवसि । यद्वा । मरुतोऽपि त्यागाद्वृष्ट्यादिविषयोद्वारयितासि [?] । यस्मादेवं तस्मात् हे मरुतां वेधो विधातः स तादृशस्त्वं चिकित्वान् ज्ञेतनावान् [?] अस्मदनुग्रहविषयज्ञानोपेतः सन् नोऽस्मभ्यं सुम्ना सुखानि मरुदायत्तानि वृष्ट्यादिरूपाणि वनुष्व । देहि । तानि तव हि प्रेष्ठा । तव खलु प्रियतमानि । हिशब्दः अयमिन्द्रो मरुत्सखा । ऋ. ८-६३-२ [?] । इत्यादिश्रुतिषु प्रसिद्ध्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Indra is great, since he protects even these great Maruts without abandoning them; as creator of the Maruts, let him, kindly disposed to us, give the rain-like blessings that are dearest to him.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *yataḥ* — for whatever reason; *tvam* — you; *mahaḥ cit* — exceedingly great; *etān* — these Marut-gods; *tyajasaḥ* — from anger

### Printed p. 148  (PDF 168)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 169".)*

(from abandonment concerning rain and the like); *varūtā (asi)* — you are the protector; *(ataḥ* — for that reason*)* *mahaḥ cit asi* — you are indeed great-souled; *he marutām vedhaḥ* — O creator of the Marut-gods, Indra; *saḥ* — such as you are; *cikitvān* — having the knowledge of a favour towards us; *naḥ* — to us; *sumnā* — (Marut-bound) happinesses in the form of rain and the like; *vanuṣva* — be the giver; *(tāni* — those happinesses*)*; *tava* — to you; *preṣṭhā hi* — are known to be most dear.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, since you protect without ever leaving them even the greatest Marut-gods, you are in truth great-souled; O Indra, creator of the Marut-gods, with a mind of favour towards us, grant us the happinesses in the form of rain and the like, which are most dear to you.

**English Translation (as printed):** You, Indra, are mighty from the might of those of whom you are the protector against abandonment: therefore, creator of the Maruts, favourably-minded towards us, grant us those blessings which are most dear to you.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***marutaḥ mahaścit; tyajasaḥ varūtā; mahato'pi sāmarthyātiśayavattvāt tvaṃ nirapekṣeṇāpi snehāt na tyajasi*** — here Indra is addressed. The matter of the origin of the Marut-gods is stated both in the Bṛhaddevatā and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. The goddess Diti, desiring a son who would subdue Indra, obtained the favour of the sage Kaśyapa and, while she was living under a vow and was with child, Indra entered her womb and with his thunderbolt cut the embryo into seven parts; when the infant wept, Indra said "*mā ruda*" ("do not weep"), and so the name *marut* arose for them. Afterwards Diti awoke and, as she said, "let these fragments of the embryo live and be your helpers along with Indra", Indra consented and made the Marut-gods his friends. This is indicated here.

Both Indra and the Marut-gods are of great power; both are independent in their action and do not seek help from one another. Even so, because Indra, though by his own power very powerful, is in friendship with these Marut-gods, one kind of meaning is that Indra's abundant greatness is made manifest: this is one meaning for the word *tyajasaḥ* (continued on the next page).

---

### Printed p. 149  (PDF 169)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 9"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue.)*

(*tyajasaḥ* continued) … it is explained that the word means "from abandonment". Many mighty persons, in relation to other powerful persons, are accustomed to foster their friendship for some purpose or other. Indra, though he was independent in this way and abandoned them (the Marut-gods) at the time of their very origin, is afterwards in friendship with them; this shows that Indra's abundant greatness is made manifest. Thus the meaning is described.

In the second meaning, the sense "anger" is given to the word *tyajasaḥ*. The word *tyajas* is read among the names of anger (Ni. 2-[?]). Indra, regarding them as enemies and knowing, at the very time of their origin, that they would act to subdue him, though angry with them, afterwards becomes *varūtā* — one who protects them: so the glory of Indra is said to be praiseworthy. This meaning is explained.

In the third meaning, in "*maruto'pi tyāgāt vṛṣṭyādi viṣayāt vārayitāsi*": because Indra makes the Marut-gods refrain (from) the work of bringing about rain, Indra is the *marutāṃ vedhāḥ vidhātaḥ* — one who is the maker in respect of the Marut-gods; thus Indra's greatness is described.

***cikitvān na sumnā vanuṣva*** — the word *cikitvān* means in general "one who has consciousness, one who has knowledge"; but here, "*asmadanugrahaviṣayajñānopetaḥ*" — one who has the knowledge of favouring us, who perform sacrifices — is the sense explained. The word *sumnā* is read among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-[?]); therefore, "*marudāyattāni vṛṣṭirūpāṇi*": the happiness favoured to the sacrificer by Indra is that which is governed by the Marut-gods, in the form of rain; and by this explanation it is wished that Indra may favour us, the sacrificers, with all the happiness that arises through it.

***tava hi preṣṭhā*** — by this sentence it is described that happiness of this kind, since it arises from the Marut-gods who are Indra's friends, is an object of Indra's affection. And in the ṛk

> अयमिन्द्रो मरुत्सखा

> *ayam indro marutsakhā*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?]) the fact that Indra is a friend of the Marut-gods is stated.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *mahaḥ* (in *mahataḥ* the *ta* is dropped in the Veda); *asi* (root *as bhuvi*; *laṭ* 2nd singular; *nighāta*); *tyajasaḥ* (root *tyaja hānau*; affix *asun* by "*sarvadhātubhya asun*" (Uṇ.); accent on the first syllable because of the *n* marker; ablative singular form); *varūtā* (root *vṛñ varaṇe*; irregular, ending in *tṛc*, by "*grasitaskabhita…*", Pā. Sū. 7-2-34 [?]; accent on the last syllable since it ends in a *cit* affix).
