*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 9".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> पूर्वमन्त्रे मरुतामिन्द्रसाहाय्यमुक्तम् । अत्रेन्द्रस्य मरुत्साहाय्यमुच्यते । हे इन्द्र ते मरुतोऽयुज्रन् । युज्यन्ते । त्वया [?] युक्ता भवन्तीत्यर्थः । कीदृशास्ते । विश्वकृष्टीर्विश्वकृष्टयो राज्यत्वेन सर्वजनवन्तः । किंच मर्त्यत्रा मर्त्येषु मर्त्यार्थं निष्षिधो निःशेषेणोदकस्य सेक्तॄन् मेघान् विदानासो जानानाः । किंच येषां मरुतां पृत्सुतिः सेना स्वर्मीळ्हस्य प्रधनस्य सुखसेक्तुः प्रकृष्टधनवतो वृत्रादिसंग्रामस्य सातौ लाभे जयो निमित्तभूते सति सेना हासमाना हासं कुर्वती हर्षयुक्ता भवति । यद्वा । सुखेन मिह्यते जलं यस्मिन् ताद्दृशस्य प्रधनस्य प्रकृष्टोदकाख्यधनसाधनस्य संग्रामस्य सातौ । मेघभेदनायेति यावत् । येषामीदृशी सेनास्ति ते मरुतोऽयुज्रन्निति संबन्धः ॥

*Gist:* The Maruts join Indra, rulers over all men, knowing the water-shedding clouds that rain for mortals; their army exults at the victory in the battle with Vṛtra, or in the cloud-splitting that wins the waters.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *(yeṣām)* *marutām* — of which Marut-gods; *pṛtsutiḥ* — the army; *svarmīḷhasya* — conducive to heaven (conducive to happiness); *pradhanasya* — of the battle in which excellent wealth is gained (such as the battle with Vṛtra); *sātau* — in the matter of gain (victory); *[atha vā* — or*]* *svarmīḷhasya* — easily obtainable water; *pradhanasya* — of the cloud possessing excellent water as wealth; *sātau* — in (your) bringing about victory; *hāsamānā* — laughing (delighted); *te* — those; *viśvakṛṣṭīḥ* — distinguished by all people; *martyatrā* — for human beings (among men); *niṣṣidhaḥ* — clouds that sprinkle water in abundance; *vidānāsaḥ* — those who know (the Marut-gods); *ayujran* — (with you) are joined.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, the Marut-gods, distinguished by all people (that is, rulers of men), and urging for men the rain-causing clouds, are with you alone; through the victory in the battle with Vṛtra and the like that you achieve, or through the splitting of the cloud, these Marut-gods become delighted.

**English Translation (as printed):** Rulers over all men, and impelling towards man the water-shedding clouds, they are united, Indra, (with you): the host of Maruts is delighted by (your) acquisition of heaven-bestowing wealth.

### Printed p. 152  (PDF 172)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 169".)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

The help that Indra gave to the Marut-gods was stated in the preceding mantra; the help that Indra receives from the Marut-gods is stated in this mantra.

***viśvakṛṣṭīḥ*** — Sāyaṇa changes this word into the nominative plural *viśvakṛṣṭayaḥ* and, by "*rājyatvena sarvajanavantaḥ*", explains that the Marut-gods, regarding all as their realm, with the idea that all must be protected, are in affection of one kind towards all beings.

***martyatrā niṣṣidhaḥ vidānāsaḥ*** — *martyārthaṃ niḥśeṣeṇa udakasya sektṝn meghān vidānāsaḥ jānānāḥ*: the Marut-gods know that the clouds send down waters for the prosperity of men; this sense too is explained.

***marutāṃ pṛtsutiḥ pradhanasya sātau hāsamānā*** — for the word *pṛtsuti* the sense "army" is given by the Nirukta-writer, and the word *pradhana* is explained by him:

> न्यक्रन्दयन्नुपयन्त एनममेहयन्वृषभं मध्य आजेः ।
> तेन सूभर्वं शतवत्सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः प्रधने जगाय ॥

> *nyakrandayann upayanta enam amehayan vṛṣabhaṃ madhya ājeḥ |*
> *tena sūbharvaṃ śatavat sahasraṃ gavāṃ mudgalaḥ pradhane jagāya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-102-5 [?]). Here "*pradhana iti saṃgrāma nāma prakīrṇānyasmin dhanāni bhavanti*" — wealth is lavishly spent in it, so *pradhana* denotes battle, war, according to the Nirukta-writer's explanation. Following this, Sāyaṇa explains it as "battle", and, because this bestows happiness, "*sukhasektuḥ prakṛṣṭadhanavato vṛtrādisaṃgrāmasya lābhe jaye nimittabhūte sati senā harṣayuktā bhavati*": the army of the Marut-gods is joyful, because victory is to be obtained in the battle with a Vṛtra possessing abundant wealth that bestows happiness, in the war of conduct to be waged with Asuras beginning with Vṛtra.

In the second meaning, since *svarmīḷhasya* is an adjective of *pradhanasya*: "*sukhena mihyate jalaṃ yasmin tādṛśasya pradhanasya prakṛṣṭodakākhyadhanasādhanasya saṃgrāmasya sātau meghabhedanāya*" — in a battle in which water, a wealth, is obtained with ease, that is, for the sake of the splitting of the cloud, which is the means to the wealth called water: thus the sense is explained, that the army of the Marut-gods is ready for the help of Indra.

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अम्यक् सा त इन्द्र ऋष्टिरस्मे सनेम्यभ्वं मरुतो जुनन्ति ।
> अग्निश्चिद्धि ष्मातसे शुशुक्वानापो न द्वीपं दधति प्रयांसि ॥ ३ ॥

> *amyak sā ta indra ṛṣṭirasme sanemyabhvaṃ maruto junanti |*
> *agniściddhi ṣmātase śuśukvānāpo na dvīpaṃ dadhati prayāṃsi ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अम्यक् । सा । ते । इन्द्र । ऋष्टिः । अस्मे इति । सनेमि । अभ्वम् । मरुतः । जुनन्ति ।
> अग्निः । चित् । हि । स्म । आतसे । शुशुक्वान् । आपः । न । द्वीपम् । दधति । प्रयांसि ॥ ३ ॥

> *amyak | sā | te | indra | ṛṣṭiḥ | asme iti | sanemi | abhvam | marutaḥ | junanti |*
> *agniḥ | cit | hi | sma | ātase | śuśukvān | āpaḥ | na | dvīpam | dadhati | prayāṃsi ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र ते तव सा प्रसिद्धा ऋष्टिर्वज्राख्यायुधविशेषोऽस्मे अस्मदर्थम् अम्यक् । प्राप्नोति मेघसमीपे । एवं च सति मरुतोऽपि सनेमि । अह्नायेति षट् पुराणनामानीत्यादि [?] सनेमि पुराणनाम । पुराणं चिरकालं संगृहीतमभ्वमुदकं जुनन्ति । क्षिपन्ति । वर्षन्तीत्यर्थः । वृष्ट्या सस्यादिसमृद्धौ सत्यामग्निश्चिद्धि ष्म । हि स्मेति पूरणे । अग्निरप्यातसे संतते कर्मणि निमित्तभूते सति शुशुक्वान् दीप्यमानो वर्तते । पश्चात्प्रयांसि चरुपुरोडाशादिहवींषि दधति । धारयन्ति ददति वा यजमानाः । किमिव आपो न द्वीपम् । द्विपार्श्वस्थोदकवान् पर्वतादिर्द्वीपः । तं यथापो धारयन्ति तद्वत् । यद्वा । आयुधमेवोच्यते । वज्राख्यायुधविशेषो [?] ऽतसे काष्ठसमूहे शुशुक्वान् दीपयन्नग्निश्चित् । चिच्छब्द उपमार्थे । दधि चिदित्युपमार्थे । नि. १-४ [?] । इति यास्केनोपमार्थस्योक्तत्वात् ॥ काष्ठे ज्वलन्नग्निरिव । तद्वद्दीप्तो वर्तते । एतदेव दीप्तत्वमपेक्ष्य स इत्युक्तम् [?] । एवं च सत्यापो द्वीपमिव वृष्ट्युदकानि प्रयांसि सस्याद्यन्नानि दधति । धारयन्ति । एतत्सर्वं महानुभावस्येन्द्रस्य वीर्यं सामर्थ्यमितीन्द्रस्य स्तुतिः ॥ [reading of the last sentence doubtful]

*Gist:* Indra's famous thunderbolt reaches the cloud for us; the Maruts pour down the old-stored water, and rain brings abundance; the sacrificers hold up the oblations as waters hold an island, and the bolt blazes like fire in a pile of wood.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *te* — your; *sā* — that famous; *ṛṣṭiḥ* — thunderbolt-weapon; *asme* — for us (to bring about rain); *amyak* — approaches (the clouds); *marutaḥ* — the Marut-gods; *sanemi* — from a long time; *abhvam* — water; *junanti* — throw down (pour out); *agniḥ cit hi sma* — fire too —

### Printed p. 155  (PDF 175)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 9".)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 3, continued)* — *ātase* — for the continuous (sacrificial) rite; *śuśukvān* — blazing brightly (he is); *āpaḥ* — waters; *dvīpaṃ na* — as an island (which they hold, that is, surround); *prayāṃsi* — oblations (such as *caru* and *puroḍāśa*); *dadhati* — they hold (offer). [*Or:* *(ṛṣṭiḥ* — the thunderbolt-weapon*)* *ātase* — in a pile of wood; *śuśukvān* — blazing brightly; *agniḥ cit* — like fire (it blazes); *āpaḥ* — waters; *dvīpaṃ na* — as an island (they surround); *prayāṃsi* — food in the form of crops and the like; *dadhati* — they hold (support).]

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, your weapon, the thunderbolt, approaches the clouds, to cause rain; for the sake of the sacrificial rite Agni also blazes; and (the sacrificers) with offerings such as *caru* and *puroḍāśa* surround the fire, as waters surround an island.

**English Translation (as printed):** Your weapon, Indra, is at hand for our (good); the Maruts send down the long-accumulated rain; Agni is blazing for the ceremony; the oblations encompass him as the waters (surround) an island.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***ṛṣṭiḥ asme amyak*** — here Indra is addressed. The word *ṛṣṭi* means "*vajrākhyāyudhaviśeṣaḥ*": it is well known by the name of the thunderbolt-weapon, and the sense is that it is Indra's weapon; "*asmadvṛṣṭyarthaṃ meghasamīpe prāpnoti*" — it is employed near the clouds to bring down the waters of rain for us, the sacrificers. The Nirukta-writers explain the word *amyak*, citing this very ṛk,

> अम्यक् सा त इन्द्र ऋष्टिरस्मे सनेम्यभ्वं

> *amyak sā ta indra ṛṣṭirasme sanemyabhvaṃ*

as "*amāktīti vā abhyuktīti vā*" [as read]; Durgācārya says "*ṛṣṭirabhidheyo māṃ eṣā pratyañci tām āmoṣāpratyañcite…, śatravaḥ manyante*" [garbled in the reading]: the enemies think "Indra's weapon called *ṛṣṭi* is directed towards me"; and because "*nityakālaṃ śatrūn prati abhigaitva bhavatīti*" [as read] — it is always facing the enemies — it is well known as *amyak*. Thus the sense is explained.

***marutaḥ sanemi abhvaṃ junanti*** — *cirakālaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ udakaṃ varṣanti*: when the weapon of Indra called *ṛṣṭi* is employed near the clouds, the clouds, with the water they have collected for a very long time, are made to pour it out, and rain is produced: this is the meaning stated. The word *abhva* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]) and also among the names of great things (Ni. 3-[?]); here the sense "water" is explained.

### Printed p. 156  (PDF 176)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 169".)*

***sanemi*** — this word is stated among the names of "old" (Ni. 3-[?]); even so, in the ṛk

> शं नो भवन्तु वाजिनो हवेषु देवताता मितद्रवः स्वर्काः ।
> जम्भयन्तोऽहिं वृकं रक्षांसि सनेम्यस्मद्युयवन्नमीवाः ॥

> *śaṃ no bhavantu vājino haveṣu devatātā mitadravaḥ svarkāḥ |*
> *jambhayanto'hiṃ vṛkaṃ rakṣāṃsi sanemy asmad yuyavann amīvāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-35-7 [?]), the use of the word *sanemi* in the sense *kṣipram* ("quickly") is shown. The Nirukta-writer gives two meanings for the word *sanemi*: "old" or "of a long past time", and *kṣipra* (alertness); of these Sāyaṇa has taken "old". And this very thing in his commentary: "*sanemi ahnāye ti ṣaṭ purāṇanāmāni…; sanemi purāṇanāma; purāṇaṃ ciraṃ kālaṃ saṃgṛhītam*" [as read]: since it is read among the six names of "old" in the Nirukta, the sense "old (ancient)" is supported for the word *sanemi*; it is explained that the waters have been gathered for a very long time.

For the latter half of this ṛk, two kinds of meaning are explained. Both follow the filler (*pūraṇa*) and comparison meanings of the word *cit* in *agniścid dhi ṣma*. In the first meaning, the word *agni* is the qualified word: *agniḥ ātase santate karmaṇi nimittabhūte sati śuśukvān* — after the crops have been produced by rain and the like, for the sacrificial rites and the like, he blazes in brightness; and, in order to satisfy the fire thus shining, *prayāṃsi dadhati carupuroḍāśādihavīṃṣi dhārayanti dadati vā yajamānāḥ* — the sacrificers hold (offer) oblations or pour them into the fire; the oblations held by the sacrificers are compared, "*āpo na dvīpam*", to waters holding an island. The sense of the word *dvīpa* is also explained: "*dvipārśvastodakavān parvatādiḥ*" — a place such as a mountain, with water on two sides; "*taṃ yathā āpo dhārayanti*" — as waters hold the island; so the way of comparison, that the oblations are held between Agni and the sacrificers, is described.

The Nirukta-writer, explaining the sense of the particle *cit*: "*cid ity eṣo anekakarmā*" — the particle *cit* is used in many senses — explains it, and these (continued on the next page).

### Printed p. 157  (PDF 177)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 9"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 3 continue.)*

(*cit* continued) — … explaining them, he shows, by the sentence "*dadhi cid ity upamārthe*", that the particle *cit* is used here in the sense of comparison. Following this, Sāyaṇa, citing "*cicchabdaḥ upamārthe dadhi cid ity upamārthe* (Ni. 1-[?]) *iti yāskenoktatvāt*", says "*yadvā āyudham evocyate vajrākhyāyudhaviśeṣo ātase kāṣṭhasamūhe śuśukvān dīpayann agniścit*": the weapon named thunderbolt of Indra is here spoken of; and, explaining the sense that it shines as a fire shines in a heap of timber, he comments "*kāṣṭhe jvalann agnir iva tadvad dīpto vartate*". The abundance of Agni's brightness is stated by the word *sā*. He explains and confirms the comparison sentence "*āpo na dvīpam*" as "*āpaḥ dvīpam iva vṛṣṭyudakāni sasyādyannāni dhārayanti*": as waters hold an island by surrounding it, the rain-waters hold the crops and food.

***ātase*** — *saṃtate karmaṇi*: the sense "continuously (as in continual) practised" is explained for the word *atas*. The Nirukta-writer cites

> आपान्तमन्युस्तृपलप्रभर्मा धुनिः शिमीवाञ्छरुमाँ ऋजीषी ।
> सोमो विश्वान्यतसा वनानि नार्वागिन्द्रं प्रतिमानानि देभुः ॥

> *āpāntamanyus tṛpalaprabharmā dhuniḥ śimīvāñ charumāṃ ṛjīṣī |*
> *somo viśvāny atasā vanāni nārvāg indraṃ pratimānāni debhuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-99-[?]). Here, for the word *atasā*, Durgācārya explains "*anupakṣīṇāni*" — "growing, undiminished". Sāyaṇa gives the same sense by "*saṃtate*".

Sū. 7-1-39 [?]); *junanti* (the root *ju*, of motion, a Sautra root; *laṭ* 3rd plural; *jhi* → *anta*; *śnā* by "*kryādibhyaḥ śnā*"; loss of its *ā* by "*śnābhyastayor ātaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 6-4-112 [?]; *nighāta* of the verb); *ātase* (root *ata sātatyagamane*; the affix *asac* by an Uṇādi sūtra (cited, garbled); accent on the last syllable by "*citaḥ*"; locative); *śuśukvān* (root *śuca dīptau*; for *liṭ* the substitute *kvasu* by "*kvasuśca*", Pā. Sū. 3-2-107 [?]

— the affix being the occasion, reduplication and the like occur, and by *vyatyaya* the velar substitution (*kutva*) comes; the accent of *vasu* remains); *dvīpam* (*dvirgatā āpo yasmin iti dvīpam*; the substitute *ī* for the *a* of *apa* when *dvi* is the first member, by "*dvyantarupasargebhyo'pa īt*", Pā. Sū. 6-3-97 [?]); *dadhati* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *laṭ* 3rd plural; since "*hi ca*", Pā. Sū. 8-1-34 [?] prevents the *nighāta*, the first syllable of the reduplicated word is acute by "*abhyastānām ādiḥ*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-189 [?]). ‖ 3 ‖

*(ornamental rule)*

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वं तू न इन्द्र तं रयिं दा ओजिष्ठया दक्षिणयेव रातिम् ।
> स्तुतश्च यास्ते चकनन्त वायोः स्तनं न मध्वः पीपयन्त वाज्यैः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tvaṃ tū na indra taṃ rayiṃ dā ojiṣṭhayā dakṣiṇayeva rātim |*
> *stutaśca yāste cakananta vāyoḥ stanaṃ na madhvaḥ pīpayanta vājyaiḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वम् । तु । नः । इन्द्र । तम् । रयिम् । दाः । ओजिष्ठया । दक्षिणयाऽइव । रातिम् ।
> स्तुतः । च । याः । ते । चकनन्त । वायोः । स्तनम् । न । मध्वः । पीपयन्त । वाज्यैः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tvam | tu | naḥ | indra | tam | rayim | dāḥ | ojiṣṭhayā | dakṣiṇayā 'iva | rātim |*
> *stutaḥ | ca | yāḥ | te | cakananta | vāyoḥ | stanam | na | madhvaḥ | pīpayanta | vājyaiḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र त्वं तु तुरवधारणे । त्वमेव नोऽस्मदर्थं तं रयिं त्वद्दानयोग्यं गवादिधनं दाः । देहि । यस्मादितरेभ्योऽपि त्वमेव बहुप्रदः । अतोऽतिमहद्धनं देहीत्यर्थः । वयं त्वोजिष्ठयौजस्वितमया परिक्रमणार्हया [?] दक्षिणया समृद्धिसाधनया गवादिलक्षणयेत्विजमिव रातिं दातारं त्वां प्रीणयाम इति शेषः । यद्वा । दक्षिणाशब्दो देयद्रव्यसामान्यवचनः । रातिशब्दो बन्धुवचनः । हिरण्यादिसारवद्द्रव्यप्रदानेन बन्धुं यथा वशीकुर्वन्ति तद्वत्त्वां वशीकुर्म इत्यर्थः । किंच वायोर्धौतेयुवक्षेपिष्ठस्य [?] शीघ्रवरप्रदस्य ते । कर्मणि षष्ठी । वायुं त्वां स्तुतो येऽस्मदीयाः स्तोतारश्च कनन्त कामयन्ते [?] अस्तुवन् । याः स्तुतयस्त्वानेवा— [the bhāṣya continues on the next page]

> *he indra tvaṃ tu turavadhāraṇe | tvameva no 'smadarthaṃ taṃ rayiṃ tvaddānayogyaṃ gavādidhanaṃ dāḥ | dehi | yasmāditarebhyo 'pi tvameva bahupradaḥ | ato 'timahaddhanaṃ dehītyarthaḥ | vayaṃ tvojiṣṭhayaujasvitamayā parikramaṇārhayā [?] dakṣiṇayā samṛddhisādhanayā gavādilakṣaṇayetvijamiva rātiṃ dātāraṃ tvāṃ prīṇayāma iti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | dakṣiṇāśabdo deyadravyasāmānyavacanaḥ | rātiśabdo bandhuvacanaḥ | hiraṇyādisāravaddravyapradānena bandhuṃ yathā vaśīkurvanti tadvattvāṃ vaśīkurma ityarthaḥ | kiṃca vāyordhauteyuvakṣepiṣṭhasya [?] śīghravarapradasya te | karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī | vāyuṃ tvāṃ stuto ye 'smadīyāḥ stotāraśca kananta kāmayante [?] astuvan | yāḥ stutayastvānevā— [the bhāṣya continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 159  (PDF 179)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 9"; the bhāṣya of Ṛk 4 concludes.)*

> कामयन्तेति वा योजना ॥ कनतेर्ण्यन्ताल्लुङि चङ्रूपम् [?] । चङ्यन्यतरस्यामिति [?] चङः पूर्वमुत्तराक्षरमुदात्तम् । त्वां होत्रादयो वाज्यैर्वाजलक्षणैरन्नैः [?] पीपयन्त । आप्याययन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । मध्वो मधुरस्य स्तन्यस्य लाभाय वाज्यैः सारवद्भिरन्नविशेषैः स्तनं न । तं यथाप्याययन्ति तद्वदयं त्वां बहुकृतप्रदानाय [?] स्तुत्या हविषाप्याययामः । त्वं तु दातव्यत्वेन प्रसिद्धं धनं सर्वदा देहीत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* The ṛtvijs feed you with strong food-offerings, as a woman's breast is nourished for sweet milk; and you, give us the wealth that is to be given.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *ojiṣṭhayā* — exceedingly strong (most excellent); *dakṣiṇayā iva* — as with a gift that is a means of prosperity (as one satisfies the priests with cows and the like); *rātim* — you, the giver (we satisfy). [*Or:* *ojiṣṭhayā* — most excellent; *dakṣiṇayā* — with a gift; *rātim iva* — as relatives (are won over), so you too we win over with praise and oblations and the like.] *(kiṃca* — and*)* *vāyoḥ* — of you, who are quick to grant boons; *te* — you; *stutaḥ* — (which, ours) the praisers; *cakananta* — praise (desire); *yāḥ stutaḥ ca* — and which (our) praises; *cakananta* — desired; *madhvaḥ* — sweet (for the gain of milk); *vājyaiḥ* — (substantial) with food and the like; *stanam na* — as one nourishes (a woman's) breast; *(vājyaiḥ* — with oblations and the like*)* *pīpayanta* — (they) satisfy; *tvaṃ tu* — you, however; *tam* — that (fit to be offered to you); *rayim* — (cow-form) wealth; *naḥ* — to us; *dāḥ* — bestow.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, as priests are satisfied with an excellent gift consisting of cattle and the like, or as relatives are, so we satisfy you; our praises also are directed to you alone; as a woman's breast is nourished with food in order that she may give sweet milk, the priests such as the *hotṛ* nourish you with oblations; you also grant us wealth, in the form of cattle and the like, that is fit to be offered to you.

**English Translation (as printed):** Indra, quickly grant us that wealth (which you possess, for we gratify) the donor with a most worthy present: we, your praisers, offer to you, the ready-giver of boons, the laudations that would propitiate you; (and the priests) nourish you with sacrificial food, as they cherish the bosom (of a female for the sake of replenishing it) with sweet (milk).

### Printed p. 160  (PDF 180)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 169".)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***taṃ rayiṃ dāḥ*** — *tvaddānayogyaṃ gavādidhanaṃ dehi*: the word *rayi* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]), and it is explained as "*rayiriti dhananāma rāter dānakarmaṇaḥ*" (Ni. 4-[?]). Indra is described as one who gives abundant wealth beyond others: "*yasmād itarebhyo'pi tvam eva bahupradaḥ; ato'ti mahaddhanaṃ dehi*"; and by this sentence the wealth is also prayed for, that he may bestow it on us.

***ojiṣṭhayā dakṣiṇayā iva rātim*** — for this sentence two kinds of meaning are explained. The word *ojiṣṭhayā* is used as an adjective of the word *dakṣiṇā*. "*Dakṣiṇā*" is explained as wealth which is a means of prosperity and is moving (that is, living, such as cattle). As priests are satisfied by such a *dakṣiṇā*, so we satisfy Indra, who is the giver: this is one kind of meaning. The Nirukta-writer says: "*dakṣiṇā dakṣateḥ samṛddhyayati karmaṇaḥ vyṛddhaṃ samarthayatīti*" [as read] — the gift that brings prosperity; or, "*dakṣiṇo hasto dakṣateḥ utsāhakarmaṇaḥ*" — the right hand, with a force that raises enthusiasm. And among the words for gifts (Ni. 3-[?]) the word *rāti* is read.

> शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि ।
> विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥

> *śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te anyad viṣurūpe ahanī dyaur ivāsi |*
> *viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣann iha rātir astu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-1). Here the sense "gift" is given for the word *rāti*.

Sāyaṇa, in explaining the second meaning: "*dakṣiṇāśabdo deyadravyasāmānyavacanaḥ | rātiśabdo bandhuvacanaḥ*" — the word *dakṣiṇā* denotes the substance that is given; for the word *rāti* the sense "relative" is explained; "*hiraṇyādisāravaddravyapradānena bandhuṃ yathā vaśīkurvanti*" — as men win over relatives by giving costly things, gold and the like — and "*tadvat tvāṃ vaśīkurmaḥ*", "we win you over in the same way": thus the wish of the sacrificers is described.

***vāyoḥ*** — *dhautayuvakṣepiṣṭhasya śīghravarapradasya*: for the word *vāyu* the meaning "one who destroys the youthful life of enemies, one who bestows boons promptly, being alert" is explained. Yāska says: "*vāyur vāter veter vā syād gatikarmaṇaḥ; eterīti śākaṭāyanaḥ … anarthako vakāraḥ*" (Ni. 10-[?]) — whether from the root *vā* of motion, or from *iṅ gatau* … (continued on the next page).

### Printed p. 161  (PDF 181)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 9"; a signature mark "XIII 11" is printed at the foot. The Special Topics of Ṛk 4 continue.)*

(*vāyu* continued) — whether the word *vāyu* is formed from the root *vā* or from the root *iṅ*, Śākaṭāyana says that the word *vāyu* is formed from the root *iṅ*, "*anarthako vakāraḥ*" — in this word the letter *va* has no meaning: thus Yāska explains the word *vāyu*.

Sāyaṇa explains, in "*vāyoḥ te stutaḥ*", the word *te* as a genitive in the sense of the object ("*karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī*"): "*vāyuṃ tvā stutaḥ ye asmadīyāḥ stotāraḥ*" — the praisers of ours praise you, who are Vāyu (the one who moves), with praises: this is one kind of meaning.

In the second, "*yāḥ stutayaḥ tvā neva akāmayanta*" — the praises recited by the priests are directed to you alone: this meaning is explained.

***vājyaiḥ pīpayanta madhvaḥ stanaṃ na*** — here "*tvāṃ hotrādayaḥ havirlakṣaṇairannaiḥ āpyāyayanti*" and "*madhurasya stanyasya lābhāya sāravadbhir annaviśeṣaiḥ iva āpyāyayanti*" are given as the comparison: the sense is that the priests such as the *hotṛ* satisfy Indra, who bestows abundant favour, with praise and oblations, as in the world women are satisfied by substantial food in order to obtain sweet milk; it is likened thus.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *dāḥ* (root *ḍudāñ dāne*; *luṅ* in the sense of the imperative by "*chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 3-4-6 [?]; 2nd singular *sip*; loss of *i* by "*iteś ca*"; *cli* replaced by *sic*; *luk* of *sic* by "*gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu*", Pā. Sū. 2-4-77 [?]; no augment *aṭ* by "*bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge'pi*", Pā. Sū. 6-4-75 [?]; *nighāta* accent); *ojiṣṭhayā* (the affix *vini* after *ojas* in the sense of possession; *iṣṭhan* in the sense of excess after it; loss of *vin* by "*vinmatorluk*", Pā. Sū. 5-3-65 [?]; loss of the (*as*) of the *ṭi* part by "*ṭeḥ*", Pā. Sū. 6-4-155 [?]; *ṭāp* in the feminine; the first syllable acute since the affix is *ñ*-marked); *rātim* (by the force of "*bahulagrahaṇa*", *ktin* in the agent sense; acute by "*mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanaviḍāvanarakṣaśā…*", Pā. Sū. 3-3-96 [?]); *stutaḥ* (root *ṣṭuñ stutau*; by "*kviṣ ca*" [as read], Pā. Sū. 3-2-76 [?], the affix *kvip*; the augment *tuk* by "*hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-71 [?]; nominative plural form).

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वे राय इन्द्र तोशतमाः प्रणेतारः कस्य चिदृतायोः ।
> ते षु णो मरुतो मृळयन्तु ये स्मा पुरा गातूयन्तीव देवाः ॥ ५ ॥

> *tve rāya indra tośatamāḥ praṇetāraḥ kasya cidṛtāyoḥ |*
> *te ṣu ṇo maruto mṛḷayantu ye smā purā gātūyantīva devāḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वे इति । रायः । इन्द्र । तोशऽतमाः । प्रऽनेतारः । कस्य । चित् । ऋतऽयोः ।
> ते । सु । नः । मरुतः । मृळयन्तु । ये । स्म । पुरा । गातुयन्तिऽइव [?] । देवाः ॥ ५ ॥

> *tve iti | rāyaḥ | indra | tośa 'tamāḥ | pra 'netāraḥ | kasya | cit | ṛta 'yoḥ |*
> *te | su | naḥ | marutaḥ | mṛḷayantu | ye | sma | purā | gātuyanti 'iva [?] | devāḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

### Printed p. 163  (PDF 183)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 9".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र त्वे तव रायो धनविशेषाः तोशतमाः । अतिशयेन प्रीणयितारः ॥ तुष्यतेस्तोशः । छान्दसं शत्त्वम् ॥ यद्वा । ते रायो रातयो बन्धवो बन्धुभूताः सखिभूताः मरुतः तोशतमाः । तोशतिर्वधकर्मा निर्तोशयति निबर्हयतीति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तोशतमा हिंसितृतमाः अवर्षकाणां मेघानाम् । कस्य चिदृतायोः । ऋतमिति यज्ञनाम । कस्यापि यज्ञेच्छोर्यजमानस्य प्रकर्षेण निर्वोढारः । ते मरुतो नोऽस्मान् सुष्ठु मृळयन्तु । के ते । ये स्म ये खलु देवा द्योतनशीला मरुतः पुरा पूर्वं गातुयन्तीव । यज्ञगमनमिच्छन्तीव । ते आगत्य मृळयन्तु ॥

*Gist:* Indra's riches are most gladdening; or the Maruts, his kin, destroy the rainless clouds and carry through the sacrifice of anyone who wishes to sacrifice; may they, who once eagerly went to the sacrifice, make us happy.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *tve* — your; *rāyaḥ* — special wealths; *tośatamāḥ* — causing the greatest delight (exceeding satisfaction); [*or* *tve* — your; *rāyaḥ* — relatives (Marut-gods); *tośatamāḥ* — (of clouds that do not shower rain) those who especially destroy (the Marut-gods)]; *kasyacit ṛtāyoḥ* — of any one who wishes to sacrifice; *praṇetāraḥ* — those who carry the sacrifice through to its end; *ye* — which; *devāḥ sma* — Marut-gods; *purā* — before; *gātūyanti iva* — like those who wish to go to the sacrifice; *te* — those; *marutaḥ* — Marut-gods; *naḥ* — to us; *su mṛḷayantu* — may they bestow great happiness.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, your wealth is the cause of happiness (or your relatives the Marut-gods especially destroy the non-shedding clouds); for all who desire to perform a sacrifice, they become (favourably) the carriers-through of the work; those who have first desired to come to the sacrifice — may such Marut-gods make us happy.

**English Translation (as printed):** Your riches, Indra, are most delighting; the exciters of any one desirous to sacrifice: may those Maruts be propitious to us; the divine beings who were anxious to go first to the ceremony.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***tve rāyaḥ tośatamāḥ*** — *tava dhanaviśeṣāḥ atiśayena prīṇayitāraḥ*: Indra is addressed, and the wealth bestowed by Indra produces abundant delight: this is one kind of meaning.

### Printed p. 164  (PDF 184)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 169".)*

In the second meaning: "*tośatirvadhakarmā nitośayati nibarhayatīti*" (Ni. 2-[?]); since *tośate* is read among the names of killing, the word *tośatamāḥ* is explained as "*hiṃsitṛtamāḥ avarṣakāṇāṃ meghānām*" — those who destroy exceedingly the clouds that do not shed rain; and "*te rāyo rātayo bandhavo bandhubhūtāḥ sakhibhūtāḥ marutaḥ tośatamāḥ*" — the Marut-gods, who are Indra's relatives and friends and givers, destroy the clouds that do not give rain.

***kasya cid ṛtāyoḥ praṇetāraḥ*** — *ṛtam iti yajñanāma | kasyāpi yajñecchor yajamānasya prakarṣeṇa nirvoḍhāraḥ*: the word *ṛta*, which conveys the meanings "water", "a particular time", "truth" and "sacrifice", is used here in the sense of sacrifice. And the word *ṛtāyu* is used, in the ṛk

> मा नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यो रिषे धान्मा यज्ञो अस्य स्रिधदृतायोः ।

> *mā no'hir budhnyo riṣe dhān mā yajño asya sridhad ṛtāyoḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-17 [?]), in the sense of "*yajñakāmasya*", "one who desires to perform a sacrifice". It is explained that the Marut-gods, whoever the person may be who wishes to perform a sacrifice, carry through his wish.

***ye devāḥ purā gātuyantīva te naḥ mṛḷayantu*** — *dyotanaśīlāḥ yajñagamanam icchantīva marutaḥ asmān mṛḷayantu*: the gods who come to a sacrifice, the Marut-gods who shine, as those who go to the sacrifice before anyone else, may keep us, sacrificers, in great happiness; thus the prayer.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *tośatamāḥ* (root *tuṣa prītau*; affix *ac* by "*nandigrahipacādibhyaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 3-1-134 [?]; *guṇa* by "*pugantalaghūpadhasya ca*"; in the Veda *ṣ* is replaced by *ś*; *atiśayena tośāḥ tośatamāḥ*; the affix *tamap* in the sense of excess; being *p*-marked it is unaccented; in the second meaning the root is *tuśa* in the sense of killing; the process is as before); *praṇetāraḥ* (root *ṇīñ prāpaṇe*; *tṛc* in the agent sense; *guṇa* of the root's *ī* on that occasion; accent on the last syllable because it is *c*-marked; in a *prādi* compound the latter member keeps its accent as a *kṛdutarapada*).

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्रति प्र याहीन्द्र मीळ्हुषो नॄन्महः पार्थिवे सदने यतस्व ।
> अध यदेषां पृथुबुध्नास एतास्तीर्थे नार्यः पौंस्यानि तस्थुः ॥ ६ ॥

> *prati pra yāhīndra mīḷhuṣo nṝnmahaḥ pārthive sadane yatasva |*
> *adha yadeṣāṃ pṛthubudhnāsa etāstīrthe nāryaḥ pauṃsyāni tasthuḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्रति । प्र । याहि । इन्द्र । मीळ्हुषः । नॄन् । महः । पार्थिवे । सदने । यतस्व ।
> अध । यत् । एषाम् । पृथुऽबुध्नासः । एताः । तीर्थे । न । अर्यः । पौंस्यानि । तस्थुः ॥ ६ ॥

> *prati | pra | yāhi | indra | mīḷhuṣaḥ | nṝn | mahaḥ | pārthive | sadane | yatasva |*
> *adha | yat | eṣām | pṛthu 'budhnāsaḥ | etāḥ | tīrthe | na | aryaḥ | pauṃsyāni | tasthuḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र त्वं मीळ्हुष उदकसेक्तॄन्नॄन्नेतॄन्नराकारान्महो महतो मेघान् प्रति प्र याहि । अभिगच्छ । मेघानां वृत्ररूपेण नराकारत्वं युक्तम् । गत्वा च पार्थिवे सदने । पृथिवीत्यन्तरिक्षनाम । तत्संबन्धिनि स्थाने यतस्व । प्रयत्नं कुरु । तैः सह युध्यस्वेत्यर्थः । यद्वा । हविष्प्रदातॄन् कर्मनिर्वाहकान् महतो यजमानान् प्रति गच्छ । गत्वा च पार्थिवे सदने देवयजने यतस्व । यत्नं कुरु हविर्भोजनाय । अथापि यदैषां त्रैत्नाहाय्यकारिणां मरुतां संबन्धिनः पृथुबुध्नासो विस्तीर्णमूला एताः पृषद्वर्णा गन्तारो वाश्वा अर्योऽरेः शत्रोः पौंस्यानि तीर्थे न युद्धमार्ग इव तस्थुः तिष्ठन्ति मेघानाक्रमन्ते । यद्वा । येषां मरुतां पृथुबुध्नासो बृहन्मूला एताः कृष्णवर्णा मेघास्तिष्ठन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अर्योऽरणीयस्य स्वामिनः पौंस्यानि बलानि तीर्थे न राजवीथ्यां यथा तिष्ठन्ति तद्वत् ॥ [several words doubtful: त्रैत्नाहाय्यकारिणां, पृषद्वर्णा, अर्योऽरणीयस्य]

*Gist:* Indra is to go against the great man-shaped (cloud) foes and strive in the aerial abode; or to the sacrificers on earth for the oblations; the broad-rooted steeds of the Maruts stand like armies at a ford.

### Printed p. 166  (PDF 186)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 169".)*

**Pratipadārtha.** *atha yat* — when; *eṣām* — (of the Marut-gods who help you) of these; *pṛthubudhnāsaḥ* — broad-rooted (extended at the base); *etāḥ* — these variously coloured horses; *aryaḥ* — of the enemy; *pauṃsyāni* — armies (strengths); *tīrthe na* — as at a battle-ford (as they stand); [*or* *pṛthubudhnāsaḥ* — those of great roots; *etāḥ* — these black clouds; *aryaḥ* — of the master (the sacrificer); *pauṃsyāni* — forces; *tīrthe na* — as in the royal street]; *tasthuḥ* — stand; *(tadā* — then*)* *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *(tvam* — you*)* *mīḷhuṣaḥ* — those who shed water; *nṝn* — man-formed (clouds); *mahaḥ prati* — towards great clouds; *pra yāhi* — go; *(anantara* — afterwards*)* *pārthive sadane* — in the place of the atmosphere; *yatasva* — strive (make an effort in battle); [*or* *mīḷhuṣaḥ* — givers of oblations; *nṝn* — performers of rites; *mahaḥ* — honoured sacrificers; *prati pra yāhi* — go toward with the intention; *(tataḥ)* *pārthive sadane* — in the sacrificial hall belonging to the earth; *yatasva* — make an effort (to partake of the oblations)].

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, going against the great clouds of human form (in the form of Vṛtra and the like) that abide in the sky, fight with them (or: setting out toward the honoured sacrificers who offer oblations, strive in the sacrificial halls for the food of the oblations); at that time the broad-rooted horses belonging to the Marut-gods stand ready for your help, like the armies of an enemy standing at the battle-ford.

**English Translation (as printed):** Go, Indra, to the mighty rain-shedding leaders (of the clouds), and exert yourself in (your) aerial dwelling; for their broad-footed steeds stand (firm) like the manly energies of an enemy in the field of battle.

### Printed p. 167  (PDF 187)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 9".)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***mīḷhuṣaḥ*** — *udakasektṝn*: the word *mīḷha* is read among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-[?]). Here the sense "those who sprinkle waters" is explained.

***nṝn*** — *jagannetṝn narākārān vā*: the word *nara* is read among the names of man (Ni. 2-[?]). It is explained as "those who nourish (the world) abundantly", or as "those who have the form of men"; and by "*mahaḥ marutaḥ*" it is wished that Indra should face the clouds filled with greatness. Since the Nirukta-writers refer to the clouds by the word *vṛtra*, it is established that "*meghānāṃ vṛtrarūpeṇa narākāratvaṃ yuktam*" — for the clouds, in the form of Vṛtra, to have human shape is fitting.

***pārthive sadane yatasva*** — the word *pṛthivī* is read among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 1-[?]); "*pṛthivītyantarikṣanāma tatsaṃbandhini sthāne yatnaṃ kuru taiḥ saha yudhyasva*": "the word *pṛthivī* is a name of the atmosphere; make an effort in the place connected with it; fight with them": one kind of meaning, spoken as addressed to Indra. Sāyaṇa gives another: "*yadvā haviṣpradātṝn karmanirvāhakān mahato yajamānān pratigaccha gatvā ca pārthive sadane devayajane yatasva | havirbhojanāya yatnaṃ kuru*" — going to the great sacrificers who offer oblations and carry out the rites of the sacrifice, make an effort in the sacrificial hall belonging to the earth, in order to partake of the oblations. By this, for the words *pārthive sadane* the meaning in the first sense is "the region of the atmosphere" and in the second "the place of the worship of the gods, or the sacrificial altar in the form of the earth". The matter of the earth being the sacrificial altar is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā.

***eṣāṃ pṛthubudhnāsaḥ etāḥ aryaḥ pauṃsyāni tīrthe na tasthuḥ*** — *marutāṃ saṃbandhinaḥ vistīrṇamūlāḥ pṛṣadvarṇāḥ gantāro vā aśvāḥ arer śatroḥ yuddhamārga iva meghān ākramante*: the word *etaśa* is read among the names of the horse (Ni. 1-[?]); by the word *pṛṣatyaḥ* in "*pṛṣatyo marutām*" (Ni. 2-[?]) the vehicles of the Marut-gods are indicated as *pṛṣatyaḥ* (spotted deer). Here the horses of the Marut-gods are described as *pṛṣadvarṇāḥ* (spotted-coloured) and as having vast root (back) regions; as the armies of an enemy stand against the way of war, so they attack the clouds: this is one kind of meaning explained.

### Printed p. 168  (PDF 188)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 169".)*

In the second meaning: the word *aryaḥ* is read among the names of the lord (Ni. 3-[?]); so "*araṇīyasya svāminaḥ (yuddhodyamādinā) gamanaśīlānāṃ prabhor (balaṃ) senā rājavīthyāṃ yathā tiṣṭhanti*" — as the army (strength) of a lord who goes forth with the intention of fighting stands massed in the royal street; "*eṣāṃ marutāṃ pṛthubudhnāso bṛhanmūlāḥ etāḥ kṛṣṇavarṇāḥ meghāstiṣṭhanti*" — these clouds, belonging to the Marut-gods who give help to Indra, with vast root regions and black in colour, stand together: this meaning is explained.

The word *pauṃsyāni* is read among the names of strength, and *pauṃsye* among the names of war (Ni. 2-[?]). Here the meaning "army" is explained.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *mīḷhuṣaḥ* (root *miha secane*; by "*dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃśca*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-12 [?], the form ending in *kvasu* is given as irregular; before the accusative plural *śas*, *saṃprasāraṇa* by "*vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam*", the preceding form; the *u* is acute by the affix's accent); *pārthive* (*pṛthivyāḥ idaṃ pārthivam, tasmin*; the affix *āñ* in the sense of relation by "*pṛthivyā āñ ñau*" [as read]; because it is *ñ*-marked, the first syllable is acute by "*ñniti ādiḥ*"; *vṛddhi* of the first vowel on that occasion; loss of *ī*); *yatasva* (root *yatī prayatne*; *loṭ* 2nd singular, affix *thās*; *va* substituted for the *ṭi* part by "*thāso se*", Pā. Sū. 3-4-80 [?]; *nighāta* since it stands after a word ending in a verb); *pṛthubudhnāsaḥ* (a *karmadhāraya* compound; accent on the last syllable by "*samāsasya*"; *asuk* before *jas* by "*ājjaserasuk*"); *tīrthe* (root *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*; affix *thak* by an Uṇādi sūtra, "*pātṛtudi…*"; *i* for the root vowel by "*ṛta iddhātoḥ*", Pā. Sū. 7-1-100 [?]; *r* follows; accent on the last syllable by the affix; locative form); *aryaḥ* (the word *ari*; before the genitive, no *guṇa* and the like by "*jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam*"; *yaṇ* substitution; the ending takes the acute by "*udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-174 [?]).

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्रति घोराणामेतानामयासां मरुतां शृण्व आयतामुपब्दिः ।
> ये मर्त्यं पृतनायन्तमूर्म्यैर्ऋणावानं न पतयन्त सर्गैः ॥ ७ ॥

> *prati ghorāṇāmetānāmayāsāṃ marutāṃ śṛṇva āyatāmupabdiḥ |*
> *ye martyaṃ pṛtanāyantamūrmyairṛṇāvānaṃ na patayanta sargaiḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्रति । घोराणाम् । एतानाम् । अयासाम् । मरुताम् । शृण्वे । आऽयताम् । उपब्दिः ।
> ये । मर्त्यम् । पृतनाऽयन्तम् । ऊर्म्यैः । ऋणऽवानम् । न । पतयन्त । सर्गैः ॥ ७ ॥

> *prati | ghorāṇām | etānām | ayāsām | marutām | śṛṇve | ā 'yatām | upabdiḥ |*
> *ye | martyam | pṛtanā 'yantam | ūrmyaiḥ | ṛṇa 'vānam | na | patayanta | sargaiḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र ते संबन्धिनां घोराणां भयानकानां शब्दाभिमानानां [?] वैतानामेतवर्णानाम् [?] अयासामयमानानां गमनशीलानां मरुतामायतामागन्तॄणां मरुतामुपब्दिः । उप गुर्वादिसमीपे गम्यते ज्ञायते उपपद्यते इति वोपब्दिर्वाक् । शृण्वे । श्रूयते । कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ ते एव विशिष्यन्ते । ये मरुतो मर्त्यं मरणधर्माणमूर्म्यैः स्वरक्षणैरुदकनिगमनसाधनैर्वा पृतनायन्तं पृतनामात्मन इच्छन्तं वैरिणं मेघं वा सर्गैः सृष्ट्यैः [?] स्वकीयप्रहारविशेषैः पतयन्त । पातयन्ति । तेषामेव ध्वनिः श्रूयत इत्यर्थः । पातने दृष्टान्तः । सर्गैर्ऋणवानं न ॥ छन्दसीवनिपाविति वनिप् ॥ ऋणवन्तमधमर्णमृणिनमिव [?] । तं यथा पीडयित्वा तदीयं धनमुपहरन्ति तद्वत् । एवं महानुभावा मरुतस्त्वानुगा इतीन्द्रस्य स्तुतिः ॥

*Gist:* The sound of Indra's fearsome, dark-hued, swift Maruts is heard as they come; with their own blows they bring down the foe or the cloud, as men press a debtor and carry off his goods.

### Printed p. 170  (PDF 190)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 169".)*

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *ye* — which Marut-gods; *ūrmyaiḥ* — by protective acts; *pṛtanāyantam* — desiring victory in battle; *martyam* — the enemy of mortal nature; [*or* *ūrmyaiḥ* — by means of the flow of water; *pṛtanāyantam* — desiring victory in battle (to shed water); *martyam* — the impermanent cloud]; *sargaiḥ* — by (self-protecting) blows; *ṛṇāvānam na* — like a contemptible enemy (as one presses him); *patayanta* — they cause to fall downward (as rain); *(teṣām* — of such*)* *te* — your; *ghorāṇām* — fearsome (proud of their sound); *etānām* — of the variously coloured; *ayāsām* — of the moving; *āyatām* — of those who approach from before; *marutām* — of the Marut-gods; *upabdiḥ* — the sound as they near; *prati* — echoing; *śṛṇve* — is heard.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, the sound of your Marut-gods — fearsome, variously coloured, swift, coming from above — is heard echoing; they bring down, as in battle, the impermanent cloud that desires victory (in the form of the splitting of the cloud).

**English Translation (as printed):** The noise of the formidable, dark-coloured, swift-moving, and advancing Maruts, is everywhere echoed; (the noise) of them who strike down their mortal (foes), gathering in a host against them, by their self-defending blows, as (they strike down) a contemptible enemy.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***ghorāṇām*** — *bhayānakānāṃ śabdābhimānānāṃ vā*: those who cause fear, and those who produce abundant sound, are well known; thus the meaning is explained for *marutām*; and that the Marut-gods are of variegated appearance and always in motion. In describing their greatness he explains *ā yatām upabdiḥ āgantṝṇām, vāk śṛṇve śrūyate*: the sound of those who come to the sacrifice is heard.

***upabdiḥ*** — this word is read among the names of speech (Ni. 1-[?]); "*upa gurvādisamīpe gamyate jñāyate upapadyate iti vā*" — as it is known near a teacher and the like, or as it is acceptable (*upapadyate*), it is *vāk* ("speech"): thus Sāyaṇa explains.

### Printed p. 171  (PDF 191)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 9"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 7 continue.)*

***martyam*** — this word is read among the names of man (Ni. 2-[?]). Here, giving the sense "*maraṇadharmāṇam*" ("one who has the nature of dying"), it is used as a qualifier of the word *pṛtanāyantam*.

***ūrmyaiḥ pṛtanāyantam*** — the word *pṛtanā* is read among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]). Here two kinds of meaning are explained. First: the cloud, by its means for flowing (descent) of water, as though itself wishing to wage a battle by the means of water's movement, is of such a desire. Second: the enemy, wishing to wage war by means of his own protective devices — the Marut-gods are meant to strike clouds that wish to fight like enemies; *sargaiḥ* — by their own hurled blows (their arrows), *patayanta* — they cause to fall; this meaning is explained, and so "*teṣām eva dhvaniḥ śrūyate*": the sound of the Marut-gods striking the clouds is heard.

***sargaiḥ ṛṇavānaṃ na*** — *ṛṇavantam adhamarṇam iva*: as a person who is liable to pay a debt, a low-ranking enemy, is made to fall by blows (as when one is felled), so the Marut-gods make the clouds fall by their blows: thus a comparison is given concerning the felling of the cloud by the Marut-gods. *evaṃ mahānubhāvā marutaḥ tvadanugāḥ iti indrasya stutiḥ* — thus the Marut-gods, endowed with great greatness, are Indra's followers; Indra's greatness is shown to be excessive.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *ghorāṇām* (root *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; affix *ac* by an Uṇādi sūtra, "*saṃterac ghur ca*" [as read]; the substitute *ghur* for the root; *guṇa* of the light penultimate on that occasion; accent on the last syllable since it is *c*-marked; genitive plural); *etānām* (root *iṇ gatau*; affix *tan* by an Uṇādi sūtra [cited]; *guṇa* on that occasion; being *n*-marked, the first syllable is acute); *ayāsām* (root *aya gatau*; affix *ac* since it belongs to *pacādi*; accent on the last syllable since it is *c*-marked; the augment *suṭ* before the genitive plural by *vyatyaya*); *śṛṇve* (root *śru śravaṇe*; by "*vyatyayo bahulam*" the agent-affix in the passive; *laṭ* 3rd singular, affix *ta*; *e* for the *ṭi* part; *śṛ* substituted for the root by "*śruvaḥ śṛc*" [as read]; *śnu* inserted; the *t* of the affix dropped by "*lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu*", Pā. Sū. 7-1-41 [?]; *yaṇ* substitution; *nighāta* of the verb).

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वं मानेभ्य इन्द्र विश्वजन्या रदा मरुद्भिः शुरुधो गोअग्राः ।
> स्तवानेभिः स्तवसे देव देवैर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ ८ ॥

> *tvaṃ mānebhya indra viśvajanyā radā marudbhiḥ śurudho goagrāḥ |*
> *stavānebhiḥ stavase deva devairvidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वम् । मानेभ्यः । इन्द्र [?] । विश्वऽजन्या । रद । मरुत्ऽभिः । शुरुधः । गोऽअग्राः ।

> *tvam | mānebhyaḥ | indra [?] | viśva 'janyā | rada | marut 'bhiḥ | śurudhaḥ | go 'agrāḥ |*
> *stavānebhiḥ | stavase | deva | devaiḥ | vidyāma | iṣam | vṛjanam | jīra 'dānum ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र त्वं मानेभ्यो मानार्थम् । चित्रेनेत्यर्थः [?] ॥ तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी ॥ विश्वजन्या विश्वजन्यः ॥ सो रेफाकारः [?] ॥ विश्वे प्राणिन उत्पादनीया यस्य तादृशस्त्वं सर्वजनहितशक्त्या वा मरुद्भिः सह शुरुधः शोकस्य रोधयित्रीः शोषिका गोअग्रा गर्जितमुदकं वाग्रे पुरुतो यासां ता मेघपङ्क्तीः रद । विलिख । विदारय । हे देव द्योतमान त्वं स्तवानेभिः स्तूयमानैर्देवैरन्यैर्मरुदादिभिर्ऋत्विग्भिर्वा स्तवसे । स्तूयसे ॥ उभयत्र कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ विद्यामेत्ययं व्याख्यातः ॥

*Gist:* Indra, with the Maruts, for his own honour and the good of all, is to split the rows of water-bearing clouds that dry up sorrow; praised by the other gods and priests, may we obtain food, strength and long life through him.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *viśvajanyā* — benevolent to all; *tvam* — you; *marudbhiḥ* — with the Marut-gods; *śurudhaḥ* — those that obstruct grief (the streams from the clouds, which remove sorrow with rain); *go-agrāḥ* — clouds that have water in front (thundering); *mānebhyaḥ* — for your own honour (and); *(viśvajanyā* — for the good of all*)*; *rada* — split; *(he)* *deva* — O shining Indra; *tvam* — you; *stavānebhiḥ* — by those who are praised; *devaiḥ* — by the Marut-gods and other gods; [*or* *stavānebhiḥ* — by those who are praising; *devaiḥ* — by the priests]; *stavase* — are praised; *(vayam* — we*)* *iṣam* — food; *vṛjanam* — strength; *jīradānum* — long life; *vidyāma* — (by your favour) may we obtain.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, accompanied by the Marut-gods, for your own honour and for the good of all, split the rows of clouds that have water in front and that hold back sorrow, and thus make them rain; as the shining one, you are praised by the Marut-gods and other gods (or priests); may we too, by your favour, obtain food, strength and long life.

**English Translation (as printed):** Associated with the Maruts, Indra, for your own honour and the good of all, pierce the exhilarating receptacles of the waters, for you, Indra, are glorified by the lauded divinities: may we obtain for you food, strength, and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***mānebhyaḥ*** — *mānārthaṃ citreṇa*: the Nirukta-writer, explaining the word *māna*:

> देवानां माने प्रथमा अतिष्ठन् कृन्तत्रादेषामुपरा उदायन् ।
> त्रयस्तपन्ति पृथिवीमनूपा द्वा बबूकं वहतः पुरीषम् ॥

> *devānāṃ māne prathamā atiṣṭhan kṛntatrād eṣām uparā udāyan |*
> *trayas tapanti pṛthivīm anūpā dvā babūkaṃ vahataḥ purīṣam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-3). Here, for the words *devānāṃ māne*, the sense of *nirmāṇa* ("construction") is given for the word *māna*. Sāyaṇa gives the sense "for honour" for *māna*, and says "*citreṇa*" in explanation.

***viśvajanyā*** — *viśvajanyaḥ*: Yāska explains the word *viśvajanya* in the ṛk

> उदु ज्योतिरमृतं विश्वजन्यं विश्वानरः सविता देवो अश्रेत् ॥

> *ud u jyotir amṛtaṃ viśvajanyaṃ viśvānaraḥ savitā devo aśret ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-53-2 [?]), as the sense "*sarvalokahitam*" ("beneficial to all the world") has been explained by Durgācārya: "*viśve prāṇinaḥ utpādanīyāḥ yasya*" — he whose power is to create all beings is *viśvajanya*; or the power related to him is *viśvajanīya*; and, "*sarvajanahitaśaktyā*", Indra, who has a power beneficial to all people: "*go agrāḥ garjitamudakaṃ vā agre yāsāṃ tā meghapaṅktīḥ*" — the rows of clouds that have thunder or water before them; he explains that, together with the Marut-gods, Indra should *rada* — split — them.

***śurudhaḥ*** — *śokasya rodhayitrīḥ śoṣikāḥ*: Yāska, citing the ṛk

> ऋतस्य हि शुरुधः सन्ति पूर्वीः

> *ṛtasya hi śurudhaḥ santi pūrvīḥ*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-23-8 [?]), gives for the word *śurudha* the sense "*śurudha āpo bhavanti śucaṃ saṃrundhanti*": the waters stop sorrow, destroy distresses. Here Sāyaṇa explains the same sense, "those that hold back or destroy griefs".

***stavase*** — Indra is addressed by the word *deva*, because he shines; "*devaiḥ anyaiḥ marudādibhiḥ ṛtvigbhirvā stūyase*" — praised by the other gods beginning with the Maruts who praise, and by the priests: the great glory of Indra is described.

***vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum*** — by this sentence it is said that the sacrificers wish to obtain, through Indra's favour, food, strength, victory and a gift-giving power, and, as the sacrifice will be completed by the coming of the gods, that they may obtain them. The word *vṛjana* is read among the names of strength (Ni. 2-[?]).

## Sūkta 170 — *na nūnam asti* (Anuvāka 23, sixth Sūkta; 5 ṛks)

*(Heading, p. 175: "The hundred and seventieth Sūkta" — ನೂರ ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> न नूनमस्तीति पञ्चर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तमागस्त्यमैन्द्रम् । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । न नूनं पञ्चागस्त्येन्द्रे हविषि मरुतामुद्यत इन्द्रागस्त्ययोः संवादे ऐन्द्रस्तत्राद्या तृतीया चेन्द्रवाक्यं चतुर्थी चादौ बृहती तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभ इति । सूक्तस्येन्द्रागस्त्यसंवादरूपत्वादाद्या तृतीया चतुर्थी चेन्द्रवाक्यम् । अतस्तासां यस्य वाक्यं तेन स ऋषिः । शिष्टे अगस्त्यवाक्ये । अतस्तयोः स एवर्षिः । आद्या च बृहती केतसिस्रोऽनुष्टुभः [?] । अन्त्याविशेषात् त्रिष्टुप् ॥ विशेषविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥ अत्र यास्कः । अगस्त्य इन्द्राय हविर्निरुप्य मरुद्भ्यः संप्रदित्सां चकार स इन्द्र एत्य परिदेवयां चक्रे । नि. १-३ [?] । इति ॥

*Gist:* The sixth sūkta (*na nūnam asti*), of five ṛks, by Agastya, to Indra; a dialogue between Indra and Agastya about an oblation meant for the Maruts; the first ṛk is a bṛhatī, the next three anuṣṭubh, the last triṣṭubh (as read).

### Printed p. 176  (PDF 196)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 170".)*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This Sūkta beginning *na nūnam asti* is the sixth Sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has five ṛks. Agastya and Indra are the ṛṣis of this Sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "*na nūnaṃ pañcāgastyendre haviṣi marutām udyata indrāgastyayoḥ saṃvāde aindras tatrādyā tṛtīyā cendravākyaṃ caturthī cādau bṛhatī tisro'nuṣṭubha*" [as read]. Since this Sūkta is a dialogue between Indra and Agastya, the first, third and fourth ṛks are Indra's words; hence the ṛṣi of those ṛks is Indra. The remaining ṛks — that is, the second and fifth — being Agastya's words, Agastya himself is the ṛṣi of them. The first ṛk is of the Bṛhatī metre; the three that follow are of the Anuṣṭubh metre; the last ṛk is of the Triṣṭubh metre. The special application (*viniyoga*) is indicated by the indicatory sign (*laiṅgika*). In this matter Yāska says in his Nirukta: "*agastya indrāya haviḥ nirupya marudbhyaḥ saṃpraditsāṃ cakāra sa indra etya paridevayāṃ cakre*" (Ni. 1-[?]) — that is, Agastya, having prepared an oblation for Indra, wished to give it to the Marut-gods; whereupon Indra came and, in anger, reproached Agastya for this action, in a manner of non-acceptance (*agrahapūrvaka* [as read]).

**॥ ॐ ॥** Sūkta—170
Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 23 ‖ Sūkta 170 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 10 ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 5 · Ṛṣi: ṛks 1, 3, 4 Indra; ṛks 2, 5 Agastya · Devatā: Indra · Chandas: ṛk 1 *bṛhatī*; ṛks 2–4 *anuṣṭubh*; ṛk 5 *triṣṭubh*.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतम् ।
> अन्यस्य चित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं वि नश्यति ॥ १ ॥

> *na nūnamasti no śvaḥ kastadveda yadadbhutam |*
> *anyasya cittamabhi saṃcareṇyamutādhītaṃ vi naśyati ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> न । नूनम् । अस्ति । नो इति । श्वः । कः । तत् । वेद । यत् । अद्भुतम् ।
> अन्यस्य । चित्तम् । अभि । सम्ऽचरेण्यम् । उत । आऽधीतम् । वि । नश्यति ॥ १ ॥

> *na | nūnam | asti | no iti | śvaḥ | kaḥ | tat | veda | yat | adbhutam |*
> *anyasya | cittam | abhi | sam 'careṇyam | uta | ā 'dhītam | vi | naśyati ‖ 1 ‖*

### Printed p. 177  (PDF 197)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 10"; a signature mark "XIII 12" is printed at the foot.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> परिदेवनप्रकारः प्रतिपाद्यते । इन्द्र आह । अद्येतेनं [?] यदस्ति तन्नूनमद्य नास्ति । नूनमत्र विचिकित्सार्थे । अत्राद्येति यद्यपि नास्ति तथाप्युत्तरवाक्ये श्व इति दर्शनादद्येति गम्यते । तथा श्वोऽपि नूनं नो । उशब्दोऽवधारणे । श्वस्तनमपि नैव नास्ति । अद्य यथास्मदर्थं निरुप्तमस्मभ्यं नास्ति किल श्वः कथं लप्स्यत इति भावः । यदद्भुतमन्यस्मै निरुप्यान्यस्मै दत्तमिति यदस्ति वैपरीत्यं तत्को वेद । यद्वा । यदद्भुतं भावि कार्यं यदस्ति तत्को वेद । अद्य श्वो वा लभ्यत इत्याशा न कार्येत्युक्तं भवति । तदेवाह । अभि सञ्चरेण्यं सर्वतः सञ्चार्यस्यान्यस्य चित्तं मानसं जानातीति शेषः । उतापि चाधीतमाध्यातं [?] चिन्तितमपि न दृश्यं [?] किमु सकृत्स्पृष्टं वि नश्यतीति ॥

*Gist:* Indra laments: what exists today is not certain, nor what will be tomorrow; who can know such a wonder (that what was prepared for one is given to another)? The mind of another is unsteady, and even what was well studied is forgotten.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(adya* — what may happen today*)* ; *nūnam* — certainly; *nāsti* — is not known; *śvaḥ* — tomorrow (what may happen, too); *no* — will not be known (so); *yat adbhutam* — what wonderful matter; *tat* — that; *kaḥ* — what man by himself; *veda* — can know?; *abhi* — everywhere (in all subjects); *saṃcareṇyam* — moving about; *anyasya* — of another man; *cittam* — the mind; *(jānāti* — knows?*)* ; *uta* — also; *ādhītam* — that which has been well practised; *vi naśyati* — is lost (forgotten in the course of time).

**Bhāvārtha.** (Indra speaks thus:) O Agastya, what will happen today or tomorrow is not known to anyone. Who by himself can know such a wonderful matter (that is, the events that will occur in the future)? How, then, could one know the mind of another man who is engaged in various activities? It cannot be; for even a matter that has been well practised is forgotten in the course of time.

**English Translation (as printed):** (Indra speaks),— It is not certain what to-day or what tomorrow will yield to us: who comprehends this mystery? Verily, the mind of any other (being) is of an unsteady (nature), and even that which has been profoundly studied, is (in time) forgotten.

### Printed p. 178  (PDF 198)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 170".)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***na nūnam*** — *adyatanaṃ yadasti tadadya nāsti | nūnamatra vicikitsārthe*: among the three kinds of divisions made by time — past, present, future — the meaning is that the division belonging to the present, "today", does not exist. In this ṛk the word *adya* ("today") is not used. Even so, since in the following sentence the word *śvaḥ* ("tomorrow"), denoting future time, is used, Sāyaṇa explains that it is proper to supply (*adhyāhāra*) the word *adya* in this sentence: "*adya iti yadyapi nāsti tathāpi uttaravākye śvaḥ iti darśanāt adyeti gamyate*". Yāska says:

> नूनमिति विचिकित्सार्थीयो भाषायामुभयमन्वध्यायं विचिकित्सार्थीयश्च पदपूरणश्च

> *nūnam iti vicikitsārthīyo bhāṣāyām ubhayam anvadhyāyaṃ vicikitsārthīyaś ca padapūraṇaś ca*

(Ni. 1-[?]) — the word *nūnam* is used in the sense of doubt (*vicikitsā*) in the ordinary language also, and in the Veda (*chandas*) it is used both in the sense of doubt and in the sense of a filler (*padapūraṇa*): thus he explains. Durgācārya explains the word *vicikitsā* as "*vicikitsā nāma vivekapūrvako avadhāraṇābhiprāyaḥ*" — doubt is, in situations where doubt arises, the intention of arriving at a decision through deliberation. Sāyaṇa supports that here the word *nūnam* is used in the sense of *vicikitsā*.

***śvaḥ nūnaṃ na*** — *tathā śvastanam api naiva nāsti*: just as there is no division made by present time, the designation of future time, *śvaḥ* ("tomorrow"), is also absent: this meaning is explained. Here Sāyaṇa cites Yāska:

> अत्र यास्कः—अगस्त्य इन्द्राय हविर्निरुप्य मरुद्भ्यः संप्रदित्सां चकार स इन्द्र एत्य परिदेवयाञ्चक्रे

> *atra yāskaḥ—agastya indrāya havirnirupya marudbhyaḥ saṃpraditsāṃ cakāra sa indra etya paridevayāñcakre*

(Ni. 1-[?]) — Yāska says that when the sage Agastya had prepared an oblation for Indra and wished to give it to the Marut-gods, Indra, since the oblation prepared for him was to be offered to others, lamented his sorrow; the meaning that this is indicated by this mantra is given, and he quotes this statement.

***adya yathā asmadarthaṃ niruptam asmabhyaṃ nāsti kila śvaḥ kathaṃ lapsyate*** — "today the oblation prepared for us is not available to us; how shall it be obtained tomorrow?": the manner of Indra's grief is described thus: "Having prepared the oblation for me today, when I did not get it, how can I hope that I shall get it tomorrow?"

***yadadbhutaṃ tat ko veda*** — *anyasmai nirupyānyasmai dattam iti yadasti vaiparītyaṃ tat ko veda*: that one prepares an oblation for one and gives it to another — who can know such a reversal? (continued on the next page).

---

### Printed p. 179  (PDF 199)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 10"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue.)*

(*yadadbhutaṃ tat ko veda* continued) … no one knows that an event of this kind (the abnormal change in an oblation) will take place: thus one kind of meaning is explained. ***yadvā yadadbhutaṃ bhāvi kāryaṃ yadasti tat ko veda adya śvo vā labhyate ityāśā na kāryā*** — "who knows which wonder-causing event will come about in future time? Therefore no hope should be held, either now or tomorrow, that the oblation prepared for me will be obtained": it is said that this is Indra's sorrowful remark; Sāyaṇa explains the second meaning also.

***abhi saṃcareṇyaṃ cittaṃ*** — *sarvataḥ saṃcārī anyasya mānasam*: the mind of others is of a nature always to move, and there is no stability; so he understands that, because of this, what has been prepared for me now is not obtained. ***uta api ca ādhītaṃ vinaśyati*** — "though I, Indra, was sure that the oblation I prepared for myself would reach me, it is lost (it will be destroyed), and does not reach me; who knows beforehand such a wonderful non-receipt of this oblation?": thus Indra's words, indicating distress, are described.

Yāska, citing this ṛk, explains it. In this explanation the sense that the word *nūnam* is used in the sense of doubt (the sense of decision) is shown:

> न नूनमस्त्यद्येतेनं नो एव श्वस्तनम् । अद्य अस्मिन् द्यवि द्युरित्यह्नो नामधेयं द्योतत इति सतः । श्व उपाशंसनीयः कालः । ह्यो हीनः कालः । कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतं कस्तद्वेद यदभूत् । इदमसीतरदद्भुतमभूतेनिव [?] । अन्यस्य चित्तमभिसंचरेण्यम् अभिसंचारि ॥ अन्यो नानेयः । चित्तं चेततेः । उताधीतं विनश्यतीति । अप्याध्यातं विनश्यतीति । अध्यातम् अभिप्रेतम् ॥ [as read; garbled in places]

> *na nūnamastyadyetenaṃ no eva śvastanam | adya asmin dyavi dyurityahno nāmadheyaṃ dyotata iti sataḥ | śva upāśaṃsanīyaḥ kālaḥ | hyo hīnaḥ kālaḥ | kastadveda yadadbhutaṃ kastadveda yadabhūt | idamasītaradadbhutamabhūteniva [?] | anyasya cittamabhisaṃcareṇyam abhisaṃcāri ‖ anyo nāneyaḥ | cittaṃ cetateḥ | utādhītaṃ vinaśyatīti | apyādhyātaṃ vinaśyatīti | adhyātam abhipretam ‖ [as read; garbled in places]*

(Ni. 1-[?]). The word *nūnam* conveys a decision, after discriminating deliberation. The word *dyavi*, formed from the root *dyut* meaning "to shine", denotes *ahas* (the day), and here the form belonging to "today" is indicated by it: what is decided to occur in the daytime is not obtained; in the same way, since the hope was that it would be fulfilled, there is no certainty about even the future time that the oblation will reach me. The word *śvaḥ* denotes a time to be hoped for (*upāśaṃsanīya*); *hyaḥ* denotes a past (*hīna*) time; for *adbhuta*, the past sense *abhūt* ("was") is explained; "now what was prepared for me is not for me; in the future also — to whom does it come, to me or to another? who knows this with certainty?" thus he says.

### Printed p. 180  (PDF 200)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 170".)*

(*anyasya cittam* continued) — the mind of another is given to wandering, of a restless nature; therefore it is meant that what has been prepared now will not reach me. It is also said that the words *uta*, *api* and *atha* are, in the Veda, synonymous words that convey one and the same sense. For the words *adya*, *śvaḥ*, *hyaḥ*, *adbhutam*, *anyaḥ*, *cittam*, *ādhītam* the explanation of meaning given is: "*dyotata iti sataḥ*"; "*śvaḥ upāśaṃsanīyaḥ kālaḥ*"; "*hyaḥ hīnaḥ kālaḥ*"; "*adbhutam abhūt*"; "*anyaḥ nāneyaḥ*"; "*cittaṃ cetateḥ*"; "*ādhyātam abhipretam*".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *asti* (since the *nighāta* is prevented by "*nipātair yad yadihanta…*", Pā. Sū. 8-1-30 [?], the accent of the root remains); *veda* (root *vida jñāne*; the substitute *ṇal* for the 3rd person singular of *laṭ* by "*vido laṭo vā*", Pā. Sū. 3-4-83 [?]; *guṇa* of the light penultimate; *nighāta* of the verb); *adbhutam* (root *bhū sattāyām*; when *ad* is the first member, the affix *ḍutac* by "*adi bhuvo ḍutac*" (Uṇ.); because of the *ḍ* marker the *ū* of the *ṭi* part is dropped; the first syllable is acute by *vyatyaya*); *saṃcareṇyam* (root *cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ*; the preverb *sam*; by *bahulagrahaṇa* the Uṇādi affix *enya*; the first syllable of the affix is acute; in a *prādi* compound the latter member keeps its accent); *ādhītam* (root *iṅ adhyayane*; *kta* in the passive; the preverb keeps its accent by "*gatir anantaraḥ*", Pā. Sū. 6-2-49 [?]); *naśyati* (root *naśa adarśane*; *laṭ* 3rd singular; *nighāta* of the verb). ‖ 1 ‖

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> किं न इन्द्र जिघांससि भ्रातरो मरुतस्तव ।
> तेभिः कल्पस्व साधुया मा नः समरणे वधीः ॥ २ ॥

> *kiṃ na indra jighāṃsasi bhrātaro marutastava |*
> *tebhiḥ kalpasva sādhuyā mā naḥ samaraṇe vadhīḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

---

### Printed p. 181  (PDF 201)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 10".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> किम् । नः । इन्द्र । जिघांससि । भ्रातरः । मरुतः । तव ।
> तेभिः । कल्पस्व । साधुऽया । मा । नः । सम्ऽअरणे । वधीः ॥ २ ॥

> *kim | naḥ | indra | jighāṃsasi | bhrātaraḥ | marutaḥ | tava |*
> *tebhiḥ | kalpasva | sādhu 'yā | mā | naḥ | sam 'araṇe | vadhīḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> इदमगस्त्यवाक्यम् । हे इन्द्र नोऽस्मान् अनपराधिनः किं जिघांससि । हन्तुमिच्छसि । कथमवध्यत्वमिति अत आह । मरुतस्तव भ्रातरः । त्वया भोगप्रदानेन भरणीया [?] इत्यर्थः । अतो वयमवध्या इत्युक्तं भवति । मरुतामिन्द्रभ्रातृत्वमेकस्मिन्नेवादितिगर्भ उत्पन्नत्वात् । सा चोत्पत्तिः पुराणादिषु प्रसिद्धा । सन्तु भ्रातरस्तथापि किमिति अत आह । तेभिस्त्वैर्मरुद्भिः सह साधुया साधु त्वं कल्पस्व । कल्पय हविर्भागं तैः सह युद्धं वा [?] । नोऽस्मान् समरणे संग्रामे मा वधीः । मा हिंसीः । यद्वा । लुप्तोपमा दृष्टान्तः । संग्रामे यथा विरोधिनं हंसि न तथास्मानिति ॥

*Gist:* This is Agastya's speech: Indra, why do you wish to slay us, who are blameless? The Maruts are your brothers, born of the same womb; be on good terms with them and share the oblation, and do not kill us in battle.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *marutaḥ* — the Marut-gods; *tava bhrātaraḥ* — your brothers (those nourished by you); *naḥ* — (blameless) us; *kim* — for what reason; *jighāṃsasi* — do you wish to kill?; *tebhiḥ* — with those Marut-gods; *sādhuyā* — in a peaceful way; *kalpasva* — (the portion of the oblation) cause to be shared; *naḥ* — us; *saṃ araṇe* — in battle (in the fight); *mā vadhīḥ* — do not kill (do not slay).

**Bhāvārtha.** (Agastya says to Indra:) O Indra, the Marut-gods are among those nourished by you (your brothers); why do you wish to kill us, who are blameless? Share the oblation with them in peace; do not kill us in battle (out of enmity).

**English Translation (as printed):** (Agastya),— Why, Indra, do you purpose to slay us: the Maruts are your brethren: share with them (the offering) in peace; destroy us not in enmity.

### Printed p. 182  (PDF 202)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 170".)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this Sūkta, which has the form of a dialogue between Indra and the sage Agastya, it is stated in the first mantra that Indra, learning that the sage Agastya has the intention of offering to the Marut-gods the oblation prepared for him, expressed his regret. By this mantra the reply that Agastya gave to Indra is expressed. This is what Sāyaṇa, in the bhāṣya, has explained as "*idam agastyavākyam*" ("this is Agastya's speech").

Addressing Indra, ***naḥ kiṃ jighāṃsasi*** — *asmān anaparādhinaḥ hantum icchasi kim*: "why do you wish to kill us, who have committed no fault?" — by putting this as a question, and by stating the reply that "since we, the sages, have done no wrong, we do not deserve punishment", he gives the reason, *marutaḥ tava bhrātaraḥ* — "the Marut-gods are your brothers". *Tvayā bhogapradānena bharaṇīyāḥ* — "the Marut-gods are to be supported by you through the giving of enjoyments": since they are nourished by you, we, who wish to offer oblations to your dependents, do not deserve to be punished: so the meaning is explained. Yāska says:

> भ्राता भरतेः [?] भरतिकर्मणो हरते भागं भर्तव्यो भवतीति वा

> *bhrātā bharateḥ [?] bharatikarmaṇo harate bhāgaṃ bhartavyo bhavatīti vā*

(Ni. 4-[?]) — the word *bhrātṛ*, formed from the root *bhṛ* (*bhṛñ*), is explained as one who obtains a share or one who is to be nourished (*bharaṇārha*). Sāyaṇa explains that the Marut-gods are Indra's brothers "*ekasminn eva aditigarbha utpannatvāt*" — because they were born in one and the same womb, the womb of the goddess Aditi, Indra's mother [as printed here; compare p. 148, where the origin of the Maruts is told of Diti] — and that "*sā ca utpattiḥ purāṇādiṣu prasiddhā*" — the order in which the Marut-gods came into being is well known in the Purāṇas and other books. This matter is stated also in the Bṛhaddevatā.

***tebhiḥ sādhuyā kalpasva*** — *taiḥ marudbhiḥ saha sādhutvaṃ kalpaya haviḥbhāgaṃ taiḥ saha yuddhaṃ vā*: Agastya, addressing Indra, says: "adopt a kind disposition toward your brothers, and grant them at least a share of the oblation; or else fight them".

***naḥ samaraṇe mā vadhīḥ*** — *asmān saṃgrāme yathā virodhinaṃ haṃsi*: "do not kill us as you kill an enemy in battle": thus the reply is given. In this sentence there is a view that the word expressing the comparison is dropped (*lupta-upamā*); and another meaning is given: "do not, by fighting, kill us, with whom there is no relation of comparison". The word *samaraṇa* is read among the names of battle (Ni. 2-[?]); "*saha maraṇaṃ yasmin*" — that in which the death of many beings occurs together at once — thus battle is described.

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> किं नो भ्रातरगस्त्य सखा सन्नति मन्यसे ।
> विद्मा हि ते यथा मनोऽस्मभ्यमिन्न दित्ससि ॥ ३ ॥

> *kiṃ no bhrātaragastya sakhā sannati manyase |*
> *vidmā hi te yathā mano 'smabhyaminna ditsasi ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 184  (PDF 204)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 170".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> किम् । नः । भ्रातः । अगस्त्य । सखा । सन् । अति । मन्यसे ।
> विद्म । हि । ते । यथा । मनः । अस्मभ्यम् । इत् । न । दित्ससि ॥ ३ ॥

> *kim | naḥ | bhrātaḥ | agastya | sakhā | san | ati | manyase |*
> *vidma | hi | te | yathā | manaḥ | asmabhyam | it | na | ditsasi ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> इदमिन्द्रवाक्यम् । हे भ्रातः हे अगस्त्य । हविष्प्रदानवरप्रदानाभ्यां परस्परोपकारत्वाद्भ्रातृत्वम् । तादृशस्त्वं सखा सन् अस्मद्धितकार्यपि सन्नोऽस्मान्निमति [?] मन्यसे । कस्मादपराधादतिक्रम्य मनुषे । अपलपसि । नायमपलापः । किंतु तथ्यमेवेति चेत् उच्यते । गन्तव्यं ते तव मनो मानसं यथा यथावत् सत्तद्विद्म । जानीमः । कथं जानीथेति उच्यते । अस्मभ्यमिन्न दित्ससि । अस्मदर्थं निरुप्तमस्मभ्यं दातुं नेच्छस्येव । इदेवार्थे ॥ [reading doubtful in places]

*Gist:* Indra's speech: Agastya, a friend and brother (through mutual boons), why do you slight me? We know your mind: you do not wish to give us what was prepared for us.

**Pratipadārtha.** *he bhrātaḥ agastya* — O brotherly Agastya; *sakhā san* — though a friend to me (though a benefactor); *naḥ* — us (me); *kim ati manyase* — why do you treat (me) with disregard?; *te* — your; *manaḥ* — mind; *yathā* — truly; *vidma hi* — we know well; *asmabhyam* — to us; *na dittsasi it* — you have no wish at all to give (oblations and the like).

**Bhāvārtha.** O brother Agastya, although you are a friend (a benefactor) to me, why do you disregard me? We know it well: you have no wish to give us oblations and the like.

**English Translation (as printed):** (Indra),—Wherefore, brother Agastya, do you, who are my friend, treat me with disregard? Verily, we know what is in your mind: you do not intend to give us anything.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

Sāyaṇa, explaining that Indra speaks these words, says that Indra addressed the sage Agastya as ***he bhrātaḥ*** ("O brother"), and that Indra's brotherhood with the sage Agastya is *haviṣpradānavarapradā-* (continued on the next page).

---

### Printed p. 185  (PDF 205)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 10"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 3 continue.)*

(*he bhrātaḥ agastya* continued) — …*nābhyāṃ parasparopakārakatvāt*: Indra grants boons, and the sage Agastya offers oblations to Indra; since this arises from mutually beneficial action, the brotherhood is thus supported.

***sakhā san naḥ kim ati manyase*** — by this sentence the reproach spoken by Indra is expressed: "since the two of us are of a reciprocally helpful disposition, *asmaddhitakāryapi san* — you, intent on doing us good, though you are attached (Agastya) to us, forgetting the intention you hold regarding us, *kasmād aparādham atikramya manuṣe*, *apalapasi* — you know that I have committed no offence. As you said before, if you place your trust in me, the share of the oblation will be offered to the Marut-gods. For this reason you commit a transgression with respect to me and impute it to me as my fault (that Indra has caused the Marut-gods to be without oblations)": this meaning is understood from the word *apalapasi*.

The intention stated in the preceding ṛk exposes Indra's own fault (the fault outside him), and, taking it as an offence of Agastya against Indra, "*nāyam apalāpaḥ kiṃtu tathyam eva*" ("this is not a denial but the very truth") is explained; its reply is stated by the next sentence.

***gantavyaṃ, te manaḥ yathā vidma*** — by the word *gantavya* it is suggested that Indra, having understood the intention of Agastya, either approved of it, or rejected it with contempt. "Your mind's intention is entirely known to me": thus it is explained. The intention of your mind — "*asmabhyam in na dittsasi*" — is that you do not wish to offer the oblation prepared for us to us; and by the sentence "*asmadarthaṃ niruptam asmabhyaṃ dātuṃ necchasyeva*", Indra supports that this is your offence, that you do not wish to give us what has been prepared for us: thus it is explained.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *manyase* (root *mana jñāne*, *divādi*; *laṭ* 2nd singular; *nighāta*); *vidma* (root *vida jñāne*, *adādi*; *laṭ* 1st plural, affix *mas*; *ma* substituted by "*vido laṭo vā*", Pā. Sū. 3-4-83 [?]; *luk* of *śap* by "*adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ*"; since it stands at the beginning of a *pāda* there is no *nighāta*; accent on the last syllable by the affix; the long vowel in the Saṃhitā by "*dvyacotastiṅaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 6-3-135 [?]); *dittsasi* (root *ḍudāñ dāne*; *san* in the sense of wish by "*dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā*"; reduplication by "*sanyaṅoḥ*"; the substitute *ī* for the *ā* of the root by "*sani mīmāghurabhalabhaśakapatapadām…*", Pā. #### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अरं कृण्वन्तु वेदिं समग्निमिन्धतां पुरः ।
> तत्रामृतस्य चेतनं यज्ञं ते तनवावहै ॥ ४ ॥

> *araṃ kṛṇvantu vediṃ samagnimindhatāṃ puraḥ |*
> *tatrāmṛtasya cetanaṃ yajñaṃ te tanavāvahai ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अरम् । कृण्वन्तु । वेदिम् । सम् । अग्निम् । इन्धताम् । पुरः ।
> तत्र । अमृतस्य । चेतनम् । यज्ञम् । ते । तनवावहै ॥ ४ ॥

> *aram | kṛṇvantu | vedim | sam | agnim | indhatām | puraḥ |*
> *tatra | amṛtasya | cetanam | yajñam | te | tanavāvahai ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> इदमिन्द्रवाक्यम् । अपरेऽगस्त्यवाक्यमाहुः । हे ऋत्विजो यूयम् अगस्त्योऽस्य [?] ज्ञीकेतवान् [?] तस्माद्वेदिमरं कृण्वन्तु । संमार्जनपर्युक्षणादिना परिचरन्तु । तथा पुरः पुरस्तादग्निमाहवनीयादिकं संमिन्धताम् । इध्मप्रक्षेपेण प्रज्वालयन्तु । तत्राग्नावमृतस्यामरणलक्षणस्य वेदत्वस्य [?] चेतनं प्रज्ञापकं यज्ञं हे अगस्त्य ते त्वदीयं त्वं चाहं च तनवावहै ॥ अगस्त्यवाक्यपक्षे शिष्टमवशिष्टम् । तत्र वेद्यामृतस्य तत्स्थापनस्य हविषो वा चेतनं प्रज्ञापनमासादनं कुरुत । आवां पत्नीयजमानौ अध्वर्युर्यजमानौ वा हे इन्द्र ते त्वदर्थं यज्ञं तनवावहै ॥ [reading doubtful in places]

*Gist:* Indra's speech (others say Agastya's): let the priests prepare the altar and kindle the fire in front; there let us two perform the sacrifice, which gives knowledge of the immortal.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he ṛtvijaḥ* — O priests (you)*)* ; *vedim* — the altar-ground (the altar); *araṃ kṛṇvantu* — adorn (with sweeping and the like); *puraḥ* — in front; *agnim* — the *āhavanīya* fire and the like; *saṃ indhantu* — kindle with fuel; *(O Agastya)* ; *tatra* — in that kindled fire; *amṛtasya* — of the immortal (knowledge of); *cetanam* — that which makes known (and); *te* — your

### Printed p. 187  (PDF 207)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 10".)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 4, concluded)* — *(te)* related to you; *yajñam* — the sacrifice; *tanavāvahai* — let us perform. [*tatra* — on the altar-ground; *amṛtasya* — of the oblation that accomplishes immortality; *cetanam* — make that tasting (that is, prepare the oblation); *(āvām* — the sacrificer, I, and my wife, or both of us, the priest and the sacrificer*)* ; *te* — for you; *yajñam* — the sacrifice; *tanavāvahai* — we shall perform.]

**Bhāvārtha.** O priests, decorate the altar-ground, kindle the *āhavanīya* and other fires with fuel; in that fire, O Agastya, let both of us (I, Indra, and you) together perform the sacrifice which makes known the immortal [*or*: prepare, on that altar-ground, the oblations and the like that accomplish immortality; afterwards, O Indra, let both of us — Agastya and I, or I and my wife, or I and the priests — perform the sacrifice for you].

**English Translation (as printed):** (Agastya),—Let the priests decorate the altar; let them kindle the fire to the east; and then let us both consummate the sacrifice, the inspirer of immortal (wisdom).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

*araṃ kṛṇvantu vediṃ, samagnim indhatāṃ puraḥ, yajñaṃ te tanavāvahai* — these sentences are, in one kind of meaning, explained as spoken by Indra to Agastya; in the second kind of explanation, it is described that the sage Agastya has said this to Indra.

Indra, addressing the priests, says: ***agastyo yat aṅgīkṛtavān tasmāt vediṃ araṃ kṛṇvantu*** — "since Agastya has agreed, on hearing my words, to offer me the oblation, you adorn the sacrificial altar by sweeping (*sammārjana*) and sprinkling (*paryukṣaṇa*) and the like; and ***purastāt āhavanīyāgniṃ idhmaprakṣepeṇa prajvālayantu*** — kindle the *āhavanīya* fire in front, by putting in fuel, with the sacrifices to the gods in view, so that the fuel may be offered in the *āhavanīya* fire": thus he has spoken.

***amṛtasya*** — *amaraṇalakṣaṇasya devatvasya*: the word *amṛta* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]), and among the names of gold (Ni. 1-[?]).

> रुशद्वत्सा रुशती श्वेत्यागादारैगु कृष्णा सदनान्यस्याः ।
> समानबन्धू अमृते अनूची द्यावा वर्णं चरत आमिनाने ॥

> *ruśadvatsā ruśatī śvetyāgād āraig u kṛṣṇā sadanāny asyāḥ |*
> *samānabandhū amṛte anūcī dyāvā varṇaṃ carata āmināne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-2). Here, for the word *amṛte*, "*amaraṇadharmāṇau*" — "those who are ever without death" — is explained.

### Printed p. 188  (PDF 208)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 170".)*

> वनस्पते रशनया नियूया पिप्यतेवयो वयुनानि विद्वान् ।
> वहा देवत्रा दिधिषो हवींषि प्र च दातारममृतेषु वोचः ॥

> *vanaspate raśanayā niyūyā pipyatevayo vayunāni vidvān |*
> *vahā devatrā didhiṣo havīṃṣi pra ca dātāram amṛteṣu vocaḥ ‖*

(Ni. 8-[?]). Here the sense "among the gods" is explained for *amṛteṣu*. It is said that the word means "those who are never subject to death and have the form of gods"; and by the sentence "*amṛtasya cetanaṃ yajñam*" the greatness of the sacrifice is described.

***te*** — since this word is a pronoun, it is explained that in Indra's sentence the sacrifice belongs to the sage Agastya, and that Indra and the sage Agastya together perform the sacrifice.

In the view that it is Agastya's speech to Indra, the meaning given for the word *te* is *tvadartham* — "for Indra"; "*vedyām amṛtasya tatsthāpanasya haviṣo vā cetanaṃ prajñāpanam āsādanaṃ kuruta*" — on the altar, prepare the materials and the oblations that accomplish a sacrifice which confers immortality; and "*āvāṃ patnī yajamānau adhvaryuyajamānau vā yajñaṃ tanavāvahai*" — it is explained that the wife and the sacrificer, or the *adhvaryu* and the sacrificer, together perform the sacrifice for Indra alone.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *kṛṇvantu* (root *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*; *loṭ* 3rd plural, *anta*; *u*-insertion; the affix *u* in place of the *a*-final by "*dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca*", Pā. Sū. 3-1-80 [?]; since the root is *it*-marked, *num* is inserted; *nighāta*); *vedim* (root *vida jñāne*; affix *in* by an Uṇādi sūtra, "*hṛṣipiruhivṛti…*"; *guṇa* of the light penultimate by "*pugantalaghūpadhasya ca*"; first syllable acute by "*ñnityādirnityam*"; accusative singular); *indhatām* (root *ñi indhī dīptau*; *loṭ* 3rd plural; *nighāta*); *cetanam* (root *citī saṃjñāne*; affix *lyuṭ*; *ana* for *yu* by "*yuvoranākau*"; *guṇa* of the light penultimate; the syllable before the affix is acute by "*liti*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 [?]).
