#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वमीशिषे वसुपते वसूनां त्वं मित्राणां मित्रपते धेष्ठः ।
> इन्द्र त्वं मरुद्भिः सं वदस्वाध प्राशान ऋतुथा हवींषि ॥ ५ ॥

> *tvamīśiṣe vasupate vasūnāṃ tvaṃ mitrāṇāṃ mitrapate dheṣṭhaḥ |*
> *indra tvaṃ marudbhiḥ saṃ vadasvādha prāśāna ṛtuthā havīṃṣi ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वम् । ईशिषे । वसुऽपते । वसूनाम् । त्वम् । मित्राणाम् । मित्रऽपते । धेष्ठः ।
> इन्द्र । त्वम् । मरुत्ऽभिः । सम् । वदस्व । अध । प्र । अशान । ऋतुऽथा । हवींषि ॥ ५ ॥

> *tvam | īśiṣe | vasu 'pate | vasūnām | tvam | mitrāṇām | mitra 'pate | dheṣṭhaḥ |*
> *indra | tvam | marut 'bhiḥ | sam | vadasva | adha | pra | aśāna | ṛtu 'thā | havīṃṣi ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> इदमगस्त्यवाक्यम् । हे वसूनां वसुपतेऽतिप्रभूतानां पुरोडाशाज्यादिधनानां स्वामिन् हे इन्द्र त्वमीशिषे । ईश्वरो भवसि । सर्वस्य वृत्त्यै वृत्तिभ्यां बहुत्वं नित्यं संबन्धश्च प्रतिपद्यते [?] । यद्वा । हे वसुपते वसूनामीशिष इति योजना । द्वितीयो वसुशब्दोऽनुवादो वा । तथा हे मित्राणां मित्रपतेऽस्मदादिमित्रस्य नित्यं पालकेन्द्र त्वं धेष्ठः । सर्वस्यातिशयेन धारकोऽसि । हे इन्द्र त्वमुक्तमहिमस्त्वं मरुद्भिः सं वदस्व । तैः सार्धं सम्यक्कृतमिति वदस्व । अधापि च त्वमृतुथा ऋतावृतौ । उपलक्षणमेतत्कालस्य । तत्तद्यागकाले हवींष्याज्यचर्वादीनि प्राशान प्रकर्षेण भुङ्क्ष्व ॥

*Gist:* Agastya's reply: Indra, lord of the wealth of oblations and best supporter of friends, speak well with the Maruts and eat the oblations in each season of sacrifice.

### Printed p. 190  (PDF 210)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 170".)*

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *vasūnāṃ vasupate* — lord of all wealth, such as *puroḍāśa*, *ājya* and the like, O Indra; *tvam* — you; *īśiṣe* — are the lord; *(he)* *vasupate* — O master of wealth; *tvam* — you; *vasūnām* — of wealth in the form of *puroḍāśa*, *ājya* and the like; *īśiṣe* — are lord; *(tathā* — likewise*)* *mitrapate* — O protector of all friends, Indra; *mitrāṇām* — of your friends (to us); *dheṣṭhaḥ* — (you are) the mighty supporter; *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *marudbhiḥ* — with the Marut-gods; *tvam* — you; *saṃ vadasva* — speak (saying that the act was well done); *adha* — and; *ṛtuthā* — according to the season (in the season of the sacrifice); *havīṃṣi* — oblations such as *ājya* and *caru*; *pra aśāna* — eat abundantly.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, you alone are lord of all wealth such as *puroḍāśa* and the like; and to friends such as us you are a mighty supporter; such as you are, in company with the Marut-gods, praise our act as well done, and, in their seasons, eat abundantly the oblations (offered by us) such as *ājya*.

**English Translation (as printed):** (Agastya),—You, Vasupati, are the lord of riches; you, Mitrapati, are the firm stay (of us), your friends: Declare, Indra, along with the Maruts, (your approval of our acts), and partake of the oblation offered in due season.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

This mantra is explained as spoken by the sage Agastya in reply to Indra's words.

***vasūnāṃ vasupate — tvam īśiṣe*** — *atiprabhūtānāṃ puroḍāśājyādidhanānāṃ svāmin tvam īśvaro bhavasi sarvasya | yadvā vasūnām īśiṣe | dvitīyo vasuśabdo anuvādo vā*: two kinds of meaning are explained for this sentence. In the first, Indra, by his abundant prosperity, is lord of wealth such as *puroḍāśa* and *ājya*, and of everything else, and is the master of all; here the first word *vasu* denotes excess (*atiśaya*). In the second meaning, it is explained that Indra is lord over the Vasus; the second word *vasu* is said to be an *anuvāda* (a restatement). Yāska says that the word *vasu* is a restatement, and has shown it by examples. Among the names of the guards (*rakṣin*), the word *vasavaḥ* is read.

> सुगा वो देवाः सुपथा अकर्म य आजग्मेदं सवनं जुषाणाः ।
> जक्षिवांसः पपिवांसश्च विश्वेऽस्मे धत्त वसवो वसूनि ॥

> *sugā vo devāḥ supathā akarma ya ājagmedaṃ savanaṃ juṣāṇāḥ |*
> *jakṣivāṃsaḥ papivāṃsaś ca viśve'sme dhatta vasavo vasūni ‖*

(Ni. 12-[?]). Here the gods are addressed by the word *vasavaḥ*; for the second word *vasu* the meaning "wealth" is stated.

---

### Printed p. 191  (PDF 211)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 10"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 5 continue.)*

> ज्मया अत्र वसवो रन्ते [?] देवा उरावन्तरिक्षे मर्जयन्त शुभ्राः [?] ।
> अर्वाक्पथ उरुज्रयः कृणुध्वं श्रोता दूतस्य जग्मुषो नो अस्य ॥ [as read]

> *jmayā atra vasavo rante [?] devā urāvantarikṣe marjayanta śubhrāḥ [?] |*
> *arvākpatha urujrayaḥ kṛṇudhvaṃ śrotā dūtasya jagmuṣo no asya ‖ [as read]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-3 [?]). Here the word *vasavaḥ* is explained as meaning *agni*.

***vasavaḥ ādityaraśmayaḥ vivasanāt syāt dyusthānāḥ*** (Ni. 12-[?]) — the word *vasu* is applied to the rays of the sun. And in the ṛk

> सुगुरसत्सुहिरण्यः स्वश्वो बृहदस्मै वय इन्द्रो दधाति ।
> यस्त्वायन्तं वसुना प्रातरित्वो मुक्षीजयेव पदिमुत्सिनाति ॥

> *sugurasat suhiraṇyaḥ svaśvo bṛhad asmai vaya indro dadhāti |*
> *yas tvāyantaṃ vasunā prātaritvo mukṣījayeva padim utsināti ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-125-2) the word *vasunā* is explained as *annena* ("by food"). By the sentence "*vṛttyā vṛttibhyāṃ bahutvaṃ nityasaṃbandhaś ca pratipādyate*" it is established that the multiplicity of wealth and the constant relation of Indra with wealth are proved.

***mitrapate*** — by this word, "*asmadādimitrasya nityaṃ pālakena*" — "the constant protector of friends such as us (Agastya himself and the others)" — is the sense, and Indra is addressed by it. ***tvaṃ dheṣṭhaḥ*** — *sarvasyātiśayena dhārako'si*: "you are the one who supports everything exceedingly, more than others do": thus the meaning is explained.

***marudbhiḥ saṃvadasva*** — *taiḥ sākaṃ samyak kṛtam iti vadasva*: "may the great Indra say, together with the Marut-gods, that the sacrifice has been well (closely) performed": this wish is expressed.

***ṛtuthā havīṃṣi prāśāna*** — *ṛtāv ṛtau tattadyāgakāle ājyacarvādīni prakarṣeṇa bhuṅkṣva*: "in each season, at each time of sacrifice, enjoy abundantly the *ājya*, *caru* and the like": the hope is expressed that at each sacrifice Indra will come and eat abundantly the oblations put into the fire.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *īśiṣe* (root *īśa aiśvarye*; *se* replaces the 2nd singular of *laṭ*; the augment *iṭ* by "*īśaḥ se*", Pā. Sū. 7-2-77 [?]; *ṣ* for the affix; *nighāta*); *dheṣṭhaḥ* (after the *tṛc*-ending word *dhātṛ*, the affix *iṣṭhan* in the sense of excess; the loss of *tṛc* by "*turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu*", Pā. Sū. 6-4-154 [?]; by "*prakṛtyaikāc*" there is *prakṛtibhāva*, so the *ṭi* part is not dropped; *guṇa*; first syllable acute because the affix is *ñ*-marked).

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 170".)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 5, continued; noted briefly)*: *vadasva* (root *vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci*; *ātmanepada* by "*vyaktavācāṃ samuccāraṇe*", Pā. ## Sūkta 171 — *prati va* (Anuvāka 23, seventh Sūkta; 6 ṛks)

*(Heading, p. 192: "The hundred and seventy-first Sūkta" — ನೂರ ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> प्रति व इति षडृचं सप्तमं सूक्तमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभं मारुतम् । आद्ये द्वे केवलमारुते । शिष्टाश्चतस्रो मरुत्वदिन्द्रदेवताकाः । प्रति वः षण्मारुतं तु चेतसोऽन्त्या मरुत्वतीया [?] इत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ विशेषविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

*Gist:* The seventh sūkta (*prati va*), of six ṛks, by Agastya, to the Maruts in triṣṭubh; the first two ṛks are to the Maruts alone, the other four to Indra with the Maruts.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This Sūkta beginning *prati va* is the seventh Sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has six ṛks. Agastya is the ṛṣi of this Sūkta; the Marut-gods are the deities; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The first two ṛks are addressed to the Marut-gods alone; the remaining four ṛks have Marut and Indra as deities. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "*prati vaḥ ṣaṇmārutaṃ tu cetaso'ntyā marutvatīyā*" [as read]. The special application (*viniyoga*) of this Sūkta is by the indicatory sign.

**॥ ॐ ॥** Sūkta—171
Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 23 ‖ Sūkta 171 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 11 ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 6 · Ṛṣi: Agastya · Devatā: ṛks 1–2 the Maruts; ṛks 3–6 Indra with the Maruts · Chandas: *triṣṭubh*.

### Printed p. 193  (PDF 213)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11"; a signature mark "XIII 13" is printed at the foot. The page opens with a note on the group of sūktas, quoting the Bṛhaddevatā.)*

**Note (Kannada).** In the first maṇḍala, the last 38 [?] sūktas are divided in the Bṛhaddevatā into two groups. From the 165th sūkta to the 170th, it tells in the form of a story the conversation that took place between Indra and the Marut-gods, and how, between them, the sage Agastya entered, praised the Marut-gods and Indra and brought them peace. From the 171st to the 1[8–9]? [?] it speaks of the sūktas composed in the course of showing the relationship and love between Agastya and Lopāmudrā. The nature of the conversation between Indra and the Marut-gods, and its description in the Bṛhaddevatā, has been shown earlier (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, Part 12, p. 679).

> स तानभिजगामाशु निरूप्यैन्द्रं हविस्तदा ।
> मरुतश्चाभितुष्टाव सूक्तैस्तन्निस्त्रिभिः [?] ॥

> *sa tānabhijagāmāśu nirūpyaindraṃ havistadā |*
> *marutaścābhituṣṭāva sūktaistannistribhiḥ [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-48 [?]). Agastya, as soon as he had heard their conversation, went himself towards them and had the oblation prepared for Indra. Together with it, he praised the Marut-gods with three sūktas composed of mantras beginning "*tan nu vocāma*" (1-166 to 1-168 [?]), it is described; and

> महश्चिदिति चैवेन्द्रं सहस्रमिति चैतया ।
> निरुप्तं तद्धि हिङ्कृत्येन्द्रं मरुद्भ्यो दातुमिच्छति ॥ [as read]

> *mahaściditi caivendraṃ sahasramiti caitayā |*
> *niruptaṃ taddhi hiṅkṛtyendraṃ marudbhyo dātumicchati ‖ [as read]*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-49 [?]). By the mantra "*mahaścit*" (1-169) he praised Indra, and by the mantra "*sahasram*" (1-167-1) he became ready to offer to the Marut-gods the oblation prepared for Indra. In the Nirukta this matter is told thus:

> अगस्त्य इन्द्राय हविर्निरुप्य मरुद्भ्यः संप्रदित्सां चकार । स इन्द्र एत्य परिदेवयां चक्रे ॥

> *agastya indrāya havirnirupya marudbhyaḥ saṃpraditsāṃ cakāra | sa indra etya paridevayāṃ cakre ‖*

(Ni. 1-[?]). By this, Indra, having found dissatisfaction, opposed it.

> विज्ञायावेक्ष्य तद्भावमिन्द्रो नेति तमब्रवीत् ।
> न श्वो नाद्यैतनं ह्यस्ति वेद कस्तद्यदद्भुतम् ॥

> *vijñāyāvekṣya tadbhāvamindro neti tamabravīt |*
> *na śvo nādyaitanaṃ hyasti veda kastadyadadbhutam ‖*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-50 [?]). Understanding this feeling, Indra rejected it with "*na nūnam asti*" (1-170). But since he refused it without making his purpose known, Agastya asks the question:

> कस्य चित्त्वर्थसंचारे चित्तनेव विनश्यति ।
> किं न इत्यब्रवीदिन्द्रमागस्त्योऽभ्रातरस्तव ॥ [as read; the lines continue on p. 194]

> *kasya cittvarthasaṃcāre cittaneva vinaśyati |*
> *kiṃ na ityabravīdindramāgastyo 'bhrātarastava ‖ [as read; the lines continue on p. 194]*

### Printed p. 194  (PDF 214)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

> मरुद्भिः संप्रकल्पस्व वधीर्मा नः शतक्रतो ।
> किं नो भ्रातरिति त्वस्यां इन्द्रो मान्यमुपालभत् ॥ [as read]
> अगस्त्यस्त्वरमित्येस्यां क्षुब्धमिन्द्रं प्रशामयत् ।
> प्रादात्सवनं कृत्वा तेभ्य एव च तद्धविः ॥

> *marudbhiḥ saṃprakalpasva vadhīrmā naḥ śatakrato |*
> *kiṃ no bhrātariti tvasyāṃ indro mānyamupālabhat ‖ [as read]*
> *agastyastvaramityesyāṃ kṣubdhamindraṃ praśāmayat |*
> *prādātsavanaṃ kṛtvā tebhya eva ca taddhaviḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-51 to 53 [?]). By this refutation, it is shown that his not making known his purpose was of no use; by the mantra "*kiṃ naḥ*" (1-170-2) he makes known that the Marut-gods, too, are Indra's friends. Afterwards, by the mantra "*kiṃ no bhrātaḥ*", when Indra is entreated, he is slightly angered and reproaches. Yet, with the mantra "*araṃ*" (1-170-4) he appeased Indra and offered a share of the oblation to the Marut-gods.

> सुते चकार सोमेऽथ तानिन्द्रः सोमपीथिनः ।
> तस्माद्विद्यान्निपातेन ऐन्द्रेषु मरुतः स्तुतान् ॥

> *sute cakāra some 'tha tānindraḥ somapīthinaḥ |*
> *tasmādvidyānnipātena aindreṣu marutaḥ stutān ‖*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-54). As soon as the *soma* was pressed, Indra apportioned it to the Marut-gods also and made them drink it. Therefore it must be understood that, even if Indra is praised in a sūkta, the Marut-gods are also praised in his company, as his attendants.

> प्रीतात्मा पुनरेवर्षिस्तांस्तुष्टाव पृथक् पृथक् ।
> मरुतः प्रति सूक्ताभ्यां इन्द्रं षड्भिः परैस्तु सः ॥

> *prītātmā punarevarṣistāṃstuṣṭāva pṛthak pṛthak |*
> *marutaḥ prati sūktābhyāṃ indraṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ paraistu saḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-55). By this, Agastya, who was satisfied, praised them again, separately: with two sūktas (1-171 and 1-172 [?]) he praised the Marut-gods; and with the sūktas from 1-173 to 1-178 [?] he praised Indra.

> स्तुतश्च तैर्भिश्चेन्द्र स्तुतास इति त्रैः सह ।
> मरुद्भिः सह मरुत्वांस्तत्र सोऽभवत् ॥

> *stutaśca tairbhiścendra stutāsa iti traiḥ saha |*
> *marudbhiḥ saha marutvāṃstatra so 'bhavat ‖*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-56). Four mantras (1-173-3 to 6 [?]) praise Indra. But since Indra needs the Marut-gods at every place, the epithet *marutvān* is natural to him: thus it is stated in the Bṛhaddevatā, and afterwards the loving conversation that took place between the sage Agastya and Lopāmudrā is described.

### Printed p. 195  (PDF 215)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11".)*

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्रति व एना नमसाहमेमि सूक्तेन भिक्षे सुमतिं तुराणाम् ।
> रराणता मरुतो वेद्याभिर्नि हेळो धत्त वि मुचध्वमश्वान् ॥ १ ॥

> *prati va enā namasāhamemi sūktena bhikṣe sumatiṃ turāṇām |*
> *rarāṇatā maruto vedyābhirni heḷo dhatta vi mucadhvamaśvān ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्रति । वः । एना । नमसा । अहम् । एमि । सुऽउक्तेन । भिक्षे । सुऽमतिम् । तुराणाम् ।
> रराणता । मरुतः । वेद्याभिः । नि । हेळः । धत्त । वि । मुचध्वम् । अश्वान् ॥ १ ॥

> *prati | vaḥ | enā | namasā | aham | emi | su 'uktena | bhikṣe | su 'matim | turāṇām |*
> *rarāṇatā | marutaḥ | vedyābhiḥ | ni | heḷaḥ | dhatta | vi | mucadhvam | aśvān ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः वो युष्मानहं प्रत्येमि । अभिगच्छामि । केन साधनेन । नमसा नमस्कारेण हविषा वा । नम इत्यन्ननाम । तथा सूक्तेन शोभनवचनेन स्तुतिरूपेण । तुराणां त्वरमाणानां शत्रूणां हिंसकानां वा युष्माकं सुमतिं शोभनां मतिमनुग्रहबुद्धिं भिक्षे । याचे । इन्द्रस्यैव पुनरर्विप्रदानादिदं याच्यते [?] । किंच हे मरुतः यूयं वेद्याभिर्वेदिकव्याभिः [?] स्तुतिभी रराणता रममाणेन मनसेत्थंभूताः सन्तो हेळः । क्रोधनामैतत् । क्रोधं युष्मदभिक्रमजनितं नि धत्त । निकृष्टं धारयत । त्यजतेत्यर्थः । तथाश्वान् वि मुचध्वम् । रथेभ्यो वियोजयत । क्रोधात्सुनिर्गमनं मा कुरुतेत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Agastya approaches the Maruts with homage and a hymn, begging their good will; with minds delighted by his praises they should lay down their anger and unyoke their horses.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *aham* — I; *enā namasā* — with this salutation or oblation (together with); *vaḥ* — to you; *prati emi* — I approach with that intention; *(tathā* — likewise*)* *sūktena* — with a good speech (in the form of praise); *turāṇām* — (for those who are eager) (in respect of enemies), or of those who harm; *sumatim* — (towards us) the mind of favour; *bhikṣe* — I ask; *(kiṃca* — and*)* *(he marutaḥ)* *vedyābhiḥ* — (by our) praises; *rarāṇatā* — with a delighted mind (being united with them); *heḷaḥ* — your anger; *ni dhatta* — lay down (give up); *(tathā* — and*)* *aśvān* — (chariot) horses; *vi mucadhvam* — unyoke (you, enraged, so that you may not come back from the chariot).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, I approach you with a salutation; praising you, I beg you to show favour to us; O Maruts, delighted by our praises, give up your anger; do not come to us in anger; and, likewise, unyoke your chariot horses.

### Printed p. 196  (PDF 216)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

**English Translation (as printed):** I approach you, Maruts, with this reverential homage, and with a hymn implore your favour against eager (foes): with minds pacified by our praises, suppress your anger, and let loose your horses.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***namasā*** — *namaskāreṇa haviṣā vā*: the word *namas* is read also among the names of food (Ni. 2-[?]). It is explained that the sage Agastya makes the Marut-gods content by saluting them and by offering oblations.

***sūktena turāṇāṃ sumatiṃ bhikṣe*** — *śobhanavacanena stutirūpeṇa tvaramāṇānāṃ śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsakānāṃ vā*: the word *tura* is explained by Yāska with the example

> प्रातर्जितं भगमुग्रं हुवेम वयं पुत्रमदितेर्यो विधर्ता ।
> आध्रश्चिद्यं मन्यमानस्तुरश्चिद्राजा चिद्यं भगं भक्षीत्याह ॥

> *prātarjitaṃ bhagam ugraṃ huvema vayaṃ putram aditer yo vidhartā |*
> *ādhraś cid yaṃ manyamānas turaś cid rājā cid yaṃ bhagaṃ bhakṣīty āha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-41-2). In this ṛk, "*tura iti yamanāma tarater vā tvarater vā*" — the word *tura*, formed from the root *tṝ* or the root *tvar*, is explained as denoting Yama, who is swift in destroying beings. Sāyaṇa explains this word as "those who harm", or "enemies": when Agastya had prepared an oblation for Indra and then offered it to the Marut-gods, Indra himself having taken it, he salutes the Marut-gods who act quickly — so that, in respect of him (Agastya), they may not perform the acts of enemies or harmful acts (that is, may not be angry) — offers them oblations, praises them with excellent speech, and prays for *sumati*, "the mind of favour", which indicates satisfaction, that they may show it toward him. The word *tura* is also used as a synonym of *śakti* ("power").

> सदिद्धि ते तुविजातस्य मन्ये सहः सहिष्ठ तुरतस्तुरस्य ।
> उग्रमुग्रस्य तवसस्तवीयोऽरध्रस्य रध्रतुरो बभूव ॥

> *sad id dhi te tuvijātasya manye sahaḥ sahiṣṭha turatas turasya |*
> *ugram ugrasya tavasas tavīyo 'radhrasya radhraturo babhūva ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-18-4 [?]). In this ṛk the word is used both in the sense of power and in the sense of killing. For the words *turataḥ turasya*, the explanation "*asmān hiṃsataḥ; śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsituḥ balavato vā*" is given: "one capable of subduing enemies who harm", as an epithet of Indra in the first half; and "*radhraturaḥ — vaśīkaraṇīyānāṃ sapatnānāṃ hiṃsakasya tava balam*" — your strength, as one who kills the enemies to be subdued — is used in the second half. And (continued on the next page)

### Printed p. 197  (PDF 217)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue.)*

> यं वर्धयन्तीद्गिरः पतिं तुरस्य राधसः ।
> तमिन्न्वस्य रोदसी देवी शुष्मं सपर्यतः ॥

> *yaṃ vardhayantīd giraḥ patiṃ turasya rādhasaḥ |*
> *tam in nv asya rodasī devī śuṣmaṃ saparyataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-44-5 [?]) — in it the meaning "of a powerful enemy" (*balavataḥ śatroḥ*) is given [as read]. And further,

> ता वामेषे रथानामिन्द्राग्नी हवामहे ।
> पती तुरस्य राधसो विद्वांसा गिर्वणस्तमा ॥

> *tā vām eṣe rathānām indrāgnī havāmahe |*
> *patī turasya rādhaso vidvāṃsā girvaṇastamā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-86-4 [?]). In ṛks of this kind, for *turasya rādhasaḥ* the meanings "*jaṅgamarūpasya dhanasya*" and "of wealth that moves, that is unstable" are given: the word is used as an epithet of things that are moving in nature, fit for transactions, and capable of quick movement. In ṛks like 1-61-13 [?] it is used as a synonym of Yama. In the present context it is an epithet of the Marut-gods, as "those who harm enemies".

The word *sumati* is explained by Yāska with the example

> धाता ददातु दाशुषे प्राचीं जीवातुमक्षिताम् ।
> वयं देवस्य धीमहि सुमतिं सत्यधर्मणः ॥

> *dhātā dadātu dāśuṣe prācīṃ jīvātum akṣitām |*
> *vayaṃ devasya dhīmahi sumatiṃ satyadharmaṇaḥ ‖*

(Ath. Saṃ. 7-17-2 [?]). In this ṛk and in other places Sāyaṇa has explained that it expresses the meaning *kalyāṇī matiḥ* ("an auspicious mind"). However, the word *sumati* is used not only in the sense of the mind of divine favour, but also in the sense of a prayer made by a man, or of a man's best wish. For example:

> तुभ्यं भरन्ति क्षितयो यविष्ठ बलिमग्ने अन्तित ओत दूरात् ।
> आ भन्दिष्ठस्य सुमतिं चिकिद्धि बृहत्ते अग्ने महि शर्म भद्रम् ॥

> *tubhyaṃ bharanti kṣitayo yaviṣṭha balim agne antita ota dūrāt |*
> *ā bhandiṣṭhasya sumatiṃ cikiddhi bṛhat te agne mahi śarma bhadram ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-10).

> प्र वो महे महिवृधे भरध्वं प्रचेतसे प्र सुमतिं कृणुध्वम् ।
> विशः पूर्वीः प्र चरा चर्षणिप्राः ॥

> *pra vo mahe mahivṛdhe bharadhvaṃ pracetase pra sumatiṃ kṛṇudhvam |*
> *viśaḥ pūrvīḥ pra carā carṣaṇiprāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-10). In ṛks of this kind, "*stotuḥ sutim ā jānīhi*" is explained as "know the praise of the praiser", and "*indrāya su ṣuṣṭutiṃ pra kurute*" as "he offers excellent praise toward Indra". And in

> यूयं न उग्रा मरुतः सुचेतुनारिष्टग्रामाः सुमतिं पिपर्तन ।
> यत्रा वो दिद्युद्रदति क्रिविर्दती रिणाति पश्वः सुधितेव बर्हणा ॥

> *yūyaṃ na ugrā marutaḥ sucetunāriṣṭagrāmāḥ sumatiṃ pipartana |*
> *yatrā vo didyud radati krivirdatī riṇāti paśvaḥ sudhiteva barhaṇā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-166-6).

### Printed p. 198  (PDF 218)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

in the ṛk explained earlier, for *sumatiṃ pipartana*, Sāyaṇa has explained "*śobhanabuddhiṃ pūrayata*" — "fulfil good understanding". Here "good understanding" cannot mean the mind of favour of the deities; and since *pipartana* is used, the meaning "fulfil our excellent desired objects" is natural. On this same ṛk 1-166-6 the scholar Max Müller says:

*In our passage the Verb* पिपर्तन, *fill or fulfil, indicates in what sense* सुमति *ought to be taken.* सुमतिं पिपर्तन *is no more than* कामं पिपर्तन. [S. B. E. XXXII. P. 221].

That is, "fulfil our desired object" is the meaning; and this meaning is natural. But in the present ṛk the words *sumatiṃ bhikṣe* would mean "I ask the Marut-gods for a mind of favour".

Addressing the Marut-gods by "*he marutaḥ*", ***vedyābhiḥ rarāṇatā*** — "with the praises recited by the sage Agastya, understanding his wish, *ramamāṇena manasā*, may they have minds in a state of joy": thus the meaning is explained.

***rarāṇatā*** — this word is formed from the root *raṇ*. In general it means a word of the form of praise (*stotra*), but in some contexts the word is also used in the sense of joy. The Nirukta-writers show this use, citing

> नाहमिन्द्राणि रारण सख्युर्वृषाकपेरृते ।
> यस्येदमप्यं हविः प्रियं देवेषु गच्छति विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ॥

> *nāham indrāṇi rāraṇa sakhyur vṛṣākaper ṛte |*
> *yasyedam apyaṃ haviḥ priyaṃ deveṣu gacchati viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-12 [?]), where for the word *rāraṇa* the sense "*ramasva*" ("rejoice") is given. Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "sound" in some places. For example:

> यः सोमं सख्ये तव रारणद्देव मर्त्यः ।
> तं दक्षः सचते कविः ॥

> *yaḥ somaṃ sakhye tava rāraṇad deva martyaḥ |*
> *taṃ dakṣaḥ sacate kaviḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-[?]). In such ṛks, "*raṇati etat tvayoktarūpeṇa tvāṃ stauti*" — "with this form of word (praise) he praises you" — is the explanation. Generally, the use in the sense of joy is the more frequent.

***heḷaḥ ni dhatta aśvān vi mucadhvam*** — the word *heḷas* is read among the names of anger (Ni. 2-[?]). The Marut-gods: "*yuṣmadabhikramajanitaṃ krodhaṃ nikṛṣṭaṃ dhārayata tyajata*" (continued).

### Printed p. 199  (PDF 219)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 conclude.)*

(*heḷaḥ ni dhatta* continued) — … they are begged to give up the anger arisen because they were transgressed against. And "***krodhāt punar gamanaṃ mā kuruta***": the prayer of the sage Agastya is expressed here, that the horses be unyoked from the chariots prepared for the coming to the sacrifice, and that, being angry, they should not go back.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *namasā* (root *ṇamu prahvatve śabde ca*; Uṇādi affix *asun*; the first syllable is acute because it is *n*-marked); *emi* (root *iṇ gatau*; *laṭ* 1st singular; *nighāta*); *sūktena* (root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; affix *kta*; *saṃprasāraṇa* and the preceding form by "*vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-15 [?]; accent on the last syllable by "*nañ subhyām*", Pā. Sū. 6-2-172 [?]); *bhikṣe* (root *bhikṣa yācñāyām*; *laṭ* 1st singular; *nighāta*); *sumatim* (root *mana jñāne*; *ktin* with the acute by "*mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā uḍudāttaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 3-3-96 [?]; the latter member keeps its accent); *turāṇām* (root *tura tvaraṇe*; affix *ka* by "*igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 3-1-135 [?]; because it is *k*-marked there is no *guṇa* of the light penultimate; or, root *turvī hiṃsāyām*; the affix *aṭ* [as read] because it belongs to *pacādi*; Vedic loss of *v*; accent on the last syllable by the affix; genitive plural); *rarāṇatā* (root *raṇu krīḍāyām*; *śānac* in the sense of the present; *luk* of *śap* by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*"; reduplication on that occasion, and by *vyatyaya* *a* for the *m*-final of the root; before the instrumental *ṭā*, an extra *t* appears); *dhatta* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *loṭ* 2nd plural; since it stands at the beginning of a *pāda* there is no *nighāta*; accent on the last syllable by the affix); *mucadhvam* (root *muclṛ mokṣaṇe*, *tudādi*; *loṭ* 2nd plural, affix *dhvam*; when the *ṭi* part takes *e*, *am* replaces it by "*savābhyāṃ vāmau*", Pā. ### Printed p. 200  (PDF 220)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> एष वः स्तोमो मरुतो नमस्वान्हृदा तष्टो मनसा धायि देवाः ।
> उपेमा यात मनसा जुषाणा यूयं हि ष्ठा नमस इद्वृधासः ॥ २ ॥

> *eṣa vaḥ stomo maruto namasvānhṛdā taṣṭo manasā dhāyi devāḥ |*
> *upemā yāta manasā juṣāṇā yūyaṃ hi ṣṭhā namasa idvṛdhāsaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एषः । वः । स्तोमः । मरुतः । नमस्वान् । हृदा । तष्टः । मनसा । धायि । देवाः ।
> उप । ईम् । आ । यात । मनसा । जुषाणाः । यूयम् । हि । स्थ । नमसः । इत् । वृधासः ॥ २ ॥

> *eṣaḥ | vaḥ | stomaḥ | marutaḥ | namasvān | hṛdā | taṣṭaḥ | manasā | dhāyi | devāḥ |*
> *upa | īm | ā | yāta | manasā | juṣāṇāḥ | yūyam | hi | stha | namasaḥ | it | vṛdhāsaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः एष वः स्तोम इदानीं क्रियमाणप्रकारो वो युष्माकम् । युष्मदर्थ इत्यर्थः । कीदृशोऽयम् । नमस्वान् । नम इत्यन्ननाम । हविर्लक्षणान्नवान् । न केवलं स्तुतिमात्रं भक्षणायापि हविरपि युष्माकमित्यर्थः । किंच हृदा तष्टो युष्मन्निवेदनबुद्ध्यै [?] संपादितः । ताद्दृशः स्तोमो हे देवा देवनशीलाः मनसास्मदनुग्रहवता चित्तेन धायि । धार्यताम् । तदर्थं मनसादरया बुद्ध्या जुषाणा ईमेनां स्तुतिं तद्धविश्च सेवमाना उपा यात । उपागच्छतैव । मा विलम्बं कुरुत । यूयं नमसोऽन्नस्य हविरूपस्य वृधासः स्थ ह । वर्धयितारो भवथ खलु । अतो गन्तव्यमेव । इत्पूरणः ॥

*Gist:* This praise, with its oblation of food, devised in the heart, is for you; take it up with a kindly mind and come near without delay, for you are the increasers of this offering.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *namasvān* — endowed with salutation (oblation); *eṣaḥ stomaḥ* — this praise; *vaḥ* — (is) for you; *hṛdā* — heartily; *taṣṭaḥ* — made ready (a praise of the heart); *(he)* *devāḥ* — O shining Marut-gods; *manasā* — with a respectful mind; *dhāyi* — let (it) be held (accepted); *yūyam* — you; *namasaḥ* — of food in the form of the oblation; *vṛdhāsaḥ stha hi it* — are (certainly) the increasers; *manasā* — with respect (with understanding); *īm* — this (offered by us) (salutation or praise); *juṣāṇāḥ* — being those who enjoy; *upa āyāta* — come near.

### Printed p. 201  (PDF 221)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, this praise of ours, accompanied by salutation (oblation) for you, has been composed with the whole heart. Accept it with respect and, since you are the increasers of the oblation, come with glad hearts to receive our oblation.

**English Translation (as printed):** This praise, accompanied by offerings, Maruts, ir [sic] for you, offered from the heart: accept it, divinities, with favour, and come with willing minds (to receive) these (laudations), for you are the augmenters of sacrificial food.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***vaḥ stomaḥ namasvān hṛdā taṣṭaḥ*** — *idānīṃ kriyamāṇaprakāraḥ havirlakṣaṇānnavān yuṣmannivedanabuddhyai saṃpāditaḥ*: our hymn, addressed to the Marut-gods and being recited for them, and our wish to offer the oblation prepared for them, are both intended only to obtain their favour; and by "*manasā dhāyi asmadanugrahavatā cittena dhāryatām*" it is prayed that the shining Marut-gods may hear our praises with a mind of favour towards us.

Here the words *hṛdā taṣṭaḥ manasā dhāyi* make clear the poet's intention in the composition. They indicate the skill and the delight-giving quality of the poet's making.

***taṣṭaḥ*** — "*takṣatiḥ karotikarmā*" (Ni. 4-[?]). This word is used wherever a skill of construction is indicated.

> आ ते अग्न ऋचा हविर्हृदा तष्टं भरामसि ।

> *ā te agna ṛcā havir hṛdā taṣṭaṃ bharāmasi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-47 [?])

> हृदिस्पृशो मनसा वच्यमाना अस्मभ्यं चित्रं वृषणं रयिं दाः ।

> *hṛdispṛśo manasā vacyamānā asmabhyaṃ citraṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ rayiṃ dāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-47-2 [?]). As described in places like these, the meaning is that both the quality of giving delight to the mind and the skill that goes with devotion are present.

***manasā juṣāṇāḥ īṃ upā yāta*** — *ādarayā buddhyā enāṃ stutiṃ taddhaviś ca sevamānāḥ mā vilambaṃ kuruta*: "with a mind of affection towards us who praise, come in haste, so that you may hear our praise and partake of our oblation; may it come to our sacrifice": thus the prayer is made. Here, regarding the particle *īm*, (the Nirukta says:) "*atha ye … [as read]*" (Ni. 1-[?])

### Printed p. 202  (PDF 222)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

— the particles *kam*, *īm*, *it*, *u* are used in sentences as fillers of the sentence, and in metres as fillers of the word, say the Nirukta-writers. But "*evam uccāvaceṣv artheṣu nipatanti te upekṣitavyāḥ …*" [as read; Ni. 1-9 [?]]: since it has been said that the use of these in a given text must be understood according to the meaning and the rules of that śāstra, here Sāyaṇa gives, for the particle *īm*, the meaning *enāṃ stutim*, "this praise". The word *it* is described as used in the sense of a filler (*padapūraṇa*). *Yūyaṃ namasaḥ vṛdhāsaḥ stha hi* — "*havīrūpasya annasya vardhayitāro bhavatha khalu*": the Marut-gods are indeed the increasers of food in the form of the oblation: this is a well-established matter.

> रोदसी हि मरुतश्चक्रिरे वृधे मदन्ति वीरा विदथेषु घृष्वयः ।

> *rodasī hi marutaś cakrire vṛdhe madanti vīrā vidatheṣu ghṛṣvayaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-85-1). Since the Marut-gods are the cause of the increase of heaven and earth, and also the cause of the growth of the world, the sacrificers, by their favour, rejoice in the sacrifices and in the accomplishment of the wealth of their lives; their happiness and delight are described in many places. But here one point has to be noted: in one or two places it is stated that the Marut-gods, apart from being the producers of the food that is useful for the oblation, do not themselves partake of the oblation as other deities do. For example:

> अहुतादो वा देवानां मरुतः [?]

> *ahutādo vā devānāṃ marutaḥ [?]*

(Śat. Brā. 4-5-2-16 [?]). Although it is stated emphatically that the Marut-gods do not eat what has been offered, it must be noted that in those places the word *ahuta* ("unoffered") food does not mean the oblation that is generally offered. Therefore in the present ṛk, for "*vaḥ stomaḥ namasvān hṛdā taṣṭaḥ*", the meaning that the hymn was composed together with oblation-food is natural.

> सीदता बर्हिरुरु वः सदस्कृतं मादयध्वं मरुतो मध्वो अन्धसः ।

> *sīdatā barhir uru vaḥ sadaskṛtaṃ mādayadhvaṃ maruto madhvo andhasaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-85-6). In places such as these, the prayer "be satisfied with the drinking of the sweet *soma* juice" is clear.

Sū. 8-4-2 [?]; accent on the last syllable by "*citaḥ*"); *stha* (root *as bhuvi*; *laṭ* 2nd plural; *nighāta*); *vṛdhāsaḥ* (root *vṛdhu vṛddhau*; affix *ka* by "*igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ*", Pā. #### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स्तुतासो नो मरुतो मृळयन्तूत स्तुतो मघवा शंभविष्ठः ।
> ऊर्ध्वा नः सन्तु कोम्या वनान्यहानि विश्वा मरुतो जिगीषा ॥ ३ ॥

> *stutāso no maruto mṛḷayantūta stuto maghavā śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ |*
> *ūrdhvā naḥ santu komyā vanānyahāni viśvā maruto jigīṣā ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> स्तुतासः । नः । मरुतः । मृळयन्तु । उत । स्तुतः । मघऽवा । शंऽभविष्ठः ।
> ऊर्ध्वाः । नः । सन्तु । कोम्या । वनानि । अहानि । विश्वा । मरुतः । जिगीषा ॥ ३ ॥

> *stutāsaḥ | naḥ | marutaḥ | mṛḷayantu | uta | stutaḥ | magha 'vā | śaṃ 'bhaviṣṭhaḥ |*
> *ūrdhvāḥ | naḥ | santu | komyā | vanāni | ahāni | viśvā | marutaḥ | jigīṣā ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> ते मरुतः स्तुतासः स्तुताः सन्तो नोऽस्मान् मृळयन्तु सुखयन्तु । उतापि च मघवा । मघमिति धननाम । अस्मद्दातव्येन बहुधनेन तद्वानिन्द्रः स्तुतः शंभविष्ठः सुखस्य भावयितृतमः सन्नस्मान्मृळयतु । किंच हे मरुतः नोऽस्माकं जिगीषा ॥ जिगातेर्गतिकर्मणो जिगीषा ॥ जिगीषितव्यानि प्राप्तव्यान्यत्र [?] त्रात्रानुभूयमानानि [?] विश्वा सर्वाण्यहानि दिवसान्यूर्ध्वान्येतान्युपर्युपरि श्रिया यशसा वोत्स्वान्यानि [?] कोम्या कामयानि स्पृहणीयानि वनानि सर्वैः संभजनीयानि सन्तु । जिगीषा जेतुमिष्यानि जेतव्यानि च संश्रिति वा योज्यम् [?] । एवं कृत्वा मरुत इन्द्रश्च सुखयन्त्वित्यर्थः ॥ [garbled in the second half]

*Gist:* May the Maruts, praised, and Maghavan Indra, praised, give us happiness, and may all our days be elevated and desirable.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(te)* *marutaḥ* — those Marut-gods; *stutāsaḥ* — (praised by us); *naḥ* — us; *mṛḷayantu* — may they give happiness; *uta* — and; *stutaḥ* — praised; *maghavā* — (giver of wealth to us) Indra, the wealthy; *śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ* — extremely beneficent; *(mṛḷayatu* — may he favour us with happiness*)* ; *(kiṃca* — and*)* *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *naḥ* — to us; *jigīṣā* — (those to be attained) to be won; *viśvā ahāni* — all days; *ūrdhvāḥ* — excellent; *komyā* — desirable (worthy to be desired); *vanāni* — (for all) the sources of happiness; and; *(jigīṣā* — worthy of victory*)* ; *santu* — may they be (by your favour).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, praised by us, give us happiness; and may Indra, the lord of wealth, also praised, be a bringer of happiness; and, O Marut-gods, as all wish, may we, in the days to come (by your favour), live happily and in excellent fashion.

**English Translation (as printed):** May the Maruts, now hymned, bestow happiness upon us: may Maghavan, now glorified, be propitious to us: Maruts, may all the *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 205  (PDF 225)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11".)*

*(English Translation of Ṛk 3, concluded)* — … ensuing days that may be expected by us prove gratifying, and full of enjoyment.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***he marutaḥ stutāsaḥ*** — addressing the Marut-gods, it is prayed that they, praised by the sacrificers who perform sacrifices for them, make us happy. Yāska cites

> क्षेत्रस्य पते मधुमन्तमूर्मिं धेनुरिव पयो अस्मासु धुक्ष्व ।
> मधुश्चुतं घृतमिव सुपूतमृतस्य नः पतयो मृळयन्तु ॥

> *kṣetrasya pate madhumantam ūrmiṃ dhenur iva payo asmāsu dhukṣva |*
> *madhuścutaṃ ghṛtam iva supūtam ṛtasya naḥ patayo mṛḷayantu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-57-3 [?]). In this ṛk, for the word *mṛḷayantu* the meaning "*mṛḷayatiḥ* [*dayā*]*karma vā*" [as read] is explained. Durgācārya says "*mṛḷayantu nityam asmān rakṣantu pūjayantu vā*" — may they protect us, or may they bring us honour (worship).

***maghavā stutaḥ śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ*** — the word *magha* is read among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]); and "*maghamiti dhananāmadheyaṃ maṃhater dānakarmaṇaḥ*" (Ni. 1-[?]) — the word *magha*, formed from the root *maṃh* ("to give"), denotes wealth: so Yāska explains. Sāyaṇa, for this word, says "*maghamiti dhananāma asmaddātavyabahudhanena tadvān indraḥ*": *magha* means wealth, and Indra, possessing abundant wealth to be given properly to the sacrificers, is well known as *maghavā*.

It has been said earlier that the word *maghavat* may also be construed as referring to the sacrificer. In other places it is explained that *maghavā* is Indra together with Viṣṇu — Indra, who obtains Viṣṇu's help in his battles with Asuras and others; for stating this meaning there is the authority of the Śruti:

> स उ एव मुखः स विष्णुः । ते ते इन्द्रो मुखवानभवत् [?] । मुखवान् ह वै तं मघवानित्याचक्षते परोक्षं परोक्षकामा हि देवाः ॥ [as read]

> *sa u eva mukhaḥ sa viṣṇuḥ | te te indro mukhavānabhavat [?] | mukhavān ha vai taṃ maghavānityācakṣate parokṣaṃ parokṣakāmā hi devāḥ ‖ [as read]*

(Śat. Brā. 14-1-1-13 [?]). Since Indra has Viṣṇu — the sacrifice (*yajña*) — as his mouth (*mukha*), the gods, who are fond of the indirect, call him *maghavān* indirectly: so the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa explains. In some places, too, the companionship of Indra, the Marut-gods and Viṣṇu is well known. For example:

> एता अग्न आशुषाणासो इष्टीर्युवोः सचाभ्यश्याम वाजान् ।
> मेन्द्रो नो विष्णुर्मरुतः परि ख्यन् यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥

> *etā agna āśuṣāṇāso iṣṭīr yuvoḥ sacābhyaśyāma vājān |*
> *mendro no viṣṇur marutaḥ pari khyan yūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-46-2 [?]), where Indra and the Marut-gods are besought together with Viṣṇu. Besides this, it is indicated in some places that the word *mārutaḥ* is an epithet of Viṣṇu. For example:

> अग्न इन्द्र वरुण मित्र देवाः शर्धः प्र यन्त मारुतोत विष्णो ।
> उभा नासत्या रुद्रो अध ग्नाः पूषा भगः सरस्वती जुषन्त ॥

> *agna indra varuṇa mitra devāḥ śardhaḥ pra yanta mārutota viṣṇo |*
> *ubhā nāsatyā rudro adha gnāḥ pūṣā bhagaḥ sarasvatī juṣanta ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-[?])

### Printed p. 206  (PDF 226)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

> तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विना क्रतुं सचन्त मारुतस्य वेधसः ॥

> *tam asya rājā varuṇas tam aśvinā kratuṃ sacanta mārutasya vedhasaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-156-4). In places such as these, some hold that the words *mārute* and *mārutasya* are epithets of Viṣṇu. Explaining this, the scholar Max Müller says:

*Vishnu, whose character in the hymns of the Veda is very different from that assumed by him in later periods of Hindu religion, must be taken here as the friend and companion of Indra. Like Maruts, he assisted Indra in his battle against Vritra and the conquest of the clouds. When Indra was forsaken by all the Gods, Vishnu came to his help.*

*In VII. 68. 8. Indra, Vishnu and Maruts are called upon to-gether* [sic] *Nay,* मारुते, *belonging to the Maruts becoms* [sic] *actually an epithet of Vishnu. (V. 46. 2.) and in I 156. 4,* मारुतस्य *has been pointed out by Roth as an appellation of Vishnu.* (S. B. E. Vol. XXXII. P. 134)

But in the opinion of some, these words become epithets of Viṣṇu; Sāyaṇa has not stated this view. In the present ṛk, the word *maghavā* alone may be taken to mean either Indra who is wealthy, or Indra together with Viṣṇu.

This Indra (praised by the sacrificers), hearing the praises recited by the sacrificers, and, to the sacrificers who have praised him, calling "*sukhasya bhāvayitṛtamaḥ*" — "may there be abundant happiness" — prays "*asmān mṛḷayatu*" — that he make us, who perform sacrifices, happy.

***jigīṣā*** — *jigīṣitavyāni prāptavyāni uttarottarānubhūyamānāni*: those that are to be obtained by the sacrificers, ready to be enjoyed, or those that remain in the future; *viśvā* (continued)

### Printed p. 207  (PDF 227)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 3 continue.)*

(*viśvā* continued) — *ahāni*, all the days, *ūrdhvāḥ santu*: may they be excellent, each higher than the other in fame (*yaśas*) and in prosperity (*śrī*): thus it is wished.

For the word *komyā*, the sense *kāmyāni spṛhaṇīyāni* — "desirable" — is given: in the days to be lived through in future, since all our desired objects will be fulfilled, it is wished that they be praiseworthy; and *vanāni*: that they be worthy of being sought by all.

The word *vana* is read among the names of the ray (*raśmi*) (Ni. 1-[?]) and among the names of water (*udaka*) (Ni. 1-[?]). Along with these, the word is used in the Ṛk Saṃhitā in many other senses. "*vana saṃbhaktau*" — either from the root *van* giving the meaning of strong desire (*ākāṅkṣā*), or from the root *vanu yācane* giving the meaning "ask, pray"; since forms like *vanāni*, *vanāmahe*, *vanete* — names and verbal forms — are derived and used, a few examples may be given for understanding these meanings and variations. In uses of noun-words or adjectives:

> घृषुं पावकं वनिनं विचर्षणिं रुद्रस्य सूनुं हवसा गृणीमसि ।

> *ghṛṣuṃ pāvakaṃ vaninaṃ vicarṣaṇiṃ rudrasya sūnuṃ havasā gṛṇīmasi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-12 [?]) — here "*vanavantam, udakavantam*", the word *vana* in the sense of water;

> वनानि विभ्यो नकिरस्य ता व्रता देवस्य सवितुर्मिनन्ति ।

> *vanāni vibhyo nakiras ya tā vratā devasya savitur minanti |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-2 [?]) — in ṛks of this kind *vanāni* means "trees";

> पारावतस्य रातिषु द्रवच्चक्रेष्वाशुषु । तिष्ठं वनस्य मध्य आ ॥

> *pārāvatasya rātiṣu dravaccakreṣv āśuṣu | tiṣṭhaṃ vanasya madhya ā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-34-18 [?]) — here a part of the chariot is meant. Likewise, looking at the uses of verbal forms, in the example cited in the Nirukta (Ni. 5-2 [?]):

> त्वया वयं मघवन्पूर्व्ये धन इन्द्रत्वोताः सासह्याम पृतन्यतो वनुयाम वनुष्यतः ॥

> *tvayā vayaṃ maghavan pūrvye dhana indratvotāḥ sāsahyāma pṛtanyato vanuyāma vanuṣyataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-132-1 [?]) and

> अस्माकेभिर्नृभिर्वयं सासह्याम पृतन्यतो वनुयाम वनुष्यतो नभन्तामन्यके समे ॥

> *asmākebhir nṛbhir vayaṃ sāsahyāma pṛtanyato vanuyāma vanuṣyato nabhantām anyake same ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-40-7 [?])

### Printed p. 208  (PDF 228)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. Sū. 171".)*

— in these ṛks the sense "kill" is expressed; and in

> कविर्हि देवस्य सहसा चकानः सुम्नमग्निर्वनते वावृधानः ।

> *kavir hi devasya sahasā cakānaḥ sumnam agnir vanate vāvṛdhānaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-10 [?]) the sense "gives" (*prayacchati*);

> वनेम पूर्वीरर्यो मनीषा अग्निः सुशोको विश्वान्यश्याः ।

> *vanema pūrvīr aryo manīṣā agniḥ suśoko viśvāny aśyāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-20-1 [?]). In places like these, *vanema* is explained as "let us serve with reverence"; and in

> प्रियाँ आपिधीर्वनिषीष्ट मेधिर आ वनिषीष्ट मेधिरः ।

> *priyāṃ āpidhīr vaniṣīṣṭa medhira ā vaniṣīṣṭa medhiraḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-7 [?]) the sense is "may he accept with love and serve"; and so there are still other meanings. Since many meanings are thus possible, in the present ṛk the meaning *saṃbhajanīyāni* ("to be shared, worthy of being enjoyed in common by all") may also be given for *vanāni*.

In the second meaning, "*viśvā ahāni sarvāṇi divasāni jigīṣā santu — jetum iṣvāni jetavyāni ca santu*": it is explained that all the days that the sacrificers have to live through may be victorious for them. The main intention is the prayer that Indra and the Marut-gods, favouring the sacrificers in this way, may keep them in happiness.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *stutāsaḥ* (root *ṣṭuñ stutau*; *kta* in the passive; *asuk* before *jas* by "*ājjaserasuk*"); *mṛḷayantu* (root *mṛḍa sukhane*; *loṭ* 3rd plural; *nighāta*); *śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ* (*śaṃ bhāvayitā*; after the *tṛc*-ending *śaṃbhavitṛ*, the affix *iṣṭhan* in the sense of excess by "*tuścchandasi*"; the loss of *tṛc* before it by "*turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu*"; *guṇa* of *u* by "*ogguṇaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 6-4-146 [?]; *av*; first syllable acute by "*ñnityādirnityam*"); *ūrdhvā* (in the neuter, loss of *śi* by "*śeścchandasi bahulam*"; likewise *luk* of *śi* in *komyā* and *viśvā*); *komyā* (root *kanu kāntau*; affix *ṇyat* by "*ṛhaloṇyat*"; with *ādivṛddhi* the Vedic *o* arises; accent on the last syllable by *vyatyaya*).

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अस्मादहं तविषादीषमाण इन्द्राद्भिया मरुतो रेजमानः ।
> युष्मभ्यं हव्या निशितान्यासन्तान्यारे चकृमा मृळता नः ॥ ४ ॥

> *asmādahaṃ taviṣādīṣamāṇa indrādbhiyā maruto rejamānaḥ |*
> *yuṣmabhyaṃ havyā niśitānyāsantānyāre cakṛmā mṛḷatā naḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्मात् । अहम् । तविषात् । ईषमाणः । इन्द्रात् । भिया । मरुतः । रेजमानः ।
> युष्मभ्यम् । हव्या । निऽशितानि । आसन् । तानि । आरे । चकृम । मृळत । नः ॥ ४ ॥

> *asmāt | aham | taviṣāt | īṣamāṇaḥ | indrāt | bhiyā | marutaḥ | rejamānaḥ |*
> *yuṣmabhyam | havyā | ni 'śitāni | āsan | tāni | āre | cakṛma | mṛḷata | naḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः शृणुत । अहमस्मात्प्रसिद्धात्तविषाद्बलवत इन्द्रात्तत्प्रकाशाद्भियो भीत्येषमाणः पलायमानः पुरतः स्थातुमशक्तः तथा रेजमानो वेपमानश्चाभवम् । ततश्च किमायातमिति अत आह । यानि युष्मभ्यं हव्या हवींषि निशितानि संस्कृतान्यासन् तानि तान्येवारे चकृम । दूरे कृतवन्तो वयमिन्द्रभयात् । अतो नोऽस्मानपराधिनो मृळत । मृळयत । सुखयत ॥

*Gist:* Agastya, trembling in fear of mighty Indra, tells the Maruts that the oblations prepared for them were put far away through fear of Indra; he begs them to give happiness to him, who is blameless.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *aham* — I; *asmāt* — from this well-known (and); *taviṣāt* — powerful; *indrāt* — Indra (from near him); *bhiyā* — from fear; *īṣamāṇaḥ* — running away (unable to stand before him); *rejamānaḥ* — trembling (I am); *(yāni)* *havyā* — the oblations; *yuṣmabhyam* — for you; *niśitāni* — prepared; *āsan* — were; *tāni* — those; *āre* — far away; *cakṛma* — (through fear of Indra) we have put; *(therefore)* *naḥ* — us (who are blameless); *mṛḷata* — make happy.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, from fear of this mighty Indra, unable to stand before him, I run, trembling; the oblations that had been prepared for you I have put far away out of fear of him. Therefore make me, who am blameless, happy.

### Printed p. 210  (PDF 230)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

**English Translation (as printed):** Maruts, through fear of that violent Indra, I fly, trembling, (from his presence): the oblations that had been prepared for you have been put away: nevertheless, have patience with us.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this ṛk it is explained that the sage Agastya, frightened of Indra, makes an effort to avert his fear and begs the Marut-gods. This context is of the nature of a dialogue. The companionship of Indra and the Marut-gods is well known in the Śruti, and the friendship between them has been said. Even so, Indra, to show his prowess, says openly that he has no help at all from the Marut-gods and that he himself has not been benefited by them. In this context, since Indra was angry, the sage Agastya, who had offered oblations to the Marut-gods, walks in fear. Here that fear is expressed. What, then, is the nature of the friendship between Indra and the Marut-gods in the present context? Even so, what is the cause of this discord should be considered.

The eternal companionship between Indra and the Marut-gods, the relation of king and subjects between them, the offering of oblations to Indra, the chief, along with the Marut-gods in the sacrificial rites, and Indra's receiving the help of the Marut-gods in battle with Vṛtra and other Asuras, are stated many times in the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. Indra, having joined the Marut-gods, is said to have a separate story compared with the other gods; for example:

> आतिथ्येन वै देवा इष्ट्वा । तान् स्वमुदविन्दत् [?] ते चतुर्धा व्यद्रवन्नन्योऽन्यस्य श्रिया तिष्ठमाना अग्निर्वसुभिः सोमो रुद्रैर्वरुण आदित्यैरिन्द्रो मरुद्भिर्बृहस्पतिर्विश्वेदेवैः ।

> *ātithyena vai devā iṣṭvā | tān svamudavindat [?] te caturdhā vyadravannanyo 'nyasya śriyā tiṣṭhamānā agnirvasubhiḥ somo rudrairvaruṇa ādityairindro marudbhirbṛhaspatirviśvedevaiḥ |*

(Śat. Brā. 3-4-3-1 [?]). Formerly, when the gods had performed the *Ātithya* rite, ill-will arose among them; each unable to bear the other's glory, they went apart in four groups: Agni with the Vasus, Soma with the Rudras, Varuṇa with the Ādityas, Indra with the Marut-gods, and Bṛhaspati (with …) *(continued)*

---

### Printed p. 211  (PDF 231)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 4 continue.)*

(*Bṛhaspati* continued) — with the Viśvedevas; thus, each forming a separate group, they came together. In this story the close relation, in which Indra joined with the Marut-gods and made companionship with them, is told. Besides, in many places it is said that Indra is the king and the Marut-gods are the subjects. For example, in the same Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:

> क्षत्रं वा इन्द्रो विशो मरुतो विशा वै क्षत्रियो बलवान् भवति ।

> *kṣatraṃ vā indro viśo maruto viśā vai kṣatriyo balavān bhavati |*

(Śat. Brā. 4-3-1-6 [?]). Indra is the *kṣatra*, the ruling power, the king; the Marut-gods are the subjects (*viśaḥ*). By the cooperation of the subjects the king becomes strong; and with the help of the Marut-gods Indra's valour gains increase: this is indicated. Because such a close relationship and companionship exists, the Śrutis show the way in which oblations are offered with Indra and the Marut-gods together as the objects of the invocation. And

> स नो मरुद्भिर्वृषभ श्रवो धा उग्र उग्रेभिः स्थविरः सहोदाः ।

> *sa no marudbhir vṛṣabha śravo dhā ugra ugrebhiḥ sthaviraḥ sahodāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-5 [?]; this is the second half of the very next ṛk of this sūkta). With such ṛks, Indra and the Marut-gods are together invoked and offered oblations; and, describing this companionship, the Bṛhaddevatā says

> मरुद्भिः सह यत्रेन्द्रो मरुत्वांस्तत्र सोऽभवत् ।

> *marudbhiḥ saha yatrendro marutvāṃs tatra so'bhavat |*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-56 [?]). By sentences of this kind the epithet indicating relation with these deities is explained. But in the present sūkta, the discord between them and Indra's anger have been indicated as an effect of the dialogue between Indra and the Marut-gods. The cause of this anger has been shown earlier, in the following way:

> क्व स्या वो मरुतः स्वधासीद्यन्मां एकं समधत्ताहिहत्ये ।
> अहं ह्युग्रस्तविषस्तुविष्मान्विश्वस्य शत्रोरनमं वधस्नैः ॥

> *kva syā vo marutaḥ svadhāsīd yan māṃ ekaṃ samadhattāhihatye |*
> *ahaṃ hy ugras taviṣas tuviṣmān viśvasya śatror anamaṃ vadhasnaiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-165-8). "O Marut-gods, to say that you did the slaying of the serpent (Vṛtra) is false. Where was that power of yours? My own power, being unique, did not seek the help of any other power when Vṛtra was slain; I alone am of terrible and wonderful power and greatness": thus, in a spirit of contempt for the Marut-gods, he expresses his anger. Here that anger is indicated. It is well known that Indra received the help of the Marut-gods at the time of killing Vṛtra. Even so, when the Marut-gods, understanding the matter, asked Indra that they too should be given a share in the oblation intended for Indra, Indra said that he had had no help at all from them, and that he had himself killed all his enemies by his own power.

### Printed p. 212  (PDF 232)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

The Nirukta-writers, pointing out this very matter, speak thus:

> अगस्त्य इन्द्राय हविर्निरुप्य मरुद्भ्यः संप्रदित्सां चकार । स इन्द्र एत्य परिदेवयाञ्चक्रे ।

> *agastya indrāya havirnirupya marudbhyaḥ saṃpraditsāṃ cakāra | sa indra etya paridevayāñcakre |*

(Ni. 1-[?]). When the sage Agastya prepared an oblation intended for Indra, and wished to offer to the Marut-gods a share in it, Indra objected in this matter without any expectation (of it); so, understanding the context, the Nirukta-writers explain this part, citing the ṛk

> न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतम् । अन्यस्य चित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं विनश्यति ॥

> *na nūnamasti no śvaḥ kastadveda yadadbhutam | anyasya cittamabhi saṃcareṇyamutādhītaṃ vinaśyati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-170-1). With the force of that anger diminished, so that it may not afflict him, and with the aim that the Marut-gods too should have their rightful share of the oblation, the Marut-gods are here addressed and entreated. After such conciliatory words, Indra's friendship grew as before and he himself gave his share of the oblation to the Marut-gods. The sage describes this matter in the eighth maṇḍala, praising thus:

> वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथादीषमाणा विश्वे देवा अजहुर्ये सखायः ।
> मरुद्भिरिन्द्र सख्यं ते अस्त्वथेमा विश्वाः पृतना जयासि ॥

> *vṛtrasya tvā śvasathād īṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahur ye sakhāyaḥ |*
> *marudbhir indra sakhyaṃ te astv athemā viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāsi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-7 [?]). "O Indra, your friendship with the Marut-gods is famous. Give them also a share of your oblation, and conquer all your enemies with their help": thus the prayer is made.

***īṣamāṇaḥ*** — the root *īṣa* is used in the senses of motion, of violence, and of non-seeing (*adarśana*); in everyday usage it is not found, but in the Ṛk Saṃhitā this word is used only in the sense of motion. For example:

> सम्यक्स्रवन्ति सरितो न धेना अन्तर्हृदा मनसा पूयमानाः ।
> एते अर्षन्त्यूर्मयो घृतस्य मृगा इव क्षिपणोरीषमाणाः ॥

> *samyak sravanti sarito na dhenā antar hṛdā manasā pūyamānāḥ |*
> *ete arṣanty ūrmayo ghṛtasya mṛgā iva kṣipaṇor īṣamāṇāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-58-6). In this ṛk the meaning of this word is clear: as the deer, frightened of the hunter, run far away and hide themselves, both movement and non-visibility are indicated by the simile. In the same way

> वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथादीषमाणा विश्वे देवा अजहुर्ये सखायः ।

> *vṛtrasya tvā śvasathādīṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahurye sakhāyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-7 [?]).

---

### Printed p. 213  (PDF 233)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11".)*

(*īṣamāṇaḥ* continued) — in the ṛk quoted above also, the state of all the gods fleeing, frightened of Vṛtra, is shown by the word *īṣamāṇāḥ*. In the present ṛk the sage himself describes the state of Agastya, who fled in fear of Indra's anger.

***niśitāni*** — the word *niśita* is not used in everyday speech in the sense of "sharp, keen". In the Kaṭhopaniṣad:

> क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ।

> *kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṃ pathas tat kavayo vadanti |*

(Kaṭha Up. 1-3-14), where the difficulty of crossing the edge of a razor (a barber's knife) is well known as the description of the sharpness. In the Ṛk Saṃhitā this word is generally used in the sense "well prepared"; in the present ṛk it is an epithet of *havyā* ("prepared oblations").

***ahaṃ asmāt taviṣāt indrāt bhiyā īṣamāṇaḥ rejamānaḥ*** — *prasiddhāt balavataḥ indrāt bhītyā palāyamānaḥ puraḥ sthātum aśaktaḥ vepamānaś cābhavam*: here it is explained that the sage Agastya, afraid of the powerful Indra, unable to stand before him, was trembling. Agastya's overstepping with respect to Indra, and his regret for it afterwards, are stated in ṛk 1-170-1. Because Indra made known his displeasure at the transgression, the conversation that the sage Agastya held with Indra is stated in ṛk 1-170-2. Again, the conversation in which Indra, having heard Agastya's reply, asked, along with the priests and with the sage Agastya himself, to obtain his own share of the oblation, is stated in ṛk 1-170-[4?]. In this matter, the defeat brought about by Indra is told here by the sage Agastya, addressing the Marut-gods: thus the narrative context is indicated here.

***yuṣmabhyaṃ havyā niśitāni tāni āre cakṛma*** — addressing the Marut-gods: "*yuṣmabhyaṃ saṃskṛtāni havīṃṣi dūre kṛtavanto vayam indrabhayāt*" — "we have put far away, out of fear of Indra, the oblations that were prepared for you": declaring his offence thus, ***naḥ mṛḷata ataḥ aparādhinaḥ asmān sukhayata*** — "for this reason, being guilty (of the offence of disrespect to you, or of what amounts to a rebuke of you), may the Marut-gods forgive our offence and keep us in happiness": thus the prayer of the mantra-seer Agastya is described here.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *taviṣāt* (root *tava*, a Sautra root; affix *ṭiṣac* by an Uṇādi sūtra, "*taverṇidvā*" [as read]; accent on the last syllable since it is *c*-marked; ablative singular); *īṣamāṇaḥ* (root *īṣa gatihiṃsādarśaneṣu*; *śānac* for *laṭ*; the vikaraṇa *śap*; the augment *muk* by "*āne muk*", Pā. Sū. 7-2-82 [?]; because *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented by "*tāsyanudāttet…*", the accent of the root remains); *bhiyā* (root *ñibhī bhaye*; affix *kvip*; instrumental singular; the ending takes the acute by "*sāvekācastṛtīyādiḥ*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 [?]); *rejamānaḥ* (root *reja kampane*; *śānac* for *laṭ*; the augment *muk* and the accent as before); *niśitāni* (root *śo tanūkaraṇe*; affix *kta* in the passive; the substitute *i*-ending for the root by "*śācchoranyatarasyām*", Pā. Sū. 7-4-41 [?]; the preverb *ni* takes the acute by "*gatir anantaraḥ*"); *cakṛma* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *liṭ* 1st plural; *nighāta* since it stands after a word ending in a verb); *mṛḷata* (root *mṛḍa sukhane*; since the causal action is shown, the causal sense is included; *loṭ* 2nd plural; because it stands after a word ending in a verb there is no *nighāta*, and by the accent of the *vikaraṇa* it becomes acute on the middle syllable). ‖ 4 ‖

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> येन मानासश्चितयन्त उस्रा व्युष्टिषु शवसा शश्वतीनाम् ।
> स नो मरुद्भिर्वृषभ श्रवो धा उग्र उग्रेभिः स्थविरः सहोदाः ॥ ५ ॥

> *yena mānāsaścitayanta usrā vyuṣṭiṣu śavasā śaśvatīnām |*
> *sa no marudbhirvṛṣabha śravo dhā ugra ugrebhiḥ sthaviraḥ sahodāḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> येन । मानासः । चितयन्ते । उस्राः । विऽउष्टिषु । शवसा । शश्वतीनाम् ।
> सः । नः । मरुत्ऽभिः । वृषभ । श्रवः । धाः । उग्रः । उग्रेभिः । स्थविरः । सहःऽदाः ॥ ५ ॥

> *yena | mānāsaḥ | citayante | usrāḥ | vi 'uṣṭiṣu | śavasā | śaśvatīnām |*
> *saḥ | naḥ | marut 'bhiḥ | vṛṣabha | śravaḥ | dhāḥ | ugraḥ | ugrebhiḥ | sthaviraḥ | sahaḥ 'dāḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

### Printed p. 215  (PDF 235)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11". The zoom confirms the Pada word *mānāsaḥ*; the Saṃhitā of Ṛk 5 above has been set accordingly.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र येन शवसा बलभूतेन त्वयानुगृहीता मानासो मान्यास्त्वयाभिमानिता वो उस्रा रश्मयः शश्वतीनां नित्यानां बह्वीनामुषसां व्युष्टिषु सतीषु प्रकाशेषु सत्सु चितयन्ते चेतयन्ते प्राणिनां स्वस्वव्यवहाराय प्रज्ञापयन्ति । ऐन्द्र्यां दिशि तेनैवानुगृहीता उषसो रश्मय उद्गच्छन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् । हे वृषभ वर्षितरिन्द्र स तादृशस्त्वं मरुद्भिः सहितः श्रवो धाः । सर्वत्र श्रूयमाणमन्नं धेहि । स्थापय । देहीत्यर्थः । कीदृशस्त्वम् । उग्र उद्गूर्णबलः सहोदाः । परा... [?] भवसामर्थ्यं बलं सहः । तस्य दाता स्थविरः पुरातनः । कीदृशैर्मरुद्भिः । उग्रेभिः क्रूरबलैः । एवं महानुभावोऽस्मभ्यमन्नं देहि ॥

*Gist:* Indra's strength favours the honoured rays of the eternal dawns, which wake all living beings to their tasks; may he, fierce, ancient, giver of strength, with the fierce Maruts, grant us food.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *indra* — O Indra; *mānāsaḥ* — honourable (the object of your esteem); *usrāḥ* — the rays; *śaśvatīnām* — of the eternal; *uṣasām* — of the dawns; *vyuṣṭiṣu* — when they shine; *śavasā* — by the strength; *yena* — by which (favoured by you); *citayante* — they make living beings (in their own activities) alert; *(he)* *vṛṣabha* — O Indra, who rain wishes; *saḥ* — such as you are; *ugraḥ* — of fierce strength; *sahodāḥ* — giver of strength; *sthaviraḥ* — ancient; *ugrebhiḥ* — with those of fierce nature; *marudbhiḥ* — with the Marut-gods; *saḥ* (*sahitaḥ*) — accompanied; *naḥ* — for us; *śravaḥ* — food; *dhāḥ* — establish (grant).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, the rays of the morning, the object of your esteem, at the dawning of the eternal dawns make all living beings alert to their own activities. O Indra, granter of wishes, fierce, giver of strength, ancient, together with the fierce Marut-gods, grant us food.

**English Translation (as printed):** The rays of the ever-recurring mornings, favoured, Indra, by your vigour, confer consciousness as they shine: showerer of benefits, ancient (of days), bestower of strength, fierce, (and attended) by the fierce Maruts, grant us (abundant) food.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***usrāḥ śavasā mānāsaḥ*** — *raśmayaḥ balabhūtena tvayā anugṛhītāḥ mānyāḥ tvayā abhimānitā vā*: the word *śavas* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]) and among the names of strength (Ni. 2-[?])

### Printed p. 216  (PDF 236)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

(Ni. 3-[?]). Here, addressing Indra, it is said that Indra is "strong, or endowed with strength". The word *usrāḥ* is used as an epithet of the word *usra*; two meanings are explained: that the rays are worthy of honour, being favoured by Indra who is of the form of strength; or that they are esteemed by Indra who is of the form of strength. The word *usra* is read among the names of rays (Ni. 1-[?]).

According to Sāyaṇa's explanation the word *mānāsaḥ* is an epithet of *usrāḥ*. But the scholar Max Müller has interpreted it in another way. His translation is as follows:

*Thou, through whom the Manas see the Mornings, whenever the eternal dawns flash forth with power, O Indra, O Strong hero, grant thou glory to us with the Maruts, terrible with the terrible ones, strong and a giver of victory.* [S. B. E. XXXII. P. 289].

According to this translation the word *mānāsaḥ* means the descendants of the sage Mānya (the seers born in the lineage of Mānya). Since Sāyaṇa also gives this same meaning elsewhere, in another context, it cannot be said that this translation is wrong. For example:

> तद्वां नरा नासत्यावनु ष्याद्यद्वां मानास उचथमवोचन् ।
> अस्मादद्य सदसः सोम्यादा विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥

> *tad vāṃ narā nāsatyāv anu ṣyād yad vāṃ mānāsa ucatham avocan |*
> *asmād adya sadasaḥ somyād ā vidyām eṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-182-8). In this ṛk Sāyaṇa has interpreted *mānāsaḥ* as "*pūjāvantaḥ asmadīyāḥ hotrādayaḥ*" — "our worshipful *hotṛ* priests and others". And in the same way here too, if it were said: "O Indra, by your favour the descendants of Māna (the *mānasas*), seeing the light of the morning every day at the appearance of the dawn, become engaged in their duties", that would be the purport. In these contexts, for the words *mānasaḥ*, *mānyasya*, *mānāsaḥ* there is a difference between the meaning given by the English scholars and Sāyaṇa's explanation. For example:

> एष वः स्तोमो मरुत इयं गीर्मान्दार्यस्य मान्यस्य कारोः ।

> *eṣa vaḥ stomo maruta iyaṃ gīr māndāryasya mānyasya kāroḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-165-15). In this ṛk the word *mānyasya*, though it is an epithet of Agastya, is explained by Sāyaṇa as "*varapradānādinā mānyasya*" — "worthy of honour because of the granting of boons and the like". Max Müller says thus: *(continued)*

---

### Printed p. 217  (PDF 237)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11"; the Max Müller quotation from p. 216 concludes.)*

*"I translate* मान्य, *the son of* मान, *because, the poet so called in I. 189-8 is in all probability, the same as our* मांदार्य मान्य. *But it may also be Manya the descendant of* मांदारि." [S. B. E. XXXII. P. 206].

And, explaining in this very ṛk the meaning of the word *mānāsaḥ*, he says:

*The* मानासः *are the people of* मान्य *and there is no necessity for taking* मान *with Grassmann as a general name for poet.* [S. B. E. XXXII. P. 291].

Thus he states his own opinion.

Here, if, as Sāyaṇa explains, the word *mānāsaḥ* is made an epithet of *usrāḥ*, then the purport is that by the favour of Indra the rays, at the very appearance of the dawn, make living beings engaged in their various activities. Here the question what connection the rays of the sun have with Indra has no occasion to arise; for it is well known that Indra is the presiding deity of the eastern quarter. Moreover,

> भगश्चैवार्यमा चांशश्च मित्रो वरुण एव च ।
> धाता चैव विधाता च विवस्वांश्च महाद्युतिः ॥
> त्वष्टा पूषा तथैवेन्द्रो द्वादशो विष्णुरुच्यते ।

> *bhagaś caivāryamā cāṃśaś ca mitro varuṇa eva ca |*
> *dhātā caiva vidhātā ca vivasvāṃś ca mahādyutiḥ ‖*
> *tvaṣṭā pūṣā tathaivendro dvādaśo viṣṇur ucyate |*

(Bṛ. Dev. 5-146, 147 [?]). Thus the Bṛhaddevatā counts Indra as one of the twelve Ādityas. And

> तद्वा एष एवेन्द्रः । य एष तपति ।

> *tad vā eṣa evendraḥ | ya eṣa tapati |*

(Śat. Brā. 1-6-4-18 [?]) — in this sentence of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa the identity of Indra and the blazing Āditya is stated. And, describing Indra's greatness,

> युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमरुषं चरन्तं परि तस्थुषः । रोचन्ते रोचना दिवि ॥

> *yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣaṃ carantaṃ pari tasthuṣaḥ | rocante rocanā divi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-6-1). It is described that Indra himself, in the forms of all the deities — Agni, Vāyu, Āditya and the rest — carries out the functions of all. Therefore the appearance of the dawn and, after it, the diffusion of the rays of the Āditya are accomplished by the favour of Indra: this is the purport.

***śaśvatīnāṃ vyuṣṭiṣu citayante*** — *nityānāṃ bahvīnām uṣasāṃ prakāśeṣu satsu prāṇināṃ svasvavyavahārāya prajñāpayanti*: taking the differences of days (*ahan*) as the occasion, it is explained that the dawns are many. At the appearance of the several dawns, the rays favoured by Indra produce in each being (continued)

### Printed p. 218  (PDF 238)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

the consciousness suited to the activities that each living being carries on; and by explaining "*aindryāṃ diśi tenaivānugṛhītā uṣaso raśmaya udgacchantīti prasiddham*" — "it is well known that, in the eastern quarter, the rays of the dawn, favoured by Indra, rise" — he describes the rising of the dawn, and explains that these rays give this power, namely that, when the dawn has risen, living beings acquire the knowledge suited to their respective activities.

The eternal Uṣas rises every day and lights up the world according to her rule. This view is praised in many places:

> पुराणी देवि युवतिः पुरंधिरनु व्रतं चरसि विश्ववारे ।

> *purāṇī devi yuvatiḥ puraṃdhir anu vrataṃ carasi viśvavāre |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-61-1).

> ईयुषीणामुपमा शश्वतीनां विभातीनां प्रथमोषा व्यश्चैत् ।

> *īyuṣīṇām upamā śaśvatīnāṃ vibhātīnāṃ prathamoṣā vyaśvait |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-15). She is praised as beginningless, eternal, bright, and a means of lighting up. And

> वाजिनीवती सूर्यस्य योषा चित्रामघा राय ईशे वसूनाम् ।

> *vājinīvatī sūryasya yoṣā citrāmaghā rāya īśe vasūnām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-48-3 [?]). In ṛks of this kind the relation of husband and wife between Indra, who is of the nature of the Āditya, and Uṣas is described. The purport is that, with the appearance of Uṣas, the rays of the Āditya spread and give consciousness to all living beings who lie almost dead.

> व्यु१षा आवः पथ्या३ जनानां पञ्च क्षितीर्मानुषीर्बोधयन्ती ।

> *vy uṣā āvaḥ pathyā janānāṃ pañca kṣitīr mānuṣīr bodhayantī |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-79-1 [?]). In many such places the benefit that has come to the world from the goddess Uṣas is described. That whole purpose is accomplished only by the favour of Indra, the lord of the entire world: this is the intention of the present ṛk. It has therefore been said, "*śavasā yena citayante*".

***vṛṣabha*** — *varṣiteḥ*: Indra is addressed by the word *vṛṣabha* as "one who sends rain". And, Indra is ***ugraḥ*** — *udgūrṇabalaḥ*, one filled with strength; ***sahodāḥ*** — *parābhavasāmarthyaṃ balaṃ sahaḥ tasya dātā*: since *sahas* is well known as the capacity for defeating others, Indra is the giver of that power of overcoming (the capacity to subdue others); ***sthaviraḥ*** — *purātanaḥ*: Indra has existed for a very long time: thus it is described.

---

### Printed p. 219  (PDF 239)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 5 continue.)*

(*śravaḥ dhāḥ* …) ***saḥ*** — *tādṛśaḥ*: Indra, thus impelled by greatness, ***ugrebhiḥ*** — *krūrabalaiḥ* — together with the Marut-gods of fierce power, ***śravo dhāḥ*** — *sarvatra śrūyamāṇam annaṃ dehi*: "give us the food that is well known everywhere and is needed by all": thus it is described.

***sahodāḥ*** — *parābhavasāmarthyaṃ sahaḥ tasya dātā*: the word *sahas* is read among the names of strength; but here the meaning "the power to overcome others" is given for *sahas*, and it is described that Indra grants it.

***vṛṣabha*** — *varṣiteḥ*: Sāyaṇa gives the meaning "one who sends rain". The Nirukta-writer says: "*prajāṃ varṣatīti vā atibṛhatir īte iti vā tad vṛṣakarmā varṣaṇād vṛṣabhaḥ*" [as read]; and Durgācārya explains "*prajotpattikāraṇaṃ retasiñcati*" — because he sprinkles seed for the production of progeny — "or because he renders his own body exceedingly vigorous for sprinkling semen": in this sense the word *vṛṣabha* is used.

> मरुत्वा इन्द्र वृषभो रणाय पिबा सोममनुष्वधं मदाय ।
> आ सिञ्चस्व जठरे मध्व ऊर्मिं त्वं राजासि प्रदिवः सुतानाम् ॥

> *marutvā indra vṛṣabho raṇāya pibā somam anuṣvadhaṃ madāya |*
> *ā siñcasva jaṭhare madhva ūrmiṃ tvaṃ rājāsi pradivaḥ sutānām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-47-1). Here the meaning of *vṛṣabhaḥ* is explained as *varṣitā rasānām* ("one who sprinkles the juices").

> प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं यं पूरवो वृत्रहणं सचन्ते ।
> वैश्वानरो दस्युमग्निर्जघन्वाँ अधूनोत्काष्ठा अव शम्बरं भेत् ॥

> *pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ yaṃ pūravo vṛtrahaṇaṃ sacante |*
> *vaiśvānaro dasyum agnir jaghanvāṃ adhūnot kāṣṭhā ava śambaraṃ bhet ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-6). In this ṛk also, for *vṛṣabhasya* the meaning "one who sprinkles the juices" is explained.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *mānāsaḥ* (root *mana jñāne*; by *bahulagrahaṇa*, *ghañ* in the agent sense; *ādivṛddhi* by "*ata upadhāyāḥ*", Pā. Sū. 7-2-116 [?]; since the affix is *ñ*-marked the first syllable is acute; *asuk* before *jas* by "*ājjaserasuk*"); *citayante* (root *citī saṃjñāne*; *ṇic* by "*hetumati ca*"; by the statement "*sañjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ*" there is no *guṇa* of the light penultimate; *laṭ* 3rd plural after the *ṇic*; as the *nighāta* is prevented by "*yadvṛttānnityam*", the accent of *ṇic* remains).

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वं साहीन्द्र सहीयसो नॄन्भवा मरुद्भिरवयातहेळाः ।
> सुप्रकेतेभिः सासहिर्दधानो विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ ६ ॥

> *tvaṃ sāhīndra sahīyaso nṝnbhavā marudbhiravayātaheḷāḥ |*
> *supraketebhiḥ sāsahirdadhāno vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वम् । साहि । इन्द्र । सहीयसः । नॄन् । भव । मरुत्ऽभिः । अवयातऽहेळाः ।
> सुप्रऽकेतेभिः । ससहिः । दधानः । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥ ६ ॥

> *tvam | sāhi | indra | sahīyasaḥ | nṝn | bhava | marut 'bhiḥ | avayāta 'heḷāḥ |*
> *supra 'ketebhiḥ | sasahiḥ | dadhānaḥ | vidyāma | iṣam | vṛjanam | jīra 'dānum ‖ 6 ‖*
