### Printed p. 221  (PDF 241)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र त्वं साहि । रक्ष । कान् । सहीयसो नॄन् सहस्वितमान् त्वदनुग्रहेणातिप्रवृद्धबलान्नेतॄन्नरानस्मान् मरुतो वा । किंच मरुद्भिः साकमस्मास्ववयातहेळा भव । अपगतमन्युर्भव । मरुत्सु वा तथा भव । किंच सुप्रकेतेभिः शोभनप्रज्ञानैर्मरुद्भिः सह सासहिः शत्रूणामभिभविता सन्दधानोऽस्मदभिमतस्य धारयिता भवेति शेषः । शिष्टो व्याख्यातः ॥ [reading doubtful in places]

*Gist:* Indra is to protect us, made exceedingly strong by his favour (or the Maruts), to put away anger against us and the Maruts, and, with the wise Maruts, to overcome enemies and uphold what we desire.

**Pratipadārtha.** *he indra* — O Indra; *tvam* — you; *sahīyasaḥ* — (by your favour) exceedingly strong; *nṝn* — (us) men, or the leaders (Marut-gods); *pāhi* — protect; *(kiṃca* — and*)* *marudbhiḥ* — accompanied by the Marut-gods; *avayātaheḷāḥ* — free from anger (towards us); *bhava* — be; *(and)* *marudbhiḥ* — with the Marut-gods; *supraketebhiḥ* — with the Marut-gods of excellent knowledge; *sāsahiḥ* — overcoming (enemies); *dadhānaḥ (bhava)* — be the upholder (of what is desired by us); *(vayam* — we, by your favour*)* *iṣam* — food; *vṛjanam* — strength; *jīradānum* — long life; *vidyāma* — may we obtain.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, protect us, who are of great strength by your favour; accompanied by the Marut-gods, give up your anger against us; together with the Marut-gods, endowed with good knowledge, overcome our enemies, and grant us food, strength and long life.

**English Translation (as printed):** Do you, Indra, cherish the vigorous leaders (of the rains), be free from displeasure against the Maruts: overcoming (our) enemies along with the intelligent (Muruts [sic]), support us (so that) we may obtain food, strength, and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***sahīyaso nṝn*** — here Indra is addressed. The word *sahas* is read among the names of strength by the Nirukta-writers (Ni. 2-[?]). From this: "*sahasvitamān tvadanugraheṇa atipravṛddhabalān*" — we sacrificers, whose strength has greatly increased by Indra's favour; the prayer is made that Indra may be our protector.

### Printed p. 222  (PDF 242)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

For the word *nṝn*, Sāyaṇa explains "*netṝn asmān marutaḥ vā*" — in two ways: "us, the leaders" or "the Marut-gods". The epithet *sahīyasaḥ* — "exceedingly strong" — fits both meanings. If the sage means himself and his descendants, it means that by Indra's favour they have obtained strong strength. Or, if it is an epithet of the Marut-gods, the power of the Marut-gods is described: their natural and collective power, and the heroic deeds performed in various ways by that power, are indicated by many epithets, such as *yujyebhiḥ pauṃsyebhiḥ*.

> सप्त सप्त हि मरुतो गणस्तस्मान्मारुतः सप्तकपालः ।

> *sapta sapta hi maruto gaṇas tasmān mārutaḥ saptakapālaḥ |*

(Śat. Brā. 2-5-1-13 [?])

> सप्त सप्त हि मारुतो गणः सर्वमेव्यैतेन रथं प्रीणाति ।

> *sapta sapta hi māruto gaṇaḥ sarvamevyaitena rathaṃ prīṇāti |*

(Śat. Brā. 5-4-3-17 [?]). From sentences of this kind it is understood that the Marut-gods are always in groups, and that in such a group a certain consciousness and power are naturally present. Therefore the epithet *sahīyasaḥ* is proper in the present ṛk.

***nṝn*** — it is explained also as "*netṝn prajārūpiṇaḥ marutaḥ*" — "the Marut-gods, who are leaders and who are of the nature of subjects": the Marut-gods are well known as the subjects of the deities.

> स एतान्मैन्द्रीं मरुत्वतीमजुहोत् [?] । क्षत्रं वा इन्द्रो विशो मरुतः क्षत्रं वै विशो निषेद्धा ॥ [as read]

> *sa etānmaindrīṃ marutvatīmajuhot [?] | kṣatraṃ vā indro viśo marutaḥ kṣatraṃ vai viśo niṣeddhā ‖ [as read]*

(Śat. Brā. 2-5-2-37 [?]). From sentences of this kind the meaning is understood; hence for the word *nṝn* the other meaning, *marutaḥ*, is also proper. The word *nara* is used in the Ṛk Saṃhitā itself, in many places, as an epithet of the Marut-gods. For example:

> चित्रैरञ्जिभिर्वपुषे व्यञ्जते वक्षःसु रुक्माँ अधि येतिरे शुभे ।
> अंसेष्वेषां नि मिमृक्षुरृष्टयः साकं जज्ञिरे स्वधया दिवो नरः ॥

> *citrair añjibhir vapuṣe vy añjate vakṣaḥsu rukmāṃ adhi yetire śubhe |*
> *aṃseṣv eṣāṃ ni mimṛkṣur ṛṣṭayaḥ sākaṃ jajñire svadhayā divo naraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-4)

> विश्ववेदसो रयिभिः समोकसः संमिश्लास्तविषीभिर्विरप्शिनः ।
> अस्तार इषुं दधिरे गभस्त्योरनन्तशुष्मा वृषखादयो नरः ॥

> *viśvavedaso rayibhiḥ samokasaḥ saṃmiślās taviṣībhir virapśinaḥ |*
> *astāra iṣuṃ dadhire gabhastyor anantaśuṣmā vṛṣakhādayo naraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-10). In many ṛks of this kind the word *naraḥ* shows the nature of the Marut-gods. In the same way, in the present ṛk too, *nṝn* may be taken to mean the Marut-gods.

---

### Printed p. 223  (PDF 243)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 6 continue.)*

***marudbhiḥ avayātaheḷāḥ bhava*** — it is wished that Indra, together with the Marut-gods, be free from anger toward us, or *apagatamanyur bhava* — that Indra be of a reconciled mind in respect of the Marut-gods. The word *heḷas* is read among the names of anger (Ni. 2-[?]); hence it is used here in the sense of anger.

***suprakeṭebhiḥ sāsahiḥ*** — it is prayed that Indra overcome our enemies together with the Marut-gods who are possessed of excellent knowledge, and that he may be *asmadabhimatasya dhārayitā bhava* — the one who accomplishes our desired objects, the sacrificers. The word *praketa* is explained by the Nirukta-writers with the example

> इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिराग्राच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा ।
> यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवायँ एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥

> *idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotir āgāc citraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā |*
> *yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāyaṃ evā rātry uṣase yonim āraik ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-1). In this ṛk *praketa* is explained as *prakṛṣṭatamaḥ* ("the most excellent"); Durgācārya gives the meaning *prajñātatamaḥ* ("the best known").

***vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum*** — by this sentence it is wished that we, the sacrificers, may obtain, by Indra's favour, food, strength, and the power of giving gifts. The sage Agastya has placed this sentence at the end of the sūktas that he recited. The word *iṣa* is read among the names of food, and the word *vṛjana* among the names of strength, as Yāska says; this has been said in many places earlier.

But the word *vṛjana* is not used only in the sense of strength. In the Ṛk Saṃhitā this word is also used so as to indicate other senses: violence, war, a mighty enemy, a mighty deity, and so on. For example:

> आषाढ्हं युत्सु पृतनासु पप्रिं स्वर्षामप्सां वृजनस्य गोपाम् ।

> *āṣāḍhaṃ yutsu pṛtanāsu papriṃ svarṣām apsāṃ vṛjanasya gopām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-30 [?]). Here, "*vṛjyate'nena iti vṛjanaṃ balam*" — that by which one is surrounded (protected) — "strength" is the meaning (or, since it protects, the meaning is strength). And

> मरुत्स्तोत्रस्य वृजनस्य गोपा वयमिन्द्रेण सनुयाम वाजम् ।

> *marutstotrasya vṛjanasya gopā vayam indreṇa sanuyāma vājam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-11). In ṛks of this kind, "*śatrūṇāṃ kṣepsuḥ indrasya*" — the meaning "Indra, who hurls enemies down" is given, and the strength of that Indra is indicated. Moreover, in the sense of "enclosure", this word means "a deceit that hides the truth" when used with the sense of truth; or "a house that grants protection". For example:

> यद्वा मरुत्वः परमे सधस्थे यद्वावमे वृजने मादयासे ।

> *yad vā marutvaḥ parame sadhasthe yad vāvame vṛjane mādayāse |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-101-8).

### Printed p. 224  (PDF 244)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 171".)*

— in ṛks of this kind Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning "house". The Skandasvāmin has explained *varjite yoṣaiḥ* as a sacrifice free of faults.

> दशस्या नः पुर्वणीक होतर्देवेभिरग्ने अग्निभिरिधानः ।
> रायः सूनो सहसो वावसाना अति स्रसेम वृजनं नांहः ॥

> *daśasyā naḥ purvaṇīka hotar devebhir agne agnibhir idhānaḥ |*
> *rāyaḥ sūno sahaso vāvasānā ati srasema vṛjanaṃ nāṃhaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-11-6) — in it the meaning "a harmful enemy";

> मा नो अज्ञाता वृजना दुराध्यो३माशिवासो अव क्रमुः ।

> *mā no ajñātā vṛjanā durādhyo māśivāso ava kramuḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-32-27 [?]) — in ṛks of this kind, "violence";

> विश्वेष्वेनं वृजनेषु पामि यो मे कुक्षी सुतसोमः पृणाति ।

> *viśveṣv enaṃ vṛjaneṣu pāmi yo me kukṣī sutasomaḥ pṛṇāti |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-28-2 [?]). In many ṛks beginning with these, the meaning is "war" (*saṃgrāma*) that is full of violence or of strength. And when "*vṛjyate'nena*" is said,

> युक्ता मातासीद्धुरि दक्षिणाया अतिष्ठद्गर्भो वृजनीष्वन्तः ।

> *yuktā mātāsīd dhuri dakṣiṇāyā atiṣṭhad garbho vṛjanīṣv antaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-9). In places of this kind the meanings "possessing water", "rows of clouds" are given. In many places this word is also used for an enemy, in the sense of one who is crooked (*vañcane, vakra*), by its qualities. The meaning of the word must be stated according to the context. In the present ṛk it means strength, or protection full of strength, or a house full of protection. By the change of the gender of this word the change of meaning is known. In giving the purport of the ṛk 1-165-11 [?], the scholar Max Müller, explaining this word, says:

*वृजन means an enclosure, whether it be derived from* वृज् *to ward off or from* वृज् *in the sense of clearing as in* वृक्तबर्हिः. *In either case the meaning remains much the same, namely, a field cleared for pasture or agriculture. In this sense,* वृजन *is neuter while as a masculine it means powerful, invigorating.* [S. B. E. XXXII. P 208]

That is, he holds that when the word *vṛjana* is used in the masculine, it means strength. But the Nirukta-writers, in neuter use alone, have read this word among the names of strength: "*vardhaḥ, vargaḥ, vṛjanam*" (Ni. 2-[?]).

***jīradānum*** — the special meanings of this word are explained in the ṛk 1-173-13 [?].

---

### Printed p. 225  (PDF 245)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 11"; a signature mark "XIII 15" is printed at the foot.)*

***vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum*** — this prayer is, in each of the sūktas composed by the sage Agastya, the concluding portion. This is a peculiarity of this sage's composition. Such repeated portions are well known by the name *udarka*. This kind of composition is seen in the sūktas of other sages as well — Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha, Gṛtsamada and the rest. In all, as stated in the Bṛhaddevatā, in the compositions of these eight sages — Bharadvāja, Gṛtsamada, Vasiṣṭha, Nodhā, Agastya, Vimada, Nabhāka and Kutsa — such repeated portions occur, and they may also be called *abhyāsa* ("repetition"). *Abhyāsa* means repeating a stated meaning again:

> उक्तार्थानामपि वाक्यं आदरातिशयोद्योतनाय पुनः पठ्यते ।

> *uktārthānām api vākyaṃ ādarātiśayodyotanāya punaḥ paṭhyate |*

— even a sentence whose sense has already been stated is read again to show an excess of regard. In such repetition there is no fault whatever. In such contexts the intensity of feeling is seen, as the Nirukta-writers support:

> अभ्यासे भूयांसमर्थं मन्यन्ते यथा होऽहोदर्शनीयोऽहो दर्शनीयेति ।

> *abhyāse bhūyāṃsam artham manyante yathā ho 'hodarśanīyo 'ho darśanīyeti |*

(Ni. 10-42 [?]). By the repetition, an intensification of feeling and a special force of effect appear. In the example "How beautiful she is!", in describing her beauty an excess of regard is seen. In the same way, to show the excess of regard in the highest feeling, repetitions of sentences occur very often. This matter has been explained in connection with the sūkta of the sage Parucchepa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]). Or, *udarka* means the mantra recited at the time of the completion of the sacrifice.

> या गोमतीरुषसः सर्ववीरा व्युच्छन्ति दाशुषे मर्त्याय ।
> वायोरिव सूनृतानामुदर्के ता अश्वदा अश्नवत्सोमसुत्वा ॥

> *yā gomatīr uṣasaḥ sarvavīrā vyucchanti dāśuṣe martyāya |*
> *vāyor iva sūnṛtānām udarke tā aśvadā aśnavat somasutvā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-18). In ṛks of this kind *udarka* means "completion, conclusion of the recitation". In the same way, in the present ṛks too, it means the completion of the sūkta together with them.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *sahīyasaḥ* (*sahaḥ balam asya asti iti sahasvī*; the affix *vin* in the sense of possession by "*asmāyāmedhāsrajo viniḥ*"; after it, the affix *īyasun* in the sense of excess; loss of *vin* by "*vinmatorluk*"; loss of the *ṭi* part by "*ṭeḥ*", Pā. Sū. 6-4-155 [?]; first syllable acute by "*ñnityādirnityam*"; accusative plural form).

### Printed p. 226  (PDF 246)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 172".)*

*(Grammar of Ṛk 6, concluded; noted briefly)*: *bhava* (root *bhū sattāyām*; *loṭ* 2nd singular; since it stands at the beginning of a *pāda*, no *nighāta*; since *śap* is unaccented, the accent of the root remains; the long vowel in the Saṃhitā by "*dvyacotastiṅaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 6-3-135 [?]); *avayātaheḷāḥ* (*avayātaḥ heḷaḥ yasmāt saḥ*; in the *bahuvrīhi* the first member keeps its accent); *supraketebhiḥ* (root *kita jñāne*; affix *ac*; *śobhanaḥ praketaḥ yeṣāṃ te taiḥ*; by "*nañsubhyām*" the last syllable of the latter member is acute; since *iṭ* before *bhis* is optional, *e* occurs); *sāsahiḥ* (root *ṣaha abhibhave*; by the statement "*utsargaś chandasi*" the affix *ki* by "*ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca*", Pā. Sū. 3-2-171 [?]; because there is no *liḍvadbhāva*, reduplication of the root; Vedic lengthening of the reduplicative syllable; accent on the last syllable by the affix); *dadhānaḥ* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *śānac* for *laṭ*; *ślu* as the vikaraṇa; reduplication and the rest on that occasion; first syllable acute by "*abhyastānām ādiḥ*"). ‖ 6 ‖

*Here ends the hundred and seventy-first Sūkta.* (ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ನೂರ ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂದನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತ ಮುಗಿದುದು.)

## Sūkta 172 — *citro va* (Anuvāka 23, eighth Sūkta; 3 ṛks)

*(Heading, p. 226: "The hundred and seventy-second Sūkta" — ನೂರ ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> चित्रो व इति तृचात्मकमष्टमं सूक्तमागस्त्यं मारुतं गायत्रम् । चित्रस्तृचं गायत्रमित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ लैङ्गिको विशेषविनियोगः ॥

*Gist:* The eighth sūkta (*citro vaḥ*), of three ṛks, by Agastya, to the Maruts, in gāyatrī metre.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This Sūkta beginning *citro vaḥ* is the eighth Sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has three ṛks. Agastya is the ṛṣi of this Sūkta; the Marut-gods are the deities; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said "*citrastṛcaṃ gāyatram*". The special application (*viniyoga*) is by the indicatory sign.

---

### Printed p. 227  (PDF 247)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 12".)*

**॥ ॐ ॥** Sūkta—172
Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 23 ‖ Sūkta 172 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 12 ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 3 · Ṛṣi: Agastya · Devatā: the Maruts · Chandas: *gāyatrī*.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> चित्रो वोऽस्तु यामश्चित्र ऊती सुदानवः ।
> मरुतो अहिभानवः ॥ १ ॥

> *citro vo 'stu yāmaścitra ūtī sudānavaḥ |*
> *maruto ahibhānavaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> चित्रः । वः । अस्तु । यामः । चित्रः । ऊती । सुऽदानवः ।
> मरुतः । अहिऽभानवः ॥ १ ॥

> *citraḥ | vaḥ | astu | yāmaḥ | citraḥ | ūtī | su 'dānavaḥ |*
> *marutaḥ | ahi 'bhānavaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः वो युष्माकं यामोऽस्मद्यज्ञागमनमस्माभिश्चायनीयः [?] पूज्य आश्चर्यभूतो वास्तु । भवतु । न केवलमागमनमेव चित्रं किंतु हे सुदानवः शोभनदाना हे अहिभानवोऽहीयमानप्रकाशाः युष्माकं संबन्धी चित्रः स आगम ऊत्यै रक्षणायेष्टार्पणाय वा युक्तश्च भवतु । तदागमनं शीघ्रमस्तु अभिमतप्रदं चास्त्वित्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* May the coming of the Maruts, bountiful and of undiminished splendour, be wonderful and bring us protection and the fulfilment of our desires.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *vaḥ* — your; *yāmaḥ* — coming (to our sacrificial hall); *citraḥ* — wonderful, causing astonishment; *astu* — be; *(ca)* *sudānavaḥ* — givers of excellent gifts; *ahibhānavaḥ* — of unfailing splendour, O Marut-gods; *citraḥ* — wondrous; *ūtī* — for (our) protection or for (our) accomplishment of desired objects; *(bhavatu* — be*)*.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, givers of excellent gifts and of unfailing splendour, may your coming (to our sacrificial hall) be wondrous, and may your coming bring us protection or the accomplishment of our desired objects.

### Printed p. 228  (PDF 248)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 172".)*

**English Translation (as printed):** Maruts, of inseparable splendour, may your coming be marvellous, liberal benefactors, for our protection.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***vaḥ yāmaḥ citraḥ astu*** — *yuṣmākam asmadyajñāgamanaṃ cāyanīyaḥ pūjyaḥ āścaryabhūto vā bhavatu*: the Marut-gods are addressed. It is described that their coming to our sacrifice, and their making us worthy of honour, are such as to cause astonishment to all.

It is well known that the vehicle of the Marut-gods and the manner of their movement are highly attractive. By the many epithets such as "*viśvaiḥ, viṣvāsaḥ, viśvayomarut*" [as read], the collective manner of movement of the Marut-gods is described. Here the prayer "*yāmaḥ citram astu*" is that your coming may be attractive and worthy of honour. The word *citra* is used both in the sense of beauty and in the sense of what is worthy of honour. In the manner of the Marut-gods' movement, these two qualities are complete. This description can be seen in the ṛks cited below:

> त्विषीमन्तो अध्वरस्येव दिद्युत्त्रेषु [?] च्यवनसो जुह्वो नाग्नेः ।
> अर्चत्रयो धुनयो न वीरा भ्राजज्जन्मानो मरुतो अधृष्टाः ॥

> *tviṣīmanto adhvarasyeva didyut treṣu [?] cyavanaso juhvo nāgneḥ |*
> *arcatrayo dhunayo na vīrā bhrājajjanmāno maruto adhṛṣṭāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-66-10 [?])

> त्वं वृधन्तं मारुतं भ्राजदृष्टिं रुद्रस्य सूनुं हवसा विवासे । [?]
> दिवः शर्धायु शुचयो मनीषा गिरयो नापः उग्रा अस्पृध्रन् ॥ [as read]

> *tvaṃ vṛdhantaṃ mārutaṃ bhrājadṛṣṭiṃ rudrasya sūnuṃ havasā vivāse | [?]*
> *divaḥ śardhāyu śucayo manīṣā girayo nāpaḥ ugrā aspṛdhran ‖ [as read]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-66-11 [?]). In ṛks of this kind the manner of movement of the Marut-gods is compared to the brightness of the attractive and pure flames of the sacrificial fire. In the same way, there are such examples in many other contexts.

***sudānavaḥ ahibhānavaḥ*** — by these words, which indicate qualities, the Marut-gods are described as *śobhanadānāḥ* — "givers of excellent gifts, who confer beneficial favours" — and as *ahīyamānaprakāśāḥ* — "those whose splendour increases abundantly without failing"; and it is with these very words that they are addressed.

***sudānavaḥ*** — *śobhanadānāḥ*: "those who give most generously, such as Indra and the rest" is the sense. The word *sudānavaḥ* also has the meaning "those full of sap" or "givers of sap". This word is (continued on the next page).

---

### Printed p. 229  (PDF 249)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 12"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue.)*

(*sudānavaḥ* continued) — used as an epithet; in some places *rasadātāraḥ* ("givers of sap") means those who send down excellent rain-water.

> पिन्वन्त्यपो मरुतः सुदानवः पयो घृतवद्विदथेष्वाभुवः ।

> *pinvanty apo marutaḥ sudānavaḥ payo ghṛtavad vidatheṣv ābhuvaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-6). In many places it is an epithet of the Marut-gods, and rain-water is prayed for from them. For the Marut-gods the epithet *jīradānu* also exists. In both senses the generosity of the deities is shown. But the generosity indicated by the word *sudānavaḥ* may be a quality of the sacrificer too, apart from the nature of the deities such as the Maruts:

> इषं पृञ्चन्ता सुकृते सुदानव आ बर्हिः सीदतं नरा ।

> *iṣaṃ pṛñcantā sukṛte sudānava ā barhiḥ sīdataṃ narā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-47-9 [?])

> सेदग्ने अस्तु सुभगः सुदानुर्यस्त्वा नित्येन हविषा य उक्थैः ।

> *sed agne astu subhagaḥ sudānur yas tvā nityena haviṣā ya ukthaiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4-8 [?]). In ṛks like these, *sudānuḥ* is an epithet of the sacrificer, who is an excellent giver. In ṛks such as 10-[?]-2, the word *dānu* may be taken to mean the *soma* juice. Besides,

> उत्तरा सूरधरः पुत्र आसीद्दानुः शये सहवत्सा न धेनुः ।

> *uttarā sūradharaḥ putra āsīd dānuḥ śaye sahavatsā na dhenuḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-9)

> सहदानुं पुरुहूत क्षियन्तमहस्तमिन्द्र सं पिणक्कुणारुम् ।

> *sahadānuṃ puruhūta kṣiyantam ahastam indra saṃ piṇak kuṇārum |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-30-8). In ṛks like these *dānu* means "the Asura woman, mother of Vṛtra". But when *sudānavaḥ* is used, the meaning is "generous givers"; in the present ṛk it is an epithet of the Marut-gods, and their generosity is shown. The special description of this was given when the word *jīradānu* was explained in the ṛk of the 173rd sūkta [as printed].

***yuṣmākaṃ saṃbandhī citraḥ sa āgamanaḥ ūtī rakṣaṇāya iṣṭatarpaṇāya vā bhavatu*** — "may your coming, worthy of honour, be for the protection of us, or for the fulfilment of our desires": thus it is wished. By "*tadāgamanaṃ śīghram astu abhimataprada ca astu*", the prayer is understood that the Marut-gods come quickly and fulfil our desired objects.

***ūtī*** — *ūtyai rakṣaṇāya iṣṭatarpaṇāya vā*: the word *ūti* is explained by Yāska as "*ūtir avanāt*" — from the root *ava*, conveying the meaning "protect", the word *ūti* has the meaning "protection". And in

> आ त्वा रथं यथोतये सुम्नाय वर्तयामसि ।
> तुविकूर्मिमृतीषहमिन्द्र शविष्ठ सत्पते ॥

> *ā tvā rathaṃ yathotaye sumnāya vartayāmasi |*
> *tuvikūrmim ṛtīṣaham indra śaviṣṭha satpate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-68-1)

### Printed p. 230  (PDF 250)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 172".)*

in this ṛk *ūtaye* is explained as "*avanāya rakṣaṇāya*": here, in the second meaning, "*iṣṭatarpaṇāya vā*" shows the manner of the protection.

***ahibhānavaḥ*** — Sāyaṇa explains this word as *ahīyamānaprakāśāḥ* — "those who have splendour that is not diminished in the least and is growing". But the English translators, taking the word *ahi* as "serpent", mean "those who have brightness like serpents". Their translation is:

*O Maruts, you bounteous givers, shining like snakes.* [S. B. E. XXXII. P. 293].

Or, if *ahi* is taken to mean "cloud", then *ahibhānavaḥ* may be said to have the brightness of the lightning that resides within the cloud. The Nirukta-writer, explaining the word *ahigopāḥ*, says

> अहिगोपा अतिष्ठन् । अहिना गुप्ताः । अहिरयनादेत्यन्तरिक्षे ।

> *ahigopā atiṣṭhan | ahinā guptāḥ | ahir ayanād ety antarikṣe |*

(Ni. 2-17 [?]). They have explained *ahi* as "cloud"; so, if here too the meaning "cloud" is given for *ahi*, it cannot be wrong. How?

> ते क्षोणीभिररुणेभिर्नाञ्जिभी रुद्रा ऋतस्य सदनेषु वावृधुः ।
> निमेघमाना अत्येन पाजसा सुश्चन्द्रं वर्णं दधिरे सुपेशसम् ॥

> *te kṣoṇībhir aruṇebhir nāñjibhī rudrā ṛtasya sadaneṣu vāvṛdhuḥ |*
> *nimeghamānā atyena pājasā suścandraṃ varṇaṃ dadhire supeśasam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-13). In ṛks of this kind the dwelling of the Marut-gods in the clouds — being within the clouds — and their shining with the lustre of gold, are described. Therefore the description given for the epithet *ahibhānavaḥ* in the present ṛk is like that in the ṛk above.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *yāmaḥ* (root *yā prāpaṇe*; Uṇādi affix *man*; the first syllable is acute since it is *n*-marked); *ūtī* (by "*ūtiyūtijūti…*", Pā. Sū. 3-3-97 [?] the word is formed irregularly from the root *av* with the affix *ktin* and the acute; before the dative singular, the lengthening to the preceding similar vowel by "*supāṃ sulak…*", Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]).

### Printed p. 231  (PDF 251)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 12"; grammar of Ṛk 1 concluded.)*

*(Grammar, noted briefly)*: *sudānavaḥ* (*śobhanaḥ dānuḥ yasya saḥ*; in the vocative the *āmantrita* accent, *nighāta*, applies); *marutaḥ* (since it stands at the beginning of a *pāda*, the *āmantrita nighāta* does not apply; the first syllable is acute by "*āmantritasya ca*", Pā. Sū. 6-1-198 [?]); *ahibhānavaḥ* (by "*āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat*" the preceding word, though present, is treated as non-existent, since there is no word after this, *nighāta* does not come, and, as before, the first syllable is acute). ‖ 1 ‖

*(ornamental rule)*

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आरे सा वः सुदानवो मरुत ऋञ्जती शरुः ।
> आरे अश्मा यमस्यथ ॥ २ ॥

> *āre sā vaḥ sudānavo maruta ṛñjatī śaruḥ |*
> *āre aśmā yamasyatha ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आरे । सा । वः । सुऽदानवः । मरुतः । ऋञ्जती । शरुः ।
> आरे । अश्मा । यम् । अस्यथ ॥ २ ॥

> *āre | sā | vaḥ | su 'dānavaḥ | marutaḥ | ṛñjatī | śaruḥ |*
> *āre | aśmā | yam | asyatha ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे सुदानवः शोभनदाना मरुतः वो युष्माकं संबन्धिन्यृञ्जती प्रसाधयन्ती स्वतेजसा स्वात्मानमलंकुर्वती प्रसिद्धिं प्राप्नुवाना वा सा प्रसिद्धा शरुर्हिंसका ऋष्टिरारे दूरे भवतु । तथा यमस्यथ क्षिपथ सोऽश्मा व्यापक आयुधविशेष आरे । दूरनामैतत् । दूरे भवतु । मां न प्राप्नोतु । यद्वा । आरेशब्द आराच्छब्दपर्यायः । स च दूरे समीपे च वर्तते । अत्र समीपवचनः । यमस्मत्तोऽन्यमस्यथ तं वैरिणमस्माकमुपलोपमः [?] कशिन आयुधविशेष आरे समीपं प्राप्नोतु ॥

*Gist:* May the Maruts' bright, harmful shaft, and the stone they hurl, be far from us; or, in the second sense, may it come near (the enemies).

**Pratipadārtha.** *sudānavaḥ* — O excellent givers; *(he)* *marutaḥ* — O Marut-gods; *vaḥ* — your; *ṛñjatī* — shining with brilliance; *sā śaruḥ* — that (famous) harmful weapon; *āre* — far (be); *yam* — which weapon; *asyatha* — you hurl; *(saḥ)* *aśmā* — that (pervading) weapon (hard as a stone); *āre* — far away (from us) (be). [*Or:* *yam* — which weapon; *asyatha* — you hurl (at our enemy, in his direction); *(saḥ)* *aśmā* — that hard weapon like a stone; *āre* — near (of that enemy) (be).]

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, excellent givers, may your harmful weapon, shining with brilliance, be far from us; may the stone-like weapon that you hurl be far from us; (or: may the weapon that you hurl bring our enemy near).

### Printed p. 232  (PDF 252)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 172".)*

**English Translation (as printed):** Maruts, liberal benefactors, may your bright destructive (shaft) be far from us: may the stone which you hurl be far from us.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***ṛñjatī*** — *prasādhayantī svatejasā svātmānam alaṅkurvatī prasiddhiṃ prāpnuvānā vā*: this word is used here as an epithet of the word *śaruḥ*, which denotes the weapon called *ṛṣṭi* belonging to the Marut-gods. The Nirukta-writer says "*ṛñjatiḥ prasādhanakarmā*" (Ni. 6-[?]): the word *ṛñjati* is used in the sense of "adorn"; and in the ṛk

> दूतं वो विश्ववेदसं हव्यवाहममर्त्यम् ।
> यजिष्ठमृञ्जसे गिरा ॥

> *dūtaṃ vo viśvavedasaṃ havyavāham amartyam |*
> *yajiṣṭham ṛñjase girā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-8-1 [?]) he shows the use [as printed: *yajiṣṭham*]. Sāyaṇa addresses the Marut-gods as "*sudānavaḥ marutaḥ*", "givers of many excellent things". It is explained that their weapon *ṛṣṭi* shines with its own brilliance, or is well known for destroying enemies; and that, though that weapon is harmful toward enemies, it should be far from us, the sacrificers.

***āre aśmā yamasyatha*** — *vyāpakaḥ āyudhaviśeṣaḥ dūre bhavatu māṃ na prāpnotu*: "the pervading weapon that you hurl, sent to punish, let it be far from us (since we are not their enemies)": so it is said, taking the word *āre* in the sense "far". In the second meaning, "*āreśabdaḥ ārāccabdaparyāyaḥ | sa ca dūre samīpe ca vartate*" — the word *āre*, being a synonym of the word *ārāt*, conveys both "far" and "near"; here the meaning "near" is explained, and "*asmatto'nyaṃ yaṃ vairiṇam*" — "the enemy other than us" — (continued).

---

### Printed p. 233  (PDF 253)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 12"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 2 conclude.)*

(*asyatha* continued) — *asmākam upalopamaḥ kaśinaḥ āyudhaviśeṣaḥ taṃ vairiṇaṃ samīpaṃ prāpnotu*: the weapon launched by the Marut-gods who are being worshipped in the sacrifice, at enemies other than us, the sacrificers, though hard as a stone, should reach the proximity of those enemies and destroy them: this is wished. The word *āre* is read among the names of "far" (Ni. 3-20 [?]). Sāyaṇa here explains the usage as a synonym of *ārāt*, in the sense of "far" or "near".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *ṛñjatī* (the root *ṛñj* is used in the sense of adorning; *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; when the feminine is intended, *ṅīp* by "*ugitaś ca*", Pā. Sū. 4-1-6 [?]; since *ṅīp* comes after a *śatṛ* without *num*, it takes the acute by "*śatur anumo nadyajādī*"); *śaruḥ* (root *śṛ hiṃsāyām*; *śṛṇāti iti śaruḥ*; affix *un* by an Uṇādi sūtra, "*śṛ svṛ snihi…*"; *guṇa* of the root's *ṛ* on that occasion, with *r* following); *aśmā* (root *aśū vyāptau*; affix *manin* by an Uṇādi sūtra, "*aśeśkikibhyāṃ chandasi*" [as read]; since it is *n*-marked, the first syllable is acute); *asyatha* (root *asu kṣepaṇe*; *laṭ* 2nd plural; since *yat* is connected, no *nighāta*; since *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented by "*tāsyanudāttet…*", the accent of the root remains; *śyan* being *n*-marked, the first syllable is acute). ‖ 2 ‖

*(ornamental rule)*

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तृणस्कन्दस्य नु विशः परि वृङ्क्त सुदानवः ।
> ऊर्ध्वान्नः कर्त जीवसे ॥ ३ ॥

> *tṛṇaskandasya nu viśaḥ pari vṛṅkta sudānavaḥ |*
> *ūrdhvānnaḥ karta jīvase ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 234  (PDF 254)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 172".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तृणऽस्कन्दस्य । नु । विशः । परि । वृङ्क्त । सुऽदानवः ।
> ऊर्ध्वान् । नः । कर्त । जीवसे ॥ ३ ॥

*(The Pada is printed on p. 233 and the Saṃhitā likewise; the bhāṣya begins on p. 234.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मरुतः सुदानवः शोभनदानाः यूयं तृणस्कन्दस्य तृणवच्चलनस्वभावस्य शुष्यमाणस्य वा ममा विशः पुत्रभृत्यादिरूपाः प्रजा नु क्षिप्रं परि वृङ्क्त । परिवर्जयत । बाधापरिहारेण रक्षत । यद्वा । उक्तलक्षणकालस्यासुरविशेषस्य वा प्रजाः परिवर्जयत । किंच नोऽस्मानूर्ध्वान् कर्त । कुरुत । जीवसे चिरजीवनायेति ॥ [reading doubtful in places]

*Gist:* Maruts, protect the people (sons, servants) of me, restless as grass, and make us excellent for long life; or (in the second sense) destroy the people of the Asura Tṛṇaskanda.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he)* *sudānavaḥ* — O liberal ones, Marut-gods (you); *tṛṇaskandasya* — of one who, like grass, is restless by nature, or who withers (my); *viśaḥ* — the sons, servants and the like; *nu* — quickly; *pari vṛṅkta* — protect, removing obstacles; [*or* *tṛṇaskandasya* — of the Asura named Tṛṇaskanda; *viśaḥ* — the sons, servants and the like (the peoples); *nu* — quickly; *pari vṛṅkta* — destroy]; *(kiṃca* — and*)* *naḥ* — us; *jīvase* — in order to live (long); *ūrdhvān* — excellent; *kartā* — make.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Marut-gods, of liberal gifts, protect, by removing hindrances, my sons, servants and the rest, who am restless as grass; and make us excellent in life, so that we may live long.

**English Translation (as printed):** Maruts, liberal benefactors, protect my people, (although I be) as insignificant as grass: lift us up, that we may live.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

***tṛṇaskandasya*** — *tṛṇavat calanasvabhāvasya śuṣyamāṇasya vā*: since this word is used as an epithet of the word *mama* (meaning the sacrificer), it is described that the sacrificer is of a nature that moves like a blade of grass. Or, Sāyaṇa has also said that it is a proper name (*aṅkita-nāma*): by "*uktalakṣaṇakālasya asuraviśeṣasya vā*" it can be taken that *Tṛṇaskanda* is a certain Asura. In that case *tṛṇaskanda* means one who moves, hidden within a cloud — his quality is indicated. The word *tṛṇa* means "cloud": "a cloud, thickened, rubbed and torn; then the rain falls". "*tṛdyate'sau iti tṛṇaḥ*" — formed from the root *tṛd* ("to tear"), rubbed and torn: therefore the cloud has the name *tṛṇa*: this is Durgācārya's explanation. "*tṛndyāt tṛṇam*" … (continued)

---

### Printed p. 235  (PDF 255)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 12".)*

(*tṛṇaskandasya* continued) — the Nirukta-writers have given the derivation of this word in another context (Ni. 1-[?]); the meaning is "make move", from the root *skand*. Or *tṛṇaskanda* may mean a locust that hops and flies. In the same way, the movement of that Asura may be so described. Since this word is used in the Ṛk Saṃhitā in this one place only, the meaning has to be stated suitably here.

***viśaḥ nu parivṛṅktā*** — two kinds of meaning are explained for this sentence. In the first, the word *viśaḥ* is explained as the sons and the servants — the progeny and the rest — connected with the sacrificer; the prayer is that the Marut-gods, by removing hindrances, protect these progeny, so that they are not troubled in any way. In the second meaning, ***yadvā uktalakṣaṇakālasya asuraviśeṣasya vā prajāḥ parivarjayata*** — "destroy the progeny of the time of the kind described, which causes distress to the sacrificer, or of an Asura named Tṛṇaskanda — his sons and servants of evil nature": the favour of the Marut-gods is wished. The word *viśaḥ* is read among the names of men (Ni. 2-[?]). And

> जराबोध तद्विविड्ढि विशे विशे यज्ञियाय ।
> स्तोमं रुद्राय दृशीकम् ॥

> *jarābodha tad viviḍḍhi viśe viśe yajñiyāya |*
> *stomaṃ rudrāya dṛśīkam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-114-4 [?]). In this ṛk the words *viśe viśe* are used in the sense of *manuṣyasya manuṣyasya* ("of each man"). Sāyaṇa explains *putrabhṛtyādirūpāḥ prajāḥ* ("progeny in the form of sons, servants and the like").

***naḥ ūrdhvān kartā jīvase*** — *asmān cirajīvanāya kuruta*: the prayer is that the Marut-gods grant that we, the sacrificers, may live for a very long time. "*ūrdhva ucchritaḥ bhavati*" (Ni. 2-[?]) — the meaning is "elevated". In general the word is used to show worldly elevation, but in the present ṛk it means exceedingly excellent material and spiritual progress.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: *tṛṇaskandasya* (*tṛṇavat skandaḥ pariścalanaṃ yasya*; accent on the last syllable by the rule for compounds); *vṛṅkta* (root *vṛjī varjane*; *loṭ* 2nd plural; since there is no *liṅvadbhāva*, *ta* by "*tasthasthamipāṃ tāntaṃtāmaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 3-4-101 [?]; *śnam* as vikaraṇa; loss of its *a* by "*śnasoralloṇaḥ*" [as read], Pā. Sū. 6-4-111 [?]; *anusvāra* for *n* by the following-class nasal; *nighāta*).

*(Grammar of Ṛk 3, concluded; noted briefly)*: *kartā* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *loṭ* 2nd plural; when *ta* arises, *tana* replaces it by "*taptanaptanthanāśca*", Pā. Sū. 7-1-45 [?]; *luk* of the vikaraṇa by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*"; since the affix is *p*-marked, no *ñ*-ness comes; *guṇa* by "*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*"; *r* follows; *nighāta*); *jīvase* (root *jīva prāṇadhāraṇe*; in the sense of an infinitive the affix *ase* by "*tumarthe sese…*", Pā. Sū. 3-4-9 [?]; the first syllable of the affix is acute; since it ends in a diphthong (*ejanta*), it gets the name *avyaya* by "*kṛnmejantaḥ*", Pā. Sū. 1-1-39 [?]). ‖ 3 ‖

## Sūkta 173 — *gāyat sāma* (Anuvāka 23, ninth Sūkta; 13 ṛks)

*(Heading, p. 236: "The hundred and seventy-third Sūkta" — ನೂರ ಎಪ್ಪತ್ತಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> गायत्साम [?] इति त्रयोदशर्चं नवमं सूक्तमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभमैन्द्रम् । गायत्स्तोत्रीया [?] इत्यनुक्रान्तम् ॥ समूळ्हे दशरात्रे तृतीयेऽहनि छन्दोमे मरुत्वतीये शस्त्र एतत्सूक्तम् । विश्वजितोऽग्निं नर इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । तृतीयस्येन्द्रः स्वाहा गायत्साम । आ. ८-७ [?] । इति ॥

*Gist:* The ninth sūkta (*gāyat sāma*), of thirteen ṛks, by Agastya, to Indra, in triṣṭubh; used in the Marutvatīya litany of the third day of the ten-day Samūḍha rite.

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This Sūkta beginning *gāyat sāma* is the ninth Sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has thirteen ṛks. Agastya is the ṛṣi of this Sūkta; Indra is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said "*gāyatstotrīyā*" [as read]. In the sacrifice called *samūḍha*, performed over ten days, the application of this Sūkta in the Marutvatīya-śastra mantras at the time of the recitation of the mantras of the third (*chandoma*) day is stated by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section beginning *viśvajito'gniṃ naraḥ*, by the sūtra "*tṛtīyasyendraḥ svāhā gāyatsāma*" (Āś. 8-7 [?]).

### Printed p. 237  (PDF 257)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 13".)*

**॥ ॐ ॥** Sūkta—173
Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 23 ‖ Sūkta 173 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 13, 14, 15 ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 13 · Ṛṣi: Agastya · Devatā: Indra · Chandas: *triṣṭubh*.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> गायत्साम नभन्यं यथा वेरर्चाम तद्वावृधानं स्वर्वत् ।
> गावो धेनवो बर्हिष्यदब्धा आ यत्सद्मानं दिव्यं विवासान् ॥ १ ॥

> *gāyatsāma nabhanyaṃ yathā verarcāma tadvāvṛdhānaṃ svarvat |*
> *gāvo dhenavo barhiṣyadabdhā ā yatsadmānaṃ divyaṃ vivāsān ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> गायत् । साम । नभन्यम् । यथा । वेः । अर्चाम । तत् । वावृधानम् । स्वःऽवत् ।
> गावः । धेनवः । बर्हिषि । अदब्धाः । आ । यत् । सद्मानम् । दिव्यम् । विवासान् ॥ १ ॥

> *gāyat | sāma | nabhanyam | yathā | veḥ | arcāma | tat | vāvṛdhānam | svaḥ 'vat |*
> *gāvaḥ | dhenavaḥ | barhiṣi | adabdhāḥ | ā | yat | sadmānam | divyam | vivāsān ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इन्द्र नभन्यं नभस्यं नभसि भवं नभोव्यापिनं हिंसकं वा राक्षसादिकस्य । नभतिर्वधकर्मा नभत्यर्दतीति वधकर्मसु गणनात् । तादृशं साम हे इन्द्र यथा वेः येन प्रकारेण वेत्सि तथा गायत् । गायत्युद्गाता । तत्तस्मात्कारणाद्वावृधानं वर्धमानं स्वर्वत् फलभूतेन स्वर्गेण तद्वच्छस्त्रं यथा वेः तथार्चाम । पूजयाम । शंसाम इत्यर्थः । स्तुतशमनुशंसतीति न्यायात् । यद्वा । तदुक्तलक्षणं साम वावृधानं सर्वत्र यथा भवति तथार्चाम । किंच धेनवो दोग्ध्र्योऽदब्धा अहिंसिता गावो यद्बर्हिषि सद्मानं सीदन्तं दिव्यं दिवि भवमिन्द्रं त्वामा विवासान् । विवासतिः परिचरणकर्मा । आगत्य परिचरन्ति क्षीरं दुहन्ति तथार्चाम ॥ [reading doubtful in places]

*Gist:* As the Udgātṛ sings the sky-reaching Sāman that you know, so we praise it, a Sāman that grows and confers heaven, as the unharmed cows serve you, the heavenly Indra, seated on our sacred grass.

**Pratipadārtha.** *(he indra)* — O Indra; *nabhanyam* — sky-pervading (harmful to Rākṣasas and the like); *sāma* — the Sāman; *yathā* — in what manner; *veḥ* — you know (it); *(tathā)* — in the same manner; *gāyat* — (the *udgātṛ*) sings; *tat* — for that reason; *vāvṛdhānam* — which grows; *svarvat* — conferring the fruit of heaven; *sāma* — the Sāman; *arcāma* — (as you are worthy of acceptance) we offer (praise); [*or* *svarvat* — heaven-possessing; *tat* — that Sāman; *vavṛdhānam* — as it prospers everywhere; *arcāma* — we praise]; *(kiṃca* — and*)* *dhenavaḥ* — milk-giving; *adabdhāḥ* — unharmed; *gāvaḥ* — cows; *barhiṣi* — on the *kuśa* grass; *sadmānam* — seated; *divyam* — heavenly; *yat* — as; *ā vivāsān* — they come and serve; *(tathā arcāma* — so we worship*)*.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, the Sāman that the *udgātṛ* priests sing is worthy of your acceptance and pervades the sky; we praise that very Sāman as the means of prosperity, conferring heaven; and, as unharmed milk-giving cows serve you, the heavenly one, seated on the *kuśa* grass in our sacrificial hall, with their milk, so we worship you.

### Printed p. 238  (PDF 258)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

**English Translation (as printed):** The priests chant the heaven-ascending Sama, as you know (it) for such (praise) do we venerate as the cause of increase and conferrer of heaven, whence the eows [sic] unimpeded, do honour to the divine (Indra), who is seated on the sacred grass.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

Sāyaṇa states that the present sūkta, 1-173, belongs to the *Marutvatīya* litany (*śastra*) which the *hotṛ* has to recite at the time of the midday pressing, saying "*samūḍhe daśarātre tṛtīye chandome marutvatīye śastre etat sūktam*" ("in the *samūḍha* ten-day rite, on the third, *chandoma*, day, in the Marutvatīya litany, this sūkta"). To know what place this sūkta has in that litany, one must first know the nature of the Marutvatīya litany. A prior story explaining the nature of this litany is cited in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. If one examines the section on the Marutvatīya litany, the Marut-gods, having shown their trust, appear as a cause of faith to Indra, and Indra desires that, along with them, a share in the oblation offered to him be obtained also.

> इन्द्रो वै वृत्रं हनिष्यन्त्सर्वा देवता अब्रवीदनु मोपतिष्ठध्वमुप मा ह्वयध्वमिति तथेति तं हनिष्यन्त आद्रवन्नोऽन्वेन्नामं वै हनिष्यन्ते आद्रवन्ति हन्तेमान् भीषया इति [?] तानभिप्राश्चसीत् [?] तस्य श्वसथादीषमाणा विश्वे देवा अद्रवन्मरुतो हैनं नाजहुः प्रहर भगवो जहि वीरयस्वेत्येवैनमेतां वाचं वदन्त उपातिष्ठन्त ॥ [as read]

> *indro vai vṛtraṃ haniṣyantsarvā devatā abravīdanu mopatiṣṭhadhvamupa mā hvayadhvamiti tatheti taṃ haniṣyanta ādravanno 'nvennāmaṃ vai haniṣyante ādravanti hantemān bhīṣayā iti [?] tānabhiprāścasīt [?] tasya śvasathādīṣamāṇā viśve devā adravanmaruto hainaṃ nājahuḥ prahara bhagavo jahi vīrayasvetyevainametāṃ vācaṃ vadanta upātiṣṭhanta ‖ [as read]*

(Ai. Brā. 3-20 [?]).

### Printed p. 239  (PDF 259)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 13"; the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue.)*

(Aitareya Brāhmaṇa story, continued; given in Kannada) — When Indra was about to kill Vṛtra, he said to all the gods, "Help me in this work of killing Vṛtra"; and when he asked thus, they agreed, saying "so be it", and came running for it. Then the Asura Vṛtra, saying "They are coming to kill me; I shall frighten them", let loose his breath. At once all the gods, terrified, fled. But the Marut-gods alone did not leave Indra; they urged Indra, "Strike him, use your whole strength against him" — this very matter is praised in the ṛk

> वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथादीषमाणा विश्वे देवा अजहुर्ये सखायः ।
> मरुद्भिरिन्द्र सख्यं ते अस्त्वथेमा विश्वाः पृतना जयासि ॥

> *vṛtrasya tvā śvasathād īṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahur ye sakhāyaḥ |*
> *marudbhir indra sakhyaṃ te astv athemā viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāsi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-7). Therefore Indra, remembering the help the Marut-gods had given him in his time of distress, [says the Brāhmaṇa]:

> सोऽवेदिमे वै किल मे सखिना [?] इमे माकामयन्त हन्तेमानस्मिन्नुक्थे आभजा इति तानेतस्मिन्नुक्थे आभजदथ हैते तर्ह्येभे एव निष्केवल्ये उक्थे आसतुः । मरुत्वतीयं ग्रहं गृह्णाति मरुत्वतीयं प्रगाथं शंसति मरुत्वतीयं सूक्तं शंसति मरुत्वतीयो निविदं दधाति मरुतां सा भक्तिः ॥ [as read]

> *so 'vedime vai kila me sakhinā [?] ime mākāmayanta hantemānasminnukthe ābhajā iti tānetasminnukthe ābhajadatha haite tarhyebhe eva niṣkevalye ukthe āsatuḥ | marutvatīyaṃ grahaṃ gṛhṇāti marutvatīyaṃ pragāthaṃ śaṃsati marutvatīyaṃ sūktaṃ śaṃsati marutvatīyo nividaṃ dadhāti marutāṃ sā bhaktiḥ ‖ [as read]*

(Ai. Brā. 3-20 [?]). "These Marut-gods are my true friends. They pleased me. Therefore I shall give them, too, a share in the *uktha* I had designed for myself": so resolving, he gave them a share. For the Marut-gods he took the cup (*graha*), he recited the *pragātha*, and so on; thus it is said, in the context of the Marutvatīya litany, that he honoured them in many ways. And

> इन्द्रं वै वृत्रं जघ्निवांसं नास्तृतेति [?] मन्यमानाः सर्वा देवता अजहुस्तं मरुत एव स्वापयो नाजहुः । प्राणा वै मरुतः स्वापयः प्राणा हैवैनं तं नाजहुस्तस्मादेषोऽच्युतः स्वापिमान् प्रगाथः शस्यते आस्वापे स्वापिभिरिति ॥ [as read]

> *indraṃ vai vṛtraṃ jaghnivāṃsaṃ nāstṛteti [?] manyamānāḥ sarvā devatā ajahustaṃ maruta eva svāpayo nājahuḥ | prāṇā vai marutaḥ svāpayaḥ prāṇā haivainaṃ taṃ nājahustasmādeṣo 'cyutaḥ svāpimān pragāthaḥ śasyate āsvāpe svāpibhiriti ‖ [as read]*

(Ai. Brā. 3-16 [?]). At the time of the killing of Vṛtra all the gods abandoned Indra; only the Marut-gods, as his friends, as his vital breaths, did not abandon him. Because they did not abandon Indra, this indicates the very close relation between Indra and the Marut-gods; and, besides, in describing the nature of the Marutvatīya *graha*, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also tells of the relation between Indra and the Marut-gods

### Printed p. 240  (PDF 260)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

and likewise, of the relation of king and subjects between them. The nature of the Marutvatīya *graha*, *pragātha*, *nivid* and the litanies, mentioned in the sentence of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa quoted above, will be explained later.

"*tṛtīye chandome marutvatīyaśastre etat sūktam*" — Sāyaṇa has said this in the introduction to the sūkta. In a *dvādaśāha* (twelve-day rite), the *stomas* to be recited on the seventh, eighth and ninth days are called *chandoma*. In three orders — *caturviṃśa*, *catuścatvāriṃśa* and *aṣṭacatvāriṃśa* — the *chandoma stomas* have forms of praise. Among them the present sūkta belongs to the third *chandoma*. This is only a part of the Marutvatīya litany. How the remaining sūktas are used in the Marutvatīya litany will be explained later.

***nabhanyam*** — *nabhasi bhavaṃ nabhanyaṃ nabhovyāpinam | hiṃsakaṃ vā rākṣasādikasya | nabhate ardayati*: the word *nabhate*, among the names of killing, is read by Yāska (Ni. 2-[?]). Sāyaṇa, accepting the reading *nabhasyam* [as printed] for *nabhanyam*, explains it as an epithet of the word *sāma*: two kinds of meaning are explained — that this Sāman pervades the atmosphere because it is sung loudly (with a tremor), and that it harms the Rākṣasas and the like, who cause evil.

***nabhanyaṃ sāma yathā veḥ*** — another kind of meaning may also be given to this. The same sentence is quoted in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, and Keith, the English scholar, in translating it, gives a meaning at variance with that which Sāyaṇa explains:

*"Let him say the Saman, springing forth as of a bird."* [Harward Oriental Series Vol. 25 p. 245].

Here *veḥ yathā* is taken as "as of a bird", and *nabhanyam* as "that which manifests itself of itself, flashes forth". This meaning is not at all improper; it suits the context. There is also a basis for stating the purport in this manner: as a bird flies quickly to approach, so the devotee approaches Indra swiftly; the comparison with a bird is made in the Ṛk Saṃhitā itself. For example:

> वयः सुपर्णा उप सेदुरिन्द्रं प्रियमेधा ऋषयो नाधमानाः ।
> अप ध्वान्तमूर्णुहि पूर्धि चक्षुर्मुमुग्ध्यस्मान्निधयेव बद्धान् ॥

> *vayaḥ suparṇā upa sedur indraṃ priyamedhā ṛṣayo nādhamānāḥ |*
> *apa dhvāntam ūrṇuhi pūrdhi cakṣur mumugdhy asmān nidhayeva baddhān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-73-11 [?]). This ṛk also belongs among the Marutvatīya *nivid* mantras. Here, for the word *vayaḥ*, the Nirukta-writers show the derivation, *(continued)*

### Printed p. 241  (PDF 261)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 4, Varga 13"; a signature mark "XIII 16" is printed at the foot.)*

(*vayaḥ* continued)

> वयो वेर्बहुवचनम् । सुपर्णाः सुपतनाः ।

> *vayo ver bahuvacanam | suparṇāḥ supatanāḥ |*

(Ni. 4-3 [?]). The plural of *vi* is *vayaḥ*: as birds of excellent plumage come flying, the sages come quickly and approach Indra: so the meaning is given for the word *vi*. And

> गन्तृत्वात्, पक्षिसादृश्याद्वा मरुतोऽत्र वयः उच्यन्ते

> *gantṛtvāt, pakṣisādṛśyādvā maruto 'tra vayaḥ ucyante*

— because of their quality of moving attractively and because of their resemblance to birds, the Marut-gods themselves are here called *vayaḥ*: so Sāyaṇa has explained in many places (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-19-3 [?]). As there, so here also *veḥ yathā* can be taken to mean "like a bird". Then one has to know what *nabhanya* means. For the word *nabhanya* Sāyaṇa earlier gave the meaning

> नभसि आकाशे भवो नभस्वान् वायुरिव ।

> *nabhasi ākāśe bhavo nabhasvān vāyuriva |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. bhāṣya 1-169-3 [?]) — "like the wind (*nabhasvān*) that is in the sky" — this word being used as an epithet of the Vāyu who dwells in the sky. The Nirukta-writers include the word *nabhati* among the names of killing, with "*nabhati, ardati*" (Ni. 2-19 [?]); therefore Sāyaṇa, on that basis, giving a different meaning in the present ṛk — "*nabhovyāpinaṃ hiṃsakaṃ vā rākṣasādikasya*" — says that the sense is "harmful to Rākṣasas". But

> प्र ब्राह्मणो अङ्गिरसो नक्षन्त प्र क्रन्दनुर्नभन्यस्य वेतु ।
> प्र धेनव उदप्रुतो नवन्त युज्यातामद्री अध्वरस्य पेशः ॥

> *pra brāhmaṇo aṅgiraso nakṣanta pra krandanur nabhanyasya vetu |*
> *pra dhenava udapruto navanta yujyātām adrī adhvarasya peśaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-42-1), where for the words *nabhanyasya stotrasya* they give the meaning "praise" (*stuti*). In this context, as Keith says, "springing forth", the inner feeling, shining forth in a poetic form of praise, in the form of a hymn, approaches Indra: this is what it means; then the resemblance to a bird is fitting. The scholar Monier-Williams too, in his Sanskrit-English Dictionary, gives for this word the meaning "springing forth (as a hymn, horse etc.)".

Therefore, in the sentence "*nabhanyaṃ sāma yathā veḥ*" of the present ṛk, it is more appropriate than Sāyaṇa's reading, which makes *veḥ* a verb form, to take *veḥ* as the genitive of the word *vi* ("of a bird"), and to say that the hymn (Sāman), attractive and swift as a bird, arises from the heart and approaches Indra. The meaning of the word *sāma* also supports this.

### Printed p. 242  (PDF 262)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

***sāma*** — the Nirukta-writers, explaining the derivation of this word, say

> साम सम्मितमृचा [?] अस्य केट् [?] ऋचा संमीयते इति नैदानाः ।

> *sāma saṃmitam ṛcā asya keṭ ṛcā saṃmīyate iti naidānāḥ |*

(Ni. 7-12 [?]) — either because it shows its measure through the measure of the ṛk, or, from the root *as* (*kṣepaṇe*), with the meaning *ase*, it came to be well known as *sāma*: thus it is said. And the opinion of the experts in the Nidāna science is also stated, that since it is of the same measure as the ṛk, it has the name *sāma*. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa describes as follows the relation between the ṛk and the Sāman:

> ऋक्च वा इदमग्रे साम चास्तां सैव नाम ऋगासीदमो नाम साम सा वा ऋक्सामोपावदत्सह मिथुनं संभवाव प्रजात्या इति नेत्यब्रवीत्साम ज्यायान्वा अतो मम महिमेति ते द्वे भूत्वोपावदतां तेन प्रतिचन समवदते ताः तिस्रो भूत्वोपावदंस्तत्तिसृभिः समभवत्स्मात्तिसृभिस्तुवन्ति तिसृभिरुद्गायन्ति तिसृभिर्हि साम संमितं तस्मादेकस्य बह्व्यो जाया भवन्ति नैकस्यै बहवः सह पतयो यद्वै तत्सा चामश्च समभवतां तत्साम्नः सामत्वम् ॥ [as read; garbled in places]

> *ṛkca vā idamagre sāma cāstāṃ saiva nāma ṛgāsīdamo nāma sāma sā vā ṛksāmopāvadatsaha mithunaṃ saṃbhavāva prajātyā iti netyabravītsāma jyāyānvā ato mama mahimeti te dve bhūtvopāvadatāṃ tena praticana samavadate tāḥ tisro bhūtvopāvadaṃstattisṛbhiḥ samabhavatsmāttisṛbhistuvanti tisṛbhirudgāyanti tisṛbhirhi sāma saṃmitaṃ tasmādekasya bahvyo jāyā bhavanti naikasyai bahavaḥ saha patayo yadvai tatsā cāmaśca samabhavatāṃ tatsāmnaḥ sāmatvam ‖ [as read; garbled in places]*

(Ai. Brā. 3-23 [?]). In the beginning the ṛk and the Sāman were together. The ṛk was in the form of a female, and the Sāman in the form of a male. Then the ṛk approached the Sāman and said, "Let both of us unite in a marital relation and bring forth progeny"; the Sāman said, "No, my greatness is more than yours." Then the ṛk, taking two forms, asked again; even then the Sāman did not agree. Taking three forms, she asked, and the Sāman agreed; since the Sāman was joined with three ṛks, they praise with three ṛks (a *tṛca*), and sing with three ṛks. Therefore, in the world too, it is established that a man has many wives, and that a woman does not have many husbands. Thus, because the ṛk and the Sāman were united — *sā* + *ama* — the name *sāma* became well known.

The relation between the ṛk, which is of the nature of a hymn (*arka*), and the Sāman is described in many places as a marital relation. In the Śatapatha and other Brāhmaṇas, and in the Chāndogya and other Upaniṣads, the ṛk is indicated as the wife and the Sāman as the husband.

> तद्यथा पितुः पुत्रमेवं त्रीणि प्रथमान्याहाथ कस्माद्वै कामयोः संक्रामतीति साम वा ऋचः पतिस्तद्यत्त्रापि यथा पितुः पुत्रमेवं ब्रूयाद्यथा [as read, garbled; continues on the next page]

> *tadyathā pituḥ putramevaṃ trīṇi prathamānyāhātha kasmādvai kāmayoḥ saṃkrāmatīti sāma vā ṛcaḥ patistadyattrāpi yathā pituḥ putramevaṃ brūyādyathā [as read, garbled; continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 243  (PDF 263)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13".)*

Continuation of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa quotation (reading garbled, as printed):

> पतिग्ंसंतं पुत्रं ब्रूयात् [?] … तस्माद्यज्ञ [?] … त्रिः संतनोतीति पितरं पुत्रं पौत्रं तांस्तत्सन्तनोति तस्मादु तेभ्य एक एव पदधाति [?]

> *patigṃsaṃtaṃ putraṃ brūyāt [?] … tasmād yajña [?] … triḥ saṃtanotīti pitaraṃ putraṃ pautraṃ tāṃs tat santanoti tasmād u tebhya eka eva padadhāti [?]*

(Śa. Brā. 8-1-2-9 [?]). Gist: when the relation of father and son is spoken of, the question arises what is fitting to compare it with in the case of the Sāman and the ṛk; the Sāman is the husband (*pati*) of the ṛk, and the husband's place is shown accordingly. The Sāman has three stages, father, son, grandson (*pitṛ, putra, pautra*), as the ṛk has three verses; thus the relation of the ṛk and its husband, the Sāman, is made known.

In the same way the Chāndogya Upaniṣad also shows the relation of the ṛk and the Sāman, describing it in one way on the *adhidaivata* side and in another on the *adhyātma* side. As on the adhidaivata side (Chā. Up. 1-6-1 to 8 [?]):

> इयमेवर्गग्निः साम तदेतदेतस्यामृच्यध्यूढं साम तस्मादृच्यध्यूढं साम गीयत इयमेव सा अग्निरमस्तत्साम ॥ १ ॥

> *iyam evarg agniḥ sāma tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyata iyam eva sāgnir amas tat sāma ‖ 1 ‖*

> अन्तरिक्षमेवर्ग्वायुः साम तदेतदेतस्यामृच्यध्यूढं साम तस्मादृच्यध्यूढं साम गीयतेऽन्तरिक्षमेव सा वायुरमस्तत्साम ॥ २ ॥

> *antarikṣam evarg vāyuḥ sāma tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate 'ntarikṣam eva sā vāyur amas tat sāma ‖ 2 ‖*

> द्यौरेवर्गादित्यः साम तदेतदेतस्यामृच्यध्यूढं साम तस्मादृच्यध्यूढं साम गीयते द्यौरेव सादित्योऽमस्तत्साम ॥ ३ ॥

> *dyaur evarg ādityaḥ sāma tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate dyaur eva sādityo 'mas tat sāma ‖ 3 ‖*

> नक्षत्राण्येवर्क्चन्द्रमाः साम तदेतदेतस्यामृच्यध्यूढं साम तस्मादृच्यध्यूढं साम गीयते नक्षत्राण्येव सा चन्द्रमा अमस्तत्साम ॥ ४ ॥

> *nakṣatrāṇy evark candramāḥ sāma tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate nakṣatrāṇy eva sā candramā amas tat sāma ‖ 4 ‖*

In this passage, earth, atmosphere, heaven and the stars are the ṛk; fire, air, the sun and the moon are the Sāman. The relation between the ṛk and the Sāman is thus the relation between the deities and their seats; the ṛk is *sā*, the deity is *ama*, and the two together are known as *sāma*. In the same manner on the *adhyātma* side (Chā. Up. 1-7-1 to 9 [?]):

> अथाध्यात्मं वागेवर्क्प्राणः साम तदेतदेतस्यामृच्यध्यूढं साम तस्मादृच्यध्यूढं साम गीयते । वागेव सा प्राणोऽमस्तत्साम ॥ १ ॥

> *athādhyātmaṃ vāg evark prāṇaḥ sāma tad etad etasyām ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma tasmād ṛcy adhyūḍhaṃ sāma gīyate | vāg eva sā prāṇo 'mas tat sāma ‖ 1 ‖*

> चक्षुरेवर्गात्मा साम … चक्षुरेव सात्माऽमस्तत्साम ॥ २ ॥

> *cakṣur evarg ātmā sāma … cakṣur eva sātmā 'mas tat sāma ‖ 2 ‖*

> श्रोत्रमेवर्ग्मनः साम … श्रोत्रमेव सा मनोऽमस्तत्साम ॥ ३ ॥

> *śrotram evarg manaḥ sāma … śrotram eva sā mano 'mas tat sāma ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 244  (PDF 264)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

Speech, eye, ear and the rest are the ṛk; breath, self (*ātman*) and mind and the rest are the Sāman: the seats and their indwellers. Speech and the others are the ṛks (*sā*); breath and the others are the *ama*; the two together make the Sāman. This is the explanation of the adhyātma side.

Thus, in speaking of the relation of the ṛk and the Sāman, the omnipresence of ṛk and Sāman is described in the *adhidaivata* form (the three worlds, earth etc., and the deities of this world, Agni etc., being in this form) and in the *adhyātma* form.

> स एष ये चैतस्मादर्वाञ्चो लोकास्तेषां चेष्टे मनुष्यकामानां चेति तद्य इमे वीणायां गायन्त्येतं ते गायन्ति तस्मात्ते धनसनयः ।

> *sa eṣa ye caitasmād arvāñco lokās teṣāṃ ceṣṭe manuṣyakāmānāṃ ceti tad ya ime vīṇāyāṃ gāyanty etaṃ te gāyanti tasmāt te dhanasanayaḥ |*

(Chā. Up. 1-7-6 [?]). Gist: he is lord of all the worlds that lie within (this) and of all human desires; those who sing this Sāman in the manner of the lute-players obtain wealth of every kind.

> अथ य एतदेवं विद्वान्साम गायत्यभ्यां स गायति सोऽमुनैव स एष यो ऽमुष्मात्पराञ्चो लोकास्ताꣳश्चाप्नोति देवकामांश्च । कं ते कामम् आगायानीत्येष ह्येव कामागानस्येष्टे य एवं विद्वान्साम गायति साम गायति ॥ [as read; the Kannada print is partly garbled]

> *atha ya etad evaṃ vidvān sāma gāyaty abhyāṃ sa gāyati so 'munaiva sa eṣa yo 'muṣmāt parāñco lokās tāṃś cāpnoti devakāmāṃś ca | kaṃ te kāmam āgāyānīty eṣa hy eva kāmāgānasyeṣṭe ya evaṃ vidvān sāma gāyati sāma gāyati ‖*

(Chā. Up. 1-7-8 and 9 [?]). Gist: from this singing all desires, common to the paths of the gods and men, are obtained; so the *udgātṛ* may ask, "By this singing, let such-and-such wish of yours be fulfilled", because the one who sings this holy Sāman is able to bring about every kind of desire, of this world and the next.

> स य एतदेवं विद्वान्सामेत्युपास्ते अभ्याशो ह यदेनं साधवो धर्मा आ च गच्छेयुरुप च नमेयुः ।

> *sa ya etad evaṃ vidvān sāmety upāste abhyāśo ha yad enaṃ sādhavo dharmā ā ca gaccheyur upa ca nameyuḥ |*

(Chā. Up. 2-1-4 [?]). One who knowing this truth reveres the Sāman as good (*sādhu*) — good duties come to him always as protectors, and for the protection of his own self they approach him and serve him. Thus the power of the Sāman is described in many ways; besides, the description of the divisions of the Sāman ("one should revere the five-fold Sāman" and so on) and its praise are manifold, and [the page continues on p. 245].

### Printed p. 245  (PDF 265)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

…the Sāman is praised in many ways as the direct means of the soul's welfare; as the description is very extensive, those words of praise cannot be cited here; they may be seen in the Chāndogya and other Upaniṣads.

Therefore, for ***nabhanyaṃ sāma yathā veḥ***, it can be understood that the most excellent hymn of praise, rising from the heart, goes swiftly like a bird and brings the deity near.

Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya on the second half of the ṛk:

> वव्यृधानं स्वर्वत् अर्चाम । वर्धमानं फलभूतेन स्वर्गेण तद्वत् शस्त्रं यथा वेः तथा पूजयामः शंसामः । स्तुतेमनु शंसेतीति न्यायात् ।

> *vavṛdhānaṃ svarvat arcāma | vardhamānaṃ phalabhūtena svargeṇa tadvat śastraṃ yathā veḥ tathā pūjayāmaḥ śaṃsāmaḥ | stutemanu śaṃsetīti nyāyāt |*

The *udgātṛ*, a priest, sings from the Sāmaveda, and, knowing that singing is that which pervades the sky and destroys Rākṣasas, we the sacrificers, following that, address Indra and, abundantly reciting the *śastra*-mantras that proclaim the qualities of Indra, the giver of heaven's fruit, worship Indra; following the maxim "one should recite (*śaṃsa*) after the praise", we offer *śaṃsana* after the *stuti*; thus one meaning is made. Another meaning is that the Sāman sung by the *udgātṛ* priest — in the second sense Sāyaṇa gives "*tadṛklakṣaṇaṃ sāma vavṛdhānaṃ sarvatra yathā bhavati tathā arcāma*" — as it grows everywhere, so we praise and worship Indra with *śastra*-mantras.

***dhenavaḥ — gāvaḥ — adabdhāḥ — dogdhryaḥ — gāvaḥ — ahiṃsitāḥ***: the Nirukta-writers have read the word *dhenu* in the Vāṅmaya list (Ni. 2-... [?]).

The words formed from the root *dabh* ("to injure, destroy") are numerous and are commonly Vedic; the word *adabdha* ("unharmed, not destroyed") is also commonly Vedic. Generally, when Agni is asked for protection, the adjective and noun appear together: *adabdhebhiḥ pāyubhiḥ*; *adabdhebhiḥ gopābhiḥ*:

> अदब्धेभिस्तव गोपाभिरिष्टेऽस्माकं पाहि त्रिषधस्थ सूरीन् ।

> *adabdhebhis tava gopābhir iṣṭe 'smākaṃ pāhi triṣadhastha sūrīn |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-2 [?]). In many ṛks this usage is found.

***dhenavaḥ*** — "*dhenur dhayate vā, dhinoti vā; dhayater asau vatsena iti; tarpayati asau payasā*" (Ni. 11-43 [?]): because milk is drawn by the calf, or because it satisfies with its milk — the cows are called *dhenu* either because milk is drawn from them by pressing, or because they cause satisfaction by giving milk.

### Printed p. 246  (PDF 266)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

> उप ह्वयेः सुदुघां धेनुमेतां सुहस्तो गोधुगुत दोहदेनाम् ।
> श्रेष्ठं सवं सविता साविषन्नोऽभीद्धो घर्मस्तदु षु प्र वोचम् ॥

> *upa hvaye sudughāṃ dhenum etāṃ suhasto godhug uta dohad enām |*
> *śreṣṭhaṃ savaṃ savitā sāviṣan no 'bhīddho gharmas tad u ṣu pra vocam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-26 [?]): the Nirukta-writers quote this ṛk and explain the word *dhenu* with the adjective *sudughām*. In this ṛk two meanings are given to *dhenu*: as explained above, "the cow that is filled with milk", and secondly: "*vṛṣṭyā prīṇayitrīṃ meghalakṣaṇāṃ dhenum*" — as an ordinary cow gratifies the sacrificer with milk, so the cloud gratifies the world with rain; hence the name *dhenu* is known for the cloud, and this *dhenu* in cloud form is milked by Āditya, the sun.

> धेनुं च पृश्निं वृषभं सुरेतसं विश्वाहा शुक्रं पयोऽस्य दुक्षत ।

> *dhenuṃ ca pṛśniṃ vṛṣabhaṃ suretasaṃ viśvāhā śukraṃ payo 'sya dukṣata |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-160-3 [?]). In such ṛks the word *dhenu* is a synonym of the earth (*pṛthivī*); since the earth satisfies the world with grain and other riches, this identity is stated.

Sāyaṇa, using this word as an adjective of the word *gāvaḥ*, gives the meaning "(cows) yielding abundant milk".

The word *gauḥ* is read by the Nirukta-writers in the Vāṅmaya list (Ni. 2-... [?]); *gaur iti pṛthivyā nāmadheyam* — "*gauḥ* is a name of the earth" — also stated among the names of the earth (Ni. 1-... [?]). In *gobhis sannaddho asi vīḷeyasva* ("bound with cow-hide [strips], be strong"), *carman* and *ślīṣman* are conveyed by the word *go*. "*Jyāpi gaur ucyate ādityo 'pi gaur ucyate suṣumṇo raśmir ekaḥ eva gauriti ucyate sarve 'pi raśmayo gāva ucyante*" (Ni. 2-... [?]): thus for the word *go* many meanings are stated — hide, phlegm, bow-string, the sun, the *suṣumnā* artery, and so forth.

Sāyaṇa explains *dhenu* as "cows" and gives the meaning that the cows which yield abundant milk, sitting on the sacred grass —

> बर्हिषि सदन्तं दिव्यं आविवासार्ह बर्हिषि सीदन्तं दिविभवं इन्द्रं त्वां आगत्य परिचरन्ति क्षीरं दुहन्ति तथा अर्चाम

> *barhiṣi sadantaṃ divyaṃ āvivāsārha barhiṣi sīdantaṃ divibhavaṃ indraṃ tvāṃ āgatya paricaranti kṣīraṃ duhanti tathā arcāma*

— just as the cows serve with their milk Indra, the dweller in heaven, who sits comfortably on the sacred grass, so we the sacrificers worship Indra. [Reading of this quotation uncertain: [?]]

***svarvat — phalabhūtena svargeṇa tadvat śastraṃ*** — "the *śastra* that is the means of heaven's fruit." The *svar* word, with a suffix, is used a hundred times in the Ṛk-saṃhitā; the word *svar* alone is also well known, but the meaning is not clearly known in every place. In some places [the page continues on p. 247].

### Printed p. 247  (PDF 267)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

…the meaning differs from place to place, and must be fixed according to context. Here, having understood the meaning of the root form of the word *svar*, the import of *svarvat* is explained. Words such as *svardṛśaḥ*, *svarvid* are to be understood only in their own contexts.

*Svaḥ*, *pṛśniḥ*, *nākaḥ* and the like — this word is read in the general lists of names. "*Sādhāraṇāny etāni ṣaḍ divaś cādityasya ca*" — "*svaḥ, pṛśniḥ, nākaḥ, gauḥ, viṣṭapam, nabhaḥ*": these six words are common terms both for the sky and for the sun, the Nirukta-writers say (Ni. 2-14 [?]). Then, as to the root of *svar* and how the word is derived, when it is used for the sun:

> स्वरादित्यो भवति सु अरणः, सु ईरणः, स्वतो रसान्, स्वतो भासं ज्योतिषाम् । स्वतो भासेति वा ।

> *svarāditya bhavati su araṇaḥ, su īraṇaḥ, svato rasān, svato bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām | svato bhāseti vā |*

(Ni. 2-14 [?]). Because he goes far, or because he draws up (the waters) completely and destroys (darkness), or because he enters into the juices and is within them, or because he spreads his own light in the circle of fire so as to be one with it, or because he is all-pervading in the form of splendour — the sun has this name; and for this reason the sky also, by "*yaten dyauvyākhyātā*" [?], has this name, the Nirukta-writers say.

> स्वरादित्यो भवति स एनानि सारयति ।

> *svarāditya bhavati sa enāni sārayati |*

(Ni. 5-4 [?]). By making the rays move, also, the sun has the name *svaḥ*. Where this word is used in the Ṛk-saṃhitā:

> प्रत्यङ् देवानां विशः प्रत्यङ्ङुदेषि मानुषान् । प्रत्यङ् विश्वं स्वर्दृशे ॥

> *pratyaṅ devānāṃ viśaḥ pratyaṅṅ udeṣi mānuṣān | pratyaṅ viśvaṃ svardṛśe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-5 [?]) — in such ṛks it means the world of heaven; and

> त्मना वहन्तो दुरो व्यृण्वन्नन्ते विश्वे स्व ᳚ निर्दृशीके ।

> *tmanā vahanto duro vy ṛṇvann ante viśve sva … nirdṛśīke |* [as read; garbled: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-68-10 [?]) — in such places *svaḥ* means "in the sky". And again

> दा नो अग्ने बृहतो दाः सहस्रिणो दुरो न वाजं श्रुत्या अपा वृधि । प्राची द्यावापृथिवी ब्रह्मणा कृधि स्वर्ण शुक्रमुषसो वि दिद्युतः ॥

> *dā no agne bṛhato dāḥ sahasriṇo duro na vājaṃ śrutyā apā vṛdhi | prācī dyāvāpṛthivī brahmaṇā kṛdhi svar ṇa śukram uṣaso vi didyutaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-2-2 [?]) — in such ṛks it is explained as "the sun". Likewise, words such as *svarvat*, formed with the suffix *vat*, are to be explained according to context. For example —

### Printed p. 248  (PDF 268)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

> यो इन्द्र भुज आभरः स्वर्वाँ असुरेभ्यः । स्तोतारमिन्मघवन्नस्य वर्धय ये च त्वे वृक्तबर्हिषः ॥

> *yo indra bhuja ābharaḥ svarvāṃ asurebhyaḥ | stotāram in maghavann asya vardhaya ye ca tve vṛktabarhiṣaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-92-1 [?]). Here *svarvān* means "possessing happiness" or "possessing heaven". Or the word *svaḥ* is a synonym for "all"; "*sarvaṃ bhūtajātaṃ ātmanā vivṛtaṃ vā*" [as read, doubtful: [?]]. The word *svaḥ* having the meanings happiness, heaven or "all", *svarvān* means one who has happiness, heaven, or everything: all these meanings fit Indra as an epithet. And again:

> तं शिशीता स्वध्वरं सत्यं सत्यानमृत्विजम् । उतो नु चिद्य ओहत आण्डा शुष्णस्य भेदत्यज्जैः स्वर्वतीरपो नभन्तामन्यके समे ॥

> *taṃ śiśītā svadhvaraṃ satyaṃ satyānam ṛtvijam | uto nu cid ya ohata āṇḍā śuṣṇasya bhedaty ajjaiḥ svarvatīr apo nabhantām anyake same ‖* [as read; partly doubtful: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-40-11 [?]). In such places *svarvatīḥ apaḥ*, as an epithet of waters, means "waters (found) in *divya*, the heavenly world (*svargaloka*)"; the epithet describes also the qualities of Agni and other deities. For example —

> ज्योतिष्मतीमदितिं धारयत्क्षितिं स्वर्वतीमा सचेते दिवेदिवे जागृवांसा दिवेदिवे ।

> *jyotiṣmatīm aditiṃ dhārayat kṣitiṃ svarvatīm ā sacete dive-dive jāgṛvāṃsā dive-dive |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-136-3 [?]). Here *svarvatī* is an epithet of Aditi; in the ṛk, as explained there, it is "bringing about heaven through the accomplishment of the sacrifice". And

> आ ते शुष्मो वृषभ एतु पश्चादोत्तरादधरादा पुरस्तात् । आ विश्वतो अभि समेत्वर्वाङिन्द्र द्युम्नं स्वर्वद्दोहस्व ॥ [?]

> *ā te śuṣmo vṛṣabha etu paścād ottarād adharād ā purastāt | ā viśvato abhi sametv arvāṅ indra dyumnaṃ svarvad dohasva ‖* [as read; partly doubtful: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-19-9 [?]). In such ṛks *svarvat* indicates "wealth possessed of happiness" (*sukhayuktaṃ dhanam*). In the present ṛk, as an epithet of *sāman*, it may be taken to mean "that which brings about heaven" or "that which brings about the happiness of heaven".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)**

***gāyat*** — root *gai śabde*; by "*chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭaḥ*" the *laṅ* is in the present sense; third person singular. Vedically it has no augment *a*.

***nabhanyam*** — *nabhasi bhavaḥ nabhanyaḥ*: in the sense "being in", the suffix *yat*; Vedically *sa* is replaced by *na*; by "*tit svaritam*" the *svarita* accent arises.

### Printed p. 249  (PDF 269)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

Grammar page, noted briefly (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā, continued; sūtra numerals are small type, marked [?]):

- ***veḥ*** — root *vid jñāne*; Vedically *laṅ* in the present sense; second person singular, *sip*, the *i* dropped (*lopa*), *luk* for *śap*; guṇa for the light vowel of the root by "*hal-jyā-bhyaḥ*…" [?]; *d* of the root to *ru* by "*dakṣa*…" [?]; the visarga Vedically takes no augment; the accent is *nighāta*.
- ***arcāma*** — root *arca pūjāyām*; *loṭ*, first person plural; because it stands after a *tiṅ*, no *nighāta* accent; the root accent remains.
- ***vavṛdhānam*** — root *vṛdhu vṛddhau*; *śānac* for *laṭ*; "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" gives *śluḥ* in place of *śap*; reduplication, with a long vowel in the reduplicative syllable of the Saṃhitā; *cit*-accent (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 [?]) — end-udātta.
- ***adabdhāḥ*** — *naña* (negative) compound; by "*tatpuruṣe*…" [?] the fore-member keeps its natural accent.
- ***divyam*** — *divi bhavam divyam*; *yat* suffix by the *daṇḍādi* group; by the suffix the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***vivāsān*** — *vivāsa* is used in the sense of "serving"; *leṭ*, third person plural, *jhi* replaced by *an*; *i* dropped by "*itaś ca lopaḥ*" [?]; the augment *āṭ* by "*leṭo 'ḍāṭau*" [?]; *yadyoga* (because there is a relative), no *nighāta*; by transposition the first syllable is *udātta*. ‖ 1 ‖

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> अर्चद्वृषा वृषभिः स्वेदुहव्यैर्मृगो नाश्नो अति यज्जुगुर्यात् ।
> प्र मन्दयुर्मनां गूर्त होता भरते मर्यो मिथुना यजत्रः ॥ २ ॥

> *arcad vṛṣā vṛṣabhiḥ svedūhavyair mṛgo nāśno ati yaj jugurvāt |*
> *pra mandayur manāṃ gūrta hotā bharate maryo mithunā yajatraḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

> अर्चत् । वृषा । वृषऽभिः । स्वऽइदुहव्यैः [?] । मृगः । न । अश्नः । अति । यत् । जुगुर्यात् ।

> *arcat | vṛṣā | vṛṣa-bhiḥ | sva-idu-havyaiḥ [?] | mṛgaḥ | na | aśnaḥ | ati | yat | jugurvāt |*
> *pra | mandayuḥ | manām | gūrte | hotā | bharate | maryaḥ | mithunā | yajatraḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (as read; doubtful passages marked [?])

> वृषा हविषां वर्षिताऽयं यजमानः स्वेदुहव्यैः स्वायत्तैर्दुग्धहविष्कैः [?] । यद्वा । स्वयंप्राप्तैर्दोहकं [?] हव्यं येषां तादृशैः । वृषभिर्वर्षकैर्हविर्भिः [?] अध्वर्य्वादिभिर्विशिष्टः सन् अर्चत् । अर्चयतीन्द्रं । यद्वा । वृषा फलस्य वर्षिताऽयमिन्द्र उक्तलक्षणैर्ऋत्विग्भिरर्च्यते । यद्यस्मादश्नो व्यापकः पानाद्यर्थं धावन् मृगो न हरिणादिरिवायमिन्द्रोऽश्नोऽशनशीलः सन् अति जुगुर्यात् । अत्यर्थमुद्युङ्क्ते हविर्भक्षणाय । यथा मृगः क्षुत्पिपासादितः शीघ्रमुद्युङ्क्ते तथायमिन्द्रोऽपि । यस्मादेवं तस्मादर्चति । यद्वा । … भक्षयेत् तथार्चतीत्यर्थः [?] । किंच हे गूर्तोदूर्णेन्द्र [?] मनां मननं स्तोत्रमिच्छतां देवानां मन्दयुः स्तुतियुक्तो मर्यो होता मानुष इतन्नामुक ऋत्विग् यजत्रो यागनिष्पादकः सन् मिथुना मिथुनानि युग्मरूपाणि याज्यापुरोनुवाक्यादीनि मिथुनौ वा जायापतिरूपः सन् प्र भरते । प्रकर्षेण संपादयति । तस्मादर्चतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *vṛṣā haviṣāṃ varṣitā 'yaṃ yajamānaḥ svedūhavyaiḥ svāyattair dugdhahaviṣkaiḥ [?] | yadvā | svayaṃprāptair dohakaṃ [?] havyaṃ yeṣāṃ tādṛśaiḥ | vṛṣabhir varṣakair havirbhiḥ [?] adhvaryvādibhir viśiṣṭaḥ san arcat | arcayatīndraṃ | yadvā | vṛṣā phalasya varṣitā 'yam indra uktalakṣaṇair ṛtvigbhir arcyate | yad yasmād aśno vyāpakaḥ pānādyarthaṃ dhāvan mṛgo na hariṇādir ivāyam indro 'śno 'śanaśīlaḥ san ati jugurvāt | atyarthaṃ udyuṅkte havirbhakṣaṇāya | yathā mṛgaḥ kṣutpipāsāditaḥ śīghram udyuṅkte tathāyam indro 'pi | yasmād evaṃ tasmād arcati | yadvā | … bhakṣayet tathārcatīty arthaḥ [?] | kiṃca he gūrtodūrṇendra [?] manāṃ mananaṃ stotram icchatāṃ devānāṃ mandayuḥ stutiyukto maryo hotā mānuṣa itannāmuka ṛtvig yajatro yāganiṣpādakaḥ san mithunā mithunāni yugmarūpāṇi yājyāpurononuvākyādīni mithunau vā jāyāpatirūpaḥ san pra bharate | prakarṣeṇa saṃpādayati | tasmād arcatīty arthaḥ ‖*

*Gist:* the sacrificer, showerer of oblations, worships Indra with the Adhvaryu and the other priests and their oblations; as a hungry deer runs to drink, so Indra, being hungry, hastens to the oblations; therefore the priest, as a pair, offers *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

*yat* — because; *aśnaḥ* — the pervasive (one who runs for drinking etc.); *mṛgaḥ na* — like a deer; (*aśnaḥ* — hungry); *ati jugurvāt* — strives greatly (for eating the oblation); *tat* — therefore; [or *aśnaḥ* — he who runs for drink etc.; *mṛgaḥ na* — like a deer; *yat ati jugurvāt* — (Indra) who exerts himself quickly]; *vṛṣā* — the sacrificer, the rainer of oblations; *svedu-havyaiḥ* — with the self-prepared oblations; *vṛṣabhiḥ* — with the Adhvaryu and the other givers of oblations; *arcat* — worships (Indra); [or *vṛṣā* — Indra, the rainer of desires; *svedu-havyaiḥ* — by those of well-prepared oblations; *vṛṣabhiḥ* — by the Adhvaryu etc., the givers of oblations; *arcat* — is worshipped]; (*kiñca* — further) (*he*) *gūrte* — O Indra, the valiant in effort; *manām* — of the gods fond of praise; *mandayuḥ* — the one intent on praising; *maryaḥ* — [continues on p. 251].
