### Printed p. 251  (PDF 271)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued)* *hotā* — the mortal invoking-priest; *yajatraḥ* — as the accomplisher of the sacrifice; *mithunā* — the pairs, i.e. *yājyā*, *puronuvākyā* and the like (or, as husband and wife); *pra bharate* — abundantly brings about.

**Bhāvārtha**

O valiant Indra, the sacrificer, the giver of oblations, assisted by the Adhvaryu and the other priests, worships you; to receive those oblations, you hasten swiftly, like a deer tormented by hunger and thirst running to drink water. The mortal *hotṛ*, loving the praise of the gods, praises them and recites the *yājyā*, *puronuvākyā* and other verses.

**Printed English**

The showerer (of the oblation, the offerer of the sacrifice, assisted) by (the priests), presenting the oblations which have been provided by himself, adores (Indra), in order that he may hasten (to the rite), as a (thirsty) deer to the water. The mortal invoker (of the gods), O mighty Indra, whilst glorifying them who are desirous of praise, presents a twofold offering (to you).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***vṛṣā svedūhavyaiḥ vṛṣabhir arcat*** — *haviṣāṃ varṣitā ayaṃ yajamānaḥ | svāyattair dugdhahaviṣkaiḥ [?] | yadvā svayaṃ prāptaidhakaṃ havyaṃ yeṣāṃ tādṛśaiḥ haviṣkṛdbhir adhvaryvādibhiḥ viśiṣṭaḥ san arcayatīndram |* Sāyaṇa has given two meanings to this sentence. The word *vṛṣā* is used in the sense of the sacrificer who offers oblations. The word *svedūhavyaiḥ* is an epithet of the fires, and also an epithet of the priests Adhvaryu and the rest. By this, the first meaning is given: the sacrificer, offering oblations to the gods, kindled by fuel (sticks) and oblations — worships Indra with the fire (of fires). In the second meaning: the sacrificer, together with the Adhvaryu and other priests who are ready to offer the oblations they have in abundance, worships Indra with many oblations. *Yadvā vṛṣā phalasya varṣitā indra uktalakṣaṇair ṛtvigbhir arcyate*: or, Indra, who like rain pours out the desired fruits for the sacrificers, is worshipped by the priests, the Adhvaryu and the others, who have prepared abundant oblations.

### Printed p. 252  (PDF 272)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

Here the two words *vṛṣā* and *vṛṣabhiḥ* are both derived from the root *vṛṣ*. The commentator, in this context, says that the first word *vṛṣā* comes from the root *vṛṣ* (with the meaning "to sprinkle, to shower": *vṛṣu secane*; *vṛṣa śaktibandhane*), which gives the sense of raining, pouring; and the second word *vṛṣabhiḥ* from the root which gives the meaning of strength and capacity — as will be understood from the explanation proper to this context. But the adjective *vṛṣan* and the other adjectives derived from this root are used again and again in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, and so these words cannot be said to carry one fixed meaning; according to the various contexts the meaning has to be given. Therefore, having first briefly noted in which meanings the word *vṛṣan* is chiefly used, let us then examine what its special sense is when used as an epithet in the present ṛk, whether of Indra or of the priests or of the other deities.

The word *vṛṣan* is used in many places in the sense *pumān* ("male"), "one with the power to sprinkle"; the word is used as an indication of *pumān* — as a synonym for "man", or for other living beings such as the horse.

> यो ते इन्द्र दधुषो वर्धयन्ति महि क्षत्रं स्थविरं वृष्ण्यं च ।

> *yo te indra dadhuṣo vardhayanti mahi kṣatraṃ sthaviraṃ vṛṣṇyaṃ ca |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-8 [?]) — here *vṛṣṇyam* means *vṛṣatvam*, "manhood" (*puṃstvam*); and

> स्तुतश्च श्रवस्यन्नवसोप मुद्रिग्यक्त्वा हरी वृषणा योह्यर्वाङ् ।

> *stutaś ca śravasyan nava sopa mudrigyaktvā harī vṛṣaṇā yohy arvāṅ |* [as read; doubtful: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-177-1 [?]) — here *vṛṣaṇā* means "youthful"; and

> भूषन्न योधि बभ्रूषु नम्नते वृषेव पत्नीरभ्येति रोरुवत् ।

> *bhūṣan na yodhi babhrūṣu namnate vṛṣeva patnīr abhy eti roruvat |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-140-6 [?]) — here *vṛṣā iva* means "like a bull (ox) that sprinkles (*sektā*)"; and

> मिनाति श्रियं जरिमा तनूनामपू नु पत्नीर्वृषणो जगम्युः ।

> *mināti śriyaṃ jarimā tanūnām apū nu patnīr vṛṣaṇo jagamyuḥ |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-179-1 [?]) — in such ṛks *vṛṣaṇaḥ* means *sektāraḥ puruṣāḥ*, "men who sprinkle (seed)"; and in many other places, similarly, the word is used in meanings that indicate masculine gender and show the power of the male creature. And further —

---

### Printed p. 253  (PDF 273)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

> वृषा वां मेघो वृषणा पीपाय गोर्न सेके मनुषो दशस्यन् ।

> *vṛṣā vāṃ megho vṛṣaṇā pīpāya gor na seke manuṣo daśasyan |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-8 [?]);

> दस्मो हि ष्मा वृषणं पिन्वसि त्वचं कं चिद्यावीररुं शूर मर्त्यं परिवृणक्षि मर्त्यम् ।

> *dasmo hi ṣmā vṛṣaṇaṃ pinvasi tvacaṃ kaṃ cid yāvīrarum śūra martyaṃ parivṛṇakṣi martyam |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-33-3 [?]);

> ता तू ते सत्या तुविनृम्ण विश्वा प्र धेनवः सिस्रते वृष्ण ऊध्नः ।

> *tā tū te satyā tuvinṛmṇa viśvā pra dhenavaḥ sisrate vṛṣṇa ūdhnaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-22-6 [?]).

In such places *vṛṣan* is used in the sense of "sprinkler": *varṣakaḥ*, *varṣaṇaparamanaskaḥ* — one who pours down water, one who pours out desired objects. Besides this, other meanings also appear, but in many places the chief sense of the word *vṛṣṇya* is, again and again, extraordinary power, valour (*vīrya*):

> आ प्यायस्व समेतु ते विश्वतः सोम वृष्ण्यम् ।

> *ā pyāyasva sametu te viśvataḥ soma vṛṣṇyam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-16 [?]);

> महाँ असि महिष वृष्ण्येभिर्धनस्पृदुग्र सहमानो अन्यान् ।

> *mahāṃ asi mahiṣa vṛṣṇyebhir dhanaspṛd ugra sahamāno anyān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-46-2 [?]);

> वि चर्मणीव धिषणे अवर्तयद्वैश्वानरो विश्वमधत्त वृष्ण्यम् ।

> *vi carmaṇīva dhiṣaṇe avartayad vaiśvānaro viśvam adhatta vṛṣṇyam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-3 [?]).

In many such ṛks the word *vṛṣṇya* generally means strength and prowess. Moreover, as *vṛṣan* is used in many contexts as a synonym of Indra and other deities, in such places one must infer according to the context which deity is meant. For example —

> अपोषा अनसः सरत्संपिष्टादह बिभ्युषी । नि यत्सीं शिश्नथद्वृषा ।

> *apoṣā anasaḥ saratsampiṣṭād aha bibhyuṣī | ni yat sīṃ śiśnathad vṛṣā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-10 [?]) — here it can be conjectured that it is a synonym of Indra. But in many places it causes doubt as to which deity is meant. Sometimes even Sāyaṇācārya himself, as in the present ṛk, shows doubt, and his explanation of this adjective is not so conclusive.

> वृषा छन्दुर्भवति हर्यतो वृषा क्षेमेण धेनां मघवा यदिन्वति ।

> *vṛṣā chandur bhavati haryato vṛṣā kṣemeṇa dhenāṃ maghavā yad invati |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-55-4 [?])

### Printed p. 254  (PDF 274)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

— and just as the meaning has been given in that ṛk, in the ṛk in hand, for the word *vṛṣā* he first says "*vṛṣā haviṣāṃ varṣayitā yajamānaḥ*" and then "*yadvā vṛṣā indraḥ*", leaving room for doubt. Since it is used in so many senses, the meaning that fits the idea in each context has to be taken. In describing this pregnant word, the English commentator Max Müller has written as follows of the depth of the ideas expressed by this word:

> In *vṛṣan* we have one of those words which it is almost impossible to translate accurately. It occurs over and over again in the Vedic hymns and if we once know the various ideas which it either expresses or implies we have little difficulty in understanding its import in a vague and general way, though we look in vain for corresponding terms in any modern language and we shall see how difficult it would be to translate such terms without losing either the key-note that was still sounding, or the harmonies which were set vibrating by it in the minds of the poets and their listeners. [S.B.E. vol. XXXII, p. 138-139]

In the ṛk at hand the word may be taken to denote either the priests of the oblations, or those possessed of valour, or those who shower desired objects — Indra and the others.

***aśnaḥ mṛgo na atijuguryāt — vyāpakaḥ pānādyarthaṃ dhāvan hariṇādir iva ayam indraḥ aśanaśīlaś ca atyarthaṃ udyuṅkte havirbhakṣaṇāya*** — "*aśnaḥ*" is the word among the names read in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-... [?]). Here *vyāpakaḥ* ("pervading") is said to refer to the deer, and *aśanaśīlaḥ* ("given to eating") to Indra; the word *na* is used with two kinds of connection; so *mṛga iva indraḥ*: Indra, like a deer hastening for drink and the like (to drink water), swiftly comes and is ready to accept our oblations — thus one kind of meaning is given, with the comparison to a deer.

***mṛgaḥ*** — "*mṛgo mārṣṭer gatikarmaṇaḥ*" (Ni. 1-20 [?]): from the root *mṛj*, which means going, the word is formed; "*nityaṃ hy asau gacchati*": it gives the sense that it is always moving; or "*anveṣaṇaśīlo vā*" — one who is always seeking his food; this is the sense.

***yathā kṣutpipāsāditaḥ mṛgaḥ śīghram udyuṅkte tathāyam indro 'pi*** — just as a deer, suffering the pains of hunger and thirst, runs swiftly for its food and drink, so Indra comes swiftly to accept the oblations: this is how the second meaning is explained.

---

### Printed p. 255  (PDF 275)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

***yadvā ayam indraḥ aśno mṛga iva atijuguryāt bhakṣayet tathā arcatīti*** — "Or this Indra, like a deer hungry and fatigued by thirst, devours (the oblation) and so is worshipped": the meaning is that, as a deer with great hunger and thirst seeks to satisfy its hunger and gains satisfaction, so the sacrificer, after satisfying Indra's hunger, worships him as one who has reached satisfaction.

***jugurvāt — jugurvāt, jugurviḥ, jugurvaṇiḥ*** and the like: all these words are to be known as formed from the root *jvar* (*jyā* [?]). The Nirukta-writers include the word *jarate* among the names of *arcati* ("praising") and *karman* (Ni. 3-... [?]). With the prefix *abhi* it is more commonly used. For example —

> अभी नो अग्न उक्थमिज्जुगुर्या द्यावाक्षामा सिन्धवश्च स्वगूर्ताः ।

> *abhī no agna ukthām ij jugurvā dyāvākṣāmā sindhavaś ca svagūrtāḥ |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-140-13 [?]) — *abhimukhyena stuhi* means "praise specially", i.e. "give the assent of acceptance". And

> प्र स्तोषदुप गासिषच्छ्रवत्साम गीयमानं । अभि राधसा जुगुर्त् ।

> *pra stoṣad upa gāsiṣac chravat sāma gīyamānaṃ | abhi rādhasā jugurat |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-81-5 [?]). In such ṛks *abhigṛṇāti* means "accepts"; thus, in the activity of worship and in the activity of accepting, this word is used to show a special kind of respect; in the present ṛk also it is used in the sense of respectful acceptance.

***manāṃ mandayuḥ maryaḥ hotā yajatraḥ*** — O Indra, the mortal priest called *hotṛ*, who sings the praise of the gods who wish to hear praise, being the one who accomplishes the sacrifice, [this is one sense of the sentence]; and this *hotṛ* also brings together the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* mantras: so one meaning is stated. In the second meaning this *hotṛ* priest, acting in the manner of husband and wife (*patipatnī*-form) and performing the sacrifice again and again, worships Indra: thus the sacrificer worships Indra — this is the meaning given.

***gūrte*** — the word *gūrta* here means "strongly active"; also "praised", "worthy of praise".

> तं वः सखायो मदाय पुनानमभि गायत । शिशुं न यज्ञैः स्वदयन्त गूर्तिभिः ॥

> *taṃ vaḥ sakhāyo madāya punānam abhi gāyata | śiśuṃ na yajñaiḥ svadayanta gūrtibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-103-1 [?]) — here *gūrtibhiḥ* means "by praises, by hymns"; and

> तं गूर्तयो नेमन्निषः परीणसः समुद्रं न संचरणे सनिष्यवः । पतिं दक्षस्य विदथस्य नू सहो गिरिं न वेना अधि रोह तेजसा ॥

> *taṃ gūrtayo nemanniṣaḥ parīṇasaḥ samudraṃ na saṃcaraṇe saniṣyavaḥ | patiṃ dakṣasya vidathasya nū saho giriṃ na venā adhi roha tejasā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-56-2 [?]).

### Printed p. 256  (PDF 276)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

In such places *gūrta* also means "praisers" (*stotāraḥ*). In the present ṛk it means "the praiseworthy prowess of Indra".

***maryaḥ — martyo manuṣyo maraṇadharmā*** — because he is subject to death (*maraṇadharma*, i.e. mortal) the man is called *marya* (Ni. 3-... [?]).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***arcat*** — root *arca pūjāyām*; Vedic *laṅ*.
- ***svedūhavyaiḥ*** — *svayam it prāptaṃ havyaṃ yeṣāṃ te*; *svedūhavyāḥ* — *taiḥ*; by "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*" the fore-member keeps its own accent.
- ***jugurvāt*** — root *gṝ śabde*; in *liṅ*, "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" gives *śluḥ* for the *vikaraṇa*; by the same rule the root takes *ut* and *r* becomes *ra*; reduplication of the root, owing to *śluḥ*; the *ku*-class changes to *cu* by "*kuhoś cuḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-4-62 [?]); because of the relative (*yadyoga*), no *nighāta* accent; since *yāsuṭ* is *udātta*, end-udātta results.
- ***mandayuḥ*** — "he wishes himself (*ātmanaḥ*) to be *mandana*": *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 [?]) gives *kyac*; "*kyāc chandasi*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-170 [?]) gives the suffix *u*; "*ato lopaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 [?]) drops the *a* of *kyac*; the suffix accent remains.
- ***manām*** — root *mana jñāne*; suffix *kvip* in the agent sense; genitive plural form; by "*sānvekāc chṛtīyādiḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 [?]) the case-ending is *udātta*.
- ***bharate*** — root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*; *laṭ*, third person singular; being in the *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; the *sārvadhātuka* *la*, *śap* being *anudātta*, the root accent remains.
- ***maryaḥ*** — root *mṛṅ prāṇatyāge*, used in the causal-implicit sense (*antarbhāvitaṇyartha*); "*chandasi niṣṭarkya-*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-123 [?]) makes the suffix *yat* by *nipātana*; by "*bahulagrahaṇa*" it appears in the agent sense; by "*yato nāvaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-213 [?]) the first syllable is *udātta*.
- ***mithunā*** — root *mitha* (*saurā*); suffix *unan* by "*kṣudhipiśi*—" (Uṇ. Sū. 3-... [?]), which is *kit*; therefore the light-vowel guṇa does not occur; in the neuter, "*śeś chandasi bahulam*" gives loss of *śi*.
- ***yajatraḥ*** — root *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; suffix *atran* by "*amīnakṣi yajivadhi*—" (Uṇ. Sū. 3-... [?]); being *nit*, the first syllable is *udātta*. ‖ 2 ‖

**Sūkta 173, Ṛk 3**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> नक्षद्धोता परि सद्म मिता यन्भरद्गर्भमा शरदः पृथिव्याः ।
> क्रन्ददश्वो नयमानो रुवद्गौरन्तर्दूतो न रोदसी चरद्वाक् ॥ ३ ॥

> *nakṣad dhotā pari sadma mitā yan bharad garbham ā śaradaḥ pṛthivyāḥ |*
> *krandad aśvo nayamāno ruvad gaur antar dūto na rodasī carad vāk ‖ 3 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> नक्षत् । होता । परि । सद्म । मिता । यन् । भरत् । गर्भम् । आ । शरदः । पृथिव्याः ।
> क्रन्दत् । अश्वः । नयमानः । रुवत् । गौः । अन्तः । दूतः । न । रोदसी इति । चरत् । वाक् ॥ ३ ॥

> *nakṣat | hotā | pari | sadma | mitā | yan | bharat | garbham | ā | śaradaḥ | pṛthivyāḥ |*
> *krandat | aśvaḥ | nayamānaḥ | ruvat | gauḥ | antaḥ | dūtaḥ | na | rodasī iti | carat | vāk ‖ 3 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> होता होमनिष्पादकोऽयमग्निः मिता परिमिता सद्म सदनानि गार्हपत्यादिस्थानानि परि यन् परितो गच्छन् नक्षत् । व्याप्नोति । व्याप्य च शरदः संवत्सरसंबन्धिनं पृथिव्या भूमव्याश्च संबन्धिनं गर्भं गर्भस्थानीयमन्नं हविर्लक्षणमा भरत् । आहरति । स्वीकरोति । संभरति वा । संवत्सरपर्यन्तं वर्धितं भूम्या मुत्पन्नमित्यर्थः । यद्वा । संवत्सरसंबन्धिनं वसन्तादिकाले ज्योतिष्टोमादिषु दीयमानं पार्थिवं हविर्भरत् । वसन्ते वसन्ते ज्योतिषा यजेतेति श्रुतेः । तथा कृत्वा क्रन्दत् अश्वः । लुप्तोपमम् एतत् । अश्व इव क्रन्दति हर्षातिशयात् । किं कुर्वन् । नयमानो नयदिन्द्रायु हविर्भारं । किंच गौर्गन्तोद्वृत्तो वृष इव रुवत् । रौति । शब्दायते । किं कुर्वन् । दूतो न वार्ताहरो दूत इव रोदसी रोदस्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योरन्तर्मध्ये रोदस्योरन्तरावाक् स्तूयमानः स्तुवन् वा देवांश्चरत् । चरति । गच्छति । हविःस्वीकाराय पृथिवीं तत्प्राणाय द्युलोकं च परिभ्रमतीत्यर्थः ॥ वक्तेः कर्तरि कर्मणि वा क्विब्बचेत्यादिना क्विब्दीर्घः संप्रसारणाभावश्च ॥ [as read; doubtful in places: [?]]

> *hotā homaniṣpādako 'yam agniḥ mitā parimitā sadma sadanāni gārhapatyādisthānāni pari yan parito gacchan nakṣat | vyāpnoti | vyāpya ca śaradaḥ saṃvatsarasaṃbandhinaṃ pṛthivyā bhūmavyāś ca saṃbandhinaṃ garbhaṃ garbhasthānīyam annaṃ havirlakṣaṇam ā bharat | āharati | svīkaroti | saṃbharati vā | saṃvatsaraparyantaṃ vardhitaṃ bhūmyā mutpannam ity arthaḥ | yadvā | saṃvatsarasaṃbandhinaṃ vasantādikāle jyotiṣṭomādiṣu dīyamānaṃ pārthivaṃ havir bharat | vasante vasante jyotiṣā yajeteti śruteḥ | tathā kṛtvā krandat aśvaḥ | luptopamam etat | aśva iva krandati harṣātiśayāt | kiṃ kurvan | nayamāno nayad indrāyu havirbhāraṃ | kiṃca gaur gantodvṛtto vṛṣa iva ruvat | rauti | śabdāyate | kiṃ kurvan | dūto na vārtāharo dūta iva rodasī rodasyor dyāvāpṛthivyor antar madhye rodasyor antarāvāk stūyamānaḥ stuvan vā devāṃś carat | carati | gacchati | haviḥsvīkārāya pṛthivīṃ tatprāṇāya dyulokaṃ ca paribhramatīty arthaḥ ‖ vakteḥ kartari karmaṇi vā kvib bacetyādinā kvib dīrghaḥ saṃprasāraṇābhāvaś ca ‖* [?]

*Gist:* Agni, the *hotṛ*, going round the measured stations (Gārhapatya etc.), accepts the oblation, the "embryo" of the year and of the earth; he neighs like a horse, bellows like a bull, and goes as a messenger between heaven and earth.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

*hotā* — Agni, the accomplisher of offering into the fire; *mitā* — the measured; *sadma* — the Gārhapatya and other stations; *pari yan* — moving about on all sides; *nakṣat* — pervades (then); *śaradaḥ* — pertaining to the year (up to the year's end); *pṛthivyāḥ* — pertaining to the earth (that arose on the earth); *garbham* — the oblation that is like the earth's embryo; *ā bharat* —

### Printed p. 258  (PDF 278)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

accepts (brings about); [or *śaradaḥ* — belonging to the year, offered in the Jyotiṣṭoma and other sacrifices performed in the spring and other seasons; *pṛthivyāḥ garbham* — the oblation arisen as the embryo of the earth; *ā bharat* — accepts] (receives); *nayamānaḥ* — (carrying oblations to Indra and the others); *aśvaḥ krandat* — neighs (with joy) like a horse (and); *dūtaḥ na* — like a messenger who brings news; *rodasī antaḥ* — between heaven and earth; *vāk* — being praised (praising the gods); *carat* — moving about; *gauḥ* — like a bull; *ruvat* — makes a noise.

**Bhāvārtha**

Agni, the accomplisher of the *homa*, pervades the Gārhapatya and other measured stations, and accepts the oblation, in the form of food, which is the earth's embryo, offered in the Jyotiṣṭoma and the others; then, carrying it to Indra and the others, he neighs with joy like a horse, and, as a messenger who brings news to the gods, moving between heaven and earth, he bellows like a bull.

**Printed English**

The invoker (of the gods, Agni), pervades the measured stations (of the altars), and accepts that (oblation), which is the germ of the year and of the earth; as a horse neighs when bringing (the offering to Indra), as a bull bellows like a messenger proclaiming (his message) between heaven and earth.

*(The printed English reads "between and earth" at the line-break — "between heaven and earth" is meant; as printed: "between and earth" [sic].)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***hotā — homaniṣpādako 'yam agniḥ*** — Although the word *hotṛ* generally designates the priest who invites the deities to receive the oblations, here it is explained to mean Agni, who invites the deities to come and receive the oblations offered by the sacrificers, offers them, and performs the sacrifice. This meaning is chiefly used with respect to Agni.

Besides, *homaniṣpādakam āhvātāraṃ vā*: the one who accomplishes the *homa* by offering oblations, or the one who calls the deities: thus two kinds of action belong to the *hotṛ*; so the meanings of the word *hotṛ* have been stated. This very intention is explained in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa in the form of a discussion (*carcā*); it shows the position of the *hotṛ* in the sacrifice [the passage continues on p. 259].

### Printed p. 259  (PDF 279)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

> यज्ञो वै देवेभ्य उदक्रामत्तमिष्टिभिः प्रैषयैश्चैन्य [?] दिष्टिभिः प्रैषयैश्चैन्द्रस्तदिष्टीनामिष्टित्वं तमन्वविन्दन् । अनुवित्तयज्ञो राध्नोति य एवं वेद । आहूतयो वै नामैता यदाहुतयु [?] एताभिर्वै देवान्यजमानो ह्वयति तदाहुतीनामाहूतित्वं । ऊतयः खलु वै ता नामु [?] याभिर्देवा यजमानस्य हवमायंति यो वै पंथानो याः स्रोतयस्ता वा ऊतयस्त उ एवैतत्स्वर्गयाणा यजमानस्य भवंति ॥

> *yajño vai devebhya udakrāmat tam iṣṭibhiḥ praiṣayaiś caint ya [?] diṣṭibhiḥ praiṣayaiś caindras tad iṣṭīnām iṣṭitvaṃ tam anvavindan | anuvittayajño rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda | āhūtayo vai nāmaitā yad āhutayu [?] etābhir vai devān yajamāno hvayati tad āhutīnām āhūtitvaṃ | ūtayaḥ khalu vai tā nāmu [?] yābhir devā yajamānasya havam āyanti yo vai panthāno yāḥ srotayas tā vā ūtayas ta u evaitat svargayāṇā yajamānasya bhavanti ‖* [as read, garbled in places]

(Ai. Brā. 1-2 [?]). Once the sacrifice went away from the gods; then, by offering oblations (*āhuti*), they got it back again. *Āhuti* is the invitation (*āhvāna*) of the deity by pronouncing its name, i.e. an act of "calling". If one is then asked why one who offers the oblations is called *hotṛ* —

> तदाहुर्यदन्यो जुहोत्यथ योऽसु चाह यजति च कस्मात्तं होतेत्याचक्षत इति । यद्वाव स तत्र यथाभाजसं देवता आमुमावहामुमावहेत्यावाहयति तदेव होतुर्होतृत्वं होता भवति । होतेत्येनमाचक्षते य एवं वेद ॥

> *tad āhur yad anyo juhoty atha yo 'su cāha yajati ca kasmāt taṃ hotety ācakṣata iti | yad vāva sa tatra yathābhājasaṃ devatā āmum āvahāmum āvahety āvāhayati tad eva hotur hotṛtvaṃ hotā bhavati | hotety enam ācakṣate ya evaṃ veda ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ai. Brā. 1-2 [?]). The one who offers the oblation is one person, and the one who recites the mantra is another; to the question how the name *hotṛ* is justified, the answer is that the one who recites the mantra invites the deities, in proportion to the offering made, "Bring this one, bring that one", and so calls them; hence he too is called *hotṛ* (Ai. Brā. [as above]). Then,

> मनो वै यज्ञस्य वैत्रावरुणो वाग्यज्ञस्य होता ।

> *mano vai yajñasya vaitrāvaruṇo vāg yajñasya hotā |*

(Ai. Brā. 6-5 [?]) — by this sentence the identity of the *hotṛ* with the speech that recites the mantra is stated. And again —

> सीद होतः स्व उ लोके चिकित्वानित्यग्निर्वै देवानां होता तस्यैष स्वो लोको यदुत्तरवेदीनाभिः … नि होता होतृषदने विदान इत्यग्निर्वै देवानां होता तस्यैतद्धोतृषदनं यदुत्तरवेदीनाभिः ॥

> *sīda hotaḥ sva u loke cikitvān ity agnir vai devānāṃ hotā tasyaiṣa svo loko yad uttaravedīnābhiḥ … ni hotā hotṛṣadane vidāna ity agnir vai devānāṃ hotā tasyaitad dhotṛṣadanaṃ yad uttaravedīnābhiḥ ‖* [as read; part omitted in the print with dots]

(Ai. Brā. 3-2 [?]). In such sentences Agni, the accomplisher of the *homa*, is addressed as the *hotṛ* of the gods. So in the present ṛk the word *hotāram* can be taken to mean "the accomplisher of the *homa*", or "the invoker". By words such as *krandad aśvaḥ* the *hotṛ*-hood of Agni is described.

### Printed p. 260  (PDF 280)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

***nakṣat — vyāpnoti*** — *aṃśati, nakṣati, āksāṇaḥ* and so on are read among the ten names of the action of pervading (Ni. 2-... [?]); so *abhinakṣati* is "pervades on all sides, praises everywhere": the meaning is "to praise"; for example —

> प्र पर्वता अनवन्त प्र गावः प्र ब्रह्माणो अभिनक्षन्त इन्द्रम् ।
> सरस्वतीं याम् पितरो हवन्ते दक्षिणा यज्ञमभिनक्षमाणाः ॥

> *pra parvatā anavanta pra gāvaḥ pra brahmāṇo abhinakṣanta indram |*
> *sarasvatīṃ yām pitaro havante dakṣiṇā yajñam abhinakṣamāṇāḥ ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-… [?]; 10-17-8 [?]). In such ṛks *abhinakṣantaḥ*, *abhinakṣamāṇāḥ* mean "standing, praising on all sides". Here the sacrificial fire stands pervading the Gārhapatya and other stations of the sacrifice.

***mitā sadma pariyan nakṣat*** — the word *sadma* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-... [?]), of battle (Ni. 2-... [?]), of house (Ni. 3-... [?]), and, in "*sadmanī*", among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-... [?]). Here it is used in the sense of a house, a dwelling-place. The meaning described here is that Agni, in accordance with his own name "Gārhapatya", fitted to his dwelling, which is prescribed in the Śāstra, pervades fully his own measured dwelling-place.

***śaradaḥ pṛthivyāḥ garbham ā bharat*** — "he accepts or brings together the oblation, in the nature of food standing as the embryo, pertaining to the year and to the earth." The word *śarad* means the autumn season: "*śaracchṛtā asyām oṣadhayo bhavanti*" — "the season when the plants (of the herbs, the roots and the like) dry up": thus it is said; or "*śīrṇā āpo*" — the season in which the waters dry up (Ni. 4-... [?]). Agni accepts, or causes to arise, the food in the form of oblation that is produced on the earth until the end of the year and is dried up in the autumn season: this is the meaning given.

In the second sense: "*vasante vasante jyotiṣā yajeta*" — by this *śruti* the one who in spring practises the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice in order to perform the Jyotiṣṭoma and other such sacrifices; in these seasons, prescribed in the Śāstra beginning with spring, which come round until the year is complete, he accepts the oblation, endowed with the beauty arisen on earth: so this meaning is given.

The same is shown in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, pointing out the relation of Agni, spring and the oblation:

> तद्यदेतेऽत्रोपदधाति संवत्सर एषोऽग्निरिमे उ लोकाः संवत्सरस्तस्यायमेव लोकः प्रथमा चितिरयमस्य लोको वसन्त ऋतुस्तस्यादेतेऽत्रोपदधाति यदेवास्यैते आत्मनस्तदस्मिन्नेतत्प्रतिदधाति तस्मादेतेऽत्रोपदधाति ॥

> *tad yad ete 'tropadadhāti saṃvatsara eṣo 'gnir ime u lokāḥ saṃvatsaras tasyāyam eva lokaḥ prathamā citir ayam asya loko vasanta ṛtus tasyād ete 'tropadadhāti yad evāsyaite ātmanas tad asmin etat pratidadhāti tasmād ete 'tropadadhāti ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Śa. Brā. 8-4-3-10 [?]).

### Printed p. 261  (PDF 281)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

In these sentences the identity of Agni and the year is first stated, and then the identity of the first layer (*prathamā citi*) and spring is shown. And again —

> यद्येवैतेऽत्रोपदधाति । प्रजापतिरेषोऽग्निः संवत्सर उ प्रजापतिस्तस्य प्रतिष्ठैव प्रथमा चितिः प्रतिष्ठोऽस्य वसन्त ऋतुस्तद्यदेतेऽत्रोपदधाति … तेऽन्तर्हिते विश्वज्योतिष उपदधाति प्रजा वै विश्वज्योतिः … ऋतुभिर्हीवं गर्भे सन्तं संपश्यन्त्यृतुभिर्जातम् ॥ [as read, dots in the print]

> *yady evaitte 'tropadadhāti | prajāpatir eṣo 'gniḥ saṃvatsara u prajāpatis tasya pratiṣṭhaiva prathamā citiḥ pratiṣṭho 'sya vasanta ṛtus tad yad ete 'tropadadhāti … te 'ntarhite viśvajyotiṣa upadadhāti prajā vai viśvajyotiḥ … ṛtubhir hīvaṃ garbhe santaṃ saṃpaśyanty ṛtubhir jātam ‖* [?]

(Śa. Brā. 8-4-3-10 [?]). By such sentences, showing the identity of earth and year, and of the year and the others, it is explained that the food, the oblation, produced in the year's womb arose as if in the womb of the earth.

***krandad aśvaḥ — aśva iva krandati harṣātiśayāt*** — In this sentence the word *iva*, which denotes comparison, is not used, but it is explained that Agni, accepting the oblations, makes a sound like a horse that is delighted: he makes a sounding noise.

***nayamānaḥ gauḥ ruvat — nayann indrāyu havirbhāram*** — it is explained that Agni leads the loads of oblations in heaps for Indra. For the word *gauḥ* the meaning is given as "an ox" (one that carries a burden); Agni is compared to a well-fed ox that carries a load and makes a sound.

***dūto na rodasī antaḥ vāk carat*** — "Agni, like a messenger who carries the present to each, moving between heaven and earth, being himself praised by the priests (or, going himself in praise of the deities)", with the explanation "*haviḥsvīkārāya pṛthivīṃ tatprāpaṇāya dyulokaṃ ca paribhramati*": Agni comes to the earth to accept the oblations, and goes to heaven to bring the accepted oblations to the deities. The order of this movement of Agni is described. In this movement of Agni the comparison with the messenger who bears news is made clear.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***nakṣat*** — root *nakṣ vyāptau*; Vedic *laṅ* in the present sense; third person singular; no augment; because in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; the *sārvadhātuka* *la* being *anudātta*, the root accent remains.
- ***sadma*** — root *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; the suffix *manin* (by *ṭoṇādi*, i.e. the *uṇādi* list); being *nit*, the first syllable is *udātta*.

### Printed p. 262  (PDF 282)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

- ***yan*** — root *iṇ gatau*; *laṭ* with *śatṛ*; *iṇo yaṇ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-81 [?]) gives *yaṇ*; the suffix accent is *udātta* on the first syllable.
- ***bharat*** — root *hṛñ haraṇe* [as printed]; Vedic *laṅ* in the present sense; third person singular; no augment; by "*hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi*" the *ha* becomes *bha*; in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; *śap* being *pit*, the root accent remains.
- ***krandat*** — root *kradi āhvāne rodane ca*; *laṭ* with *śatṛ*; by "*idito num dhātoḥ*" the root takes *num*; or, as before, Vedic *laṅ*; the root accent remains.
- ***nayamānaḥ*** — root *ṇīñ prāpaṇe*; *laṭ* with *śānac*; *śap* as the *vikaraṇa*; guṇa of the root; *āna* replaced by *mu* [?]; by "*āne muk*" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-82 [?]) the augment *muk*; since the *sārvadhātuka* *la* is *anudātta*, by the rule "*tāsy anudāttet*" the root accent remains.
- ***ruvat*** — root *ru śabde*; *laṭ* with *śatṛ*; by "*acchnā-dhātu-bhruvāṃ*…" [?] *uvaṅ* substitution; the suffix accent is first-syllable *udātta*.
- ***carat*** — root *cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ*; Vedic *laṅ* in the present sense; third person singular; by "*bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi*" no augment; *nighāta* accent for a *tiṅ*.
- ***vāk*** — root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *kvip* by "*kvibvacipracchi*…" (Uṇ. Sū. 2-… [?]) in the agent or in the passive sense; long vowel; no *saṃprasāraṇa*; at the end of the word *ku* (*c* becomes *k*). ‖ 3 ‖

> जुजोषदिन्द्रो दस्मवर्चा नासत्येव सुग्म्यो रथेष्ठाः ॥ ४ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (as read; doubtful passages marked [?])

> ता तान्यषतराणि व्याप्ततराणि वा हवींष्यस्मा इन्द्राय तदर्थं कर्म । कुर्वन्तः संपादयन्तः । कृञश्छन्दसि वर्तमानार्थे लुङ् [?] मन्त्रे घसेति च्लेर्लुक् [?] । छन्दस्युभयथेत्यार्धधातुकत्वेन जित्वाद्गुणः [?] । च्यौत्नानि च्यावयितॄणि दृढानि स्तोत्राणि कर्माणि स्वकीयानि सामर्थ्यानि वा देवयन्तो देवानात्मन इच्छन्तो यजमानाः प्र भरन्ते । प्रकर्षेण संपादयन्ति । तद्वद्यमपि संपादयाम इत्यर्थः । दस्मवर्चाः दर्शनीयतेजाः शत्रूपक्षयणबलो वा नासत्येव नासत्याविवाश्विनाविव । तौ हि द्यावापृथिव्यात्मानौ । तावि सुग्म्यः सुगम्यः सुखेन गन्तुं शक्यो रथेष्ठाः रथे वर्तमान एवंभूतः सन् जुजोषत् । अस्मत्संबन्धि तं स्तोत्रादि कर्म सेवताम् ॥

> *tā tāny aṣatarāṇi vyāptatarāṇi vā havīṃṣy asmā indrāya tadarthaṃ karma | kurvantaḥ saṃpādayantaḥ | kṛño chandasi vartamānārthe luṅ [?] mantre ghaseti ceḥ luk [?] | chandasy ubhayatheti ārdhadhātukatvena jitvād guṇaḥ [?] | cyautnāni cyāvayitṝṇi dṛḍhāni stotrāṇi karmāṇi svakīyāni sāmarthyāni vā devayanto devān ātmana icchanto yajamānāḥ pra bharante | prakarṣeṇa saṃpādayanti | tadvad vayam api saṃpādayāma ity arthaḥ | dasmavarcāḥ darśanīyatejāḥ śatrūpakṣayaṇabalo vā nāsatyeva nāsatyāv ivāśvināv iva | tau hi dyāvāpṛthivyātmānau | tāv i sugmyaḥ sugamyaḥ sukhena gantuṃ śakyo ratheṣṭhāḥ rathe vartamāna evaṃbhūtaḥ san jujoṣat | asmatsaṃbandhi taṃ stotrādi karma sevatām ‖* [?]

*Gist:* Doing for Indra those most abundant oblations, the sacrificers, desiring the gods, bring firm praises and acts; may Indra, of beautiful lustre, easy to approach, in his car like the Aśvins, accept them.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

*aṣatarā* — abundantly flowing (pervading); *tā* — those oblations; *asmai* — for this Indra; *karma* — by action (accomplishing); *devayantaḥ* — the sacrificers who desire the gods (their favour); *cyautnāni* — firm praise-form actions; *pra bharante* — (the sacrificers) abundantly accomplish; *dasmavarcāḥ* — one of beautiful lustre, or of strength that destroys enemies; *nāsatyā iva* — like the Aśvins; *sugmyaḥ indraḥ* — Indra, easy in his going; *ratheṣṭhāḥ* — seated in his car; *jujoṣat* — may he accept (our praises etc.).

**Bhāvārtha**

The sacrificers, desiring the favour of the gods, perform praises and other acts in abundance. We too, in the same way, accomplish oblations that flow abundantly, etc. May Indra, beautiful to behold and easy of access like the Aśvins, seated in his car, accept our praises and so on.

**Printed English**

We offer to him (Indra), the most pious (oblations): the worshippers of the gods present to him substantial (adorations): may he, of conspicuous lustre, standing in his car, and light-moving like the Ashwins, be gratified (by our worship).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***aṣatarā asmai karma — aṣatarāṇi vyāptatarāṇi vā havīṃṣi indrāya saṃpādayāmaḥ*** — the sacrificers who perform sacrifice, in the sacrifice directed to Indra, for the satisfaction of Indra,

### Printed p. 264  (PDF 284)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

prepare abundant oblations, or oblations that extend over a long time: so the meaning is given.

***cyautnāni devayantaḥ prabharante — dṛḍhāni stotrāṇi karmāṇi sāmarthyāni vā devān ātmana icchanto yajamānāḥ prakarṣeṇa saṃpādayanti*** — The word *cyautna* is read among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]). It may mean actions by which enemies are driven from their places (made to flee); or, since it causes the deities, who listen to the praises recited by the sacrificers, to come to the sacrificer's presence, the Sāyaṇa explanation gives two meanings of *cyautnāni*: "actions" or "hymns". Sacrificers who wish to obtain the attention of the deities by offering oblations in sacrifices dedicated to them perform their acts according to their capacity and please the deities with praises: this meaning is given.

The Nirukta-writers read *cyautna* among the names of strength: *ojaḥ*, *pājaḥ* and so on (Ni. 2-9 [?]).

> तव च्यौत्नानि वज्रहस्त तानि नव यत्पुरो नवतिं च सद्यः ।

> *tava cyautnāni vajrahasta tāni nava yat puro navatiṃ ca sadyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-… [?]) — in such ṛks the word is used as a synonym of *bala* (strength). And

> तमिच्च्यौत्नैरार्यन्ति तं कृतेभिश्चर्षणीयः । एष इन्द्रो वरिवस्कृत् ।

> *tam ic cyautnair āryanti taṃ kṛtebhiś carṣaṇīyaḥ | eṣa indro varivaskṛt |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-… [?]) — in such places it is "praise endowed with strength"; and

> स यो न मुहे न एथू जनो भूत्स्नमन्तु नामा चुमुरिं धुनिं च । वृणक्पिप्रुं शम्बरं शुष्णमिन्द्रः पुरां च्यौत्नाय शयथाय नू चित् ॥

> *sa yo na muhe na ethū jano bhūtsnam antu nāmā cumuriṃ dhuniṃ ca | vṛṇak pipruṃ śambaraṃ śuṣṇam indraḥ purāṃ cyautnāya śayathāya nū cit ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-18-8 [?]) — in such ṛks it means "that which is the means of destruction, being endowed with strength"; the meaning is to be taken according to the respective contexts. This word is formed from the root *cyu* ("to fall, to shake": one who causes to fall or to tremble).

***dasmavarcāḥ — darśanīyatejāḥ śatrūpakṣayaṇabalo vā*** — the word *varcas* is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9 [?]). Sāyaṇa explains that it is used in the sense of "radiance" or "strength"; the meaning given is that Indra is of lustre worthy of being seen from all sides and has strength that destroys enemies.

The word *dasma* has two kinds of meaning: one "destroyer of enemies", the other "of beautiful form". If it is formed from the root *dasi darśanadaṃśanayoḥ* ("to see, to bite"), then it means *darśanīyaḥ* "beautiful (to behold)"; if from the root *dasu upakṣaye* ("to waste, to destroy"), it means "destroyer of enemies" — [continues on p. 265].

---

### Printed p. 265  (PDF 285)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

…meaning "destroyer of enemies". Since both these powers belong to Indra and the other deities, it is shown that for the word *dasma* either of these two meanings may be taken. For example —

> त्वं भगो न आ हि रत्नमिषे परिज्मेव क्षयसि दस्मवर्चाः ।

> *tvaṃ bhago na ā hi ratnam iṣe parijmeva kṣayasi dasmavarcāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-13-2 [?]);

> पूषा सुबन्धुर्दिव आ पृथिव्या इळस्पतिर्मघवा दस्मवर्चाः ।

> *pūṣā subandhur diva ā pṛthivyā iḷas patir maghavā dasmavarcāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-4 [?]).

In such ṛks, as the first, "*śatrūpakṣayaṇabalaḥ*" means "one with the power to destroy enemies"; and as the second, "*varca iti rūpanāma | dasmaṃ darśanīyaṃ varcaḥ yasya tādṛśaḥ*" — "*varcas* is a name of form; one whose form is beautiful to behold" — the bhāṣya-writers thus show it to mean one whose form is delightful. The word *dasmavarcāḥ* is used as an epithet of Indra and the other deities in many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā; in the ṛk in hand also it describes, as an epithet of Indra, his power to destroy enemies and his lovely form.

***sugmyaḥ*** — "easily attained (by the sacrificer)", and ***ratheṣṭhāḥ*** — "moving in the car itself": so the meaning is stated.

***nāsatyeva — nāsatyāv iva aśvināv iva tau hi dyāvāpṛthivyātmānau*** — the Nirukta-writers, quoting

> ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमाः सधस्थं विश्वे अभि सन्ति देवाः ।
> ता अध्वर उशतो यक्ष्यग्ने श्रुष्टीवे भगं नासत्या पुरंधिम् ॥

> *te hi yajñeṣu yajñiyāsa ūmāḥ sadhasthaṃ viśve abhi santi devāḥ |*
> *tā adhvara uśato yakṣy agne śruṣṭī bhagaṃ nāsatyā puraṃdhim ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-4 [?]),

this ṛk, have given the meaning of the word *nāsatya*: "*satyāv eva nāsatyāv ity aurṇavābhaḥ, satyasya praṇetārāv ity āgrāyaṇaḥ, nāsikāprabhavau babhūvatur iti vā*" (Ni. 6-13 [?]) — as to the word *nāsatya*, they state the opinion that *nāsatyau* are the Aśvins. The opinion of the teacher Aurṇavābha is stated: the Aśvin deities are known as *nāsatyau* because they always speak the truth. The teacher Āgrāyaṇa accepts the same explanation of the word *nāsatya* ("*satyāv eva nāsatyau*"), and says the word *satya* means water or sacrifice, so that the Aśvin deities are those who accomplish the sacrifice. As said in the Bṛhaddevatā, there is another explanation: the Aśvins were born from the nose-region of Saṃjñā, the goddess, who, to be recognized as the Saṃjñā deity in the form of a mare, assumed the form of a mare when Sūrya, taking the form of a horse, looked at her.

Sāyaṇa: here the word *nāsatyāveva* means "like the Aśvin deities"; he says "*tau hi dyāvāpṛthivyātmānau*" — the Aśvin deities are of the nature of heaven and earth, as it is stated; that is, they come

### Printed p. 266  (PDF 286)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

from the form of heaven and earth, and so are able to go comfortably, and to move in the chariot; Indra also, like them, is *sugmya* and a dweller in the car; and *asmatsaṃbandhi taṃ stotrādi karma sevatām* — "may he, along with us, the sacrificers who perform them, be pleased with the sacrificial acts, the praises and so on": so the sacrificers' prayer is stated.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***tā*** — from the form *tāni*; by "*śeś chandasi bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 [?]) *śi* is dropped.
- ***karma*** — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; Vedic *luṅ* in the present sense (*chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*, Pā. Sū. 3-4-6 [?]); first person plural, *masa* suffix; *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* gives loss of *s*; *mantre ghasa-hvara*… (Pā. Sū. 2-4-80 [?]) gives *luk* for *cli*; by "*chandasy ubhayathā*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-117 [?]) the suffix is classed as *ārdhadhātuka*, and therefore the *ñit* guṇa; by "*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*" the root takes guṇa for the *ik*; *raparatva*; since it follows a *tiṅanta*, *nighāta* accent.
- ***cyautnāni*** — root *cyuṅ cyutau*; suffix *tnaṇ* by "*janidācyuvaḥ*…" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-… [?]); being *ṇit*, by "*aco ñṇiti*" the *u* is lengthened (vṛddhi); the final syllable is *udātta* by suffix accent.
- ***devayantaḥ*** — "they wish for the gods for themselves": by "*supa ātmanaḥ kyac*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 [?]) *kyac*; the *laṭ* comes after it and is replaced by *śatṛ*; third person plural.
- ***bharante*** — root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*; *laṭ*, third person plural; *nighāta* for a *tiṅ*.
- ***jujoṣat*** — root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*; in *loṭ* the *vyatyaya* gives *śap*; Vedically the root is reduplicated; or "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" replaces *śap* by *śluḥ*; thereafter by *vyatyaya* *śap*; by the statement "*bahulaṃ chandasīti vaktavyam*", "*nābhyastasyācīṇiti sārvadhātuke*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-87 [?]) — the guṇa required by it does not occur here; being in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; "*abhyastānām ādiḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189 [?]) makes the first syllable *udātta*.
- ***dasmavarcāḥ*** — *dasma varcaḥ yasya saḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*: the fore-member keeps its accent.
- ***sugmyaḥ*** — *sumu gantavyaḥ sugmyaḥ*; root *gamḷ gatau*; the suffix *ka* by the statement "*ghañarthe ka vidhānam*"; being *kit*, "*gamahanajana*…" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-98 [?]) drops the penultimate…

**Sūkta 173, Ṛk 5**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> तमु ष्टुहीन्द्रं यो ह सत्वा यः शूरो मघवा यो रथेष्ठाः ।
> प्रतीचश्चिद्योधीयान्वृषण्वान्ववव्रुषश्चित्तमसो विहन्ता ॥ ५ ॥

> *tam u ṣṭuhīndraṃ yo ha satvā yaḥ śūro maghavā yo ratheṣṭhāḥ |*
> *pratīcaś cid yodhīyān vṛṣaṇvān vavavruṣaś cit tamaso vihantā ‖ 5 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> तम् । ऊं इति । स्तुहि । इन्द्रम् । यः । ह । सत्वा । यः । शूरः । मघऽवा । यः । रथेऽस्थाः ।
> प्रतीचः । चित् । योधीयान् । वृषण्ऽवान् । ववव्रुषः । चित् । तमसः । विऽहन्ता ॥ ५ ॥

> *tam | ūṃ iti | stuhi | indram | yaḥ | ha | satvā | yaḥ | śūraḥ | magha-vā | yaḥ | rathe-sthāḥ |*
> *pratīcaḥ | cit | yodhīyān | vṛṣaṇ-vān | vavavruṣaḥ | cit | tamasaḥ | vi-hantā ‖ 5 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> तमु तमेवेन्द्रं स्तुहि । हे होतः स्तुतिं कुरु । किमस्याधिक्यमिति उच्यते । यो ह यः खलु सत्वा अतिप्रभूतबलः । यद्वा । सत्वा सादकः शत्रूणां । यश्च शूरः शौर्योपेतो मघवा बलवान्नन्नवान्वा । यश्च रथेष्ठा रथे वर्तमानः । किंच प्रतीचश्चित् प्रत्यभिमुखं योद्धॄनपि योधीयान् योद्धृतमः । प्रतिपूर्वादञ्चतेः क्विनन्ताल्लुप्तनकारादच्छसि [?] अचश्च इत्येकारलोपे चावपि दीर्घः । अञ्चेश्छन्दस्यसर्वनामस्थानमिति विभक्तिरुदात्ता [?] ॥ वृषण्वान् । वृषाणो वर्षितारो वज्रादयः । तद्वान् । वृषा ते वज्र उत ते वृषा रथः [?] । ऋ. २-१६-६ । इति हि निगमः । तथा ववव्रुषश्चित्तमसः आवरकस्यापि तमसो मेघादेर्विहन्ता विशेषेण घातकः । यस्मादेनं महानुभावः तस्मात्स्तुहि ॥ [as read; partly doubtful: [?]]

> *tam u tam evendraṃ stuhi | he hotaḥ stutiṃ kuru | kim asyādhikyam iti ucyate | yo ha yaḥ khalu satvā atiprabhūtabalaḥ | yadvā | satvā sādakaḥ śatrūṇāṃ | yaś ca śūraḥ śauryopeto maghavā balavān annavān vā | yaś ca ratheṣṭhā rathe vartamānaḥ | kiṃca pratīcaś cit pratyabhimukhaṃ yoddhṝn api yodhīyān yoddhṛtamaḥ | pratipūrvād añcateḥ kvinantāl luptanakārād acchasi [?] acaś ca ity ekāralope cāvapi dīrghaḥ | añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam iti vibhaktir udāttā [?] ‖ vṛṣaṇvān | vṛṣāṇo varṣitāro vajrādayaḥ | tadvān | vṛṣā te vajra uta te vṛṣā rathaḥ [?] | ṛ. 2-16-6 | iti hi nigamaḥ | tathā vavavruṣaś cit tamasaḥ āvarakasyāpi tamaso meghāder vihantā viśeṣeṇa ghātakaḥ | yasmād enaṃ mahānubhāvaḥ tasmāt stuhi ‖* [?]

*Gist:* O *hotṛ*, praise that very Indra: he is very mighty or a destroyer of enemies, a hero, rich, standing in his car, the best of fighters even against opponents who face him, with bulls (i.e. showering weapons such as the thunderbolt), and the destroyer of the all-enveloping darkness (cloud).

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

*yaḥ ha* — he who indeed (is Indra); *satvā* — one of abundant strength, or the destroyer of enemies; *yaḥ* — who; *śūraḥ* — heroic one (and); *maghavā* — rich in strength or in food; *yaḥ* —

### Printed p. 268  (PDF 288)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

who; *ratheṣṭhāḥ* — standing in his chariot; *pratīcaḥ cit* — even among those who face and fight; *yodhīyān* — the most excellent fighter; *vṛṣaṇvān* — one who has the thunderbolt and the other weapons, (and); (*yaḥ* — who) *vavavruṣaḥ cit tamasaḥ* — of the cloud that envelops all things; *vihantā* — the destroyer (of the cloud); *tam u* — that very one; *indram* — Indra; *stuhi* — praise.

**Bhāvārtha**

(O *hotṛ*,) praise Indra, who is of great prowess, heroic, rich in wealth, standing in his car, a fighter who faces his foes, a wielder of the thunderbolt and other weapons, a destroyer of the cloud and other things that are of the nature of the enveloping darkness.

**Printed English**

Glorify that Indra who is mighty, who is a hero, possessing abundant wealth, standing in his car, a valiant combatant against adversaries, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the disperser of all-enveloping gloom.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***tam u ṣṭuhi*** — by this sentence the address to the *hotṛ*-priests, "praise Indra", is made; the command of the sage who sees the mantra is stated here.

***yo ha satvā — atiprabhūtabalaḥ, yadvā sādakaḥ śatrūṇām*** — Indra is "of great strength" or "the destroyer of enemies": so the meaning is given.

***maghavā — balavān annavān vā*** — the Nirukta-writers read the word *magha* among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-10 [?]): "*maghaṃ iti dhananāmadheyaṃ maṃhater dānakarmaṇaḥ*" — the word *magha*, derived from the root *maṃh* which means giving, signifies wealth, they explain. Sāyaṇa takes the word *magha* in the senses "strength" or "food", and so gives the meaning "one who has strength or one who has food" for Indra.

Indra is *pratīcaś cit yodhīyān* — "the most excellent among the warriors who fight facing the enemy who is waging battle" — and *vṛṣaṇvān* — "possessing weapons such as the thunderbolt, which help in showering rain". Sāyaṇa, explaining the word *vṛṣaṇvān* as "*varṣitāraḥ*", says that it means weapons such as the thunderbolt, which are producers of rain; and to convey this same meaning —

---

### Printed p. 269  (PDF 289)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 13"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

> वृषा ते वज्र उत ते वृषा रथो वृषणा हरी वृषभाण्यायुधा । वृष्णो मदस्य वृषभ त्वमीशिष इन्द्र सोमस्य वृषभस्य तृप्णुहि ॥

> *vṛṣā te vajra uta te vṛṣā ratho vṛṣaṇā harī vṛṣabhāṇy āyudhā | vṛṣṇo madasya vṛṣabha tvam īśiṣa indra somasya vṛṣabhasya tṛpṇuhi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-35-6 [?]) — this ṛk is quoted. And as to Indra's being *vavavruṣaś cit tamasaḥ vihantā*, "the destroyer of the enveloping darkness", the great might of Indra is thereby described.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***stuhi*** — root *ṣṭuñ stutau*; *loṭ* second person singular; *nighāta* accent for a *tiṅ*.
- ***satvā*** — root *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; the suffix *kvanip* ("*prasera sadyoḥ stuṭ ca*", Uṇ. Sū. 4-… [?]), prescribed by the rule, applies in the plural to this root also; the suffix, being *pit*, is *anudātta*, so the root accent remains.
- ***pratīcaḥ*** — *prati* is a preposition; root *añcu gatipūjanayoḥ*; *kvin* suffix by "*ṛtvik dadhṛk…*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-59 [?]); *anidātāṃ halaḥ upadhāyāḥ kṅiti* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-24 [?]) drops the penultimate nasal; because of *bha* designation before a *śas* ending, *acaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-138 [?]) drops the *a* of the root; the root having *a* standing before the nasal-*a*-vowel, and following, "*cau*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-138 [?]) lengthens the preceding vowel; by the statement "*añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam*" the case ending is *udātta*.
- ***yodhīyān*** — the word *yodhin*, in the sense of excess, takes the suffix *īyasun*; by "*turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-154 [?]) the *ṭi* of *tṛc* (agent suffix) is dropped; by "*prakṛtyaikāc*" the natural form is retained, so the *ṭi*-loss does not occur; being *nit*, the suffix takes the first-syllable *udātta* by "*ñnityādir nityam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 [?]).
- ***vavavruṣaḥ*** — root *vṛñ āvaraṇe*, *curādi*; *kvasu* for *liṭ*; reduplication on account of the suffix; Vedically an extra *va* syllable appears; in the genitive, by "*vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-131 [?]), *saṃprasāraṇa*, with the earlier form; by "*śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-60 [?]) *ṣatva*; the *kvasu*-suffix accent remains.
- ***vihantā*** — root *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *tṛc* in the agent sense; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent. ‖ 5 ‖

**Sūkta 173, Ṛk 6**

### Printed p. 270  (PDF 290)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> प्र यदित्था महिना नृभ्यो अस्त्यरं रोदसी कक्ष्ये नास्मै ।
> सं विव्य इन्द्रो वृजनं न भूमा भर्ति स्वधावाँ ओपशमिव द्याम् ॥ ६ ॥

> *pra yad itthā mahinā nṛbhyo asty araṃ rodasī kakṣye nāsmai |*
> *saṃ vivya indro vṛjanaṃ na bhūmā bharti svadhāvāṃ opaśam iva dyām ‖ 6 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> प्र । यत् । इत्था । महिना । नृऽभ्यः । अस्ति । अरम् । रोदसी इति । कक्ष्ये इति । न । अस्मै ।
> सम् । विव्ये । इन्द्रः । वृजनम् । न । भूम [?] । भर्ति । स्वधाऽवान् । ओपशंऽइव । द्याम् ॥ ६ ॥

> *pra | yat | itthā | mahinā | nṛ-bhyaḥ | asti | aram | rodasī iti | kakṣye iti | na | asmai |*
> *sam | vivye | indraḥ | vṛjanam | na | bhūma [?] | bharti | svadhā-vān | opaśaṃ-iva | dyām ‖ 6 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> यद्यै इन्द्रो महिना महत्त्वेन स्वैश्वर्येण नृभ्यो नेतृभ्यः कर्मनिर्वाहकेभ्यो यजमानेभ्यः प्राप्ति प्रभवति ईष्वे [?] स्वर्गादिप्रदाने रक्षितुं अस्मै रक्षकायेन्द्राय रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ कक्ष्ये कक्ष्ययेते सती संचाराय नारं नालं । न पर्याप्ते । जगतोऽधीशस्येन्द्रस्य संचारायाल्पत्वाद्द्यावापृथिव्यौ न पर्याप्ते इत्यर्थः । सृष्ट्यादेपि सृष्टुर्महिम्नोऽधिकत्वादिति भावः । अयमिन्द्रो वृजनं न भूमं भूमिं भूतानि वा वृजनं न वृजनमिव ॥ वृजेः कर्तनार्थस्येदं रूपम् । तदिव तद्यथावृणोति तथायमपि स्वतेजसा सं विव्ये । सम्यग्वावृणोति लोकत्रयम् । किंचायं स्वधावाननवान् वृष्टिलक्षणोदकवान्वा द्यां दिवं भर्ति बिभर्ति । धारणे दृष्टान्तः । ओपशमिव । ईषदुपशेते इत्योपशं शृङ्गं । तद्वृषभ इव । यद्वा । परस्परं समीपे वर्तमानं क्षित्यन्तरिक्षाख्यं लोकद्वयमोपशं । तदिव द्यां बिभर्ति । लोकत्रयमपि बिभर्तीत्यर्थः ॥ भृञोऽलोट्‌ छान्दसः शपो लुक् ॥ [as read; partly doubtful: [?]]

> *yad yai indro mahinā mahattvena svaiśvaryeṇa nṛbhyo netṛbhyaḥ karmanirvāhakebhyo yajamānebhyaḥ prāpti prabhavati īṣve [?] svargādipradāne rakṣituṃ asmai rakṣakāyendrāya rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyau kakṣye kakṣyayete satī saṃcārāya nāraṃ nālaṃ | na paryāpte | jagato 'dhīśasyendrasya saṃcārāyālpatvād dyāvāpṛthivyau na paryāpte ity arthaḥ | sṛṣṭyāder api sraṣṭur mahimno 'dhikatvād iti bhāvaḥ | ayam indro vṛjanaṃ na bhūmaṃ bhūmiṃ bhūtāni vā vṛjanaṃ na vṛjanam iva ‖ vṛjeḥ kartanārthasyedaṃ rūpam | tad iva tad yathā vṛṇoti tathāyam api svatejasā saṃ vivye | samyag vāvṛṇoti lokatrayam | kiṃcāyaṃ svadhāvān annavān vṛṣṭilakṣaṇodakavān vā dyāṃ divaṃ bharti bibharti | dhāraṇe dṛṣṭāntaḥ | opaśam iva | īṣad upaśete ity opaśaṃ śṛṅgaṃ | tad vṛṣabha iva | yadvā | parasparaṃ samīpe vartamānaṃ kṣity-antarikṣākhyaṃ lokadvayam opaśaṃ | tad iva dyāṃ bibharti | lokatrayam api bibhartīty arthaḥ ‖ bhṛño 'loṭ chāndasaḥ śapo luk ‖* [?]

*Gist:* Because of his greatness Indra is able to protect and give heaven to the sacrificers who carry out the rites; heaven and earth are too small for his movement; he covers the three worlds with his splendour and, rich in food and water, bears heaven like a horn.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

*yat* — because Indra; *itthā* — truly; *mahinā* — by his own greatness (lordship); *nṛbhyaḥ* — to the leaders (to the sacrificers who carry out the rites); *pra asti* — is able to grant heaven and other fruits, or to protect; *asmai* — (protecting) to this Indra; *kakṣye* — extending to the sides (as in the sense of the hip-girdle); *rodasī* — earth and atmosphere; *na aram* — are not sufficient (for his movement); *indraḥ* — this Indra; *bhūma* — the earth; *vṛjanaṃ na* — like a covering the sky; *saṃ vivye* — (with his lustre, the three worlds) pervades; (*kiñca ayam* — further this)

---

### Printed p. 271  (PDF 291)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 14"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

*(Pratipadārtha concluded)* …this Indra); *svadhāvān* — rich in food (in the form of rain-water); *opaśam iva* — as a bull bears its horn, or like the earth and atmosphere, which lie near each other; *bharti* — bears (he is the support).

**Bhāvārtha**

Indra, the protector of the sacrificers who carry out the rites, of great glory, has overspread the regions of earth and atmosphere; as the sky covers the earth, so he covers the three worlds with his splendour; and, endowed with food (in the form of rain-water), as he is the support of earth and atmosphere, so he is the support of heaven too.

**Printed English**

Heaven and earth are insufficient for the girth of that Indra, who, with his greatness, rules over the leaders (of sacrifice): as the atmosphere encompasses the earth, so he encompasses (the three worlds), and, being the master of the rain, he upholds the sky as well as the firmament and the earth.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***mahinā nṛbhyaḥ pra asti — mahattvena svaiśvaryeṇa netṛbhyaḥ karmanirvāhakebhyaḥ yajamānebhyaḥ prabhavati*** — By the power of his greatness, filled with majesty, Indra is worshipped by the sacrificers who carry out the sacrificial rites: so the meaning is given. The word *nṛ* is read among the names of horses (Ni. 1-... [?]) and among the names of men (Ni. 3-... [?]); here it is used in the sense of the sacrificers who perform the rites.

***itthā*** — the word is read among the *satya* names ("truth"): *bṭ, śrat* and so on (Ni. 3-10 [?]). Showing the explanation of the word *itthā*, the Nirukta says: "*itthā amutheti etena vyākhyātam*" (Ni. 5-5 [?]) — "*itthā* is explained by the word *amuthā*", as said; "*amuthā yathāsāv iti vyākhyātam*" (Ni. 3-16 [?]) — *amuthā* is used both in the sense of "truly" and in the sense of "in that manner". Likewise the use of the word *itthā* is to be understood; so —

> त्यं चिदित्था कत्पयं शयानमसूर्ये तमसि वावृधानम् ।

> *tyaṃ cid itthā katpayaṃ śayānam asūrye tamasi vāvṛdhānam |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-32-2 [?])

### Printed p. 272  (PDF 292)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

— quoting this ṛk, the Nirukta (Ni. 6-3 [?]) shows that the word *itthā* means "truly". Durgācārya explains it as "in this manner" (*amunā prakāreṇa*) and Sāyaṇa as "*amuṣminn antarikṣaloke*", "in that atmospheric world"; in the ṛk at hand it is used in the sense of "truly".

***kakṣye — kakṣyā rajjuḥ raśmasya — kakṣaṃ sevate*** — "*kakṣyā* (girth) — the rope, of the horse's *raśmi*; it serves the *kakṣa*; *kakṣo gāhateḥ, kasa iti nāmakaraṇaḥ | khyāter vārthakyo 'bhyāsaḥ | kim asmin khyānam iti | kaṣater vā | tatsamānāny aṅgāni manuṣyasya kakṣo bāhumūlasāmānyāt*" [as read; garbled: [?]] (Ni. 2-… [?]). The band tied around the belly of the horse is called *kakṣyā*. The word *kakṣyā* may be formed with the suffix *ṣya* [?] added to the root *gāh* used in the sense of "entering within"; or from the reduplicated form of the root *khyā*; or its source may be the root *kaṣ* with the sense of *ujjh* (rubbing); hence the armpit (*kakṣa*) of a man is well known by the name; that is, it may be taken to mean "heaven and earth, which resemble the armpit in their interval".

Besides, the Nirukta-writers read the word *kakṣyā* among the names of "fingers" (Ni. 3-... [?]) and for the use of this word, in

> दशावनिभ्यो दशकक्ष्येभ्यो दशयोक्त्रेभ्यो दशयोजनेभ्यः । दशाभीशुभ्यो अर्चताजरेभ्यो दश धुरो दश युक्ता वहद्भ्यः ॥

> *daśāvanibhyo daśakakṣyebhyo daśayoktrebhyo daśayojanebhyaḥ | daśābhīśubhyo arcatājarebhyo daśa dhuro daśa yuktā vahadbhyaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-7 [?]) the meaning given here for the word *kakṣyā* is "fingers". In the ṛk at hand it means the interval between heaven and earth.

***asmai rodasī kakṣye nālam*** — the word *rodasī* is read among the names of heaven and earth (Ni. 3-... [?]). The meaning is given that heaven and earth, though they are travelling in their own paths, are not enough for the movements of Indra, who protects the sacrificers performing the rites; and, "*jagato 'dhīśasya indrasya saṃcārāya alpatvāt dyāvāpṛthivyau na paryāpte | sṛṣṭyāder api sraṣṭur mahimno 'dhikatvāt*": since the greatness of the maker of creation is greater than the greatness of the thing created, Indra, who is lord of the world, finds the space in heaven and earth insufficient to move about in. By this it is indicated that the greatness of heaven and earth is less than that of Indra.

***araṃ — alam | paryāpte ity arthaḥ*** — "enough": the sense is that it be enough to give satisfaction. As it gives the sense of "sufficient", this word is used also in the senses "prepare, serve".

### Printed p. 273  (PDF 293)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 14"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; signature mark "XIII 18" at foot.)*

> वायवा याहि दर्शतेमे सोमा अरंकृताः ।

> *vāyav ā yāhi darśate me somā araṃkṛtāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-1);

> अरं कृण्वन्तु वेदिं समग्निमिन्धतां पुरः ।

> *araṃ kṛṇvantu vediṃ sam agnim indhatāṃ puraḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-170-4 [?]) —

in such ṛks *araṃkṛta*, *araṃkṛṇvantu* mean "prepare, make ready"; and in

> त्वमग्ने द्रविणोदा अरंकृते त्वं देवः सविता रत्नधा असि ।

> *tvam agne draviṇodā araṃkṛte tvaṃ devaḥ savitā ratnadhā asi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-7 [?]) the meaning is "worship, serve". In the ṛk at hand, as in these,

> सोमारुद्रा धारयेथामसुर्यं प्र वामिष्टयोऽरमश्नुवन्तु ।

> *somārudrā dhārayethām asuryaṃ pra vām iṣṭayo 'ram aśnuvantu |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-74-1 [?])

and similar ṛks, the meaning is "sufficient to give satisfaction".

***vṛjanaṃ na bhūma saṃvivye — bhūmiṃ bhūtāni vā vṛjanam iva | tad iva tad yathā āvṛṇoti tathā ayam api svatejasā samyag vāvṛṇoti lokatrayam*** — the word *vṛjana* is read among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]). It is compared to the way strength covers the earth and living beings. Here, by the word *bhūma*, the meaning "earth or living beings" is given. As that strength covers the earth and the living beings, so Indra has covered the three worlds with his splendour: so the meaning is described.

***svadhāvān — annavān vṛṣṭilakṣaṇodakavān vā*** — the word *svadhā* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-... [?]) and among the names of food (Ni. 2-... [?]). This name is used in yet another sense; here Indra, as one who has food and who has waters in the form of rain, is said to uphold the world of heaven: so the meaning is described.

***svadhāvān*** — Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "possessing food, possessing waters in the form of rain". In some places Sāyaṇa himself has given two meanings for the word *svadhayā*: "*ātmīyena tejasā; havirlakṣaṇena annena vā*" ("by his own splendour; or by food in the form of oblation"); since, in the ṛk at hand, the power of Indra is said to exceed the greatness of heaven and earth, here *tejovān* ("splendid") seems the more suitable meaning. The Nirukta-writers have included this word both among the names of water (Ni. 1-... [?]) and among the names of food (Ni. 2-... [?]). In many contexts the meaning of the word *svadhā* is "one's own greatness, one's own splendour, or self-support". For example —

### Printed p. 274  (PDF 294)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

> शश्वत्पुरोषा व्युवास देव्यथो अद्येदं व्यावो मघोनी । अथो व्युच्छादुत्तराँ अनु द्यूनजरामृता चरति स्वधाभिः ॥

> *śaśvat purā uṣā vyuvāsa devy atho adyedaṃ vy āvo maghonī | atho vyucchād uttarāṁ anu dyūn ajarāmṛtā carati svadhābhiḥ ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-13 [?]) — in this ṛk, used about Uṣas, the word means "by *ātmīyaistejobhiḥ*", "by her own splendours". Likewise —

> यदन्तरिक्षे पतथः पुरुभुजा यद्वेमे रोदसी अनु । यद्वा स्वधाभिरधितिष्ठथो रथमत आ यातमश्विना ॥

> *yad antarikṣe patathaḥ purubhujā yad ve me rodasī anu | yad vā svadhābhir adhitiṣṭhatho ratham ata ā yātam aśvinā ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-10-6 [?]) — here too the word means "with splendours (*tejobhiḥ*) or with strengths of one's own"; that is, "with your own splendours or your own powers". And

> न मृत्युरासीदमृतं न तर्हि न रात्र्या अह्न आसीत्प्रकेतः । आनीदवातं स्वधया तदेकं तस्माद्धान्यन्न परः किं चनास ॥

> *na mṛtyur āsīd amṛtaṃ na tarhi na rātryā ahna āsīt praketaḥ | ānīd avātaṃ svadhayā tad ekaṃ tasmād dhānyan na paraḥ kiṃ canāsa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-2) — in this ṛk Sāyaṇa explains "*svasmin dhīyate dhriyate āśritya vartate iti svadhā*" — that which is held in itself, supported, and abides depending on itself, is *svadhā*; as it rests on its own support, the word is explained as an epithet of Īśvara (the Supreme Brahman), as that of the *māyā*, the wonderful power. In the same way the word may be understood in the present ṛk: Indra, by his extraordinary splendour, by his greatness, by the power that protects the worlds, has encompassed all the worlds. Besides —

> स्वधामनु श्रियं नरो महि त्वेषा अमवन्तो वृषप्सवः । वहन्ते अह्रुतप्सवः ॥

> *svadhām anu śriyaṃ naro mahi tveṣā amavanto vṛṣapsavaḥ | vahante ahrutapsavaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-20-7 [?]);

> वि विद्युतो न वृष्टिभी रुचाना अनु स्वधा मायुयुर्यैर्ऋभमाणाः । [?]

> *vi vidyuto na vṛṣṭibhī rucānā anu svadhā māyuyuryair ṛbhamāṇāḥ |* [as read; garbled: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-… [?])

— in such ṛks, since the usages "*svadhām anu*", "*anu svadhām*" occur, the meanings "naturally", "by nature", "as is proper to them" arise. And

> अचिक्रया यत्स्वधया सुपर्णो हव्यं भरन्मनवे देवजुष्टम् ।

> *acikrayā yat svadhayā suparṇo havyaṃ bharan manave devajuṣṭam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-4 [?]) — "by the chariot" is the meaning here; and

> अपश्यं ग्रामं वहमानमाराद्अचक्रया स्वधया वर्तमानम् ।

> *apaśyaṃ grāmaṃ vahamānam ārād acakrayā svadhayā vartamānam |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-27-19 [?]).

### Printed p. 275  (PDF 295)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 14"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

In such places Sāyaṇa explains it as "*senayā*" ("with the army"); it shows the nature of a thing possessed of splendour. In the ṛk at hand, the word *svadhāvān* can be said to describe the might of Indra, who is of great glory.

***opaśam iva — īṣad upaśete ity opaśaṃ śṛṅgaṃ tad vṛṣabha iva*** — the horn (*śṛṅga*), because it arises slightly (little) on the head, is explained as having the sense of the word *opaśa*. In the matter of Indra's supporting the three worlds, it is explained in one way by comparing him to a bull, which carries without effort the horn that has grown in a slight rise on its head. In the second meaning: "*parasparaṃ samīpe vartamānaṃ kṣity-antarikṣākhyaṃ lokadvayam opaśaṃ tad iva dyāṃ bibharti | lokatrayam api bibhartīty arthaḥ*" — as one holds the two worlds, known as earth and atmosphere, which lie close to each other, so Indra holds the world of heaven; the sense is that he holds the three worlds. By this the abundant greatness of Indra, who guards the three worlds without effort, is described.

***rodasī*** — *rodasī* means heaven and earth. The word *rodasī*, which is a "marked" (*aṅkita*) name, in many contexts also indicates the name of a person (the wife of Rudra). Therefore this word is used both in the singular and in the dual; the meaning is to be given according to the contexts. The Nirukta-writers, quoting

> उताभये पुरुहूत श्रवोभिरेको दृळ्हमवदो वृत्रहा सन् । इमे चिदिन्द्र रोदसी अपारे यत्संगृभ्णा मघवन् काशिरित्ते ॥

> *utābhaye puruhūta śravobhir eko dṛḷham avado vṛtrahā san | ime cid indra rodasī apāre yat saṃgṛbhṇā maghavan kāśir it te ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-5 [?]), in explaining the word *rodasī* there, say

> रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ विरोधनात् ।

> *rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyau virodhanāt |*

(Ni. 6-1 [?]) — since both are bound and restricted by a limited boundary (*sīmā*), the name *rodasī* is known for heaven and earth; this is the derivation of the dual *rodasī*. Again, to give the meaning of the word in the singular, they say

> रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नी

> *rodasī rudrasya patnī*

(Ni. 11-49 [?]) — *rodasī* is the wife of Rudra; and

> रथं नु मारुतं वयं श्रवस्युमा हुवामहे । आ यस्मिन्तस्थौ सुरणानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ॥

> *rathaṃ nu mārutaṃ vayaṃ śravasyum ā huvāmahe | ā yasmin tasthau suraṇāni bibhratī sacā marutsu rodasī ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-56-8 [?]).

### Printed p. 276  (PDF 296)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

— quoting this ṛk, he points out that here *rodasī* is the "marked" name meaning Rudra's wife. But here another problem arises: *rudrapatnī*, "Rudra's wife" — either the wife of the deity Rudra, or — since the word *rudra* may also mean the Maruts — the consort of the Marut deities: to leave room for this doubt, Sāyaṇa has commented in two ways. Explaining the ṛk at hand, he says:

> रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नी मरुतां माता । यद्वा रुद्रो वायुः । तस्य पत्नी माध्यमिका देवी ॥

> *rodasī rudrasya patnī marutāṃ mātā | yadvā rudro vāyuḥ | tasya patnī mādhyamikā devī ‖*

(Sā. Bhā.). *Rodasī* may be one meaning: the wife of Rudra and the mother of the Maruts. Or, since the word *rudra* has the meaning "wind", *rodasī* is the wife of the wind: the speech of the middle region (*mādhyamikā vāk*): thus it is explained in two ways. And

> परा शुभ्रा अयासो यव्या साधारण्येव मरुतो मिमिक्षुः । न रोदसी अप नुदन्ते घोरा जुषन्त वृधं सख्याय देवाः ॥

> *parā śubhrā ayāso yavyā sādhāraṇyeva maruto mimikṣuḥ | na rodasī apa nudante ghorā juṣanta vṛdhaṃ sakhyāya devāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-167-4 [?]) — in explaining this ṛk, as shown before:

> रोदसा शब्देन रोदनस्वभावो रुद्रः । तस्य स्त्री रोदसीति केचिदाहुः । अपरे तु मरुतां स्त्रियो रोदसीति नामधेयमित्याहुः । अयमेव पक्षो युक्त उत्तरत्रैवं व्यवहारात् ।

> *rodasā śabdena rodanasvabhāvo rudraḥ | tasya strī rodasīti kecid āhuḥ | apare tu marutāṃ striyo rodasīti nāmadheyam ity āhuḥ | ayam eva pakṣo yukta uttaratraivaṃ vyavahārāt |* [as read: [?]]

By the word *rodasa*, Rudra, of weeping nature; his wife is *rodasī*, some say; others say that the wives of the Maruts bear the name *rodasī*. This latter view is the proper one, because of the usage in what follows: this is the opinion he gives. *Rodasī* is thus (one view) the wife of Rudra; (another) the wife of the Maruts; of these the second seems the right one, he says. Further —

> जोषद्यदीमसुर्या सचध्यै विषितस्तुका रोदसी नृमणाः ॥

> *joṣad yad īm asuryā sacadhyai viṣitastukā rodasī nṛmaṇāḥ ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-167-5 [?]) — in explaining this ṛk he states that *rodasī* here is *marutpatnī* "Maruts' wife", *vidyut* "lightning"; she is the wife of the Maruts, or is known by this name *vidyut* ("lightning"). He has also quoted the passage in which this *rodasī* is stated to be present in the sight of (i.e. as an attendant of) the Maruts. Further, examining other cases where *rodasī* is used —

> ते इदुग्राः शवसा धृष्णुषेणा उभे युजन्त रोदसी सुमेके । अध स्मैषु रोदसी स्वशोचिरामवत्सु तस्थौ न रोकः ॥

> *te id ugrāḥ śavasā dhṛṣṇuṣeṇā ubhe yujanta rodasī sumeke | adha smaiṣu rodasī svaśocir āmavatsu tasthau na rokaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-66-6 [?]) — in this single ṛk the word *rodasī* has been used in two meanings. Here, for the first word Sāyaṇa gives "*dyāvāpṛthivyau*" ("heaven and earth"), and for the second "*rudrasya patnī mādhyamikī vāk*" ("Rudra's wife, the speech of the middle region"). And again —

### Printed p. 277  (PDF 297)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 14"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

> मिमय्क्ष येषु रोदसी नु देवी सिषक्ति पूषा अभ्यर्धयज्वा । श्रुत्वा हवं मरुतो यद्ध याथ भूमा रेजन्ते अध्वनि प्रविक्ते ॥ [as read: [?]]

> *mimayakṣa yeṣu rodasī nu devī siṣakti pūṣā abhyardhayajvā | śrutvā havaṃ maruto yad dha yātha bhūmā rejante adhvani pravikte ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-50-5 [?]) — here also he has interpreted *devī dyotamānā mādhyamikā vāk*, "the shining speech of the middle region". Explaining Ṛk 1-167-3 [?], the scholar Max Müller, on the word *rodasī* used in the senses lightning (*vidyut*), speech of the middle region and heaven and earth, has written as follows:

> In our verse, we take वाक् in the sense of thunder, but as a feminine, of the lightning and thunder as the two companions of the Maruts, represents the first, रोदसी or lightning, as the recognised wife, hiding herself in the house, while the other, the loud thunder, is represented as a more public companion of the Maurts [sic]. This contrast, if it is really what the poet intended, throws a curious light on the social character of the Vedic times, as it presupposes two classes of wives, not necessarily simultaneous, however — a house wife, who stays at home and is not much seen, and a wife who appears in public and takes part in the society…… The loud voice of the thunder as well as the usual hiding of the lightning might well suggest this comparison. [S.B.E. XXXII p. 276]

> *In our verse, we take vāk in the sense of thunder, but as a feminine, of the lightning and thunder as the two companions of the Maruts, represents the first, rodasī or lightning, as the recognised wife, hiding herself in the house, while the other, the loud thunder, is represented as a more public companion of the Maurts [sic]. This contrast, if it is really what the poet intended, throws a curious light on the social character of the Vedic times, as it presupposes two classes of wives, not necessarily simultaneous, however — a house wife, who stays at home and is not much seen, and a wife who appears in public and takes part in the society…… The loud voice of the thunder as well as the usual hiding of the lightning might well suggest this comparison. [S.B.E. XXXII p. 276]*

Pointing out thus the difference between the singular and the dual uses, the Bṛhaddevatā likewise says:

> रोदसी देवपत्नीनाम् अथर्वाङ्गिरसे यथा ।

> *rodasī devapatnīnām atharvāṅgirase yathā |*

(Bṛ. De. 2-143 [?]) — according to the school of the Atharvāṅgirasas (Atharvaveda), *rodasī* is one among the wives of the gods: this is an example of the singular use. And

> द्वे द्वे पदे संस्तुते रोदसी च देवाश्चार्धर्चेन विभक्तमन्यत् ।

> *dve dve pade saṃstute rodasī ca devāś cārdharcena vibhaktam anyat |* [as read: [?]]

(Bṛ. De. 4-6 [?]) — in all such places where the dual is used, the meaning is "heaven and earth".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***mahinā*** — root *mahī pūjāyām*; by "*in sarvadhātubhyaḥ*" the suffix *in*; third (instrumental) singular; by *vyatyaya* the case ending is *udātta*.

### Printed p. 278  (PDF 298)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 173".)*

- ***asti*** — because of the relative (*yadyoga*) no *nighāta* accent; *tip* being *pit*, the root accent remains.
- ***aram*** — "*vālamūlalaghu*…" (Pā. Sū. 8-2-18 [?]) gives *repha* substitution for *la*.
- ***vivye*** — root *vī gatyādiṣu*; by "*chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*" *liṭ* in the present sense; third person singular; *nighāta* for a *tiṅ*.
- ***vṛjanam*** — root *vṛjī varjane*; used here in the agent sense; the suffix *kyu* by "*kyaspyāvṛji*…" (Uṇ. Sū. 2-… [?]); by "*yuvor anākau*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 [?]) *yu* becomes *ana*; being *kit*, the guṇa of the light vowel does not occur; the suffix accent is first-syllable *udātta*.
- ***bharti*** — root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*; *laṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" gives *luk* for *śap*; by "*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*" guṇa for *ik*; *ra* follows; since in *pādādi* position no *nighāta*; *tip* being *pit* is *anudātta*, so the root accent remains.
- ***svadhāvān*** — by "*mādhupadhāyāś ca*" (Pā. Sū. 8-2-9 [?]) *va* for the *m* of the suffix *mat*; "*dīrghād aṭi samānapāde*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-9 [?]) *ru* for the *n*; "*āto 'ṭi nityam*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-3 [?]) — by this rule the *ā* takes nasalization (*anunāsika*) always.
- ***opaśam*** — root *śīṅ svapne*; when the two prefixes *āṅ* and *upa* are in construction, by "*bahulagrahaṇa*" the suffix *ḍa*; being *ḍit*, the *ṭi* is dropped; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent. ‖ 6 ‖

**Sūkta 173, Ṛk 7**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> समत्सु त्वा शूर सतामुराणं प्रपथिन्तमं परितंसयध्यै ।
> सजोषस इन्द्रं मदे क्षोणीः सूरिं चिद्ये अनुमदन्ति वाजैः ॥ ७ ॥

> *samatsu tvā śūra satām urāṇaṃ prapathintamaṃ paritaṃsayadhyai |*
> *sajoṣasa indraṃ made kṣoṇīḥ sūriṃ cid ye anumadanti vājaiḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> समत्ऽसु । त्वा । शूर । सताम् । उराणम् । प्रऽपथिन्ऽतमम् । परिऽतंसयध्यै ।
> सऽजोषसः । इन्द्रम् । मदे । क्षोणीः । सूरिम् । चित् । ये । अनुऽमदन्ति । वाजैः ॥ ७ ॥

> *samat-su | tvā | śūra | satām | urāṇam | pra-pathin-tamam | pari-taṃsayadhyai |*
> *sa-joṣasaḥ | indram | made | kṣoṇīḥ | sūrim | cit | ye | anu-madanti | vājaiḥ ‖ 7 ‖*
