**Sūkta 175, Ṛk 2**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> आ नस्ते गन्तु मत्सरो वृषा मदो वरेण्यः ।
> सहावाँ इन्द्र सानसिः पृतनाषाळमर्त्यः ॥ २ ॥

> *ā nas te gantu matsaro vṛṣā mado vareṇyaḥ |*
> *sahāvāṃ indra sānasiḥ pṛtanāṣāḷ amartyaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> आ । नः । ते । गन्तु । मत्सरः । वृषा । मदः । वरेण्यः ।
> सहस्वान् [?] । इन्द्र । सानसिः । पृतनाषाट् । अमर्त्यः ॥ २ ॥

> *ā | naḥ | te | gantu | matsaraḥ | vṛṣā | madaḥ | vareṇyaḥ |*
> *sahasvān [?] | indra | sānasiḥ | pṛtanāṣāṭ | amartyaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (as read; doubtful passages marked [?])

> हे इन्द्र ते त्वां नोऽस्मदीयो मत्सरो मर्षणसाधनः सोम आ गन्तु । आगच्छतु । कीदृशोऽयं । वृषा वर्षकः मदस्तर्पयिता वरेण्यो वरणीयः सहावान् सहायवान् सहसा बलेन तद्वान्वा सानसिः संभजनीयः पृतनाषाट् शत्रुसेनाया अभिभविता अमर्त्योऽविनाशी । ईदृशः सोमस्त्वामागच्छतु । यद्वा । उत्तरार्धे इन्द्रपरतयापि व्याख्येयं । हे इन्द्र सहावानस्मद्दत्तसोमसहायवान् बलवान्वा सानसिरस्माभिः संभजनीयः पृतनाषाडमर्त्यश्च भवसि ॥

> *he indra te tvāṃ no 'smadīyo matsaro marṣaṇasādhanaḥ soma ā gantu | āgacchatu | kīdṛśo 'yaṃ | vṛṣā varṣakaḥ madas tarpayitā vareṇyo varaṇīyaḥ sahāvān sahāyavān sahasā balena tadvān vā sānasiḥ saṃbhajanīyaḥ pṛtanāṣāṭ śatrusenāyā abhibhavitā amartyo 'vināśī | īdṛśaḥ somas tvām āgacchatu | yadvā | uttarārdhe indraparatayāpi vyākhyeyaṃ | he indra sahāvān asmaddattasomasahāyavān balavān vā sānasir asmābhiḥ saṃbhajanīyaḥ pṛtanāṣāḍ amartyaś ca bhavasi ‖*

*Gist:* O Indra, may our Soma, which is exhilarating, strengthening, satisfying, choice and imperishable, come to you; or, taking the second half as addressed to Indra: you, strong, companionable, enjoyable, overthrower of hosts, immortal.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

(*he*) *indra* — O Indra; *naḥ* — our; *vṛṣā* — the giver of desired objects; *madaḥ* — satisfying; *vareṇyaḥ* — desirable; *sahāvān* — endowed with companions (strength); *sānasiḥ* — enjoyable; *pṛtanāṣāṭ* — the destroyer of enemies, and; *amartyaḥ* — imperishable; *matsaraḥ* — the Soma juice, the means of gladness; *te* — to you; *ā gantu* — may it come. [Or *naḥ* — ours; *vṛṣā*, *madaḥ*, *vareṇyaḥ* — the giver of desired objects, the satisfier, the choice; *matsaraḥ* — the Soma juice that is offered by us as the means of gladness; *te ā gantu* — may it come to you (drinking it, you); *sahāvān* — mighty; *sānasiḥ* — attainable by us; *pṛtanāṣāṭ* — the destroyer of enemies; *amartyaḥ* — the imperishable (be).]

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra, may the Soma juice that is offered by us, which gives desired objects, satisfaction, delight, and is the means of gladness, come to you; drinking it, be strong, attainable by us, a destroyer of enemies, and imperishable.

### Printed p. 370  (PDF 390)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

**Printed English**

May our Soma libation reach you, (for it is) exhilarating, invigorating, inebriating, most precious: it is companionable, Indra, enjoyable, the overthrower of hosts, immortal. [As printed: "ove r-thrower" is a broken letter-space in the print.]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk it is explained that the words *matsaraḥ*, *vṛṣā*, *madaḥ*, *vareṇyaḥ*, *sahāvān*, *sānasiḥ*, *pṛtanāṣāṭ*, *amartyaḥ* are used as epithets of the Soma juice. The meaning of these words has already been explained in the preceding ṛks, so it will not be described again here.

***pṛtanāṣāṭ*** — the word *pṛtanā* is read among the names of battle (Ni. 2-17 [?]). Since those who fight in battle are the soldiers of armies, here the meaning "enemy-army" (*śatrusenā*) is given: "*śatrusenāyāḥ abhibhavitā*" — the explanation is given that the Soma produces the power to conquer the enemy's army.

This word is well established as an epithet of Indra, describing Indra's distinction; but in the Ṛk-saṃhitā it is not only an epithet of Indra, but an epithet of Agni and other deities as well, indicating their prowess. For example —

> कृणोत धूमं वृषणं सखायोऽस्रेधन्त इतन वाजमच्छ । अयमग्निः पृतनाषाट् सुवीरो येन देवासो असहन्त दस्यून् ॥

> *kṛṇota dhūmaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ sakhāyo 'sredhanta itana vājam accha | ayam agniḥ pṛtanāṣāṭ suvīro yena devāso asahanta dasyūn ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29-9 [?]) — here "*pṛtanopalakṣitaṃ yuddhaṃ sahamānaḥ*" ("the one who withstands battle, which is indicated by *pṛtanā*") is the sense of the prowess of Agni that is shown; and "*vyāpriyante atra yoddhāraḥ iti pṛtanāḥ saṃgrāmāḥ*" — since it is the place where warriors gather together in groups, the word *pṛtanā* is used for battle in one place (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-49-2 [?]); and further,

> इमं नरो मरुतः सश्चता वृधं यस्मिन्रायः शेवृधासः । अभि ये सन्ति पृतनासु दूढ्यो विश्वाहा शत्रुमादभुः ॥

> *imaṃ naro marutaḥ saścatā vṛdhaṃ yasmin rāyaḥ śevṛdhāsaḥ | abhi ye santi pṛtanāsu dūḍhyo viśvāhā śatrum ādabhuḥ ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-16-2 [?]) — here, in *pṛtanāsu*, Sāyaṇa in another place explains the word "*senāsu tadupalakṣiteṣu saṃgrāmeṣu*" — "in armies, in the battles that are indicated by them". The Nirukta-writers include this word among the names of battle (Ni. 2-17 [?]). Since in such battles, with enemy armies, he bears his own strength and the strength of his enemies, it is natural that this epithet should apply to Indra or to Agni; but in the ṛk at hand it is an epithet of Soma.

### Printed p. 371  (PDF 391)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

***matsaraḥ*** — for this word two meanings are possible: "the cause of delight", and, as another, "envy" (*mātsarya*). The Nirukta-writers too have given two meanings for this word.

> मत्सरः सोमो मन्दतेस्तृप्तिकर्मणः ।

> *matsaraḥ somo mandates tṛptikarmaṇaḥ |*

(Ni. 2-25 [?]) — from the root *mad* (*mandate*), meaning "to cause satisfaction", the word is used as a synonym of the Soma juice; and "*matsara iti lobha nāma*" — "*matsara* is a name for greed": since it shows excessive desire and rivalry (*ahamahamikā*), the Nirukta-writers explain the name *matsara*. In the ṛk at hand it may mean "the cause of delight", or "excellent, in rivalry with the Soma juices of other sacrifices".

Having given these meanings of the words in the Bhāṣya, Sāyaṇa explains: "*uttarārdhaḥ indraparatayā vyākhyeyaḥ*" — it is proper to explain the second half as addressed to Indra.

From this, addressing Indra with "*he indra*", Indra is *asmaddattasomasahāyavān* ("having as companion the Soma given by us"), that is, the one who has as friend the Soma juice offered by the sacrificer; or *balavān*, "strong"; *sānasiḥ* — "worthy to be obtained by the sacrificers"; *pṛtanāṣāṭ amartyaś ca* — one who has the power to carry out battles and defeat the enemy armies, and who is free from the nature of death: so Indra's abundant greatness is described.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***gantu*** — root *gamḷ gatau*; *loṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; by "*eruḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-86 [?]) *u*; "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" gives *luk* for the *vikaraṇa*; the *m* of the root becomes *anusvāra*, *parasavarṇa*; *nighāta* for a *tiṅ*.
- ***vareṇyaḥ*** — root *vṛñ varaṇe*; by "*vṛñaḥ eṇyaḥ*" (Uṇ. Sū. 3-… [?]) the suffix *eṇya*; the suffix being the cause, guṇa of the *ik* of the root; *ra* follows; the first syllable is *udātta*, as in *vṛṣādi*.
- ***sahāvān*** — when *matup* comes, by "*mādhupadhāyāś ca*" (Pā. Sū. 8-2-9 [?]) the *m* becomes *v*; by "*anyeṣām api dṛśyate*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 [?]) the preceding vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā; when *indra* follows, by "*dīrghād aṭi samānapāde*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-9 [?]) *ru* for the *n*; by "*ato 'ṭi nityam*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-3 [?]) the *ā* takes nasalization.
- ***sānasiḥ*** — root *ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*; by "*sānasivarṇasi*…" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-… [?]) the suffix *asi*, the lengthening, and the end-*udātta* accent are fixed by *nipātana*.

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

- ***pṛtanāṣāṭ*** — root *saha marṣaṇe*; by "*chandasi sahaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-63 [?]) the suffix *ṇvi*; by "*ate upadhāyāḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116 [?]) *vṛddhi* of the penultimate; by "*sahes sāḍaḥ saḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-56 [?]) at the end of the word the *s* of the root becomes *ṣ*; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent. ‖ 2 ‖

**Sūkta 175, Ṛk 3**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> त्वं हि शूरः सनिता चोदयो मनुषो रथम् ।
> सहावान्दस्युमव्रतमोषः पात्रं न शोचिषा ॥ ३ ॥

> *tvaṃ hi śūraḥ sanitā codayo manuṣo ratham |*
> *sahāvān dasyum avratam oṣaḥ pātraṃ na śociṣā ‖ 3 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> त्वम् । हि । शूरः । सनिता । चोदयः । मनुषः । रथम् ।
> सहस्वान् [?] । दस्युम् । अव्रतम् । ओषः । पात्रम् । न । शोचिषा ॥ ३ ॥

> *tvam | hi | śūraḥ | sanitā | codayaḥ | manuṣaḥ | ratham |*
> *sahasvān [?] | dasyum | avratam | oṣaḥ | pātram | na | śociṣā ‖ 3 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (as read; doubtful passages marked [?])

> हे इन्द्र त्वं खलु शूरः शौर्योपेतः सनिता दातासि । अतो मनुषो मानुष्यस्य मे रथं रंहणं स्पन्दनं मनोरथं वा स्वर्गगमनसाधनं यज्ञाख्यं रथं वा चोदयः । प्रेरय । किंच त्वं सहावान् सोमसहायवान् बलवान्वा भूत्वा दस्युमुपक्षपयितारमव्रतमकर्माणमनुष्ठायिनमोषः । दह । किमिव । शोचिषा दीप्त्या ज्वालयाग्निः पात्रं न स्वाधारं पात्रविशेषमिव । योगाधिकारी सन् योनि न यजते तं दहेत्यर्थः ॥ [?]

> *he indra tvaṃ khalu śūraḥ śauryopetaḥ sanitā dātāsi | ato manuṣo mānuṣyasya me rathaṃ raṃhaṇaṃ spandanaṃ manoratham vā svargagamanasādhanaṃ yajñākhyaṃ rathaṃ vā codayaḥ | preraya | kiṃca tvaṃ sahāvān somasahāyavān balavān vā bhūtvā dasyum upakṣapayitāram avratam akarmāṇam anuṣṭhāyinam oṣaḥ | daha | kim iva | śociṣā dīptyā jvālayāgniḥ pātraṃ na svādhāraṃ pātraviśeṣam iva | yogādhikārī san yoni na yajate taṃ dahety arthaḥ ‖* [?]

*Gist:* O Indra, you are a hero and a giver; urge on the chariot of the man who sacrifices (the sacrificial "chariot" that carries him to heaven); and, strong and companioned by Soma, burn up the *dasyu*, the rite-less one, by your blaze, as fire burns a vessel.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

(*he indra* — O Indra); *śūraḥ* — the heroic; *tvaṃ hi* — you alone; *sanitā* — (to us) the giver (therefore); *manuṣaḥ* — me, a man; *ratham* — the chariot of my desire (the chariot in the form of the sacrifice that conveys to heaven); *codayaḥ* — urge on; (*kiñca tvam* — and you) *sahāvān* — endowed with the companion Soma (powerful); *dasyum* — the destroyer; *avratam* — one who has no rites and acts, and such persons; *śociṣā* — by your flame (as fire); *pātraṃ na* — as the fire burns a vessel which is its own support; *oṣaḥ* — burn.

### Printed p. 373  (PDF 393)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra, you are a hero and also our giver; urge on the chariot of my desire (the sacrifice) of me, a man, so that it may prosper; and you, mighty one (who are lord of the rites), burn the one who performs no acts of sacrifice, and the violent one, as fire burns with its flame a vessel that is its own support.

**Printed English**

You are a hero, a benefactor, accelerate the vehicle of man (that bears him to heaven); consume, mighty one, the irreligious Dasyu, as a (wooden) vessel is burnt by fire.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***sanitā — dātā*** — explaining that this word is used in the sense of "of a generous nature", Sāyaṇa explains that Indra, being a giver, should, for the sacrificer who is a man, *rathaṃ — raṃhaṇaṃ spandanaṃ manoratham vā svargagamanasādhanaṃ yajñākhyaṃ ratham vā codayaḥ* — urge on the chariot, or the movement, or the desire, or the chariot of sacrifice that is the means of going to heaven, so that the wishes of the sacrificers may be fulfilled, or that the sacrifice, the chariot that enables the sacrificers to go to heaven, may be carried to completion.

***rathaḥ*** — the word *ratha*: "*ratho raṃhater gatikarmaṇaḥ sthiratevā syād viparītasya*" [as read: [?]] — formed from the root *raṃh*, meaning "to go"; or from *sthira* (steady) with the change of letters, so that the word *ratha* comes from the opposite; and "*athavā ramaṇāmo 'smiṃs tiṣṭhatīti vā rapater vā rasater vā*" (Ni. 9-12 [?]) — "he who fights has a comfortable seat in it", and from the root *rap* or from the root *ras*: so it is explained. The Nirukta-writers —

> वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा प्रतरणः सुवीरः । गोभिः संनद्धो असि वीळयस्वास्था ता ते जयतु जेत्वानि ॥

> *vanaspate vīḍvaṅgo hi bhūyā asmatsakhā prataraṇaḥ suvīraḥ | gobhiḥ saṃnaddho asi vīḷayasvāsthātā te jayatu jetvāni ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-26 [?]) — quoting this ṛk, they have shown the form of the chariot. But since the word *ratha* is formed from the root *raṃh*, which has the sense of "going", the word is used in several places as an epithet of sons also. In the ṛk at hand, Sāyaṇa has explained the word *ratha* in two ways: as a "desire" (*manoratha*), which is of the nature of movement, and as the chariot in the form of the sacrifice, which is the means of going to heaven.

### Printed p. 374  (PDF 394)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

***sahāvān — somasahāyavān balavān vā*** — the word *sahaḥ* is read among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]). The Nirukta-writers, the word *sahāvān* —

> त्यमू षु वाजिनं देवजूतं सहावानं तरुतारं रथानाम् । अरिष्टनेमिं पृतनाजमाशुं स्वस्तये तार्क्ष्यमिहा हुवेम ॥

> *tyam ū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtaṃ sahāvānaṃ tarutāraṃ rathānām | ariṣṭanemiṃ pṛtanājam āśuṃ svastaye tārkṣyam ihā huvema ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-178-1 [?]) — has been explained as *sahasvantam* in the ṛk quoted. Durgācārya: "*sahāvānaṃ sahaḥ balaṃ tena tadvantam*" — he explained *sahas* as strength, and the word as "one who has it". Sāyaṇa here describes Indra as one who has Soma as a helper, or as one possessed of strength.

***dasyuṃ — upakṣapayitāram*** — Yāska: "*dasyur dasyateḥ kṣayārthād upadasyanty asmin rasāḥ upadāsayati iti karmāṇi*" (Ni. 7-23 [?]) — the word *dasyu*, formed from the root *dasu* meaning "to injure, destroy", is explained in the sense: "that in which the waters are dried up, the rites destroyed". Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "destroyer".

This word *dasyuṃ* is used as an epithet of the word *avratam*. For the word *avratam*, "*akarmāṇam ananuṣṭhāyinaṃ*" is the meaning given — "the one who destroys all, without performing acts of sacrifice". The command "burn" (*daha* for *oṣaḥ*) is also given for Indra here. In this connection: "*śociṣā pātraṃ na jvālayāgniḥ svādhāraṃ pātraviśeṣam iva*" — as fire, by its flame, burns the fuel that is its support, a fuel-vessel; "*yogādhikārī yo na yajate taṃ daha*" — even the man who has the qualifications for performing sacrifice, but remains inactive, without performing the sacrifice, may be burned by Indra; this is said by way of a simile.

The word *deva* is of the nature of illumination, brightness, giving (Ni. 7-15 [?]); and the meanings opposed to these are given by the word *dasyu*: destructive, full of darkness, and violent. Vṛtra and all the other *asuras* belong to the group of *dasyus*. As they restrained the water, withholding it from flowing, and hid the light, Indra, by destroying them, let the water flow and let the light come out; hence the epithet *dasyuhā* ("slayer of *dasyus*") has been used for Indra in many places.

Although the word *dasyu* is used in many places as a synonym of *rākṣasa* and the like, it is also used in some places for men who are without rites. For example —

---

### Printed p. 375  (PDF 395)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

> त्वं ह नु त्यददमायो दस्यूँ रेकः कृष्वीरवनो रार्याय ।

> *tvaṃ ha nu tyad adamāyo dasyūṃr ekaḥ kṛṣvīr avano rāryāya |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-18-3 [?]). In such ṛks, for the word *dasyūn*, "men without rites" is the meaning given. Since Indra has destroyed *dasyus* of the form of Vṛtra and other *asuras*, and *dasyus* of the form of men who perform no rites, the epithet *dasyuhā* (slayer of *dasyus*) is natural for him.

> कुवित्सस्य प्र हि व्रजं गोमन्तं दस्युहा गमत् ।

> *kuvit sasya pra hi vrajaṃ gomantaṃ dasyuhā gamat |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-45-24 [?]). In many such ṛks this epithet shows Indra's extraordinary power, and also the protection of the world that arises through the slaying of *dasyus*. And —

***ārya, dasyu*** — it is the opinion of some that these two words are conventional terms denoting two different groups of people. The historians have discussed the distinction between these two groups: that the *ārya* are Sanskrit-speaking (*saṃskṛta*) and the *dasyus* are not Sanskrit-speaking and of different colour. This matter will be explained, with examples, further on.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***sanitā*** — root *ṣaṇu dāne*; by "*dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64 [?]) *ṣa* becomes *sa* at the beginning; in the agent sense the suffix *tṛn*; by "*ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-35 [?]) the augment *iṭ*; by "*jñ-ityādir nityam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 [?]) the first syllable is *udātta*.
- ***codayaḥ*** — root *cuda preraṇe*; by "*chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6 [?]) *laṅ* in the sense of *loṭ*; by "*satyāpapāśa*…" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-25 [?]) *ṇic* in its own sense; *sip*, *śap*; because *śap* is the cause, guṇa for the *ṇic*, substitution *aya*; since *ṇic* is the cause, guṇa for the light penultimate vowel of the root; because it is in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; the *ṇic* accent remains.
- ***dasyum*** — root *dasu upakṣaye*; by "*yujimuni śuṃdhi*…" (Uṇ. Sū. 3-100 [?]) the suffix *yuc*; since it belongs to the *vṛṣādi* group, the first syllable is *udātta*; since the substitution *anādeśa* (for *yu*) is prescribed for *ukāra* *ityādi*, no *anādeśa* occurs here.
- ***avratam*** — *na vidyate vratam yasya saḥ tam*; by "*naño subhyām*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172 [?]) the final member takes *udātta* accent.
- ***oṣaḥ*** — root *uṣa dāhe*, *bhvādi*; to show the sense of *loṭ*, Vedic *laṅ*; second person singular; Vedically no augment; because it is in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*;

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

*śap* being *anudātta*, the root accent remains.

- ***śociṣā*** — root *śuca śokte*; by "*arciśucihu*…" (Uṇ. Sū. 2-… [?]) the suffix *iṣi*; the suffix accent is first-syllable *udātta*; instrumental singular. ‖ 3 ‖

**Sūkta 175, Ṛk 4**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> मुषाय सूर्यं कवे चक्रमीशान ओजसा ।
> वह शुष्णाय वधं कुत्सं वातस्याश्वैः ॥ ४ ॥

> *muṣāya sūryaṃ kave cakram īśāna ojasā |*
> *vaha śuṣṇāya vadhaṃ kutsaṃ vātasyāśvaiḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> मुषाय । सूर्यम् । कवे । चक्रम् । ईशानः । ओजसा ।
> वह । शुष्णाय । वधम् । कुत्सम् । वातस्य । अश्वैः ॥ ४ ॥

> *muṣāya | sūryam | kave | cakram | īśānaḥ | ojasā |*
> *vaha | śuṣṇāya | vadham | kutsam | vātasya | aśvaiḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (as read; doubtful passages marked [?])

> हे कवे क्रान्तदर्शिन्निन्द्र ईशानः समर्थः सन् सूर्यं सूर्यस्य ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति षष्ठ्यैकवचनस्य द्वितीयैकवचनादेशः ॥ तत्संबन्धि चक्रमेकनेमि [?] ओजसा बलेन सामर्थ्यातिशयेन मुषाय । अमुष्णाः ॥ छन्दसि शायजसीति शायजादेशः ॥ पूर्वं सूर्यरथस्य चक्रद्वयमस्ति । एकमिन्द्रो मुमुष इतीतिहासः । तथा च मन्त्रान्तरं । प्रान्यच्चक्रमवृहः सूर्यस्य कुत्सायान्यत् । ऋ. ५-२९-१० [?] । इति । किंच शुष्णाय एतन्नामकायासुराय तद्वधार्थं । द्वितीयार्थे वा चतुर्थी । शुष्णं हन्तुमित्यर्थः । कुत्सं कर्तनसाधनं वधं वज्रं वातस्य वायोरश्वैरश्वैर्वायुवेगैर्वाश्वैर्युक्तः सन् वह । अवहः । शुष्णं हन्तुं वज्रमुदारयः । यद्वा । शुष्णवधाय वज्रमवहः । तं च हत्वा तदीयैः वायुवेगैरश्वैस्तदुपलक्षितैस्तदीयैर्धनैः कुत्सं महर्षिमगमः । शुष्णासुरधनं कुत्सायादा इत्यर्थः । तथा चान्यत्र त्वं कुत्सं शुष्णहत्येष्वावित । ऋ. १-१०६-६ [?] । कुत्सायु शुष्णमशुषं । ऋ. ४-१६-१२ [?] । इत्यादीति ॥

> *he kave krāntadarśinn indra īśānaḥ samarthaḥ san sūryaṃ sūryasya ‖ supāṃ suluk iti ṣaṣṭhyaikavacanasya dvitīyaikavacanādeśaḥ ‖ tatsaṃbandhi cakram ekanemi [?] ojasā balena sāmarthyātiśayena muṣāya | amuṣṇāḥ ‖ chandasi śāyajasīti śāyajādeśaḥ ‖ pūrvaṃ sūryarathasya cakradvayam asti | ekam indro mumuṣa itītihāsaḥ | tathā ca mantrāntaraṃ | prānyac cakram avṛhaḥ sūryasya kutsāyānyat | ṛ. 5-29-10 [?] | iti | kiṃca śuṣṇāya etannāmakāyāsurāya tadvadhārthaṃ | dvitīyārthe vā caturthī | śuṣṇaṃ hantum ity arthaḥ | kutsaṃ kartanasādhanaṃ vadhaṃ vajraṃ vātasya vāyor aśvair aśvair vāyuvegair vāśvair yuktaḥ san vaha | avahaḥ | śuṣṇaṃ hantuṃ vajram udārayaḥ | yadvā | śuṣṇavadhāya vajram avahaḥ | taṃ ca hatvā tadīyaiḥ vāyuvegair aśvais tadupalakṣitais tadīyair dhanaiḥ kutsaṃ maharṣim agamaḥ | śuṣṇāsuradhanaṃ kutsāyādā ity arthaḥ | tathā cānyatra tvaṃ kutsaṃ śuṣṇahatyeṣv āvitha | ṛ. 1-106-6 [?] | kutsāyu śuṣṇam aśuṣaṃ | ṛ. 4-16-12 [?] | ity ādīti ‖* [?]

*Gist:* O Indra, you, the mighty, by your power took away the sun's one wheel (the Sun's chariot has two wheels); and, drawn by the wind-swift horses, you drove forth the cutting thunderbolt to slay Śuṣṇa and gave his wealth to the sage Kutsa.

### Printed p. 377  (PDF 397)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

(*he*) *kave* — O wise Indra; *īśānaḥ* — you who are capable; *sūryam* — of the sun; *cakram* — one wheel of the chariot; *ojasā* — by your surpassing power; *muṣāya* — have carried off; (*kiñca* — and) *śuṣṇāya* — for the sake of destroying the *asura* called Śuṣṇa; *kutsam* — the cutting instrument; *vadham* — the thunderbolt; *vātasya* — (swift) of the wind's speed; *aśvaiḥ* — joined with the horses; *vaha* — carried (taken); [or *śuṣṇāya* — for the destruction of the *asura* Śuṣṇa; *vadham* — the thunderbolt; *vaha* — you carried (to slay him); *vātasya* — equal in speed to the wind; *aśvaiḥ* — joined with the horses of that Śuṣṇa (with wealth indicated by horses); *kutsam* — the sage called Kutsa (have reached).]

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra, you, the capable one, by the surpassing power of your strength, took away one wheel of the Sun's chariot; and, holding the thunderbolt, you slew the *asura* called Śuṣṇa, and, becoming possessed of his wind-swift horses and his wealth, reached the sage Kutsa and gave him that wealth.

**Printed English**

Sage Indra, who are the lord, you have carried off by your strength one wheel of (the chariot of) the sun. Take up your bolt for the death of Shushna, and proceed with your horses, swift as the wind, to Kutsa.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***kave — krāntadarśinn indra*** — Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning of this word in this way. In some other places Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning of this word in two ways. First, citing the Śruti sentence "*yo vā anūcānās te kavayaḥ*" [as read: [?]] he says that *kavi* means a learned one who has studied the Vedas along with the Vedāṅgas; second, following the Nirukta sentence which gives *manīṣī* (Ni. 3-15 [?]), he says that the meaning "intelligent" (*medhāvin*) may be taken.

> मेधावी कविः क्रान्तदर्शनो भवति कवतेर्वा ।

> *medhāvī kaviḥ krāntadarśano bhavati kavater vā |*

(Ni. 12-13 [?]) — thus the Nirukta-writers have given the derivation of the word *kavi*. Derived from the root *kram*, it can mean "one whose vision is beyond"; or, from the root *kūṅ* (*kuṅ śabde*), "he who is worthy to be praised, a praiser": so the Nirukta derivation shows. What is the nature of a *kavi*? To know the nature and power of a *kavi*, one must know where the word *kavi* is used in the Ṛk-saṃhitā.

### Printed p. 378  (PDF 398)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

The words *ṛṣi*, *sumedhas*, *dhīra*, *rebha* may all be said to be used for the same sense, to point out whatever special nature the word *kavi* denotes. He who has an extraordinary, supernatural power to know all the activities of the times past, future and present is *dhīra*; he is *ṛṣi*; he too is *kavi*. One who has this power is worthy also of the creation of poetry (*kāvya*) in the form of praise. Hence the praisers too bear the names *kavi*, *rebha* and the like. In worldly literature and in works on poetics too, there are the words *kavi*, *kāvya*; the explanation there, it will be said further on in the context, is somewhat different from this. To know the true nature of the *kavi*, the Nirukta-writers —

> विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुञ्चते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे । वि नाकमख्यत्सविता वरेण्योऽनु प्रयाणमुषसो वि राजति ॥

> *viśvā rūpāṇi prati muñcate kaviḥ prāsāvīd bhadraṃ dvipade catuṣpade | vi nākam akhyat savitā vareṇyo 'nu prayāṇam uṣaso vi rājati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-2 [?]) — quoting this ṛk, explain what nature the word *kavi*, which is an epithet of Savitṛ, shows. Since Savitṛ illuminates all the forms of the universe, this epithet is given to Savitṛ, it is understood; that is, the power to hide, and make shine by his power, those parts that are hidden, covered, and not visible to the world's eye, and make them visible to the world. In this same sense the name *kavi* is also well known for the praiser who has the power of praise. This idea occurs in the Ṛk-saṃhitā:

> ब्रह्मा कृणोति वरुणो गातुविदं तमीमहे । व्यूर्णोति हृदा मतिं नव्यो जायतामृतं विप्तं नो अस्य रोदसी ॥

> *brahmā kṛṇoti varuṇo gātuvidaṃ tam īmahe | vyūrṇoti hṛdā matiṃ navyo jāyatām ṛtaṃ viptaṃ no asya rodasī ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-105-15 [?]) — in this ṛk, too, as in other ṛks, it is indicated: for the word *vyūrṇoti*, Sāyaṇa gives the meaning "*uccārayati*, *prakāśayati*" — "utters, reveals". The root *ūrṇuñ* (*ūrṇuñ ācchādane*) means "to cover", "to veil"; with the prefix *vi* it becomes "to uncover" — that is, the sense of removing the covering. The purport: it has the power of creation in the form of revealing a feeling hidden in the mind, and the power of showing, by revealing, a thing that is hidden: these are the special qualities of the *kavi*, or of the praiser. From this it is known that the word *kavi*, being the common quality of Savitṛ and of the praiser, is a special epithet for both. The same characteristic and the poetic character are described in the Ṛk-saṃhitā:

> समानं नीळं वृषणो वसानाः सं जग्मिरे महिषा अर्वतीभिः । ऋतस्य पदं कवयो नि पान्ति गुहा नामानि दधिरे पराणि ॥

> *samānaṃ nīḷaṃ vṛṣaṇo vasānāḥ saṃ jagmire mahiṣā arvatībhiḥ | ṛtasya padaṃ kavayo ni pānti guhā nāmāni dadhire parāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-5-2 [?]).

### Printed p. 379  (PDF 399)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

> बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं यत्प्रैरत नामधेयं दधानाः । यदेषां श्रेष्ठं यदरिप्रमासीत्प्रेणा तदेषां निहितं गुहाविः ॥

> *bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ yat praírata nāmadheyaṃ dadhānāḥ | yad eṣāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yad ariprām āsīt preṇā tad eṣāṃ nihitaṃ guhāviḥ ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-1 [?]) — in all such ṛks this idea is made evident: the *kavis*, having entered the path of *ṛta*, bear the highly secret and most excellent names in their very deep hearts; and, having revealed them, they make them known to the world: so it is described. This *kavi* is attainable by an instrument of vision and light itself.

> यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायन् तामन्वविन्दन्नृषिषु प्रविष्टाम् । तामाभृत्या व्यदधुः पुरुत्रा तां सप्त रेभा अभि सं नवन्ते ॥

> *yajñena vācaḥ padavīyam āyan tām anv avindann ṛṣiṣu praviṣṭām | tām ābhṛtyā vy adadhuḥ purutrā tāṃ sapta rebhā abhi saṃ navante ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-3 [?]). The sages, seers of things beyond the senses, obtained, by the means of sacrifice, the speech that had been hidden; afterwards, for the benefit of the people of the world, they gave them instruction. This speech that is of the nature of the universe is served by metres such as Gāyatrī; and so on: thus the identity of the creation in the form of revealing speech, and of the act in the form of sacrifice, is shown; and in some places the relation of cause and effect is also shown. The same idea is stated in the Śatapatha and other Brāhmaṇas:

> आयुरेतेजो ज्योतिः प्रविशति य एतमनु वा ब्रूते भक्षयति वा तस्य व्रतेचर्या यो सृष्ट्यै ॥ [as read; garbled: [?]]

> *āyur etejo jyotiḥ praviśati ya etam anu vā brūte bhakṣayati vā tasya vratecaryā yo sṛṣṭyai ‖* [?]

(Śa. Brā. 14-1-3-26 [?]) — here the identity of the act, preceded by the utterance of the mantra, and of new creation is stated. In the ṛk at hand it is an epithet describing the extraordinary quality of Indra, who is endowed with knowledge of what lies beyond the senses and is omniscient. Because this epithet is used in many places, it should be construed according to the respective contexts.

***īśānaḥ sūryaṃ cakraṃ ojasā muṣāya — sarvārthaḥ san sūryasya ekaṃ cakraṃ sāmarthyātiśayena amuṣṇāḥ*** — Indra, by his strength, took away one of the two wheels of the Sun's chariot: the sense is given, and it is stated that "*pūrvaṃ sūryarathasya cakradvayam asti, ekam indro mumuṣa itītihāsaḥ*" — "there were formerly two wheels of the Sun's chariot; Indra stole one": that this is known in the tradition (*itihāsa*), and he cites the ṛk:

> प्रान्यच्चक्रमवृहः सूर्यस्य कुत्सायान्यद्वरिवो यातवेऽकः ।

> *prānyac cakram avṛhaḥ sūryasya kutsāyānyad varivo yātave 'kaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-29-10 [?]).

***śuṣṇāya — etannāmakāya asurāya śuṣṇaṃ hantum*** — in order to destroy the *asura* known by the name Śuṣṇa, ***vātasya aśvaiḥ*** — joined with the horses having the speed of the wind, or

### Printed p. 380  (PDF 400)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

with the horses of Śuṣṇa — Indra, having the *kutsa* (cutting) thunderbolt, carried it. ***athavā taṃ ca hatvā tadīyair dhanaiḥ kutsaṃ maharṣim agamaḥ*** — the word *kutsa*, taken as an epithet of the thunderbolt, gives one meaning, "the instrument of cutting". In the second meaning it is explained that Indra, having destroyed Śuṣṇa, gave all the wealth of the *asura* Śuṣṇa to the great sage named Kutsa. And —

> त्वं कुत्सं शुष्णहत्येष्वाविथारन्धयोऽतिथिग्वाय शंबरम् । महान्तं चिदर्बुदं नि क्रमीः पदा सनादेव दस्युहत्याय जज्ञिषे ॥

> *tvaṃ kutsaṃ śuṣṇahatyeṣv āvitha arandhayo 'tithigvāya śambaram | mahāntaṃ cid arbudaṃ ni kramīḥ padā sanād eva dasyuhatyāya jajñiṣe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-6 [?]);

> कुत्सायु शुष्णमशुषं नि बर्हीः प्रपित्वे अह्नः कुयवं सहसा ।

> *kutsāyu śuṣṇam aśuṣaṃ ni barhīḥ prapitve ahnaḥ kuyavaṃ sahasā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16-12 [?]).

In these ṛks Sāyaṇa has quoted them to show that this meaning is stated; and he explains that the same intention is expressed in other mantras. The word *śuṣṇa* is read by Yāska among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9 [?]). And —

> नियद्वृणक्षि श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि शुष्णस्य चित्व्रन्दिनो रोरुवद्वना । प्राचीनेन मनसा बर्हणावता यदद्या चित्कृणवः कस्त्वा परि ॥

> *ni yad vṛṇakṣi śvasanasya mūrdhani śuṣṇasya cit vrandino roruvad vanā | prācīnena manasā barhaṇāvatā yad adyā cit kṛṇavaḥ kas tvā pari ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-5 [?]). In this ṛk the meaning "*śuṣṇasya śoṣayitur ādityasya*" — "of Śuṣṇa, of the dryer, i.e. of the Āditya" — is explained.

> न्याविध्यदिलीबिशस्य दृळ्हा वि शृङ्गिणमभिनच्छुष्णमिन्द्रः । यावत्तरो मघवन् यावदोजो वज्रेण शत्रुमवधीः पृतन्युम् ॥

> *ny āvidhyad ilībiśasya dṛḷhā vi śṛṅgiṇam abhinac chuṣṇam indraḥ | yāvat taro maghavan yāvad ojo vajreṇa śatrum avadhīḥ pṛtanyum ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-33-12 [?]). Here the word *śuṣṇa* is used in the sense of *śuṣṇaṃ balavantaṃ meghaṃ*, "the mighty cloud".

***kutsaṃ*** — here the commentary of Sāyaṇa shows that two kinds of meaning may be given for the word *kutsa*. First, as an epithet of the thunderbolt, "*kutsa-kartana-sādhanam*" (the instrument of cutting, being the means of cutting); second, "*kutsaṃ kutsanāmānam ṛṣim*" — he explains it as "the sage called Kutsa". If it is explained as "sage", it is the praise of Indra that he killed the *asura* Śuṣṇa and helped Kutsa.

The close connection of Kutsa and of Indra is learned from the descriptions in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. The epithet *ārjuneya* for Kutsa occurs in many places. For the word *ārjuneya* it may be "son of the woman Arjunī". Or "*arjuna* is a name of Indra (*arjuna itīndrasya nāma*), *tasya putraḥ*": since Kutsa is Indra's son, the epithet *ārjuneya* is natural: thus another meaning may be given. To support that Indra has the name *Arjuna*, Sāyaṇa, in some places,

### Printed p. 381  (PDF 401)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

…quotes the Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā mantra:

> एतद्वा इन्द्रस्य गुह्यं नाम यदर्जुनः ।

> *etad vā indrasya guhyaṃ nāma yad arjunaḥ |*

and, further —

> अहं कुत्समार्जुनेयं न्यृंजेऽहं कविरुशना पश्यता मा ।

> *ahaṃ kutsam ārjuneyaṃ nyṛṃje 'haṃ kavir uśanā paśyatā mā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-1 [?]);

> दासं यच्छुष्णं कुयवं न्यस्मा अरन्धय आर्जुनेयाय शिक्षन् ।

> *dāsaṃ yac chuṣṇaṃ kuyavaṃ ny asmā arandhaya ārjuneyāya śikṣan |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-2 [?]);

> वहत्कुत्समार्जुनेयं शतक्रतुः त्सरद्गन्धर्वमस्तृतम् ।

> *vahat kutsam ārjuneyaṃ śatakratuḥ tsarad gandharvam astṛtam |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-1-11 [?]) —

in such ṛks, for the words *ārjuneya* and the like, Sāyaṇa too has explained "*arjunyāḥ putraṃ kutsaṃ*" — "Kutsa, the son of Arjunī": that is, Kutsa, the son of the woman Arjunī. Since it is said in other Śrutis that the words *Arjuna*, *Arjunī* are connected with Indra, the two kinds of explanation above may be said to give one and the same meaning. For example —

> फल्गुनीष्वग्नी आदधीत । एता वा इन्द्रनक्षत्रं यत्फल्गुन्योऽर्जुनस्य प्रतिनाम्न्योऽर्जुनो ह वै नामेन्द्रो यदस्य गुह्यं नामार्जुन्यो वै नाम्नैतास्ता एतेकत्परोक्षमाचक्षते फल्गुन्य इति को हेतस्यार्हति गुह्यं नाम ………………… ।

> *phalgunīṣv agnī ādadhīta | etā vā indranakṣatraṃ yat phalgunyo 'rjunasya pratināmnyo 'rjuno ha vai nāmendro yad asya guhyaṃ nāmārjunyo vai nāmnaitās tā etekat parokṣam ācakṣate phalgunya iti ko hetasyārhati guhyaṃ nāma ………………… |*

(Śa. Brā. 2-1-2-11 [?]);

> इन्द्रो भवति यच्छ क्षत्रियो यदु च यजमानस्तस्मादाहारिष्ठोऽर्जुन इति ।

> *indro bhavati yac cha kṣatriyo yad u ca yajamānas tasmād āhāriṣṭho 'rjuna iti |*

(Śa. Brā. 5-4-1-2 [?]).

The *Phalgunī* are the lunar mansions of Indra; they are also associated with his name. Indra has the name *Arjuna*, and the *Phalgunīs* are also called *Arjunīs*; since this is said in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and in other places, Kutsa may be called by two names, "son of Indra" and "son of Ārjunī". In many places of the Ṛk-saṃhitā it is shown that Kutsa conquered his enemies with the help of Indra; thus the relation of Indra and Kutsa is shown.

> त्वं शुष्णं वृजने पृक्ष आणौ यूने कुत्साय द्युमते सचाहन् ।

> *tvaṃ śuṣṇaṃ vṛjane pṛkṣa āṇau yūne kutsāya dyumate sacāhan |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-63-3 [?]);

> कुत्साय यत्र पुरुहूत वन्वञ्छुष्णमनन्तैः परियासि वध्नैः ।

> *kutsāya yatra puruhūta vanvañ chuṣṇam anantaiḥ pariyāsi vadhnaiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-121-9 [?]) —

in such ṛks, as well as in many other places, the description is that Indra killed Śuṣṇa to help Kutsa. And again —

### Printed p. 382  (PDF 402)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

> अहं पितेव वेतसूनभिष्टये तुग्रं कुत्साय स्मदिभं च रन्धयम् ।

> *ahaṃ piteva vetasūn abhiṣṭaye tugraṃ kutsāya smadibhaṃ ca randhayam |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-49-4 [?]) — here Indra himself says, "For Kutsa I subdued Vetasu, Tugra, Smadibha and others, all the enemies, and helped my friend." And —

> त्वमस्मै कुत्समतिथिग्वमायुं महे राज्ञे यूने अरन्धनायः ।

> *tvam asmai kutsam atithigvam āyuṃ mahe rājñe yūne arandhanāyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-53-10 [?]);

> य आयुं कुत्समतिथिग्वमर्दयो वावृधानो दिवेदिवे ।

> *ya āyuṃ kutsam atithigvam ardayo vāvṛdhāno dive-dive |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-53-2 [?]) — in such ṛks Indra is also described as having subdued Kutsa and others.

***vadhaṃ*** — the Nirukta-writers have read *vadha* among the names of strength. When this word is used in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, it is often an epithet of the thunderbolt, which is the instrument that is used with strength and is the means of killing. For example,

> स्वयं सो अस्मदा निदो वधैरजेत दुर्मतिम् ।

> *svayaṃ so asmad ā nido vadhair ajeta durmatim |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-129-6 [?]) — in such ṛks (1-129-6; 2-20-2; 6-20-4 and others [?]) the words *vadhaiḥ*, *vadham* are used in the sense of weapons such as the thunderbolt, the instruments of killing. For this instrument of killing it is not a rule that it must be Indra's thunderbolt; any weapon that is used with strength may be a synonym of this. For example —

> अरे गोहा नृहा वधो वो अस्तु सुम्नेभिरस्मे वसवो नमध्वम् ।

> *are gohā nṛhā vadho vo astu sumnebhir asme vasavo namadhvam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-17 [?]) — here, addressing the Maruts, a prayer is made that their weapon may not harm the sacrificers. In the ṛk at hand it means Indra's thunderbolt.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***muṣāya*** — root *muṣa steye*, *kryādi*; *loṭ*, second person singular, *sip*; *hi* substituted for it; by "*chandasi śāyajapi*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-84 [?]) the substitution *śāyac* for the *vikaraṇa*; because it is *sārvadhātuka*… "*sārvadhātukam apit*" (Pā. Sū. 1-2-4 [?]), being *jit*, the light-vowel guṇa does not occur; because it is in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; the suffix is *cit*, so by "*cita*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 [?]) the end syllable is *udātta*.
- ***kave*** — root *ku śabde*; by "*ajiriśiḥ*" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-… [?]) the suffix *i*; making that the cause, *guṇa*, *avādeśa* (*av*); vocative singular; the vocative (*āmantrita*) takes *nighāta* accent.

### Printed p. 383  (PDF 403)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

- ***īśānaḥ*** — root *īśa aiśvarye*; in the sense of *laṭ*, the substitution *śānac*; since the *ṅit*-less *śānac* takes the accent on the suffix, it is *anudātta*, so the root accent remains.
- ***vaha*** — root *vaha prāpaṇe*; by *vyatyaya* *loṭ* for *laṅ*; second person singular; because it is in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; *śap* being *anudātta*, the root accent remains.
- ***sūryam*** — root *ṣū gatau*; by "*rājasūyasūrya*…" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-114 [?]) the suffix *kyap* is formed by *nipātana*; by the statement "*supāṃ suluk*"… "*supo bhavanti*" the genitive singular receives the substitution of the accusative singular.
- ***vadham*** — root *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; by "*hanaś ca vadhaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-3-76 [?]) the suffix *ap* in the sense of action; with it, the substitution *vadha*, with the accent *anta-udātta*; by "*ato lopaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 [?]) the *a* is dropped; by "*anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-161 [?]) the suffix *ap* takes the *udātta* accent. ‖ 4 ‖

**Sūkta 175, Ṛk 5**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> शुष्मिन्तमो हि ते मदो द्युम्निन्तम उत क्रतुः ।
> वृत्रघ्ना वरिवोविदा मंसीष्ठा अश्वसातमः ॥ ५ ॥

> *śuṣmintamo hi te mado dyumnintama uta kratuḥ |*
> *vṛtraghnā varivovidā maṃsīṣṭhā aśvasātamaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> शुष्मिन्ऽतमः । हि । ते । मदः । द्युम्निन्ऽतमः । उत । क्रतुः ।
> वृत्रऽघ्ना । वरिवःऽविदा । मंसीष्ठाः । अश्वऽसातमः ॥ ५ ॥

> *śuṣmin-tamaḥ | hi | te | madaḥ | dyumnin-tamaḥ | uta | kratuḥ |*
> *vṛtra-ghnā | varivaḥ-vidā | maṃsīṣṭhāḥ | aśva-sātamaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (as read; doubtful passages marked [?])

> हे इन्द्र ते तव मदः सोमपानजनितः शुष्मिन्तमो बलवत्तमः । उताषि च ते क्रतुः कर्म व्यापारोऽस्मदर्थो द्युम्निन्तमोऽतिशयेनान्नवान् यशोवान्वा ॥ उभयत्रायस्मयोदीनि छन्दसीति भसंज्ञायो बाधितत्वान्न लोपः [?] ॥ हे इन्द्र अश्वसातमोऽश्वोपलक्षितबहुधनदास्त्वं वृत्रघ्ना वृत्रघातिनौ वरिवोविदा धनस्य वा परिचरणस्य वा वेदयितारौ लंभयितारौ तव मदक्रतू मंसीष्ठाः । अनुज्ञातवानसि । शत्रुघातिनौ धनदातारौ च स्यातामित्यनुग्रहमकरोरित्यर्थः ॥

> *he indra te tava madaḥ somapānajanitaḥ śuṣmintamo balavattamaḥ | utāpi ca te kratuḥ karma vyāpāro 'smadartho dyumnintamo 'tiśayenānnavān yaśovān vā ‖ ubhayatrāyasmayodīni chandasīti bhasaṃjñāyo bādhitatvān na lopaḥ [?] ‖ he indra aśvasātamo 'śvopalakṣitabahudhanadās tvaṃ vṛtraghnā vṛtraghātinau varivovidā dhanasya vā paricaraṇasya vā vedayitārau laṃbhayitārau tava madakratū maṃsīṣṭhāḥ | anujñātavān asi | śatrughātinau dhanadātārau ca syātām ity anugraham akaror ity arthaḥ ‖* [?]

*Gist:* O Indra, your exhilaration (from Soma) is the most mighty, and your action for us the most abundant in renown; you, giver of wealth in horses, have approved that these two, your exhilaration and your action, be slayers of enemies and givers of wealth.

### Printed p. 384  (PDF 404)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

(*he indra* — O Indra); *te* — your; *madaḥ* — (Soma-drinking-produced) exhilaration; *śuṣmintamaḥ* — the most strong; *uta* — and; (*te* — your) *kratuḥ* — (for us) the act, or activity; *dyumnintamaḥ* — the most abundant (in strength); (*he indra* — O Indra); *aśvasātamaḥ* — you, the giver of many riches indicated by horses; (your exhilaration and your acts) *vṛtraghnā* — are such as to slay Vṛtra (enemies); *varivovidā* — such as bring wealth to us (to be); *maṃsīṣṭhāḥ* — you have given permission.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra, your exhilaration, produced by drinking the Soma juice, is very great, and your acts, which are for our sake, are exceedingly beneficial. O Indra, may this exhilaration of yours and these acts be the powers that kill enemies and bestow riches; by you they have been favoured.

**Printed English**

Your inebriety is most intense; nevertheless, Your acts (for our good) are most beneficent. You desire, bountiful giver of horses, that (both your inebriety and your beneficence should be the means of) destroying enemies and distributing riches.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Addressing Indra, it is said that the exhilaration that arises in Indra from drinking Soma is more abundant than that of other exhilarating things, as described in the sentence ***madaḥ śuṣmintamaḥ balavattamaḥ***.

***kratuḥ — karma*** — Yāska explains that the word *kratu* means "act or wisdom" (*karma vā prajñā vā*) (Ni. 2-28 [?]). And in the Ṛk-saṃhitā —

> यो जात एव प्रथमो मनस्वान्देवो देवान्क्रतुना पर्यभूषत् । यस्य शुष्माद्रोदसी अभ्यसेतां नृम्णस्य महा स जनास इन्द्रः ॥

> *yo jāta eva prathamo manasvān devo devān kratunā paryabhūṣat | yasya śuṣmād rodasī abhyasetāṃ nṛmṇasya mahnā sa janāsa indraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-12-1 [?]) — quoting this ṛk, the Nirukta-writers (Ni. 10-10 [?]) have shown the special meaning of the word *kratu*. Although the meaning "act" is commonly given for the word *kratu*, it is learned from the use of the word in several places that this word has a special excellence in being greatly distinctive in the act; and that its chief meaning is "resolve" (*saṅkalpa*), which impels an act. This meaning is learned from the ṛk quoted below.

---

### Printed p. 385  (PDF 405)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; signature mark "XIII 25" at foot.)*

> सुप्रवाचनं तव वीर वीर्यं यदेकेन क्रतुना विन्दसे वसु । जातूष्ठिरस्य प्र वयः सहस्वतो या चकर्थ सेन्द्र विश्वास्युक्थ्यः ॥

> *supravācanaṃ tava vīra vīryaṃ yad ekena kratunā vindase vasu | jātūṣṭhirasya pra vayaḥ sahasvato yā cakartha sendra viśvāsy ukthyaḥ ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-13-11 [?]). In this ṛk, for the word *kratunā* Sāyaṇa has explained "*karmaṇā*". It is proper here to say "*saṅkalpa*" (resolve) rather than "action". Explaining this very example, the scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit-English Dictionary, has explained *ekena karmaṇā* as "Through the mere will" (*kevala saṅkalpamātreṇa*). This is the natural meaning in this context; for here the prowess of Indra is described, and it is more natural to say that Indra "destroyed enemies by mere will" than that he destroyed them by a single act.

Whenever the word *kratu* is used as a synonym of *karman*, this word shows the resolve that is the basis of the act and the purpose directed to the act: it points out the spiritual existence of man, and the same purpose. For example —

> त्वं सोम क्रतुभिः सुक्रतुर्भूस्त्वं दक्षैः सुदक्षो विश्ववेदाः । त्वं वृषा वृषत्वेभिर्महित्वा द्युम्नेभिर्द्युम्न्यभवो नृचक्षाः ॥

> *tvaṃ soma kratubhiḥ sukratur bhūs tvaṃ dakṣaiḥ sudakṣo viśvavedāḥ | tvaṃ vṛṣā vṛṣatvebhir mahitvā dyumnebhir dyumny abhavo nṛcakṣāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-2 [?]) — in this ṛk the two words *kratu* and *dakṣa* describe the extraordinary qualities of the god Soma: Soma is addressed as one endowed with the highest knowledge. Likewise —

> ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्यानाः स्वेन युक्तासः क्रतुना वहन्ति । इन्द्रवायू वीरवाहं रथं वामीशानयोरभि पृक्षः सचन्ते ॥

> *te satyena manasā dīdhyānāḥ svena yuktāsaḥ kratunā vahanti | indravāyū vīravāhaṃ rathaṃ vām īśānayor abhi pṛkṣaḥ sacante ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-90-5 [?]) — here, by the word *kratunā*, the knowledge and the resolve that are the root of human activity, of the nature of sacrifice, are indicated. Since all worldly activity is of the nature of sacrifice, the sacrifice that is the root of this universal and also of individual acts is the *saṅkalpa* of man. The individuality of man must be complete with this resolve and purpose. Therefore man is described as "*kratumaya*" (made of resolve). The Upaniṣads and other texts describe this same point thus:

> सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत । अथ खलु क्रतुमयः पुरुषो यथाक्रतुरस्मिंल्लोके पुरुषो भवति तथेतः प्रेत्य भवति स क्रतुं कुर्वीत ।

> *sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma tajjalān iti śānta upāsīta | atha khalu kratumayaḥ puruṣo yathākraturasmiṃl loke puruṣo bhavati tathetaḥ pretya bhavati sa kratuṃ kurvīta |*

(Chā. Up. 3-14-1 [?]).

### Printed p. 386  (PDF 406)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

— the Upaniṣad says that the man is made of resolve (*kratumaya*). Explaining here what *kratu* is, the teacher Śaṅkara has spoken the following in his commentary:

> क्रतुं कुर्वीत क्रतुर्निश्चयोऽध्यवसाय एवमेव नान्यथेत्यविचलः प्रत्ययस्तं क्रतुं कुर्वीतोपासीतेत्यनेन व्यवहितेन संबन्धः । किं पुनः क्रतुकरणेन कर्तव्यं प्रयोजनं । कथं वा क्रतुः कर्तव्यः । क्रतुकरणं चाभिप्रेतार्थसिद्धिसाधनं कथं ? इत्यस्यार्थस्य प्रतिपादनार्थमथेत्यादि ग्रन्थः । ………… यस्मात् क्रतुमयः क्रतुप्रायोऽध्यवसायात्मकः पुरुषो जीवः । यथाक्रतुर्यादृशः क्रतुः अस्य सोऽयं यथाक्रतुर्यथाध्यवसायः यादृङ्निश्चयः अस्मिन्निह पुरुषो भवति तथेतोऽस्माद्देहात् प्रेत्य मृत्वा भवति । क्रतुनानुरूपफलात्मको भवतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *kratuṃ kurvīta kratur niścayo 'dhyavasāya evam eva nānyathety avicalaḥ pratyayas taṃ kratuṃ kurvītopāsītety anena vyavahitena saṃbandhaḥ | kiṃ punaḥ kratukaraṇena kartavyaṃ prayojanaṃ | kathaṃ vā kratuḥ kartavyaḥ | kratukaraṇaṃ cābhipretārthasiddhisādhanaṃ kathaṃ ? ity asyārthasya pratipādanārtham athety ādi granthaḥ | ………… yasmāt kratumayaḥ kratuprāyo 'dhyavasāyātmakaḥ puruṣo jīvaḥ | yathākratur yādṛśaḥ kratuḥ asya so 'yaṃ yathākratur yathādhyavasāyaḥ yādṛṅ niścayaḥ asminn iha puruṣo bhavati tathetо 'smād dehāt pretya mṛtvā bhavati | kratunānurūpaphalātmako bhavatīty arthaḥ ‖* [as read; dots in the print: [?]]

(Śāṅkarabhāṣya on Chā. Up. 3-14-1).

*Kratu* means firm resolve (*niścaya*), a mind's resolution (*manaḥsaṅkalpa*) and unwavering faith (*śraddhā*). Thus the worship (*upāsanā*) of the *kratu*, which is of the nature of resolve and is full of faith, ought to be done by man without fail; whether in this world or, after the dissolution of the earthly body, in the next, the existence of man follows the nature of his *kratu*. And the worship of *kratu* has its fruit; if there is no worship of *kratu*, the highest fruit is not obtained: so Śaṅkara's commentary explains.

Discussing here whether the word *kratu* means "resolve" or "purpose" (*dhyeya*), Edgerton, an English scholar, quotes the sentence of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and the passage cited above, and then explains the meaning of the word *kratu* thus —

> The word क्रतु is not easy to define. Eggeling translates it "understanding" but with an alternative "will; purpose" which is more in accord with the Hindu commentator on the passage who says that क्रतु means निश्चय, अध्यवसाय, i.e, "fixed determination." It seems to mean man's mental costitution as a whole, the "total frame of mind," but with a strong flavourof will, Conscious purpose, or determination………………Man's क्रतु therefore would be his mental make up in general, but particularly any fixed determination he may entertain with regard to his future life. And his क्रतु at the moment of death decides his destiny after death. (Annals of Bhandarkar Institute. Vol. VIII. p. 223)

> *The word kratu is not easy to define. Eggeling translates it "understanding" but with an alternative "will; purpose" which is more in accord with the Hindu commentator on the passage who says that kratu means niścaya, adhyavasāya, i.e, "fixed determination." It seems to mean man 's mental costitution as a whole, the "total frame of mind," but with a strong flavourof will, Conscious purpose, or determination………………Man 's kratu therefore would be his mental make up in general, but particularly any fixed determination he may entertain with regard to his future life. And his kratu at the moment of death decides his destiny after death. (Annals of Bhandarkar Institute. Vol. VIII. p. 223)*

[As printed: "costitution", "flavourof" [sic].]

The gist: both in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (10-6-3-1 [?]) and in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (3-14-1), for the word *kratu* the translator Eggeling first says "knowledge" (*jñāna*), and then "resolve",

---

### Printed p. 387  (PDF 407)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

…and the meaning of the synonym *dhyeya* ("object of meditation") is also given. On the whole, he says, in this word the meaning is "a mental resolve (*manaḥsaṅkalpa*) that determines the abiding states of man".

In many parts of the Ṛk-saṃhitā, for this word, the meaning is "sacrifice" (*yajña*) also; but with the same purport it suggests the sacrifice that is of the nature of resolve (*saṅkalpātmaka*). For example —

> साकं हि शुचिना शुचिः प्रशास्ता क्रतुनाजनि । विद्वाँ अस्य व्रता ध्रुवा वया इवानु रोहते ॥

> *sākaṃ hi śucinā śuciḥ praśāstā kratunājani | vidvāṃ asya vratā dhruvā vayā ivānu rohate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-5-4 [?]) —

in all such ṛks this idea becomes plain. Since the existence of man and his future states of becoming rest upon this action that is of the form of *kratu*, a warning is given to men on this matter, step by step, in the Upaniṣads and elsewhere.

> ॐ क्रतो स्मर कृतं स्मर क्रतो स्मर कृतं स्मर ।

> *oṃ krato smara kṛtaṃ smara krato smara kṛtaṃ smara |*

(Īśā. 17) — thus in the Īśā and the Bṛhadāraṇyaka and other Upaniṣads (Bṛ. Up. 5-15-1 [?]), the Self, of the nature of resolve, is addressed and instructed. For the word *krato*, Śaṅkarācārya has given the meaning "O one of the nature of resolve". But in the Aitareya Upaniṣad, in explaining the spiritual (*adhyātma*) nature —

> संज्ञानमाज्ञानं विज्ञानं प्रज्ञानं …………स्मृतिः संकल्पः क्रतुः ।

> *saṃjñānam ājñānaṃ vijñānaṃ prajñānaṃ ………… smṛtiḥ saṃkalpaḥ kratuḥ |*

(Ai. Up. 3-2 [?]) — *saṅkalpa* and *kratu* are stated as separate qualities of the Self.

In this way, the word is used not only where the spiritual qualities are shown, but also where the physical acts of man are shown. For example —

> न हि नु यादधीमसीन्द्रं को वीर्या परः । तस्मिन्नृम्णमुत क्रतुं देवा ओजांसि सं दधुरर्चन्ननु स्वराज्यम् ॥

> *na hi nu yād adhīmasīndraṃ ko vīryā paraḥ | tasmin nṛmṇam uta kratuṃ devā ojāṃsi saṃ dadhur arcann anu svarājyam ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-15 [?]) —

in such ṛks the word *kratu* means "heroic action"; and

> यस्याजस्रं शवसा मानमुक्थं परिभुजद्रोदसी विश्वतः सीम् । स सारिशत्क्रतुभिर्मन्दसानो मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥

> *yasyājasraṃ śavasā mānam uktham paribhuj rodasī viśvataḥ sīm | sa sāriśat kratubhir mandasāno marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-14 [?]) — in this and other ṛks it also means "sacrificial act". So also in the senses of power, wealth, greatness and the like this word is used.

### Printed p. 388  (PDF 408)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

Here the function of this word — ***asmadarthaḥ*** — is for us, the sacrificers: the act performed by Indra for us. ***dyumnintamaḥ — atiśayena annavān yaśovān vā*** — the meaning is explained that it is for the sake of giving us abundant food or fame. Yāska —

> शतं ते शिप्रिन्नूतयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु । जहि वधर्नुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे द्युम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ॥

> *śataṃ te śiprinn ūtayaḥ sudāse sahasraṃ śaṃsā uta rātir astu | jahi vadhar nuṣo martyasyāsme dyumnam adhi ratnaṃ ca dhehi ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-25-3 [?]) — quoting this ṛk, he explains that the word *dyumna* is "*dyotater yaśo vā annaṃ vā kāntiyinda belagisu*" — from the root *dyut*, meaning "to shine": the word *dyumna* ("*dyu*-") is explained as "fame" or "food".

***aśvasātamaḥ — aśvopalakṣitabahudhanadāḥ*** — it is explained that Indra graciously bestows abundant wealth, including horses.

***varivovidā — dhanasya vā paricaraṇasya vā vedayitārau laṃbhayitārau*** — the word *varivaḥ* is read among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-… [?]). Sāyaṇa says that Indra's exhilaration and his action, in the sense of a historical meaning (*aitihāsika*), restrain the *asura* Vṛtra, and, in that sense, cause rain to arise by cleaving the cloud; he explains that in respect of us, the sacrificers, who perform the sacrifice for the sake of giving things like wealth and restraining enemies, ***tau śatrughātinau dhanadātārau ca syātām ity anugraham akaroḥ*** — Indra graciously grants that these two, the exhilaration and the action, may be destroyers of enemies and givers of wealth.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***śuṣmintamaḥ*** — *śuṣmaṃ balam asya asti iti śuṣmī*; by "*ata ini-ṭhanau*" (Pā. Sū. 5-2-115 [?]) in the possessive sense the suffix *ini*; to it, in the sense of excess, the suffix *tamap*; by "*ayaḥśmayādīni chandasi*" (Pā. Sū. 1-4-20 [?]) the *bha* designation applies to the one preceding *tamap*; therefore no dropping occurs, because the designation *pada* is the cause; since *tamap* is *pit*, it is *anudātta*; the suffix accent of *ini* remains. The same operations occur in *dyumnintamaḥ*.
- ***madaḥ*** — root *mada tṛptiyoge*; by "*madoʼnupasarge*" (Pā. Sū. 3-3-67 [?]) the suffix *ap*; being *pit*, it is *anudātta*, so the root accent remains.
- ***vṛtraghnā*** — root *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; the suffix *kvip*; Vedically, by the *bha* designation, the dropping of the *a* of the root; by "*supāṃ suluk*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) the substitution *ā* for the dual; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent.

> *yathā pūrvebhyo jaritṛbhya indra maya ivāpo na tṛṣyate babhūtha |*

> *yathā | pūrvebhyaḥ | jaritṛ-bhyaḥ | indra | mayaḥ-iva | āpaḥ | na | tṛṣyate | babhūtha |*
> *tām | anu | tvā | ni-vidam | johavīmi | vidyāma | iṣam | vṛjanam | jīra-dānum ‖ 6 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (as read; doubtful passages marked [?])

> हे इन्द्र पूर्वेभ्यो जरितृभ्यः पुरातनेभ्यो गरितृभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यो मयु [?] इव बभूथ । मयः सुखं । सुखस्वरूपमिवाभवः । तद्वत् स्तोतृभ्योऽस्मभ्यं सुखो भव । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । तृष्यते आपो न तृषार्तस्योदकानि यथा सुखकराणीति तद्वत् । तस्मात्तां निविदं स्वप्रसिद्धां स्तुतिं त्वा तुभ्यमनु जोहवीमि । पुनः पुनः करोमि । यद्वा । तां निविदमनु ॥ तृतीयार्थे । पा. १-४-८५ [?] । इत्येनोः कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वम् ॥ तया स्तुत्या त्वां जोहवीमि । पुनः पुनराह्वयामि । विद्यामेति व्याख्यातम् ॥

> *he indra pūrvebhyo jaritṛbhyaḥ purātanebhyo garitṛbhyaḥ stotṛbhyaḥ stotṛbhyo mayu [?] iva babhūtha | mayaḥ sukhaṃ | sukhasvarūpam ivābhavaḥ | tadvat stotṛbhyo 'smabhyaṃ sukho bhava | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | tṛṣyate āpo na tṛṣārtasyodakāni yathā sukhakarāṇīti tadvat | tasmāt tāṃ nividaṃ svaprasiddhāṃ stutiṃ tvā tubhyam anu johavīmi | punaḥ punaḥ karomi | yadvā | tāṃ nividam anu ‖ tṛtīyārthe | pā. 1-4-85 [?] | ity enoḥ karmapravacanīyatvam ‖ tayā stutyā tvāṃ johavīmi | punaḥ punar āhvayāmi | vidyāmeti vyākhyātam ‖*

*Gist:* O Indra, as you were happiness itself to the ancient praisers, like water to the thirsty, so be to us; by that same well-known praise (*nivid*) I call on you again and again; that we may obtain food, strength and long life.

### Printed p. 390  (PDF 410)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

(*he*) *indra* — O Indra; *pūrvebhyaḥ* — to the ancient; *jaritṛbhyaḥ* — praisers; *tṛṣyate* — to the thirsty; *āpaḥ na* — as waters are the cause of satisfaction; *mayaḥ iva* — as of the nature of happiness; *yathā* — as; *babhūtha* — you were (so to us also you be happy-natured); (therefore) *tām* — that well-known; *nividam anu* — following the praise (of yours); *tvā* — you; *johavīmi* — I repeatedly invoke; *iṣam* — food; *vṛjanam* — strength; *jīradānum* — long life; *vidyāma* — may we obtain (by your grace).

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra, as you were happiness-giving to the ancient praisers, as waters give satisfaction to the thirsty, so be to us also happiness-giving; I praise you again and again with those well-known words of praise; bestow on us food, strength and long life.

**Printed English**

Inasmuch, Indra, as you have been the-(giver of) happiness to your ancient encomiasts, like water to one who is thirsty, therefore I constantly repeat this your praise, that I may thence obtain food, strength, and long life. [As printed: "the-(giver of)".]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Describing the delight that Indra gives to praisers, and likening the satisfaction arising from that delight to the satisfaction obtained by the thirsty from drinking water, the sage-seer of this sūkta also resolves to praise, with *nivid* mantras, the Indra who gives such satisfaction, as the earlier praisers praised.

***nividaṃ johavīmi — nivid*** mantras: it is resolved that "I offer *nivid* mantras". Earlier, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-2 [?], in describing the special matters of that ṛk, by the mantra "*sa pūrvayā nividā*" the greatness of the *nivid* mantras, which was indicated there, was explained. (Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Part 8 [?], pp. 74–76.) But that mantra was addressed to Agni, and the *nivid* mantras expressly indicated there being Agni's, only the mantras whose deity is Agni were described in that context. In the ṛk in hand, as it is addressed to Indra, the influence and the applications of the *nivid* mantras are described in the manner suited to this context.

Mantras which describe the extraordinary qualities of a deity, or of a group of deities, and invoke them, are well known by the name *nivid* mantras. The Bṛhaddevatā, pointing out this very fact —

> कर्मैव तावत्सवित्र्यां निविदि स्तौति कर्मणा । यद्धेनुः सप्त्यै नड्वाहौ वोळ्हा दोग्ध्र्याशुरेव वा ॥

> *karmaiva tāvat savitryāṃ nividi stauti karmaṇā | yad dhenuḥ saptyai naḍvāhau voḷhā dogdhry āśur eva vā ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Bṛhaddevatā 3-30 [?]) — from *dogdhrī* ("milking") the cow is meant, from *āśu* ("swift") the horse, from *voḷhā* ("carrying the load") the ox: so their special qualities are to be known by these epithets; by the *nivid* mantras the individual qualities of the respective deities are to be understood, from the descriptions of their respective acts. For example,

> अभि त्वा देव सवितरीशानं वार्याणाम् । सदावन्भागमीमहे ॥

> *abhi tvā deva savitar īśānaṃ vāryāṇām | sadāvan bhāgam īmahe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3 [?]) — in this ṛk, the *nivid* mantras, addressed to the deity Savitṛ, show the speciality of Savitṛ by describing his extraordinary acts. The relation of cause and effect between the greatness of the *nivid* mantras and the creation of the world, and between those great mantras, is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows:

> प्रजापतिर्वा इदमेक एवाग्र आस सोऽकामयत प्रजायेय भूयान्स्यामिति स तपोऽतप्यत स वाचमयच्छत्संवत्सरस्य परस्ताद्द्वाऽहरत्ताद्वादशकृत्वो द्वादशपदा वा एषा निविदेतां वाव तां निविदं व्याहरत्तां सर्वाणि भूतान्यसृज्यन्त ।

> *prajāpatir vā idam eka evāgra āsa so 'kāmayata prajāyeya bhūyān syām iti sa tapo 'tapyata sa vācam ayacchat saṃvatsarasya parastād dvā 'harat tād dvādaśakṛtvo dvādaśapadā vā eṣā nivid etāṃ vāva tāṃ nividaṃ vyāharat tāṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny asṛjyanta |* [as read; garbled: [?]]

(Ai. Brā. 10-1 [?]). In the beginning Prajāpati was alone; he desired to create progeny and to become many; and, for a year, observing silence, he practised austerity. Afterwards, uttering the *nivid* mantras of twelve great sentences twelve times, he created all beings in the world: so the effect of these mantras is stated; and, further, the speciality of these mantras at the time of the rites and the order of their application is explained thus —

> गर्भा वा एते उक्थानां यन्निविदस्तद्यत्प्रातःसवने धीयन्ते तस्मात्पराञ्चो गर्भाः पराञ्चः संभवन्ति । यन्मध्यतो मध्यंदिने धीयन्ते तस्मान्मध्ये गर्भा धृताः । यदन्ततस्तृतीयसवने धीयन्ते तस्मादमुतोऽर्वाञ्चो गर्भाः प्रजायन्ते प्रजात्यै । प्रजायते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद । पेशा वा एते उक्थानां यन्निविदस्तद्यत्पुरस्तादुक्थानां प्रातःसवने धीयन्ते यथैव प्रवणयते पेशः कुर्यात्तादृक्तद्यन्मध्यतो मध्यंदिने धीयन्ते यथैव मध्यतः पेशः कुर्यात्तादृक्तद्यदन्ततस्तृतीयसवने धीयन्ते यथैवावप्रजनतः पेशः कुर्यात्तादृक्तत् । सर्वतो यज्ञस्य पेशसा शोभते य एवं वेद ।

> *garbhā vā ete ukthānāṃ yan nividas tad yat prātaḥsavane dhīyante tasmāt parāñco garbhāḥ parāñcaḥ saṃbhavanti | yan madhyato madhyaṃdine dhīyante tasmān madhye garbhā dhṛtāḥ | yad antatas tṛtīyasavane dhīyante tasmād amuto 'rvāñco garbhāḥ prajāyante prajātyai | prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda | peśā vā ete ukthānāṃ yan nividas tad yat purastād ukthānāṃ prātaḥsavane dhīyante yathaiva pravaṇayate peśaḥ kuryāt tādṛk tad yan madhyato madhyaṃdine dhīyante yathaiva madhyataḥ peśaḥ kuryāt tādṛk tad yad antatas tṛtīyasavane dhīyante yathaivāvaprajanataḥ peśaḥ kuryāt tādṛk tat | sarvato yajñasya peśasā śobhate ya evaṃ veda |* [as read; the print breaks off at the foot of the page and resumes on p. 392: [?]]

### Printed p. 392  (PDF 412)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

(Ai. Brā. 11-10 [?]). The *nivid* mantras are in the form of an embryo for the *ukthas*: that is, those recited at the morning pressing stand first, in the front, to the *ukthas*; therefore the embryos too are born with the face turned away (*parāṅmukha*). At the midday pressing these mantras are recited in the midday; hence the embryos are held in the middle. At the time of the third pressing the *nivid* mantras are recited in the latter part; hence the embryo that is formed gives birth to the child with its face turned down (*avāṅmukha*). The one who knows this truth is united with progeny and also with riches in animals. The *nivid* mantras are in the form of ornaments for the *ukthas*, and increase their beauty and brilliance. The mantras recited at the morning pressing are like the ornament of the upper part of the body, the mantras recited at the midday are like the ornament of the middle region, and those of the third pressing are like the ornament of the lower part; all are producers of embellishment. One who knows this adorns the sacrifice, and himself shines. And again,

> सौर्यो वा एता देवता यन्निविदस्तद्यत्प्रातःसवने धीयन्ते मध्यतो मध्यंदिने तेतस्तृतीयसवन आदित्यस्यैव तेषु तेतमनु पर्यायावर्तन्ते । पेश्भो वै देवा यज्ञं समभरंस्तस्मात्पेश्भो निविदः शस्यन्ते । यद्वै तद्देवा यज्ञं समभरंस्तस्माद्वदः समभवत्तस्मादाहुरश्वं निविदां शंस्त्रे दद्यादिति तमु खलु वरमेव ददति । न निविदः पदमतीयात् यद्यन्निविदः पदमतीयाद्यज्ञस्य तच्छिद्रं कुर्याद्यज्ञस्य वै छिद्रं स्रवद्यजमानोऽनु पापीयान् भवति तस्मान्न निविदः पदमतीयात् । न निविदः पदे विपरिहरेद्यन्निविदः पदे विपरिहरेन्मोहयेद्यज्ञं मुग्धो यजमानः स्यात्तस्मान्न निविदः पदे विपरिहरेत् । न निविदः पदे समस्येद्यन्निविदः पदे समस्येद्यज्ञस्य तदायुः संहरेत्प्रमायुको यजमानः स्यात्तस्मान्न निविदः पदे समस्येत् । प्रेदं ब्रह्म प्रेदं क्षत्रमित्येते एव समस्येद्ब्रह्मक्षत्रयोः संश्रित्यै तस्माद्ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं च संश्रिते । न तृचं न चतुर्ऋचमतिमन्येत निविद्धानमन्येकैकं वै निविदः पदमृचं सूक्तं प्रति तस्मान्न तृचं न चतुर्ऋचमतिमन्येत निविद्धानं निविदा ह्येव स्तोत्रमतिशस्तं भवति ।

> *saurya vā etā devatā yan nividas tad yat prātaḥsavane dhīyante madhyato madhyaṃdine tetas tṛtīyasavana ādityasyaiva teṣu tetam anu paryāyāvartante | peśbho vai devā yajñaṃ samabharaṃs tasmāt peśbho nividaḥ śasyante | yad vai tad devā yajñaṃ samabharaṃs tasmād vadaḥ samabhavat tasmād āhur aśvaṃ nividāṃ śaṃstre dadyād iti tam u khalu varam eva dadati | na nividaḥ padam atīyāt yady annividaḥ padam atīyād yajñasya tac chidraṃ kuryād yajñasya vai chidraṃ sravad yajamāno 'nu pāpīyān bhavati tasmān na nividaḥ padam atīyāt | na nividaḥ pade viparihared yan nividaḥ pade viparihared mohayed yajñaṃ mugdho yajamānaḥ syāt tasmān na nividaḥ pade vipariha】ret | na nividaḥ pade samasyed yan nividaḥ pade samasyed yajñasya tad āyuḥ saṃharet pramāyuko yajamānaḥ syāt tasmān na nividaḥ pade samasyet | predaṃ brahma predaṃ kṣatram ity ete eva samasyed brahmakṣatrayoḥ saṃśrityai tasmād brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca saṃśrite | na tṛcaṃ na caturṛcam atimanyeta nividdhānam anyaikaikaṃ vai nividaḥ padam ṛcaṃ sūktaṃ prati tasmān na tṛcaṃ na caturṛcam atimanyeta nividdhānaṃ nividā hy eva stotram atiśastaṃ bhavati |* [as read; very garbled in the print: [?]]

(Ai. Brā. 11-11 [?]). The *nivid* deities are all connected with the Sun: the mantras of the morning, midday and third pressings follow the course of the Sun from his rising till his setting. The gods collected the sacrifice by the metres of the foot (*pādātmaka*); therefore the *nivid* mantras are in the form of feet (*pāda*) …

### Printed p. 393  (PDF 413)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

…in the form of sentences (*vākya*). All the portions of the sacrifice were put together by the deities into a single whole, and from that, the horse was born; therefore a rule is laid down that a gift of a horse must be made to the priest who recites these mantras. One must not go beyond any *pada* in the *nivid* mantras; if any *pada* is skipped, it makes a break in the sacrifice itself, and that brings harm to the sacrificer. The sentences in these mantras must not be joined together; nor may one put what precedes after, and what follows before. If this is done, a *saṃdhi*-fault arises in the sacrificial action; and the sacrificer too becomes bewildered. If two sentences are put together, the sacrificer's life too is shortened and he may come to death; hence, in mantra recitation, no confusion by mixing sentences should be made. Only the two mantras *predaṃ brahma*, *predaṃ kṣatram*, which are pure in nature and of the nature of divine speech, may be mixed: therefore the *brahma*-lustre and the *kṣatra*-lustre should be mixed. The *nivid* mantras are to be recited as three or four ṛks, and must not be neglected; the *nivid*, by its *brahma* function, makes the recitation of the praise more important.

> एकां परिशिष्य तृतीयसवने निविदं दध्यात् । यद्द्वे परिशिष्य दध्यात्प्रजननं तदुपहन्याद्गर्भिस्त्रैजा व्यर्धयेत् तस्मादेकामेव परिशिष्य तृतीयसवने निविदं दध्यात् । न सूक्तेन निविदमतिपद्येत येन सूक्तेन निविदमतिपद्येत न तत्सूक्तं पुनरुपनिवर्तेत नाप्स्तुहमेव तत् । अन्यत्र द्दैवतं तच्छन्दसं सूक्तमाहृत्य तस्मिन्निविदं दध्यात् । मा प्र गाम पथो वयं मा यज्ञादिन्द्र सोमिनः । मान्तः स्थुर्नो अरातय इत्यरातीयत एव तदपहन्ति । यो यज्ञस्य प्रसाधनस्तन्तुर्देवेष्वाततः । तमाहुतं नशीमहीति । प्रजा वै तन्तुः प्रजामेवास्मा एतत्तन्तनोति । मनो न्वाहुवामहे नाराशंसेन सोमेनेति । मनसा वै यज्ञस्तायते मनसा क्रियते । सैव तत्र प्रायश्चित्तिः प्रायश्चित्तिः ॥

> *ekāṃ pariśiṣya tṛtīyasavane nividaṃ dadhyāt | yad dve pariśiṣya dadhyāt prajananaṃ tad upahanyād garbhis traijā vyardhayet tasmād ekām eva pariśiṣya tṛtīyasavane nividaṃ dadhyāt | na sūktena nividam atipadyeta yena sūktena nividam atipadyeta na tat sūktaṃ punar upanivarteta nāpstuham eva tat | anyatra daivataṃ tacchandasaṃ sūktam āhṛtya tasmin nividaṃ dadhyāt | mā pra gāma patho vayaṃ mā yajñād indra sominaḥ | māntaḥ sthur no arātaya ity arātīyata eva tad apahanti | yo yajñasya prasādhanas tantur deveṣv ātataḥ | tam āhutaṃ naśīmahīti | prajā vai tantuḥ prajām evāsmā etat tantanoti | mano nv āhuvāmahe nārāśaṃsena somenety | manasā vai yajñas tāyate manasā kriyate | saiva tatra prāyaścittiḥ prāyaścittiḥ ‖* [as read; garbled in places: [?]]

(Ai. Brā. 11-11 [?]). In the third pressing, one *ṛk* is to be left over and the *nivid* put with it; if two ṛks are left over and put together, the power of generation is destroyed; then, the power of conceiving is lost, and people become unable to bear an embryo. So, in a sūkta that has no *nivid* connected with it, one must not recite that sūkta without adding a *nivid*; once one has recited it, it is not proper to add it again afterwards. If this loss occurs, one should choose another sūkta that has the same deity and the same metre and add these *nivid* mantras to it. In such a case:

### Printed p. 394  (PDF 414)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 175".)*

> मा प्र गाम पथो वयं मा यज्ञादिन्द्र सोमिनः । मान्तः स्थुर्नो अरातयः ॥

> *mā pra gāma patho vayaṃ mā yajñād indra sominaḥ | māntaḥ sthur no arātayaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-57-1 [?]) — having first prayed "May we not go astray from the path; may we not be cut off from the sacrifice; may evil-minded powers not come to dwell among us", the sūkta accompanied by the *nivid* mantras is to be recited. Then the sacrificial work proceeds, free of any delusion, without obstacle, and the destruction of evil powers also results. The sacrificer recites: "*yo yajñasya prasādhanas tantur deveṣv ātataḥ tam āhutaṃ naśīmahi*" — "May the thread of the fruit of the sacrifice that is spread among the deities extend to us, the sacrificers" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-57-2 [?]); and offspring, as the thread, as the form of continuity of the family, is obtained for the sacrificers in unbroken succession.

> तद्यदेतां पुरस्तात्सूक्तस्य निविदं दधाति प्रजात्यै । प्रजायते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद ॥

> *tad yad etāṃ purastāt sūktasya nividaṃ dadhāti prajātyai | prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 10-2 [?]). For this reason the *hotṛ* gets offspring as the fruit of reciting the *nivid* mantras at the beginning of a sūkta. It is said elsewhere also that one who knows this obtains the continuity of progeny, and the other riches. It is learned from many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā that the recitation of mantras, with faith that it gives the most excellent fruit, is traditional, when invoking the respective deities, in praising them: the nature of each deity, their power, the great acts they have accomplished, and so on. For example —

> ताँ पूर्वया निविदा हूमहे वयं भगं मित्रमदितिं दक्षमस्रिधम् ।

> *tāṃ pūrvayā nividā hūmahe vayaṃ bhagaṃ mitram aditiṃ dakṣam asridham |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-3 [?]);

> जुषेथां यज्ञं बोधतं हवस्य मे सत्तो होता निविदः पूर्व्या अनु ।

> *juṣethāṃ yajñaṃ bodhataṃ havasya me satto hotā nividaḥ pūrvyā anu |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-36-6 [?]);

> किमु ष्विदस्मै निविदो भनन्तेन्द्रस्यावद्यं दिधिषन्त आपः ।

> *kim u ṣvid asmai nivido bhananta indrasyāvadyaṃ didhiṣanta āpaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-18-6 [?]);

> वि यद्वाचं कीस्तासो भरन्ते शंसन्ति के चिन्निविदो मनानाः ।

> *vi yad vācaṃ kīstāso bharante śaṃsanti ke cin nivido manānāḥ |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-62-10 [?]) —

in these and other places the greatness of the *nivid* mantras is praised.

---

### Printed p. 395  (PDF 415)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 18 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

In the ṛk at hand (1-175-6 [?]) the *nivid* mantras addressed to Indra are indicated by the sentence *tām anu tvā nividaṃ johavīmi*. There is also a slight difference of opinion in determining which sūktas are accompanied by *nivid* mantras addressed to the deity Indra. For example —

> जनिष्ठा उग्रः सहसे तुराय निविद्धानमेकाहिकम् ।

> *janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāya nividdhānam ekāhikam |* [as read; reading of the second half doubtful: [?]]

(Ai. [?] 1-2-2 [?]). The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says that the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-73 [?], beginning with the ṛk *janiṣṭhā ugraḥ*, goes with *nivid* mantras. But in the Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka (1-3 [?]) it is said that the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-19 [?], beginning with the ṛk *mahāṃ indro nṛvad*, goes with these mantras. Thus the seer of the sūkta, in the ṛk at hand, has made known his resolve: "I will praise Indra with *nivid* mantras that praise Indra's nature, his prowess and his distinctive excellence."

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***jaritṛbhyaḥ*** — root *jṝṣ vayohānau*; here used in the sense of praising; in the agent sense the suffix *tṛc*; augment *iṭ*; guṇa for the *ṛ* of the root; since it is *cit*, the end syllable is *udātta*; dative plural.
- ***tṛṣyate*** — root *ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām*; *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; by "*divādibhyaḥ śyan*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-69 [?]) the *vikaraṇa* *śyan*; by "*tāsyanudāttet*…" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 [?]) the *śatṛ* is *anudātta*; since the *vikaraṇa* is *nit*, the first syllable is *udātta*; dative singular.
- ***babhūtha*** — root *bhū sattāyām*; *liṭ*, second person singular; by "*babhūthātatanthā*…" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-64 [?]) the absence of *iṭ* is fixed by *nipātana*; by "*nipātair yad yadi*…" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30 [?]), because of *yathā*, *nighāta* is prohibited; since *thal* is *lit*, by "*liti*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 [?]) the syllable before the suffix takes *udātta* accent.
- ***johavīmi*** — root *hu dānādanayoḥ*; after the *yaṅluganta* (intensive with *luk*), *laṭ*; first person singular, *mip*; by "*yaño vā*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-94 [?]) the augment *īṭ* for *mip*; since it stands after a *tiṅ* [as read: *ati…* [?]], *nighāta* accent comes. ‖ 6 ‖

Here ends the hundred and seventy-fifth (175th) Sūkta.
