### Printed p. 425  (PDF 445)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 19 [?]"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". The page repeats, with the same sense, the matter of pp. 393–394 above.)*

*(Special Topics continued)* …in the third pressing one ṛk is to be left over and the *nivid* mantras are to be put with it. But if both ṛks are left over and the *nivid* put with them, a loss of power arises; then the capacity of conceiving is lost; therefore only one is to be left over and put with it; then the sacrificial action is completed. It must not be done by leaving out two: if so, the power of generation is destroyed, and people lose the power to bear an embryo. In a sūkta that does not accept *nivid* mantras, one should not recite that sūkta without joining them; once it has been recited, it is not proper to add them again. If such an omission occurs, one should choose another sūkta of the same deity and the same metre, and add these *nivid* mantras to it. In such a case —

> मा प्र गाम पथो वयं मा यज्ञादिन्द्र सोमिनः । मान्तः स्थुर्नो अरातयः ॥

> *mā pra gāma patho vayaṃ mā yajñād indra sominaḥ | māntaḥ sthur no arātayaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-57-1 [?]) — "May we not go astray from the path; may we not be cut off from the sacrifice; may evil-minded powers not come to dwell among us": having first prayed thus, one should recite the sūkta accompanied by the *nivid* mantras. Then the sacrificial work proceeds without any delusion, free of obstacle, and the destruction of evil powers also results. "May the thread of the fruit of the sacrifice that is spread among the deities extend to us, the sacrificers" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-57-2 [?]) — so the sacrificer prays; the thread of offspring, in the form of continuity of the family, is obtained by the sacrificer in unbroken succession.

> तद्यदेतां पुरस्तात्सूक्तस्य निविदं दधाति प्रजात्यै । प्रजायते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद ॥

> *tad yad etāṃ purastāt sūktasya nividaṃ dadhāti prajātyai | prajāyate prajayā paśubhir ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 10-2 [?]). For this reason the *hotṛ* obtains offspring as the fruit of reciting the *nivid* mantras at the beginning of a sūkta. It is said elsewhere also that the sacrificer who knows this obtains good offspring, and then all the other riches. It is learned from many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā that, in invoking the respective deities with faith that the recitation of mantras gives the most excellent fruit, it is traditional to praise their nature, power, great acts and so on. For example —

> ताँ पूर्वया निविदा हूमहे वयं भगं मित्रमदितिं दक्षमस्रिधम् ।

> *tāṃ pūrvayā nividā hūmahe vayaṃ bhagaṃ mitram aditiṃ dakṣam asridham |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-3 [?]);

> जुषेथां यज्ञं बोधतं हवस्य मे सत्तो होता निविदः पूर्व्या अनु ।

> *juṣethāṃ yajñaṃ bodhataṃ havasya me satto hotā nividaḥ pūrvyā anu |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-36-6 [?]);

### Printed p. 426  (PDF 446)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 176".)*

> किमु ष्विदस्मै निविदो भनन्तेन्द्रस्यावद्यं दिधिषन्त आपः ।

> *kim u ṣvid asmai nivido bhananta indrasyāvadyaṃ didhiṣanta āpaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-18-6 [?]);

> वि यद्वाचं कीस्तासो भरन्ते शंसन्ति के चिन्निविदो मनानाः ।

> *vi yad vācaṃ kīstāso bharante śaṃsanti ke cin nivido manānāḥ |* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-62-10 [?]) —

in these and other places the greatness of the *nivid* mantras is praised.

In the ṛk at hand (1-176-6 [?]) the *nivid* mantras addressed to Indra are indicated by the sentence *tām anu tvā nividaṃ johavīmi*. There is also a slight difference of opinion in determining which sūktas are accompanied by *nivid* mantras addressed to the deity Indra. For example —

> जनिष्ठा उग्रः सहसे तुराय निविद्धानमेकाहिकम् ।

> *janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāya nividdhānam ekāhikam |* [as read; reading of the second half doubtful: [?]]

(Ai. Ā. 1-2-2 [?]). It is said in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa that the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-73 [?], beginning with the ṛk *janiṣṭhā ugraḥ*, goes with *nivid* mantras. But in the Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka (1-3 [?]) it is said that the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-19 [?], beginning with the ṛk *mahāṃ indro nṛvad*, goes with these mantras. Thus the seer of the sūkta, in the ṛk at hand, has made known his resolve: "I will praise Indra with *nivid* mantras that praise Indra's nature, prowess and distinctive excellence."

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — the notes on the words of this ṛk are the same as those given for Sūkta 175 Ṛk 6 (p. 395 above); noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***jaritṛbhyaḥ*** — root *jṝṣ vayohānau*, used here in the sense of praising; the agent suffix *tṛc*; augment *iṭ*; guṇa for the *ṛ*; since *cit*, the end syllable is *udātta*; dative plural.
- ***tṛṣyate*** — root *ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām*; *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; by "*divādibhyaḥ śyan*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-69 [?]) the *vikaraṇa* *śyan*; by "*tāsyanudāttet*…" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 [?]) the *śatṛ* is *anudātta*; the first syllable is *udātta* since the *vikaraṇa* is *nit*; dative singular.
- ***babhūtha*** — root *bhū sattāyām*; *liṭ*, second person singular; by "*babhūthātatanthā*…" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-64 [?]) the absence of *iṭ* by *nipātana*; by "*nipātair yad yadi*…" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30 [?]) no *nighāta*, because of *yathā*; since *thal* is *lit*, by "*liti*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 [?]) the syllable before the suffix takes *udātta* accent.
- ***johavīmi*** — root *hu dānādanayoḥ*; after *yaṅ luk*, *laṭ*, first person singular *mip*; by "*yaño vā*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-94 [?]) the augment *īṭ* for *mip*; since it stands after a *tiṅ* [as read: *ati…* [?]], *nighāta* accent. ‖ 6 ‖

Here ends the hundred and seventy-sixth (176th) Sūkta.

## SŪKTA 177 (the hundred and seventy-seventh Sūkta)

### Printed p. 427  (PDF 447)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 20"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**Anukramaṇikā (Sanskrit, as read; doubtful passages marked [?])**

> आ चर्षणिप्रा इति पञ्चर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तमागस्त्यमैन्द्रं त्रैष्टुभम् । आ चर्षणिप्राः पञ्चेत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ होत्रकशस्त्रेषु स्तोमवृद्धावस्य विशेषविनियोगः । ऐन्द्राणि त्रैष्टुभान्यमरुच्छान्यान्यवापेरन् । आ. ८-७ [?] । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥

> *ā carṣaṇiprā iti pañcarcaṃ trayodaśaṃ sūktam āgastyam aindraṃ traiṣṭubham | ā carṣaṇiprāḥ pañcety anukramaṇikā ‖ hotrakaśastreṣu stomavṛddhāv asya viśeṣaviniyogaḥ | aindrāṇi traiṣṭubhāny amarucchānyāny avāperan | ā. 8-7 [?] | iti sūtritatvāt ‖* [?]

**Anuvāda (Kannada, translated)**

This sūkta beginning *ā carṣaṇiprāḥ* is the thirteenth sūkta in the twenty-third anuvāka. It has five ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Agastya; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated as "*ā carṣaṇiprāḥ pañca*". When the priests of the *hotṛ* class recite the *śastra* mantras for the increase of the *stoma*, this sūkta has a special application (*viniyoga*), as is explained by the sūtra "*aindrāṇi traiṣṭubhāny amarucchānyāny avāperan*" in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Āś. 8-7 [?]).

**Sūkta — 177**

Maṇḍala — 1 ‖ Anuvāka — 23 ‖ Sūkta — 177 ‖

Number of ṛks in the sūkta — 5 ‖

**Ṛk 1**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> आ चर्षणिप्रा वृषभो जनानां राजा कृष्टीनां पुरुहूत इन्द्रः ।
> स्तुतः श्रवस्यन्नवसोप मद्रिग्युक्त्वा हरी वृषणा याह्यर्वाङ् ॥ १ ॥

> *ā carṣaṇiprā vṛṣabho janānāṃ rājā kṛṣṭīnāṃ puruhūta indraḥ |*
> *stutaḥ śravasyann avasopa madrig yuktvā harī vṛṣaṇā yāhy arvāṅ ‖ 1 ‖*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> आ । चर्षणिऽप्राः । वृषभः । जनानाम् । राजा । कृष्टीनाम् । पुरुऽहूतः । इन्द्रः ।
> स्तुतः । श्रवस्यन् । अवसा । उप । मद्रिक् । युक्त्वा । हरी इति । वृषणा । आ । याहि । अर्वाङ् ॥ १ ॥

> *ā | carṣaṇi-prāḥ | vṛṣabhaḥ | janānām | rājā | kṛṣṭīnām | puru-hūtaḥ | indraḥ |*
> *stutaḥ | śravasyan | avasā | upa | madrik | yuktvā | harī iti | vṛṣaṇā | ā | yāhi | arvāṅ ‖ 1 ‖*

### Printed p. 428  (PDF 448)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 177".)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (as read; doubtful passages marked [?])

> अयमिन्द्रश्चर्षणिप्राः । चर्षणयो मनुष्याः । तेषां धनादिना प्रीणयिता । जनानां सर्वेषां वृषभः कामानां वर्षिता । तथा कृष्टीनां मनुष्यनामैतत् । मनुष्याणां राजा स्वामी पुरुहूतो बहुभिराहूतः । ईदृश इन्द्रोऽस्मानाजानात्वागच्छतु वा [?] । उत्तरार्धः परोक्षवादः । हे इन्द्र स्तुतोऽस्माभिः श्रवस्यन् हविर्लक्षणान्नमिच्छन्नवसास्मद्रक्षणेन तर्पणेन वा युक्तः सन्मद्र्यगभिमुखमञ्चन् वृषणा वर्षकौ युवानौ हरी अश्वौ युक्त्वा रथे योजयित्वार्वागस्मदभिमुखमा याहि । आगच्छ ॥

> *ayam indraś carṣaṇiprāḥ | carṣaṇayo manuṣyāḥ | teṣāṃ dhanādinā prīṇayitā | janānāṃ sarveṣāṃ vṛṣabhaḥ kāmānāṃ varṣitā | tathā kṛṣṭīnāṃ manuṣyanāmaitat | manuṣyāṇāṃ rājā svāmī puruhūto bahubhir āhūtaḥ | īdṛśa indro 'smān ājānātv āgacchatu vā [?] | uttarārdhaḥ parokṣavādaḥ | he indra stuto 'smābhiḥ śravasyan havirlakṣaṇānnam icchann avasāsmadrakṣaṇena tarpaṇena vā yuktaḥ san madryag abhimukham añcan vṛṣaṇā varṣakau yuvānau harī aśvau yuktvā rathe yojayitvārvāg asmadabhimukham ā yāhi | āgaccha ‖* [?]

*Gist:* May this Indra — the satisfier of men with wealth, the showerer of desires, lord of men, called by many — come to us; O Indra, praised by us and wishing for the oblation-food, harness your two young bay horses to your chariot and come to us.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

*carṣaṇiprāḥ* — he who gives men joy (by wealth and the like); *janānām* — to all people; *vṛṣabhaḥ* — the showerer of desires; *kṛṣṭīnām* — to men; *rājā* — lord; *puruhūtaḥ* — called by many (in many ways); *indraḥ* — Indra; *ā* — let him come (let him know us); (*he indra* — O Indra); *stutaḥ* — praised by us; *śravasyan* — wishing for the oblation-food; *avasā* — with our protection (with satisfaction); *madrik* — setting out towards us; *vṛṣaṇā* — young; *harī* — (your) two horses; *yuktvā* — harnessing (to the chariot); *arvāṅ* — towards us; *ā yāhi* — come.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra, you satisfy men with wealth and the like; you are the giver of desired objects to mankind, the lord of the human race, called by many. Praised by us, accept the oblation-food that we offer, and, for our protection, harness your two young horses to your chariot, and come to us.

**Printed English**

May Indra, who is the cherisher of men, the benefactor of menkind, the lord of men, the adored of many, (come to us). Indra, you who are praised (by us), and are desirous of the oblation, harness your vigorous steeds, and come down to me for (my) preservation. [As printed: "menkind"; "come down to me for (my) preservation" [sic].]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk, describing Indra's lordship and his generosity, a prayer is made for his coming towards the sacrificial act. Here, in describing Indra's lordship and chiefship, the epithets ***carṣaṇiprāḥ***; ***vṛṣabho janānām***; ***rājā kṛṣṭīnām*** deserve notice. Here

### Printed p. 429  (PDF 449)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 20"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". The sentence "Here" at the foot of p. 428 continues:)*

the three words *carṣaṇi*, *jana* and *kṛṣṭi* are synonyms of "man"; but since they are used in different contexts, they should be understood as epithets that show the variety in the nature and in the occupations of man.

***carṣaṇi*** — this word is mostly used in the plural only. Its formation and the variety of its meanings were explained earlier, in the Special Topics of the 2nd ṛk of the 176th sūkta (pp. 402–404 above). It is formed either from the root *car*, meaning "to move about", or from the root *kṛṣ*, meaning "to cultivate". Although this is the root meaning, in many places where the word is used Sāyaṇa has explained it as "men who have the sight of the nature of knowledge". It was also shown earlier that this word is used as an epithet not only of men but also of Indra and the other deities, who possess extraordinary knowledge. The epithets *rājā carṣaṇīnām* and *carṣaṇiprāḥ* too are used mostly of Indra and Agni [Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-100-1 [?]; 5-39-4 [?] and so on]; the purport is that Indra is the protector of men who are wise, who are seers of sūktas and who perform sacrifices. The word *kṛṣṭi* also has the general meaning "those born as men". The Nirukta-writers —

> आ दधिक्राः शवसा पञ्च कृष्टीः सूर्य इव ज्योतिषापस्ततान ।

> *ā dadhikrāḥ śavasā pañca kṛṣṭīḥ sūrya iva jyotiṣāpas tatāna |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-38-10 [?]) — in this ṛk, for the words *pañca kṛṣṭīḥ* they give the meaning *pañca janān* (Ni. 10-18 [?]), i.e. all classes of men. About this word Keith gives the following explanation:

> कृष्टि denotes 'people' in general from the Rig-Veda onwards. Its common and regular use in this sense appears to show that the Aryans, when they invaded India, were already Agriculturists, though the employment of the words reffering to ploughing mentioned under कृषि indicates that not all of the people devoted themselves equally to that occupation. Indra and Agni are Par exellence the lords of men. the word (कृष्टि) Sometimes is further defined by the addition of an adjective meaning "belonging to mankind" (मानुषीः : मानवीः).

> *kṛṣṭi denotes 'people ' in general from the Rig-Veda onwards. Its common and regular use in this sense appears to show that the Aryans, when they invaded India, were already Agriculturists, though the employment of the words reffering to ploughing mentioned under kṛṣi indicates that not all of the people devoted themselves equally to that occupation. Indra and Agni are Par exellence the lords of men. the word (kṛṣṭi) Sometimes is further defined by the addition of an adjective meaning "belonging to mankind" (mānuṣīḥ : mānavīḥ).*
>
> [Vedic Index of Names and Subjects. By Keith anc Maedoneth [Vol. I. P. 183.]

[As printed; "reffering", "exellence" and "anc" are the print's misprints: [sic]; the Sanskrit words in the English are set in Kannada letters in the print.]

From the above explanation it is indicated that the word *kṛṣṭi* shows the Āryas to have been engaged in agriculture and other occupations: that is, it points to their way of life.

### Printed p. 430  (PDF 450)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 177".)*

> स युध्मः सत्वा खजकृत्समद्वा तुविम्रक्षो नदनुमाँ ऋजीषी । बृहद्रेणुश्च्यवनो मानुषीणामेकः कृष्टीनामभवत्सहावा ॥

> *sa yudhmaḥ satvā khajakṛt samadvā tuvimrakṣo nadanumāṃ ṛjīṣī | bṛhadreṇuś cyavano mānuṣīṇām ekaḥ kṛṣṭīnām abhavat sahāvā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-18-2 [?]) — in such ṛks the usage is found with the epithet *mānuṣīṇāṃ kṛṣṭīnām*.

Like the words *carṣaṇi* and *kṛṣṭi*, which are synonyms for the human race, the word *kṣiti*, which gives the meaning "settled, dwelling", is also used in such contexts. *Manuṣyāḥ*, *naraḥ* and so on are read among the names of men (Ni. 3-7 [?]).

It is said that Indra is the protector of the people who perform sacrifices, their guide, the lord who protects them all: thus Indra's extraordinary and universally dear qualities are described. Hence the epithet ***puruhūtaḥ — bahubhir āhūtaḥ*** — "he who is called by many". A prayer is made that such an Indra may come towards our sacrifice.

***śravasyan — havirlakṣaṇam annam icchan*** — this shows Indra's wish too: "desiring the food that is in the form of oblation". For the word *śravas* the two meanings "food" and "fame" are possible. The Nirukta-writers —

> आसस्राणासः शवसानमच्छेन्द्रं सुचक्रे रथ्यासो अश्वाः । अभि श्रव ऋज्यन्तो वहेयुर्नू चिन्नु वायोरमृतं वि दस्येत् ॥

> *āsasrāṇāsaḥ śavasānam acchendraṃ sucakre rathyāso aśvāḥ | abhi śrava ṛjyanto vaheyur nū cin nu vāyor amṛtaṃ vi dasyet ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-32-3 [?]) — in explaining this ṛk, for the word *śrava* they say "*śrava ity annanāma śrūyata iti śruteḥ*" [as read: [?]] — *śrava* is a name of food; since it is universally well known, i.e. is heard by all, the word *śrava*, formed from the root *śru*, means food (Ni. 10-3 [?]). And

> इन्द्रस्य यस्य सुमुखं सहो महि श्रवो नृम्णं च रोदसी सपर्यतः ।

> *indrasya yasya sumukhaṃ saho mahi śravo nṛmṇaṃ ca rodasī saparyataḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-50-1 [?]) — in this, "*śravaṇīyaṃ yaśaḥ*" — "that which is heard by all", i.e. fame well known everywhere — is the meaning they have given (Ni. 11-9 [?]). Since food is the cause of fame for givers, it may also be taken to mean food that brings fame. On this basis —

> बृहत्या श्रीकामो यशस्कामः कुर्वीत । श्रीर्वै यशश्छन्दसां बृहती । श्रियमेव यश आत्मन्धत्ते ॥

> *bṛhatyā śrīkāmo yaśaskāmaḥ kurvīta | śrīr vai yaśaś chandasāṃ bṛhatī | śriyam eva yaśa ātman dhatte ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 1-5 [?]).

### Printed p. 431  (PDF 451)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 20"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

— in this passage the identity of *Śrī* (prosperity), which is of the nature of the wealth of grain and the like, and of the fame (*yaśas*) obtained by it, is stated. The basis of fame is the wealth of food and the like; and if there is wealth of food and the like, fame comes of itself; hence both meanings are possible for the word *śrava*. In the ṛk at hand it may be taken to mean food in the form of oblation, which is the means to the sacrificer's fame.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***carṣaṇiprāḥ*** — root *prā pūraṇe*; the suffix *kvip*; by "*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 [?]) the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent.
- ***vṛṣabhaḥ*** — root *vṛṣu secane*; the suffix *abhac* of the *ṭoṇādika* (*uṇādi*) group; since it is *cit*, by "*citaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 [?]) the end syllable is *udātta*.
- ***kṛṣṭīnām*** — genitive plural; by "*nāmanyatarasyām*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-177 [?]) the *nām* takes *udātta* accent.
- ***śravasyan*** — *śravaḥ annam ātmana icchan śravasyan*; by "*supa ātmanaḥ kyac*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 [?]) the suffix *kyac*; after *kyac*, *laṭ* with the substitution *śatṛ*; nominative singular; by the *kyac* accent the end syllable is *udātta*.
- ***madryak*** — root *añcu gatipūjanayoḥ*; by "*pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-109 [?]) the desired form is obtained.
- ***yuktvā*** — root *yujir yoge*; since instigation is shown, the root contains *ṇic* in its sense; by "*samānakartṛkayoḥ pūrvakāle*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-21 [?]) the suffix *ktvā*; by "*coḥ kuḥ*" the *j* of the root becomes *k*; *cartva*; by the suffix accent the end syllable is *udātta*.
- ***yāhi*** — root *yā prāpaṇe*; *loṭ*, second person singular; *nighāta* for a *tiṅ*. ‖ 1 ‖

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> ये ते वृषणो वृषभास इन्द्र ब्रह्मयुजो वृषरथासो अत्याः ।
> ताँ आ तिष्ठ तेभिरा याह्यर्वाङ् हवामहे त्वा सुत इन्द्र सोमे ॥ २ ॥

> *ye te vṛṣaṇo vṛṣabhāsa indra brahmayujo vṛṣarathāso atyāḥ |*
> *tāṃ ā tiṣṭha tebhir ā yāhy arvāṅ havāmahe tvā suta indra some ‖ 2 ‖*

### Printed p. 432  (PDF 452)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 177".)*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> ये । ते । वृषणः । वृषभासः । इन्द्र । ब्रह्मऽयुजः । वृषऽरथासः । अत्याः ।
> तान् । आ । तिष्ठ । तेभिः । आ । याहि । अर्वाङ् । हवामहे । त्वा । सुते । इन्द्र । सोमे ॥ २ ॥

> *ye | te | vṛṣaṇaḥ | vṛṣabhāsaḥ | indra | brahma-yujaḥ | vṛṣa-rathāsaḥ | atyāḥ |*
> *tān | ā | tiṣṭha | tebhiḥ | ā | yāhi | arvāṅ | havāmahe | tvā | sute | indra | some ‖ 2 ‖*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya** (as read; doubtful passages marked [?])

> हे इन्द्र ते तव संबन्धिनो वृषणो वर्षका युवानो वर्षणवन्तो वा वृषभासः श्रेष्ठा ब्रह्मयुजः परिवृढेन मन्त्रेण युज्यमाना वृषरथासो वर्षणरथवन्तः । तत्र नियुक्ता इत्यर्थः । ईदृशा अत्या अश्वा ये सन्ति तान् आ तिष्ठ आश्रय । आरोह । तेभिस्तैरर्वागस्मदभिमुखमा याहि । आगच्छ । वयं च हे इन्द्र सोमे सुते सति त्वा त्वां हवामहे । आह्वयामः ॥

> *he indra te tava saṃbandhino vṛṣaṇo varṣakā yuvāno varṣaṇavanto vā vṛṣabhāsaḥ śreṣṭhā brahmayujaḥ parivṛḍhena mantreṇa yujyamānā vṛṣarathāso varṣaṇarathavantaḥ | tatra niyuktā ity arthaḥ | īdṛśā atyā aśvā ye santi tān ā tiṣṭha āśraya | āroha | tebhis tair arvāg asmadabhimukham ā yāhi | āgaccha | vayaṃ ca he indra some sute sati tvā tvāṃ havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ ‖* [?]

*Gist:* O Indra, mount those horses of yours — young and showering, excellent, yoked by mantra, harnessed to the rain-giving chariot — and come to us on them; we call you when the Soma is pressed.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, translated)**

(*he*) *indra* — O Indra; *vṛṣaṇaḥ* — those that shower (desires), or are in their prime; *vṛṣabhāsaḥ* — excellent; *brahmayujaḥ* — those that are harnessed by mantra alone; *vṛṣarathāsaḥ* — those yoked to a desire-showering chariot; *te* — your; *atyāḥ* — horses; *ye* (*santi*) — which there are; *tān* — them; *ā tiṣṭha* — mount; *tebhiḥ* — yoked with them; *arvāṅ* — turned towards (us); *ā yāhi* — come; (*vayaṃ ca* — and we); (*he*) *indra* — O Indra; *some* — the Soma juice; *sute* (*sati*) — being pressed; *tvām* — you; *havāmahe* — we invoke.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra, mount those excellent horses of yours which are to be harnessed by mantra alone, yoked to your wish-granting chariot, and in their prime, and come towards us; we also, having prepared the Soma juice, call you.

**Printed English**

Mount, Indra, your steeds, who are young and vigorous, tractable to prayer, and harnessed to a bounty-shedding car: come down with them to us. We invoke you, Indra, the libation being poured out.

### Printed p. 433  (PDF 453)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 20"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; signature mark "XIII 28" at foot.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***vṛṣaṇaḥ, vṛṣabhāsaḥ, vṛṣarathāsaḥ*** — these words are epithets of Indra's horses and show the special capacities of those horses. The differences of meaning in these words, which are formed from the word *vṛṣan*, and their usages, will be explained in the Special Topics of the following ṛk. Only the epithets *brahmayujaḥ* and *atyāḥ* are explained here.

***brahmayujaḥ — parivṛḍhena mantreṇa yujyamānāḥ*** — "harnessed by the utterance of the exalted (*parivṛḍha*) mantra" is an epithet of Indra's horses. The word *brahma* as used here is formed from the root *bṛhi*, meaning "to grow", and means a mantra that has grown, i.e. a powerful mantra. The word *brahmayujaḥ* here, like the word *brahmavāhaḥ* ("borne by prayer"), is used in many places as an epithet of Indra's horses. There, "*brahmaṇā mantrarūpeṇa stotreṇa ūhyamānāḥ prāpyamāṇendra*" — Indra, who is to be reached by praise in the form of mantra; here too, the horses harnessed by praise.

> ब्रह्मणा ते ब्रह्मयुजा युनज्मि हरी सखाया सधमाद आ शू । स्थिरं रथं सुखमिन्द्राधितिष्ठन्प्र जानन्विद्वाँ उप याहि सोमम् ॥

> *brahmaṇā te brahmayujā yunajmi harī sakhāyā sadhamāda ā śū | sthiraṃ rathaṃ sukham indrādhitiṣṭhan pra jānan vidvāṃ upa yāhi somam ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-35-4 [?]) — in such ṛks the process by which Indra's horses are harnessed to his chariot by the power of the mantra is described; in the ṛk at hand the same point is shown.

***atyāḥ — aśvāḥ*** — Indra's horses. ***āpekṣitapradeśaṃ prati atanaśīlāḥ*** — "of the nature and power of going to the place desired": this is the sense, and it is not only for horses that this word is an epithet; it is also an epithet of Agni and of the Āditya (Sun).

> एष प्र पूर्वीरव तस्य चम्रिषोऽत्यो न योषामुदयंस्त भुर्वणिः । दक्षं महे पाययते हिरण्ययं रथमावृत्या हरियोगमृभ्वसम् ॥

> *eṣa pra pūrvīr ava tasya camriṣo 'tyo na yoṣām udayaṃsta bhurvaṇiḥ | dakṣaṃ mahe pāyayate hiraṇyayaṃ ratham āvṛtyā hariyogam ṛbhvasam ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-56-1 [?]) — in this ṛk *atyaḥ* is used as a synonym of "horse"; and

> अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते पृथिव्यामत्यो न यंसद्यक्षभृद्विचेताः । मृगाणां न हेतयो यन्ति चेमा बृहस्पतेरहिमायाँ अभि द्यून् ॥

> *asya śloko divīyate pṛthivyām atyo na yaṃsad yakṣabhṛd vicetāḥ | mṛgāṇāṃ na hetayo yanti cemā bṛhaspater ahimāyāṃ abhi dyūn ‖* [as read: [?]]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-190-4 [?]) — in such ṛks *atanaśīlaḥ* ("the one who goes") means the Āditya also: the Sun, who moves about. In the ṛk at hand it is a word that is a synonym of horse.

### Printed p. 434  (PDF 454)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 177".)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***brahmayujaḥ*** — *brahmaṇā yujyante iti brahmayujaḥ*; root *yujir yoge*; by "*satsūdviṣadruhaduhayujavidabhidacchidajinīrājām upasarge 'pi kvip*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-61 [?]) the suffix *kvip*; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent; nominative plural.
- ***vṛṣarathāsaḥ*** — a *bahuvrīhi* compound; by "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*" the fore-member keeps its natural accent; when *jas* follows, by "*ajjhanasyerasuk*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50 [?], sūtra name as read) the augment *asuk*.
- ***tān + ā*** — by "*dīrghād aṭi samānapāde*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-9 [?]) *ru* for the *n*; by "*ato 'ṭi nityam*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-3 [?]) the preceding *ā* always takes nasalization.
- ***tiṣṭha*** — root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *loṭ*, second person singular; *nighāta* for a *tiṅ*.
- ***havāmahe*** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" gives *saṃprasāraṇa* in *laṭ*; first person plural; because it is in *pādādi* position no *nighāta*; the *la* *sārvadhātuka* being *anudātta* (by "*tāsyanudāttet*…"), the root accent remains.
- ***sute*** — root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; the suffix *kta* by the *niṣṭhā* rule; by the suffix accent the end syllable is *udātta*; locative singular. ‖ 2 ‖

### Printed p. 435  (PDF 455)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 20"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 435.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे इन्द्र त्वं रथमा तिष्ठ । आश्रयस्व यज्ञगमनार्थम् । कीदृशं रथम् । वृषणं वर्षकं कामानाम् । किमर्थमिति चेत् उच्यते । ते त्वदर्थं वृषा वर्षकः सोमः सुतः । अभिषुतः । तथा मधूनि मधुराणि घृतक्षीरादीनि परिषिक्ता । परितः सिक्तानि संपादितानि । यद्वा । मधूनि मधुराः सोमरसाः चमसेषु पूरिताः । आगमनप्रकार उच्यते । हे वृषभ वर्षकेन्द्र वृषभ्यां वर्षकाभ्यां हरिभ्यां युक्त्वा रथं योजयित्वा क्षितीनां कर्मसु निवसतां यजमानानामस्माकमनुग्रहाय । क्षितीनां वृषभेति वा योज्यम् । प्रवता वेगवता रथेन मद्रिक् [?] अस्मदभिमुखमेव [?] उप याहि ॥

*Gist:* Indra is asked to mount his showering chariot, since Soma is pressed and sweet offerings (ghee, milk) are ready; harnessing the two showering horses, he is to come swiftly towards us for our benefit.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **Indra** — O Indra! **te** — for you; **vṛṣā** — the one that showers desired objects, **somaḥ** — the Soma juice, **sutaḥ** — has been pressed (**tathā**, likewise), **madhūni** — sweet things such as ghee and milk, **pariṣiktā** — are sprinkled all around [or: **madhūni** — sweet Soma juices, **pariṣiktā** — are filled in the cups]. (Therefore) **vṛṣaṇam** — the giver of what is wanted, **ratham** — your chariot, **ā tiṣṭha** — mount; **kṣitīnām** — of the people (performing rites), the sacrificers; (*he*) **vṛṣabha** — O Indra who grants desires; **vṛṣabhyām** — with the showering, **haribhyām** — with the two (horses), **yuktvā** — having harnessed (the chariot), **kṣitīnām** — for the sacrificers who perform rites, our own favour; **pravatā** — with the swift chariot; **madrik** — towards us, facing us; **upa yāhi** — come near to us.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra, who showers desires! The Soma juice, which showers desires and is sweet, has been pressed and placed for you in the cups (and sweet things such as ghee are ready). Therefore mount your chariot that showers what is wanted: O Indra, giver of desired things to the sacrificers, harness to the chariot the two horses that give what is wanted, and, for the favour of us the sacrificers, sit in the swift chariot and come facing us.

**Printed English**

> Ascend your bounty-shedding car, for, for you the Soma, the showerer of benefiits [sic], is effused, the sweet libations are prepared. Bounty-shedding Indra, having harnessed them, came [sic] with your vigorous steeds for (the good of) mankind; come with your rapid (car) to my presence.

### Printed p. 436  (PDF 456)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 177"; page 436.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

*vṛṣaṇaṃ ratham; vṛṣā somaḥ; vṛṣabhyāṃ haribhyām; vṛṣabha* — and so on: words formed from the word *vṛṣan* are used as epithets of the chariot, of Soma, of Indra's horses and of Indra himself. Although the sense of the root is one and the same, these epithets have differences of meaning suited to the context.

The words *vṛṣā* (from the root *vṛṣu secane* — "to sprinkle, to rain", giving what is wanted) and *vṛṣaṇa* are probably formed from that root; the words *vṛṣabhyām*, *vṛṣabha* are probably formed from the second root *vṛṣa śaktibandhane* ("to bind strength") that gives the sense "power and capacity". The word *vṛṣan* and the other epithets derived from this root have to be given the sense that suits the context.

The word *vṛṣan* is used in many places in the sense of one possessed of the power to sprinkle, "male"; this word is used either as a synonym of *puruṣa* ("man"), the masculine-indicating word, or as a synonym of horses and other creatures.

> ये त इन्द्र ददुषो वर्धयन्ति महि क्षत्रं स्थविरं वृष्ण्यं च ।

> *ye ta indra daduṣo vardhayanti mahi kṣatraṃ sthaviraṃ vṛṣṇyaṃ ca |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-8 [?]) — in this the word *vṛṣṇyam* is *vṛṣatvam* and *puṃstvam* ("manliness");

> स्तुतः श्रवस्यन्नवसोप मद्रिग्युक्त्वा हरी वृषणा योह्यर्वाङ् ।

> *stutaḥ śravasyannavasopa madrigyuktvā harī vṛṣaṇā yohyarvāṅ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-82-3 [?]) — in the preceding ṛk *yuvānā* is said to mean "those who have attained", and in

> भूषन्न योधि बभ्रूषु नम्नते वृषेव पत्नीरभ्येति रोरुवत्

> *bhūṣanna yodhi babhrūṣu namnate vṛṣeva patnīrabhyeti roruvat*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-140-6 [?]) — *vṛṣā iva* is "like a bull that performs sprinkling (*secana*)"; and in

> मिनाति श्रियं जरिमा तनूनामप्यू नु पत्नीर्वृषणो जगम्युः ॥

> *mināti śriyaṃ jarimā tanūnāmapyū nu patnīrvṛṣaṇo jagamyuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-179-1 [?]) — *vṛṣaṇaḥ* is "*sektāraḥ puruṣāḥ*" (sprinklers, men). So also in many other places this word, indicating the masculine as it does, is used in meanings that show the power of male creatures. And in the same manner:

> वृषा वां मेघो वृषणा पीपाय गोर्न सेके मनुषो दशस्यन्

> *vṛṣā vāṃ megho vṛṣaṇā pīpāya gorna seke manuṣo daśasyan*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-8 [?]) — [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 437  (PDF 457)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 20"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 437.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

> दस्मो हि ष्मा वृषणं पिन्वसि त्वचं कं चिद्यावीररुं [?] शूर मर्त्यं परिवृणक्षि मर्त्यम् ॥

> *dasmo hi ṣmā vṛṣaṇaṃ pinvasi tvacaṃ kaṃ cidyāvīraruṃ [?] śūra martyaṃ parivṛṇakṣi martyam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-129-3 [?])

> ता तो ते सत्या तुविनृम्ण विश्वा प्र धेनवः सिस्रते वृष्ण ऊध्नः ॥

> *tā to te satyā tuvinṛmṇa viśvā pra dhenavaḥ sisrate vṛṣṇa ūdhnaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-23-6 [?])

— in such places *vṛṣṇaḥ* is used in the sense "the one who sprinkles water, the one who sprinkles desired objects" (*varṣakaḥ, varṣaṇaparamanasyaḥ* — as read [?]). Besides this, other meanings also occur here and there, in an unusual manner; yet the word *vṛṣṇya* has chiefly the sense of an extraordinary power and virility (*vīrya*), as seen in many places:

> आ प्यायस्व समेतु ते विश्वतः सोम वृष्ण्यम्

> *ā pyāyasva sametu te viśvataḥ soma vṛṣṇyam*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-16 [?])

> महाँ असि महिष वृष्ण्येभिर्धनस्पृदुग्र सहमानो अन्यान्

> *mahā~ asi mahiṣa vṛṣṇyebhirdhanaspṛdugra sahamāno anyān*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-46-2 [?])

> वि चर्मणीव धिषणे अवर्तयद्वैश्वानरो विश्वमधत्त वृष्ण्यम्

> *vi carmaṇīva dhiṣaṇe avartayadvaiśvānaro viśvamadhatta vṛṣṇyam*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-3 [?])

— in these and many other ṛks the sense of *vṛṣṇya* is common: virility (*vīrya*) and prowess. Besides, since in many contexts the word *vṛṣan* is used as a synonym of Indra and other deities, in such places it must be inferred, in keeping with the context, that this or that deity is meant.

> अपोषा अनसः सरत्संपिष्टादह बिभ्युषी । नि यत्सीं शिश्नथद्वृषा

> *apoṣā anasaḥ saratsaṃpiṣṭādaha bibhyuṣī | ni yatsīṃ śiśnathadvṛṣā*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-10 [?])

— here it can be inferred that *vṛṣā* is a synonym of Indra. But in many places there is doubt about which deity is meant; and sometimes even Sāyaṇācārya, when giving the sense of this epithet, does not state a definite opinion. For example:

> वृषा छन्दुर्भवति हर्यतो वृषा क्षेमेण धेनां मघवा यदिन्वति

> *vṛṣā chandurbhavati haryato vṛṣā kṣemeṇa dhenāṃ maghavā yadinvati*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-55-4 [?]) — in this ṛk he gives room for doubt, saying first that *vṛṣā* is "*haviṣāṃ varṣayitā yajamānaḥ*" (the sacrificer who rains down oblations), and then "*yadvā vṛṣā indraḥ*" ("or *vṛṣā* is Indra"). Thus, because the word is used in many meanings, in each place the meaning suited to it has to be made out. In explaining this word, rich in suggestion, the English commentator Max Müller has shown the depth of the ideas it conveys, as follows:

### Printed p. 438  (PDF 458)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 177"; page 438.)*

> "In Vrishan we have one of those words which it is almost impossible to translate accurately. It accurs [sic] over and over again in the Vedic hymns and if we once know the various ideas which it either expresses or implies, we have little difficulty in understanding its import in a vague and general-way, though we look in vain for corresponding terms in any modern language.......................and we shall see how difficult it would be to translate such terms without losing either the key-note that was still sounding or the harmonies which were set vibrating by it in the minds of the poets and their listeners.
> [F. Max Muller S. B. E. Vol. XXXII. P. 138–39]"

In the ṛks under consideration it can be said that the word *vṛṣan* is used in all the senses stated above.

***haribhyām — harī indrasya*** (Ni. 3-25 [?]) — the Nirukta-writers have stated that this name is well known for Indra's horses.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***pariṣiktā*** — root *ṣicir kṣaraṇe*; the suffix *kta* by *niṣṭhā*; by "*coḥ kuḥ*" the *c* of the root becomes *k*-class; by "*gatir anantaraḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49 [?]), as an exception to the *kṛdutta* rule of the final member's natural accent, the fore-member (*pari*, a *gati*) keeps its natural accent. In the neuter plural, by "*śeś chandasi bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 [?]) there is elision of *śi*.
- ***kṣitīnām*** — root *kṣi nivāsagatyoḥ*; by "*striyāṃ ktin*" the suffix *ktin*; genitive plural; by "*nāmanyatarasyām*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-177 [?]) the *udātta* accent comes on *nām*.
- ***pravatā*** — by "*upasargāc chandasi dhātvarthe*" (Pā. Sū. 5-1-118 [?]) the suffix *vati* after *pra*; the suffix takes the *ādyudātta* accent; instrumental singular. ‖ 3 ‖

*(ornamental rule)*

**Sūkta 177, Ṛk 4**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> अयं यज्ञो देवया अयं मियेध इमा ब्रह्माण्ययमिन्द्र सोमः ।
> स्तीर्णं बर्हिरा तु शक्र प्र याहि पिबा निषद्य वि मुचा हरी इह ॥ ४ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> अयम् । यज्ञः । देवऽयाः । अयम् । मियेधः । इमा । ब्रह्माणि । अयम् । इन्द्र । सोमः ।
> स्तीर्णम् । बर्हिः । आ । तु । शक्र । प्र । याहि । पिब । निऽसद्य । वि । मुच । हरी इति । इह ॥ ४ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अहर्गणेषु मध्येष्वहःसु हारियोजनग्रहस्य याज्या । अग्निष्टोमोऽत्यग्निष्टोम इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । अयं यज्ञो देवया अयं मियेध इतीतरेषु । आ ६-१० [?] इति ॥ हे इन्द्र अयं यज्ञो देवयाः देवान् [?] गच्छन् [?] भवति । तथायं यज्ञो मियेधः । मेधः पशुः । पशुर्वै मेध इति हि श्रुतिः । इमानि [?] ब्रह्माणि मन्त्राः । अयं सुतः सोमः । स्तीर्णं बर्हिः । आसनायास्तृता दर्भाः । एते पदार्थास्त्वदुचिता एवं संपादिताः । हे शक्रेन्द्र तु पुनः किमित्युक्ते आ प्र याहि । प्रकर्षेण शीघ्रमागच्छ । आगत्य च निषद्य बर्हिष्युपविश्य पिब सोमम् । तदर्थमिहास्मिन्देवयजने हरी अश्वौ वि मुच । वियोजय ॥ छान्दसो नुमभावः ॥

*Gist:* This ṛk is the *yājyā* of the *hāriyojana* cup on the middle days of the *ahargaṇa* (Āśvalāyana, Śrauta-sūtra 6-10 [?]); Indra is told that sacrifice, victim, mantras, Soma and spread grass are ready, and is asked to come quickly, sit, drink and unyoke his horses here.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **Indra** — O Indra! **ayaṃ yajñaḥ** — this sacrifice; **devayāḥ** — goes towards the deities (is intended for the deities); **ayam** — this; **miyedhaḥ** — the sacrificial victim (the animal fit to be offered); **imā** — these; **brahmāṇi** — the mantras; **ayam** — this; **somaḥ** — (pressed) Soma juice; **barhiḥ** — the *darbha* grass; **stīrṇam** — has been strewn (for a seat); (therefore) (*he*)

### Printed p. 440  (PDF 460)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 177"; page 440.)*

**śakra** — O Indra; **tu** — again; **ā pra yāhi** — come quickly; (having come) **niṣadya** — sitting (on the *darbha* grass); **piba** — drink (the Soma juice); (for that) **iha** — in this sacrificial hall; **harī** — your two horses; **vi muca** — unyoke (from the chariot).

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra! This sacrifice, which is for the deities; this victim fit for the sacrifice; these mantras; this pressed Soma; these spread *darbha* grass — all of these are ready for you. Therefore, O Indra, come quickly, unyoke the horses from the chariot, sit on the *darbha* seat, and drink the Soma juice.

**Printed English**

> This is the sacrifice offered to the g..ds [sic]: this is the offering of the victim: these are the prayers: this Indra, is the Soma juice: the sacred grass is ready strewn: come therefore, Indra, quickly, sit down, drink (the libation). here let loose your steeds.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***ahargaṇeṣu madhyeṣv ahaḥsu hāriyojanagrahasya yājyā*** — with these words Sāyaṇa has stated the application (*viniyoga*) of this mantra. For the word *hāriyojana* a general sense can be given: Indra yokes his bay horses (*hari*) to the chariot. Since in the present context the drinking of Soma by Indra and Indra's yoking of the horses to the chariot are both included, it is understood that the name *hāriyojana-graha* ("the cup of the harnessing of the bays") covers all these items. In the Ṛk-saṃhitā the word *hāriyojana* is used in only two places; but the mantras belonging to this cup are different (elsewhere). Therefore the two questions — what meaning the commentator gave to this word, and what the special sense is of the ṛks connected with the *hāriyojana-graha* — have to be examined here.

> इवा ते हारियोजना सुवृक्तीन्द्र ब्रह्माणि गोतमासो अक्रन् ।
> ऐषु विश्वपेशसं धियं धाः प्रातर्मक्षू धियावसुर्जगम्यात् ॥

> *ivā te hāriyojanā suvṛktīndra brahmāṇi gotamāso akran |*
> *aiṣu viśvapeśasaṃ dhiyaṃ dhāḥ prātarmakṣū dhiyāvasurjagamyāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-16 [?]) — in this the word *hāriyojana* is an epithet of Indra. Sāyaṇa has explained: ***haryor aśvayor yojanaṃ yasmin rathe sa tathoktaḥ | tasya svāmitvena saṃbandhī hāriyojanaḥ indraḥ*** — "the chariot in which the yoking of the two bays is done is so called; Indra, who is related to it as its owner, is *hāriyojana*"; that is, the meaning is "the Indra on whose chariot the horses called *hari* are fastened". But, … [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 441  (PDF 461)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 20"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 441.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

> स घा तं वृषणं रथमधि तिष्ठाति गोविदम् ।
> यः पात्रं हारियोजनं पूर्णमिन्द्र चिकेतति योजा न्विन्द्र ते हरी ॥

> *sa ghā taṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ rathamadhi tiṣṭhāti govidam |*
> *yaḥ pātraṃ hāriyojanaṃ pūrṇamindra ciketati yojā nvindra te harī ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-82-5 [?]) — here *hāriyojana-mety-saṃjñakam* (as read [?]): Sāyaṇa explains it as "the vessel full of Soma, mixed with grain (*dhānā*), that is called *hāriyojana*"; *hāri* means grain-mixed Soma juice. In the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa, in the portion called *Hāriyojana-graha*, two ṛks connected with that cup are prescribed. Of these, the first is:

> तिष्ठा सु कं मघवन्मा परा गाः सोमस्य नु त्वा सुषुतस्य यक्षि ।
> पितुर्न पुत्रः सिचमा रभे त इन्द्र स्वादिष्ठया गिरा शचीवः ॥

> *tiṣṭhā su kaṃ maghavanmā parā gāḥ somasya nu tvā suṣutasya yakṣi |*
> *piturna putraḥ sicamā rabhe ta indra svādiṣṭhayā girā śacīvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-35-2 [?]) — and the second is the ṛk 1-82-5 cited above; so it is explained that these are the two mantras of this occasion. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā the matter of the *hāriyojana* is given thus:

> हरिरसि हारियोजनो हर्योः स्थाता वज्रस्य भर्ता पृश्नेः प्रेता तस्य ते देव सोमेस्वयजुषः [?] स्तुतस्तोमस्य शस्त्रोक्थस्य हरिवन्तं ग्रहं गृह्णामि हरीः स्थ हर्योर्धानाः सह सोमा इन्द्राय स्वाहा ॥

> *harirasi hāriyojano haryoḥ sthātā vajrasya bhartā pṛśneḥ pretā tasya te deva somesvayajuṣaḥ [?] stutastomasya śastrokthasya harivantaṃ grahaṃ gṛhṇāmi harīḥ stha haryordhānāḥ saha somā indrāya svāhā ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-4-38 [?]) — explaining the word *hāriyojana* used here, Bhaṭṭabhāskara says:

> हरिरसीति । सोमः एवोच्यते । हरिरिन्द्रः । स एव त्वमसीतीन्द्रात्मना सोमः स्तूयते । यद्वा हरिर्हर्ता अभिमतानां श्रेयसामाहर्ता त्वमसि । हारियोजनः हरिः अश्वविशेषः योजनो वाहनं यस्य स हरियोजनः इन्द्रः तस्य स्वभूतः हारियोजनः इन्द्रोऽसीत्यर्थः ।

> *harirasīti | somaḥ evocyate | haririndraḥ | sa eva tvamasītīndrātmanā somaḥ stūyate | yadvā harirhartā abhimatānāṃ śreyasāmāhartā tvamasi | hāriyojanaḥ hariḥ aśvaviśeṣaḥ yojano vāhanaṃ yasya sa hariyojanaḥ indraḥ tasya svabhūtaḥ hāriyojanaḥ indro 'sītyarthaḥ |*

— he has given the sense that *hāriyojana* is the Soma; "*hari* means Indra's horses; the one who has those horses as his vehicle is *hariyojana*, i.e. Indra; since it belongs to that Indra, the name *hāriyojana* became well known." In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa the same matter is explained thus:

> अथ हारियोजनं गृह्णाति । छन्दांसि वै हारियोजनश्छन्दांस्येवैतत्संतर्पयति तस्माद्धारियोजनं गृह्णाति ॥

> *atha hāriyojanaṃ gṛhṇāti | chandāṃsi vai hāriyojanaśchandāṃsyevaitatsaṃtarpayati tasmāddhāriyojanaṃ gṛhṇāti ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 4-4-3-2 [?]) — and so on, the matter of the *hāriyojana-graha* has been explained. In the present context there is no need for a detailed account of it; therefore, when occasion for explaining it arises later, the nature of this cup and its nature as a limb of the rite will be given. In the mantra at hand, which is connected with such a *hāriyojana-graha*, [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 442  (PDF 462)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 177"; page 442.)*

… "*ayaṃ yajñaḥ; ayam miyedhaḥ*" — "this sacrifice is offered; this animal is offered", and so on — Indra is directly addressed.

***yajñaḥ*** — "*yajña*" means in the gross sense an act of worship (*pūjākarma*). The Nirukta-writers explain the derivation of this word at length:

> यज्ञः कस्मात् प्रख्यातं यजति कर्मेति नैरुक्ताः । याच्ञो भवतीति वा । यजुरुन्नो भवतीति वा । बहुकृष्णाजिन इत्यौपमन्यवः । यजूंष्येनं नयन्तीति वा ॥

> *yajñaḥ kasmāt prakhyātaṃ yajati karmeti nairuktāḥ | yācño bhavatīti vā | yajurunno bhavatīti vā | bahukṛṣṇājina ityaupamanyavaḥ | yajūṃṣyenaṃ nayantīti vā ‖*

(Ni. 3-19 [?]) — "*yajña* is the well-known rite of worship", is the view of the Nirukta-writers. Some say it is a petition made in the presence of the deities (*yācñā*); others, that it is that in which *yajus* mantras raise up (*unna*); others, that it is so called because black antelope skins are numerous in it (so Aupamanyava); still others, that the *yajus* mantras lead it forward — so they give different etymologies.

***miyedhaḥ*** — here this word is used as a synonym of *paśu* ("animal"). *Miyedha* means "fit for *medha*", i.e. fit for sacrifice or fit for praise. It is used in some places also as a synonym of *yajña*. For example:

> आ देवानामग्रयावेह यातु नराशंसो विश्वरूपेभिरश्वैः ।
> ऋतस्य पथा नमसा मियेधो देवेभ्यो देवतमः सुषूदत् ॥

> *ā devānāmagrayāveha yātu narāśaṃso viśvarūpebhiraśvaiḥ |*
> *ṛtasya pathā namasā miyedho devebhyo devatamaḥ suṣūdat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-20-3 [?], as read) — here *miyedhaḥ* is explained *medhyaḥ yajñahitaḥ stutiyogyo vā* ("fit for the sacrifice, beneficial to the sacrifice, or worthy of praise") as an epithet of Agni; and

> अग्निं होतारं प्र वृणे मियेधे गृत्सं कविं विश्वविदममूरम् ।
> स नो यक्षद्देवताता यजीयान्राये वाजाय वनते मघानि ॥

> *agniṃ hotāraṃ pra vṛṇe miyedhe gṛtsaṃ kaviṃ viśvavidamamūram |*
> *sa no yakṣaddevatātā yajīyānrāye vājāya vanate maghāni ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-19-1 [?]) — here *miyedhe asmābhiḥ kriyamāṇe 'smin yajñe* ("in this sacrifice being performed by us") is used as a synonym of the sacrifice.

In the ṛk at hand, *medhaḥ paśuḥ*: the commentator states that the word *miyedha* is a synonym of *paśu*, which is fit for the sacrifice, and to support his meaning he cites the *śruti* sentence "*paśur vai medhaḥ*" ("the animal is the sacrifice"). Likewise in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also:

> कतमो यज्ञ इति पशव इति ।

> *katamo yajña iti paśava iti |*

(Śa. Brā. 11-2-3-6 [?]) — [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 443  (PDF 463)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 20"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 443.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — by this sentence, *yajña* is "animal" and the animal is *yajña*: the identity (*tādātmya*) of the two words is shown and explained. On that same basis, in the ṛk at hand also *medha* can be taken as *paśu*. "This is your animal" — so Indra is addressed.

***śakra — sarvakāryeṣu samarthaḥ indraḥ*** — "Indra, capable in all tasks": the epithet indicates Indra's capacity. In the Ṛk-saṃhitā this epithet is used also of other deities; but here it is a unique epithet, describing Indra's exceeding power.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***devayāḥ*** — root *yā prāpaṇe*; suffix *kvip*; nominative singular; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent.
- ***miyedhaḥ*** — from *medhaḥ*, with a Vedic change of letters (*varṇavikāra*) in the form.
- ***imā*** — by "*śeś chandasi bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 [?]) the elision of *śi* in the neuter plural.
- ***stīrṇam*** — root *stṛñ ācchādane*; suffix *kta* in the passive; by "*ṛta iddhātoḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-100 [?]) *i* for the root vowel, with *r* following; by "*hali ca*" lengthening; by "*radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 8-2-42 [?]) *n* for the *t* of the *kta* suffix; by *raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ* (sūtra named only) the *ṇ*; by the suffix accent the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***piba*** — root *pā pāne*; *loṭ*, second person singular; since it is in *pādādi* position no *nighāta*; *śap* being *pit*, the root accent remains; by "*dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-135 [?]) lengthening in the Saṃhitā.
- ***niṣadya*** — root *ṣad viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; suffix *ktvā*; by "*samāse 'nañpūrve ktvo lyap*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-37 [?]) *lyap* replaces it; being *pit* it is *anudātta*; by "*upasargāt sunoti…*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-65 [?]) *ṣatva*; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent.
- ***muca*** — root *muñc mokṣaṇe*; *loṭ*, second person singular; by "*śe muceādīnām*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-59 [?]) the *num* augment that would be required does not occur, being Vedic; as before, lengthening in the Saṃhitā by "*dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ*". ‖ 4 ‖

**Sūkta 177, Ṛk 5**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> ओ षु सुष्टुत इन्द्र याह्यर्वाङुप ब्रह्माणि मान्यस्य कारोः ।
> विद्याम वस्तोरवसा गृणन्तो विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ ५ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> ओ इति । सुऽस्तुतः । इन्द्र । याहि । अर्वाक् । उप । ब्रह्माणि । मान्यस्य । कारोः ।
> विद्याम । वस्तोः । अवसा । गृणन्तः । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥ ५ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे इन्द्र सुष्टुतोऽस्माभिः सम्यक्स्तुतः सन्नर्वाङ् [?] अस्मदभिमुखमा याहि । आगच्छैव [?] । मा विलम्बय [?] । किमुद्दिश्य । मान्यस्य माननीयस्य कारोः स्तोतुः होतुः कर्तुर्यजमानस्य वा ब्रह्माणि मन्त्रानुपोपलक्ष्य । गृणन्तः स्तुवन्तोऽभिमतं शब्दयन्तो वा वयमवसा त्वद्रक्षणेन रक्षिताः सन्तो वस्तोः वस्तुं सुखेन संस्थातुमहनि वा सर्वेष्वहःस्वन्नादिकं विद्याम । लभेमहि । विद्यामेत्यादि व्याख्यातम् ॥

*Gist:* Indra, well praised by us, is asked to come at once towards us for the mantras of the honoured sacrificer; protected by him, we shall get dwelling in comfort, food, strength and long life.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **Indra** — O Indra; **suṣṭutaḥ** — well praised (by us); **mānyasya** — of the honoured; **kāroḥ** — of the praiser, the priest, or of the sacrificer who performs the rite; **brahmāṇi** — the mantras; **upa** — having in view; **arvāk** — facing us; **o yāhi** — come right here; **gṛṇantaḥ** — we, who praise you or express what we desire; **avasā** — protected by your protection; **vastoḥ** — for dwelling in comfort, or on all days, **vidyāma** — may we obtain; **iṣam** — food; **vṛjanam** — strength; **jīradānum** — long life; **vidyāma** — may we obtain (by your favour).

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra! Being well praised by us, come facing us, with the mantras of the praising, honoured sacrificer in view; and for us, protected by you, for dwelling in comfort, grant food, strength and long life.

### Printed p. 445  (PDF 465)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 20"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 445.)*

**Printed English**

> Glorified by us, Indra, come to (our) presence to accept the prayers of the venerable offerer (of the oblation); so that we may ever enjoy prosperity through your protection, and thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***brahmāṇi*** — the word *brahma* has been explained earlier with many other senses. In the ṛk at hand, as in the preceding ṛk, the word is used in the sense "mantras"; i.e. mantras that have grown (*parivṛḍha*).

***kāroḥ — stotur hotuḥ kartur yajamānasya*** — "of the praiser, the *hotṛ*, the doer, the sacrificer": it is explained as the one who both praises and performs the sacrifice. The Nirukta-writers have listed the word *kāru* among the names of the praiser (*stotṛ*) (Ni. 3-19 [?]). The author of the Bṛhaddevatā has used this word in the sense "poets, i.e. the ṛṣis who are seers of the sūktas":

> अग्नेस्तु योनि [?] सूक्तानि पञ्च सामानि कारवः ।
> षड्विंशतिस्तथेन्द्रस्य प्राहुः सूर्यस्य सप्त च ॥

> *agnestu yoni [?] sūktāni pañca sāmāni kāravaḥ |*
> *ṣaḍviṃśatistathendrasya prāhuḥ sūryasya sapta ca ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-22 [?])

> पृथक्त्वेन समासैस्तु यज्ञे यच्चैस्यते [?] नृभिः ।
> स्तुवन्त्याप्रीषु तेनेमं नराशंसं तु कारवः ॥

> *pṛthaktvena samāsaistu yajñe yaccaisyate [?] nṛbhiḥ |*
> *stuvantyāprīṣu tenemaṃ narāśaṃsaṃ tu kāravaḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-27 [?]) — in such sentences *kāravaḥ* is used as a synonym of the word "poets", *kavi*, meaning "those who praise". In the Ṛk-saṃhitā also:

> प्रदक्षिणिदभि [?] गृणन्ति कारवो वयो वदन्त ऋतुथा शकुन्तयः ।
> उभे वाचौ वदति सामगा इव गायत्रं च त्रैष्टुभं चानु राजति ॥

> *pradakṣiṇidabhi [?] gṛṇanti kāravo vayo vadanta ṛtuthā śakuntayaḥ |*
> *ubhe vācau vadati sāmagā iva gāyatraṃ ca traiṣṭubhaṃ cānu rājati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-43-1 [?])

> वि चेदुच्छन्त्यश्विना उषासः प्र वां ब्रह्माणि कारवो भरन्ते ।
> ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सविता देवो अश्रेद्बृहदग्नयः [?] समिधा जरन्ते ॥

> *vi ceducchantyaśvinā uṣāsaḥ pra vāṃ brahmāṇi kāravo bharante |*
> *ūrdhvaṃ bhānuṃ savitā devo aśredbṛhadagnayaḥ [?] samidhā jarante ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-72-4 [?]) — in these and other ṛks *stotāraḥ* ("praisers") is the sense in which the word is used. In the ṛk at hand also, the sacrificer who is the praiser…

… is the meaning. [The sentence runs on from the previous page.]

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***suṣṭutaḥ*** — root *ṣṭuñ stutau*; suffix *kta* in the passive; by "*gatir anantaraḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49 [?]) the *gati* (*su*) takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***kāroḥ*** — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; by "*kṛvāpā…*" (Uṇ. [?]) the suffix *uṇ*; the *nimitta* gets *vṛddhi*; *raparatva*; by the suffix accent the final syllable is *udātta*; genitive singular.
- ***vastoḥ*** — root *vas nivāse*; in the sense of the infinitive, by "*īśvare tosunkasunau*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-13 [?]) the suffix *tosun*; since the suffix has *ñ* as marker, by "*ñnityādir nityam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 [?]) the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***gṛṇantaḥ*** — root *gṝ śabde*; *laṭ* replaced by *śatṛ*; by "*pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-80 [?]) shortening of the root; by "*śnābhyastayor ātaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-112 [?]) elision of the *ā* of the *vikaraṇa*; since *ṛ* precedes, *ṇatva*; the suffix takes the *ādyudātta* accent. ‖ 5 ‖

## Sūkta 178 (the 178th Sūkta; "Nūra eppatteṃṭaneya sūktavu")

***yaddha syā*** — *pañcarcaṃ caturdaśaṃ sūktam āgastyam aindraṃ traiṣṭubham | yaddha syety anukramaṇikā ‖ viśeṣaviniyogaḥ pūrvavat ‖*

*Translation of the introduction:* This Sūkta beginning "*yaddha syā*" is the fourteenth sūkta in the twenty-third Anuvāka. It has five ṛks. Its ṛṣi is Agastya; Indra is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā begins "*yaddha syā*". "As before" means: as in the preceding sūkta, this sūkta has a special application — for the augmenting of the *stoma*, in the recitation (*śaṃsana*) of *śastra* mantras.

**Sūkta 178**

Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 23 ‖ Sūkta 178 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 21 ‖

### Printed p. 447  (PDF 467)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 447.)*

**Sūkta 178, Ṛk 1**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> यद्ध स्या त इन्द्र श्रुष्टिरस्ति यया बभूथ जरितृभ्य ऊती ।
> मा नः कामं महयन्तमा धग्विश्वा ते अश्यां पर्याप आयोः ॥ १ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> यत् । ह । स्या । ते । इन्द्र । श्रुष्टिः । अस्ति । यया । बभूथ । जरितृऽभ्यः । ऊती ।
> मा । नः । कामम् । महयन्तम् । आ । धक् । विश्वा । ते । अश्याम् । परि । आपः । आयोः ॥ १ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे इन्द्र यद्वा स्यासौ [?] प्रसिद्धा श्रुष्टिः सर्वत्र श्रूयमाणा सम्पृद्धिस्ते त्वास्ति [?] यया जरितृभ्यः स्तोतृभ्य ऊत्यै रक्षणाय बभूथ समर्थो भवसि नोऽस्माकं महयन्तमस्मान्महतः कुर्वाणं कामममीष्टं मा धक् । मा दाक्षीः । ते तव सम्बन्धीनि विश्वा सर्वाणि भोगजातान्याप आप्तव्यानि [?] । यद्वा । विश्वा सर्वा आप आप्ताः श्रुतयः [?] आयोर्मनुष्यस्योचिताः । पर्यश्याम् । परितो व्याप्नुयाम् ॥

*Gist:* Indra possesses a well-known, widely heard prosperity by which he protects his praisers; may he not frustrate our desire for greatness, and may we obtain all that is fit for man by his favour.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **Indra** — O Indra; **yat ha** — for which reason; **syā** — that well-known; **śruṣṭiḥ** — prosperity heard of everywhere; **te** — for you; **asti** — there is; **yayā** — by which; **jaritṛbhyaḥ** — of the praisers; **ūtī** — for protection; **babhūtha** — you are capable; (therefore) **naḥ** — our; **mahayantam** — greatness-seeking; **kāmam** — desire; **mā ā dhak** — do not frustrate; **āyoḥ** — fit for man; **te** — related to you; **viśvā āpaḥ** — all obtainable enjoyments etc.; **pari aśyām** — may I obtain (by your favour).

**Bhāvārtha**

O Indra! You have well-known prosperity by which you are able to protect your praisers. Therefore do not frustrate our wish for greatness; and may we obtain, from among the enjoyments that are yours, those that are fit for men.

### Printed p. 448  (PDF 468)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 448.)*

**Printed English**

> Inasmuch, Indra, as the praise by which you are (induced to bestow) protection on your adorers is heard (by all), therefore disappoint not the desire (that would raise us) to greatness: may I obtain, through your (favour), all things that are obtainable by man.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***śruṣṭiḥ*** — "*śruṣṭīti kṣipranāma āśu aṣṭīti*" — the word *śruṣṭi*, which gives the sense "to pervade quickly", the Nirukta-writers have said is to be counted among the names of "swift" (*kṣipra*) (Ni. 6-12 [?]); and to show the usage of the word, the Ṛk-saṃhitā ṛk

> ता अध्वर उशतो यक्ष्यग्ने श्रुष्टी भगं नासत्या पुरंधिम् ।

> *tā adhvara uśato yakṣyagne śruṣṭī bhagaṃ nāsatyā puraṃdhim |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-4 [?]) is cited and explained. Sāyaṇa too takes it as "swift". But in the ṛk at hand only, *śruṣṭiḥ — sarvatra śrūyamāṇā samṛddhiḥ* ("prosperity heard of everywhere") — he explains it as "prosperity renowned in all regions". Since this is said, the root here has to be different. Note how others elsewhere explain the same word:

> वनेषु जायुर्मर्तेषु मित्रो वृणीते श्रुष्टिं राजेवाजुर्यम् ।

> *vaneṣu jāyurmarteṣu mitro vṛṇīte śruṣṭiṃ rājevājuryam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-67-1 [?]) — in this ṛk the Nirukta-writers' own derivation is cited (Ni. 6-12 [?]): "one who performs rites quickly" — so it is explained that the word is used as a synonym of the sacrificer. Thus different meanings, too, become possible according to the context. For example:

> नकिष्ट एता व्रता मिनन्ति नृभ्यो यदेभ्यः श्रुष्टिं चकर्थ ।

> *nakiṣṭa etā vratā minanti nṛbhyo yadebhyaḥ śruṣṭiṃ cakartha |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-69-9 [?]) — in this ṛk "*śu āśu aśnute vyāpnotīti śruṣṭir yajñaphalarūpaṃ sukham*" ("what quickly pervades — *śruṣṭi* — is the happiness that is the fruit of the sacrifice") it is used as a synonym of "happiness", because it quickly reaches the sacrificer along with the performance of the sacrifice. Likewise in the Ṛk-saṃhitā,

> गिरा च श्रुष्टिः सभरा असन्नो नेदीय इत्सृण्यः पक्वमेयात् ।

> *girā ca śruṣṭiḥ sabharā asanno nedīya itsṛṇyaḥ pakvameyāt |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-101-9 [?]) — it is explained as "food". And again:

> आपी वो अस्मे पितरेव पुत्रोग्रेव रुचा नृपतीव तुर्यै [?] ।
> इर्यैव पुष्ट्यै किरणेव भुज्यै श्रुष्टीवानेव हवमा गमिष्टम् ॥

> *āpī vo asme pitareva putrogreva rucā nṛpatīva turyai [?] |*
> *iryaiva puṣṭyai kiraṇeva bhujyai śruṣṭīvāneva havamā gamiṣṭam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-106-4 [?]) — [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 449  (PDF 469)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 449; signature mark "XIII 29".)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … in this ṛk he explains it in two ways: first as "*śruṣṭīvān iva kṣipravantau aśvāv iva*" ("like two swift horses") and second as "*sukhavantau puruṣāv iva*" ("like two men possessed of happiness"), giving the import. Thus the meaning suited to the context has to be told for this word. The scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit–English Dictionary, has included for this word the sense "obedience, willing service"; that too has "swift" as its import: the word is evidently used when one means doing a thing at once, according to another's wish. Taking all together, the sense of the word should be given in keeping with the context. In the ṛk at hand Sāyaṇa's explanation is "prosperity (*saṃpat-samṛddhi*) that wins renown swiftly [?]".

***āyoḥ*** — the word *āyu* is here explained as "man" (*manuṣya*). For this word too the meaning has to be given according to the context. This word may denote a person who has attained [the power of] going about, or a community. The Nirukta-writers also support this view; thus in the Nirukta:

> मा नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुरिन्द्र ऋभुक्षा मरुतः परि ख्यन् ।
> यद्वाजिनो देवजातस्य सप्तेः प्रवक्ष्यामो विदथे वीर्याणि ॥

> *mā no mitro varuṇo aryamāyurindra ṛbhukṣā marutaḥ pari khyan |*
> *yadvājino devajātasya sapteḥ pravakṣyāmo vidathe vīryāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]62-1 [?]) — the word *āyu* in this ṛk is explained; here *āyu* means "wind" (*vāyu*). *āyuś ca vāyur ayanaḥ* — "*āyu* is Vāyu, the goer"; because the one that moves about throughout the universe (*viśvam*) [as read: "*etihy asau viśvam* [?]"] is wind, the name *āyu* (with elision of the *v*) is said to be well known — Durgācārya has so explained (Ni. 9-3 [?]). Besides, the word *āyu* is used in the senses *āyuḥ* ("life") and *manuṣya*, and in many places it is also used as a proper name, pointing to different persons. For example:

> येन ज्योतींष्यायवे मनवे च विवेदिथ ।
> मन्दानो अस्य बर्हिषो वि राजसि ॥

> *yena jyotīṃṣyāyave manave ca viveditha |*
> *mandāno asya barhiṣo vi rājasi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-15-3 [?]) — here *aurvaśeyāyu*: *āyuve, manave ca* — it is understood that "Āyu" and "Manu" are different persons; here *āyu* is used as a proper name. Some English commentators (Vedic Subjects and Proper Names, by Macdonell & Keith, Vol. I) —

> त्वमस्मै कुत्समतिथिग्वमायुं महे राज्ञे यूने अरन्धनायः ।

> *tvamasmai kutsamatithigvamāyuṃ mahe rājñe yūne arandhanāyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-53-10 [?])

### Printed p. 450  (PDF 470)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 450.)*

> य आयुं कुत्समतिथिग्वमर्दयो वावृधानो दिवेदिवे ।

> *ya āyuṃ kutsamatithigvamardayo vāvṛdhāno divedive |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-53-2 [?]) — citing these two ṛks, they infer that the person called *Āyu* must be an adversary of Indra. Since *arandhanāyuḥ* and *ardayaḥ* ("subdued", "harassed") occur — "he harassed him, he made him his own" — they say that he is understood to be Indra's enemy. But in this context, in the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, for "*ardayaḥ*" Sāyaṇa says: "*āyuṃ āyunāmānam ṛṣiṃ varapradānena pīḍayasi*" — "you oppress the ṛṣi named Āyu by giving him boons" — and explains that Indra burdens devotee-friends like Āyu with the load of granting boons and so "harasses" them. But this is an imported meaning; the explanation is not natural. Besides:

> मा नो गुह्या रिप आयोरहन्दभन्नशविष्ठा [?] मा आभ्यो रीरधो दुच्छुनाभ्यः ।

> *mā no guhyā ripa āyorahandabhannaśaviṣṭhā [?] mā ābhyo rīradho ducchunābhyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-32-2 [?]) — in this, for the word *āyoḥ* Sāyaṇa himself has stated plainly: *śatrubhūtasya manuṣyasya* — "of the man who is an enemy". And again:

> युयोप नाभिरुपरस्यायोः प्र पूर्वाभिस्तिरते राष्टि शूरः ।

> *yuyopa nābhiruparasyāyoḥ pra pūrvābhistirate rāṣṭi śūraḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-104-4 [?]) — here too: "*āyoḥ pareṣām upadravārtham itas tato gacchataḥ kuyavasya asurasya*" — "of the Asura Kuyava, who goes hither and thither to molest others", is the sense he gives. It is established that this is a person in the form of an enemy. But again:

> कुत्सस्यायोरतिथिग्वस्य वीरान्न्यावृणग्भरता सोममस्मै ।

> *kutsasyāyoratithigvasya vīrānnyāvṛṇagbharatā somamasmai |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-7 [?]) — in such places Kutsa, Atithigva and Āyu are all evidently stated to be friends needed by Indra. Thus there are persons named Āyu who are enemies of the deities and of sacrificers; the Āyu who is Indra's friend is another; the Āyu who is Agni's friend is yet another; and the fact that there was a lineage known by the name Āyu is known from many *śruti* sentences. For example:

> उर्वश्यसीत्यथोत्तरारणिमाज्यविलापनीमुपस्पृशत्यायुरसीति तामभिनिदधाति पुरूरवा असीत्यैर्वशी वाप्सराः पुरूरवाः पतिरथ यत्तस्मान्मिथुनादजायत तदायुरेवैनमेवैष एतस्मान्मिथुनाद्यज्ञं जनयति [?]

> *urvaśyasītyathottarāraṇimājyavilāpanīmupaspṛśatyāyurasīti tāmabhinidadhāti purūravā asītyairvaśī vāpsarāḥ purūravāḥ patiratha yattasmānmithunādajāyata tadāyurevainamevaiṣa etasmānmithunādyajñaṃ janayati [?]*

(Śa. Brā. 3-4-1-20 [?]) — [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 451  (PDF 471)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 451.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … in this [sentence] it is said that Āyu was born of Urvaśī and Purūravas, and so the identity (*tādātmya*) of Āyu and Agni is stated. Likewise:

> आयुषो न मध्यादित्यग्निर्वा आयुः ।

> *āyuṣo na madhyādityagnirvā āyuḥ |*

(Śa. Brā. 2-2-1-15 [?]) — in this sentence also the identity of Agni and Āyu is stated. But there it is one view that the word *āyu* is a proper name (*aṅkitanāma*); another view is that it is not. Since in many places the word *āyoḥ* has been explained as "Manu", it can be understood that this is Manu, one of the Prajāpatis who were creators.

In many places the words *āyuḥ*, *āyoḥ* are used as synonyms of "the man (*mānava*) who is a performer of sacrifices, who goes about (*ayana*, *saṃcāra*) hither and thither for the performance of sacrifice". For example:

> होत्राभिरग्निर्मनुषः स्वध्वरो राजा विशामतिथिश्चारुरायवे ।

> *hotrābhiragnirmanuṣaḥ svadhvaro rājā viśāmatithiścārurāyave |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-2-8 [?])

> इमं विधन्तो अपां सधस्थे द्वितादधुर्भृगवो विक्ष्वा [?] आयोः [?] ।

> *imaṃ vidhanto apāṃ sadhasthe dvitādadhurbhṛgavo vikṣvā [?] āyoḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-4-2 [?])

> प्र स्वादनं पितूनामस्ततातिं चिदायवे [?] ।

> *pra svādanaṃ pitūnāmastatātiṃ cidāyave [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-2-6 [?]) — in these and many other ṛks the word *āyu* is understood from the bhāṣya to mean the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice. But Oldenberg and other English translators take all these as proper names and have rendered the ṛks accordingly. Thus, since the word is used in many senses, in the ṛk at hand it means "man who performs a sacrifice".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***asti*** — by "*hi ca*" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34 [?]) the prohibition of *nighāta* occurs, so the root accent remains.
- ***jaritṛbhyaḥ*** — root *jṛṣ vayohānau* (used here in the sense of praising); the suffix *tṛc* in the agent; by "*citaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 [?]) the final syllable is *udātta*; dative plural.
- ***ūtī*** — by "*ūtiyūtijūti…*" (Pā. Sū. 3-3-97 [?]) *ktin* is irregularly formed with *udātta*; dative singular; by "*supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇa…*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) the *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening as single substitute.

### Printed p. 452  (PDF 472)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 452.)*

- ***mahayantam*** — root *mah pūjāyām*; by "*hetumati ca*" the suffix *ṇic*; after *ṇic*, *laṭ* comes and *śatṛ* replaces it; *śap* being the cause, the *ṇic* takes *guṇa* and *ayādeśa*; the *lasārvadhātuka* accent by "*tāsyanudāttet…*" is *anudātta*, so the *ṇic* accent remains; accusative singular.
- ***dhak*** — root *dah bhasmīkaraṇe*; by "*mā ṅi luṅ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-3-175 [?], as read) *luṅ*; second person singular, *sip*; loss of *i*; by "*mantre ghasahvaranaśavṛdahādvṛc…*" (Pā. Sū. 2-4-80 [?]) *cli* is elided; by "*halyabbhyo…*" the *sip* is elided; by "*dādeḥ dhātor ghaḥ*" the *h* of the root becomes *gh*; by "*ekāco baśo bhaṣ…*" (sūtra named) the initial *d* becomes *dh*; by "*vāvasāne*" *cartva*; by "*namājñyoge*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-74 [?]) the *aṭ* augment does not occur; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***viśvā*** — by "*śeś chandasi bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 [?]) elision of *śi*.
- ***aśyām*** — root *aśū vyāptau*; by "*vyatyayo bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 [?]) *parasmaipada*; *liṅ*, first person singular; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" elision of the *vikaraṇa*; *yāsuṭ* augment; *nighāta* accent.
- ***āyoḥ*** — root *iṇ gatau*; by "*chandasīṇaḥ*" (Uṇ. 1-2 [?]) the suffix *uṇ*; by "*āco ñṇiti*" *vṛddhi*; *āy* substitution; the final syllable *udātta* by the suffix accent; genitive singular. ‖ 1 ‖

**Sūkta 178, Ṛk 2**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> न घा राजेन्द्र आ दभन्नो या नु स्वसारा कृणवन्त योनौ ।
> आपश्चिदस्मै सुतुका अवेषन्गमन्न इन्द्रः सख्या वयश्च ॥ २ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> न । घ । राजा । इन्द्रः । आ । दभत् । नः । या । नु । स्वसारा । कृण्वन्त । योनौ ।
> आपः । चित् । अस्मै । सुऽतुकाः । अवेषन् । गमत् । नः । इन्द्रः । सख्या । वयः । च ॥ २ ॥

> *na | gha | rājā | indraḥ | ā | dabhat | naḥ | yā | nu | svasārā | kṛṇvanta | yonau |*
> *āpaḥ | cit | asmai | su 'tukāḥ | aveṣan | gamat | naḥ | indraḥ | sakhyā | vayaḥ | ca ‖ 2 ‖*

### Printed p. 453  (PDF 473)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 453.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अयं राजा राजमानः ईश्वरो वेन्द्रो नोऽस्मदीयानि कर्माणि ना दभत् । सर्वतो न हिंस्यात् । कानीति उच्यते । यो यानि कर्माणि वृष्ट्यादिरूपाणि स्वसारा परस्परं स्वसृभूते स्वयंसरणभूते अहोरात्रे । नु पूरणः । योनौ स्वकीये स्थाने कृण्वन्त ॥ द्विवचनस्थाने बहुवचनं ॥ कुरुतः ॥ कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । धिन्विकृण्व्योर च इत्यप्रत्ययः । बहुलग्रहणाच्छप् ॥ तानिन्द्रोऽपि अनुजानाति इत्यर्थः । स्वसृभूतावध्वर्युर्यजमानौ वा कुरुतः । यद्वा । स्वसारौ अङ्गुलयः योनौ फलोत्पादनस्थाने यज्ञे यानि कृतवन्तः तानीति योज्यम् । किंचास्मै इन्द्राय सुतुकाः शोभनबलहेतवः अन्नाद्या आपः हवींषि अवेषन् । व्याप्नुवन्ति । सोऽस्मभ्यमिन्द्रः सख्या सख्यानि वयः च प्रभूतमन्नं च गमत् । गमयतु ॥ [as read; several words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Indra is not to frustrate the rain-and-other acts that Day and Night (or the two priests, or the fingers) perform in their place; oblations strengthen him, and may he bring us friendship and abundant food.

**Pratipadārtha**

**yā nu** — which (acts such as rain); **svasārā** — the mutually sister-like day and night; **yonau** — in their own place; **kṛṇavanta** — do; [or **yā** — which acts; **svasārā** — the *adhvaryu* and the sacrificer, like sisters; **yonau** — in the sacrifice; **kṛṇavanta** — do;] [or **svasārā** — the fingers; **yonau** — in the sacrifice, the place producing the fruit; **kṛṇavanta** — do;] (**tāni** — those); **naḥ** — our (acts); **rājā** — the shining, or sovereign; **indraḥ ghā** — Indra; **na ā dabhat** — let him not obstruct; (**kiṃ ca** — and further); **asmai** — to this Indra; **sutukāḥ** — causes of good strength; **āpaḥ cit** — the oblations etc.; **avēṣan** — pervade; **naḥ** — to us; **indraḥ** — Indra; **sakhyā** — friendship; **vayaḥ ca** — and abundant food; **gamat** — may he bring.

**Bhāvārtha**

Let Indra not obstruct the acts, such as rain, which the day and night, sister-like, carry on in their own places (or which the *adhvaryu* and sacrificers perform in the sacrifice). All oblations, causes of strength, go to Indra alone. May his friendship and abundant food be granted to us.

**Printed English**

> Let not the royal Indra frustrate those our actions, which the sisters, (day and night), are directing to their object. May these invigorating offerings propitiate him, so that he may bestow upon us friendly (regard), and (abundant) food.

### Printed p. 454  (PDF 474)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 454.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In the ṛk at hand Sāyaṇa has stated three kinds of meaning for the word *svasārā*: first, "day and night"; second, the *adhvaryu* and the sacrificer, who are "like sisters"; third, the fingers, which are the means for the sacrificial act. Accordingly the word *yoni* too has to be explained in agreement with these meanings. First: ***yā nu svasārā yonau kṛṇavanta*** means: the acts such as rain which day and night, as sisters, perform in their own place. To see that this is right, one has to examine the natures of day and night and the acts by which they help each other.

Uṣas (Dawn) is said to be the elder sister of Night. With the rising of Uṣas, Night becomes invisible and gives place to her sister.

> अरुषस्य दुहितरा विरूपे स्तृभिरन्या पिपिशे सूरो अन्या ।
> मिथस्तुरा विचरन्ती पावके मन्म श्रुतं नक्षत ऋच्यमाने ॥

> *aruṣasya duhitarā virūpe stṛbhiranyā pipiśe sūro anyā |*
> *mithasturā vicarantī pāvake manma śrutaṃ nakṣata ṛcyamāne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-49-3 [?]) — in many such ṛks, describing the relation between Night and Uṣas, it is explained how both, by their constant, regulated movement, cause the life of the world. Day and night, being the mothers who cause the birth of Parjanya (rain), the fruit of the sacrifice, and likewise of food, are thus the root cause.

> नक्तोषासौ च ये देव्यावाग्नेय्यावेव ते स्मृते ।

> *naktoṣāsau ca ye devyāvāgneyyāveva te smṛte |*

(Bṛ. De. 3-8 [?])

> नक्तोषासा वर्णमामेम्याने धापयेते शिशुमेकं समीची ।

> *naktoṣāsā varṇamāmemyāne dhāpayete śiśumekaṃ samīcī |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-5 [?]) — in such places day and night are said to help Agni, the lord of the sacrifice, to drink the oblations. And because of this relation:

> आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ ।
> दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥

> *ā suṣvayantī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau |*
> *divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-6 [?]) — in such ṛks day and night are said to be the sacrificer's neighbours. Because they are connected with the things of the sacrifice that bring about worldly affairs, they have the epithet *ṛtasya mātarā* ("the two mothers of the *ṛta*"). Such sister-like day and night, in their own place, carry out the acts such as rain … [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 455  (PDF 475)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 455.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … so it is explained. Here the word *yoni* means "place of origin". Many other meanings of the word *yoni* have been given earlier; among them, "place of origin" is the one most commonly known in usage.

> वेदिषदे प्रियधामाय सुद्युते धासिमिव प्र भरा योनिमग्नये ।

> *vediṣade priyadhāmāya sudyute dhāsimiva pra bharā yonimagnaye |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-140-1 [?]) — in such ṛks it is well known that *yoni* denotes the place called the altar (*vedi*). In Saṃhitā sentences such as "*ā sve yonau niṣīdatu*" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-40 [?]) and in Brāhmaṇa sentences such as "*eṣa ha vā asya svo yonir yadagnir agneḥ* [?]" (Ai. Brā. 1-18 [?]) this meaning is explained too. Besides this, for "*yonau*" in the ṛk at hand, Sāyaṇa has explained *yoni* as a synonym of *yajña* ("the sacrifice, the place that produces fruit"). This meaning is also natural. For, since the sacrifice is the cause of the origin and the maintenance of all worlds, and is the means of binding, in mutual relation, all beings from the gods downward, it has the epithets *bhuvanasya yoniḥ*, *bhuvanasya nābhiḥ* ("womb of the world", "navel of the world") and so on. Since the sacrifice is the place of origin for all worldly dealings, it is well known as *yoni*. Thus:

> स एतेन यज्ञेन देवेभ्य आत्मानं निरक्रीणीत स यद्वै तेन [?] यथैव [?] यत्वे [?] प्रजापतिर्देवेभ्य आत्मानं प्रायच्छदेवमेवैष एतद्देवेभ्य आत्मानं प्रयच्छति तस्मादु संयत एवैतां रात्रिं चिचरिषेद्यथा हविषा चरेदेवं हविर्ह्येष देवानां भवति ।

> *sa etena yajñena devebhya ātmānaṃ nirakrīṇīta sa yadvai tena [?] yathaiva [?] yatve [?] prajāpatirdevebhya ātmānaṃ prāyacchadevamevaiṣa etaddevebhya ātmānaṃ prayacchati tasmādu saṃyata evaitāṃ rātriṃ cicariṣedyathā haviṣā caredevaṃ havirhyeṣa devānāṃ bhavati |*

(Śa. Brā. 11-1-8-3 [?]) — Prajāpati, pleased with the sacrifice of the gods, offered himself to them; afterwards he made again a counterpart of himself, a substitute for the sacrifice (*yajña-pratinidhi*). Thus, for the sake of the sacrifice, he created his own likeness; and those who understood this reflection call Prajāpati, the womb of the world, by the name *yajña*. This sacrifice is the thread that shows the single connection of everything in the world; it is also called "the wheel of the world" (*viśvacakra*). For example:

> अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसंभवः ।
> यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥
> कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।
> तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥

> *annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasaṃbhavaḥ |*
> *yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ ‖*
> *karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam |*
> *tasmātsarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam ‖*

(Bha. Gī. 3-14 to 15, as printed [?]) — from the sacrifice, which is action, comes rain; from rain, food; from food, the beings. This sacrifice in the form of action arose from Brahman. Therefore, beginning with the creation of the world, for all kinds of worldly dealings and for the recurring cycle that is the wheel of the world, the supreme Brahman is constantly established in the sacrifice. [The passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 456  (PDF 476)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 456.)*

… and so on: in the Gītā and elsewhere the sacrificer's role in the sacrifice is described as taught in Vedic statements. This truth of the sacrifice, described as "*bhuvanasya yoniḥ*" ("the womb of the world"), the Ṛk-saṃhitā praises in this way also in various other portions. For example:

> यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजन्त देवास्तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् ।
> ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचन्त यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः सन्ति देवाः ॥

> *yajñena yajñamayajanta devāstāni dharmāṇi prathamānyāsan |*
> *te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacanta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-16 [?]) — the gods worshipped Prajāpati in the form of the sacrifice, by the sacrifice, which was their own resolve (*saṅkalpa*) in form and meditative in nature. All the cosmic laws (*dharma*) have this sacrifice as their root. These very laws of the sacrifice, established in the intermediate region, are in the places of the gods who dwell in heaven. It is by the sacrifice that all beings obtain the food and the strength that sustain them. This sacrifice itself places the three worlds in their stability. Thus:

> कल्पन्तेऽस्मा इमे लोका ऊर्जं प्रजासु दधाति त्रिरात्रेणैवेमं लोकं कल्पयति त्रिरात्रेणान्तरिक्षं त्रिरात्रेणामुं लोकं यथा गुणे गुणमन्वस्यत्येवमेवैतल्लोके लोकमन्वस्यति धृत्या अशिथिलं भावाय ।

> *kalpante 'smā ime lokā ūrjaṃ prajāsu dadhāti trirātreṇaivemaṃ lokaṃ kalpayati trirātreṇāntarikṣaṃ trirātreṇāmuṃ lokaṃ yathā guṇe guṇamanvasyatyevamevaitalloke lokamanvasyati dhṛtyā aśithilaṃ bhāvāya |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 7-3-4-3 [?]) — through this sacrifice in the form of nine nights, the three worlds obtained coherence. By a three-night rite he set the earth in order, by a three-night rite the intermediate region, and by the remaining three-night rite the heavenly world: Prajāpati established them with the sacrifice's own power of maintenance. As the weaver joins thread with thread (warp and woof, *otaprota*) to make cloth, so, to prevent looseness and to produce for all a single bond-like power, he established for the three worlds, in their fixed positions, the relation of warp and woof. This sacrifice is the pulse (*nāḍi*) of the life of the world. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa describes this very thing:

> सर्वेषां वा एष भूतानां सर्वेषां देवानामात्मा यद्यज्ञस्तस्य समृद्धिमनु यजमानः प्रजया पशुभिर्ऋध्यते ।

> *sarveṣāṃ vā eṣa bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ devānāmātmā yadyajñastasya samṛddhimanu yajamānaḥ prajayā paśubhirṛdhyate |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-3-2-1 [?]) — the sacrifice is stated to be the soul of all men and of all deities. Thus, in the order of the world, for every individual to attain an existence full of its own power, the sacrifice is the thread that links the general with the particular. This sacrifice, in the form of a thread, grows along with the expansions and contractions of the world; at one time it expands, at another it contracts … [the passage continues on the next page.]
