### Printed p. 457  (PDF 477)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 457.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … together with the motion of the world it takes on its own motion. Explaining this point, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa gives the derivation of the word *yajña* thus:

> अथ यस्माद्यज्ञो नाम । घ्नन्ति वा एनमेतद्यदभिषुण्वन्ति तद्यदेनं तन्वते तदेनं जनयन्ते स तायमानो जायते स यज्ञा [?] यते [?] तस्माद्यज्ञो यज्ञो ह वै नाम्यैतद्यज्ञ इति [?] ..........

> *atha yasmādyajño nāma | ghnanti vā enametadyadabhiṣuṇvanti tadyadenaṃ tanvate tadenaṃ janayante sa tāyamāno jāyate sa yajñā [?] yate [?] tasmādyajño yajño ha vai nāmyaitadyajña iti [?] ..........*

(Śa. Brā. 3-9-4-23 [?]) — at the time of pressing (*abhiṣava*) they kill it; then they cause it to be born again. Because it is born together with a motion of expansion, it became known by the name *yajña*. This sacrifice, being always in keeping with the states of the world, is beneficial to the world. How? —

> भुज्युः सुपर्ण इति । यज्ञो वै भुज्युः यज्ञो हि सर्वाणि भुनक्ति यज्ञो गन्धर्वः ..........

> *bhujyuḥ suparṇa iti | yajño vai bhujyuḥ yajño hi sarvāṇi bhunakti yajño gandharvaḥ ..........*

(Śa. Brā. 9-4-1-11 [?]) — the sacrifice expects all beings for its offering (*āhuti*), and again goes out for the benefit of all beings. In this way, by showing the identity-relation (*tādātmya*) of the principle of the world and the sacrifice with other things, it is stated that the sacrifice itself is the cause of all worldly dealings, that the very relation in the form of a thread is the navel of the world. This is what is indicated in the ṛk at hand by the word *yoni*.

In this womb of the world, the *svasṛ*s ("sisters"), having performed their acts, are ready to see that those who engage in the world's dealings suffer no obstruction. These *svasṛ*s may be:

1. in the form of day and night; or
2. in the form of the sacrificer and the *adhvaryu*; or
3. in the form of the fingers, the instruments of the sacrifice (the Nirukta-writers have counted the word *svasṛ* among the names of the fingers, Ni. 3-9 [?]). — So Indra is prayed to make the acts performed in such a womb of the world faultless and fruitful.

***sutukāḥ*** — Sāyaṇa explains this word as "*śobhanabalopetāḥ*" ("endowed with good strength"). The Nirukta-writers explain *sutuka* as "of excellent movement", and in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, describing Agni's advance:

> स आ वक्षि महि न आ च सत्सि दिवस्पृथिव्योररतिर्युवत्योः ।
> अग्निः सुतुकः सुतुकेभिरश्वै रभस्वद्भी रभस्वाँ एह गम्याः ॥ [as read [?]]

> *sa ā vakṣi mahi na ā ca satsi divaspṛthivyoraratiryuvatyoḥ |*
> *agniḥ sutukaḥ sutukebhiraśvai rabhasvadbhī rabhasvā~ eha gamyāḥ ‖ [as read [?]]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-3-7 [?])

### Printed p. 458  (PDF 478)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 458.)*

— citing this ṛk, he explains "*sutukenaḥ*" [as read [?]]. In this cited ṛk Sāyaṇa too says: "*tukir gatyarthaḥ | sugamaḥ stotṛbhiḥ yaṣṭṛbhiś ca sukhena prāptavyaḥ*" ("*tuk* means going; easy to go to, easily reached by praisers and sacrificers"). But according to the Nirukta-writers' derivation, the word seems to describe here the excellent going, or the advance, of Agni. In the ṛk at hand, as an epithet of *āpaḥ* it can only mean "that which gives its fruit quickly".

***rājā indraḥ*** — "*rājamānaḥ īśvaro vā*" ("shining, or sovereign"): the word *rājā* is an epithet of Indra, in the sense "shining" or "universal emperor". Indra has the epithets *samrāṭ*, *svarāṭ* and the like in many places. For example, in the Ṛk-saṃhitā:

> आवासृजन्त जिव्रयो न देवा भुवः सम्राळिन्द्र सत्ययोनिः । [as read [?]]

> *āvāsṛjanta jivrayo na devā bhuvaḥ samrāḷindra satyayoniḥ | [as read [?]]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-19-2 [?]) — in this ṛk *samrāṭ* is described as the protector of all the worlds and the abode (*niyāsa*) of truth. And likewise:

> सम्राळन्यः स्वराळन्य उच्यते वां महान्तावुद्रावरुणा [?] महावसू ।
> विश्वे देवासः परमे व्योमनि सं वामोजो वृषणा सं बलं दधुः ॥

> *samrāḷanyaḥ svarāḷanya ucyate vāṃ mahāntāvudrāvaruṇā [?] mahāvasū |*
> *viśve devāsaḥ parame vyomani saṃ vāmojo vṛṣaṇā saṃ balaṃ dadhuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-68-2 [?]) — in such ṛks Indra and Varuṇa, who are independent of any other, are described by the epithets *samrāṭ*, *svarāṭ*. The greatness that lies in these epithets of Indra and Varuṇa, and the special character of the epithets, will be explained later in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. In the ṛk at hand also, by the epithet *rājā*, the same idea is shown.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***ghā*** — by "*ṛcitunughamakṣu…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-133 [?]) lengthening in the Saṃhitā.
- ***dabhat*** — root *dambhu dambhe*; *laṅ* used in the sense of *loṭ* in Vedic; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" elision of the *vikaraṇa*; by "*bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi*" the *aṭ* augment does not occur; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***yā*** — by "*śeś chandasi bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 [?]) elision of *śi*.
- ***svasārā*** — by "*supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇa…*" the dual takes *ā* substitution.

### Printed p. 459  (PDF 479)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 459.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, continued)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***kṛṇavanta*** — root *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*; Vedic *laṭ* in the present sense; by "*vyatyayo bahulam*" the *ātmanepada* and, for the dual, the plural suffix; *jhi* has *anta* substituted; by "*dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-80 [?]) the suffix *u*, with *a* substituted for the final; by "*ato lopaḥ*" its elision; Vedic *śap*; taking that as the cause, *guṇa* for the suffix *u*, with *av* substitution; the Vedic *aṭ* augment occurs; because of *yad*-connection there is no *nighāta* accent; the *lasārvadhātuka* being *anudātta*, the *vikaraṇa* accent remains.
- ***sutukāḥ*** — in a *bahuvrīhi*, the fore-member's accent being set aside, by "*dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-135 [?], as printed) the hind-member takes *ādyudātta*.
- ***āveṣan*** — root *viṣḷ vyāptau*; Vedic *laṅ* plural, Vedic *śap*; by "*pugantalaghūpadhasya ca*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86 [?]) *guṇa* for the short penultimate vowel; *aṭ* augment for the stem; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***gamat*** — root *gamḷ gatau*; because the causative activity is intended, it is *antarbhāvitaṇyartha* (contains the sense of the causative); Vedic *luṅ* in the sense of *loṭ*; with *tip* following, by "*puṣādidyutādi…*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-55 [?]) *aṅ* in place of *cli*; the Vedic *aṭ* does not occur; being in a *tiṅanta* word no *nighāta* accent appears; the suffix being *pit*, the root accent remains.
- ***sakhyā*** — *sakhyur bhāvaḥ sakhyam*; by "*sakhyur yaḥ*" the suffix *ya*; by "*yasyeti ca*" elision of *i*; final *udātta* by the suffix accent; in the neuter plural, by "*śeś chandasi bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 [?]) elision of *śi*. ‖ 2 ‖

> प्रभर्ता रथं दाशुष उपाक उद्यन्ता गिरो यदि च त्मना भूत् ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 460  (PDF 480)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 460.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अयमिन्द्रः शूरो विक्रान्तः सन्नृभिः संग्रामनेतृभिर्मरुद्भिः सहितः सन्पृत्सु संग्रामेषु जेता जयशीलः शत्रूणां तथा नाधमानस्य त्वदनुग्रहं याचमानस्य कारोः स्तोतुर्हवमाह्वानं श्रोता भवति । किंच यदि च यदा च त्मनात्मनानन्यप्रेरित एव गिरः स्तुतिरूपाणि वचांसि स्तोत्वानोद्यन्ता [?] भूत् भवेत् तदा दाशुषो हविर्दात्वतो यजमानस्योपाके समीपे रथं प्रभर्ता । सम्यक् प्रभरति ॥ जेतेत्यादिषु तृनन्तेषु न लोकाव्ययेत्यादिना कर्मणि षष्ठीप्रतिषेधः ॥ यदा स्तुतिं श्रोतुमिच्छति तदा स्वयमेव शीघ्रं रथं धावयित्वा योगं प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः ॥ [as read; several words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Indra, the brave victor with the Maruts, hears the call of the one who begs his favour; and when he wishes to hear praise, he himself quickly drives his chariot near the sacrificer.

**Pratipadārtha**

**śūraḥ** — the hero; **indraḥ** — Indra; **nṛbhiḥ** — together with the leaders in battle, the Maruts; **pṛtsu** — in battles; **jetā** — victorious; (**tathā** — likewise) **nādhamānasya** — of the one who begs his favour; **kāroḥ** — of the praiser; **havam** — the call; **śrotā** — becomes the hearer; **yadi ca** — and whenever; **tmanā** — of himself (impelled by none); **giraḥ** — the words of praise (the praisers); **udyantā bhūt** — becomes the one who takes up; (**tadā** — then) **dāśuṣaḥ** — of the sacrificer who gives oblations; **upāke** — near; **ratham** — the chariot; **prabhartā** — becomes the one who brings it quickly.

**Bhāvārtha**

Indra, who is a hero, who has the Maruts for companions, and who is victorious in battles, listens to the call of the sacrificer who longs for his favour; and when he wishes to hear the praises, he drives his chariot swiftly to the sacrificer's side.

**Printed English**

> Indra, the hero, the victor in battles, along with the leaders (of his hosts, the Maruts), will hear the invocation of his supplicating worshipper, and when disposed to accept his praises, will, of his own accord, drive his chariot close to the donor (of the oblation).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***kāroḥ*** — this word is explained as "the sacrificer who offers praise". The Nirukta-writers have counted the word *kāru* among the names of the *stotṛ* (praiser) (Ni. 3-8 [?]); explaining that words such as *rebhaḥ*, *jaritā* are known as synonyms, and in the Ṛk-saṃhitā … [the passage continues on the next page.]

**Special Topics (continued)**

> दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै ।
> प्रचोदयन्ता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशन्ता ॥

> *daivyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai |*
> *pracodayantā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśantā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-7 [?]) — in this ṛk *kartārau ṛtvijau* ("the two doers, the priests") is explained: the two persons who are the agents of the sacrificial act, i.e. the two *ṛtvij*s. The author of the Bṛhaddevatā has used this word in the sense of "poets", i.e. the ṛṣis who are the seers of sūktas, showing the sense "makers of praise".

> अग्नेस्तु योनि [?] सूक्तानि पञ्च सामानि कारवः ।
> षड्विंशतिस्तथेन्द्रस्य प्राहुः सूर्यस्य सप्त च ॥

> *agnestu yoni [?] sūktāni pañca sāmāni kāravaḥ |*
> *ṣaḍviṃśatistathendrasya prāhuḥ sūryasya sapta ca ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-22 [?])

> पृथक्त्वेन समासैस्तु यज्ञे यच्चैस्यते [?] नृभिः ।
> स्तुवन्त्याप्रीषु तेनेमं नराशंसं तु कारवः ॥

> *pṛthaktvena samāsaistu yajñe yaccaisyate [?] nṛbhiḥ |*
> *stuvantyāprīṣu tenemaṃ narāśaṃsaṃ tu kāravaḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-27 [?]) — in such sentences it is said that the *kāru*s sing praise, and this is explained as a synonym of "poet". In the Ṛk-saṃhitā also:

> प्रदक्षिणिदभि [?] गृणन्ति कारवो वयो वदन्त ऋतुथा शकुन्तयः ।
> उभे वाचौ वदति सामगा इव गायत्रं च त्रैष्टुभं चानु राजति ॥

> *pradakṣiṇidabhi [?] gṛṇanti kāravo vayo vadanta ṛtuthā śakuntayaḥ |*
> *ubhe vācau vadati sāmagā iva gāyatraṃ ca traiṣṭubhaṃ cānu rājati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-43-1 [?]) — in these and other ṛks the sense is *stotāraḥ* ("praisers"). In the ṛk at hand too the meaning is the poets (ṛṣis) who are the makers of the praise.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***jetā*** — root *ji jaye*; the suffix *tṛn* in the agent; taking that as the cause, *guṇa* for the *i* of the root; by "*ñnityādir nityam*" the *ādyudātta* accent. In combination with this and the next three *tṛnanta* words, although by "*kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti*" (Pā. Sū. 2-3-65 [?]) the genitive would arise for the object, by "*na lokāvyayaniṣṭhākhalarthatṛnām*" (Pā. Sū. 2-3-69 [?]) the prohibition applies, so the genitive does not occur.
- ***pṛtsu*** — the word *pṛtanā*; when the locative plural follows, by the *vārttika* "*māṃsapṛtanāsānūnāṃ māṃspṛtsnūvo śasādau vā vācyaḥ*" the substitution *pṛt*. By "*ūḍidaṃpadādi…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 [?]) the case-ending takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***nādhamānasya*** — root *nādhṛ yācñāyām*; *śānac* for *laṭ*; *śap* as the *vikaraṇa*; by "*ānemuk*" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-82 [?]) the augment *muk*; by "*tāsyanudāttet…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 [?]) the *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta*, so the root accent remains.

### Printed p. 462  (PDF 482)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 462.)*

- ***dāśuṣaḥ*** — root *dāś dāne*; by "*dāśvān sāhvān…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-12 [?]) the *kvasu*-final form is irregularly derived; the genitive singular following, since it has the name *bha*, *saṃprasāraṇa* occurs, with the earlier form; by the suffix accent the middle syllable is *udātta*.
- ***prabhartā*** — root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*; the suffix *tṛn* in the agent; *guṇa* for the root vowel; *raparatva*; by "*tāda ca niti kṛtyatau*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50 [?]) the *gati* (*pra*) keeps its natural accent.
- ***tmanā*** — from the form *ātmanā*; by "*mantreṣv āṅy ādeḥ ātmanaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-141 [?]) elision of the initial *a*. ‖ 3 ‖

**Sūkta 178, Ṛk 4**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> एवा नृभिरिन्द्रः सुश्रवस्या प्रखादः पृक्षो अभि मित्रिणो भूत् ।
> समर्य इषः स्तवते विवाचि सत्राकरो यजमानस्य शंसः ॥ ४ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> एव । नृऽभिः । इन्द्रः । सुऽश्रवस्या । प्रऽखादः । पृक्षः । अभि । मित्रिणः । भूत् ।
> सऽमर्ये । इषः । स्तवते । विऽवाचि । सत्राऽकरः । यजमानस्य । शंसः ॥ ४ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अयमिन्द्रो नृभिः कर्मनिर्वाहकैर्यजमानैर्दत्तं पृक्षो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं सुश्रवस्या शोभनान्नेच्छयोऽन्नेच्छुर्वा प्रखादः प्रकर्षेण खादिता एवमेवैवमेव [?] पूर्वं यथा तथैव मित्रिणः सहायवतोऽपि यजमानस्य शत्रूनभि भूत् । अभिभवति । यद्वा । नृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिर्मरुद्भिः सहितोऽयमिन्द्रः सुश्रवस्या प्रखादः सन्नेवमेव मित्रिण ऋत्विग्मरुन्मित्रवतो यजमानस्यार्थे तदभिमतायाभि भूत् । अभिमुखेन वा भवति । तस्य हविः स्वीकृत्य तदभिमतायाभिभवतीत्यर्थः । अथ तथाभूतः सन् विवाचि विविधपरस्परा [?] आह्वानध्वनियुक्ते समर्ये संग्रामे विविधस्तोत्रशस्त्रध्वनियुक्ते समर्ये मर्त्ययुक्ते यज्ञे वा तन्मित्रं यजमानस्य शंसः शंसकः सन् सत्राकरः फलानां सत्यकार्ययमिन्द्र [?] इषो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं स्तवते । स्तौति ॥ [as read; the middle of the passage is doubtful [?]]

### Printed p. 463  (PDF 483)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 463.)*

**Pratipadārtha**

**indraḥ** — Indra; **nṛbhiḥ** — by the sacrificers who carry out the rites; **pṛkṣaḥ** — the food in the form of the oblation; **suśravasyā** — from desire of good food, or from desire for food; **prakhādaḥ** — the good eater (he becomes); **eva** — in just that way; **mitriṇaḥ** — (the sacrificer) who has helpers; **abhi bhūt** — overcomes (his enemies); [or: **nṛbhiḥ** — with the Maruts, the deities who lead the rain; **indraḥ** — this Indra; **suśravasyā** — from desire for auspicious food; **pṛkṣaḥ** — oblation-food; **prakhādaḥ** — good eater; **eva** — likewise; **mitriṇaḥ** — of the sacrificer united with *ṛtvij*s, Maruts and friends; **abhi bhūt** — becomes favourable (for his desire)]; **vivāci** — in the many-voiced, i.e. in the battle where calls are exchanged; **samarye** — in the battle [or: **vivāci** — in the sacrifice with its manifold stotra and śastra sounds; **samarye** — in the sacrifice attended by men]; **yajamānasya** — of the sacrificer; **śaṃsaḥ** — the praiser; **satrākaraḥ** — the maker of true fruits; **indraḥ** — Indra; **iṣaḥ** — the oblation-food; **stavate** — praises.

**Bhāvārtha**

This Indra, desirous of good food, eats abundantly the oblation-food given by the sacrificers, and becomes favourable to the sacrificer who has priests and others with him; in the sacrifice, filled with the manifold sounds of *stotra* and the like, praising the sacrificer, he praises the oblation-food the sacrificer has given.

**Printed English**

> Verily, Indra, through desire of (sacrificial) food, is the devourer (of that which is presented) by (his) worshippers, and overcomes (the adversaries) of his friend: in the many-voiced assembly (of men), Indra, the faithful (performer of his promise), commending (the piety) of his worshipper, approves of the (offered) food.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***samarye*** — Sāyaṇa explains *samarye* as "in the sacrifice accompanied by mortals". Generally, since the word *samarya* is included among the names of "battle" (*saṃgrāma*) (Ni. 2-9 [?]), it means "battle". "*maryāḥ manuṣyāḥ taiḥ saha vartate iti samaryaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ*" — "that which is together with men (*marya*) is *samarya*, battle": since men are always gathered in a group in a battle, it is called *samarya*. In compounds with words of victory, such as *samaryajit*, the word *samarya* is fixed in the sense "battle". But when the word *samarya* stands alone, it need not have the meaning "war"; what is "with men (*marya*)" is not only the battlefield; it may also be a sacrifice. For example:

> यो वां यज्ञो नासत्या हविष्मान्कृतब्रह्मा समर्यो भवाति ।

> *yo vāṃ yajño nāsatyā haviṣmānkṛtabrahmā samaryo bhavāti |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-70-6 [?]) — here the meaning is "the sacrificer, the doer of the sacrifice, together with priests and mortals". In the ṛk at hand also, in the same way, *samarya* is explained as a sacrifice connected with mortal men. But in common usage the word *samarya* is mostly a synonym of "battle". In the ṛk at hand there is room for that sense as well, as is shown; for:

### Printed p. 464  (PDF 484)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 464.)*

… when "*vivāci samarye*" is said: if *samarye* is taken in the sense of battle, then to the epithet *vivāci* the meaning is "*vividhaparasparāhvānadhvaniyukte*" — "having the sounds of manifold mutual calls" — i.e. possessing the sound of calling one another for help; and if *samarye* is taken to mean *yajñe* ("in the sacrifice"), then to the epithet *vivāci* the meaning is "*vividhastotraśastradhvaniyukte*" — "having the sounds of manifold stotras and śastras". Following this sense, the meaning of "*mitriṇaḥ abhibhūt*" also has to be stated. In the sense of battle: "*mitriṇaḥ sahāyavataḥ asi (yajamānasya) śatrūn abhibhavati*" — the enemies of the sacrificer, even though they have many friends in battle, can be defeated; and in the sense of the sacrifice it means that Indra helps the sacrificer who has priests and other friends of manifold kinds.

***satrākaraḥ*** — the word *satrā* is included among the names of "true" (*satya*) (Ni. 3-13 [?]); the words *satrājit*, *satrāsaha* also show truth of act or of fruit. In some places the word *satrā* is also given the meaning "always". For example:

> तुविग्रये वह्नये दुष्टरीतवे सत्रासाहे नम इन्द्राय वोचत ।

> *tuvigraye vahnaye duṣṭarītave satrāsāhe nama indrāya vocata |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-21-2 [?]) — in ṛks such as this it is explained as *sarvadā abhibhavitre* or *mahataḥ abhibhavitre* ("who always overcomes", "who overcomes the great"). Since "always" means constantly and without once failing, and subduing enemies is meant, here too the sense is "true".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***evā*** — by "*nipātasya ca*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136 [?]) lengthening in the Saṃhitā.
- ***suśravasyā*** — by "*supa ātmanaḥ kyac*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 [?]) *kyac* in the sense of desiring for oneself; by "*apratyayāt*" (Pā. Sū. 3-3-102 [?]) the suffix *a* after a *kyac*-final stem; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent; being feminine and ending in *a*, *ṭāp*; the instrumental singular following, by "*supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇa…*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) the *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening.

### Printed p. 465  (PDF 485)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 465; signature mark "XIII 30".)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, continued)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***prakhādaḥ*** — root *khād bhakṣaṇe*; by "*nandigrahapacādibhyo…*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134 [?]) the suffix *ac* in the agent; being *cit*, the final syllable is *udātta*; in the *prādi* compound the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent.
- ***mitriṇaḥ*** — *mitram asya asti iti mitrī*; by "*ata iniṭhanau*" (Pā. Sū. 5-2-115 [?]) the suffix *ini* in the sense of possession; genitive singular; by the suffix accent the *i* is *udātta*.
- ***samarye*** — root *mṛṅ prāṇatyāge*; by "*chandasi niṣṭarkya devahūya…*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-123 [?], as read) the *yat*-final form is irregularly derived; in the compound the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent.
- ***stavate*** — root *ṣṭuñ stutau*; *laṭ*, third person singular, suffix *ta*; *ṭe ēt*; the Vedic *śap* is not elided (as printed [?]); *guṇa* for the *u*, *av* substitution; being *atiṅanta*, *nighāta* accent.
- ***vivāci*** — *vividhāḥ vāco yasmin tasmin*; by "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*" the fore-member keeps its natural accent.
- ***satrākaraḥ*** — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; by *pacādi* (the class of words beginning with *paca*) the suffix *ac*; taking that as the cause, *guṇa* for the *ṛ*; the rest is a genitive compound; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent. ‖ 4 ‖

**Sūkta 178, Ṛk 5**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> त्वया वयं मघवन्निन्द्र शत्रूनभि ष्याम महतो मन्यमानान् ।
> त्वं त्राता त्वमु नो वृधे भूर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ ५ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> त्वया । वयम् । मघऽवन् । इन्द्र । शत्रून् । अभि । स्याम । महतः । मन्यमानान् ।
> त्वम् । त्राता । त्वम् । ऊँ इति । नः । वृधे । भूः । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥ ५ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे मघवन्धनवन्निन्द्र त्वया सहायेन वयं यजमाना महतो मन्यमानानतिबलानवध्यान्मन्यमानाञ्छत्रूनभि स्याम । अभिभवितारो भवेम । हे इन्द्र त्वं त्राता नोऽस्माकं रक्षकः । अतस्त्वमु त्वमेव नोऽस्माकं वृधे धनादिवर्धनाय भूः । भव । विद्यामेत्यादि गतम् ॥

> *he maghavandhanavannindra tvayā sahāyena vayaṃ yajamānā mahato manyamānānatibalānavadhyānmanyamānāñchatrūnabhi syāma | abhibhavitāro bhavema | he indra tvaṃ trātā no 'smākaṃ rakṣakaḥ | atastvamu tvameva no 'smākaṃ vṛdhe dhanādivardhanāya bhūḥ | bhava | vidyāmetyādi gatam ‖*

### Printed p. 466  (PDF 486)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 178"; page 466.)*

*(The bhāṣya of Ṛk 5 ends on this page, as written above: "… vidyāmety ādi gatam".)*

*Gist:* With Indra's help may we overcome enemies who think themselves mighty; he is our protector; may he increase our wealth, and grant food, strength and long life.

**Pratipadārtha**

**maghavan** — O wealthy (Indra); (*he*) **Indra** — O Indra; **tvayā** — with you as helper; **vayam** — we, the sacrificers; **mahataḥ manyamānān** — who think themselves exceedingly strong and unassailable; **śatrūn** — the enemies; **abhi syāma** — may we overcome; (*he*) **Indra** — O Indra; **tvam** — you; **trātā** — the protector for us; (therefore) **tvam u** — you indeed; **naḥ** — for our; **vṛdhe** — increase of wealth etc.; **bhūḥ** — be; **iṣam** — food; **vṛjanam** — strength; **jīradānum** — long life; **vidyāma** — may we obtain.

**Bhāvārtha**

O wealthy Indra! You alone are our protector; by your aid alone have we overcome the enemies who thought themselves strong and unassailable. Grant us the increase of wealth and the like, and food, strength and long life.

**Printed English**

> By you, [o]pulent [first letter faint in print] Indra, may we overcome our mighty and formidable enemies: you are our protector: may you be propitious to our prosperity, that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***maghavan*** — the word *magha* is included among the names of "wealth" (Ni. 3-9 [?]). The Nirukta-writers' derivation of this word is as follows:

> "मघमिति धननामधेयं मंहतेर्दानकर्मणः"

> *"maghamiti dhananāmadheyaṃ maṃhaterdānakarmaṇaḥ"*

(Ni. 1-7 [?]) — the Nirukta-writers explain that the word *magha* is formed from the root *maṃh*, which has the sense of giving, and gives the sense "wealth"; and, citing the ṛk of the Ṛk-saṃhitā:

> नूनं सा ते प्रति वरं जरित्रे दुहीयदिन्द्र दक्षिणा मघोनी ।
> शिक्षा स्तोतृभ्यो माति धग्भगो नो बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥

> *nūnaṃ sā te prati varaṃ jaritre duhīyadindra dakṣiṇā maghonī |*
> *śikṣā stotṛbhyo māti dhagbhago no bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-21 [?]) — they have explained the meaning of the word *maghonī*. In the same way, in the ṛk at hand, [it is] an epithet of Indra. Since he has *magha* ("wealth") in him, Indra is called *maghavā* … [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 467  (PDF 487)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 21"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 467.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … a synonym. Besides this, *maghavā* cannot be called wrong even if it is said to mean "Indra united with Viṣṇu". For Indra obtains Viṣṇu's help when fighting the Asuras and others, and since the name *makha* is well known for Viṣṇu, the Śruti gives support for this meaning in such contexts. For example:

> स उ एव मखः स विष्णुः । तत इन्द्रो मखवानभवन्मखवान्ह वै तं मघवानित्याचक्षते परोक्षं परोक्षकामा हि देवाः ।

> *sa u eva makhaḥ sa viṣṇuḥ | tata indro makhavānabhavanmakhavānha vai taṃ maghavānityācakṣate parokṣaṃ parokṣakāmā hi devāḥ |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-13 [?]) — since Viṣṇu is *makha*, and Indra is such a possessor of *makha*, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa explains the word *maghavan*: the deities, who love the indirect, call that *makhavān* "*maghavān*". And:

> इन्द्राविष्णू दृंहिताः शम्बरस्य नव पुरो नवतिं च श्नथिष्टम् ।

> *indrāviṣṇū dṛṃhitāḥ śambarasya nava puro navatiṃ ca śnathiṣṭam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-99-5 [?]) — in such ṛks Indra, together with Viṣṇu, is described as having slain the Asuras; and because he is united with such a Viṣṇu there is the epithet *maghavā*.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***syāma*** — root *asa bhuvi*; *liṅ* [printed *laṅ* [?]], first person (plural); *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent. Since the prefix *abhi* precedes, by "*upasargaprāduḥbhyām astir yacparaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-87 [?]) the initial *s* becomes *ṣ*.
- ***mahataḥ*** — by "*bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam*" (*vārttika*) the case-ending takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***manyamānān*** — root *man avabodhane*; *laṭ*, with *śānac* substituted; *śyan* as the *vikaraṇa*; by "*ānemuk*" the augment *muk*; the *lasārvadhātuka* being *anudātta*, and *śyan* having *ñ* as marker, by "*ñnityādir nityam*" the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***trātā*** — root *trai pālane* (*trāṅ*); the suffix *tṛc* in the agent; by "*ād eś ca upadeśe 'śiti*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-45 [?]) *ā* for the root; being *cit*, the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***vṛdhe*** — root *vṛdhu vardhane*; the suffix *kvip*; dative singular; by "*sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 [?]) the case-ending takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***bhūḥ*** — root *bhū sattāyām*; Vedic *luṅ* in the sense of *loṭ*; second person singular; the augment *aṭ* does not occur. ‖ 5 ‖

## Sūkta 179 (the 179th Sūkta; "Nūra eppattoṃbhattaneya sūktavu")

> पूर्वीरहमिति षडृचं पञ्चदशं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभम् । उपान्त्या बृहती । अत्र त्रयाणां द्व्यृचानां लोपामुद्रागस्त्यशिष्यैर्दृष्टत्वात्त एवर्षयः [?] । सूक्तप्रतिपाद्योऽर्थो रतिर्देवता । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । पूर्वीः षड्जायापत्योर्लोपामुद्रायाा अगस्त्यस्य च द्व्यृचाभ्यां रत्यर्थं संवादं श्रुत्वान्तेवासी ब्रह्मचार्यन्त्ये बृहत्यदी अपश्यदिति ॥ विशेषविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥ [as read; garbled in places [?]]

*Translation of the introduction:* This Sūkta beginning "*pūrvīraham*" is the fifteenth sūkta in the twenty-third Anuvāka. It has six ṛks. The ṛṣi is Agastya; the metre is Triṣṭubh — but the penultimate ṛk (the fifth) is of Bṛhatī metre. In this sūkta, since the mantras are seen by two persons at a time — that is, Lopāmudrā for Ṛks 1–2, Agastya for Ṛks 3–4, and Agastya's disciple for Ṛks 5–6 — those very persons are the ṛṣis of the respective ṛks. The subject taught in the sūkta, *rati* ("conjugal love"), is its deity. The Anukramaṇikā says: "*pūrvīḥ ṣaḍ…*" — i.e. in the six ṛks of this sūkta beginning "*pūrvīraham*", the conversation that took place on the subject of *rati* between the married pair, Lopāmudrā and the ṛṣi Agastya, is told in Ṛks 1–4; the matter that their pupil heard this conversation is told in Ṛks 5–6. Only the fifth ṛk is of Bṛhatī metre; the remaining ṛks are of Triṣṭubh metre. The special application (*viśeṣaviniyoga*) of this sūkta is *laiṅgika* (as the context indicates).

**Sūkta 179**

Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 23 ‖ Sūkta 179 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 22 ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta — 6 ‖
Ṛṣi — 1–2 Lopāmudrā; 3–4 Agastya; 5–6 Antevāsī Brahmacārī (Agastya's disciple, a student) ‖
Chandas — 1–4, 6 Triṣṭubh; 5 Bṛhatī ‖

**Sūkta 179, Ṛk 1**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> पूर्वीरहं शरदः शश्रमाणा दोषा वस्तोरुषसो जरयन्तीः ।
> मिनाति श्रियं जरिमा तनूनामप्यू नु पत्नीर्वृषणो जगम्युः ॥ १ ॥

> *pūrvīrahaṃ śaradaḥ śaśramāṇā doṣā vastoruṣaso jarayantīḥ |*
> *mināti śriyaṃ jarimā tanūnāmapyū nu patnīrvṛṣaṇo jagamyuḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

---

### Printed p. 469  (PDF 489)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 469.)*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> पूर्वीः । अहम् । शरदः । शश्रमाणा । दोषाः । वस्तोः । उषसः । जरयन्तीः ।
> मिनाति । श्रियम् । जरिमा । तनूनाम् । अपि । ऊँ इति । नु । पत्नीः । वृषणः । जगम्युः ॥ १ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> लोपामुद्राह । हे अगस्त्य अहं लोपामुद्रा पूर्वीः शरदः पुरातनान्यसंख्यातान्संवत्सरान् दोषा रात्रीर्वस्तोरहानि तथा देहं जरयन्तीरुषस उषःकालांश्च ॥ सर्वत्रात्यन्तकालसंयोगे द्वितीया ॥ अद्यैतत्कालपर्यन्तं बहुसंवत्सरं कार्त्स्न्येन त्वच्छुश्रूषया शश्रमाणा श्रान्ताभूवम् । इदानीं तु जरिमा जरा तनूनामङ्गानां श्रियं सौन्दर्यं मिनाति । हिनस्ति । एवमपि नानुगृह्णासीत्यर्थः । अप्यू नु । अपि सम्भावनायाम् । ऊ इत्यैवधारणे [?] । नु इति वितर्के । इदानीमपि किं सम्भावनीयम् । लोके हि पत्नीः स्त्रियो वृषणः सेक्तारः पुरुषा जगम्युः । गच्छेयुः । संभोगं कुर्युः । अतो मां किमित्थैवमुपेक्षसे [?] । इदानीमपि वा सम्भावयेत्यर्थः ॥ [as read; a few words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Lopāmudrā says she has served Agastya through many years, and old age now spoils her beauty; yet he does not approach her — as husbands do their wives.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he* **Agastya**) — O Agastya; **ahaṃ** — I (the one called Lopāmudrā); **pūrvīḥ** — long past; **śaradaḥ** — many years; **doṣāḥ** — nights; **vastoḥ** — days; (and) **jarayantīḥ** — causing the body to age; **uṣasaḥ** — (up to) the dawns; **śaśramāṇā** — I have grown weary in serving you; (now) **jarimā** — old age; **tanūnām** — of the limbs; **śriyam** — the beauty; **mināti** — destroys; **api ū nu** — what, now, is to be done? **loke hi** — in the world indeed; **patnīḥ** — their wives; **vṛṣaṇaḥ** — husbands who sprinkle the seed; **jagamyuḥ** — approach (for union).

**Bhāvārtha**

Lopāmudrā says: O Agastya! For many years, by day, by night and at dawns, I have been tiring myself without rest in serving you; now old age is spoiling the beauty of my limbs. What am I to do now? In the world husbands approach their wives for union. (You alone still do not favour me.)

### Printed p. 470  (PDF 490)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 470.)*

**Printed English**

> (Lopamudra),—Many years have I been serving you diligently, both day and night, and through mornings, bringing on old age: decay now imqairs [sic] the beauty of my limbs: what, therefore, is now (to be done): let husbands approach their wives.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In Ṛk-saṃhitā 1-179 the conversation that took place between Lopāmudrā and Agastya is described. The commentator of the Bṛhaddevatā has explained this episode as follows:

> ऋतौ स्नातां नृषिर्भार्यां लोपामुद्रां यशस्विनीम् । उपजल्पितुमारेभे रहःसंयोगकाम्यया ॥
> द्वाभ्यां सा श्वब्रवीद्वैग्भ्यां [?] पूर्वीरिति चिकीर्षितम् । रिरंसुस्तामथागस्त्य उत्तराभ्यामतोषयत् ॥
> विदित्वा तपसा सर्वं तयोर्भावं रिरंसतोः । श्रुत्वैनः कृतवानस्मि ब्रह्मचार्युः [?] तनो जगौ ॥

> *ṛtau snātāṃ nṛṣirbhāryāṃ lopāmudrāṃ yaśasvinīm | upajalpitumārebhe rahaḥsaṃyogakāmyayā ‖*
> *dvābhyāṃ sā śvabravīdvaigbhyāṃ [?] pūrvīriti cikīrṣitam | riraṃsustāmathāgastya uttarābhyāmatoṣayat ‖*
> *viditvā tapasā sarvaṃ tayorbhāvaṃ riraṃsatoḥ | śrutvainaḥ kṛtavānasmi brahmacāryuḥ [?] tano jagau ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 4-57 to 59 [?]) — after the ritual bath following her season (*ṛtusnāna*), Agastya, wishing union with his wife Lopāmudrā, began a conversation with her. She too, by the two ṛks "*pūrvīraham śaradaḥ*" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-179-1) and "*ye cid dhi pūrve*" (1-179-2), made known her purpose. Then Agastya, by the two ṛks "*na mṛṣā śrāntam*" (1-179-3) and "*nadasya mā rudhataḥ*" (1-179-4), made known his own wish to her and satisfied her. In this context Agastya's disciple, who by the power of his austerity (*tapas*) had understood all of what lay in the minds of the pair desiring union, and had heard this conversation — thinking that it was a sin — himself recited the two ṛks "*imaṃ nu somam*" (1-179-5) and "*agastyaḥ khanamānaḥ*" (1-179-6): so it is explained in the Bṛhaddevatā.

***doṣāḥ; vastoḥ*** — of these two words, *doṣāḥ* is read among the names of night (Ni. 3-9 [?]) and *vastoḥ* among the names of day. And explaining the meanings of the two words, the Nirukta-writers, in the Ṛk-saṃhitā's

> कुह स्विद्दोषा कुह वस्तोरश्विना कुहाभिपित्वं करतः कुहोषतुः ।
> को वां शयुत्रा विधवेव देवरं मर्यं न योषा कृणुते सधस्थ आ ॥

> *kuha sviddoṣā kuha vastoraśvinā kuhābhipitvaṃ karataḥ kuhoṣatuḥ |*
> *ko vāṃ śayutrā vidhaveva devaraṃ maryaṃ na yoṣā kṛṇute sadhastha ā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-40-2 [?]) — [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 471  (PDF 491)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 471.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … citing this ṛk, he has explained *doṣā* as "night" and *vastoḥ* as "day".

***śaradaḥ*** — "*śarac chṛtā asyām oṣadhayo bhavanti | śīrṇā āpa iti vā*" (Ni. 4-25 [?]) — "in this season the plants become ripe (*śṛta*); or the waters shrink" — whence the name "autumn". This word is not merely the name of a single season; in many places it is also used as a synonym of "year". For example, in the ṛk cited by the Nirukta-writers (Ni. 4-25 [?]):

> दीर्घायुरस्या यः पतिर्जीवाति शरदः शतम् ।

> *dīrghāyurasyā yaḥ patirjīvāti śaradaḥ śatam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-39 [?]) — here *śaradaḥ śatam* means "a hundred years".

***vṛṣaṇaḥ*** — the meanings contained in the words formed from *vṛṣan*, and the contexts of their use in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, have been explained earlier (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-177-3 [?], printed "1-77-3"). In the present context it gives the sense "*puṃs*" — a male possessed of the capacity to sprinkle.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***pūrvīḥ*** — in these first four words, by "*kālādhvanor atyantasaṃyoge*" (Pā. Sū. 2-3-5 [?]) the accusative has come, since each is connected with the sense of continuous duration.
- ***śaśramāṇā*** — root *śramu tapasi khede ca*; by "*vyatyayo bahulam*" *śānac* for *laṭ*; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" *ślu* as the *vikaraṇa*; taking that as the cause, reduplication of the root; by "*aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi*" (Pā. Sū. 8-4-2 [?], as read) *ṇatva* for the *n* of the suffix; by "*citaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 [?]) the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***vastoḥ*** — root *vasa nivāse*; the suffix *tosun* in the sense of the infinitive.
- ***jarayantīḥ*** — root *jṛṣ vayohānau*; after *ṇic*, *śatṛ*; in the feminine, since it has the marker *u*, *ṅīp*; by "*janījṛṣkñasurañjo 'mantāś ca*" the name *mit* arises; by "*mitāṃ hrasvaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-92 [?]) shortening of the penultimate vowel of the root; the *lasārvadhātuka* being *anudātta*, the *ṇic* accent remains.
- ***mināti*** — root *mīñ hiṃsāyām*, *kryādi* class; *laṭ*, third person singular; by "*pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-80 [?]) shortening of the root; being in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; the *vikaraṇa* accent remains.

### Printed p. 472  (PDF 492)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 472.)*

- ***jarimā*** — root *jṛṣ vayohānau*; in the abstract sense the *Uṇādi* suffix *imanic*; taking that as the cause, *guṇa* for the *ṛ*; by "*citaḥ*" the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***jagamyuḥ*** — root *gamḷ gatau*; *liṅ*, third person plural, with *us* for *jhi* ... (*jus* → *us*); by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" elision of the *vikaraṇa*, with reduplication; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent. ‖ 1 ‖

**Sūkta 179, Ṛk 2**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> ये चिद्धि पूर्व ऋतसाप आसन्त्साकं देवेभिरवदन्नृतानि ।
> ते चिदवासुर्ह्यन्तमापुः सं नू पत्नीर्वृषभिर्जगम्युः ॥ २ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> ये । चित् । हि । पूर्वे । ऋतऽसापः । आसन् । साकम् । देवेभिः । अवदन् । ऋतानि ।
> ते । चित् । अव । असुः । हि [?] । अन्तम् । आपुः । सम् । ऊँ इति । नु । पत्नीः । वृषऽभिः । जगम्युः ॥ २ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> सा तमेहवा [?] ॥ हे पतेऽगस्त्य ये चिद्धि येऽपि तु पूर्वे पुरातना ऋतसापः सत्यस्यापयितारो व्याप्नुवाना महर्षय आसन् ते देवेभिर्देवैः साकं सहर्तानि [?] सत्यवाक्यान्यवदन् । वदन्ति । ये महत्तपो यज्ञं वानुतिष्ठन्ति ये च देववाक्यानि देवस्तुतिरूपाणि वदन्ति ते चित् । चिदप्यर्थे । ते चिदपि अवासुः । अवक्षिपन्ति रेतः ॥ स्तुतिरुपसृष्टो विनोचने [?] वर्तते ॥ ते नह्यन्तमापुः [?] । न हि ब्रह्मचर्योदेरन्तं प्राप्नुवन् । ब्रह्मचर्यमनिषिद्धर्तुकालगमनमपि कुर्वन्तीत्यर्थः । तथा पत्नीः पत्न्यश्च तपस्यमानास्तैव [?] ऋषिभोगवर्षकैः पतिभिः सह समू न जगम्युः । उ न्विति पूरणौ । संगच्छेरन् । अतस्त्वं कथं मां नानुभवसीत्यर्थः ॥ [as read; several phrases doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Even the ancient truth-keeping seers, who spoke truths with the gods and practised austerity, were not without conjugal union at the proper time, and their wives joined their husbands; so why does he not approach her?

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he Agastya*) — O Agastya; **ye cit hi** — those who; **pūrve** — of old; **ṛtasāpaḥ** — [who practised sacrifice etc.] great seers who pervade (cause to reach) the truth … [the passage continues on the next page.]

---

### Printed p. 473  (PDF 493)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 473.)*

**Pratipadārtha (continued)** — **āsan** — they were; (**ye** — who) **devebhiḥ sākam** — together with the deities; **ṛtāni** — true utterances (the principles of truth); **avadan** — were speaking (discussing); **te cit** — those great seers also; **avāsuḥ** — emitted the seed; (*te* — they) **antam** — the end (of their *brahmacarya*); **na hi āpuḥ** — did not reach; (**tathā** — likewise) **patnīḥ** — the wives (ascetics too); **vṛṣabhiḥ** — with the husbands who rain enjoyment; **saṃ ū nu jagamyuḥ** — were united.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Agastya! The ancient great seers who performed sacrifices and the like, and who discussed the principles of truth with the deities, also had union for the sake of offspring; therefore their *brahmacarya* was not lost; and the wives, who were ascetics, united with their husbands. (Yet you alone do not favour me.)

**Printed English**

> The ancient sages, disseminators of truth, who, verily, conversed of truths with the gods, begot (progeny), nor thereby violated (their vow of continence), therefore should wives be approached by their husbands.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In the ṛk at hand, as in the ṛk before it, Lopāmudrā prays to Agastya that he fulfil her wish; she tells her husband her desire plainly. But, to make clear that neither her own *dharma* nor her husband's *dharma* suffers any breach, she cites the examples of the earlier ṛṣis: how even the great seers did not conquer desire, and, since it is natural to man, it has to be satisfied in some way. "*ye cit ṛtasāpaḥ āsan, ye devebhiḥ sākaṃ ṛtāni avadan, te cit avāsuḥ*" — those who were *ṛtasāpas* and conversed of truths (*ṛta*) with the gods even they united with their wives. Thus, in the ṛk at hand, Lopāmudrā tells her husband and begs for his company. By the words *ṛtasāpaḥ*, *ṛtāni*, the meaning suggested must here be noted above all. The word *ṛta* is one that shows both the physical (*bhautika*) principle and the ethical (*naitika*) rule. The gist of the Vedic view is that the deities, men and others all understand this path of *ṛta* and keep its rule. Lopāmudrā's argument is that even such seers, knowing the principle and keeping the rule, obtained fulfilment of desire.

### Printed p. 474  (PDF 494)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 474.)*

***ṛtasāpaḥ, ṛtāni*** — the Nirukta-writers have included the word *ṛta* among the names of "water" (Ni. 3-9 [?]). Moreover, in many places the word *ṛta* is explained as "*satyaṃ vā yajño vā*" ("truth or sacrifice") (Ni. 4-19 [?]), and so on. Sāyaṇa too, wherever the word *ṛtasāpaḥ* is used, has explained it as *yajñasprśaḥ* ("touching the sacrifice") or *satyajñāḥ* ("knowers of truth"). In many places the word *ṛta* is one that describes the universal rule. Eggeling has said:

> "Standing, as it does inter alia, for impersonal Order or Law, pervading the physical and moral world and sustaining alike the worlds of the gods and nature, the concept of the Rita may be said to have created a land-mark in the history of Vedic thought and culture"

— that the idea indicated by the word *ṛta* in Vedic culture has acquired a distinct character. The usages of this word in various contexts, and the ideas it points to, need to be briefly examined here.

The word is used in the very first sūkta of the first Maṇḍala of the Ṛk-saṃhitā. There, describing Agni's great qualities:

> राजन्तमध्वराणां गोपामृतस्य दीदिविम् ।
> वर्धमानं स्वे दमे ॥

> *rājantamadhvarāṇāṃ gopāmṛtasya dīdivim |*
> *vardhamānaṃ sve dame ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-8) — here, for "*ṛtasya gopām*", Sāyaṇa has explained "*ṛtasya satyasyāvaśyaṃbhāvinaḥ karmaphalasya*" ("of the truth, of the inevitable fruit of action"). Yāska too explains it as "*satya*" ("truth") and supports it.

Examining the original meaning of the word *ṛta* and its development, Max Müller said: at first it was a word showing the regular course (*saṃcārakrama*) of the sun, moon and others; then, following the revolutions of the sun, moon and the rest, and in keeping with the fixed *ayana*, *ṛtu* and so on, it was used as a synonym of the sacrifices (*yajña*, *yāga*) that are performed accordingly; and since this rule is reflected in them, finally this very word came to be a synonym describing the natural law or *dharma*. On this subject Keith has spoken thus:

> "In the physical world there rules a regular order ṛta [set in Kannada letters], which is clearly an inheritance from the physical; it is an easy step to the conception of the ṛta, ................ in the moral world".

> "The term for Cosmic order, ṛta and and [sic] its opposite anṛta express also moral order as in the dialogue of Yama and Yami. ṛta forbids and … [the passage continues on the next page.]

---

### Printed p. 475  (PDF 495)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 475.)*

> doubtless also commands positive action. ṛta [set in Indic letters] is more than truth, satya [Indic letters]. Law is denoted by dharma [Indic letters], which denotes that which supports and that which is supported; it applies like ṛta to all aspects of the world, to the sequence of events in Nature, to the sacrifice and to man's life."

In the physical universe, wherever the universal rule is described, it is indicated by the word *ṛta*. In the same way, in human ethical conduct also, the words *ṛta* and its opposite *anṛta* indicate the ethical rule of man and unethical conduct. Since man's sacrificial activity is directly related to both physical and ethical dealings, *ṛta* is used also as a synonym of *yajña*. Hence the word is also a synonym of *satya*, and gives a sense wider than the idea indicated by the word *satya*: this is the essence of the above sentences.

All the deities, whether singly or collectively, are described in the Ṛk-saṃhitā at every step as presiding over *ṛta* (*ṛtādhyakṣa*) and as pervaded by *ṛta*. Taking a mantra that shows this fully, the matter becomes clear:

> हंसः शुचिषद्वसुरन्तरिक्षसद्धोता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् ।
> नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसदब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतम् ॥

> *haṃsaḥ śuciṣadvasurantarikṣasaddhotā vediṣadatithirduroṇasat |*
> *nṛṣadvarasadṛtasadvyomasadabjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-40-5) — in this ṛk the universal rule is taught: to every individual in the universe a fixed place is assigned by *ṛta*. The place of the Āditya is regulated in the sky; the place of the *hotṛ* in the sacrificial altar; the place of the guest in the house; but the place of *ṛta* alone pervades the whole universe — *ṛta* is pervasive in the earth, in the intermediate region, in men, in the gods, in sacrifices and rites, in the acts of the Āditya, in mountains and the like: this is the description of this mantra. It is a statement that shows the spiritual (*ādhyātmika*) and ethical principle of the universe. Showing the greatness of this *ṛta*, the scholar Bloomfield says:

> "If therefore an ethics of the Rig-veda, rooted in the concept of Ritaf [sic] be at all conceded, it is not to be construed as an ethies o, [sic] naturalism with its apothesis of la bete humaine [sic]. It provides in the stricter sense, an ethics in accordance with the highest human

### Printed p. 476  (PDF 496)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 476.)*

> idial [sic] which was destined to realise all its ethical implications in the Law of karma [set in Indic letters, as printed with a visarga [?]]. Of that there is surely no room for misgivings; for accredited exponents of the philosophy and history of religion, like Pfleiderer, view the Rita and Karma of the Hindus as more or less hyphenated in their nature, and classify them on grounds of functional similarity, with the Nemesis of the Greeks, the Ashavaista of the Persians and the Tao of the Chinese"

As this passage also shows, *ṛta* is a word that reflects the principle of the universal rule; likewise it makes clear the ideas that exist in the beliefs of other peoples under names such as Nemesis, Tao and the like. But one more thing has to be noted here: the word *ṛta* is used in the plural in many places, and in those contexts it is not right to give it the sense "universal rule". Thus in some contexts a different meaning has to be given, according to the context. So here the special meanings of this word are briefly examined with a few examples.

> वि श्रयन्तामृतावृधो द्वारो देवीरसश्चतः ।
> अद्या नूनं च यष्टवे ॥

> *vi śrayantāmṛtāvṛdho dvāro devīrasaścataḥ |*
> *adyā nūnaṃ ca yaṣṭave ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-6) — here the deities called the Divine Doors are called *ṛtāvṛdhaḥ* ("increasing *ṛta*"); the sense here is protection of the sacrifice, and *ṛta* must here be a synonym of *yajña*. And:

> नमस्यत हव्यदातिं स्वध्वरं दुवस्यत दम्यं जातवेदसम् ।
> रथीरृतस्य बृहतो विचर्षणिरग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोहितः ॥

> *namasyata havyadātiṃ svadhvaraṃ duvasyata damyaṃ jātavedasam |*
> *rathīrṛtasya bṛhato vicarṣaṇiragnirdevānāmabhavatpurohitaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-2-8 [?]) — here Agni is described as the charioteer of *ṛta*; here *ṛta* has to mean the sacrifice; there is no room to explain it otherwise. But:

> ससस्य यद्वियुता सस्मिन्नूधन्नृतस्य धामन्रणयन्त देवाः ।
> महा अग्निर्नमसा रातहव्यो वेरध्वराय सदमिदृतावा ॥

> *sasasya yadviyutā sasminnūdhannṛtasya dhāmanraṇayanta devāḥ |*
> *mahā agnirnamasā rātahavyo veradhvarāya sadamidṛtāvā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-2-7 [?]) — in this ṛk the meaning can be given in two ways. First: there are two words, *ṛtasya dhāman* and *ṛtāvā*. Here, for the first, *ṛtasya*, Sāyaṇa has given "water" (*udaka*), and for the second, *ṛtāvā*, he has shown *ṛta* as "truth" — "*satyavān*" — as the first meaning; second: *ṛtasya dhāman* means "the womb (*yoni*) of truth", i.e. the sacrifice, and *ṛtāvā* "possessed of truth". Or between the deities and men mutual … [the passage continues on the next page.]

---

### Printed p. 477  (PDF 497)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 477.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … the relation [between deities and men]: since the sacrifice, which fosters the relation and is of the nature of truth, protects the universal rule, *ṛta* is a word that shows identity (*tādātmya*) with both the sacrifice and truth (*satya*). For example:

> ऋतेन्नृतेन [?] सपन्तेषिरं [?] दक्षमाशाते । अद्रुहा देवौ वर्धेते ॥

> *ṛtennṛtena [?] sapanteṣiraṃ [?] dakṣamāśāte | adruhā devau vardhete ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-68-4 [?]) — here Mitra and Varuṇa are praised as "those who make *ṛta* grow by *ṛta*". This sentence describes the sacrifice of the nature of truth, and truth of the nature of the sacrifice; the idea is the same as in the sentence "*yajñena yajñam ayajanta devāḥ*". Since the sacrifice, whose nature is truth, protects the universal rule, it may be said that *ṛta* is a word reflecting both these principles. (The relation of *ṛta* to deities such as Mitra and Varuṇa, and which deities are "*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*", will be explained later.)

In the ṛk at hand, Lopāmudrā, wishing for union with her husband Agastya, shows that all the ṛṣis of old — the protectors of truth and of the sacrifice, who obtained relation with the deities through the sacrifice — obtained fulfilment of desire. Since a man's desire is natural to man, and if it is not satisfied there comes an unnatural way of life, she asks for her husband's union. The same, in the later ṛk, in the conversation of Yama and Yamī, Yamī, addressing her brother Yama, says that all the ṛṣis who acted in keeping with the rule of the seasons obtained satisfaction of desire:

> ये चित्पूर्व ऋतसाप ऋतावान [?] ऋतावृधः ।
> पितॄन्तपस्वतो यम तांश्चिदेवापि गच्छतात् ॥

> *ye citpūrva ṛtasāpa ṛtāvāna [?] ṛtāvṛdhaḥ |*
> *pitṝntapasvato yama tāṃścidevāpi gacchatāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-154-4 [?]) — in this ṛk she makes a prayer asking for Yama's union. But since the wife's prayer in the ṛk at hand is just, the husband Agastya accepts it. In the ṛk cited, the prayer is made by the sister Yamī to her brother Yama, so it is an unethical dealing.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***ṛtasāpaḥ*** — root *āpḷ vyāptau*; the suffix *kvip*; in Vedic the *s* is added in addition; in the compound the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent.
- ***āsan*** — by "*hi ca*" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34 [?]) the *nighāta* accent is prohibited, so *ādyudātta* accent results.

### Printed p. 478  (PDF 498)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 478.)*

- ***avadan*** — root *vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci*; *laṅ*, third person plural; because of *yad*-connection the *nighāta* is prohibited; by the accent of the *aṭ* augment, *ādyudātta*.
- ***avāsuḥ*** — root *ṣo antakarmaṇi*; in the sense of "release" in connection with the prefix *ava*; Vedic *luṅ* in the present sense; third person plural; being in an *atiṅanta* word-position, *nighāta* accent occurs.
- ***āpuḥ*** — root *āpḷ vyāptau*; *liṭ*, third person plural; by "*hi ca*" the *nighāta* is prohibited; by the suffix accent the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***patnīḥ*** — by "*supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇa…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-[?]) with *jas* following, the *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening. ‖ 2 ‖

**Sūkta 179, Ṛk 3**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> न मृषा श्रान्तं यदवन्ति देवा विश्वा इत्स्पृधो अभ्यश्नवाव ।
> जयावेदत्र शतनीथमाजिं यत्सम्यञ्चा मिथुनावभ्यजाव ॥ ३ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> न । मृषा । श्रान्तम् । यत् । अवन्ति । देवाः । विश्वाः । इत् । स्पृधः । अभि । अश्नवाव ।
> जयाव । इत् । अत्र । शतऽनीथम् । आजिम् । यत् । सम्यञ्चा । मिथुनौ । अभि । अजाव ॥ ३ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अगस्त्यः स्त्रामाह [?] ॥ भोः पत्नि त्वया मया न मृषा श्रान्तम् । व्यर्थं नैव खिन्नमावाभ्याम् । यद्यस्माद्देवा अवन्ति रक्षन्ति तपोभिः प्रीता देवाः । विश्वाः सर्वाः स्पृधोऽभ्यश्नवाव । अभितो व्याप्नुयाव । अत्रास्मिन्संसारे शतनीथमपरिमितभोगप्राप्तिसाधनमाजिं प्राप्तिं [?] परस्परं जयाव । जयलक्षणं सुरते संग्रामं वा जयाव । यद्यस्मात्सम्यञ्चा सम्यक्परस्परं गच्छन्तौ प्रजयन्तौ [?] वा मिथुना मिथुनौ स्त्रीपुरुषरूपौ सन्तावभ्यजाव । त्वं चाहमपि परस्परमभिजयावेत्येवं तयोक्तं संभोगं संभावयामास ॥ [as read; a few words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Agastya replies that their labour has not been in vain, the deities protect them; let them overcome all rivals and win each other in union as a couple.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*bhoḥ patni* — O wife Lopāmudrā) **yat** — because; **devāḥ** — the deities; **avanti** — (pleased with our austerities) protect; (**tat** — therefore) … [the passage continues on the next page.]

---

### Printed p. 479  (PDF 499)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 479.)*

**Pratipadārtha (continued)** — **mṛṣā** — in vain; **na śrāntam** — the labour borne by us (both) was not (in vain); **viśvāḥ** — all; **spṛdhaḥ it** — desires indeed; **abhi aśnavāva** — we two shall obtain; **atra** — in this world; **mithunau** — like husband and wife; **samyañcā** — well united with each other; **yat abhi ajāva** — if we strive well (or if one overcomes the other); **śatanītham** — which leads to immeasurable enjoyments; **ājim** — the mutual attainment; **jayāva** — we gain; [or: **ājim** — the battle in the form of love; **jayāva it** — may we two surely win].

**Bhāvārtha**

O wife Lopāmudrā! The deities, pleased with our austerities, protect us, and by their favour we obtain all our desires; so we must not call our hardship in vain. And in this world, if we two, as husband and wife, strive well, united with each other, we can attain boundless enjoyments. (May we two win enjoyment in the battle of love.)

**Printed English**

> (Agastya)—Penance has not been practised in vain: since the gods protect us, we may indulge all our desires: in this world we may triumph in many conflicts, if we exert ourselves mutually together.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk Agastya gives his wife Lopāmudrā his answer and gives his consent to unite with her as she desired. But one more special point has to be noted here. In this conversation, desire is not shown as the primary objective. All the religious acts, such as sacrifices, have been performed; therefore, having produced the satisfaction of the deities and obtained their favour, Agastya afterwards expresses this wish. Particularly, in "*na mṛṣā śrāntam …*" — when he says that the toil they bore in austerity is not in vain — it is well known that the satisfaction of the deities is for the favouring of men. In the results that fit this effort, Agastya wishes to enjoy the worldly pleasure that is brought about by the favour of the deities.

***spṛdhaḥ*** — the Nirukta-writers have listed the word *spṛdh* among the names of "battle" (*saṃgrāma*). But in the ṛk at hand Sāyaṇa has explained it as "desire" (*apekṣā*). If it is derived from the root *spardh*, then the sense "desire" also arises.

### Printed p. 480  (PDF 500)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 480.)*

The restraint of desire, being an extremely hard means, is here likened to battle.

***ājim*** — "*ājayenasyājavanasyeti vā*" (Ni. 9-23 [?]) — "from the place for gaining victory, or from the place of swift movement": *āji* is the name of a battle. Explaining this word, the Nirukta-writers have cited the ṛk in the Ṛk-saṃhitā:

> न्यक्रन्दयन्नुपयन्त एनममेहयन्वृषभं मध्य आजेः ।
> तेन सूभर्वं शतवत्सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः प्रधने जिगाय ॥

> *nyakrandayannupayanta enamamehayanvṛṣabhaṃ madhya ājeḥ |*
> *tena sūbharvaṃ śatavatsahasraṃ gavāṃ mudgalaḥ pradhane jigāya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-102-9 [?]) — and have given the above explanation for the word *ājeḥ* occurring in it. In the ṛk at hand also Sāyaṇa has given two meanings: first, *ājiṃ parasparaprāptim* ("mutual attainment"); and second, *surataruupasaṅgrāmaṃ vā* ("or the battle in the form of love-union") [as read].

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***śrāntam*** — root *śramu tapasi khede ca*; the suffix *kta*; by the suffix accent the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***avanti*** — root *ava rakṣaṇe*; *laṭ*, third person plural; because of *yad*-connection no *nighāta* occurs; by "*tāsyanudāttet…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 [?]) the *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta*, so the root accent remains.
- ***aśnavāva*** — root *aśū vyāptau*, *svādi* class; by "*vyatyayo bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 [?]) *parasmaipada*; *loṭ*, first person dual; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***jayāva*** — root *ji jaye*; *loṭ*, first person dual; being in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; the *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta*, so the root accent remains.
- ***śatanītham*** — root *nīñ prāpaṇe*; by "*panikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan*" (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]) the suffix *kthan*; in a *bahuvrīhi* compound, by "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*" the fore-member keeps its natural accent; accusative singular.
- ***samyañcā*** — by "*supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇa…*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) *ā* in place of the dual *au*.
- ***ājāva*** — root *aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ*; *loṭ*, first person dual; because of *yad*-connection no *nighāta*; the root accent remains. ‖ 3 ‖

### Printed p. 481  (PDF 501)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 481; signature mark "XIII 31".)*

**Sūkta 179, Ṛk 4**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> नदस्य मा रुधतः काम आगन्नित आजातो अमुतः कुतश्चित् ।
> लोपामुद्रा वृषणं नी रिणाति धीरमधीरा धयति श्वसन्तम् ॥ ४ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> नदस्य । मा । रुधतः । कामः । आ । अगन् । इतः । आऽजातः । अमुतः । कुतः । चित् ।
> लोपामुद्रा । वृषणम् । नि । रिणाति । धीरम् । अधीरा । धयति । श्वसन्तम् ॥ ४ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अथ चतुर्थ्याह्यगस्त्य आह ॥ हे जाये नदस्य नदनस्य जपशब्दयितुर्जपाध्ययनकर्तो रुधतो रेतो निरोद्धुर्ब्रह्मचर्यमास्थितस्य ॥ उभे कर्मणि षष्ठ्यौ ॥ उक्तलक्षणं मां कामः आगन् । आगमत् । नदस्य मा रुधतः काम आगमदिति निरुक्तम् । ५-२ [?] । कस्य हेतोरिति उच्यते । इतस्त्वत्संगमनिमित्तात् तथामुतो वसन्तादिकालात् कुतश्चित्कारणादाजातः सर्वत उत्पन्नः । यद्वा । इत एतल्लोकजनितादमुतो लोकान्तरजनिताद्वा कुतश्चिन्निमित्तात्कामात् । कथमिति उच्यते । इयं लोपामुद्रा वृषणं रेतसः प्रवर्तकं मां नी रिणाति । नितरां गच्छतु । किंच धीरं धीमन्तं नियमादविचालिनं श्वसन्तं महाप्राणं महाबलमधीरा कातरैषा योषिद्धयति । उपभुङ्क्ताम् ॥ [as read; a few words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Agastya says that desire has arisen in him, an ascetic, from her closeness or some other cause; let Lopāmudrā approach him — a restless woman can unsettle even a firm and strong man.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he jāye* — O wife) **nadasya** — of me, the one who mutters (study of *japa*); **rudhataḥ** — who restrains the seed (practising *brahmacarya*); **mā** — to me; **itaḥ** — from this cause (union with you); **amutaḥ** — from that cause (the time of spring and the like); or **kutaścit** — from some other cause; [or **itaḥ** — born of this world; or **amutaḥ** — born of the other world; **kutaḥ cit** — from some cause;] **ājātaḥ** — arisen; **kāmaḥ** — desire for objects; **ā agan** — has come; (*iyam*) **Lopāmudrā** — this Lopāmudrā; **vṛṣaṇam** — me, who impel the seed; **ni riṇāti** — (let her) approach; **kiṃ ca** — and further; **adhīrā** — the restless woman; **dhīram** — the wise (man); **śvasantam** — of great strength; **dhayati** — enjoys.

### Printed p. 482  (PDF 502)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 482.)*

**Bhāvārtha**

O Lopāmudrā! In me, who am devoted to the study and muttering of *japa* and to the vow of *brahmacarya*, desire has arisen, either from your closeness or from some other cause; therefore approach me, who impel the seed. A restless woman makes even a man who is wise and strong lose his steadiness.

**Printed English**

> Desire, either from this cause or from that, has come upon me whilst engaged in prayer and suppressing (passion): let Lopamudra approach her husband: the unsteady famale [sic] beguiles the firm and resolute man.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk Agastya, giving his wife Lopāmudrā once more assurance, says that he will satisfy her; and he also makes his own wish plain. The Nirukta-writers have given the following explanation of this ṛk:

> "नदस्य मा रुधतः कामु [?] आगमत् । संरुद्धप्रजननस्य ब्रह्मचारिण इत्यृषिपुत्र्या विलपितं वेदयन्ते ॥"

> *"nadasya mā rudhataḥ kāmu [?] āgamat | saṃruddhaprajananasya brahmacāriṇa ityṛṣiputryā vilapitaṃ vedayante ‖"*

(Ni. 3-2 [?]) — "With the ṛṣi who has controlled himself, I [as a wife] must be the object of his tenderness; he has no desire; he is a *brahmacārin*" and so on: the ṛṣi's daughter laid her sorrow before him. Here some contradiction is seen between the Bṛhaddevatā statement and the Nirukta statement. In the Bṛhaddevatā:

> रिरंसुस्तामथागस्त्य उत्तराभ्यामतोषयत् ।

> *riraṃsustāmathāgastya uttarābhyāmatoṣayat |*

(Bṛ. De. 4-58 [?]) — it is said that Agastya, with the following two ṛks, that is, the 3rd and the 4th ṛks of the sūkta at hand, made known his wish and gratified his wife Lopāmudrā. But according to the Nirukta statement it follows that this is the speech of Lopāmudrā, and that she makes known her mental distress by these words. Durgācārya has given the following explanation of the Nirukta statement:

> अगस्त्यलोपामुद्राब्रह्मचारिसूक्तसंवादे लोपामुद्रया इयमार्षम् । सा अब्रवीदगस्त्यं भर्तारमभिप्रेत्य "नदस्य नदस्य ..........." । इत्येवं विलपमाना कामार्ता लोपामुद्रा राजर्षिपुत्रिका । ......... एवं लोपा-

> *agastyalopāmudrābrahmacārisūktasaṃvāde lopāmudrayā iyamārṣam | sā abravīdagastyaṃ bhartāramabhipretya "nadasya nadasya ..........." | ityevaṃ vilapamānā kāmārtā lopāmudrā rājarṣiputrikā | ......... evaṃ lopā-*

— [the passage continues on the next page.]

She is Agastya's wife; there is also a story that Agastya himself fashioned her, from the wish to obtain a beautiful wife, and left her in the Vidarbha king's palace. It is described in this way in the Mahābhārata. Since it follows the statements of the Bṛhaddevatā, it is quoted here:

> ततः प्रसवसन्तानं चिन्तयन्भगवानृषिः । आत्मनः प्रसवस्यार्थे नापश्यत्सदृशीं स्त्रियम् ॥
> स तस्य तस्य सत्त्वस्य तत्तदङ्गमनुत्तमम् । संगृह्य तत्स्वैरङ्गैर्निर्ममे [?] स्त्रियमुत्तमाम् ॥
> स तां विदर्भराजाय पुत्रकामाय काम्यते । निर्मितामात्मनोऽर्थाय मुनिः प्रादान्महातपाः ॥

> जातमात्रां च तां दृष्ट्वा वैदर्भः पृथिवीपतिः । प्रहर्षेण द्विजातिभ्यो न्यवेदयत भारत ॥

> ततः स भार्यामभ्येत्य प्रोवाच पृथिवीपतिः । महर्षिर्वीर्यवानेष क्रुद्धः शापाग्निना दहेत् ॥

> न मत्कृते महीपाल पीडामभ्येतुमर्हसि । प्रयच्छ मामगस्त्याय त्राह्यात्मानं मया पितः ॥

### Printed p. 484  (PDF 504)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 484.)*

> गङ्गाद्वारमथागम्य भगवानृषिसत्तमः । उग्रमातिष्ठत तपः सह पत्न्यानुकूलया ॥
> सा प्रीत्या बहुमानाच्च पतिं पर्यचरत्तदा । अगस्त्यश्च परां प्रीतिं भार्यायां चान्वगच्छत ॥
> ततो बहुतिथे काले लोपामुद्रां विशांपते । तपसा द्योतितां स्नातां ददर्श भगवानृषिः ॥
> स तस्याः परिचारेण शौचेन च दमेन च । श्रिया रूपेण च प्रीतो मैथुनायाजुहाव ताम् ॥

> *gaṅgādvāramathāgamya bhagavānṛṣisattamaḥ | ugramātiṣṭhata tapaḥ saha patnyānukūlayā ‖*
> *sā prītyā bahumānācca patiṃ paryacarattadā | agastyaśca parāṃ prītiṃ bhāryāyāṃ cānvagacchata ‖*
> *tato bahutithe kāle lopāmudrāṃ viśāṃpate | tapasā dyotitāṃ snātāṃ dadarśa bhagavānṛṣiḥ ‖*
> *sa tasyāḥ paricāreṇa śaucena ca damena ca | śriyā rūpeṇa ca prīto maithunāyājuhāva tām ‖*

(Mahābhārata, Vana-parva, 94–95 [?]; as read, several words doubtful [?]; a line is given in print with dots)

— Afterwards the ṛṣi Agastya wished to obtain the fruit of progeny; but no wife suitable to him was to be found. So he himself fashioned a girl suited to him, and left her in the house of the Vidarbha king, who desired a son. The Vidarbha king was delighted at obtaining her, and his friends all congratulated him on gaining such a beautiful daughter. They gave her the name Lopāmudrā. She grew up happily in the palace of the Vidarbha king and attained youth. Then Agastya came and asked the Vidarbha king to give her to him as wife. The king did not like it; but, afraid that the angry ṛṣi might curse him, he went to ask his wife's leave. Then Lopāmudrā herself came to her father's aid and said, "Give me to Agastya." Afterwards the Vidarbha king gave her in marriage to Agastya with due rites. Having obtained Lopāmudrā as his wife, Agastya wished her too to follow the rule of the ṛṣis; so he had her put off her ornaments and the like, and she too, at his word, put on bark garments, as her husband desired. Having got such a suitable wife, he practised severe austerity with her on the bank of the Gaṅgā. She too served him with respect and love for her husband, and was his helper. Once, when Lopāmudrā had bathed after her season, Agastya, pleased by her purity of body, by her beauty and by her love for her husband, desired her company — so the story is told in the Mahābhārata. But in the Ṛk-saṃhitā it is told that Lopāmudrā, worn by hard austerity, obtained rest and wished for her husband's company; in the Mahābhārata it is Agastya himself who wished. The rest of the story is the same. As in the Bṛhaddevatā — "*ṛtusnātāṃ ṛṣir bhāryāṃ lopāmudrāṃ yaśasvinīm | upajalpitum ārebhe rahaḥsaṃyogakāmyayā*" — so also in the Mahābhārata, "*tapasā dyotitāṃ snātāṃ dadarśa bhagavān ṛṣiḥ*". In the sequence of this story there is no great difference between the Vedic description and the description in the Itihāsa. That same matter the Nirukta-writers have stated as "*ṛṣiputryā vilapitam*" ("the lament of a ṛṣi's daughter").

### Printed p. 485  (PDF 505)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 485.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

***nadasya — nadanasya japaśabdayituḥ japādhyayanakartuḥ*** — one who sounds the recitation (*japa*), who studies and mutters it; Sāyaṇa explains it as "the praiser" (*stutikartā*), the one who utters words of *japa*, *stotra* and the like. The Nirukta-writers, giving an explanation of this ṛk, have given the derivation of the word as follows:

> "ऋषिर्नदो भवति नदतेः स्तुतिकर्मणः"

> *"ṛṣirnado bhavati nadateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ"*

(Ni. 5-2 [?]) — the word *nada*, formed from the root *nad* ("to praise"), means "the ṛṣi who is the praiser". The word is used in many places as a synonym of *ṛṣi*. For example:

> रसद्गन्धर्वीरस्या च योषणा नदस्य नादे परि पातु नो मनः ।

> *rasadgandharvīrasyā ca yoṣaṇā nadasya nāde pari pātu no manaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-11-2 [?]) — there are in this the two words *nadasya* and *nāde*; of these, *nadasya* is explained as "of the praiser", and *nāde* as "in the sound of praise". But the meaning "praiser" is not required in every place where the word occurs. For example:

> उक्षन्ते अश्वा अत्या इवाजिषु नदस्य कर्णैस्तुरयन्त आशुभिः ।

> *ukṣante aśvā atyā ivājiṣu nadasya karṇaisturayanta āśubhiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-3 [?]) — here *nadasya* is explained as *śabdavataḥ meghasya* ("of the sounding cloud").

***ni riṇāti*** — the word *riṇāti* is read among the names of motion (*gati*). Here it is explained as "let her approach". This meaning follows the order of the words of the ṛk. For, as Sāyaṇa says, if this sentence is by Agastya, then "she approaches"; or, if, according to the Nirukta-writers' view, it is Lopāmudrā's sentence, then it means "it burns". In general this word is used mostly in the meanings "to dry up, to burn". For example:

> पुरूणि दस्मो नि रिणाति जम्भैराद्रोचते वन आ विभावा ।

> *purūṇi dasmo ni riṇāti jambhairādrocate vana ā vibhāvā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-148-4 [?]) — just as in such ṛks it gives the sense "to burn", so in the ṛk at hand, too, since there is no room for fulfilment of desire in the love of a self-restrained ascetic, to explain it as "it burns the body" would not be wrong. The words *itaḥ* and *amutaḥ* likewise vary in meaning.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***nadasya*** — root *nad avyakte śabde*; by "*nandigrahapacādibhyo…*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134 [?]) the suffix *ac*; by "*citaḥ*" the final syllable is *udātta*; the genitive is in the sense of the object (*karmārthe ṣaṣṭhī*).

### Printed p. 486  (PDF 506)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 486.)*

- ***rudhataḥ*** — root *rudhir āvaraṇe*; *śatṛ* substituted for *laṭ*; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" elision of the *vikaraṇa*; genitive singular; by "*śatur anumo nadyajādī*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173 [?]) the case-ending that follows the *num*-less *śatṛ* takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***agan*** — root *gamḷ gatau*; *laṅ*, third person singular, *tip*; by "*itaś ca*" elision of the *i*; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" elision of the *vikaraṇa*; by "*hal ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt…*" elision of the *tip*; by "*mo no dhātoḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 8-2-64 [?], as read) *n* in place of the final *m* of the root; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***ājātaḥ*** — by "*gatir anantaraḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49 [?]), since it stands in a *krānta*-word, the *gati* (*ā*) takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***riṇāti*** — root *rī gatireṣaṇayoḥ*, *kryādi* class; *laṭ*, third person singular; by "*pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-80 [?]) shortening of the root vowel; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***adhīrā*** — a *naña*-*tatpuruṣa* compound; by "*tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2 [?]) the fore-member (an indeclinable) keeps its natural accent.
- ***dhayati*** — root *dhet pāne*; *laṭ*, third person singular, *tip* following; *śap* as the *vikaraṇa*; taking that as the cause, *e* becomes *ay*; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***śvasantam*** — root *śvas prāṇane*; *śatṛ* substituted for *laṭ*; elision of *śap*; by the suffix accent the first syllable is *udātta*; accusative singular. ‖ 4 ‖

**Sūkta 179, Ṛk 5**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> इमं नु सोममन्तितो हृत्सु पीतमुप ब्रुवे ।
> यत्सीमागश्चकृमा तत्सु मृळतु पुलुकामो हि मर्त्यः ॥ ५ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> इमम् । नु । सोमम् । अन्तितः । हृत्ऽसु । पीतम् । उप । ब्रुवे ।
> यत् । सीम् । आगः । चकृम । तत् । सु । मृळतु । पुलुऽकामः । हि । मर्त्यः ॥ ५ ॥

> *imam | nu | somam | antitaḥ | hṛt 'su | pītam | upa | bruve |*
> *yat | sīm | āgaḥ | cakṛma | tat | su | mṛḷatu | pulu 'kāmaḥ | hi | martyaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

### Printed p. 487  (PDF 507)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 487.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अथानयोर्दम्पत्योः सम्भोगसंलापं श्रुत्वा तत्पाश्चात्यशिष्यस्तं चिकीर्षुरुत्तराभ्यां [?] द्वाभ्यामाह । अनयोर्विनियोगः शौनकेनोक्तः ॥ इमं नु सोममित्येते द्वे ऋचौ प्रयतो जपन् । सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति पापेभ्यश्च प्रमुच्यते । ऋग्वि. १-२६ [?] ॥ इति ॥ उपेत्य मनसा प्राप्य प्रार्थयते । किं ब्रवीति उच्यते । यदागो गुर्वोः कामप्रलापश्रवणविषयं पापं चकृम कृतवन्तो वयं तत्तस्मादागसः स सोमः सु सम्यग्मृळतु । सुखयतु । पापजनितदुःखं मा करोत्वित्यर्थः । महत्त्वापमनुभुज्यमानं [?] प्रार्थनया कथं लुप्यते इति अत आह । हि यस्मान्मर्त्यो मनुष्यः पुलुकामो बहुकामनावान् । अल्पेनैव कर्मणा बहुकामानाकालयति [?] । यस्मादेवं तस्मात्परिहरेत्यर्थः । यद्वा । अयमपवर्जनीयेऽतेयो [?] प्राप्यते इवेत्याह । पुलुकामो हि खलु मर्त्यः कामहतः सन् कामेन निरुद्ध एव वर्तते । अतस्तयोरुक्तैकोऽयुक्तः [?] । केचिद्बह्वश्रवणदोषोऽपि प्रामादिकोऽस्माकं प्राप्तेन सोमेन परिहर्तव्य इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । अयं मन्त्रश्चन्द्रपरो व्याख्येयो मनसोऽभिमानित्वाच्च तस्य पापस्यापि मनस्येव सम्भावितत्वात् । अस्मिन्पक्षे हृत्सु पीतं हृदयस्थितमित्यर्थः । शिष्टं स्पष्टम् ॥ [as read; several phrases doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Hearing the couple's talk of union, their pupil, wishing to atone for it, says in these two ṛks that men are full of desires and begs Soma to remove the sin; Soma may be the juice or (in another view) the moon, the deity of the mind.

**Pratipadārtha**

**hi** — because; **martyaḥ** — man; **pulukāmaḥ** — desiring much gain from little work; **yat sīm** — which (this: the hearing of the guru-wife's talk of desire); **āgaḥ** — sin; **cakṛma** — we have done; **tat** — that sin; **su mṛḷatu** — may it be made well, easy (so that no fault arises from the sin); **nu** — now; **hṛtsu pītam** — drunk with the heart (drunk by the mind); **imaṃ somam** — this Soma juice; **antitaḥ** — from near; **upa bruve** — I pray; [or **hṛtsu pītam** — residing in the heart (the moon, the deity of the mind); **imaṃ somam** — this moon; **antitaḥ upa bruve** — I draw near and pray.]

**Bhāvārtha**

Men are full of desires; therefore, for this sin done by us (by the pupil) — the fault of hearing the talk of desire of the guru-couple — I draw near and pray to this Soma, drunk in the mind, that it be removed. (I pray the Moon, the presiding deity of the mind, to remove the sin.)

### Printed p. 488  (PDF 508)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 488.)*

**Printed English**

> (Pupil),—I beseech the Soma juice, which has been drunk in my heart, that it may fully expiate the sin we have committed: man is subject to many desires.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

This ṛk has been explained in two or three ways. Here Agastya's pupil indicates repentance for his sinful act. The repentance may be for the sin arising from having heard the conversation about desire between Agastya and Lopāmudrā. Or, since the natural faults of man are many, and among these desire is outstanding, he may be expressing repentance for such a fault. And the means of removing this sin must be a prayer addressed to Soma. But here, for the word *somam*, there is room for dispute whether the meaning is the Soma juice or the moon. Therefore Sāyaṇa too could not give a definitive meaning for this ṛk. First:

> *āgaḥ — gurvoḥ kāmapralāpaśravaṇaviṣayaṃ pāpaṃ kṛtavantaḥ tasmād āgasaḥ sukhayatu*

— "may there be removal of the sin that comes from hearing the conversation about the desire of our gurus (the couple)"; and second:

> *pulukāmo hi martyaḥ kāmahataḥ san kāmena niruddha eva vartate*

— "man, afflicted by manifold desires, lives hindered by desire, and so commits sin; may there be removal of such sin". But the means of removing the sin is a prayer addressed to Soma. What is the sense of Soma? It may be the Soma juice or the moon. In the Ṛgveda the word *soma* is nowhere explained as "moon". But when it is called the *Soma-devatā*, it can bear both meanings. The identity (*tādātmya*) of the deity Soma and the moon is stated in many places; and in many places this deity Soma is addressed in prayer for the removal of sin; so here there is room for both meanings.

> सोमेनादित्या बलिनः सोमेन पृथिवी मही ।
> अथो नक्षत्राणामेषामुपस्थे सोम आहितः ॥

> *somenādityā balinaḥ somena pṛthivī mahī |*
> *atho nakṣatrāṇāmeṣāmupasthe soma āhitaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-2 [?]) — as it is described here that Indra and the other deities, and the earth and the other worlds, grow by *soma*, the sense "Soma juice" fits. And even if it is explained as "moon", since the moon is the cause of the nourishment of all the worlds, it is quite natural; and in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, … [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 489  (PDF 509)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 489.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

> एष वै सोमो राजा देवानामन्नं यच्चन्द्रमाः ।

> *eṣa vai somo rājā devānāmannaṃ yaccandramāḥ |*

(Śa. Brā. 1-6-4-5 [?]) — here the identity of the moon and Soma is stated. Likewise in the sentences below also this description occurs:

> चन्द्रमा वै ब्रह्मा सोमो वै चन्द्रमाः ।

> *candramā vai brahmā somo vai candramāḥ |*

(Śa. Brā. 13-1-1-2 [?])

> सूर्य एवाग्नेयः । चन्द्रमाः सौम्यः ।

> *sūrya evāgneyaḥ | candramāḥ saumyaḥ |*

(Śa. Brā. 1-6-3-24 [?]) — thus in many places the moon is called *saumya*. Therefore, in the ṛk at hand, for "*hṛtsu pītam imaṃ somam*" the meaning "this moon who is the presiding deity of the mind and who abides in the heart" has been stated as the second meaning. And for the removal of sin:

> उरुष्या णो अभिशस्तेः सोम नि पाह्यंहसः ।
> सखा सुशेव एधि नः ॥

> *uruṣyā ṇo abhiśasteḥ soma ni pāhyaṃhasaḥ |*
> *sakhā suśeva edhi naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-15 [?]) — in such ṛks the prayer is made: "O deity Soma, protect us from calumny and blame (*apavāda*); protect us fully from the sin done by us or possible for us"; and so on. In the same way here too the pupil prays for the removal of his own sin. In the Atharvaveda:

> सोमो मा देवो मुञ्चतु यमाहुश्चन्द्रमा इति ।

> *somo mā devo muñcatu yamāhuścandramā iti |*

(At. Ve. 11-6-7 [?]) — in the prayer "may the deity Soma, whom all call the moon, release me from sin" the identity of Soma and the moon is quite plain.

***pulukāmaḥ*** — "*pulukāmaḥ purukāmaḥ, pulukāmo hi martyaḥ ity api nigamo bhavati*" (Ni. 6-4 [?]) — it shows the nature of man, who has manifold desires. Since there are so many kinds of desires, sin (*āgaḥ*) comes naturally to man; therefore the prayer is made: escape from this sin.

***āgaḥ*** — "*āñpūrvād gameḥ*" (Ni. 11-23 [?]) — to the root *gam* the prefix *ā* is added, and the form *āgaḥ* is derived. That is, the one who has done sinful acts must certainly come, as the result, to this sin-impression (*pāpasaṃskāra*) and its fruit; because the word shows this meaning, the name *āgaḥ* is well known — so the Nirukta-writers explain.

### Printed p. 490  (PDF 510)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 490.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***hṛtsu*** — by "*ūḍidaṃpadādi…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 [?]) the case-ending takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***pītam*** — root *pā pāne*; the suffix *kta* in the passive; by "*ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-66 [?]) *ī* for the *ā*; by the suffix accent the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***bruve*** — root *brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*; *laṭ*, first person singular; since it stands in an *atiṅanta* word-position, the *nighāta* accent occurs.
- ***āgaḥ*** — root *iṇ gatau*; by "*iṇa āgo 'parādhe ca*" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]) the suffix *asun*; *āg* substituted for the root; since the suffix has *n* as marker, the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***cakṛma*** — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *liṭ*, first person plural; because of *yad*-connection no *nighāta*; by the suffix accent the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***mṛḷatu*** — root *mṛḍa sukhane*; *loṭ*, second (third) person singular [as printed "madhyama"]; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***pulukāmaḥ*** — in the *bahuvrīhi*, by "*parādiś chandasi bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199 [?]) the hind-member takes the *ādyudātta* accent. ‖ 5 ‖
