### Printed p. 491  (PDF 511)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 491.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अथ विनियुक्तयोर्मध्ये द्वितीययो [?] सूक्ते षष्ठ्यन्तेवास्याह [?] ॥ अयमगस्त्यो मुद्गरुः [?] खनित्रैः फलस्योत्पादनसाधनैर्यज्ञस्तोत्रादिभिः खनमानः फलमभिमतमुत्पादयन् प्रजां प्रकर्षेण पुनःपुनर्जायमानमपत्यं कुलस्यापकेनसाधनं [?] पुत्रादिकं बलं चेच्छमानः सन् । यद्वा । प्रजां भृत्यादिरूपां चेच्छन् । ऋषिरतीन्द्रियद्रष्टा महानुभाव उग्र उद्गूर्णः संसारे सञ्चरन्नप्यपापः सन्नुभौ वर्णौ वर्णनीयावाकारौ कामं च तपश्च पुपोष । सत्या आशिषो देवेषु देवेभ्यो जगाम । प्राप्तवान् । यतोऽयं महानुभावस्तस्मादस्मान्पातीत्यर्थः ॥ [as read; several words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Agastya, a seer who has obtained from the gods blessings of true fruit, nourished both desire and austerity, seeking offspring and strength; so he protects us.

**Pratipadārtha**

**khanitraiḥ** — with the implements, such as sacrifice and *stotra*, that produce the fruit; **khanamānaḥ** — digging out the desired fruit; **prajām** — progeny, such as servants; **apatyam** — sons and grandsons, who raise up the family; **balam (ca)** — and strength; **icchamānaḥ** — desiring; **ṛṣiḥ** — the seer of what lies beyond the senses; **ugraḥ** — [though immersed in the world] sinless; **Agastyaḥ** — our teacher Agastya; **ubhau varṇau** — the two kinds of acts, desire and austerity; **pupoṣa** — fostered; (and) **deveṣu** — from the deities; **satyāḥ** — of true fruits; **āśiṣaḥ** — the blessings; **jagāma** — obtained.

**Bhāvārtha**

The ṛṣi Agastya, who achieves what he desires by means such as sacrifice and praise, who desires sons, servants, strength and the like, who sees beyond the senses and is sinless though immersed in worldly life, has come having accomplished both desire and austerity; therefore he has obtained from the deities blessings of true fruit (the favour of the deities).

**Printed English**

> Agastya, a venerable sage, working with (fit) implements, desiring progeny, offspring, and strength, practised both classes (of obligations), and received true benedictions from the gods.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***ubhau varṇau ṛṣir ugraḥ pupoṣa*** — it says that the ṛṣi Agastya made two kinds of *varṇa* flourish. For "*ubhau varṇau*" Sāyaṇa has explained "*kāmaṃ ca tapaś ca*" … [the sentence continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 492  (PDF 512)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 492.)*

… that is, desire and austerity, the two. Or it can be explained as the two kinds of wealth, this-worldly (*aihika*) and other-worldly (*āmuṣmika*): earthly wealth is the fruit of desire, and other-worldly wealth is the fruit of austerity. The sense can be that Agastya made both these fruits flourish. If one is to obtain, by one's own power, the riches of both worlds, Agastya must have had extraordinary strength of being (*sattva*); its greatness is shown by the sequence of his origin.

Since Agastya is the son of Mitra and Varuṇa, the individual powers of Mitra and Varuṇa joined and made a special power in Agastya. Agastya is well known as *Maitrāvaruṇi*; how this came about and why, the author of the Bṛhaddevatā has explained in this way:

> तयोरादित्ययोः सत्रे दृष्ट्वाप्सरसमुर्वशीम् । रेतश्चस्कन्द तत्कुम्भे न्यपतद्वासतीवरे ॥
> तेनैव तु मुहूर्तेन वीर्यवन्तौ तपस्विनौ । अगस्त्यश्च वसिष्ठश्च तत्रर्षी सम्बभूवतुः ॥
> बहुधा पतितं रेतः कलशे च जले स्थले । स्थले वसिष्ठस्तु मुनिः सम्भूत ऋषिसत्तमः ॥
> कुम्भे त्वगस्त्यः सम्भूतो जले मत्स्यो महाद्युतिः । उदियाय ततोऽगस्त्यः शम्यामात्रो महातपाः ॥
> मानेन सम्मितो यस्मात्तस्मान्मान्य इहोच्यते । यद्वा कुम्भादृषिर्जातः कुम्भेनापि हि मीयते ॥
> कुम्भ इत्यभिधानं च परिमाणस्य लक्ष्यते ॥

> *tayorādityayoḥ satre dṛṣṭvāpsarasamurvaśīm | retaścaskanda tatkumbhe nyapatadvāsatīvare ‖*
> *tenaiva tu muhūrtena vīryavantau tapasvinau | agastyaśca vasiṣṭhaśca tatrarṣī sambabhūvatuḥ ‖*
> *bahudhā patitaṃ retaḥ kalaśe ca jale sthale | sthale vasiṣṭhastu muniḥ sambhūta ṛṣisattamaḥ ‖*
> *kumbhe tvagastyaḥ sambhūto jale matsyo mahādyutiḥ | udiyāya tato 'gastyaḥ śamyāmātro mahātapāḥ ‖*
> *mānena sammito yasmāttasmānmānya ihocyate | yadvā kumbhādṛṣirjātaḥ kumbhenāpi hi mīyate ‖*
> *kumbha ityabhidhānaṃ ca parimāṇasya lakṣyate ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 5-149 to 154 [?]) — of these Ādityas, Mitra and Varuṇa both saw, in a sacrificial session (*sattra*), the heavenly courtesan Urvaśī and were infatuated; then their seed fell and dropped into the *vasatīvarī* pot (*kumbha*).

> तस्या दर्शनान्मित्रावरुणयोः रेतश्चस्कन्द ।

> *tasyā darśanānmitrāvaruṇayoḥ retaścaskanda |*

(Ni. 5-13 [?]) — at once two ascetics, ṛṣis of great vigour, Vasiṣṭha and Agastya, came into being. That is, the seed fell in the pot, in the water, and on the ground. By the seed that fell on the ground Vasiṣṭha, the best of ṛṣis, was born; Agastya was born from the pot and from the water, and the fish [*matsya*, of great brilliance]. The greatly austere Agastya, of the measure of a *śamyā* (the sacrificial peg), came out. Because he was measured (*sammita*), he is said to be "honoured" (*mānya*), and so he got the name; the story of Agastya's origin. Born of Mitra and Varuṇa, Agastya must have obtained the extraordinary powers of both; the individual powers of the two are described in the *śruti* thus:

> इमां वां मित्रावरुणा सुवृक्तिमिषं न कृण्वे असुरा नवीयः ।
> इनो वामन्यः पदवीरदब्धो जनं च मित्रो यतते ब्रुवाणः ॥

> *imāṃ vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā suvṛktimiṣaṃ na kṛṇve asurā navīyaḥ |*
> *ino vāmanyaḥ padavīradabdho janaṃ ca mitro yatate bruvāṇaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-36-2 [?], as read)

---

### Printed p. 493  (PDF 513)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 493.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … in this ṛk the individual nature and function of Mitra and Varuṇa are described. In it Varuṇa is said to be the overseer of *dharma* and *adharma* and to lead creatures to worldly dealings. In the ṛk at hand also Agastya describes these two powers. And, as is described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, the individual qualities of Mitra and Varuṇa are the root of both these kinds of power. For example:

> वागेवाग्निः प्राणोपानौ मित्रावरुणौ ।

> *vāgevāgniḥ prāṇopānau mitrāvaruṇau |*

(Śa. Brā. 3-2-2-13 [?]) — Mitra is of the nature of *prāṇa* and Varuṇa of the nature of *udāna* (*apāna* in the text as printed). As is described in the Chāndogya:

> "…… स प्राणः केच्चक्षुः [?] स आदित्यस्तदेतत्तेजोऽन्नाद्यमित्युपासीत तेजस्व्यन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद"

> *"…… sa prāṇaḥ keccakṣuḥ [?] sa ādityastadetattejo 'nnādyamityupāsīta tejasvyannādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda"*

(Chā. U. 3-13-1 [?]) — *prāṇa* has the form of the Āditya. One should meditate on it as food and brilliance. The one who knows this principle becomes radiant and an eater of food: so *prāṇa* is praised. This is a quality of this-worldly (*aihika*) wealth. Agastya, increasing the *aihika* wealth, had obtained the quality of Mitra. And Varuṇa's quality, *udāna*, is praised thus:

> "…… स उदानः स वायुः स आकाशस्तदेतदोजश्च महश्चेत्युपासीत ओजस्वी महस्वान्भवति य एवं वेद"

> *"…… sa udānaḥ sa vāyuḥ sa ākāśastadetadojaśca mahaścetyupāsīta ojasvī mahasvānbhavati ya evaṃ veda"*

(Chā. U. 3-13-3 [?]) — *udāna* is of the nature of wind and space. One should meditate on it as *ojas* ("vigour") and *mahas* ("greatness"); the one who knows this principle becomes vigorous and great: so the matter of spiritual (*adhyātmika*) wealth is praised. This is the quality of Varuṇa. Agastya obtained it and obtained the spiritual wealth in full, as is described in the ṛk at hand.

> क्रतूदक्षौ ह वा अस्य मित्रावरुणौ । एतन्नध्यात्मं स यदेव मनसा कामयत इदं मे स्यादिदं कुर्वीयेति स एव क्रतुरथ यदस्मै तत्समृध्यते स दक्षो मित्र एव क्रतुर्वरुणो दक्षो ब्रह्मैव मित्रः क्षत्रं वरुणोऽभिगन्तैव ब्रह्म कर्ता क्षत्रियः ॥

> *kratūdakṣau ha vā asya mitrāvaruṇau | etannadhyātmaṃ sa yadeva manasā kāmayata idaṃ me syādidaṃ kurvīyeti sa eva kraturatha yadasmai tatsamṛdhyate sa dakṣo mitra eva kraturvaruṇo dakṣo brahmaiva mitraḥ kṣatraṃ varuṇo 'bhigantaiva brahma kartā kṣatriyaḥ ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 4-1-4-1 [?]) — of the pair Mitra and Varuṇa, Mitra is of the nature of resolve and Varuṇa of the nature of spiritual power. To resolve for success of a work is Mitra's function; to accomplish it is Varuṇa's. Also, Mitra is of the form of *brahma* and Varuṇa of *kṣatra*; *brahman* is *kratu*, and Varuṇa is *dakṣa* for all. And:

> अयं वै लोको मित्रः असौ वरुणः ।

> *ayaṃ vai loko mitraḥ asau varuṇaḥ |*

(Śa. Brā. 12-9-2-12 [?])

### Printed p. 494  (PDF 514)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 179"; page 494.)*

— in many places Mitra is praised as this world and Varuṇa as the heavenly world. Since these same qualities lay in their son Agastya, he was able to obtain this-worldly wealth in the form of sons and others, and, in the form of *dharma*, the ethical and spiritual wealth. So in the ṛk at hand the pupil praises the great qualities of his teacher.

***ṛṣiḥ*** — since Agastya is the best among ascetics, he is praised as "ṛṣi". The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa gives the derivation of the word *ṛṣi* thus, and at the same time tells the relation of the ṛṣis to creation:

> "असद्वा इदमग्र आसीत् । तदाहुः किं तदसदासीदिति । ऋषयो वाव तेऽग्रेऽसदासीत्तदाहुः के ते ऋषय इति प्राणा वा ऋषयस्ते यत्पुरास्मात्सर्वस्मादिदमिच्छन्तः श्रमेण तपसारिषंस्तस्मादृषयः"

> *"asadvā idamagra āsīt | tadāhuḥ kiṃ tadasadāsīditi | ṛṣayo vāva te 'gre 'sadāsīttadāhuḥ ke te ṛṣaya iti prāṇā vā ṛṣayaste yatpurāsmātsarvasmādidamicchantaḥ śrameṇa tapasāriṣaṃstasmādṛṣayaḥ"*

(Śa. Brā. 6-1-1-1 [?]) — in the beginning there was only non-being (*asat*). These ṛṣis were in that form. Who are the ṛṣis? They are the *prāṇas*. Before this whole [creation], desiring it, they wearied themselves with toil and austerity (*ariṣan*); therefore they are called ṛṣis. And:

> "………… त्वयु तन्तुमेतमिति योऽसावृषिभिस्तन्तुस्ततस्तमेतदाह" [as read [?]]

> *"………… tvayu tantumetamiti yo 'sāvṛṣibhistantustatastametadāha" [as read [?]]*

(Śa. Brā. 8-6-3-23 [?]) — [they] stretched out the thread of the sacrifice that is of the nature of the world; the power of the ṛṣis, as cause of the world's expansion, is praised; hence they are also spoken of as of the nature of the creator Brahmā.

> "प्राणा वा ऋषयः प्रथमजास्तद्धि ब्रह्म प्रथमजम्"

> *"prāṇā vā ṛṣayaḥ prathamajāstaddhi brahma prathamajam"*

(Śa. Brā. 8-6-1-5 [?]) — thus the identity (*tādātmya*) of the ṛṣis and *brahman* is shown. If this is one derivation, another derivation can be set against it. As said in Vācaspatya:

> "ऋषति ज्ञानेन संसारपारम्"

> *"ṛṣati jñānena saṃsārapāram"*

— "he crosses to the far shore of *saṃsāra* by knowledge": from the root *ṛṣ* the word *ṛṣi* is formed, and means "the knower". Thus, by one derivation, the ṛṣis are the root cause of the creation of the world; by another, the cause of the cessation of *saṃsāra*. In Agastya both these powers existed: so the description of the ṛk at hand. In "*ubhau varṇau pupoṣa*", by obtaining satisfaction of desire, the power of creation is described, and by obtaining spiritual knowledge, the power which is the means for the cessation of *saṃsāra*.

### Printed p. 495  (PDF 515)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 22"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 495.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

***ṛṣī (ṛṣ) gatau*** — the word *ṛṣi*, formed from this root meaning "to go", has been explained by the derivation stated above. Besides, the scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit–English Dictionary, has noted that the word *ṛṣi* may also be formed from the root *dṛś*, and, giving the meaning of the word *ṛṣikṛt*, has stated "Causing to see, enlightening". Of the examples, the first:

> इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो न इममध्वानं यमगाम दूरात् ।
> आपिः पिता प्रमतिः सोम्यानां भृमिरस्यृषिकृन्मर्त्यानाम् ॥

> *imāmagne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo na imamadhvānaṃ yamagāma dūrāt |*
> *āpiḥ pitā pramatiḥ somyānāṃ bhṛmirasyṛṣikṛnmartyānām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-16 [?]) — in this ṛk the word *ṛṣikṛt* is an epithet of Agni. Sāyaṇa explained this word as *darśanakārī* ("one who causes to see"). Likewise:

> ऋषिमना य ऋषिकृत्स्वर्षाः सहस्रणीथः पदवीः कवीनाम् ।
> तृतीयं धाम महिषः सिषासन्त्सोमो विराजमनु राजति ष्टुप् ॥

> *ṛṣimanā ya ṛṣikṛtsvarṣāḥ sahasraṇīthaḥ padavīḥ kavīnām |*
> *tṛtīyaṃ dhāma mahiṣaḥ siṣāsantsomo virājamanu rājati ṣṭup ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-96-18 [?]) — in this ṛk also, for the word *ṛṣimanāḥ* the meaning "of a mind that sees all" and for *ṛṣikṛt* "the maker of the seeing of all" has been given. In ordinary usage, too, "seeing" (*darśana*) is a synonym of knowledge of the true principle; these are the implications. Since Agastya obtained a seeing in the form of knowledge of the true principle, he can be said to be praised as a *ṛṣi*.

***satyāḥ*** — "*satyaphalātmakavāda* (*āśiṣaḥ*)", i.e. "blessings of true fruit". The derivation and special meaning of this word will be explained in Ṛk 1-180-7 [?].

> इमं नु सोममित्येते द्वे ऋचौ प्रयतो जपन् ।
> सर्वान् कामानवाप्नोति पापेभ्यश्च प्रमुच्यते ॥

> *imaṃ nu somamityete dve ṛcau prayato japan |*
> *sarvān kāmānavāpnoti pāpebhyaśca pramucyate ‖*

(Ṛgvidhāna 1-147 [?]) — "if a man recites, with restraint, these two ṛks, '*imaṃ nu somam*' and '*agastyaḥ khanamānaḥ*', all desired objects become attainable to him and he is freed from sin": so the Ṛgvidhāna praises these mantras.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***khanamānaḥ*** — root *khanu avadāraṇe*; *śānac* in place of *laṭ*; by "*tāsyanudāttet…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 [?]) the *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta*, so the root accent remains.

### Printed p. 496  (PDF 516)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 180"; page 496.)*

- ***khanitraiḥ*** — the root as above; by "*uṣikhanibhyāṃ kit?*" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-61 [?], as read) the suffix *ṭran* [as printed *tran*]; the *iṭ* augment; by *vyatyaya* the middle syllable is *udātta*.
- ***icchamānaḥ*** — root *iṣu icchāyām*; by *vyatyaya* *śānac* in place of *laṭ*; by "*iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-77 [?]) *ccha* is substituted for the final of the root; by "*ānemuk*" the augment *muk*; by "*tāsyanudāttet…*" the *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta*, so the accent of the *śa* *vikaraṇa* remains.
- ***pupoṣa*** — root *puṣa puṣṭau*; *liṭ*, third person singular; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent. ‖ 6 ‖

Here ends the 179th Sūkta. (*iḷḷige nūra eppattoṃbhattaneya sūkta mugidudu.*)

## Sūkta 180 (the 180th Sūkta; "Nūra eṃbhattaneyu sūktavu") — beginning of the 24th Anuvāka

> अथ चतुर्विंशेऽनुवाके द्वादश सूक्तानि । तत्र युवो रजांसीति दशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभम् । तुह्यादिपरिभाषयेदमादिसूक्तपञ्चकमाश्विनम् । युवोर्दशाश्विनं [?] वा इत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ एतदादीनि तृतीयवर्जितानि पञ्च सूक्तानि प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोस्त्रैष्टुभे छन्दसि विनियुक्तानि । आथाश्विन इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । युवो रजांसीति पञ्चानां तृतीयमुद्धरेत् । आ. ४-१३ [?] । इति ॥

*Translation of the introduction:* With this sūkta the twenty-fourth Anuvāka of the first Maṇḍala begins. In this Anuvāka there are twelve sūktas; of them the sūkta "*yuvo rajāṃsi*" is the first. It has ten ṛks; its ṛṣi is Agastya; the metre is Triṣṭubh. By the technical rule (*paribhāṣā*) of the Anukramaṇikā beginning "*tu hi*", the five sūktas beginning with this one have the Aśvins as their deity (the Anukramaṇikā says "*yuvor daśāśvinam*" [?]). Of these five sūktas, leaving out the third (the 182nd sūkta [?]), the remaining four, i.e. the sūktas 180, 181, 183 and 184 [as read [?]], are applied, in the recital of the Prātaranuvāka and of the Aśvina-śastra, for the Triṣṭubh ṛks: so it is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section "*athāśvina*", "*yuvo rajāṃsīti pañcānāṃ tṛtīyam uddharet*" (Āś. 4-13 [?]).

### Printed p. 497  (PDF 517)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 23"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 497; signature mark "XIII 32".)*

**Sūkta 180**

Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 24 ‖ Sūkta 180 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 23–24 [as read [?]] ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta — 10 ‖
Ṛṣi — Agastya ‖ Devatā — Aśvinau ‖ Chandas — Triṣṭubh ‖

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 1**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> युवो रजांसि सुयमासो अश्वा रथो यद्वां पर्यर्णांसि दीयत् ।
> हिरण्यया वां पवयः प्रुषायन्मध्वः पिबन्ता उषसः सचेथे ॥ १ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> युवोः । रजांसि । सुऽयमासः । अश्वाः । रथः । यत् । वाम् । परि । अर्णांसि । दीयत् ।
> हिरण्ययाः । वाम् । पवयः । प्रुषायन् । मध्वः । पिबन्ता । उषसः । सचेथे इति ॥ १ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ युवोर्युवयोरश्वा रथवोढारो रजांसि रञ्जकाॅल्लोकान् सुयमासः शोभननियमनाः । लोकत्रयेऽसञ्चारिण [?] इत्यर्थः । कदेति आह । यद्यदा वां रथोऽर्णांस्यरणीयानभिमतदेशान् परि दीयत् परिगच्छेत् परितो गच्छति वा । तदेत्यर्थः । दीयतिर्गतिकर्मा दीयति तकतीति तैक्ष्णर्मसु [?] पाठात् । किंच रथागमनकाले वां युवयोः पवयो वज्रा रथनेमयो वा हिरण्यया हिरण्मयाः [?] प्रुषायन् । प्रुष्णन्त्यभिमतम् । यद्वा । हिरण्ययानि पवयो मधुपात्राणि वां युवाभ्यामर्थाय । यस्मादेवं तस्माद्युवां मध्वो मधुनो मधुसदृशस्य सोमरसस्य ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ सोमरसं पिबन्तावास्वादयन्तौ उषस उषःसम्बन्धिनि काले सचेथे । यज्ञं सङ्गच्छेथे । अत्र क्रमो न विवक्षितः । उषःकाल एवागत्य मधुरं सोमरसं पिबतमित्यर्थः ॥ [as read; a few words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* When the Aśvins' chariot travels to the desired places, their well-controlled horses range the worlds and the golden fellies shower what is wished; at dawn they come and drink the honey-like Soma.

### Printed p. 498  (PDF 518)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 498.)*

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he* **Aśvinau**) — O Aśvins; **yat** — when; **vām** — your; **rathaḥ** — chariot; **arṇāṃsi** — to the desired places; **pari dīyat** — goes round about; (**tadā** — then) **yuvoḥ** — of you two; **aśvāḥ** — the chariot-horses; **rajāṃsi** — the three worlds; **suyamāsaḥ** — well controlled in movement (they range); (**kiṃ ca** — and) **vām** — your; **hiraṇyayāḥ** — golden; **pavayaḥ** — the thunderbolt-weapons or the felloes of the chariot-wheels; **pruṣāyan** — shower the desired (rain the wished-for objects); [or **hiraṇyayāḥ** — golden; **pavayaḥ** — honey-vessels; **vām** — for you two; **pruṣāyan** — pour (the desired honey)]; (therefore) you two, **madhvaḥ** — honey-like Soma juice; **pibantā** — drinking; **uṣasaḥ** — at the time of dawn; **sacethe** — join (the sacrifice).

**Bhāvārtha**

O Aśvins! When your chariot sets out for the place desired, your chariot-horses range through the three worlds; your golden thunderbolt-weapons or chariot-felloes fulfil wishes (or the golden honey-vessels pour out the honey you want); therefore you two, coming at dawn to the sacrificial hall, drink the honey-like Soma juice.

**Printed English**

> Ashwins, your horses are traversers of the (three) regions, when your chariot proceeds to (its desired) quarters: the golden fellies of your wheels grant (whatever is wished for): drinking the Soma juice, you participate in the morning (rite).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***rathaḥ*** —

> रथः रंहतेर्गतिकर्मणः । स्थिरतेर्वा स्याद्विपरीतस्य । रमतेर्वा रममाणोऽस्मिंस्तिष्ठतीति वा [?] । रपतेर्वा रसतेर्वा ॥

> *rathaḥ raṃhatergatikarmaṇaḥ | sthiratervā syādviparītasya | ramatervā ramamāṇo 'smiṃstiṣṭhatīti vā [?] | rapatervā rasatervā ‖*

(Ni. 9-11 [?]) — the Nirukta-writers say that the word *ratha* is formed from the root *raṃh*, which gives the sense of motion or speed; or, by a reversal of letters, from *sthira* ("firm"); or from the root *ram*, meaning "to rejoice, to be glad while seated in it"; or from *rap* or *ras*, meaning "to make a sound". The Nirukta-writers, …[the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 499  (PDF 519)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 499.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

> वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा प्रतरणः सुवीरः ।
> गोभिः सन्नद्धो असि वीळयस्वास्थाता ते जयतु जेत्वानि ॥

> *vanaspate vīḍvaṅgo hi bhūyā asmatsakhā prataraṇaḥ suvīraḥ |*
> *gobhiḥ sannaddho asi vīḷayasvāsthātā te jayatu jetvāni ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-26 [?]) — citing this ṛk, the derivation of the word *ratha* is explained [in some places the word also denotes the sons and others who run in chariots; it is designated by this same word]. In some places this word is used also as a synonym of *āditya* (for example Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-2 [?]).

***rajāṃsi*** — "*rajo rajyater jyotir ity api raja ucyate udakaṃ raja ucyate | lokā rajāṃsy ucyante*" (Ni. 4-19 [?]) — for the word *rajas*, formed from the root *rañj*, which gives the sense of "to shine", the meanings are "light", "water" and "worlds".

> रजांसि चित्रा वि चरन्ति तन्यवो दिवः सम्राजा पयसा न उक्षतम् ।

> *rajāṃsi citrā vi caranti tanyavo divaḥ samrājā payasā na ukṣatam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-3 [?]) — citing this ṛk, the Nirukta-writers say that the word *rajāṃsi* has the meaning "worlds". In the 10th adhyāya, 44th [?] section of the Nirukta, for

> आब्जा मुक्थ्यैरहिं गृणीषे बुध्ने नदीनां रजस्सु षीदन् ।

> *ābjā mukthyairahiṃ gṛṇīṣe budhne nadīnāṃ rajassu ṣīdan |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-16 [?]) — in explaining this ṛk, it is said that *rajassu* means *udakeṣu* ("in the waters"); and in the 12th adhyāya, 6th section [?],

> एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमञ्जते ।

> *etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumañjate |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1 [?]) — in explaining this ṛk, he gives, for *rajasaḥ*, the meaning "of the intermediate region". And:

> त्रीणि भान्ति रजांस्यस्य यत्पदानि तु तेजसा ।

> *trīṇi bhānti rajāṃsyasya yatpadāni tu tejasā |*

— the author of the Bṛhaddevatā, describing the three strides of Viṣṇu over the three worlds, used the word *rajāṃsi* as a synonym of the three worlds. *Rajaḥ*, *rajāṃsi* are in general words that are synonyms of "world". But:

> यन्मा सोमासो ममदन्यदुक्थोभे भयेते रजसी अपारे ।

> *yanmā somāso mamadanyadukthobhe bhayete rajasī apāre |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-42-6 [?]) — in such ṛks this word, which is in the dual, is stated to have the technical meaning "heaven and earth" (*dyāvāpṛthivī*). In some places only, as in:

> अहश्च कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः ।

> *ahaśca kṛṣṇamahararjunaṃ ca vi vartete rajasī vedyābhiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-9-1 [?])

### Printed p. 500  (PDF 520)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 500.)*

— in one or two ṛks such as "*rajasī jagad rañjayantau*" the original meaning of the root is primary. In the ṛk at hand it means the three shining worlds.

***pavayaḥ*** — the word *pavi* is read among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23 [?]) and among the names of the thunderbolt (*vajra*) (Ni. 3-11 [?]); and also "*pavī rathanemir bhavati yad vipunāti bhūmim*" (Ni. 5-5 [?]) — the Nirukta-writers explain that the wheel of the chariot gets the name *pavi* because it digs up the earth, and, citing

> उत पव्या रथानामद्रिं भिन्दन्त्योजसा ।

> *uta pavyā rathānāmadriṃ bhindantyojasā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-53-9 [?]) — they show that in it *pavi* means the felloe of the wheel. The word *pavi* also shows the meaning "arrow-head" (*śalya*):

> पावीरवी तन्यतुरेकपादजो दिवो धर्ता सिन्धुरापः समुद्रियः ।

> *pāvīravī tanyaturekapādajo divo dhartā sindhurāpaḥ samudriyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-13 [?]) — citing this ṛk, (Ni. 12-30 [?]) "*pavī śalyo bhavati yad vipunāti kāyaṃ tadvatvevīram āyudhaṃ tadvān indraḥ pavīravān*" [as read [?]]: because it pierces the body, the arrow-head is called *pavi*; and because he possesses it, Indra has the epithet *pavīravān*, so it is explained; and

> यो जनान् महिषाँ इवातितस्थौ पवीरवान् । उतापवीरवान् युधा ।

> *yo janān mahiṣā~ ivātitasthau pavīravān | utāpavīravān yudhā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-60-2 [?]) — citing this ṛk, he has explained. In the ṛk at hand Sāyaṇa has given, as alternative meanings, "*pavayaḥ — vajrāḥ, rathanemayo vā*" (the thunderbolts, or the felloes of the chariot-wheels).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***yuvoḥ*** — the genitive dual; since the case-ending *os* follows, by the statement "*supāṃ supo bhavanti*" the substitution of the dual genitive occurs; therefore by "*yoci*" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-89 [?]) the *yā* substitution does not occur; by "*śeṣe lopaḥ*" elision of the *ṭi*; by the accent of cessation (*nivṛtti-svara*) the case-ending is *udātta*.
- ***suyamāsaḥ*** — by "*ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119 [?]) the hind-member takes the *ādyudātta* accent; with *jas* following, by "*ājjaser asuk*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50 [?]) the augment *asuk*.
- ***dīyat*** — root *dīya gatau* (a Vedic root); *leṭ*, third person singular; by "*itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97 [?]) elision of the *i*; by "*leṭo 'ḍāṭau*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 [?]) the augment *aṭ*; because of *yad*-connection no *nighāta*; the root accent remains. Yāska has read *dīyati*, *takati* among the roots of motion.

### Printed p. 501  (PDF 521)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 501.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, continued)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***hiraṇyayāḥ*** — by "*ṛtvyāvāstvyāvāstvamādhvīhiraṇyayāni chandasi*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-175 [?]) the elision of *m* occurs, and the form is irregularly derived. By the suffix accent the *a* is *udātta*; when it is combined as a single substitute with a preceding *anudātta*, by "*ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ*" it is *udātta*.
- ***pruṣāyan*** — root *pruṣa pluṣa snehanasecanapūraṇeṣu*, *kryādi* class; *leṭ*, third person plural, *anta* in place of the ending; by "*itaś ca lopaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97 [?]) elision of the final *i*; by "*chandasi śāyajapi*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-84 [?]) *śāyac* by *vyatyaya* in place of the *śnā* *vikaraṇa*; since it stands in an *atiṅanta* word, the *nighāta* accent occurs.
- ***madhvaḥ*** — when the *guṇa* and other changes in *jas* and the following cases do not occur, by the statement "*jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam*" the *yaṇ* substitution; the genitive is in the sense of the object.
- ***pibantā*** — root *pā pāne*; *śatṛ* in place of *laṭ*; *śap* as *vikaraṇa*; by "*pāghrādhmā…*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78 [?]) *piba* substituted; the *lasārvadhātuka* being *anudātta*, the root accent remains.
- ***sacethe*** — root *saca samavāye*; *laṭ*, third person dual; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent. ‖ 1 ‖

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 2**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> युवमत्यस्याव नक्षथो यद्विपत्मनो नर्यस्य प्रयज्योः ।
> स्वसा यद्वां विश्वगूर्ती भराति वाजायेट्टे मधुपाविषे च ॥ २ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> युवम् । अत्यस्य । अव । नक्षथः । यत् । विऽपत्मनः । नर्यस्य । प्रऽयज्योः ।
> स्वसा । यत् । वाम् । विश्वऽगूर्ती इति विश्वऽगूर्ती । भराति । वाजाय । ईट्टे । मधुऽपौ । इषे । च ॥ २ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां यदेत्यस्यातनशीलस्य [?] सततसञ्चारिणो विपत्मनो विविधगमनस्य विचित्रगमनस्य वा नर्यस्य मनुष्याणां हितस्य प्रयज्योः प्रकर्षेण

> *he aśvinau yuvaṃ yuvāṃ yadetyasyātanaśīlasya [?] satatasañcāriṇo vipatmano vividhagamanasya vicitragamanasya vā naryasya manuṣyāṇāṃ hitasya prayajyoḥ prakarṣeṇa*

### Printed p. 502  (PDF 522)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 502.)*

> पूज्यस्य ॥ एतानि कर्मणि षष्ठ्यन्तानि ॥ उक्तरूपं रथमववासत्त्तुदुदयोत्त्रोर्वं [?] नक्षथः व्याप्नुथो देवयजनं गन्तुम् । किंच यद्यदा हे विश्वगूर्ती सर्वस्तुत्यौ सर्वदोद्गूर्णौ वा वां युवयोः स्वसा स्वसृस्थानीया स्वयंसारिणी वोषा [?] भराति पोषयते त्वदागमनाय प्रभातं करोति । यदा हे मधुपौ मधुरस्य सोमरसस्य पातारौ युवां यजमानो वाजाय बलाय गमनाय वेषे [?] प्रभूतान्नायेट्टे स्तौति । तदा रथं प्राप्नुथ इत्यर्थः ॥ [as read; the first sentence on this page is doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* The Aśvins set out in their swift, much-worshipped chariot when their sister Dawn rises and the sacrificer praises them for strength and food.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he* **Aśvinau**) — O Aśvins; **yuvam** — you two; **yat** — when; **atyasya** — constantly moving; **vipatmanaḥ** — of varied (wonderful) motion; **naryasya** — beneficial to men; **prayajyoḥ** — especially to be honoured (your chariot); **ava nakṣathaḥ** — you set out downward (to go to the sacrificial hall); (**kiṃ ca** — and) **yat** — when; (*he*) **viśvagūrtī** — O all-praised (ever eager) Aśvins; **vām** — your; **svasā** — the sister-like (going by her own power) Dawn-goddess; **bharāti** — nourishes (you) [or rouses (you) for coming]; (**tadā** — then) (*he*) **madhupau** — O drinkers of the Soma juice; **vām** — you two; **vājāya** — for strength or for going; **iṣe ca** — and for abundant food; **īṭṭe** — (the sacrificer) praises.

**Bhāvārtha**

O all-praised Aśvins, drinkers of the Soma! When your chariot, ever moving, of wonderful motion, beneficial to men and highly worthy of honour, sets out for the sacrificial hall, as your sister-like goddess Dawn rises at your coming; then the sacrificer praises you, praying "grant strength and food".

**Printed English**

> Direct downwards (the course) of your (car) swift moving, variously going, friendly to man, and to be especially venerated, when, all adorable, your sister (dawn) prepares (for your approach), and (the institutor of the ceremony) worships you, drinkers of the Soma juice, for the sake (of obtaining) strength and food.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk both the nature of the chariot of the deities Aśvins and the relation between them and the deity Uṣas (Dawn) are described.

### Printed p. 503  (PDF 523)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 503.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

***atyasya — atanaśīlasya, satatasaṃcāriṇaḥ*** — "of one that moves constantly, that ranges without break": i.e. having the nature of moving always without a break. This word is an epithet of the chariot and shows the nature of the chariot. In general it is used as an epithet of horses and of the Āditya, who always move.

> एष प्र पूर्वीरव तस्य चम्रिषोऽत्यो न योषामुदयंस्त भुर्वणिः ।
> दक्षं महे पाययते हिरण्ययं रथमावृत्या हरियोगमृभ्वसम् ॥

> *eṣa pra pūrvīrava tasya camriṣo 'tyo na yoṣāmudayaṃsta bhurvaṇiḥ |*
> *dakṣaṃ mahe pāyayate hiraṇyayaṃ rathamāvṛtyā hariyogamṛbhvasam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-56-1 [?]) — in this ṛk *atyaḥ* is said of the horse; and

> अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते पृथिव्यामत्यो न यंसद्यक्षभृद्विचेताः ।
> मृगाणां न हेतयो यन्ति चेमा बृहस्पतेरहिमायाँ अभि द्यून् ॥

> *asya śloko divīyate pṛthivyāmatyo na yaṃsadyakṣabhṛdvicetāḥ |*
> *mṛgāṇāṃ na hetayo yanti cemā bṛhaspaterahimāyā~ abhi dyūn ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-190-4 [?]) — in this the word is used so as to mean *atanaśīlaḥ ādityaḥ* ("the Āditya, who goes always"). In the ṛk at hand it is an epithet of the chariot.

***viśvagūrtī*** — *gūrī* (*gur*), from the root meaning "to exert" (*udyamane*), the word *gūrti* is formed. The word *gūrti* means merely exertion, effort, or action; and this word's usage everywhere shows that in that effort there is both faith (*śraddhā*) and resolve (*saṅkalpa*). For example:

> यूपव्रस्का उत ये यूपवाहाश्चषालं ये अश्वयूपाय तक्षति ।
> ये चार्वते पचनं सम्भरन्त्युतो तेषामभिगूर्तिर्न इन्वतु ॥

> *yūpavraskā uta ye yūpavāhāścaṣālaṃ ye aśvayūpāya takṣati |*
> *ye cārvate pacanaṃ sambharantyuto teṣāmabhigūrtirna invatu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-6 [?]) — here Sāyaṇa explains it as "resolve joined with faith". In the same way, for words such as *svagūrti*, *rādhogūrti*, *arigūrti*, and for words like *gūrtamanāḥ*, *gūrtaśravāḥ*, *gūrtavasuḥ*, the meanings must be learnt as the context suggests. The Nirukta-writers, on the word *svagūrta*:

> समस्मिन्नञ्जायमान आसते ग्ना उतेमवर्धन्नद्यः स्वगूर्ताः ।
> महे यत्त्वा पुरूरवो रणायावर्धयन् दस्युहत्याय देवाः ॥

> *samasminnañjāyamāna āsate gnā utemavardhannadyaḥ svagūrtāḥ |*
> *mahe yattvā purūravo raṇāyāvardhayan dasyuhatyāya devāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-7 [?]) — citing this ṛk, they explain *svagūrtāḥ* there as *svayaṃgāminyaḥ* ("going of themselves"). Here the word *gūrta* has no sense such as "faith" or "resolve"; it is evident that it has only the sense of "going" (*gamana*). In the same way …

### Printed p. 504  (PDF 524)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 504.)*

> असद्यथा नो वरुणः सुकीर्तिरिषश्च पर्षदरिगूर्तः सूरिः ।

> *asadyathā no varuṇaḥ sukīrtiriṣaśca parṣadarigūrtaḥ sūriḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-186-3 [?]) — here too Sāyaṇa explains it, saying only "*śatruhananāya udyuktaḥ*" ("intent on slaying the enemy"), showing merely the sense of exertion. But in words such as *gūrtaśravāḥ*, *gūrtamavāḥ* the word *gūrta* has the sense "praiseworthy". For example:

> स प्राधतो नहुषो दंसुजूतः शर्धस्तरो नरां गूर्तश्रवाः ।

> *sa prādhato nahuṣo daṃsujūtaḥ śardhastaro narāṃ gūrtaśravāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-132-10 [?]) — in this, for the word *gūrtaśravāḥ* the meaning "of praiseworthy or manifest lustre (*udgūrṇadīptiḥ*), or of famous food (*prakhyātānnaḥ*), or of praiseworthy food" is given; and for the word *gūrtamanāḥ* in the ṛk 6-63-4 [?] the meaning "*prakarṣeṇa udyatamanāḥ*" is given. Thus, since for the word *gūrta* a meaning in keeping with the context has to be given, in the ṛk at hand the word *viśvagūrtī* is an epithet of the deities Aśvins, with the sense *sarvastutyau* ("praised by all").

***svasā bharāti*** — the word *svasṛ* here means "Uṣas" (Dawn). The relation of the Aśvin deities to Uṣas, and the part the goddess Uṣas plays in the sacrifice — her manifesting herself as the praiseworthy time — are shown here.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***nakṣathaḥ*** — root *ṇakṣ gatau*; by "*ṇo naḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-65 [?]) the initial *ṇ* becomes *n*; *laṭ*, second person dual; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***vipatmanaḥ*** — root *patḷ gatau*; the *Uṇādi* suffix *manin*; *vividhāḥ patmānaḥ yasya tasya* (one who has varied goings); in the *bahuvrīhi*, by "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*" the fore-member keeps its natural accent.
- ***naryasya*** — *narāya hitam tasya*; by "*chandasi ca*" (Pā. Sū. 5-1-67 [?]) the suffix *yat*; by "*yasyeti ca*" elision of *a*; by "*yato 'nāvaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-213 [?]) the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***viśvagūrtī*** — *viśvā gūrtiḥ yayos tau*; by "*āmantritasya ca*" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19 [?]) the *nighāta* accent occurs.
- ***bharāti*** — root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*; *leṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; by "*leṭo 'ḍāṭau*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 [?]) the augment *aṭ*; *śap* as cause, *guṇa* for the root; *raparatva* … [the passage continues on the next page.]

---

### Printed p. 505  (PDF 525)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 505.)*

… no *nighāta* accent occurs, because of *yad*-connection; *śap* and *tip* being *anudātta*, the root accent remains.

- ***īṭṭe*** — root *īḍa stutau*; *laṭ*, third person singular; by *vyatyaya* the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***iṣe*** — by "*sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 [?]) the case-ending takes the *udātta* accent. ‖ 2 ‖

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 3**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> युवं पयो उस्रियायामधत्तं पक्वमामायामव पूर्व्यं गोः ।
> अन्तर्यद्वनिनो वामृतस्पू [?] ह्वारो न शुचिर्यजते हविष्मान् ॥ ३ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> युवम् । पयः । उस्रियायाम् । अधत्तम् । पक्वम् । आमायाम् । अव । पूर्व्यम् । गोः ।
> अन्तः । यत् । वनिनः । वाम् । ऋतस्पू [?] इति ऋतस्पू [?] । ह्वारः । न । शुचिः । यजते । हविष्मान् ॥ ३ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ युवं युवामुस्रियायां गोनाम्नैतत् । भोगोत्राविण्यां [?] गवि पयोऽधत्तम् । आधारयतम् । स्थापितवन्तौ । तथामायामपक्वायां पक्वं परिपक्वं भोगयोग्यं गोसम्बन्धि दुग्धं पूर्व्यं पूर्वभवं तत्रैवोत्पन्नमुवावात्स्वादधारयतम् [?] । गवि क्षीरमुत्पाद्य पुनर्भोगाय पृथक्कृतवन्तावित्यर्थः । यद्यस्मात् हे ऋतस्पू [?] सत्यस्वरूपौ यज्ञीयहविर्भक्षयितारौ वा हे अश्विनौ वां वनिन उदकवत उदकोपलक्षितहविष्मतो यज्ञस्यान्तर्मध्ये हविष्मान् प्रदेययुक्तहविषा तद्वान् शुचिः शुद्धो यजमानो यजते पूजयति युवां तस्मादेवममुं [?] कुरुतम् । यद्वा । यद्यैवं यजमानः करोति तदेत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वनिनो वनसम्बन्धिवृक्षसमूहस्यान्तर्मध्ये ह्वारो न चोर इव । स यथा जागरूको वर्तते तथा यजमानोऽपीत्यर्थः ॥ [as read; several words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* The Aśvins put milk in the cow and ripe milk in her unripe udder; the pure sacrificer, alert like a thief in a thicket, worships them with oblations.

### Printed p. 506  (PDF 526)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 506.)*

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he* **ṛtaspū** [?]) — O Aśvins of the nature of truth (who consume the oblations of the sacrifice); **yat** — because; **haviṣmān** — the one possessed of the oblation to be given; **śuciḥ** — pure; the sacrificer; **vām** — you two; **vaninaḥ** — of the sacrifice with oblations; **antaḥ** — in the middle; [or **vaninaḥ** — of the wood-related group of trees; **antaḥ** — in the midst of]; **hvāraḥ na** — like a thief how alert (watchful); **yajate** — he worships; (**tat** — therefore); (*he* **Aśvinau**) **yuvam** — you two; **usriyāyām** — in the cow; **payaḥ** — milk; **adhattam** — placed; (and) **goḥ** — of the cow; **āmāyām** — in the unripe (udder); **pūrvyam** — first-formed; **pakvam** — ripe milk; **ava (adhattam)** — established.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Aśvins, of truth-nature, devourers of the oblations of the sacrifice! The sacrificer, pure and with oblations, worships you in the sacrifice, alert like a thief in a forest; therefore you have placed in the cows abundant milk, and in their udders ripe milk.

**Printed English**

> You have restored milk to the cow: you have (brought) down the prior mature (secretion) into the unripe (or barren) udder of the cow: the devont [sic] offerer of the oblation worships you, whose froms [sic] are truth, (as vigilant in the midst of the ceremony), as a thief (in the midst) of a thicket,

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***ṛtaspū*** [?] — that the word *ṛta* is used in the senses "truth", "sacrifice" and so on, and how *ṛta* reflects the universal rule, has been explained earlier in this same portion, in the special topics of Ṛk 1-179-2. In the ṛk at hand the deities Aśvins are described by the word *ṛtaspū* [?] as being of the nature of truth. Since they pervade the whole universe in the forms of heaven and earth, of the sun, moon and stars, and of day and night, the gist is that these two are all the forms of the world, of the nature of truth.

***vaninaḥ*** — two or three kinds of meaning are shown to be possible for this word. First: "*vaninaḥ udakavantaḥ udakopalakṣitahaviṣmato yajñasya*" ("of the sacrifice in which there is water — the sacrifice that has oblations, marked by water"); and second: "*vanasaṃbandhivṛkṣasamūhasya*" ("of the group of trees belonging to the forest").

---

### Printed p. 507  (PDF 527)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 507.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — the word *vana* has been read among the names of *raśmi* ("ray") (Ni. 1-15 [?]) and among the names of "water" (Ni. 1-12 [?]). Besides these meanings, the word is used in many other senses in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. From the root *van*, giving the sense of eager desire ("wishing to obtain"), or from the root *vas*, "to beg", or *van*, giving the sense "to ask, to pray", the forms *vanāni*, *vaninaḥ*, *vanāmahe*, *vananta* and the like are formed, as nouns and as verbs; so, to know the changes of meaning, some examples may be seen. When it is a noun it has the meanings "venerable" (*pūjya*), "water" (*udaka*), "tree of the forest", "flower and fruit"; when it is a verb, the meanings "to kill" (*kollu*), "to give" (*koḍu*), "to serve with devotion" (*bhaktiyiṃde sēvisu*) occur. The occurrences, with examples, have been explained at length earlier in this same portion in the special topics of Ṛk 1-168-3 [?]. In the ṛk at hand it means either "of the sacrifice marked by water" or "of the group of trees".

***hvāraḥ*** — *hvāra* is explained as "thief". The meanings "robber" (*taskara*) and "cheat" (*vañcaka*) came to this word by tradition; the original meaning of this word is *kuṭila*, *vakra* ("crooked", "curved").

> क्रत्वा हि द्रोणे अज्यसेऽग्ने वाजी न कृत्व्यः ।
> परिज्मेव स्वधा गयोऽत्यो न ह्वार्यः शिशुः ॥

> *kratvā hi droṇe ajyase 'gne vājī na kṛtvyaḥ |*
> *parijmeva svadhā gayo 'tyo na hvāryaḥ śiśuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-2-8 [?]) — in this ṛk the word *hvāryaḥ* shows a quality of the horse. Here it is an epithet of Agni; the common property of the horse and of Agni is suggested by this word. Just as a horse goes with a crooked movement, so also the flame of Agni spreads with crooked movement. Likewise:

> उत स्म दुर्गृभीयसे पुत्रो न ह्वार्याणाम् ।
> पुरू यो दग्धासि वनाग्ने पशुर्न यवसे ॥

> *uta sma durgṛbhīyase putro na hvāryāṇām |*
> *purū yo dagdhāsi vanāgne paśurna yavase ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-6-4 [?]) — in this ṛk the word *hvāryāṇām* means *kuṭilaṃ gacchatāṃ sarpāṇām* ("of the serpents that go crookedly"); it shows the crooked movement of serpents which go in a crooked way. Thus, with its original sense, this word is also used as a synonym of thieves and the like. Straightness is the disposition of truth; and for a cheat the quality is the lack of straight dealing; so *hvāraḥ* means "thief". And:

> वि यदस्थाद्यजतो वातचोदितो ह्वारो न वक्वा जरणा अनाकृतः ।
> तस्य पत्मन्दक्षुषः कृष्णजंहसः शुचिजन्मनो रज आ व्यध्वनः ॥

> *vi yadasthādyajato vātacodito hvāro na vakvā jaraṇā anākṛtaḥ |*
> *tasya patmandakṣuṣaḥ kṛṣṇajaṃhasaḥ śucijanmano raja ā vyadhvanaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-140-7 [?]) —

### Printed p. 508  (PDF 528)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 508.)*

— in such ṛks the meaning is *haraṭe-malla* ("a rambling talker, a wrestler of talk" [as read [?]]). The talker, since he goes beyond bounds, has no straight and fixed direction; therefore there is crookedness in him too; hence the epithet *vakvā hvāraḥ* ("crooked thief"). In the ṛk at hand the "thief" is the sense; but here one more point should be noted. Used in general as an epithet of a thief, this word shows his deceitfulness; but in the ṛk at hand it shows a general quality common to the sacrificer and to the *hvāra*; namely, as the thief carries out his theft with alertness, so the sacrificer also carries out the sacrifice: the common property of both is attention and alertness.

***usriyāyām*** — in the Ṛgveda this word is read among the names of "cow" (*go*): *usrā*, *usriyā*, and so on (Ni. 3-8 [?]). "*usriyeti gonāma | usrāviṇaḥ asyāṃ bhogāḥ*" [as read [?]] — because the milk, the means of comfort, flows out, the name *usriyā* arose; so the Nirukta-writers, citing

> उत वां विक्षु मद्यास्वन्धो गाव आपेश्च पीपयन्त देवीः ।
> उतो नो अस्य पूर्व्यः पतिर्दन्वीतं पाहि पयस उस्रियायाः ॥

> *uta vāṃ vikṣu madyāsvandho gāva āpeśca pīpayanta devīḥ |*
> *uto no asya pūrvyaḥ patirdanvītaṃ pāhi payasa usriyāyāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-153-4 [?]) — have explained it as above (Ni. 4-19 [?]).

In the ṛk at hand it is intimated that the Aśvin deities placed milk in the unripe udder of the cow; this context is intimated in many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. The story is told in some places in this way:

> शयुर्नाम राजर्षिः । सोऽश्विनौ परिचर्यया तुष्टावुवाच । मम गौर्धेनुर्निवृत्तप्रसवा वृद्धा च । तां मे धेनुं कुरुतमिति । तामस्मै अश्विनौ धेनुं चक्रतुरित्यैतिहासमाचक्षते ॥

> *śayurnāma rājarṣiḥ | so 'śvinau paricaryayā tuṣṭāvuvāca | mama gaurdhenurnivṛttaprasavā vṛddhā ca | tāṃ me dhenuṃ kurutamiti | tāmasmai aśvinau dhenuṃ cakraturityaitihāsamācakṣate ‖*

— a royal sage named Śayu pleased the Aśvins by his service. Then he said to them, "My cow is past bearing and old; make her a milch cow for me." The Aśvins made her a milch cow for him: so the tradition tells. In this connection many ṛks intimate the story. For example:

> अथेनुं दस्रा स्तर्यं विषक्तामपिन्वतं शयवे अश्विना गाम् ।

> *athenuṃ dasrā staryaṃ viṣaktāmapinvataṃ śayave aśvinā gām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-20 [?])

---

### Printed p. 509  (PDF 529)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 509.)*

> युवं धेनुं शयवे नाधिताया अपिन्वतमश्विना पूर्व्याय ।

> *yuvaṃ dhenuṃ śayave nādhitāyā apinvatamaśvinā pūrvyāya |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-8 [?])

> दशस्यन्ता शयवे पिप्यथुर्गामिति च्यवाना सुमतिं भुरण्यू ।

> *daśasyantā śayave pipyathurgāmiti cyavānā sumatiṃ bhuraṇyū |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-62-7 [?])

> ता वर्तिर्यातं जयुषा वि पर्वतमपिन्वतं शयवे धेनुमश्विना ।

> *tā vartiryātaṃ jayuṣā vi parvatamapinvataṃ śayave dhenumaśvinā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-13 [?]) — in these and many other ṛks the story is told of how the Aśvin deities changed Śayu's barren cow into a milch cow. In the ṛk at hand the same matter is shown; but the name Śayu is not given here. In some places it is said that they made the old cow able to bear again and filled her with milk; in others that they changed the barren cow into a milch cow and filled her with milk.

***āmāyām*** — "*aparipakvāyām*" — "in the unripe": it means "not matured". Here it is an adjective of the cow's udder: in the udder not yet filled, or it is used of a barren cow. It is used according to the context. That the Aśvin deities fill such an unripe udder with milk is stated, and this skill is described also of other deities. For example:

> इमौ देवौ जायमानौ जुषन्तेमौ तमांसि गूहतामजुष्टा ।
> आभ्यामिन्द्रः पक्वमामास्वन्तः सोमापूषभ्यां जनदुस्रियासु ॥

> *imau devau jāyamānau juṣantemau tamāṃsi gūhatāmajuṣṭā |*
> *ābhyāmindraḥ pakvamāmāsvantaḥ somāpūṣabhyāṃ janadusriyāsu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-40-2 [?]) — it is said that the deities Soma and Pūṣan filled with milk the udder of a young cow and changed it into the form of a milch cow. For the word *āma* the general meaning is "unripe"; though this can be used as an epithet in any context, in the Ṛk-saṃhitā the word, when it describes a cow's udder, is used only as an epithet, namely "unripe, not ripened with milk", and so it suggests the sense "an udder with no milk". For example: (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-14; 4-3-9; 2-35-6; 2-40-2; 6-77-4 [?]; 8-77-2 [?] and others).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***usriyāyām*** — root *vasa nivāse*; *vasanti iti usriyāḥ*. By the statement "*yannu padārthaviśeṣasamutthaṃ pratyayataḥ prakṛteś ca tadūhyam*" (as read [?]) it must be inferred, from the function, that the suffix *riyak* has come after the root *vas* in the agent. Since it has *k* as a marker, *saṃprasāraṇa* occurs in the root; by the suffix accent the *i* is *udātta*.

### Printed p. 510  (PDF 530)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 510.)*

- ***adhattam*** — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; it contains the sense of the causative; *laṅ*, second person dual; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***pūrvyam*** — *pūrve bhavam*; by "*bhave chandasi*" (Pā. Sū. 4-4-110 [?]) the suffix *yat*; by "*yato 'nāvaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-213 [?]) the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***hvāraḥ*** — root *hvṛ kauṭilye*; after the causative stem the suffix *ac*; by "*aco ñṇiti*" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-115 [?]) *vṛddhi* for the *ṛ*; by "*ṇer aniṭi*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-51 [?]) elision of *ṇic*; by "*citaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 [?]) the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***yajate*** — by "*yad vṛttān nityam*" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 [?]) the *nighāta* accent is prohibited, so the root accent remains. ‖ 3 ‖

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 4**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> युवं ह घर्मं मधुमन्तमत्रयेऽपो न क्षोदोऽवृणीतमेषे ।
> तद्वां नरावश्विना पश्वइष्टी रथ्येव चक्रा प्रति यन्ति मध्वः ॥ ४ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> युवम् । ह । घर्मम् । मधुऽमन्तम् । अत्रये । अपः । न । क्षोदः । अवृणीतम् । एषे ।
> तत् । वाम् । नरौ । अश्विना । पश्वऽइष्टौ । रथ्याऽइव । चक्रा । प्रति । यन्ति । मध्वः ॥ ४ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अत्रेतिहासमाहुः । प्रवर्ग्येण प्रचरन्तमत्रिं राक्षसास्तप्ते घर्मेऽपातयन् । स च तप्यमानोऽश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तौ चः [?] स्तुत्या हृष्टमनसावरक्षतामिति । अपरेऽग्नौ क्षिप्तमसालयतामित्याहुरिति [?] । हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां मधुमन्तं पयोधृतरूपाभ्यां मधुभ्यां तद्वन्तं घर्मं दीप्तं प्रवर्ग्यमेषे सौख्यमिच्छतेऽत्रये … [the bhāṣya continues on the next page]

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (continued)**

> एतन्नो [?] महर्षये क्षोदः क्षोदांसि क्षोद्यमानान्यपो नोदकानीवावृणीतम् । आवारयतम् । औष्ण्यं शैत्येन सुखं कृतवन्तौ । तप्तघर्मसकाशाद् भ्रक्षितवानित्यर्थः [?] । यद्वा । अत्रये क्षोदः । उदकनामैतत् । तेषां शैत्यं लक्ष्यते । अपः क्षोदो न । अपः इति षष्ठ्यर्थे द्वितीया । उदकानां शैत्यं यथा भवति तद्वत् । पक्षान्तरे तु घर्मं दीप्तमग्निं मधुमन्तं कृत्वावृणीतम् । सुखयतमित्यर्थः । तथा च मन्त्रान्तरम् । तप्तं घर्म्यमोम्यावन्तमत्रये [?] । ऋ. १-११९-६ [?] । इति । तत्र तस्मात् यस्मादेवं तस्मात् हे नरौ नेतारौ नराकारौ वाश्विनाश्विनौ वां युवाभ्यां पश्वइष्टिः । पशुरित्यग्नेर्नाम । अग्निः पशुरासीदित्यादि श्रुतेः । तै. सं. ५-२-१ [?] । यद्वा । पशुप्रियत्वात् पशुः इत्यादि । तस्मादग्नेरिष्टिर्भवति । अग्नौ योगः सर्वोऽपि युष्मदर्थं प्रवर्तते ... पशुसाध्यो योगो युवाभ्यां प्रवर्तत इति शेषः । आश्विनं धूम्रललाममालभेत यो दुर्ब्राह्मणः सोमं पिपासेत् । तै. सं. २-१-१० [?] । इत्यादिना श्रुतेः पशुर्विहितः । तथा मध्वः मधुसदृशाः सोमरसा अपि युवाभ्यां प्रति यन्ति । अभिगच्छन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । रथ्येव चक्रा रथसम्बन्धिनी चक्रा चक्राणीव । तानि यथा प्रवणदेशमभिगच्छन्ति तद्वत् ॥ [as read; several phrases doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Atri, thrown into the heated *gharma* fire, was cooled by the Aśvins as if by water; therefore the animal sacrifice to Agni (the *paśu* being Agni's name) is offered for them, and the honey-like Soma juices flow to them like wheels down a slope.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he* **Aśvinau**) — O Aśvins; **yuvam** — you two; **madhumantam** — endowed with honey in the form of milk and ghee; **gharmam** — the blazing fire; **eṣe** — (to him who, thrown into the fire, longs for comfort) seeking; **atraye** — to Atri; **kṣodaḥ** — the agitated (fire); **apaḥ na** — like water (cool); **avṛṇītam ha** — you made (checked the heat of the fire), made it cool; **tat** — therefore; **narau** — leaders, or of human form; (*he* **Aśvinau**); **vām** — for you two; **paśvaiṣṭiḥ** — in the fire, the sacrifice or animal sacrifice (has been set in motion); (**tathā** — likewise) **madhvaḥ** — honey-like (Soma juices too); (**vām** — to you two); **rathyā** — belonging to the chariot; **cakrā iva** — like wheels (reaching the desired place); **prati yanti** — go toward.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Aśvins! To Atri, who, thrown into the fire, was seeking release, you made the blazing fire cool, like water in motion, by means of honey in the form of milk and ghee; this is well known. Therefore, O leaders of the sacrifice, for you this animal sacrifice is set in motion, and this honey-like Soma is offered.

### Printed p. 512  (PDF 532)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 512.)*

**Printed English**

> You rendered the heat as soothing as sweet butter to Atri; wishing (for relief), and invested it with coolness, like water: therefore, for you, Ashwins, leaders (of rites), the fire-offering (is made); to you the Soma juices run like chariot wheels (down a declivity).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

To understand the ṛk at hand fully, one must know the relation among the deities Agni, Atri and the Aśvins, and know what place these have in the *gharma*, which is of the nature of the *pravargya* rite.

***madhumantaṃ gharmaṃ atraye …… avṛṇītaṃ ha*** — for this sentence Sāyaṇa has shown two kinds of construction (*anvaya*). These constructions fit the meanings that are to be given to the words *atri* and *gharma*.

1. First, Sāyaṇa has indicated this story as the background, saying that the Aśvin deities helped the great sage Atri:

> अत्रेतिहासमाहुः । प्रवर्ग्येण प्रचरन्तमत्रिं राक्षसास्तप्ते घर्मेऽपातयन् । स च तप्यमानोऽश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तौ च स्तुत्या हृष्टमनसावरक्षतामिति ॥

> *atretihāsamāhuḥ | pravargyeṇa pracarantamatriṃ rākṣasāstapte gharme 'pātayan | sa ca tapyamāno 'śvinau tuṣṭāva | tau ca stutyā hṛṣṭamanasāvarakṣatāmiti ‖*

— Atri, who was engaged in worship with the *pravargya* rite, was thrown by the Rākṣasas into the blazing fire. Then Atri prayed to the Aśvin deities for protection; pleased with him, they protected him: so the story goes.

2. Second, as in the ṛk at hand, "*madhumantaṃ gharmaṃ atraye avṛṇītam*", as it says in Ṛk 1-119-6 [?], "*taptaṃ gharmam omyāvantam atraye*" [?]. In that context Sāyaṇa explained the purport of the ṛk as shown. But here, citing Yāska's view also: "*yāskapakṣe tu atraye haviṣām akte [?] 'gnaye haviruptyarthaṃ sūryakiraṇasaṃtaptaṃ gharmaṃ naidāghaṃ ahaḥ omyāvantaṃ tṛptihetuvṛṣṭyudakopetaṃ kṛtavantau iti yojyam*" [as read [?]] — "In Yāska's view, *atri* is the fire that eats the oblations; for giving oblations to Agni, for the *gharma* blazing in the heat of the sun's rays, they made the summer day provided with satisfying rain-water": so he explains. In explaining the ṛk at hand also, Sāyaṇa, citing the very ṛk 1-119-6 [?], says "*pakṣāntare tu gharmaṃ dīptam agniṃ madhumantaṃ kṛtvā avṛṇītam* … *tathā ca mantrāntaram*" — "*taptaṃ gharma-* … [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 513  (PDF 533)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 513; signature mark "XIII 33".)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — "… *omyāvantam atraye* …" — so he explains. Therefore it appears that two meanings can be given for the word *atri*: one in the sense of the ṛṣi Atri, the other in the sense of Agni. Or, since the ṛṣi Atri is a part of Agni, identity (*tādātmya*) between the two can also be stated. In some places Atri is known as a son of Agni; in other places, as Agni in form. The story of the origin of the ṛṣi Atri is told thus in the Bṛhaddevatā:

> त्रिसांवत्सरिकं सत्रं प्रजाकामः प्रजापतिः । आहरत्सहितः साध्यैर्विश्वैर्देवैः सहेति च ॥
> तत्र वाग्दीप्तणीयोयां [?] आजगाम शरीरिणी । तां दृष्ट्वा युगपत्तत्र कस्याथ वरुणस्य च ॥
> शुक्रं चस्कन्द तद्वायुरग्नौ प्रास्यद्यदभ्यया [?] । ततोऽर्चिर्भ्यो भृगुर्जज्ञे अङ्गारेभ्योऽङ्गिरा ऋषिः ॥
> प्रजापतिं सुतौ दृष्ट्वा दृष्ट्वा वागभ्यभाषत । आभ्यामृषिस्तृतीयोऽपि भवेदत्रैव मे सुतः ॥
> प्रजापतिस्तथेत्युक्तः प्रत्यभाषत भारतीम् । ऋषिरत्रिस्ततो जज्ञे सूर्यानलसमद्युतिः ॥

> *trisāṃvatsarikaṃ satraṃ prajākāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ | āharatsahitaḥ sādhyairviśvairdevaiḥ saheti ca ‖*
> *tatra vāgdīptaṇīyoyāṃ [?] ājagāma śarīriṇī | tāṃ dṛṣṭvā yugapattatra kasyātha varuṇasya ca ‖*
> *śukraṃ caskanda tadvāyuragnau prāsyadyadabhyayā [?] | tato 'rcirbhyo bhṛgurjajñe aṅgārebhyo 'ṅgirā ṛṣiḥ ‖*
> *prajāpatiṃ sutau dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā vāgabhyabhāṣata | ābhyāmṛṣistṛtīyo 'pi bhavedatraiva me sutaḥ ‖*
> *prajāpatistathetyuktaḥ pratyabhāṣata bhāratīm | ṛṣiratristato jajñe sūryānalasamadyutiḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 5-97 to 101 [?]; as read, several words doubtful [?]) — Prajāpati, wishing for progeny, performed, together with the Sādhyas and the Viśvedevas, a sacrificial session (*sattra*) lasting three years: so it is well known. At that time the goddess Vāc came in bodily form to the *sattra*. On seeing her, the seed of Prajāpati and of Varuṇa fell at once; Vāyu cast it into the fire. Then from the flames Bhṛgu and from the embers Aṅgiras were born. The goddess Vāc, seeing these two sons, asked for another son besides these two. When Prajāpati had consented, the ṛṣi Atri, equal in brilliance to the sun and fire, was born from that seed which had been cast into the fire.

Moreover, when Yāska explains the word *atri* in the sense of Agni, he says *haviṣām attā* ("the eater of oblations"), i.e. he states that Agni has the name *atri* because he eats the oblations. That Agni eats not only oblations but everything is described in the Ṛk-saṃhitā itself. For example:

> यत्ते कृष्णः शकुन आतुतोद पिपीलः सर्प उत वा श्वापदः ।
> अग्निष्टद्विश्वादगदं कृणोतु सोमश्च यो ब्राह्मणाँ आविवेश ॥

> *yatte kṛṣṇaḥ śakuna ātutoda pipīlaḥ sarpa uta vā śvāpadaḥ |*
> *agniṣṭadviśvādagadaṃ kṛṇotu somaśca yo brāhmaṇā~ āviveśa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-16-6 [?]) — in this ṛk Agni is praised as *viśvāt*, "the eater of all". And:

### Printed p. 514  (PDF 534)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 514.)*

> युवानं विश्वपतिं कविं विश्वादं पुरुवेपसम् ।
> अग्निं शुम्भामि मन्मभिः ॥

> *yuvānaṃ viśvapatiṃ kaviṃ viśvādaṃ puruvepasam |*
> *agniṃ śumbhāmi manmabhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-44-26 [?]) — here too Agni is praised with this same epithet. On the strength of these, *atri* may be explained in many places as "Agni", fitting the context.

Besides these epithets, there are many contexts which speak of the identity (*tādātmya*) of both Agni and Atri, and these are suggested in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. For example:

> ऋषिं नरावंहसः पाञ्चजन्यमृबीसादत्रिं मुञ्चथो गणेन ।
> मिनन्ता दस्योरशिवस्य माया अनुपूर्वं वृषणा चोदयन्ता ॥

> *ṛṣiṃ narāvaṃhasaḥ pāñcajanyamṛbīsādatriṃ muñcatho gaṇena |*
> *minantā dasyoraśivasya māyā anupūrvaṃ vṛṣaṇā codayantā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-3 [?]) — in this (a ṛk addressed to the deity Aśvins) Atri has the epithet *pāñcajanya*. Likewise:

> अग्निर्ऋषिः पवमानः पाञ्चजन्यः पुरोहितः । तमीमहे महागयम् ॥

> *agnirṛṣiḥ pavamānaḥ pāñcajanyaḥ purohitaḥ | tamīmahe mahāgayam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-66-20 [?]) — and in many ṛks that follow, the word *pāñcajanya* is an epithet of Agni. Whatever meaning is given to the word *pāñcajanya*, it is a special feature that it is an epithet of both Agni and Atri; it cannot be wrong to say that the epithet suggests the closeness of their mutual relation. And, as in the ṛk at hand, the Aśvins protected Atri who was in the *gharma*; likewise:

> अग्निर्ह त्यं जरतः कर्णमावाग्निरद्भ्यो निरदहज्जरूथम् ।
> अग्निरत्रिं घर्म उरुष्यदन्तरग्निर्नृमेधं प्रजयासृजत्सम् ॥ [as read [?]]

> *agnirha tyaṃ jarataḥ karṇamāvāgniradbhyo niradahajjarūtham |*
> *agniratriṃ gharma uruṣyadantaragnirnṛmedhaṃ prajayāsṛjatsam ‖ [as read [?]]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-3 [?]) — here it is said that Agni protected Atri who was in the *gharma*. The extraordinary divine qualities of Atri are described at great length in the 40th sūkta of the 5th Maṇḍala of the Ṛk-saṃhitā. If only some mantras of that sūkta are examined, the deities who are prayed to here are Sūrya, Indra and Atri:

> यत्त्वा सूर्य स्वर्भानुस्तमसाविध्यदासुरः ।
> अक्षेत्रविद्यथा मुग्धो भुवनान्यदीधयुः ॥
> स्वर्भानोरध यदिन्द्र माया अवो दिवो वर्तमाना अवाहन् ।
> गूळ्हं सूर्यं तमसापव्रतेन तुरीयेण ब्रह्मणाविन्ददत्रिः ॥

> *yattvā sūrya svarbhānustamasāvidhyadāsuraḥ |*
> *akṣetravidyathā mugdho bhuvanānyadīdhayuḥ ‖*
> *svarbhānoradha yadindra māyā avo divo vartamānā avāhan |*
> *gūḷhaṃ sūryaṃ tamasāpavratena turīyeṇa brahmaṇāvindadatriḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-5 to 6 [?]) — as soon as Svarbhānu released the Sun from darkness, all beings were bewildered. Then Indra made the Asura fall below. Atri, with his divine sight, knew the place where the Sun was held covered by darkness: so it is said. And again, …

### Printed p. 515  (PDF 535)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 515.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

> ग्राव्णो [?] ब्रह्मा युयुजानः सपर्यन् कीरिणा देवान्नमसोपशिक्षन् ।
> अत्रिः सूर्यस्य दिवि चक्षुराधात्स्वर्भानोरप माया अधुक्षत् ॥
> यं वै सूर्यं स्वर्भानुस्तमसाविध्यदासुरः ।
> अत्रयस्तमन्वविन्दन्न ह्यन्ये अशक्नुवन् ॥

> *grāvṇo [?] brahmā yuyujānaḥ saparyan kīriṇā devānnamasopaśikṣan |*
> *atriḥ sūryasya divi cakṣurādhātsvarbhānorapa māyā adhukṣat ‖*
> *yaṃ vai sūryaṃ svarbhānustamasāvidhyadāsuraḥ |*
> *atrayastamanvavindanna hyanye aśaknuvan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-8 to 9 [?]) — in this it is said that Atri, intent on the sacrificial rite, by his divine power and by godly power set the vision of the Āditya in the sky and destroyed the power of Svarbhānu. In this same sūkta the Sun shows gratitude to Atri:

> मा मामिमं तव सन्तमत्र इरस्या द्रुग्धो भियसा नि गारीत् ।
> त्वं मित्रो असि सत्यराधास्तौ मोहावतं वरुणश्च राजा ॥

> *mā māmimaṃ tava santamatra irasyā drugdho bhiyasā ni gārīt |*
> *tvaṃ mitro asi satyarādhāstau mohāvataṃ varuṇaśca rājā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-2 [?]) — in this ṛk the Sun asks for Atri's help; and prays, "I am yours; I belong to you. Do not leave me to the Asuras." The description and the prayer in this mantra are like the prayer addressed to Agni, who is hostile to the Asuras. In these contexts, if one examines certain contexts in the fifth Maṇḍala, well known as the "Atri-maṇḍala" (the maṇḍala of Atri), a close relation is shown between Agni and Atri. For example: the author of the second sūkta of the fifth Maṇḍala is well known by the name Kumāra, born in Atri's *gotra*; but:

> कुमारं माता युवतिः समुब्धं गुहा बिभर्ति न ददाति पित्रे ।
> अनीकमस्य न मिनज्जनासः पुरः पश्यन्ति निहितमरतौ ॥

> *kumāraṃ mātā yuvatiḥ samubdhaṃ guhā bibharti na dadāti pitre |*
> *anīkamasya na minajjanāsaḥ puraḥ paśyanti nihitamaratau ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-2-1 [?]) — it is stated in the Sāyaṇa commentary that *kumāram* is an epithet of Agni. And likewise in the cases of *vasuśrut*, *īśa*, *gayu* and others, the portion belonging to Agni can be seen in the matter of the Ātreyas. Showing that the word is formed from the root *ad* ("to eat"), the Upaniṣads too praise Atri:

> वागेवात्रिर्वाचा ह्यन्नमद्यतेऽत्त्रिर्ह वै नामैतद्यदत्रिरिति सर्वस्यात्ता भवति सर्वमस्यान्नं भवति य एवं वेद ॥

> *vāgevātrirvācā hyannamadyate 'ttrirha vai nāmaitadyadatririti sarvasyāttā bhavati sarvamasyānnaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Bṛ. U. 1-2-4 [?]) — from such sentences the description of the word *atri* in the sense of the Supreme Brahman has been given. In this same sense the word *atri* is used in the Ṛk-saṃhitā in many places as an epithet of Agni.

In the ṛk at hand, the first meaning is that the Aśvin deities saved the ṛṣi Atri, who had fallen into the heated fire-pit. Second, they did the service of cooling to the Agni abiding in the *gharma* … [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 516  (PDF 536)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 516.)*

… is the meaning. But here what is *gharma*? One must know what the "service" for Agni there is. Sāyaṇa gave the meaning *pravargya* for the word *gharma*. Are *gharma* and *pravargya* words showing identity, both of one and the same meaning? What is the basis for this in the *śruti* sentences? Now the nature of the *gharma*, or of the *pravargya*, must be examined. And one must know what kind of leadership (*netṛtva*) the Aśvin deities bear in the *pravargya*. In the sentences of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka that are quoted later, in the ṛk 1-180-9 [?], the relation between the *pravargya* and the Aśvin deities is explained in detail; here that matter is stated only briefly.

> ताभ्यामेतमाश्विनमगृह्णन् । तावेतद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रत्यैधतां [?] । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । तेन सशीर्ष्णा यज्ञेन यजमानाः । अवाशिषोऽरुन्धत । अभि सुवर्गं लोकमजयन् ।

> *tābhyāmetamāśvinamagṛhṇan | tāvetadyajñasya śiraḥ pratyaidhatāṃ [?] | yatpravargyaḥ | tena saśīrṣṇā yajñena yajamānāḥ | avāśiṣo 'rundhata | abhi suvargaṃ lokamajayan |*

(Tai. Ā. 5-1-2 [?]) — the deities, having propitiated the divine physicians, the Aśvin deities, prayed: "You are physicians; unite again the *pravargya*, the head of the sacrifice, with the body of the sacrifice, in a three-day session." Then the Aśvins, obtaining for themselves a share in the fruit of the sacrifice, fulfilled the prayer of the deities. Therefore:

> यत्प्रवर्ग्यं प्रवृणक्ति । यज्ञस्यैव तच्छिरः प्रतिदधाति । तेन सशीर्ष्णा यज्ञेन यजमानाः । अवाशिषो रुन्धे । अभि सुवर्गं लोकं जयति । तस्मादेष आश्विनप्रवया इव । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः ॥

> *yatpravargyaṃ pravṛṇakti | yajñasyaiva tacchiraḥ pratidadhāti | tena saśīrṣṇā yajñena yajamānāḥ | avāśiṣo rundhe | abhi suvargaṃ lokaṃ jayati | tasmādeṣa āśvinapravayā iva | yatpravargyaḥ ‖*

(Tai. Ā. 5-1-2 [?]) — thus the greatness of this rite called *pravargya*, which even the deities honoured as foremost, is praised: by performing it, the sacrificer accomplishes his desired aims and obtains the heavenly world. Since both the Aśvin mantras and the Aśvin deities are foremost at the time of this rite, it also has the synonymous name "*āśvinapravayoḥ*" [as read [?]]. Next, the meanings of the words *gharma* and *pravargya* must be known. In the fourth *prapāṭhaka* of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka the order of its performance is told. Explaining in this context, Sāyaṇa has explained the meanings of these words, citing sentences of the fifth *prapāṭhaka*:

> स धनुः प्रतिष्कभ्याभितिष्ठत् । ता उपदीका अब्रुवन्वरं वृणामहै । अथ व इमाꣳ रन्धयाम । यत्र क्व च खनानु [?] । तदपोऽभित्र्यन्ददामेति [?] । तस्मादुपदीका यत्र क्व च खनन्ति । तदपोऽभितृन्दन्ति । वारे वृतꣳ ह्यासाम् । तस्य …

> *sa dhanuḥ pratiṣkabhyābhitiṣṭhat | tā upadīkā abruvanvaraṃ vṛṇāmahai | atha va imām̐ randhayāma | yatra kva ca khanānu [?] | tadapo 'bhitryandadāmeti [?] | tasmādupadīkā yatra kva ca khananti | tadapo 'bhitṛndanti | vāre vṛtam̐ hyāsām | tasya …*

(Tai. Ā. 5-1-[?]; as read, doubtful [?])

### Printed p. 517  (PDF 537)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 517.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

> … ज्यामप्यादन् [?] । तस्य धनुर्विप्रवमाणाꣳ [?] शिर उदवर्तयत् । तद्द्यावापृथिवी अनुप्रावर्तेताम् । यत्प्रवर्तेते । तत्प्रवर्ग्यस्य प्रवर्ग्यत्वम् । यद्घ्रां [?] ळ इत्यपतत् । तद्घर्मस्य घर्मत्वम् ।

> *… jyāmapyādan [?] | tasya dhanurvipravamāṇām̐ [?] śira udavartayat | taddyāvāpṛthivī anuprāvartetām | yatpravartete | tatpravargyasya pravargyatvam | yadghrāṃ [?] ḷa ityapatat | tadgharmasya gharmatvam |*

(Tai. Ā. 5-1-4 to 6 [?]; as read, doubtful [?]) — in this explanation a story-context is hinted at, and afterwards it is shown that names such as *gharma* became well known. As is said in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, the story context is as follows. Indra and the others performed a sacrificial session at the divine sacrificial place called Kurukṣetra. Then, when it had to be decided who among them was the best — he who first reached the end of the sacrifice by austerity, faith and performance of the sacrifice was to be counted best of all — Viṣṇu won that contest. Then Viṣṇu was held to be the best. Pride arose in him, born of such victory; Viṣṇu, full of self-esteem, took his bow, planted its end on the ground, held three arrows in his hand, and sat resting his head on the tip of the bow; among the deities no one dared face him, and all sat around him. Then, to ridicule his pride, the deities approached ants (*vamri*, *kṛmi*) and asked them to cut the bow-string; and the ants cut Viṣṇu's bow-string (in another reading, "Indra, in the form of an ant, cut the bow-string"; also a variant "*tasyendro vamrirūpeṇa dhanurjyām abhinat*" [?]). Then the tip of the bow sprang upward and the head of Viṣṇu was cut off.

When the bow-string was cut, it sounded "*ghṛṇ*" and fell, so it got the name *gharma*. The shrunk bow and the string, as soon as they were cut, spread widely, and so it became known as *pravargya*.

> मखस्य शिरोऽसीत्याह । यज्ञो वै मखः ।

> *makhasya śiro 'sītyāha | yajño vai makhaḥ |*

(Tai. Ā. 5-3-2 [?]) — in sentences such as these, the portion in which the *pravargya* is praised as the head of all sacrifices is quoted, and its pre-eminence is stated. Afterwards:

> ब्रह्मन् प्रवर्ग्येण प्रचरिष्यामः । होतर्घर्ममभिष्टुहि ।

> *brahman pravargyeṇa pracariṣyāmaḥ | hotargharmamabhiṣṭuhi |*

(Tai. Ā. 4-4-1 [?])

> ब्रह्मन् प्रचरिष्यामः । होतर्घर्ममभिष्टुहि ।

> *brahman pracariṣyāmaḥ | hotargharmamabhiṣṭuhi |*

(Tai. Ā. 4-3-1 [?]) — by such mantras the installation of the *pravargya* is carried out. The nature of the *pravargya* and its greatness will also be explained later, in a fitting context. In the ṛk at hand, to the word *gharma* …

### Printed p. 518  (PDF 538)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 518.)*

… the meaning *pravargya* has been given; it is only to show that both belong to one and the same rite.

***paśvaiṣṭiḥ*** — two ways of meaning have been given for this. First, "*paśur ity agner nāma*" ("*paśu* is a name of Agni"): since Agni too is the sacrificial animal, the sacrifice to Agni is called an animal sacrifice (*paśuyāga*); so he has quoted a sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

> अग्निः पशुरासीत्तेनायजन्त स एतं लोकमजयद्यस्मिन्नग्निः ॥

> *agniḥ paśurāsīttenāyajanta sa etaṃ lokamajayadyasminnagniḥ ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 5-2-26 [?]) — Agni was the sacrificial animal; when they had offered him as oblation, he then obtained the world in which Agni now exercises lordship; and so on. On this basis, when it is said *paśvaiṣṭiḥ*, it should be explained as "an Agni-sacrifice of the nature of an animal". Or "*athavā paśupriyatvāt paśur ity ucyate* [?] | *tasyāgneḥ iṣṭir bhavati | agnau yāgaḥ sarvo yuṣmadarthaṃ pravartate*" — since Agni is fond of the animal, the name *paśu* is itself well known for Agni. Here the oblation offered in Agni belongs to you also, and as it is an oblation offered with you in view, it is taken to be the praise in the ṛk at hand. Sāyaṇa has explained that sentences such as the following support this very meaning:

> आश्विनं धूम्रललाममालभेत यो दुर्ब्राह्मणः सोमं पिपासेत् ।

> *āśvinaṃ dhūmralalāmamālabheta yo durbrāhmaṇaḥ somaṃ pipāset |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-10-1 [?])

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***gharmam*** — "*gharmaḥ*" (Uṇ. Sū. 1-146 [?]): to the root *ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ* the suffix *mak* is added, with the *guṇa* irregularly derived; by the suffix accent the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***apaḥ*** — the accusative has come in the sense of the genitive; by "*ūḍidaṃpadādi…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 [?]) the case-ending takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***avṛṇītam*** — root *vṛṅ sambhaktau*, *kryādi* class; *laṅ*, second person dual; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***eṣe*** — root *iṣu icchāyām*; by "*anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-178 [?]) the suffix *viṭ* [as printed *vic*]; by "*pugantalaghūpadhasya ca*" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86 [?]) *guṇa* for the short penultimate vowel; dative singular; by "*sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 [?]) the case-ending takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***rathyā*** — by "*rathād yat*" (Pā. Sū. 4-3-121 [?]) the suffix *yat* in the sense of relation; by "*yato 'nāvaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-213 [?]) the *ādyudātta* accent; in the neuter plural …

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 5**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> आ वां दानाय ववृतीय दस्रा गोरोहेण तौग्र्यो न जिव्रिः ।
> अपः क्षोणी सचते माहिना वां जूर्णो वामक्षुरंहसो यजत्रा ॥ ५ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> आ । वाम् । दानाय । ववृतीय । दस्रा । गोः । ओहेन । तौग्र्यः । न । जिव्रिः ।
> अपः । क्षोणी इति । सचते । माहिना । वाम् । जूर्णः । वाम् । अक्षुः । अंहसः । यजत्रा ॥ ५ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे दस्रा शत्रूणामुपक्षपयितारावश्विनौ वां युवयोर्दानायास्मदभिमतायं [?] युवाभ्यां वाहयितुमा ववृतीय । आवर्तयामि यागदेशं ॥ वृतेरन्तर्भावितण्यर्थस्येदम् ॥ केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । गोः स्तुतिरूपाया वाचः ओहेन वहनेन साधनेन । यद्वा । आवर्तनकाल उच्यते । गोर्गन्त्र्या उषसो वहनेन । जिव्रिर्जीर्णो जयशीलो वा तौग्र्यो न तुग्र्याख्यस्य राज्ञः पुत्रो भुज्युरिव । स यथा शत्रुभिः सन्ताड्य समुद्रे पातितो युवां परितोऽस्य स्वोद्धाराय स्वसमीपमानयत तद्वदित्यर्थः [?] । इयमाख्यायिका तुग्रो ह । ऋ. १-११६-३ [?] । भुज्युमंहसः पिपृथः । ऋ. १०-६५-१३ [?] । नासत्या भुज्युम् । ऋ. १-११६-४ [?] । इत्यादिषु प्रसिद्धा च । किमाश्चर्यमहमावर्तयामीति [?] । किंच अपः क्षोणी । अप इत्यन्तरिक्षनाम । क्षोणीति पृथिवीनाम । द्यावापृथिव्यावपि वां युवयोर्माहिना माहात्म्येन युवयोः प्रसादेन सर्वोपकारिण्यावित ख्यातिं सर्वप्रदेशव्याप्तित्वं वा सचते । सेवते प्रत्येकम् । यद्वा । वां माहिना यजमानो द्यावापृथिव्यौ सचते । किंच हे यजत्रा यष्टव्यौ प्रसादादयमृषिर्जूर्णो जरया जीर्णाङ्गः सन्नंहसः पापाज्जरालक्षणात्प्रमुच्याक्षुः [?] चिरकालव्याप्तो दीर्घजीवी भूयात् । यद्वा । हे यजत्रा वां प्रसादाज्जूर्णो जीर्णो यजमानोंऽहसो दुरितस्य … [?] सोमरसरूपाणि उदकानि क्षोणी क्षोण्याम् ॥ सप्तम्यर्थे प्रगृह्यम् । भूम्यां चिरकालमक्षुः व्याप्तः सन् माहिना माहात्म्येन सचते । द्वितीयो वामित्ययुगादेराहार्थः [?] ॥ [as read; the whole is very dense, many words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Indra's counterpart prayer: the poet calls the Aśvins to the sacrifice as Bhujyu, son of Tugra, called them to rescue him from the sea; heaven and earth too serve their greatness, and the aged sacrificer asks to be freed from sin and to live long.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **dasrā** — O Aśvin deities, destroyers of enemies; **vām** — you two; **dānāya** — for giving (us what we desire); **goḥ** — of the speech in the form of praise; **ohena** — by the means; [or **goḥ** — belonging to the cow (the dawn); **ohena** — by the means (in time)]; **jivriḥ** — aged (victorious); **taugryaḥ na** — like Bhujyu the son of Tugra (calling you two to his own rescue, to his side); **ā vavṛtīya** — I desire to call (you) to the sacrificial hall. (*he*) **yajatrā** — O worshipful (venerable) Aśvins; **vām** — by your (favour); **jūrṇiḥ** [as printed *jūrṇaḥ*?] — the aged sacrificer; **aṃhasaḥ** — from sin; **apaḥ** — the Soma juices in the form of waters (obtained); **kṣoṇī** — in the earth; **akṣuḥ** — (for a long time) pervades (obtains); **māhinā** — by greatness; **vām** — you two; **sacete** — serve. **apaḥ** — the intermediate region; **kṣoṇī** — the earth; **vām** — you two; **māhinā** — by great glory (by the merit of being renowned as benefactors of the worlds); **sacete** — serve (you two). [Or: **vām** — of you two; **māhinā** — by greatness; **apaḥ kṣoṇī** — the earth and the intermediate region; **sacete** — (the sacrificer) serves; (**kiṃ ca** — and) **yajatrā** — O worshipful Aśvins; **jūrṇiḥ** — the ṛṣi whose limbs are aged; **vām** — by your favour; **aṃhasaḥ** — (freed) from the sin that is old age; **akṣuḥ** — becomes pervaded for a long time (becomes long-lived).]

**Bhāvārtha**

O Dasras! As Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, whose limbs were old, called you of old to his rescue, so I too, at the time of dawn, praising you, for the fulfilment of my wish, wish to call you to my sacrificial hall; this sacrificer, by your greatness, serves heaven and earth …

### Printed p. 521  (PDF 541)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 521.)*

**Bhāvārtha (continued)** — … serves heaven and earth; O worshipful Aśvins! this ṛṣi, whose limbs are aged, by your favour is freed from old age and attains long life.

**Printed English**

> Dasras, may I bring you, by the vehicle of my prayers, (hither), to bestow (upon me your aid), like the infirm son of Tugra: heaven and earth combine (to worship you) through your greatness: may this, your aged (worshipper), adorable (Ashwins), enjoy long life, (exempt) from sin.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***dasrā*** — "*dasu upakṣaye | śatrūṇām upakṣayitārau | yadvā devavaidyatvena rogāṇām upakṣayitārau*" — "destroyers of enemies; or, being divine physicians, destroyers of diseases". The word *dasrā* also has the sense *darśanīyau* ("beautiful of form"). In the ṛk at hand it is explained as "destroyers of enemies". Of the Aśvins, the sons of Saraṇyū, one has the name Dasra and the other Nāsatya; but in general it is the custom to speak of both together as *dasrā*. The origin and the forms of the Aśvin deities will be explained later in this same portion, in the special topics of Ṛk 1-181-4 [?].

***goḥ ohena*** — of these words two kinds of meaning for *goḥ* have been given. First, "*goḥ stutirūpāyā vācaḥ ohena vahanena sādhanena*" — "by the means of carrying, of the speech in the form of praise"; second, "*goḥ gantryāḥ uṣasaḥ vahanena*" — "by the bringing of the moving Uṣas".

The Nirukta-writers count the word *go* among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5 [?]), and give the derivation of the word as follows:

> गौरिति पृथिव्या नामधेयं यद्दूरंगता भवति यच्चास्यां भूतानि गच्छन्ति । गातेर्वौकारो नामकरणः ।

> *gauriti pṛthivyā nāmadheyaṃ yaddūraṃgatā bhavati yaccāsyāṃ bhūtāni gacchanti | gātervaukāro nāmakaraṇaḥ |*

(Ni. 2-5 [?]) — because it is spread out very far (it "goes far"), and because beings go about on it: the word *gauḥ* is a synonym of the earth. They explain that the formation of this word is possible even by adding the suffix *au* to the root *gā*; and then, …

### Printed p. 522  (PDF 542)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 522.)*

> अथापि पशुनापि भवत्येतस्मादेव ।

> *athāpi paśunāpi bhavatyetasmādeva |*

— "for this very reason" — that is, because [the word] is formed from the root *gam* or *gā*, giving the meaning stated above, the name is well known for the animal also; and having said "*ādityo 'pi gaur ucyate; sarve 'pi raśmayo gāva ucyante*" ("the Āditya too is called *gauḥ*; all the rays also are called *gāvaḥ*"), they have shown that the word *go* is used also in the senses "Āditya", "ray" and so on. And, explaining the word in the ṛk 1-164-28 [?], the Nirukta-writers have given for *gauḥ* the meaning *mādhyamikā vāk* ("the middle speech") (Ni. 11-42 [?]). In the ṛk at hand, to explain it as "speech in the form of praise" is the more fitting, as earlier:

> इमं रथमधि ये सप्त तस्थुः सप्तचक्रं सप्त वहन्त्यश्वाः ।
> सप्त स्वसारो अभि सं नवन्ते यत्र गवां निहिता सप्त नाम ॥

> *imaṃ rathamadhi ye sapta tasthuḥ saptacakraṃ sapta vahantyaśvāḥ |*
> *sapta svasāro abhi saṃ navante yatra gavāṃ nihitā sapta nāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-3 [?]) — just as *gavām* is explained here as "of speech in the form of praise", so here too the meaning "of speech in the form of praise" is in keeping.

***ohena*** — this word, formed from the root *vah*, is used in the sense of "the means of carrying". Uses such as *ohasā*, *ohabrahmāṇaḥ* are many; they are explained in the respective contexts.

***jivriḥ*** — for this word Sāyaṇa has shown in the bhāṣya that both meanings, "aged" and "victorious" (*jayaśīla*), are possible. But in the Nirukta, in the following which are cited (Ni. 3-21 [?]):

> आ त्वा रम्भं न जिव्रयो ररम्भा शवसस्पते । उश्मसि त्वा सधस्थ आ ॥

> *ā tvā rambhaṃ na jivrayo rarambhā śavasaspate | uśmasi tvā sadhastha ā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-93-10 [?])

> एना सत्या तन्वं १ सं सृजस्वाथा जिव्री विदथमा वदाथः ।

> *enā satyā tanvaṃ 1 saṃ sṛjasvāthā jivrī vidathamā vadāthaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-12 [?]) — in all these ṛks Yāska has explained it as "aged, old". But since the word *jūrṇi*, which shows old age, is used here again, in the ṛk at hand *jivri* may also be given the meaning "victorious".

***jūrṇiḥ*** — "*jarayā jīrṇāṅgaḥ*" — "one whose limbs are worn by old age": that is, one who has a body that has faded and shrivelled with age. In other places Sāyaṇa has given other meanings for the word *jūrṇi*. The Nirukta-writers have read the word *jūrṇi* among the names of "anger" (Ni. 2-7 [?]) and among the names of "swift" (*kṣipra*) (Ni. 2-9 [?]), and they explain this derivation:

> जूर्णिर्जवतेर्वा द्रवतेर्वा दूनोतेर्वा ।

> *jūrṇirjavatervā dravatervā dūnotervā |*

(Ni. 6-9 [?])
