### Printed p. 523  (PDF 543)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 523.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — the word *jūrṇi* is derived either from the root *jū*, which gives the sense of "speed", or from the root *drū*, which gives the sense "to run", or from the root *du*, which has the sense "to injure": so the commentator has shown the formation of the word. And, to show its use, citing the ṛk

> हतेमुसन्न [?] वक्षति क्षिप्ता जूर्णिर्न वक्षति ।

> *hatemusanna [?] vakṣati kṣiptā jūrṇirna vakṣati |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-19-5 [?]) — he has explained there that *jūrṇiḥ* is *śaktiḥ* ("spear-like missile"), since it is speedy, by reason of its connection with throwing (*kṣepaṇa*). But in the ṛk at hand there is no room for stating that meaning. For *jivriḥ* the meaning "victorious" must be given, and for *jūrṇiḥ* the meaning "grown old in years".

*Jivriḥ* is an epithet of the word *taugryaḥ*. Here the sacrificer compares himself to Taugrya and says that, as the latter was rescued by the favour of the Aśvin deities, so he too shares their favour.

Sāyaṇa: *taugryaḥ na tugrākhyasya rājñaḥ putro bhujyur iva | sa yathā śatrubhiḥ saṃtāḍya samudre pātito yuvāṃ parito 'syai svoddhārāya svasamīpam ānayata kenasid ity arthaḥ* [as read [?]] — "like Bhujyu, the son of the king named Tugra: as he, struck by enemies and thrown into the sea, called you for his rescue, and you brought him to your side". He gives the matter of the earlier story as background: Tugra's son Bhujyu, tormented by enemies, praised you, who were called to his side from the sea, and was pleased.

The son of Tugra, Taugrya, once, being defeated by enemies, was bound hand and foot and thrown into the middle of the sea. He prayed for help to the Aśvin deities. At once they harnessed their horses to their chariot and rescued him in a ship; so Sāyaṇa has told the story as quoted. This son of Tugra is well known by the name Bhujyu; and in many places his story is told.

That the Aśvin deities rescued this same son of Tugra who was drowning in the sea is described by Kakṣīvān, the son of Dīrghatamas, in Ṛk-saṃhitā 1-116 and 1-117 [as read [?]]; by Agastya Maitrāvaruṇi in the 182nd sūkta; by Brahmātithi of the Kaṇva *gotra* in 8-5; and by Ghoṣā, the daughter of Kakṣīvān, in 10-39. In the 182nd sūkta [?] it is described, as seen below, how they sent boats, and how the son of Tugra, filled with hope, clung to them and was saved by their favour.

> युवमेतं चक्रथुः सिन्धुषु प्लवमात्मन्वन्तं पक्षिणं तौग्र्याय कम् ।
> येन देवत्रा मनसा निरूहथुः सुपप्तनी पेतथुः क्षोदसो महः ॥
> अवविद्धं तौग्र्यमप्स्वन्तरनारम्भणे तमसि प्रविद्धम् ।
> चतस्रो नावो जठलस्य जुष्टा उदश्विभ्यामिषिताः पारयन्ति ॥

> *yuvametaṃ cakrathuḥ sindhuṣu plavamātmanvantaṃ pakṣiṇaṃ taugryāya kam |*
> *yena devatrā manasā nirūhathuḥ supaptanī petathuḥ kṣodaso mahaḥ ‖*
> *avaviddhaṃ taugryamapsvantaranārambhaṇe tamasi praviddham |*
> *catasro nāvo jaṭhalasya juṣṭā udaśvibhyāmiṣitāḥ pārayanti ‖*

### Printed p. 524  (PDF 544)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 524.)*

> कः स्विद्वृक्षो निष्ठितो मध्ये अर्णसो यं तौग्र्यो नाधितः पर्यषस्वजत् ।
> पर्णा मृगस्य पतरोरिवारभ उदश्विना ऊहथुः श्रोमताय कम् ॥

> *kaḥ svidvṛkṣo niṣṭhito madhye arṇaso yaṃ taugryo nādhitaḥ paryaṣasvajat |*
> *parṇā mṛgasya patarorivārabha udaśvinā ūhathuḥ śromatāya kam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-182-5 to 7 [?]) — "O Aśvin deities! For Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, you fashioned this sentient boat, furnished with wings. For the son of Tugra, who had fallen and was sinking in the sea, bottomless and dark, you sent four boats. For the flying birds the wings are a support in the sky; for Bhujyu, who was sinking in the sea, you made the limbs of the boat a support and a protector; from what tree did you make them?" — so the story is praised. The same matter is intimated in the ṛk at hand also.

***aṃhasaḥ*** — "*aṃhatir āhaśāṃ* [?] *haṃś cāṃhaś ca haṃteḥ*" (Ni. 4-25 [?]) — although the word *aṃhas* is formed from the root *han* that gives the sense "to injure", this word is in general used more in the sense of "sin" than in the sense of "injury". In the ṛk at hand the meaning is "evil" (*duritam*).

For the latter half of this mantra three kinds of construction have been shown to be possible. First: (1) "*jūrṇiḥ māhinā aṃhasaḥ apaḥ kṣoṇī akṣuḥ vāṃ sacete*" — the aged sacrificer, freed by your favour from sin, obtains the Soma for ever and serves you on the earth; second, (2) "*vāṃ mahinā apaḥ kṣoṇī sacete*" — by your greatness heaven and earth have both won renown as the protectors of the world; third, (3) "*vāṃ mahinā jūrṇiḥ apaḥ kṣoṇī sacete*" — by your greatness the sacrificer serves heaven and earth: so the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya shows.

***apaḥ*** — read among the names of the intermediate region (Ni. 2-8 [?]); ***kṣoṇī*** — "*kṣoṇīti pṛthivīnāma*" — *kṣoṇī* is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 1-7 [?]).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***dānāya*** — root *ḍudāñ dāne*; the suffix *yuc*; by "*yuvor anākau*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 [?]) *ana* substituted for it; by "*citaḥ*" the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***vavṛtīya*** — root *vṛtu vartane*; because the activity of the causer (*prayojaka*) is shown, it contains the sense of the causative; *liṅ*, first person singular, the ending *iṭ*; by "*iṭo 'ṭ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-106 [?]) *a* is substituted for it; by "*liṅaḥ sīyuṭ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-103 [?]) the augment *sīyuṭ*; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" *ślu* as the *vikaraṇa*; reduplication of the root; by "*liṅaḥ salopo 'ntyasya*" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-79 [?]) elision of the *s*; thus *vavṛtīya*; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.

### Printed p. 525  (PDF 545)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 525.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, continued)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***dasrā*** — by "*supāṃ sulak…*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) *ā* is substituted for the dual; being in the vocative, the *nighāta* accent occurs.
- ***jivriḥ*** — root *jyā vayohānau*; by "*jīryater krin raśca vaḥ*" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]) the suffix *krin*, with *va* substituted for the *r* of the root; since the suffix has *n* as marker, the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***jūrṇiḥ*** — root *jvara saṃtāpe*; the suffix *kta*; by "*jvarasvarasrivyaviḥ…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-20 [?]) *ūṭh* [as printed] is substituted for the *va* and the penultimate vowel of the root; by "*radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ*" the *n* for the *t* of the *niṣṭhā*; by "*raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade*" the *ṇ*; the final syllable is *udātta* by the suffix accent.
- ***yajatrā*** — root *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; by "*amināsi…yaji bandhi…*" (Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?], as read [?]) the suffix *atran*; by "*supāṃ sulak…*" *ā* in the dual of the vocative; being in the vocative, the *nighāta* accent.
- ***kṣoṇī*** — in the second meaning it is the locative singular; by "*supāṃ sulak…*" the *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening; by "*īdūtau ca saptamyarthe*" (Pā. Sū. 1-1-19 [?]) it receives the name *pragṛhya*. ‖ 5 ‖

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 6**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> नि यद्युवेथे नियुतः सुदानू उप स्वधाभिः सृजथः पुरंधिम् ।
> प्रेषद्वेषद्वातो न सूरिरा महे ददे सुव्रतो न वाजम् ॥ ६ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> नि । यत् । युवेथे इति । निऽयुतः । सुदानू इति सुऽदानू । उप । स्वधाभिः । सृजथः । पुरम्ऽधिम् ।
> प्रेषत् । वेषत् । वातः । न । सूरिः । आ । महे । ददे । सुऽव्रतः । न । वाजम् ॥ ६ ॥

> *ni | yat | yuvethe iti | ni 'yutaḥ | sudānū iti su 'dānū | upa | svadhābhiḥ | sṛjathaḥ | puram 'dhim |*
> *preṣat | veṣat | vātaḥ | na | sūriḥ | ā | mahe | dade | su 'vrataḥ | na | vājam ‖ 6 ‖*

### Printed p. 526  (PDF 546)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 526.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे सुदानू शोभनदानावश्विनौ यद्यदा नियुतोऽश्वानि [?] युवेथे नियुञ्जाथे नियोजयथः । ताभिरस्मद्यज्ञगमनाय सम्युक्तौ भवथः तदा स्वधाभिरन्नैस्तत्कारणैरुदकैर्वा पुरन्धिं बहूनां धात्रीं पृथिवीमुप सृजथः । एवं च सति सूरिः स्तोता यजमानो वातो न वायुरिव तद्वत् क्षिप्रं युवां प्रेषत् । तर्पयतु । वेषत् । व्याप्नोतु । कामयतां वा । प्रीणातेर्वेवेष्टेश्च लेटि रूपे ॥ अनन्तरं सुव्रतो नातिप्रसस्तोष्णादिकर्मवानिव [?] वाजमन्नं महे महत्त्वायायं [?] यजमान आ ददे । आदत्ते । स्वीकरोति । अजो दोऽनास्यविवरणे । पा. ७-४-५० [?] इत्यात्मनेपदम् । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्विति तलोपः । यद्वा । छान्दसे लिटि रूपम् ॥ स्वीकृत्य स्वमहत्त्वायं [?] युवानेव तर्पयित्वित्यर्थः ॥ [as read; a few words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* When the Aśvins yoke their *niyut*-horses to come to the sacrifice, they fill the earth with food-giving water; the sacrificer, swift as the wind, pleases them and, like a man of good works, receives food and greatness.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **sudānū** — O Aśvin deities of good giving; **yat** — when; **niyutaḥ** — your horses called *niyut*; **ni yuvethe** — you yoke (to the chariot); (**tat** — then); **svadhābhiḥ** — with food, or with water, the cause of food; **purandhim** — this earth, the nurse of many; **upa sṛjathaḥ** — you fill; (**evaṃ sati** — this being so) **sūriḥ** — the praiser (the sacrificer); **vātaḥ na** — like the wind (swiftly); **preṣat** — may he satisfy you two; **veṣat** — may he attain (or desire) you; **suvrataḥ na** — like a man of good deeds; **vājam** — food; **mahe** — (for his own greatness); **ā dade** — (this sacrificer) accepts [or: accepting you two, satisfies you].

**Bhāvārtha**

O Aśvins of good giving! Whenever, with a wish to come, you yoke your *niyut*-horses to the chariot, you pour out on the earth the water that is the cause of food; the sacrificer, as swift as the wind, becomes ready to please you; and, like a man of good works, by your favour obtains food, receives it, satisfies you, and attains greatness.

**Printed English**

> Bountiful givers, when you yoke your horses you replenish the earth with viands: may this your wurshipper [sic] be (swift) as the wind to propitiate and please you, that through your great (favour), he may, like a pious man obtain food.

### Printed p. 527  (PDF 547)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 527.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***sudānū*** — "*śobhanadānau*" — "the two of good giving": it is an epithet showing the quality of the Aśvin deities as most excellent givers. Its special meanings have been told earlier.

***niyutaḥ*** — the meaning of this word is "horses". By the sentence "*niyuto vāyoḥ, rāsabhāv aśvinoḥ*" (Ni. 2-25 [?]) it is well known that the *niyut*s are the vehicles of Vāyu and the asses are the vehicles of the Aśvin deities. Here the word *niyutaḥ* is fit to be taken as the horses of the Aśvin deities. There is no rule that the epithet *niyutvān* should be used only for Vāyu. For example:

> प्र वावृजे सुप्रया बर्हिरेषामा विश्पतीव बीरिट इयाते ।
> विशामक्तोरुषसः पूर्वहूतौ वायुः पूषा स्वस्तये नियुत्वान् ॥

> *pra vāvṛje suprayā barhireṣāmā viśpatīva bīriṭa iyāte |*
> *viśāmaktoruṣasaḥ pūrvahūtau vāyuḥ pūṣā svastaye niyutvān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-2 [?]) — here *niyutvān* is an epithet of Pūṣan. The Nirukta-writers, giving the derivation of this word, say "*niyutvān niyuta asyāśvāḥ | niyuto niyamanād vā niyojanād vā*" (Ni. 5-28 [?]) — that the horses are so called because they are controlled or because they are yoked. The same derivation applies to the word *niyutaḥ* in the ṛk at hand. Then, since the word is usable for horses in general, it is an epithet also of the Aśvin deities' horses.

In the sense of control (*niyamana*), the name *niyutvān* is well known also for the Lord (*Īśvara*), who controls; *niyutvān* is read among the names of Īśvara (Ni. 5-11 [?]).

***svadhābhiḥ*** — for this word the explanation is "with food, or the water that is its cause" (*annaiḥ tatkāraṇair udakair vā*). In some places for this same word the explanation is "by one's own splendour or by food" (*ātmīyena tejasā annena vā*). The Nirukta-writers have included this word among the names of "water" (Ni. 1-12 [?]) and among the names of "food" (Ni. 6-9 [?]). Besides these meanings, in many contexts the word has the meanings "by one's own greatness", "one's own splendour" and "self-support". The special meanings of the word have been told in this same portion in the special topics of Ṛk 1-176-2 [?]. Besides the meanings "food" and "water", it is a special feature that the word is used also as a synonym of the power of the Lord. For example:

> न मृत्युरासीदमृतं न तर्हि न रात्र्या अह्न आसीत्प्रकेतः ।
> आनीदवातं स्वधया तदेकं तस्माद्धान्यन्न परः किं चनास ॥

> *na mṛtyurāsīdamṛtaṃ na tarhi na rātryā ahna āsītpraketaḥ |*
> *ānīdavātaṃ svadhayā tadekaṃ tasmāddhānyanna paraḥ kiṃ canāsa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-2 [?]) — in this, *svasmin dhīyate dhriyate āśritya vartate iti svadhā* — "that which is supported in itself and rests in itself is *svadhā*": since it has self-support, *svadhā* is, as Sāyaṇa explains, an epithet of the extraordinary power, the *māyā*, of the Lord (the Supreme Brahman) … [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 528  (PDF 548)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 528.)*

… as he has explained. In the same way it is a word describing the supernatural power of Viṣṇu, Uṣas and others.

***purandhim*** — "*bahūnāṃ dhātrīṃ pṛthivīm*" — "the earth, the nurse of many": the word *purandhi* is explained as "earth", the nurse of many. This word also suggests the senses *prabhūta* ("abundance") [as read [?]], *pauṣkalya* ("fullness") and *samṛddhi* ("prosperity"), and though it is used so everywhere, since it occurs in many contexts it is clear, from the very words of the Nirukta-writers, that its meaning has to be given according to each context. For:

> ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमाः सधस्थं विश्वे अभि सन्ति देवाः ।
> ताँ अध्वर उशतो यक्ष्यग्ने श्रुष्टी भगं नासत्या पुरंधिम् ॥

> *te hi yajñeṣu yajñiyāsa ūmāḥ sadhasthaṃ viśve abhi santi devāḥ |*
> *tā~ adhvara uśato yakṣyagne śruṣṭī bhagaṃ nāsatyā puraṃdhim ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-4 [?]) — in explaining the meaning of *purandhim* in this ṛk, there:

> पुरंधिर्बहुधीस्तत्कः । पुरंधिर्भगः पुरस्तात्त्वस्यान्यादेश इत्येकम् । इन्द्र इत्यपरं स बहुकर्मतमः पुरां च दारयितृतमः । वरुण इत्यपरं तं प्रज्ञया स्तौति ।

> *puraṃdhirbahudhīstatkaḥ | puraṃdhirbhagaḥ purastāttvasyānyādeśa ityekam | indra ityaparaṃ sa bahukarmatamaḥ purāṃ ca dārayitṛtamaḥ | varuṇa ityaparaṃ taṃ prajñayā stauti |*

(Ni. 6-13 [?]) — the meaning of the word *purandhi* is "one who has abundant *dhī* (intellect)". But who is such a one? Some hold that, since the word *bhaga* occurs in the cited ṛk before this word, it is an epithet of *bhaga*. Since the word *dhī* is also read among the names of "action" (*karma*), *purandhi* means "one of manifold works", or, since it means "one who splits the enemy's cities", some hold that it is an epithet of Indra. Or, as in the sentences "*imāṃ nu kavitamasya māyām*" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-6 [?]) and the like, the Nirukta-writers have shown, citing this ṛk, that just as Varuṇa's most excellent wisdom is praised, it may be that in this ṛk too his wisdom is described, and that it may be a synonym of *varuṇa*: so they have given these different views of the intention. And, to show the superiority of the generosity of the deities toward the sacrificer, and to indicate the prosperity of the oblations and the like which the sacrificer offers to the deities, the Nirukta-writers have shown the use of this word with still other examples:

> आदायु श्येनो अभरत्सोमं सहस्रं सवां अयुतं च साकम् ।
> अत्रा पुरंधिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूराः ॥

> *ādāyu śyeno abharatsomaṃ sahasraṃ savāṃ ayutaṃ ca sākam |*
> *atrā puraṃdhirajahādarātīrmade somasya mūrā amūrāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-6 [?])

---

### Printed p. 529  (PDF 549)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 529; signature mark "XIII 34".)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — in the ṛk, for the word *purandhi*, Durgācārya (Ni. 11-2 [?]) gives "*purandhiḥ bahudhanasya dātā*" ("giver of abundant wealth"), and Sāyaṇa "*bahukarmā*" ("of many works"). Here the word is an epithet of Indra; the purport is "generous".

> नैधूतो [?] अद्रिषुतो बर्हिषि प्रियः पतिर्गवां प्रदिव इन्दुर्ऋत्वियः ।
> पुरन्धिवान्मनुषो यज्ञसाधनः शुचिर्धिया पवते सोम इन्द्र ते ॥

> *naidhūto [?] adriṣuto barhiṣi priyaḥ patirgavāṃ pradiva indurṛtviyaḥ |*
> *purandhivānmanuṣo yajñasādhanaḥ śucirdhiyā pavate soma indra te ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-62-4 [?]) — in this ṛk *purandhivān manuṣaḥ* is explained as "a man of many works", i.e. a man who performs rites, in order to satisfy the deities; and

> पावीरवी तन्यतुरेकपादजो दिवो धर्ता सिन्धुरापः समुद्रियः ।
> विश्वे देवासः शृणवन्वचांसि मे सरस्वती सह धीभिः पुरन्ध्या ॥

> *pāvīravī tanyaturekapādajo divo dhartā sindhurāpaḥ samudriyaḥ |*
> *viśve devāsaḥ śṛṇavanvacāṃsi me sarasvatī saha dhībhiḥ purandhyā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-13 [?]) — in this ṛk the Nirukta-writers (Ni. 12-30 [?]) have given the meaning "*vacanāni* (words) that are accompanied by manifold praise (*purandhyā stutyā prayuktāni*)" for this word. Sāyaṇa, saying "*bahuvidhayā prajñayā sahitā sarasvatī*", has stated that it is an epithet of Sarasvatī, who is endowed with manifold wisdom. But, from the explanation given by Durgācārya (Ni. 12-30 [?]), "*bahudhātryai; mādhyamikayā vācā*", it is known that the word *purandhi* suggests a special deity like Sarasvatī. In the same way:

> शं नो भगः शमु नः शंसो अस्तु शं नः पुरन्धिः शमु सन्तु रायः ।
> शं नः सत्यस्य सुयमस्य शंसः शं नो अर्यमा पुरुजातो अस्तु ॥

> *śaṃ no bhagaḥ śamu naḥ śaṃso astu śaṃ naḥ purandhiḥ śamu santu rāyaḥ |*
> *śaṃ naḥ satyasya suyamasya śaṃsaḥ śaṃ no aryamā purujāto astu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-35-2 [?]) — in such ṛks it appears that *purandhi* is an individual deity. Sāyaṇa too has not made it an epithet of *bhaga* and the other words in this ṛk. And:

> देवो वो भगः सविता रायो अंश इन्द्रो वृत्रस्य संजितो धनानाम् ।
> ऋभुक्षा वाज उत वा पुरन्धिरवन्तु नो अमृतासस्तुरासः ॥

> *devo vo bhagaḥ savitā rāyo aṃśa indro vṛtrasya saṃjito dhanānām |*
> *ṛbhukṣā vāja uta vā purandhiravantu no amṛtāsasturāsaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-42-5 [?]) — in this ṛk the word is a synonym of Vibhvan [?].

> पुराणी देवि युवतिः पुरन्धिरनु व्रतं [?] विश्ववारे ।

> *purāṇī devi yuvatiḥ purandhiranu vrataṃ [?] viśvavāre |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-61-1 [?]) — in such places it is an epithet of Uṣas: "possessed of many *stotras*" is the meaning. So in many places this word is used both for the wife and for woman in general: it gives the meaning of "women who are fit and ripe to bear offspring and not barren".

### Printed p. 530  (PDF 550)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 530.)*

> अग्निः सप्तिं वाजम्भरं ददात्यग्निर्वीरं श्रुत्यं कर्मनिष्ठाम् ।
> अग्नी रोदसी वि चरत्समञ्जन्नग्निर्नारीं वीरकुक्षिं पुरन्धिम् ॥

> *agniḥ saptiṃ vājambharaṃ dadātyagnirvīraṃ śrutyaṃ karmaniṣṭhām |*
> *agnī rodasī vi caratsamañjannagnirnārīṃ vīrakukṣiṃ purandhim ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-1 [?]) — in such ṛks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-13 [?]; 1-117-19 [?]) it means a woman capable of giving birth (*prasavasamartha*), a wife; and

> प्र बोधयोषः पुरन्धिं जार आ ससतीमिव ।
> प्र चक्षय रोदसी वासयोषसः श्रवसे वासयोषसः ॥

> *pra bodhayoṣaḥ purandhiṃ jāra ā sasatīmiva |*
> *pra cakṣaya rodasī vāsayoṣasaḥ śravase vāsayoṣasaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-124-6 [?]) — in such ṛks too it means a woman fit for enjoyment. Thus, when it describes manifold qualities, the word *purandhi* indicates both the abundance of those qualities and the prosperity of truth. In the ṛk at hand the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya shows that it is an epithet that describes the quality of the earth, which is full of wealth and is the supporter of the world.

***sūriḥ*** — "*stotā ayaṃ yajamānaḥ*" — "the sacrificer, who is the praiser": it shows the *stuti*-doing of the sacrificer. Since *rebhaḥ*, *jaritā*, *kāruḥ* and so on are read among the thirteen names of "praiser" (Ni. 3-13 [?]), *sūrayaḥ* means "praisers", i.e. devotees who do *stotra*. In contexts in which it gives the meaning "the discerning, the intelligent", the word *sūri* is used in many places. When it is used of the ṛṣis who have obtained an unearthly, bodily-eyed and mental vision, which grasps the true forms of the deities and the secret truths of the universe, this epithet gives a special meaning.

> तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं सदा पश्यन्ति सूरयः । दिवीव चक्षुराततम् ॥

> *tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ | divīva cakṣurātatam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-20 [?]) — in such contexts the word indicates the extraordinary power of vision of the ṛṣis, not merely of those who praise. And this word is used also of Indra and other deities, as an epithet. For example:

> मंहिष्ठमच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुवृक्तिभिः सूरिं वावृधध्यै ।

> *maṃhiṣṭhamacchoktibhirmatīnāṃ suvṛktibhiḥ sūriṃ vāvṛdhadhyai |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-3 [?]) — in such ṛks, "*vipaścitam indram*" and so on, the wisdom (*prājñatva*) of Indra and other deities is shown. Besides, the word *sūri* is used also to indicate the meanings "master" (*prabhu*), "impeller" (*preraka*), "one who sets on the right path" (*sanmārgapravartaka*). For example:

> जनो यः पज्रेभ्यो वाजिनीवानश्वावतो रथिनो मह्यं सूरिः ।

> *jano yaḥ pajrebhyo vājinīvānaśvāvato rathino mahyaṃ sūriḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-7 [?])

### Printed p. 531  (PDF 551)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 531.)*

> असद्यथा जरित्र उत सूरिरिन्द्रो रायो विश्ववारस्य दाता ।

> *asadyathā jaritra uta sūririndro rāyo viśvavārasya dātā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-33-10 [?])

> मुह्यन्त्वन्ये अभितो जनास इहास्माकं मघवा सूरिरस्तु ।

> *muhyantvanye abhito janāsa ihāsmākaṃ maghavā sūrirastu |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-81-6 [?]) — in these and other places, the epithet describes the quality of Indra and other deities, who are masters (*prabhu*) and guides on the right path. And:

> आदस्य ते कृष्णासो दक्षि सूरयः शूरस्येव त्वेषथादीषते वयः ।

> *ādasya te kṛṣṇāso dakṣi sūrayaḥ śūrasyeva tveṣathādīṣate vayaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-141-5 [?]) — in such places it is often given the meaning "path" (*mārga*), in the form of *āpa*. In the ṛk at hand the word is used in the sense of "praiser".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***yuvethe*** — root *yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ*; by "*vyatyayo bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 [?]) the ending *āthām* in the second person dual; by "*ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-79 [?]) *e* for the *ṭi*; by *vyatyaya* the *śa* *vikaraṇa*; by "*ato yeyaḥ*" … (Pā. Sū. 6-2-[?], as read [?]) *iya* for the *ā*; by "*āto lopa iṭi ca*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-64 [?]) elision of the *y*; *guṇa*; by "*aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-77 [?]) *uvaṅ* substitution; because of *yad*-connection no *nighāta* accent; the *vikaraṇa* accent remains.
- ***sṛjathaḥ*** — root *sṛja visarge*; second person dual; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***preṣat*** — root *prīñ tarpaṇe kāntau ca*; *leṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; by "*itaś ca lopaḥ*" elision of the *i*; by "*leṭo 'ḍāṭau*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 [?]) the augment *aṭ*; by "*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-34 [?]) *sip*; taking that as the cause, *guṇa* for the root; by "*ādeśapratyayayoḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-59 [?]) *ṣatva* for the *s*; being in *pādādi* position there is no *nighāta*; the suffixes being *pit*, they are *anudātta*, so the root accent remains.
- ***veṣat*** — root *vī gatyādiṣu*; *leṭ*, third person singular; the operations as before; being in an *atiṅanta* word-position, no *nighāta*; the root accent remains.
- ***dade*** — root *ḍudāñ dāne*; since it is connected with the prefix *ā*, by "*āṅo 'nāsyavivaraṇe*" (Pā. Sū. 1-3-20 [?]) it is *ātmanepada*; third person singular …

### Printed p. 532  (PDF 552)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 532.)*

… the suffix *ta*; *e* for the *ṭi*; *ślu* as *vikaraṇa*; reduplication and so on; by "*lopaś ca ātmanepadeṣu*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-41 [?]) elision of the *t*; or, in the Vedic *liṭ*; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***suvrataḥ*** — *śobhanaṃ vrataṃ yasya saḥ*; by "*nañsubhyām*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172 [?]) the final syllable of the hind-member is *udātta*. ‖ 6 ‖

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 7**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> वयं चिद्धि वां जरितारः सत्या विपन्यामहे वि पणिर्हितावान् ।
> अधा चिद्धि ष्माश्विनावनिन्द्या पाथो हि ष्मा वृषणावन्तिदेवम् ॥ ७ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> वयम् । चित् । हि । वाम् । जरितारः । सत्याः । विपन्यामहे । वि । पणिः । हितऽवान् ।
> अध । चित् । हि । स्म । अश्विनौ । अनिन्द्या । पाथः । हि । स्म । वृषणौ । अन्तिऽदेवम् ॥ ७ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> वयं चिद्धि वयमपि जरितारस्तव स्तोतारः सत्याः सत्यफलाः सन्तो विपन्यामहे । विविधं स्तुमः । पणिः पणाधारो द्रोणकलशो वि हितवान् स्थापितसोमो [?] ऽसीत् । यद्वा । पणिर्वणिग्लुब्धकोऽयष्वा हितान्नियतधनो धनाढ्योऽस्य यष्वा वि । वियुज्यताम् ॥ उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥ अथापि चिद्धि ष्म । एते त्रयः पूरणाः । हे अश्विनावनिन्द्या । प्रशस्यनाम्नैतत् । हे प्रशस्यौ वृषणौ हे कामानां वर्षितारौ युवामन्तिदेवं देवानामन्तिके पाथः । सोमं पिबथः । यद्वा । अन्तिके वर्तमानं देवान्नाप्नुवानं सोममिति योज्यम् ॥ [as read; several words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* We, your true praisers, praise you in many ways; the Soma vessel is set; you, blameless and showering, drink the Soma near the gods; the miser is to be separated.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **Aśvinau** — O Aśvin deities; **jaritāraḥ** — your praisers; **vayaṃ cit hi** — we too; **satyāḥ** — those with true fruits; **vām** — you two; **vipanyāmahe** — we praise in diverse ways; **paṇiḥ** — the *droṇa*-vessel (for the Soma); **vi hitavān** — (with the Soma) placed; [or **paṇiḥ** — the greedy trader; **hitavān** — one whose wealth is fixed; **vi (yujyatām)** — let him be separated]; (**cit hi sma** — three expletives); **adha** — and; **anindyā** — O blameless …

---

### Printed p. 533  (PDF 553)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 533.)*

**Pratipadārtha (continued)** — … (praise-worthy) Aśvins! (*he* **Aśvinau**) O Aśvins; **vṛṣaṇau** — you two, who rain down desires; **antidevam** — near the (other) deities; **pāthaḥ** — drink the Soma; [or **antidevam** — the Soma juice that reaches the deities]; **pāthaḥ sma hi** — you do drink.

**Bhāvārtha**

O blameless Aśvin deities! We, your praisers, praise you in various ways; for you the *droṇa*-vessel has been set up with the Soma; you, the showerers of desires, sit near the other deities and drink the Soma.

**Printed English**

> Your sincere adorers, we verily praise you in various ways. The pitcher has been placed (ready for the Soma juice). Irreproachable Ashwins, showerer (of benefits), drink freely of the juice in the presence of the gods.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***jaritāraḥ*** — the word *jaritṛ* has been read among the names of "praiser" (Ni. 3-19 [?]). The Nirukta-writers, citing the ṛk "*nūnaṃ sā te prati varaṃ jaritre*" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-21 [?]), explain *jaritṛ* there as *garitṛ*. "*jaritā garitā*" (Ni. 1-7 [?]) — since praise is of the nature of song, the doer of praise also becomes a singer: this is the intention of the identity. Besides, a proper name *Jaritṛ* also is known. For example:

> अयमग्ने जरिता त्वे अभूदपि सहसः सूनो नह्यन्यदस्त्याप्यम् ।
> भद्रं हि शर्म त्रिवरूथमस्ति त आरे हिंसानामप दिद्युमा कृधि ॥

> *ayamagne jaritā tve abhūdapi sahasaḥ sūno nahyanyadastyāpyam |*
> *bhadraṃ hi śarma trivarūthamasti ta āre hiṃsānāmapa didyumā kṛdhi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-142-1 [?]) — in this ṛk and the following two mantras the ṛṣi named Jaritṛ is the agent. Since *jaritṛ* means "doer of praise", in the cited ṛk the word *jaritṛ* may also be *garitṛ*, or it may be the name of the ṛṣi. As a synonym of "praiser" the word is used in many places. Because the prayers of such excellent praisers all give fruit of the nature of truth, a belief arises; and the epithet *satyāḥ* is used.

***satyāḥ*** — "*satyaphalāḥ santaḥ*" ("being those whose fruits are true") — this explains the meaning. The word *satya* is used everywhere in the Ṛk-saṃhitā chiefly in a sense that shows the most excellent and the ethical (*naitika*) worthiness and power. The acts that persons of such excellent worthiness perform are of the nature of truth. The Nirukta-writers too, making this meaning clear, have given the derivation of the word *satya* in this way:

### Printed p. 534  (PDF 554)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 534.)*

> सत्यं कस्मात् सत्सु तायते सत्सु भवं भवतीति वा ।

> *satyaṃ kasmāt satsu tāyate satsu bhavaṃ bhavatīti vā |*

(Ni. 6-13 [?]) — "Why is it *satya*? It spreads (*tāyate*) among the good (*sat*); or, it is what exists among the good": so the Nirukta-writers' derivation. By this derivation the fruit of the nature of truth, too, must be obtained by good people; the idea that "to the truthful acts of good men belongs a fruit of the nature of the good" is suggested by the description of this ṛk. By this the following is shown: although, at the beginning, the power of a deity-reviler who follows the path of untruth may be much greater than that of a deity-devotee who follows the path of truth, in the end it dwindles of itself; and the strengths of the deity-devotee grow, and that growth is the fruit of his truthful life. Thus, since in this place the word *satya* is used also in the sense of *karma*-observance, in these two contexts too it must be explained what principle of the universe this idea reflects.

> ते देवा उत्सृज्यानृतम् । सत्यमुन्नाले [?] भिरे ।

> *te devā utsṛjyānṛtam | satyamunnāle [?] bhire |*

(Śa. Brā. 9-5-1-13 [?])

> तद्यत्तत्सत्यम् । त्रयी सा विद्या ते देवा अब्रुवन् यज्ञं कृत्वेदं सत्यं तनवामहा इति ॥

> *tadyattatsatyam | trayī sā vidyā te devā abruvan yajñaṃ kṛtvedaṃ satyaṃ tanavāmahā iti ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 9-5-1-18 [?]) — the deities gave up untruth and firmly took support in truth. *Trayī* — the three Vedas — are of the nature of truth; therefore, by performing the rites enjoined in the Veda the deities wished to spread the truth. Thus, besides showing the relation of a bond between truth and conduct, it is wished that, with acts of such purity, the one who is fulfilled in them and endowed with all wealth may obtain the highest good.

> नाभिर्ऋतस्य सप्रथाः इति । सत्यं वा ऋतं वा ऋतं सत्यस्य नाभिः सप्रथा इत्येवैतदाह स नो विश्वायुः सप्रथा इति स नः सर्वायुः इत्येवैतदाह ।

> *nābhirṛtasya saprathāḥ iti | satyaṃ vā ṛtaṃ vā ṛtaṃ satyasya nābhiḥ saprathā ityevaitadāha sa no viśvāyuḥ saprathā iti sa naḥ sarvāyuḥ ityevaitadāha |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-3-1-14 [?]) — by such explanations the identity of the universal rule and truth is shown; and, by following such truth and by performing truthful acts, it is shown that a full life is obtained as fruit; and the relation of cause and effect between the fruit of truth and the act of truth is made known.

Since, along with the performance of acts of the nature of truth, the universal rule, and the nature of the deities who are its cause, have to be known, and since that knowledge is essential and can be had only through truth, this has also been explained in detail in many contexts.

### Printed p. 535  (PDF 555)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 535.)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

> सखा ह यत्र सखिभिर्नवग्वैरभिज्ञ्वा सत्वभिर्गा अनुग्मन् ।
> सत्यं तदिन्द्रो दशभिर्दशग्वैः सूर्यं विवेद तमसि क्षियन्तम् ॥

> *sakhā ha yatra sakhibhirnavagvairabhijñvā satvabhirgā anugman |*
> *satyaṃ tadindro daśabhirdaśagvaiḥ sūryaṃ viveda tamasi kṣiyantam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-39-5 [?])

> ते इद्देवानां सधमाद आसन्नृतावानः कवयः पूर्व्यासः ।
> गूळ्हं ज्योतिः पितरो अन्वविन्दन्त्सत्यमन्त्रा अजनयन्नुषासम् ॥

> *te iddevānāṃ sadhamāda āsannṛtāvānaḥ kavayaḥ pūrvyāsaḥ |*
> *gūḷhaṃ jyotiḥ pitaro anvavindantsatyamantrā ajanayannuṣāsam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-76-4 [?]) — in these and other ṛks there are many sentences that hint at earlier contexts: that all the ṛṣis, having known the true forms of the deities who are of the nature of truth, performed rites, and obtained prosperity as the fruit of what they performed. And, together with truth, there is also a prayer for well-being:

> अधा यथा नः पितरः परासः प्रत्नासो अग्न ऋतमाशुषाणाः ।
> शुचीदयन्दीधितिमुक्थशासः क्षामा भिन्दन्तो अरुणीरप व्रन् ॥

> *adhā yathā naḥ pitaraḥ parāsaḥ pratnāso agna ṛtamāśuṣāṇāḥ |*
> *śucīdayandīdhitimukthaśāsaḥ kṣāmā bhindanto aruṇīrapa vran ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-16 [?]) — in prayers such as "as our fathers obtained good fruits through the conduct of sacrifices, which are of the nature of truth, so may all our acts too give fruits that are true", the true form of the deities of *satyadharma* such as Agni is also described.

> अजो न क्षां दाधार पृथिवीं तस्तम्भ द्यां मन्त्रेभिः सत्यैः ।

> *ajo na kṣāṃ dādhāra pṛthivīṃ tastambha dyāṃ mantrebhiḥ satyaiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-67-3 [?])

> कविमग्निमुपस्तुहि सत्यधर्माणमध्वरे । देवममीवचातनम् ॥

> *kavimagnimupastuhi satyadharmāṇamadhvare | devamamīvacātanam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-7 [?])

> देवो न यः सविता सत्यमन्मा क्रत्वा निपाति वृजनानि विश्वा ।
> पुरुप्रशस्तो अमतिर्न सत्य आत्मेव शेवो दिधिषाय्यो भूत् ॥

> *devo na yaḥ savitā satyamanmā kratvā nipāti vṛjanāni viśvā |*
> *purupraśasto amatirna satya ātmeva śevo didhiṣāyyo bhūt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-73-2 [?]) — in many other places too it is shown that Agni and the other deities, by truth, upheld the earth and the other worlds, carried out the protection of the worlds, and that men also must follow this path of truth. The derivation of the word *satya* as given in the Brāhmaṇas, the Upaniṣads and others, and how the whole world is of the nature of truth, and the description of the true form which, in opposition, rejects the untrue, will be told later in the special topics of Ṛk 1-185-11 [?].

***vipanyāmahe*** — for this word the scholar Monier Williams, in his English–Sanskrit Dictionary [as printed], gives the meaning "To pride one's self or to boast", citing the ṛk at hand, 1-180-7. The word *vipanyu* is read among the names of the "intelligent" along with *vipraḥ*, *vigraḥ* and others (Ni. 3-19 [?]).

### Printed p. 536  (PDF 556)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 536.)*

— in the Ṛk-saṃhitā this word is used in the sense of stotṛs who are intelligent and devout: *tad viprāso vipanyavaḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-20 [?]); *avasā vipanyavaḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-102-5 [?]); *vipanyavo dīdhyato manīṣā* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-20-1 [?]) — in all these ṛks it is understood as "those who praise in a special way", i.e. those who praise exceedingly. In the ṛk at hand the sacrificer speaks of praising the Aśvin deities. If the meaning of the Dictionary is followed, here the sacrificer says it by pride, in order to show his devotion to excess, and the excellence of his praise, that he boasts.

***paṇiḥ*** — for the word *paṇi* Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "*vyayāsahiṣṇavo vaṇijaḥ*" ("the traders, the *vaiśyas*, who cannot bear to spend") in many places; and he cites also the opinion of Yāska: "*paṇir vaṇig bhavatīti yāskaḥ*" ("Yāska says *paṇi* is a trader"). The Nirukta-writers, explaining the meaning of this word, in citing

> इन्द्रो विश्वान्बेकनाटाँ अहर्दृश उत क्रत्वा पणीँरभि ।

> *indro viśvānbekanāṭā~ ahardṛśa uta kratvā paṇī~rabhi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-66-10 [?]) — have given, for the word *paṇi* there, the sense "*vaṇijaḥ*", those who carry on trade (Ni. 6-26 [?]); and "*paṇiḥ paṇanād vaṇik paṇyaṃ nenekti*" (Ni. 2-17 [?]) — because he trades, the *vaiśya* has the name *paṇi*; and this trader, they explain, always keeps his goods clean, fit for trade. Besides this, in some places Sāyaṇa has explained this word as "*paṇayaḥ iti lubdhakāḥ abudhyamānā yāgādīn akurvāṇā adānaśīlā asmacchatravaḥ*" — "the *paṇis*, the greedy, ignorant, not performing sacrifices and the like, not given to giving, our enemies". In the ṛk at hand two kinds of meaning are shown possible for this word. First, "*paṇādhāro droṇakalaśaḥ*" — the *droṇa*-vessel, which holds the Soma; or second, "*paṇir vaṇig lubdho 'yaṣvā hitavān niyatadhano dhanāḍhyo 'sya yaṣvā*" — a trader, greedy, not sacrificing, of fixed wealth, wealthy, "one who sacrifices to him [?]". The use of the word as a synonym of the *droṇakalaśa* is irregular. In most contexts the meanings are "one without rites", or "Asura". A race of Asuras called *paṇis* is mentioned in the second part of the Ṛk-saṃhitā [as read [?]].

Sāyaṇa has given a story concerning the Asuras called *Paṇis*. The Asuras named Paṇi stole cows from the world of the deities and kept them hidden in a mountain cave. To find them, Indra sent the divine bitch (the female dog of the world of the gods) named Saramā. That bitch went to the Paṇis, brought them under her power with attractive words, and helped to bring the cows back. In this connection the conversation that took place between the Paṇis and Saramā …

---

### Printed p. 537  (PDF 557)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 537.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … the Paṇis, Saramā shows her cleverness of intelligence. And since, by this conversation, the nature of the Paṇis is also understood to some extent, it is briefly cited here (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-108 [?]). Here the Paṇis first question Saramā:

> किमिच्छन्ती सरमा प्रेदमानड्दूरे ह्यध्वा जगुरिः पराचैः ।
> कास्मेहितिः का परितक्म्यासीत्कथं रसाया अतरः पयांसि ॥

> *kimicchantī saramā predamānaḍdūre hyadhvā jaguriḥ parācaiḥ |*
> *kāsmehitiḥ kā paritakmyāsītkathaṃ rasāyā ataraḥ payāṃsi ‖*

— "O Saramā, what do you wish for, that you have come so far, over a path that is hard to cross? What was your purpose? How did you cross the waters of the river Rasā?" When they thus ask her, how it became possible for her to cross the stream of the river Rasā, Saramā replies with cleverness:

> इन्द्रस्य दूतीरिषिता चरामि मह इच्छन्ती पणयो निधीन्वः ।
> अतिष्कदो भियसा तन्न आवत्तथा रसाया अतरं पयांसि ॥

> *indrasya dūtīriṣitā carāmi maha icchantī paṇayo nidhīnvaḥ |*
> *atiṣkado bhiyasā tanna āvattathā rasāyā ataraṃ payāṃsi ‖*

— "O Paṇis, wishing for your treasure, I have come here as the messenger of Indra; therefore the power came to me to cross the stream of Rasā." Then:

> कीदृङ्ङिन्द्रः सरमे का दृशीका यस्येदं दूतीरसरः पराकात् ।
> आ च गच्छान्मित्रमेना दधामाथा गवां गोपतिर्नो भवाति ॥

> *kīdṛṅṅindraḥ sarame kā dṛśīkā yasyedaṃ dūtīrasaraḥ parākāt |*
> *ā ca gacchānmitramenā dadhāmāthā gavāṃ gopatirno bhavāti ‖*

— "O Saramā, who is that Indra, and what is he like? Let him come here; we shall make him a friend, and let him be the keeper of our cows." So they answered, and she said:

> नाहं तं वेद दभ्यं दभत्स यस्येदं दूतीरसरं पराकात् ।
> न तं गूहन्ति स्रवतो गभीरा हता इन्द्रेण पणयः शयध्वे ॥

> *nāhaṃ taṃ veda dabhyaṃ dabhatsa yasyedaṃ dūtīrasaraṃ parākāt |*
> *na taṃ gūhanti sravato gabhīrā hatā indreṇa paṇayaḥ śayadhve ‖*

— "O Paṇis, there is none among you who is able to conquer Indra. Be the stream however deep, he is not stopped. O Paṇis, you will lie smitten by him." To that they:

> इमा गावः सरमे या ऐच्छः परि दिवो अन्तान्त्सुभगे पतन्ती ।
> कस्त एना अव सृजादयुध्वी उतास्माकमायुधा सन्ति तिग्मा ॥

> *imā gāvaḥ sarame yā aicchaḥ pari divo antāntsubhage patantī |*
> *kasta enā ava sṛjādayudhvī utāsmākamāyudhā santi tigmā ‖*

— "O Saramā, here are the cows, they range through all the regions of the intermediate region. Who can give them up without fighting? Our weapons are very sharp. No one can take these cows from us." Then:

> असेन्या वः पणयो वचांस्यनिषव्यास्तन्वः सन्तु पापीः ।
> अधृष्टो व एतवा अस्तु पन्था बृहस्पतिर्व उभया न मृळात् ॥

> *asenyā vaḥ paṇayo vacāṃsyaniṣavyāstanvaḥ santu pāpīḥ |*
> *adhṛṣṭo va etavā astu panthā bṛhaspatirva ubhayā na mṛḷāt ‖*

— "O Paṇis, however strong your army, Bṛhaspati, impelled by Indra, will not spare you," she warned. Then they:

### Printed p. 538  (PDF 558)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 538.)*

> अयं निधिः सरमे अद्रिबुध्नो गोभिरश्वेभिर्वसुभिर्न्यृष्टः ।
> रक्षन्ति तं पणयो ये सुगोपा रेकु पदमलकमा जगन्थ ॥

> *ayaṃ nidhiḥ sarame adribudhno gobhiraśvebhirvasubhirnyṛṣṭaḥ |*
> *rakṣanti taṃ paṇayo ye sugopā reku padamalakamā jagantha ‖*

— "O Saramā, we guard with courage our treasure. Your coming here is in vain." So they spoke, in pride. Afterwards Saramā, showing her cleverness of intelligence, helped Indra to plunder them: so it is told. To show the true nature of the Asuras called *Paṇi*, and in what way they gave trouble to the deities and sacrificers, that part of the story has been briefly told.

In the ṛk at hand, for the word *paṇi*, the two kinds of meaning stated have been told above.

***vṛṣaṇau*** — of the two roots *vṛṣu secane* and *vṛṣa śaktibandhane* — the root *vṛṣa* that gives the sense "to sprinkle, to rain", and the second root that gives the sense of "power and capacity" — it has been told earlier at length that the words *vṛṣan*, *vṛṣaṇā*, *vṛṣṇyebhiḥ* and the like are formed, and that the meaning has to be given in keeping with these words. In the ṛk at hand, this epithet is used to praise the Aśvin deities as "showerers of desires".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***vipanyāmahe*** — root *pana stutau*; *laṭ*, first person plural, the ending *mahiṅ*; *e* for the *ṭi*; by *vyatyaya* the *śyan* *vikaraṇa*; by "*hi ca*" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34 [?]) the *nighāta* accent is prohibited.
- ***hitavān*** — by "*dadhāter hiḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-4-42 [?]) *hi* is substituted for the root *dhā* when the suffix *kta* follows; after *kta*, *matup*; by "*mādupadhāyāś ca…*" (Pā. Sū. 8-2-9 [?]) *va* for the *m*; since *matup* is *anudātta*, the *kta* suffix accent remains.
- ***adha*** — by "*nipātasya ca*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136 [?]) lengthening in the Saṃhitā.
- ***anindyā*** — root *nidi kutsāyām*; the suffix *yat*; since it has *i* as marker, the *num* augment for the root; a *naña*-*tatpuruṣa* compound; the vocative dual following, by "*supāṃ sulak…*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) *ā* is substituted for it; being in the vocative, the *nighāta* accent occurs.

### Printed p. 539  (PDF 559)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 539.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, continued)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***pāthaḥ*** — root *pā pānे*; *laṭ*, second person dual, the ending *thas*; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" elision of the *vikaraṇa*; therefore the *pibādeśa* does not occur for the root; by "*hi ca*" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34 [?]) the *nighāta* accent is prohibited, so the suffix accent remains.
- ***vi*** — this is an *upasarga*; by "*upasargaḥ kriyāyoge*" the suitable verb has to be supplied here, and the construction is made. ‖ 7 ‖

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 8**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> युवां चिद्धि ष्माश्विनावनु द्यून्विरुद्रस्य प्रस्रवणस्य सातौ ।
> अगस्त्यो नरां नृषु प्रशस्तः कारादिव चितयत्सहस्रैः ॥ ८ ॥ [as read: *kārādhunīva* in the bhāṣya, *kārādiva* in the Saṃhitā [?]]

**Pada-pāṭha**

> युवाम् । चित् । हि । स्म । अश्विना । अनु । द्यून् । विरुद्रस्य । प्रऽस्रवणस्य । सातौ ।
> अगस्त्यः । नराम् । नृषु । प्रऽशस्तः । काराधुनीऽइव । चितयत् । सहस्रैः ॥ ८ ॥

> *yuvām | cit | hi | sma | aśvinā | anu | dyūn | virudrasya | pra 'sravaṇasya | sātau |*
> *agastyaḥ | narām | nṛṣu | pra 'śastaḥ | kārādhunī 'iva | citayat | sahasraiḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

### Printed p. 540  (PDF 560)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 540.)*

*(The Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of this Ṛk 8 is printed on p. 539 in the lower part of the page, as follows.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ युवां चिद्धि ष्मेति त्रयः पूरणाः । अनु द्यून् प्रतिदिनं विरुद्रस्य विशिष्टोष्णरूपदुःखद्रावणस्य विविधरोरूयमाणवतो वा प्रस्रवणस्य वृष्ट्युदकसंस्राव्ययस्य सातौ लाभे निमित्तभूते सत्यगस्त्य एतन्नामा महर्षिर्नरां नेतॄणां कर्मनिर्वाहकानां मनुष्याणां नृषु येषु ताद्दृशा मनुष्याः सन्ति तेषु प्रशस्तः प्रशस्यतरोऽयं सहस्रैरपरिमितैः स्तोत्रैः क्षिति तयत् [?] । चेतयति । स्तुत्या प्रबोधयति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । कारा धुनीव । कारा शब्दः । तस्य धूनयितोत्पादयिता शङ्खादिः । स इव । यद्वा । एतदप्यगस्त्यस्य विशेषणम् । कारः शब्दयिता होत्रादिः । तस्य धुनिः कम्पयिता प्रेरक इव । इवेति सम्प्रत्यर्थे । "अस्त्युपमार्थस्य सम्प्रत्यर्थे प्रयोगः" इति निरुक्तम् । २-३१ [?] ॥ [as read; a few words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* Agastya, most praised among the leaders of men, rouses the Aśvins daily with thousands of hymns, as a conch sounds, to obtain the cooling rain-flow.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he* **Aśvinau**) — O Aśvins; **narām** — of the leaders who carry out rites; **nṛṣu** — among men; **praśastaḥ** — highly praiseworthy (the foremost); [**kārādhunīva** — like the impeller of the sound-makers, the priests such as the *hotṛ*]; **Agastyaḥ** — the great ṛṣi Agastya; **virudrasya** — of the sun-like heat that causes pain; **prasravaṇasya** — of the flow of rain-water; **sātau** — for obtaining; **anu dyūn** — every day; **sahasraiḥ** — with countless *stotras*; **kārādhunīva** — like an instrument of sound such as the conch; **yuvām** — you two; **citayat** — awakens (by praise); (**cit hi sma** — sentence-fillers).

**Bhāvārtha**

O Aśvins! The great ṛṣi Agastya, the most renowned among those who carry out rites, every day, with countless *stotras*, like the sound of a conch and the like, awakens you (by praise, as if rousing you), to obtain rain-water that removes the pain of heat.

**Printed English**

> Ashwins, Agastya, eminent amongst the leaders of men, arouses you daily with numerous (invocations), like an instrument of sound, for the sake of obtaining a manifold (flow) of a torrent (of rain).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk there is a prayer of Agastya addressed to the Aśvin deities. Here the ṛṣi compares his own praise to the sound of the conch, and, by showing the simile *kārādhunīva*, he praises the excellence of his own praise.

***kārādhunīva*** — "*kārā śabdaḥ | tasya dhūnayitā utpādayitā śaṃkhādiḥ | sa eva | yadvā | etad api agastyasya viśeṣaṇam | kāraḥ śabdayitā hotrādiḥ | tasya dhuniḥ kaṃpayitā preraka iva | iveti saṃpratyarthe | 'astyupamārthasya saṃpratyarthe prayogaḥ'*" (Ni. 2-10 [?]) — so Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning of this word. According to this explanation two meanings are possible for the word *kārādhunī*. First, *kāra* is "sound" (*śabda*); the conch and the like, which shake it out and produce it, are *kārādhunī*; second, the *hotṛ* and others, who are the makers of sound in the form of praise, meaning the one who impels them. Earlier:

> ईळे द्यावापृथिवी पूर्वचित्तयेऽग्निं घर्मं सुरुचं यामन्निष्टये ।
> याभिर्भरे कारमंशाय जिन्वथस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतम् ॥

> *īḷe dyāvāpṛthivī pūrvacittaye 'gniṃ gharmaṃ surucaṃ yāmanniṣṭaye |*
> *yābhirbhare kāramaṃśāya jinvathastābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gatam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-1 [?]) — in this ṛk, in showing the meaning of the word *kāra*, Sāyaṇa says "*kāraśabdaḥ śaṅkhavāci ity abhiyuktāḥ saṃgirante | kāraṃ śabdakāriṇaṃ śaṅkham*" — "the learned say that the word *kāra* denotes the conch; *kāra* is the conch that makes sound". To support this very meaning, Skandasvāmin cites the ṛk at hand (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-180-8). In both places the meaning is "conch" …

---

### Printed p. 541  (PDF 561)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 541.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — … "conch" is the meaning stated. But the word *kāra* does not mean "conch" in all places. This word, formed from the root *kṛ*, gives merely the sense "a means of producing sound". In some places it may denote the conch; in others it may give another meaning. For example:

> चकर्थ कारमेभ्यः पृतनासु प्रवन्तवे ।

> *cakartha kāramebhyaḥ pṛtanāsu pravantave |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-131-5 [?]) — in this ṛk the word is explained as merely *siṃhanādalakṣaṇaṃ śabdam*, "a sound in the form of a lion's roar". Thus, to show that it is not invariably the conch, Skandasvāmin too has said, "*kriyata iti kāraśabdaḥ*" — "the word *kāra* here gives only the meaning of what is done", and also "*sāmarthyāt śaṅkhaḥ*" ("by capacity, the conch").

> पश्यन्त्यासो अभि कारमर्चन्ति ज्योतिश्च कृपन्ते धीभिः ।

> *paśyantyāso abhi kāramarcanti jyotiśca kṛpante dhībhiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-101-14 [?], as read [?]) — in such ṛks everywhere *kāra* has merely the sense of "doer" (*kartā*). It is for that reason that Sāyaṇa too, in the ṛk at hand, has given two explanations: first, "like the conch", and second, "the *hotṛ*, the impeller of sound". Here, for the word *iva*, in the second explanation the question what its sense is can be resolved, and he himself has given the resolution: "*astyupamārthasya saṃpratyarthe prayogaḥ*" (Ni. 2-31 [?]), according to the statement of the Nirukta-writers — *iva* means *saṃprati* ("now"). In the present context it means "now".

***virudrasya*** — this word is an epithet of *prasravaṇasya*. *Prasravaṇa* means a mass of rain-water, or a full flow. Since this full flow destroys the pain in the form of heat, or since it flows, making manifold sounds, it has the epithet *virudra*. For this word Sāyaṇa has given the explanation "*viśiṣṭoṣṇarūpaduḥkhadrāvaṇasya, vividharorūyamāṇadravaṇavato vā*". For the word *rut* the meaning "pain" is given; if *prasravaṇa* is taken to mean "that which destroys a special pain", or "that which flows with manifold sounds", it comes to mean "endowed with manifold roaring". The Nirukta-writers' derivation of the word *rudra* is as follows:

> रुद्रो रौतीति सतः । रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा । रोदयतेर्वा । "यदरुदत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वम्" इति काठकम् । "यदरोदीत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वम्" इति हारिद्रविकम् ।

> *rudro rautīti sataḥ | rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā | rodayatervā | "yadarudattadrudrasya rudratvam" iti kāṭhakam | "yadarodīttadrudrasya rudratvam" iti hāridravikam |*

(Ni. 10-5 [?])

### Printed p. 542  (PDF 562)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 542.)*

— *rudra* means "*rauti*" ("he cries, he makes the sound of thunder"): one who makes a sound like the cloud's thunder; or "*rorūyamāṇo dravati*": one who runs swiftly, thundering; or "*rodayati*": one who makes enemies weep; so the meanings come out. Following this explanation, the meaning of the word *virudra* has been stated for the ṛk at hand; the remaining explanation is not relevant to us at present. According to the first derivation, the meaning is "destruction of pain"; therefore the full flow is *virudra*. According to the second derivation, the meaning is "of the nature of thunder"; therefore also the full flow is *virudra*. Thus in the present context both meanings are natural.

***narāṃ nṛṣu praśastaḥ*** — "Among the leaders who carry out the sacrifice, the one supremely praiseworthy": Agastya has praised himself. Even though this is self-praise, here the ṛṣi has spoken of his own true greatness; there is no exaggeration in it.

> अगस्त्यः खनमानः खनित्रैः प्रजामपत्यं बलमिच्छमानः ।
> उभौ वर्णावृषिरुग्रः पुपोष सत्या देवेष्वाशिषो जगाम ॥

> *agastyaḥ khanamānaḥ khanitraiḥ prajāmapatyaṃ balamicchamānaḥ |*
> *ubhau varṇāvṛṣirugraḥ pupoṣa satyā deveṣvāśiṣo jagāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-179-6) — in explaining the purport of this ṛk it has been told how Agastya accomplished, by his great power, both the *puruṣārthas* called *dharma* and *kāma*; and what his extraordinary greatness is has been explained in detail. Therefore it can be said that in this praise there is no kind of exaggeration.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***virudrasya*** — *vividhāḥ rudrāḥ yasmin tasya*; by "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 [?]) the fore-member keeps its natural accent.
- ***prasravaṇasya*** — root *sru gatau*; the suffix *lyuṭ*; by "*yuvor anākau*" *ana* is substituted for it; since the suffix has the marker *l*, by "*liti*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 [?]) the syllable before the suffix takes the *udātta* accent; in the *prādi* compound the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent.
- ***sātau*** — by "*ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca*" (Pā. Sū. 3-3-97 [?]) *ktin* with *udātta* is irregularly formed.
- ***narām*** — genitive plural; by "*sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 [?]) the case-ending takes the *udātta* accent.

### Printed p. 543  (PDF 563)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 543.)*

- ***praśastaḥ*** — root *śaṃsu stutau*; the suffix *kta*; by "*anuditāṃ hala…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37 [?]) elision of the penultimate nasal; by "*gatir anantaraḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49 [?]) the *gati* (*pra*) takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***citayat*** — root *citī saṃjñāne*; after the causative stem, *leṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; elision of the *i*; the *aṭ* augment; by the statement "*saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ*", since *ṇic* is the cause, *guṇa* does not occur for the short penultimate vowel of the root; since *śap* is the cause, *guṇa* for *ṇic* and the *ay* substitution; being in an *atiṅanta* word-position, the *nighāta* accent occurs. ‖ 8 ‖

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 9**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> प्र यद्वहेथे महिना रथस्य प्र स्यन्द्रा याथो मनुषो न होता ।
> धत्तं सूरिभ्य उत वा स्वश्व्यं नासत्या रयिषाचः स्याम ॥ ९ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> प्र । यत् । वहेथे इति । महिना । रथस्य । प्र । स्यन्द्रा । याथः । मनुषः । न । होता ।
> धत्तम् । सूरिऽभ्यः । उत । वा । सुऽअश्व्यम् । नासत्या । रयिऽसाचः । स्याम ॥ ९ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ युवां रथस्य गमनसाधनस्य महिना महत्त्वेन यद्यस्मात्र [?] वहेथे धारयथो यज्ञम् । यद्वा । रथस्य स्वर्गगमनसाधनस्य यागस्य धुरं वहथः । तथा हे स्यन्द्रा स्यन्दनशीलौ युवां याथः । गच्छथः । स्वस्थानं यज्ञारम्भे आगच्छथः यज्ञसमाप्तौ पुनर्गच्छथश्च । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । मनुषो होता मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य होता यथा यज्ञप्रारम्भे आगच्छति कर्मणि निर्वृत्ते पुनरपगच्छति तद्वत् । आगमनसमये सूरिभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यो धत्तम् । धारयतं फलम् । उत वा स्वश्व्यं शोभनाश्वसमूहं धत्तम् । नासत्या । सत्सु भवौ सत्यौ । न असत्यौ नासत्यौ । हे ताद्दशौ त्वदनुग्रहाद्रयिषाचो धनसमवायिनः स्याम । भवेम ॥ [as read; a few words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* The Aśvins, by the greatness of their chariot (or of the sacrifice), come, bear the sacrifice, and depart like a priest after the rite; they bestow rewards and good horses; may we be enriched.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **nāsatyā** — O Nāsatyas (who are ever in truthful acts); **yat** — because; (**yuvām** — you two); **rathasya** — of (your chariot, the means of going); **mahinā** — by greatness; **pra vahethe** — you bear (support) the sacrifice; [or **mahinā** — by own greatness; **rathasya** — of the sacrifice, the means of going to heaven; **pra (vahethe)** — you bear the leadership;] (*he*) **syandrā** — O Aśvins whose nature is to glide, to go quickly; **manuṣaḥ hotā na** — like the *hotṛ* of the sacrificer (who comes at the beginning of the sacrifice and goes away after the rite); **yāthaḥ** — you go (after the sacrifice, to your own place); **sūribhyaḥ** — to the praisers (who have come for the sacrifice); **dhattam** — you bear the fruit (you favour); **uta svaśvyam vā** — or good horses (you favour); (**tat** — therefore) **rayiṣācaḥ** — endowed with wealth; **syāma** — may we be (by your favour).

### Printed p. 544  (PDF 564)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 544.)*

**Bhāvārtha**

O Nāsatyas, of gliding nature! By the greatness of your chariot you come to the sacrifice and, having carried out the sacrifice, you go away to your own place like a *hotṛ* priest after the rite; when you come to the sacrifice you bestow on the praisers excellent horses and the like; being such, favour us also with wealth and the like.

**Printed English**

> When, by the virtue of your chariot, you come (to the sacrifice), and when, like the ministering priest, (after discharging his function), you depart, gliding away, you give to the devout (worshippers a reward), though it be store of good horses: may we be enriched, Nasatyas, (by your favour,

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***rathasya*** — here the word *ratha* may mean the chariot of the Aśvin deities engaged in travelling; or, Sāyaṇa has explained, this word may be a synonym of the sacrifice (*yajña*), which is the means of going to heaven. "*rathaḥ raṃhater gatikarmaṇaḥ …*" and so on: the derivation of the Nirukta-writers has been told, and the special meanings of this word have been told earlier. "*rathaṃ raṃhaṇam ādityaṃ raṃhaṇaś cāsau muhūrte muhūrte asya nāvasthāyi syāt*" [as read [?]] — since the Āditya moves constantly, without rest for a moment, that name is explained, as already told. Formed from the root *raṃh*, which has the sense of motion, this word may also be used in the ṛk at hand as a synonym of the sacrifice, the means of going.

***rathasya mahinā pra vahethe*** — Sāyaṇa has shown that two kinds of construction are possible for this: first,

1. by the greatness of your chariot, which is the means of going, you bear the sacrifice; and second, …

### Printed p. 545  (PDF 565)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 545; signature mark "XIII 35".)*

**Special Topics (continued)**

2. … and, second, "by the greatness of the sacrifice you bear the leadership of the sacrifice, which is the means of going to heaven" — Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning of this sentence also. It may be seen that both these constructions have the authority of *śruti* sentences. That, according to the first construction, the help of the Aśvin deities is absolutely essential both for the performance of the sacrifice and for its leadership, is known from the following Ṛk-saṃhitā sentences:

> जुष्टो हि दूतो असि हव्यवाहनोऽग्ने रथीरध्वराणाम् ।
> सजूरश्विभ्यामुषसा सुवीर्यमस्मे धेहि श्रवो बृहत् ॥

> *juṣṭo hi dūto asi havyavāhano 'gne rathīradhvarāṇām |*
> *sajūraśvibhyāmuṣasā suvīryamasme dhehi śravo bṛhat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-44-2 [?])

> सवितारमुषसमश्विना भगमग्निं व्युष्टिषु क्षपः ।
> कण्वासस्त्वा सुतसोमास इन्धते हव्यवाहं स्वध्वर ॥

> *savitāramuṣasamaśvinā bhagamagniṃ vyuṣṭiṣu kṣapaḥ |*
> *kaṇvāsastvā sutasomāsa indhate havyavāhaṃ svadhvara ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-44-8 [?]) — in these two ṛks, Agni, the carrier of oblations, the divine messenger and leader of the sacrifice, is called to perform the sacrifice, together with all the deities who are awake (*upabarbudha*). Even in the morning, Agni is described as bearing the sacrifice along with the Aśvin deities; so in the leadership of the sacrifice, the Aśvins' principal role is understood. Or, by the second construction, the idea that the sacrifice, if it is to be performed fully, must be protected by the Aśvin deities, and that it is impossible without their help, is shown, and the function of carrying out the sacrifice is praised. How was the sacrifice protected by the Aśvin deities? The context of the story, which tells in what way they made the sacrifice complete, and what principal part they played in this carrying out of the sacrifice, is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. In it the cutting off of the head of Viṣṇu, who is of the nature of the sacrifice, is described, and, since the Aśvin deities restored it, they bore the leadership of the sacrifice and played the principal part in its carrying out — so that story-context is told as follows:

> देवा ह वै सत्रं निषेदुः । अग्निरिन्द्रः सोमो मखो विष्णुर्विश्वे देवा अन्यत्रैवाश्विभ्याम् । तेषां कुरुक्षेत्रं देवयजनमास । तस्मादाहुः कुरुक्षेत्रं देवानां देवयजनमिति तस्माद्यत्र क्व च कुरुक्षेत्रस्य निगच्छति तदेव मन्यत इदं देवयजनमिति तद्धि देवानां देवयजनम् । त आसत । श्रियं गच्छेम यशः स्यामान्नादाः स्यामेति । तथो इवेमे सत्त्रमासते श्रियं गच्छेम यशः स्यामान्नादाः स्यामेति । ते होचुः । यो नः श्रमेण तपसा श्रद्धया यज्ञेनाहुतिभिर्यज्ञस्योदृचं पूर्वोऽवगच्छात्स नः श्रेष्ठोऽसत्तदु नः सर्वेषाꣳ सहेति तथेति । तद्विष्णुः प्रथमः प्राप । स देवानाꣳ श्रेष्ठोऽभवत्तस्मादाहुर्विष्णुर्देवानाꣳ श्रेष्ठ

> *devā ha vai satraṃ niṣeduḥ | agnirindraḥ somo makho viṣṇurviśve devā anyatraivāśvibhyām | teṣāṃ kurukṣetraṃ devayajanamāsa | tasmādāhuḥ kurukṣetraṃ devānāṃ devayajanamiti tasmādyatra kva ca kurukṣetrasya nigacchati tadeva manyata idaṃ devayajanamiti taddhi devānāṃ devayajanam | ta āsata | śriyaṃ gacchema yaśaḥ syāmānnādāḥ syāmeti | tatho iveme sattramāsate śriyaṃ gacchema yaśaḥ syāmānnādāḥ syāmeti | te hocuḥ | yo naḥ śrameṇa tapasā śraddhayā yajñenāhutibhiryajñasyodṛcaṃ pūrvo 'vagacchātsa naḥ śreṣṭho 'sattadu naḥ sarveṣām̐ saheti tatheti | tadviṣṇuḥ prathamaḥ prāpa | sa devānām̐ śreṣṭho 'bhavattasmādāhurviṣṇurdevānām̐ śreṣṭha*

> इति । स यः स विष्णुर्यज्ञः स स यः स यज्ञोऽसौ स आदित्यस्तद्धेदं यशो विष्णुर्न शशाक संयन्तुं तदिदमप्यैतर्हि नैव सर्व इव यशः शक्नोति संयन्तुम् । स त्रिधन्वमादायोपचक्राम । स धनुरात्न्यां शिर उपस्तभ्य तस्थौ तं देवा अनभिधृष्णुवन्तः समन्तं परिण्यविशन्त । ताहाहुर्वम्र्य ऊचुः । इमा वै वम्र्यो यदुपदीका योऽस्य ज्यामुप्यादभिक्ति [?] मस्मै प्रयच्छेतेत्यन्नाद्यमस्मै प्रयच्छेमापि धन्वन्न पोऽधिगच्छेत्रेथास्मै सर्वमन्नाद्यं प्रयच्छेमेति तथेति । तस्मोपरराः [?] सत्ये । ज्यामपिजक्षुस्तस्याः छिन्नायां धनुरात्न्यै विस्फुरन्त्यै विष्णोः शिरः प्रचिच्छिदतुः ॥

> *iti | sa yaḥ sa viṣṇuryajñaḥ sa sa yaḥ sa yajño 'sau sa ādityastaddhedaṃ yaśo viṣṇurna śaśāka saṃyantuṃ tadidamapyaitarhi naiva sarva iva yaśaḥ śaknoti saṃyantum | sa tridhanvamādāyopacakrāma | sa dhanurātnyāṃ śira upastabhya tasthau taṃ devā anabhidhṛṣṇuvantaḥ samantaṃ pariṇyaviśanta | tāhāhurvamrya ūcuḥ | imā vai vamryo yadupadīkā yo 'sya jyāmupyādabhikti [?] masmai prayacchetetyannādyamasmai prayacchemāpi dhanvanna po 'dhigacchetrethāsmai sarvamannādyaṃ prayacchemeti tatheti | tasmopararāḥ [?] satye | jyāmapijakṣustasyāḥ chinnāyāṃ dhanurātnyai visphurantyai viṣṇoḥ śiraḥ pracicchidatuḥ ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-1 to 9 [?]; as read, several words doubtful [?])

— Formerly, leaving out only the Aśvin deities, all the other deities — Indra, Viṣṇu, Soma and so on — together began a sacrificial session at Kurukṣetra, the divine sacrificial place, wishing to be glorious and to be eaters of food. Then they decided that whoever of them first completed the sacrifice with all its limbs, by toil, by faith and by oblations, was to be counted the best of all; and Viṣṇu was the first to obtain that best position. Having obtained such an excellent position, Viṣṇu himself became of the nature of the sacrifice (*yajñātman*). Then pride arose in him, and there was no one to restrain it. He took his wealth-bow with its three arrows and set out; all the deities, with no courage to oppose him, sat silent. Then there came the ants (*vamri*), insects of that kind, and asked the deities, "If we gnaw the bowstring and make him bend, what reward will you give us?" Such was their request. The deities gave them the promise: "We shall give you complete food, and you will find water wherever you seek it." Then the ants gnawed through the string, and, as the cut tip of the bow sprang upward, it cut off the head of Viṣṇu. The deities, knowing that, when the head of Viṣṇu, who is of the nature of the sacrifice, was cut off, the sacrifice had become void, thought; and the Aśvin deities joined together the severed head of Viṣṇu. Therefore it is shown that the carrying out of the sacrifice was not possible without the Aśvin deities. The same matter is told in this way in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka:

> देवा वै सत्रमासत । ऋद्धिपरिमितं यशस्कामाः । तेऽब्रुवन् । यन्नः प्रथमं यश ऋच्छात् । सर्वेषां नस्तत्सहासदिति । …… तेषां मुखं वैष्णवं यश आर्छत् । ………… तस्य सिस्मियाणस्य तेजोऽपाक्रामत् । …… वारे वृतꣳ ह्यासाम् । तस्य ज्यामप्यादन् । तस्य धनुर्विप्रवमाणꣳ शिर उदवर्तयत् । तद्द्यावापृथिवी अनु प्रावर्तेताम् । यत्प्रावर्तेताम् । तत् …

> *devā vai satramāsata | ṛddhiparimitaṃ yaśaskāmāḥ | te 'bruvan | yannaḥ prathamaṃ yaśa ṛcchāt | sarveṣāṃ nastatsahāsaditi | …… teṣāṃ mukhaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ yaśa ārchat | ………… tasya sismiyāṇasya tejo 'pākrāmat | …… vāre vṛtam̐ hyāsām | tasya jyāmapyādan | tasya dhanurvipravamāṇam̐ śira udavartayat | taddyāvāpṛthivī anu prāvartetām | yatprāvartetām | tat …*

(Tai. Ā. 5-1-[?]; as read, with elisions marked in the print by dots)

### Printed p. 547  (PDF 567)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 24"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 547.)*

> … प्रवर्ग्यस्य प्रवर्ग्यत्वम् । यद्घ्रां [?] इत्यपतत् । तद्घर्मस्य घर्मत्वम् । महतो वीर्यमपस्रदिति । तन्महावीरस्य वीरत्वम् । यदस्याः समभरन्त सम्राजः संसाम्राट्त्वम् [?] । तर्ग्स्तुतं [?] देवतास्त्रेधा व्यगृह्णत । अग्निः प्रातःसवनम् । इन्द्रो माध्यन्दिनꣳ सवनम् । विश्वेदेवास्तृतीयसवनम् । तेनापशीर्ष्णा यज्ञेन यजमानाः । नाशिषोऽवारुन्धत । न सुवर्गं लोकमभ्यजयन् । ते देवा अश्विनावब्रुवन् । भिषजौ वै स्थः । इदं यज्ञस्यैशिरः [?] प्रतिधत्तमिति । तावब्रूतां वरं वृणावहै । ग्रह एव नावत्रापि गृह्यतामिति । ताभ्यामेतमाश्विनमगृह्णन् । तावेतद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रत्यधत्ताम् । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । तेन सशीर्ष्णा यज्ञेन यजमानाः । आवाशिषोऽरुन्धत । …. अभि सुवर्गं लोकं जयति । तस्मादेष आश्विनप्रवयो इव । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः ॥

> *… pravargyasya pravargyatvam | yadghrāṃ [?] ityapatat | tadgharmasya gharmatvam | mahato vīryamapasraditi | tanmahāvīrasya vīratvam | yadasyāḥ samabharanta samrājaḥ saṃsāmrāṭtvam [?] | targstutaṃ [?] devatāstredhā vyagṛhṇata | agniḥ prātaḥsavanam | indro mādhyandinam̐ savanam | viśvedevāstṛtīyasavanam | tenāpaśīrṣṇā yajñena yajamānāḥ | nāśiṣo 'vārundhata | na suvargaṃ lokamabhyajayan | te devā aśvināvabruvan | bhiṣajau vai sthaḥ | idaṃ yajñasyaiśiraḥ [?] pratidhattamiti | tāvabrūtāṃ varaṃ vṛṇāvahai | graha eva nāvatrāpi gṛhyatāmiti | tābhyāmetamāśvinamagṛhṇan | tāvetadyajñasya śiraḥ pratyadhattām | yatpravargyaḥ | tena saśīrṣṇā yajñena yajamānāḥ | āvāśiṣo 'rundhata | …. abhi suvargaṃ lokaṃ jayati | tasmādeṣa āśvinapravayo iva | yatpravargyaḥ ‖*

(Tai. Ā. 5-1-1 to 6 [?]; as read, doubtful in places [?]) — after the head of Viṣṇu, who is of the nature of the sacrifice, had been cut off, as in the story quoted above from the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, the sacrificial body that remained was divided by the deities into three parts. Then Agni took the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*), Indra the midday pressing (*mādhyandina-savana*), and the Viśvedevas the third pressing. But by that sacrifice, which had no head, they could obtain neither prosperity nor the heavenly world. Then they said to the Aśvin deities, "You are the physicians of the deities; unite again this head of the sacrifice." They asked for a boon: "Let a cup (*graha*) be taken for us two here also." The deities agreed, and the Aśvins fixed the head of the sacrifice again; hence the *āśvina* cup is taken. Thus the Aśvins became the cause of the sacrifice and received a share of it.

> मधोः पिबतमश्विनेत्याश्विनावेवैतदाहाश्विनौ ह्येतद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रत्यधत्ताम् । तावेवैतत्प्रीणात्यवरꣳ स्वाहाकारं करोति ॥

> *madhoḥ pibatamaśvinetyāśvināvevaitadāhāśvinau hyetadyajñasya śiraḥ pratyadhattām | tāvevaitatprīṇātyavaram̐ svāhākāraṃ karoti ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 14-3-2-16 [?]) — in such sentences of the *śruti*, and in Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-9 [?], the same matter is told, and the greatness of the Aśvin deities is praised.

***syandrā*** — the word *syandra* is read among the names of motion (*gati*), of action (*karma*) and also of strength (*bala*) (Ni. 3-9 [?]). It describes the beauty of motion of the Aśvin deities. There are many mantras that describe their coming and its beauty. For example:

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 548.)*

> आ तेन यातं मनसो जवीयसा रथं यं वामृभवश्चक्रुरश्विना ।
> यस्य योगे दुहिता जायते दिव उभे अहनी सुदिने विवस्वतः ॥

> *ā tena yātaṃ manaso javīyasā rathaṃ yaṃ vāmṛbhavaścakruraśvinā |*
> *yasya yoge duhitā jāyate diva ubhe ahanī sudine vivasvataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-12 [?]) — in such ṛks it is said that, as the Aśvins sit in the chariot which the Ṛbhus have built for them alone and are ready to travel, at once the goddess Uṣas, who spreads beauty over the whole world, and the day and night arise. The causes of that beauty — the Aśvin deities — come, with a speed exceeding that of the mind, towards the sacrificial place; in this description the two qualities that are suggested by the word *syandrā* are also indicated.

***sūribhyaḥ*** — the meaning of this word is "the ṛṣis, poets and intelligent ones who possess the power of vision that grasps what lies beyond the senses". The special meanings of this word and the special uses of it have been told earlier in the special topics of the sixth ṛk of this same sūkta.

***nāsatyā*** — since the Aśvin deities have the synonyms *dasrā* and *nāsatyā*, it has also been told earlier which divine quality of theirs these words show.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***vahethe*** — root *vaha prāpaṇe*; *laṭ*, second person dual; because of *yad*-connection no *nighāta*; the suffix being *anudātta* by "*tāsyanudāttet…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 [?]), the root accent remains.
- ***syandrā*** — root *syandū prasravaṇe*; by the force of the statement "*bahulam*" the *Uṇādi* suffix *ran*; in the vocative dual, by "*supāṃ sulak…*" *ā* is substituted for the case-ending; being in the vocative, the *nighāta* accent occurs.
- ***yāthaḥ*** — root *yā prāpaṇe*; *laṭ*, second person dual; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***dhattam*** — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *loṭ*, second person dual; being in *pādādi* position, no *nighāta*; by the suffix accent the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***svaśvyam*** — *śobhanānām aśvānāṃ samūhaḥ svaśvyam*; the suffix *yat* in the sense of "collection"; by "*yato 'nāvaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-213 [?]) the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***nāsatyā*** — by "*supāṃ sulak…*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) *ā* for the dual of the vocative; being in *pādādi* position, the vocative *nighāta* does not occur; by "*āmantritasya ca*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198 [?]) the *ādyudātta* accent.

**Sūkta 180, Ṛk 10**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> तं वां रथं वयमद्या हुवेम स्तोमैरश्विना सुविताय नव्यम् ।
> अरिष्टनेमिं परि द्यामियानं विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ १० ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> तम् । वाम् । रथम् । वयम् । अद्य । हुवेम । स्तोमैः । अश्विना । सुवितायै । नव्यम् ।
> अरिष्टऽनेमिम् । परि । द्याम् । इयानम् । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥ १० ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विना हे अश्विनौ वां युवयोः सम्बन्धिनं शीघ्रगमनेन स्तुत्यं रथं वयमगस्त्याद्या [?] अस्मिन्स्तुत्येऽहनि हुवेम । ह्वयेम । केन साधनेनेति उच्यते । स्तोमैः स्तोत्रैः । किमर्थम् । सुवितायै सुष्ठु प्राप्तये । कीदृशम् । नव्यं स्तुत्यं नूतनं वा तथारिष्टनेमिमहिंसितचक्रवलयं द्यां परीयानं द्युलोकस्य परितो गच्छन्तम् । विद्यामेत्यादि गतम् ॥

*Gist:* We call today, with hymns, the new, unobstructed chariot of the Aśvins that circles the sky, that we may obtain food, strength and long life.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **Aśvinā** — O Aśvins; **navyam** — new, or praiseworthy; **ariṣṭanemim** — with unharmed wheel-rim (of unobstructed motion); **dyām pari** — round the sky; **iyānam** — going; **vām** — your; **tam** — that well-known; **ratham** — chariot; **suvitāyai** — for obtaining good things; **stomaiḥ** — with hymns; **adya** — today; **vayam** — we; **huvema** — call; **iṣam** — food; **vṛjanam** — strength; **jīradānum** — long life; **vidyāma** — (by your favour we) obtain.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Aśvins! Your well-known chariot, new, of unobstructed motion, going round the sky, we call today with hymns, in order to obtain good things. Grant us food, strength and long life.

### Printed p. 550  (PDF 570)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 180"; page 550.)*

**Printed English**

> We invoke to-day, Ashwins, with hymns, for the sake of good things, your praiseworthy chariot of undamaged wheels, and traversing the sky, that we may obtain (from it) food, strength, and long iife [sic].

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***suvitāyai*** — "*suṣṭhu prāptaye*" — "for good obtaining": the meaning is "for the sake of obtaining the best". For this word, in some places, "*suṣṭhu gantavyāya yajñāya*" ("for the sacrifice that is to be well gone to") and, in others, "*sugamanāya*" ("for easy going") are given as meanings; the purport of all of them is one.

***navyam, ariṣṭanemim*** — these words are epithets of the chariot of the Aśvin deities; they show the speciality of the chariot. The greatness of this chariot will be told in the later sūktas.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***adya*** — by "*nipātasya ca*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136 [?]) lengthening in the Saṃhitā.
- ***huvema*** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *liṅ*, first person plural; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" *saṃprasāraṇa* of the root; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***suvitāyai*** — root *iṇ gatau*; the suffix *niṣṭhā* in the passive; by the statement "*tenvādīnāṃ chandasi bahulam upasaṃkhyānam*" the *u* of *su* gets the *uvaṅ* substitution; by "*sūpamānāt ktaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-144 [?]) the final syllable of the hind-member is *udātta*; dative singular.
- ***ariṣṭanemim*** — a *bahuvrīhi* compound; by "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 [?]) the fore-member keeps its natural accent.
- ***iyānam*** — root *īja gatau*; "*chandasi liṭ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-105 [?]): *liṭ* comes, and by "*liṭaḥ kānaj vā*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-106 [?]) *kānac* is substituted; by "*aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-77 [?]) the *iyaṅ* substitution; by the statement "*dvirvacanaprakaraṇe chandasi vety vaktavyam*" the reduplication and the like do not occur; by "*citaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 [?]) the final syllable is *udātta*. ‖ 10 ‖

Here ends the 180th Sūkta. (*iḷḷige nūra eṃbhattaneya sūkta mugidudu.*)
