## Sūkta 181 (the 181st Sūkta; "Nūra eṃbhattoṃdaneya sūktavu")

> कदु प्रेष्ठाविति नवर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभमाश्विनम् । कदु नवेत्यानुक्रान्तम् ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्विनियोगः पूर्वसूक्त एवोक्तः ॥

*Translation of the introduction:* This sūkta beginning "*kadu preṣṭhau*" is the second sūkta in the twenty-fourth Anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. Its ṛṣi is Agastya; the Aśvin deities are the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā says "*kadu nava*" (as read). The application, for the Triṣṭubh ṛks, at the time of the Prātaranuvāka mantra recital and the Aśvina-śastra, was told in the preceding sūkta itself.

**Sūkta 181**

Maṇḍala 1 ‖ Anuvāka 24 ‖ Sūkta 181 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 4 ‖ Varga 25, 26 ‖
Number of ṛks in the Sūkta — 9 ‖
Ṛṣi — Agastya ‖ Devatā — Aśvinau ‖ Chandas — Triṣṭubh ‖

**Sūkta 181, Ṛk 1**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> कदु प्रेष्ठाविषां रयीणामध्वर्यन्ता यदुन्निनीथो अपाम् ।
> अयं वां यज्ञो अकृत प्रशस्तिं वसुधिती अवितारा जनानाम् ॥ १ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> कत् । ऊँ इति । प्रेष्ठौ । इषाम् । रयीणाम् । अध्वर्यन्ता । यत् । उत्ऽनिनीथः । अपाम् ।
> अयम् । वाम् । यज्ञः । अकृत । प्रऽशस्तिम् । वसुधिती इति वसुऽधिती । अवितारा । जनानाम् ॥ १ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ प्रेष्ठौ प्रियतमौ वां युवां कदु कदा भविष्यति इषामिष्यमाणानामन्नानां रयीणां धनानाम् ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठ्यौ ॥ अन्नानि धनानि चोन्निनीथः ऊर्ध्वं प्रापयेथः । अध्वर्यन्ताध्वरं पारयितुमिच्छन्तौ युवानुषां [?] वृष्ट्युदकानां वृष्ट्युदकानि चोन्निनीथः उत्कृष्टमुधः [?] प्रापयेथ इति यत्तत्कदा । कस्मादेवमुच्यते इति उच्यते । अयं यज्ञोऽस्माभिरनुष्ठीयमानो वां युवयोरेव प्रशस्तिं प्रशंसां स्तुतिमकृत करोति । यज्ञे शंसनीयानि शस्त्राणि युवानेव प्रशंसन्तीत्यर्थः । यस्मादेवं तस्मात् हे वसुधिती वसुनो धनस्य धातारौ वस्त्रव्य [?] कर्माणौ तथा हे जनानामवितारावुक्तलक्षणौ युवां कदान्नानां धनानां च दातारौ भवथ इति ॥ [as read; a few words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* When will the most beloved Aśvins, wishing to carry the sacrifice through, bring up food, wealth and rain for us? This sacrifice praises only them.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he*) **preṣṭhau** — O most dear Aśvins; **ayam** — this (sacrifice performed by us); **yajñaḥ** — the sacrifice; **vām** — your; **praśastim** — praise; **akṛta** — makes; (therefore) **vasudhitī** — O holders of wealth; **janānām** — of the people; **avitārā** — protectors; **iṣām** — the food desired by us; **rayīṇām** — the wealth; **udninīthaḥ** — you bring up (lift upward); (**tathā** — likewise) **adhvaryantā** — desiring to carry the sacrifice to completion; **apām** — the rain-waters; **udninīthaḥ** — you bring up (the best of them); (**iti**) **yat** — this which; **tat** — that; **kadu** — when will it be?

**Bhāvārtha**

O dearest Aśvins, the supreme holders of wealth and protectors of all people, desirous of bringing the sacrifice to completion! When will you favour us, giving us the food, wealth and rain-water that we desire?

### Printed p. 552  (PDF 572)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 552.)*

**Printed English**

> When, beloved (Ashwins), do you bear aloft (the materials) of food and riches, that, desirous of the sacrifice, you may send down the rain: this sacrifice offers you adoration, givers of riches, protectors of men.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***adhvaryantā*** — *adhvara* is a name of the sacrifice (*yajña*): "*dhvarati hiṃsākarmā; tatpratiṣedhaḥ*" (Ni. 1-8 [?]) — the root *dhvṛ*, which gives the sense of "injury": the word *adhvara* suggests the negation of that sense; i.e. the sacrifice which is not of the nature of violence. "*etādṛśam adhvaram pārayitum icchatām yuvām*" — "you who wish to bring to completion such a non-violent sacrifice": so this word, being an epithet of the Aśvin deities, shows their importance in carrying out the sacrifice. When the head of Viṣṇu, who is of the nature of the sacrifice, was cut off, the Aśvin deities set it right and made the sacrifice complete, as told …

---

### Printed p. 553  (PDF 573)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 553.)*

… told earlier. Besides, at the very time of the *prātaḥsavana* they appear together with the goddess Uṣas and help the performance of the sacrifice; this too has been told earlier. For all these reasons the epithet *adhvaryantā* is apt for them.

This epithet is used only of the Aśvin deities, and only in the ṛk at hand. Agni, although he is the presiding deity (*adhyakṣa*) of sacrifices and the principal one in carrying out all sacrifices, does not have this epithet. Therefore it is shown by this epithet that the Aśvin deities have the principal part in the rite of sacrifice and its performance. Praising this very quality of theirs, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa describes it in this way:

> यज्ञो वै देवेभ्य उदक्रामन्नाहं वोऽन्नं भविष्यामीति नेति देवा अब्रुवन्नन्नमेव नो भविष्यसीति तं देवा विमेथिरे [?] सह्यभ्यो [?] विप्रतो ने [?] प्रबभूव ते होचुर्देवा न वै अत्तं विप्रतोऽलं भविष्यति हन्तेमं यज्ञं सम्भराम इति तथेति तं सञ्जभ्रुः । तं सम्भृत्योचुरश्विनाविमं भिषज्यतमित्यश्विनौ वै देवानां भिषजावश्विनावध्वर्यू तस्मादध्वर्यू घर्मं सम्भरतः ॥

> *yajño vai devebhya udakrāmannāhaṃ vo 'nnaṃ bhaviṣyāmīti neti devā abruvannannameva no bhaviṣyasīti taṃ devā vimethire [?] sahyabhyo [?] viprato ne [?] prababhūva te hocurdevā na vai attaṃ viprato 'laṃ bhaviṣyati hantemaṃ yajñaṃ sambharāma iti tatheti taṃ sañjabhruḥ | taṃ sambhṛtyocuraśvināvimaṃ bhiṣajyatamityaśvinau vai devānāṃ bhiṣajāvaśvināvadhvaryū tasmādadhvaryū gharmaṃ sambharataḥ ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 4-1 [?]; as read, doubtful in places [?]) — once the sacrifice left the deities, saying, "I shall not be your food." Then the deities said, "You shall indeed be our food", and with persistence they churned it. It broke up and was spoiled and was not enough. Then they gathered it together and approached the Aśvin deities, begging them to repair it and make it whole again. Because the Aśvins, the divine physicians, completed the injured sacrifice, they are praised as *adhvaryu*s ("priests who carry through the sacrifice").

***vasudhitī*** — the word *dhiti*, formed from the root *dhā* in the sense of "holding", is used in forms such as *nemadhiti*, *mitradhiti*, *vanadhiti* and the like; it gives the sense "one who holds Mitra", "one who holds wealth". In some places, for example:

> इन्द्रो अस्मे सुमना अस्तु विश्वहा राजा सोमः सुविते [?] स्यार्द्येतु नः ।
> यथायथा मित्रधितानि सन्दधुरा सर्वतातिमदितिं वृणीमहे ॥

> *indro asme sumanā astu viśvahā rājā somaḥ suvite [?] syārdyetu naḥ |*
> *yathāyathā mitradhitāni sandadhurā sarvatātimaditiṃ vṛṇīmahe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-100-4 [?]) — in such places *mitradhitāni* is explained as *mitranihitāni* ("things placed by Mitra"); the purport is just as stated above. In the ṛk at hand Sāyaṇa has explained it: "*vasunaḥ dhanasya dhātārau vastravya* [?] *karmāṇau*". *Vasu* may mean "wealth" or "dwelling"; it gives the meaning "those who hold wealth, or those who give houses (*vāsagṛha*) as gifts".

### Printed p. 554  (PDF 574)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 554.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***preṣṭhau*** — *atiśayena priyau preṣṭhau*; by "*atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau*" (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55 [?]) the suffix *iṣṭhan*; by "*priyasthira…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-157 [?]) the substitute *pra*; by "*prakṛtyaikāc*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-163 [?]) the natural form (*prakṛtibhāva*) occurs, so *guṇa*; since the suffix has *n* as marker, the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***iṣām*** — by "*sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 [?]) the case-ending takes the *udātta* accent; the genitive is in the sense of the object.
- ***adhvaryantā*** — *adhvaram ātmanaḥ icchantau*; by "*supa ātmanaḥ kyac*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 [?]) the suffix *kyac* after the word *adhvara*; by "*kavyādhvarapṛtanasyarci lopaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-4-39 [?]) elision of the last letter of the earlier part, when *kyac* follows; after *kyac*, *laṭ* comes and *śatṛ* is substituted for it; the dual following, by "*supāṃ sulak…*" *ā* is substituted; the *lasārvadhātuka* being *anudātta*, the *kyac* accent remains.
- ***udninīthaḥ*** — root *nīñ prāpaṇe*; *laṭ*, second person dual, *thas*; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" *ślu* for *śap*; reduplication and so on; because of *yad*-connection no *nighāta*; by the suffix accent the final syllable is *udātta*; by "*tiṅ citodāttavati*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-[?]) the *gati* (*ut*) is *anudātta*.
- ***akṛta*** — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; Vedic *laṅ* in the present sense; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" elision of the *vikaraṇa*; the augment *aṭ* for the stem; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent.
- ***praśastim*** — root *śaṃsu stutau*; by "*striyāṃ ktin*" the suffix *ktin*; by "*anuditāṃ hala…*" elision of the penultimate nasal; by "*tādau ca niti kṛtyatau*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50 [?]) the *gati* (*pra*) takes the *udātta* accent.
- ***vasudhitī*** — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; by "*striyāṃ ktin*", through the statement "*bahulam*", the suffix *ktin* in the agent; by "*sudhitavasudhitenemanemadhitaṃ…*" (Pā. Sū. 7-4-[?], as read [?]) *i* for the root; dual.
- ***avitārā*** — by "*supāṃ sulak…*" *ā* is substituted for the nominative dual. ‖ 1 ‖

### Printed p. 555  (PDF 575)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 555.)*

**Sūkta 181, Ṛk 2**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> आ वामश्वासः शुचयः पयस्पा वातरंहसो दिव्यासो अत्याः ।
> मनोजुवो वृषणो वीतपृष्ठा एह स्वराजो अश्विना वहन्तु ॥ २ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> आ । वाम् । अश्वासः । शुचयः । पयःऽपाः । वातऽरंहसः । दिव्यासः । अत्याः ।
> मनःऽजुवः । वृषणः । वीतऽपृष्ठाः । आ । इह । स्वऽराजः । अश्विना । वहन्तु ॥ २ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> अश्विनौ शोभनाश्वयुक्तौ वां युवामश्वासो युष्मदीया इहास्मिन्यज्ञ आ वहन्तु । प्रापयन्तु । अवशिष्टान्यश्वविशेषणानि । कीदृशास्ते । शुचयः शुद्धा दीप्ता वा पयस्पा वृष्ट्युदकस्य पातारः वातरंहसो वायुवेगाः दिव्या दिवि भवाः अत्या अतनशीलाः मनोजुवो मनोजवाः वृषणो वर्षकाः । युवान इत्यर्थः । वीतपृष्ठाः कान्तपृष्ठाः । वपुष्मन्त इत्यर्थः । स्वराजः स्वयमेव राजमानाः । ईदृशा भवन्तु ॥

*Gist:* May the pure, wind-swift, heaven-born, mind-swift horses of the Aśvins bring them to the sacrifice.

**Pratipadārtha**

(*he* **Aśvinau**) — O Aśvin deities, with excellent horses; **śucayaḥ** — pure (bright); **payaspāḥ** — drinkers of rain-water; **vātaraṃhasaḥ** — with the speed of the wind; **divyāsaḥ** — born in heaven; **atyāḥ** — ever-moving; **manojuvaḥ** — swift as the mind; **vṛṣaṇaḥ** — showering desires (youthful); **vītapṛṣṭhāḥ** — of charming bodies; **svarājaḥ** — naturally radiant; **aśvāsaḥ** — your horses; **vām** — you two; **iha** — to this sacrifice; **ā vahantu** — bring.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Aśvin deities, possessed of excellent horses! May your horses — pure, protectors of the rain-water, swift as the wind, born in heaven, ever-moving, swift as the mind, granting the wished-for objects, of charming bodies, naturally radiant — bring you two to our sacrificial hall.

### Printed p. 556  (PDF 576)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 556.)*

**Printed English**

> Ashwins, may your horses, pure, rain-drinking, swift as the wind, heaven-born, quick-moving, fleet as thought, vigorous, well-packed, and self-irradiating, bring you hither.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this mantra the words *śucayaḥ*, *vātaraṃhasaḥ* and the like are epithets of the word *aśvāsaḥ*. There is no need to give a different meaning for the question whether the Aśvins' horses are horses; "*rāsabhāv aśvinoḥ*" ("the two asses of the Aśvins") is said in the Nirukta (Ni. 2-25 [?]). There is also a view that says "*divyatejas*" ("divine brilliance"). That will be discussed later, with examples, together with the differences of view.

***śucayaḥ*** — "*śuddhāḥ, dīptā vā*" — "pure" or "shining". The Nirukta-writers give the derivation of the word thus:

> शोचतेर्ज्वलतिकर्मणः । अयमपीतरः शुचिरेतस्मादेव । निष्ट्रिक्तमस्मात् [?] पापकमिति नैरुक्ताः ॥

> *śocaterjvalatikarmaṇaḥ | ayamapītaraḥ śuciretasmādeva | niṣṭriktamasmāt [?] pāpakamiti nairuktāḥ ‖*

(Ni. 6-1 [?]) — the noun *śuci* is formed from the root *śuc*, which gives the sense "to shine"; the word means "brilliance, light". The word *śuci* too, which gives the senses "holy, pure", is derived from this same root; and the statement of the Nirukta-writers that "sin is driven away from him" is well known. On this basis *śuci* here must be explained as "pure"; or the horses may be taken as "shining".

***atyāḥ*** — "*atanaśīlāḥ*" — "of a continuously moving nature", i.e. having the nature of ranging constantly. This word need not be an epithet of the horse alone. For example:

> आ यः पुरं नार्मिणीमदीदेदत्यः कविर्नभन्योऽ नार्वा ।
> सूरो न रुरुक्वाञ्छतात्मा ॥

> *ā yaḥ puraṃ nārmiṇīmadīdedatyaḥ kavirnabhanyo ' nārvā |*
> *sūro na rurukvāñchatātmā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-149-3 [?]) — here it is an epithet of Agni and describes his independent method of ranging. And:

> अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते पृथिव्यामत्यो न यंसद्यक्षभृद्विचेताः ।
> मृगाणां न हेतयो यन्ति चेमा बृहस्पतेरहिमायाँ अभि द्यून् ॥

> *asya śloko divīyate pṛthivyāmatyo na yaṃsadyakṣabhṛdvicetāḥ |*
> *mṛgāṇāṃ na hetayo yanti cemā bṛhaspaterahimāyā~ abhi dyūn ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-190-4 [?]) — in this the word is used so that it gives the sense *atanaśīlaḥ ādityaḥ* ("the Āditya, who is of a ranging nature"). In the ṛk at hand it is an epithet of the horses of the Aśvin deities.

### Printed p. 557  (PDF 577)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 557.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — the epithets *śucayaḥ*, *divyāsaḥ*, *vītapṛṣṭhāḥ*, *svarājaḥ* and the like describe qualities that are well known for Varuṇa's horse. Moreover, according to the Nirukta sentences "*rāsabhāv aśvinoḥ*", "*ajāḥ pūṣṇaḥ*" (Ni. 2-25 [?]), the *rāsabha*s are well known as the vehicles of the Aśvin deities. The horse described in the ṛk at hand also has the other names *rāsabha* and *aja*, and there are reasons for these names. The reasons how the names *rāsabha* and *aja* came to the horse, created by Prajāpati and pervading the whole universe, are described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa as follows:

> अथ यदश्रु संक्षरितमासीत्तोऽश्वत्र [?] प्रभवदश्वत्पर्ण [?] वै तमश्व इत्याचक्षते परोक्षं परोक्षकामा हि देवा अथ यदरसदिव स रासभोऽभवदथ यः कपाले रसो लिप्त आसित्तोऽजोऽभवदथ यत्कपालमासीत्सा पृथिव्यभवत् ॥

> *atha yadaśru saṃkṣaritamāsītto 'śvatra [?] prabhavadaśvatparṇa [?] vai tamaśva ityācakṣate parokṣaṃ parokṣakāmā hi devā atha yadarasadiva sa rāsabho 'bhavadatha yaḥ kapāle raso lipta āsitto 'jo 'bhavadatha yatkapālamāsītsā pṛthivyabhavat ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 6-1-1-11 [?]; as read, doubtful in places [?]) — the deities, who love indirect speech, called the horse that pervaded the world *aśva*. When the egg split into two, the sound that came was given the name *rāsabha*. The juice smeared on the shell of the egg became the *aja*. This is the description of how Prajāpati created the horse out of Agni, who pervades the universe.

The many divine qualities of every sort that are told of the horse described in the ṛk at hand are told in many places of this horse created by Prajāpati. Not only that, but the close relation between Varuṇa and the horse, and between Prajāpati and the horse, is told in many places. For example:

> वारुणो वा अश्वः । तं देवतया व्यर्धयति । यत्प्राजापत्यं करोति । …. वारुणो वा अश्वः ॥

> *vāruṇo vā aśvaḥ | taṃ devatayā vyardhayati | yatprājāpatyaṃ karoti | …. vāruṇo vā aśvaḥ ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-9-6-1 [?]) — Sāyaṇa explains this sentence: "*aśvasyābhyonitvād varuṇasya cāpāṃ patitvād ayam aśvo vāruṇaḥ*" [as read [?]] — since the horse is born from the waters and Varuṇa is the lord of the waters, this horse belongs to Varuṇa. The scholar Eggeling, who has translated the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa into English, considering what the hidden meaning of this "horse of Varuṇa" is, has said:

> Varuna's horse is none other than the fiery races [sic] who pursues his diurnal course across the all-encompassing arch of heaven, the sphere of Varuna, the all-ruler. It is in the form of the horse that the Sun is thus lauded in the hymn.

(S. B. E. Vol. XLIV. P. XIX–XX)

### Printed p. 558  (PDF 578)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 558.)*

— he says that this horse of Varuṇa, the lord of heaven and earth and everything, is none other than the Sun, who completes his daily circuit. By the epithets *śucayaḥ* and *svarājaḥ* the horses described in the ṛk at hand may be said to be of the form of the rays of the Āditya (the Sun). Since it is described in the later ṛk, that is, the ṛk 1-181-4, that one of the Aśvin deities is of the form of Sūrya, the description of the ṛk at hand is like the description of the horse that is of the form of the Āditya's rays.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***aśvāsaḥ, divyāsaḥ*** — with *jas* following, by "*ājjaser asuk*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50 [?]) the augment *asuk*.
- ***payaspāḥ*** — root *pā pāne*; by "*ato manin…*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-74 [?]) the suffix *viṭ*; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent; by "*pāto ca bahulam*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-53 [?]) *ṣatva*; nominative plural.
- ***vātaraṃhasaḥ, vītapṛṣṭhāḥ*** — in the *bahuvrīhi* compound the fore-member keeps its natural accent.
- ***svarājaḥ*** — *svayam eva rājante iti svarājaḥ*; root *rāja dīptau*; the suffix *kvip*; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent.
- ***vahantu*** — root *vaha prāpaṇe*; *loṭ*, third person plural; *tiṅ*-final *nighāta* accent. ‖ 2 ‖

**Sūkta 181, Ṛk 3**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> आ वां रथोऽवनिर्न प्रवत्वान्त्सृप्रवन्धुरः सुविताय गम्याः ।
> वृष्णः स्थातारा मनसो जवीयानहंपूर्वो यजतो धिष्ण्या यः ॥ ३ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> आ । वाम् । रथः । अवनिः । न । प्रवत्वान् । सृप्रऽवन्धुरः । सुवितायै । गम्याः ।
> वृष्णः । स्थातारा । मनसः । जवीयान् । अहम्ऽपूर्वः । यजतः । धिष्ण्या । यः ॥ ३ ॥

> *ā | vām | rathaḥ | avaniḥ | na | pravatvān | sṛpra 'vandhuraḥ | suvitāyai | gamyāḥ |*
> *vṛṣṇaḥ | sthātārā | manasaḥ | javīyān | aham 'pūrvaḥ | yajataḥ | dhiṣṇyā | yaḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 559  (PDF 579)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 559.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> पूर्वमन्त्रेऽश्वव्याजेनाश्विनोरागमनमुक्तम् । अनेन रथव्याजेनोच्यते । हे धिष्ण्यौ उन्नतस्थानार्हौ स्थातारा स्वरथाधिष्ठानौ वां युवयोर्यो रथोऽस्ति स सुविताय शोभनफलाय गम्याः । अस्मद्यज्ञमागच्छतु ॥ पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ कीदृशो रथ इति स विशेष्यते । अवनिर्न प्रवत्वान् भूमिरिवात्यन्तविस्तारवान् सृप्रवन्धुरो विस्तीर्णपुरोभागः वृष्णो वर्षकस्याश्वस्य मनसोऽपि जवीयान् । मनोवेगवानित्यर्थः । अहम्पूर्वोऽहङ्कारपूर्वो मनस्वी वाकृत्यादारः [?] यजतो यष्टव्यः । ईदृशो रथ आगच्छतु ॥ [as read; a few words doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* In the previous ṛk the Aśvins' coming was spoken of through their horses; now through their chariot: let the broad, mind-swift, adorable chariot come to our sacrifice for our good.

**Pratipadārtha**

**dhiṣṇyā** — O worthy of an exalted place; **sthātārā** — you who stand on your own chariot, O Aśvin deities; **avaniḥ na** — vast like the earth; **pravatvān** — extremely spread out; **sṛpravandhuraḥ** — with a broad forepart; **vṛṣṇaḥ** — than the desire-showering horse; **manasaḥ** — [and] than the mind; **javīyān** — swifter; **ahaṃpūrvaḥ** — eager (as if first to arrive); **yajataḥ** — worthy of worship; **vām** — your; **yaḥ rathaḥ** — which chariot; (**saḥ** — that chariot); **suvitāya** — for auspicious fruit; **ā gamyāḥ** — may it come to our sacrifice.

**Bhāvārtha**

O Aśvin deities, exalted, standing steady on your own chariot! May your chariot — vast like the earth, broad in front, swifter than horse and mind, eager and worthy of worship — come with you to our sacrificial hall, in order to bestow on us an auspicious fruit.

**Printed English**

> Ashwins, excellent and steady, may your chariot, vast as the earth, broad-fronted, rapid as the rain, (fleet) as thought, emulative and adorable, come hither for (our) good.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***dhiṣṇyā*** — for this word Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "*unnatasthānārhau*" ("worthy of an exalted place"), i.e. "worthy of worship". Since this synonym is used also of the sacrificial places such as that of the Āgnīdhra, here too the meaning "worthy of such a place" is possible. The two words *dhiṣaṇā* and *dhiṣṇyā* have, in general, one and the same meaning. (That these two words should have a difference of meaning is very unusual.)

### Printed p. 560  (PDF 580)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 560.)*

The Nirukta-writers have read the word *dhiṣaṇā* among the names of "speech" (*vāc*) (Ni. 1-11 [?]) and among the names of "heaven and earth" (*dyāvāpṛthivī*) (Ni. 3-30 [?]). Citing

> मेद्यन्तु ते वह्नयो येभिरीयसेऽरिषण्यन्नळेळयस्वा वनस्पते ।
> आयूया धृष्णो अभिगूर्या त्वं नेष्ट्रात्सोमं द्रविणोदः पिब ऋतुभिः ॥

> *medyantu te vahnayo yebhirīyase 'riṣaṇyannaḷeḷayasvā vanaspate |*
> *āyūyā dhṛṣṇo abhigūryā tvaṃ neṣṭrātsomaṃ draviṇodaḥ piba ṛtubhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-3 [?]) — "*dhṛṣṇo dhiṣṇyo dhiṣaṇo dhiṣaṇābhavaḥ | dhiṣaṇā vāk dhiṣer dadhāty arthe | dhīsādinīti vā | dhī sāninīti vā*" [as read [?]]: from the root *dhiṣ*, which gives the sense "hold", *dhiṣaṇā* is formed in the sense of *vāc*; or it gives the idea "that which spreads understanding" or "that which gives conversation". Hence, for the word *dhiṣaṇā*, the derivation "*vāk*" is the one they show. But other meanings too are possible for this word.

> आपश्च मित्रं धिषणा च साधन्देवा अग्निं धारयन्द्रविणोदाम् ।

> *āpaśca mitraṃ dhiṣaṇā ca sādhandevā agniṃ dhārayandraviṇodām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-1 [?])

> इमां ते धियं प्र भरे महो महीमस्य स्तोत्रे धिषणा यत्त आनजे ।

> *imāṃ te dhiyaṃ pra bhare maho mahīmasya stotre dhiṣaṇā yatta ānaje |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-102-1 [?]) — in such ṛks it means "speech" or "intellect". If *vāk* is explained as speech in the form of praise, then for the word *dhiṣṇya* the meaning "worthy of praise, worthy of worship" arises, and in this sense this same word is used in many places.

> तन्नो वातो मयोभु वातु भेषजं तन्माता पृथिवी तत्पिता द्यौः ।
> तद्ग्रावाणः सोमसुतो मयोभुवस्तदश्विना शृणुतं धिष्ण्या युवम् ॥

> *tanno vāto mayobhu vātu bheṣajaṃ tanmātā pṛthivī tatpitā dyauḥ |*
> *tadgrāvāṇaḥ somasuto mayobhuvastadaśvinā śṛṇutaṃ dhiṣṇyā yuvam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-4 [?]) — in this the word *dhiṣṇyā* is an epithet of the Aśvin deities. For this, Sāyaṇa has explained "*dhiṣaṇā buddhiḥ, tadārhāv aśvinau*" — that is, "worthy of meditation". Likewise:

> युवं श्रीभिर्दर्शताभिराभिः शुभे पुष्टिमूहथुः सूर्यायाः ।
> प्र वां वयो वपुषेऽनु पप्त्नक्षद्वाणी सुष्टुता धिष्ण्या वाम् ॥

> *yuvaṃ śrībhirdarśatābhirābhiḥ śubhe puṣṭimūhathuḥ sūryāyāḥ |*
> *pra vāṃ vayo vapuṣe 'nu paptnakṣadvāṇī suṣṭutā dhiṣṇyā vām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-63-6 [?]) — in this and other contexts also (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-5-14; 8-35-13 [?]) this epithet is used as one of the Aśvin deities; it is used everywhere in the sense "worthy of praise, worthy of worship".

> कद्धिष्ण्यासु वृधसानो अग्ने कद्वाताय प्रतवसे शुभंये ।
> परिज्मने नासत्याय क्षे ब्रवः कदग्ने रुद्राय नृघ्ने ॥

> *kaddhiṣṇyāsu vṛdhasāno agne kadvātāya pratavase śubhaṃye |*
> *parijmane nāsatyāya kṣe bravaḥ kadagne rudrāya nṛghne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-3-6 [?])

### Printed p. 561  (PDF 581)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 561; signature mark "XIII 36".)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — in these ṛks, for the word *dhiṣṇyā* the meaning "place" is cited, in the sense of places such as the Āgnīdhrīya hearth (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114-9 [?]). Although "worthy of worship" is the general meaning, in some places the Nirukta-writers have read this word among the names of "heaven and earth" (*dyāvāpṛthivī*) (Ni. 3-30 [?]):

> महस्करथो वरिवो यथा नोऽस्मे क्षयाय धिषणे अनेहः ।

> *mahaskaratho varivo yathā no 'sme kṣayāya dhiṣaṇe anehaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-50-3 [?])

> समिन्द्रेणे [?] धिषणे वि ष्कभायति वृष्णः पीत्वा मद उक्थानि शंसति ।

> *samindreṇe [?] dhiṣaṇe vi ṣkabhāyati vṛṣṇaḥ pītvā mada ukthāni śaṃsati |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-44-8 [?]) — in such ṛks it means *dyāvāpṛthivī*. In some contexts the word is understood also to mean "a bag (*cīla*) that is filled with Soma juice". In some places Sāyaṇa, where none of the above meanings is at all suitable, has shown a different derivation for the word and has given an unusual meaning. For example:

> अग्ने दिवो अर्णमच्छा जिगास्यच्छा देवाँ ऊचिषे धिष्ण्या ये ।
> या रोचने परस्तात्सूर्यस्य याश्चावस्तादुपतिष्ठन्त आपः ॥

> *agne divo arṇamacchā jigāsyacchā devā~ ūciṣe dhiṣṇyā ye |*
> *yā rocane parastātsūryasya yāścāvastādupatiṣṭhanta āpaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-22-3 [?]) — in this, Sāyaṇa: "*dhiyaṃ buddhyupahitaṃ deham uṣṇantyuṣṇīkurvanti iti dhiṣṇyāḥ*" — "those who heat the body that is endowed with intellect are *dhiṣṇya*s" — since this shows pride in a body endowed with understanding, the name *dhiṣṇya* arises. In the ṛk cited it is an epithet of the deities. Thus, since the word is used in many meanings, in the ṛk at hand the meaning is: the Aśvin deities, who desire a place worthy of worship.

***avaniḥ*** — here for *avani* the meaning "earth" has been given. The Nirukta-writers have read this word among the names of "fingers" (Ni. 2-5 [?]) and among the names of "rivers" (Ni. 2-24 [?]) and of "earth" (Ni. 2-5 [?]). Besides, since the word *avani* is formed from the root *ava*, "to protect", it is an epithet of Indra and others in the sense of "protector". Showing how the meaning "finger" arose for the word *avani*, the Nirukta-writers say:

> अवनयोऽङ्गुलयो भवन्त्येवं हि कर्माणि ।

> *avanayo 'ṅgulayo bhavantyevaṃ hi karmāṇi |*

(Ni. 3-9 [?]) — they explain the meaning of this word: since the fingers protect (*ava*) the rites such as the sacrifice, the fingers have the name *avani*. And:

> यः पुष्पिणीश्च प्रस्वश्च धर्मणाधि दाने व्यं [?] वनीरधारयः ।
> यश्चासमा अजनो दिद्युतो दिव उरुरूर्वाँ अभितः सासह्युक्थ्यः ॥ [as read [?]]

> *yaḥ puṣpiṇīśca prasvaśca dharmaṇādhi dāne vyaṃ [?] vanīradhārayaḥ |*
> *yaścāsamā ajano didyuto diva ururūrvā~ abhitaḥ sāsahyukthyaḥ ‖ [as read [?]]*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-13-2 [?]) — here *avanīḥ* is *oṣadhīḥ*, "herbs": in the sense of herbs that protect life. And:

> तुभ्येदमग्ने मधुमत्तमं वचस्तुभ्यं मनीषा इयमस्तु शं हृदे ।
> त्वां गिरः सिन्धुमिवावनीर्महीरा पृणन्ति शवसा वर्धयन्ति च ॥

> *tubhyedamagne madhumattamaṃ vacastubhyaṃ manīṣā iyamastu śaṃ hṛde |*
> *tvāṃ giraḥ sindhumivāvanīrmahīrā pṛṇanti śavasā vardhayanti ca ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-11-3 [?])

### Printed p. 562  (PDF 582)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 562.)*

— in this ṛk the word *avanīḥ* is used as a synonym of the rivers that go to the sea. Thus, both in the sense of "protecting" and in the sense of "extended", the word is an epithet of river, of earth (*pṛthvī*) and the like. In the ṛk at hand it means "the extended earth".

***ahaṃpūrvaḥ*** — for this word, Sāyaṇa has explained "of a nature that has pride in itself" or "of generous mind". It is commonly used in the sense of *ahamahamikā* ("I first, I first"). Here this epithet is used to show the extreme degree of speed.

***suvitāyai*** — the meaning has been given for this word according to the context. In some places it means "for easy going" (*sugamanāya*), "for a most excellent going"; in others "for the best fruit" and "for a rite that gives fruit".

> आ रुद्रासः इन्द्रवन्तः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गन्तन ।
> इयं वो अस्मत्प्रति हर्यते मतिस्तृष्णजे न दिव उत्सा उदन्यवे ॥

> *ā rudrāsaḥ indravantaḥ sajoṣaso hiraṇyarathāḥ suvitāya gantana |*
> *iyaṃ vo asmatprati haryate matistṛṣṇaje na diva utsā udanyave ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-57-1 [?]) — in such places the word *suvitāya* is used in the sense "for a good-natured rite, for the best rite".

> पुनरेहि वृषाकपे सुविता कल्पयावहै ।

> *punarehi vṛṣākape suvitā kalpayāvahai |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-21 [?]) — in this "*suprasūtāni*" or "*supravṛttāni*" is said. That this word is used in still other senses has been told earlier, in the special topics of Ṛk 1-180-10.

***sṛpravandhuraḥ*** — the word *sṛpra* generally means "of a gliding (*sarpaṇa*) nature". For example:

> नपाता शवसो महः सूनू दक्षस्य सुक्रतो ।
> सृप्रदानू [?] इषो वास्त्वधि क्षितः ॥

> *napātā śavaso mahaḥ sūnū dakṣasya sukrato |*
> *sṛpradānū [?] iṣo vāstvadhi kṣitaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-25-5 [?]) — in such places it means "always flowing", i.e. "a giver without break". But in the ṛk at hand *vandhura* is used in the sense of the seat at the front on which the charioteer sits; there is no room here for the meaning "flowing". It can be taken as "an extremely wide seat". Sāyaṇa too has explained it in this sense. The explanation of the words *trivandhurām* and *tricakraḥ* has been given in the 34th sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34 [?]), Part 4.

### Printed p. 563  (PDF 583)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 563.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar)** — noted briefly (sūtra numerals [?]):

- ***avaniḥ*** — root *ava rakṣaṇe*; by "*artisṛdhṛdhmā…*" (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]) the suffix *ani*; the suffix takes the *ādyudātta* accent.
- ***pravatvān*** — root *vana paṇa sambhaktau*; the suffix *kvip* when *pra* precedes; by "*gamādīnām iti vaktavyam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-40 [?]) elision of the nasal *n* of the root; by "*hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk*" the augment *tuk*; the *kṛdutta* final member keeps its natural accent. *pravat asya asti iti pravatvān*; by "*mādupadhāyāś ca…*" *va* for the *m* of *matup*; since *matup* is *pit*, it is *anudātta*; nominative singular.
- ***gamyāḥ*** — root *gamḷ gatau*; by "*vyatyayo bahulam*" the second person singular ending has come in place of the third person singular of *liṅ*; by "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" elision of the *vikaraṇa*; therefore no *ā* substitution; being in an *atiṅanta* word-position, the *nighāta* accent occurs.
- ***sthātārā*** — root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; the suffix *tṛc* in the agent; the vocative dual following, by "*supāṃ sulak…*" *ā* is substituted; being in the vocative, the *nighāta* accent.
- ***yajataḥ*** — root *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; by "*bhṛmṛdṛśiyajiparvipacibhyo 'tac*" (Uṇ. Sū. 3-110 [?]) the suffix *atac*; by "*citaḥ*" the final syllable is *udātta*.
- ***dhiṣṇyā*** — root *ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye*; by "*sānasi varṇasi parṇasi…*" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]) the form is irregularly derived, ending in the suffix *ṇya*; *ā* is substituted for the case-ending *au*; being in the vocative, the *nighāta* accent. ‖ 3 ‖

**Sūkta 181, Ṛk 4**

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> इहेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा नामभिः स्वैः ।
> जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ॥ ४ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> इहऽइह । जाता । सम् । अवावशीताम् । अरेपसा । तन्वा । नामऽभिः । स्वैः ।
> जिष्णुः । वाम् । अन्यः । सुऽमखस्य । सूरिः । दिवः । अन्यः । सुऽभगः । पुत्रः । ऊहे ॥ ४ ॥

> *iha 'iha | jātā | sam | avāvaśītām | arepasā | tanvā | nāma 'bhiḥ | svaiḥ |*
> *jiṣṇuḥ | vām | anyaḥ | su 'makhasya | sūriḥ | divaḥ | anyaḥ | su 'bhagaḥ | putraḥ | ūhe ‖ 4 ‖*

### Printed p. 564  (PDF 584)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 564.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ युवां समवावशीताम् । सह सम्यग्गत्वा पुनःपुनः स्तूयेथे कामयेथां वा यज्ञम् ॥ पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ कीदृशौ युवाम् । इहेह जाता । उभाभ्यामिहशब्दाभ्यां मध्यमोत्तमस्थाने उच्येते । तयोः सम्भूतौ । चन्द्रसूर्येणेति यावत् । सूर्याचन्द्रमसाविव्येके । नि. १२-१ [?] । इति निरुक्तम् । अरेपसापौ [?] । अथर्वणस्य गुरोः शिरश्छेदनादिना पापलेपरहितावितिभावः । आथर्वणायाश्विना दधीचेऽश्व्यं शिरः प्रत्यैरयतम् । ऋ. १-११६-१२ [?] । इत्यादि मन्त्रवर्णात् । केन हेतुनेति उच्यते । तन्वा शरीरेण शरीरसौन्दर्येण निमित्तेन स्वैर्नामभिः स्वीयैर्नासत्यादिभिर्नामभिरपि । रमणीयशरीरवत्त्वान्मनोज्ञनामवत्त्वाच्च हेतोः संस्तूयेथे इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । अरेपसा तन्वेति योज्यम् । उक्तप्रकारेण गुरुशिरश्छेदादिप्यपापेन शीर्ष्णेण तादृग्जहत्त्व [?] … अपनेनेति यावत् । किंच वां युवयोरन्य एको मध्यमस्थानान्तरिक्षस्य पुत्रस्थानीयः सोमो वै जिष्णुर्जयशीलः सुमखस्य शोभनयज्ञस्य सूरिः प्रेरयिता सन्नूहे । वहति । विश्वं जगद्धारयति । चन्द्रात्तेनस्योदये सति ह्योषधिवनस्पत्यादयो वर्धन्ते । अन्योऽपर उत्तमस्थानो दिवो द्युलोकस्य पुत्रः पुत्रस्थानीय आदित्यः सुभगः शोभनरश्मिरूपधन ऊहे । वहति । कृत्स्नमेवं पृथग्जगन्निर्वाहकौ महानुभावौ युवां सह स्तूयेथे । अत्र निरुक्तम् । इहेह जातौ संस्तूयेथे पापेनालिप्यमानया तन्वा नामभिश्च स्वैर्जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमहतो बलस्येरयिता मध्यमो दिवोऽन्यः सुभगः पुत्र उह्यत आदित्यः । नि. १२-३ [?] । इति ॥ [as read; the passage is dense and several phrases are doubtful [?]]

*Gist:* The two Aśvins, born in the middle region and in the highest heaven (as moon and sun), are praised for their fair bodies and names; one, victorious, impels the good sacrifice; the other, the Āditya, bears the world.

**Pratipadārtha**

**iha** — here (in the middle region, as the moon); **iha** — here (in the highest region, as the sun); **jātā** — born; **tanvā** — by beauty of body; (and) **svaiḥ nāmabhiḥ** — by your own names, Nāsatya and others; **arepasā** — free from fault; (*he* **Aśvinau**) **yuvām** — you two; **saṃ avāvaśītām** — are praised well, again and again, or are longed for at the sacrifice; (**kiṃ ca**) **vām** — of you two; **anyaḥ** — one (in the form of the moon of the middle region); **jiṣṇuḥ** — the victorious; **sumakhasya** — of the good sacrifice; **sūriḥ** — the impeller; **ūhe** — (carries the world); (and) **divaḥ putraḥ** — the son of heaven, the highest region; **anyaḥ** — the other, in the form of the Āditya; **subhagaḥ** — rich in auspicious rays; (**ūhe** — carries the world.)

### Printed p. 565  (PDF 585)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 565.)*

**Bhāvārtha**

O Aśvin deities, who are born in the middle region (the intermediate region) and in the highest region (heaven), possessed of bodies of defined (specific) form, with names such as Nāsatya! You two, united, are praised again and again (or you become desired at the sacrifice); one of you, the master of the middle region, victorious, in the form of the Moon, impelling the sacrifice through the growth of the herbs; the other, the son-like of the highest region, heaven, in the form of the Sun, causing the world to prosper through his rays; in this way you two protect this universe.

**Printed English**

> Born here (in the middle region) and here (in the upper region), you are glorified together, as faultless in your forms and (perfect in your own many excellences): one (of you), the victorious son (of the firmament), the devout (promoter) of sacred sacrifices, the other, tee [sic] auspicious son of heaven, (each) upholds (the world).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

***jiṣṇur vām anyaḥ sumakhasya sūrir divo anyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhe*** — in this sentence the individual nature and the function of the Aśvin deities are shown. To explain their individual nature definitively is not easy; but, on the basis of the *śruti* sentences, on the opinions of scholars following the Vedic tradition, and by citing the views of English critics, the idea told in the ṛk at hand is examined here as far as possible.

"Nāsatya and the rest, deities of defined names, O Aśvins, you two, united, are praised again and again; one of you, in the form of the Moon, belonging to the middle world, victorious, impelling the sacrifice by the growth of the herbs; the other, in the form of the Sun, the son-like of the upper region, protecting the world by his rays" — thus is their individual form described in the ṛk at hand; in the Nirukta this passage is explained thus:

> इहेह च जातौ संस्तूयेते पापेनालिप्यमानया तन्वा नामभिश्च स्वैर्जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमहतो बलस्येरयिता मध्यमो दिवोऽन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊह्यत आदित्यः ॥

> *iheha ca jātau saṃstūyete pāpenālipyamānayā tanvā nāmabhiśca svairjiṣṇurvāmanyaḥ sumahato balasyerayitā madhyamo divo 'nyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhyata ādityaḥ ‖*

(Ni. 12-3 [?])

### Printed p. 566  (PDF 586)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 566.)*

> Born here and there, they two are praised together with reference to a body unstained by sin and to their own names. One of you two is the Victor, the furtherer of very great strength, i.e., belongs to the middle region; the other is considered the blessed son of heaven, i.e. the Sun.

The meaning of these sentences is as already stated above. Thus the purport of this ṛk is that one is in the form of the Sun and the other in the form of the Moon, and that both are protectors of the world. But in some other places they are praised in different ways. For that very reason the Nirukta-writers, too, have not given a definitive opinion in this matter but have told other views. That is as follows:

> अश्विनौ यद्व्यश्नुवाते सर्वं रसेनान्यो ज्योतिषान्यः । अश्वैरश्विनावित्यौर्णवाभः । तत्कावश्विनौ द्यावापृथिव्यावित्येके । अहोरात्रावित्येके । सूर्याचन्द्रमसावित्येके । राजानौ पुण्यकृतावित्यैतिहासिकाः ॥

> *aśvinau yadvyaśnuvāte sarvaṃ rasenānyo jyotiṣānyaḥ | aśvairaśvināvityaurṇavābhaḥ | tatkāvaśvinau dyāvāpṛthivyāvityeke | ahorātrāvityeke | sūryācandramasāvityeke | rājānau puṇyakṛtāvityaitihāsikāḥ ‖*

(Ni. 12-1 [?]) — "Of these deities, one pervades everywhere with water (*rasa*), the other with light; hence they have the name Aśvins": this is one view. "By means of horses they are Aśvins," says Aurṇavābha. "Who are these Aśvins?" Some say "heaven and earth"; some say "day and night"; some say "the Sun and the Moon"; the *aitihāsikas* (historians) say "two pious kings". Thus, noting the differences of opinion, citing the ṛk (1-181-4) and another unspecified mantra, they have stated the diversity of views in this matter. First:

> वसातिषु स्म चरथोऽसितौ पेश्वावि [?] ।
> कदेदमश्विना युवमभि देवा आगच्छतम् ॥ [as read [?]]

> *vasātiṣu sma caratho 'sitau peśvāvi [?] |*
> *kadedamaśvinā yuvamabhi devā āgacchatam ‖ [as read [?]]*

— as is said in this mantra, one of them is *Vasātiputra* ("the son of the night"), the other *Uṣaḥputra* ("the son of the dawn"); having said this, they afterwards explain, as shown above, citing the ṛk at hand. The scholar Macdonell, giving his opinion on this matter, has said:

> "Though they (Aśvinau [set in Kannada letters]) hold a distinct position among the Deities of of [sic] light and their appellation is Indian, their connection with any definite Phenomena of light is so obscure that their original nature is to Puzzle to [sic] the Vedic interpreters from the earliest times."

[Vedic Mythology, P. 49]

### Printed p. 567  (PDF 587)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 567.)*

**Special Topics (continued)** — if the opinions of Vedic and modern English scholars are brought together, these views are seen (table printed in English):

| Seholars [sic] | Their opinions |
|---|---|
| Yaska | Twilight before Dawn, half dark and half light. |
| Aurnavabha | Light rays. |
| Oldenberg | Morning or evening star. |
| Macdonell | Twilight or Morning stars. |
| Bloomfield | Morning or evening stars. |
| Hopekins [sic] | Transition from darkness to light. |
| Bergaine [sic] | Fire of heaven and of the altar. |
| *aitihāsikāḥ* (set in Kannada letters) | Two pious kings. |
| E. N. Ghosh | Two stars of Asvini. (Aries) |
| Weber | Twin constellation of Gemini. |
| Shama Shastry | The Sun and the Moon. |
| Max Muller | Personification of Morning and evening. |

Dr. Śyāmaśāstri has explained his own opinion on this subject in detail in the journal of the Mythic Society (Vol. XX, No. 2, P. 80–88); and he has supported the view that they are the Sun and the Moon and nobody else. If the nature of the Aśvin deities is to be determined from the descriptions in the sentences of the Ṛk-saṃhitā, the evidences cited below may be examined.

> त्वष्टा दुहित्रे वहतुं कृणोतीतीदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति ।
> यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश ॥
> अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामदधुर्विवस्वते ।
> उताश्विनावभरद्यत्तदासीदजहादु द्वा मिथुना सरण्यूः ॥

> *tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṃ kṛṇotītīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sameti |*
> *yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa ‖*
> *apāgūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇāmadadhurvivasvate |*
> *utāśvināvabharadyattadāsīdajahādu dvā mithunā saraṇyūḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-17-1 to 2) — Tvaṣṭṛ ordered that the whole universe should come together for his daughter's wedding. At her wedding the mother of Yama and the wife of Vivasvān vanished; that is, they hid her, the immortal, from the sight of mortals. Then they made a woman of the same form (*Savarṇā*) and gave her to Vivasvān. Afterwards she bore the Aśvin deities. Saraṇyū, who is well known by that name, left the Aśvin deities as her sons and went away: this is the purport of the above ṛks. And:

### Printed p. 568  (PDF 588)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 568.)*

> यमूचित्र [?] यमुसूरसूत जिह्वाया अग्रं पतदा ह्यस्थात् ।
> वपूंषि जाता मिथुना सचेते तमोहना तपुषो बुध्न एता ॥

> *yamūcitra [?] yamusūrasūta jihvāyā agraṃ patadā hyasthāt |*
> *vapūṃṣi jātā mithunā sacete tamohanā tapuṣo budhna etā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-39-3 [?]) — it is told that the mother of the twins (that is, of the Aśvin deities) gave birth to twins; both of them, in the form of bodies, destroyed darkness. The scholar Max Müller, citing this ṛk, has given his opinion on this subject in this way:

> "We might have guessed from the text itself, even without the help of the Commentator, that 'the mother of the twins' here spoken of is Dawn: but it may be stated that the commentator, too, adopts this view."

(Science of Language. Vol. II. P. 530) — that is, Sāyaṇa, in his bhāṣya, for the word *yamusūḥ* has given "*uṣo 'bhimāninī devatā* (*atra uṣaḥkāle asūta*)" ("the deity presiding over Dawn, who gave birth at the time of dawn"); so it is agreed on all hands that the mother of the Aśvin deities is the goddess Uṣas, says this scholar. Besides, that Tvaṣṭṛ gave his daughter Saraṇyū to Vivasvān, and that the Aśvin deities were born from her, is told in the Bṛhaddevatā in this way:

> अभवन्मिथुनं त्वाष्ट्रः सरण्यूस्त्रिशिराः सह । स वै सरण्यूं प्रायच्छत्स्वयमेव विवस्वते ॥
> ततः सरण्यूर्जज्ञाते यमं यमीं विवस्वतः [?] । तौ चाप्युभौ यमौ नाम्ना ज्यायांस्ताभ्यां तु वै यमः ॥
> सृष्ट्वा भर्तुः परोक्षं तु सरण्यूः सदृशीं स्त्रियम् । निक्षिप्य मिथुनं तस्यामश्वा भूत्वापचक्रमे ॥
> अविज्ञानाद्विवस्वांस्तु तस्यामजनयन्मनुम् । राजर्षिरभवत्सोऽपि विवस्वानिव तेजसा ॥
> स विज्ञाय त्वपक्रान्तां सरण्यूमश्वरूपिणीम् । त्वाष्ट्रीं प्रति जगामाशु वाजी भूत्वा सलक्षणः ॥
> सरण्यूश्च विवस्वन्तं विदित्वा हयरूपिणम् । मैथुनायोपचक्राम तां च तत्रारुरोह सः ॥
> ततस्तयोस्तु वेगेन शुक्रं तदपतद्भुवि । उपाजिघ्रच्च सा त्वश्वा तच्छुक्रं गर्भकाम्यया ॥
> आघ्रातमात्राच्छुक्रात्तु कुमारौ सम्बभूवतुः ।

> *abhavanmithunaṃ tvāṣṭraḥ saraṇyūstriśirāḥ saha | sa vai saraṇyūṃ prāyacchatsvayameva vivasvate ‖*
> *tataḥ saraṇyūrjajñāte yamaṃ yamīṃ vivasvataḥ [?] | tau cāpyubhau yamau nāmnā jyāyāṃstābhyāṃ tu vai yamaḥ ‖*
> *sṛṣṭvā bhartuḥ parokṣaṃ tu saraṇyūḥ sadṛśīṃ striyam | nikṣipya mithunaṃ tasyāmaśvā bhūtvāpacakrame ‖*
> *avijñānādvivasvāṃstu tasyāmajanayanmanum | rājarṣirabhavatso 'pi vivasvāniva tejasā ‖*
> *sa vijñāya tvapakrāntāṃ saraṇyūmaśvarūpiṇīm | tvāṣṭrīṃ prati jagāmāśu vājī bhūtvā salakṣaṇaḥ ‖*
> *saraṇyūśca vivasvantaṃ viditvā hayarūpiṇam | maithunāyopacakrāma tāṃ ca tatrāruroha saḥ ‖*
> *tatastayostu vegena śukraṃ tadapatadbhuvi | upājighracca sā tvaśvā tacchukraṃ garbhakāmyayā ‖*
> *āghrātamātrācchukrāttu kumārau sambabhūvatuḥ |*

(Bṛ. De. [?]; as read, several words doubtful [?]) — [the passage continues on the next page.]

### Printed p. 569  (PDF 589)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 569.)*

> नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च यौ स्तुतावश्विनाविति ॥
> इतिहासमिमं यास्कः सरण्यूर्देवते द्वृचे ।
> विवस्वतश्च त्वष्टुश्च त्वाष्ट्येति सह मन्यते ॥

> *nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca yau stutāvaśvināviti ‖*
> *itihāsamimaṃ yāskaḥ saraṇyūrdevate dvṛce |*
> *vivasvataśca tvaṣṭuśca tvāṣṭyeti saha manyate ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 6-162 to 7-2 [?], numerals as read) — Tvaṣṭṛ gave his daughter Saraṇyū to Vivasvān. She bore two twins, Yama and Yamī. Saraṇyū, creating a woman of her own form and entrusting the care of her two children to her without her husband's knowledge, herself took the form of a mare and went away. Not knowing this secret, Vivasvān begot Manu on that woman created by Saraṇyū. Presently, learning that she was not the real Saraṇyū, he set out to find her, taking the form of a horse. Seeing that form, she was enamoured and desired union with him. Then, from the force of his seed, two sons, **Nāsatya** and **Dasra**, were born; they are the Aśvin deities — so runs the story. The same story is told in the Harivaṃśa also. Since it follows the Paurāṇika tradition, and since in the descriptions of the subject at hand we are examining only on the basis of Vedic sentences, the Harivaṃśa account is not to the point here. As stated above, the order of origin of the Aśvin deities may be shown thus:

*(Genealogical diagram, printed in Kannada letters; given here in words, "mine"):* Tvaṣṭṛ → Triśirā and Saraṇyū. Saraṇyū — Vivasvān — Savarṇā; from Savarṇā, Manu. From Saraṇyū and Vivasvān: Yama and Yamī. Another Saraṇyū (as mare) → Nāsatya and Dasra.

And (printed in a brace): (1) Triśirā and Saraṇyū, (2) Yama and Yamī, (3) Nāsatya and Dasra — "also" (*saha*), are the twins (*yamaḷaru*).

As described in the Ṛk at hand, these two, being two luminous forms, are described in another place in another form.

### Printed p. 570  (PDF 590)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 570.)*

> अति द्रव सारमेयौ श्वानौ चतुरक्षौ शबलौ साधुना पथा ।
> अथा पितॄन्सुविदत्रां उपेहि यमेन ये सधमादं मदन्ति ॥

> *ati drava sārameyau śvānau caturakṣau śabalau sādhunā pathā |*
> *athā pitṝnsuvidatrāṃ upehi yamena ye sadhamādaṃ madanti ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-10) — regarding the pair of dogs described here, the scholar Max Müller has formed this opinion:

> "Those two dogs represent Time, in double aspect as morning and evening. Representing Time in all forms of its double aspect—as morning and evening, day and night, bright and dark fortnights, bright and dark halves of the year—the two dogs probably identical with the two Aświns."

(Seience [sic] of Languge [sic], Vol. II.) — It may be said that this pair of dogs guarding Yama may be parts of Time: that is, they may be in the forms of day and night, forenoon and evening, or the bright and dark fortnights, or the Uttarāyaṇa and Dakṣiṇāyana. Thus the Aśvin deities too may be said to be natural divisions reflecting these. Accordingly:

> धियंजिन्वा धिष्ण्या विश्पलावसू दिवो नपाता सुकृते शुचिव्रता ।

> *dhiyaṃjinvā dhiṣṇyā viśpalāvasū divo napātā sukṛte śucivratā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-182-1 [?]) — here the Aśvin deities are addressed as *divo napātā*. In the Ṛk at hand, Sāyaṇa has explained them as Soma and Sūrya. The time of their manifestation will be told in the Special Topics of the next ṛk.

**Ārepasā** — for this word the Nirukta-author explains "*pāpena alipyamānayā tanvā*": with a body not smeared with fault; *repas* means fault or sin; hence "not smeared".

**Āvāvaśītām** — the word is formed from the root *vaś*, in the two senses "to desire" or "to make manifest". Sāyaṇa gives "*punaḥ punaḥ stūyethe vā kāmayethām*" — "you are praised again and again" or "you desire again and again". Uses of this word in both senses may be seen elsewhere, e.g.:

> अच्छा कोशं मधुश्चुतमसृग्रं वारे अव्यये । अवावशन्त धीतयः ॥

> *acchā kośaṃ madhuścutamasṛgraṃ vāre avyaye | avāvaśanta dhītayaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-66-11 [?]) — here: "the fingers desired again" — [the sentence continues on the next page].

> अभि त्रिपृष्ठं वृषणं वयोधामाङ्गूषाणामवावशन्त वाणीः ।
> वना वसानो वरुणो न सिन्धूञ्छ्रत्नधा दयते वार्याणि ॥

> *abhi tripṛṣṭhaṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ vayodhāmāṅgūṣāṇāmavāvaśanta vāṇīḥ |*
> *vanā vasāno varuṇo na sindhūñchratnadhā dayate vāryāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-90-3 [?]; Sanskrit as read, several words doubtful [?]) — here also the sense is that speeches (*vāṇīḥ*) sounded. "yajñecchu") — as read [?].

**Subhagā** — this word is read among the names of wealth: "*maghaṃ, reknaḥ*" etc. (Ni. 2-10 [?]); wealth of the excellent kind. Since in the Ṛk at hand it occurs along with the word for the Sun, the meaning here is wealth in the form of rays, as it is said to be the wealth of the deity.

### Sūkta 181, Ṛk 5  (printed p. 572; PDF 592)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 572.)*

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> प्र वां निचेरुः ककुहो वशाँ अनु पिशङ्गरूपः सदनानि गम्याः ।
> हरी अन्यस्य पीपयन्त वाजैर्मथा रजांस्यश्विना वि घोष्यैः ॥ ५ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> प्र । वां । निऽचेरुः । ककुहः । वशान् । अनु । पिशङ्गऽरूपः । सदनानि । गम्याः ।
> हरी इति । अन्यस्य । पीपयन्त । वाजैः । मथा । रजांसि । अश्विना । वि । घोष्यैः ॥ ५ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनावश्विनौ वां युवयोर्मध्येऽन्यस्यैकस्य ककुहः श्रेष्ठः पिशङ्गरूपो हिरण्यरूपः पीतवर्णो वा बहुभिरश्वाद्यवयवैर्निरूप्यमाणो वा रथो वशानन्वनुलक्ष्य यथाकामं । अस्मद्यज्ञागमनेच्छयेत्यर्थः । यद्वा । वशान् स्वाधीनाः ककुहो दिशो दिगन्तरालानुक्रमेण नीचैरुच्चैश्चरन् स्वस्थानाद्देवयजनमुखं गच्छन् । सदनान्यस्मद्यागगृहाणि प्र गम्याः । प्रकर्षेण गच्छतु ॥ पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ अत्र यद्यस्येति नोक्तं तथाप्युत्तरवाक्ये तथोक्तत्वात्प्राप्यलभ्यते । अन्यस्य युवयोरन्यतमस्य हरी अश्वौ रजांसि लोकाः । अत्र लोकशब्दो जनवाचकः । ते यजमानरूपा जना इत्यर्थः । ते च मथा प्रमथनेनालोडनेन निष्पादितैर्वाजैरन्नैः क्षीरादिरूपैर्घोष्यैः स्तुतिभिश्चाह्वानादिशब्दविशिष्टैर्वा पीपयन्त । आप्याययन्ति ॥

*(Gist: the Aśvins' golden chariot comes at will to our sacrificial houses; the people, as sacrificers, feed their horses with offerings and praises. Reading doubtful in several words [?].)*

**Pratipadārtha** — (*he*) **aśvinā** — O Aśvin deities; **vāṃ** — among you two (of the one); (**kakuhaḥ** — the best one); **piśaṅgarūpaḥ** — golden-formed (yellow-hued); **vaśān anu** — following the wishes (desires) (as the mind wills); **ni cheruḥ** — moves about; [or **vaśān** — self-governed … — continues on the next page].

### Printed p. 573  (PDF 593)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 573.)*

**Pratipadārtha (continued)** — **kakuhaḥ anu** — following the quarters and intermediate quarters; **ni cheruḥ** — moves about up and down, in every direction] (that chariot); **sadanāni** — to our sacrificial houses; **pra gamyāḥ** — may it come specially; **anyasya** — of the other one; **harī** — the horses; **rajāṃsi** — the people in the form of sacrificers; **mathā** — by churning (produced); **vājaiḥ** — with food in the form of *āmikṣā* etc. (and); **ghoṣyaiḥ** — with praises; **vi pīpayanta** — they satisfy.

**Bhāvārtha** — O Aśvin deities, may that chariot belonging to one of you two, yellow-hued, moving in all the quarters and intermediate quarters, come to our sacrificial houses; and the sacrificers satisfy the horses of the other with *āmikṣā* and other foods prepared by churning, and with hymns.

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"Ashwins, may the golden–coloured (car of one of you) traversing at will, the quarters of space, come to our dwellings ; may mankind encourage the horses of the other by food, by friction, and by shouts."

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In the previous ṛk the Aśvin deities were described as the Sun, Moon and Earth [? "Sūrya-Candra-mas…" as read]; in this ṛk the order of motion of their chariot and its attractive colour are described.

> अश्विना परि वामिषः पुरोचीरीयुर्गीर्भिर्यतमाना अमृध्राः ।
> रथो ह वामृतेजा अद्रिजूतः परि द्यावापृथिवी याति सद्यः ॥

> *aśvinā pari vāmiṣaḥ purocīrīyurgīrbhiryatamānā amṛdhrāḥ |*
> *ratho ha vāmṛtejā adrijūtaḥ pari dyāvāpṛthivī yāti sadyaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-58-8 [?])

> यूयं हि देवीरृतयुग्भिरश्वैः परिप्रयाथ भुवनानि सद्यः ।
> प्रबोधयन्तीरुषसः ससन्तं द्विपाच्चतुष्पाच्चरथाय जीवम् ॥

> *yūyaṃ hi devīrṛtayugbhiraśvaiḥ pariprayātha bhuvanāni sadyaḥ |*
> *prabodhayantīruṣasaḥ sasantaṃ dvipāccatuṣpāccarathāya jīvam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-51-5 [?]) — as described in these ṛks etc., their chariot is of unobstructed motion in all the quarters, and goes round heaven, earth and the intermediate region, both at will and independently. This sense is conveyed by the sentence "*pra vāṃ nicheruḥ kakuho vaśāṃ anu*".

The word **kakuhaḥ** is read among the names of the great (*mahat*) (Ni. 3-13 [?]); hence, as an epithet of the chariot, it may mean an exceedingly excellent chariot. Or, **kakuhaḥ anu** may be taken to mean "in the ten quarters (moving independently)". The Nirukta-author has shown that the two words *kakubh* and *kakuha* are formed from the same root. The epithet **piśaṅgarūpaḥ** has been added to show the attractive colour of that chariot as it moves.

### Printed p. 574  (PDF 594)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 574.)*

For the word **piśaṅgarūpaḥ** Sāyaṇa has explained "*hiraṇyarūpaḥ, pītavarṇo vā bahubhir aśvādyavayavair nirūpyamāṇo vā rathaḥ*": a chariot of golden hue — or of yellow colour, or one that is described by many parts such as horses etc. — that is, one with a golden or white lustre, or a chariot described as endowed with many-coloured gold. When the time of appearance and of travel of the Aśvin deities is understood, the nature of this colour is understood.

> कृष्णा यद्गोष्वरुणीषु सीदद्दिवो नपाताश्विना हुवे वाम् ।

> *kṛṣṇā yadgoṣvaruṇīṣu sīdaddivo napātāśvinā huve vām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-61-4 [?])

> आ तेन यातं मनसो जवीयसा रथं यं वामृभवश्चक्रुरश्विना ।
> यस्य योगे दुहिता जायते दिव उभे अहनी सुदिने विवस्वतः ॥

> *ā tena yātaṃ manaso javīyasā rathaṃ yaṃ vāmṛbhavaścakruraśvinā |*
> *yasya yoge duhitā jāyate diva ubhe ahanī sudine vivasvataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-12 [?]) — in ṛks such as these it is told that, when Uṣas (Dawn) with her splendour makes all beings glad, and drives away the enemies, and while the sun is rising, the Aśvin deities too, in order to go to the sacrificial place, prepare their chariot, and prayer is made for their coming. At this time the rising of Uṣas, the kindling of Agni, and the rising of Aruṇa all together make the chariot of the Aśvin deities golden-hued. In describing this very arrangement, the scholar Max Mullar [sic] has said thus:

> "Thus the appearance of the Aswins, the kindling of the sacrificial fire, the break of dawn are synchronous with the first appearanee [sic] of the Sun's rays or more correctly the appearance of the light on the earth reflected from an immense number of meteors circulating around the Sun in or near the ecliptic and extending out somewhat beyond the orbit of the earth. Such meteors are more numerous precisely opposite to the sun and they cause the corralative [sic] and complementary phenomena of the reflection both thus giving rise to the laborate [sic] celestial Phenomena. connected by the Vedic Deities, the Asvinau. (अश्विनौ)"

> *"Thus the appearance of the Aswins, the kindling of the sacrificial fire, the break of dawn are synchronous with the first appearanee [sic] of the Sun 's rays or more correctly the appearance of the light on the earth reflected from an immense number of meteors circulating around the Sun in or near the ecliptic and extending out somewhat beyond the orbit of the earth. Such meteors are more numerous precisely opposite to the sun and they cause the corralative [sic] and complementary phenomena of the reflection both thus giving rise to the laborate [sic] celestial Phenomena. connected by the Vedic Deities, the Asvinau. (aśvinau)"*

(Science of Language. Vol. II.) — As thus described, as an example of the sentence-arrangement of the chariot of the Aśvin deities, which gives the chariot its golden form, the following ṛk is cited:

> अबोध्यग्निर्ज्म उदेति सूर्यो व्युषाश्चन्द्रा मह्यावो अर्चिषा ।
> आयुक्षातामश्विना यातवे रथं प्रासावीद्देवः सविता जगत्पृथक् ॥

> *abodhyagnirjma udeti sūryo vyuṣāścandrā mahyāvo arciṣā |*
> *āyukṣātāmaśvinā yātave rathaṃ prāsāvīddevaḥ savitā jagatpṛthak ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-157-1)

### Printed p. 575  (PDF 595)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 25"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 575.)*

*(Special Topics, continued.)* In this ṛk it is prayed that, with such splendour, the Aśvins should come to the house of the sacrifice, seated in the chariot that illumines the golden colour and draws the whole world towards it.

**Sadanāni** — this word can also mean "the intermediate regions"; but in the present context the purport is "sacrificial houses".

**Rajāṃsi** — the other special senses of this word have been told before; in the ṛk at hand it is taken as "world", and then the people of all the worlds — that is, the people as sacrificers — are meant. Sāyaṇa has explained the purport of the word thus: "*rajāṃsi lokāḥ ǀ atra lokaśabdo janavācakaḥ ǀ te yajamānarūpā janā ityarthaḥ*".

**Pīpayanta** — formed from the root *ōpyāyī vṛddhau* (*pyai*) in the sense of growth. This word is used both in the sense of "growth" and of "gladness".

> पीपाय स श्रवसा मर्त्येषु यो अग्नये ददाश विप्र उक्थैः ।

> *pīpāya sa śravasā martyeṣu yo agnaye dadāśa vipra ukthaiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-10-3 [?])

> उत वां विक्षु मद्यास्वन्धो गाव आपश्च पीपयन्त देवीः ।

> *uta vāṃ vikṣu madyāsvandho gāva āpaśca pīpayanta devīḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-143-4 [?]) — in ṛks such as these both senses are suggested. In the ṛk at hand also the sense is that the praise addressed to the Aśvin deities, and the food too, being full, give them perfect gladness.

**Ghoṣyaiḥ** — the word *ghoṣa* is read among the names of speech (Ni. 1-11 [?]). Though this word generally means "sound", it is used in the sense of showing a special power in that sound. In the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas etc. the word *ghoṣa* means a sound possessing a supernatural (*alaukika*) power.

> वि रोदसी अतपद्घोष एषाम् ।

> *vi rodasī atapadghoṣa eṣām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-10 [?]);

> अयामि घोष इन्द्र ।

> *ayāmi ghoṣa indra |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-93-2 [?]) — in Saṃhitā sentences such as these; and

> ता वा एताः सर्वा ऋचः सर्वे वेदाः सर्वे घोषा एकैव व्याहृतिः ।

> *tā vā etāḥ sarvā ṛcaḥ sarve vedāḥ sarve ghoṣā ekaiva vyāhṛtiḥ |*

(Ai. Ā. 1-3-2 [?]);

> मयि स्तोभो, मयि स्तोमो, मयि श्लोको मयि घोषो मयि यशः ।

> *mayi stobho, mayi stomo, mayi śloko mayi ghoṣo mayi yaśaḥ |*

(Ai. Ā. 3-1-3 [?]);

> येनेदमन्नं पच्यते यदिदमद्यते तस्यैष घोषो भवति ।

> *yenedamannaṃ pacyate yadidamadyate tasyaiṣa ghoṣo bhavati |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-9-1-? [?]);

> सर्वे स्वरा घोषवन्तो बलवन्तो वक्तव्याः ।

> *sarve svarā ghoṣavanto balavanto vaktavyāḥ |*

(Bhā. U. 2-22-3 [?]) — in such places also the word is used in the sense of a sound that is supernatural and possesses power. In the Ṛk at hand the meaning is: sound in the form of praise.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly): *kakuhaḥ* — from the word *kakubh*, *ha*-substitution for *bh* in Vedic usage; second (case) in plural, another form; *piśaṅgarūpaḥ* — a bahuvrīhi, by "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 [?]) the former member keeps its own accent; *gamyāḥ* — root *gam ṛ gatau*; "*vyatyayo bahulam*" gives the *liṅ* (ending) of the third person singular, with second-person singular ending; "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" gives *luk* for *vikaraṇa*; *yāsuṭ* augment; *tiṅ* accent *nighāta*; *pīpayanta* — root *ōpyāyī vṛddhau*, *pī* substituted for the root in Vedic usage; *ṇic*, doubling; by "*bahulaṃ chandasy-māṅyoge 'pi*"… no *āḍāgama*; by *vyatyaya* the *ṇic* accent remains; *aśvinā* — "*supāṃ sulug…*" gives ā-substitution for the case ending (au); vocative gets *nighāta* accent; *ghoṣyaiḥ* — *ghuṣir viśabdane*, *ṇyat* suffix; "*pugantalaghūpadhasya ca*" gives guṇa of the penultimate short vowel; "*ñit-ādir-nityam*" gives initial acute. (All sūtra numerals small type: `[?]`.)  ‖ 5 ‖

> एवैरन्यस्य पीपयन्त वाजैर्वेषन्तीरूर्ध्वा नद्यो न आगुः ॥ ६ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> प्र । वां । शरत्ऽवान् । वृषभः । न । निःऽसाट् । पूर्वीः । इषः । चरति । मध्वः । इष्णन् ।

### Printed p. 577  (PDF 597)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 26"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 577.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (continued)**

> न । वर्षिता यथेन्द्रः । स इव शत्रूणां निष्षाट् निःसारयिता सन् पूर्वीर्बह्वीः पुरातनीर्वेषोऽन्नानि ससस्यादीन्यृद्ध्यै प्र चरति । प्रकर्षेण गच्छति । मध्यमस्थानश्चन्द्र इति पक्षे शरद्वाञ्छरत्कालवान् । तस्मिन्नृतौ हि चन्द्रः संनद्धो भवति । तेन च तृणगुल्मौषध्यादीनि वर्धन्ते । स किमर्थमेवं करोतीत्युच्यते । मध्वः इष्णन् मधुनो मधुसदृशस्य हविषः । किमर्थं हविष इष्णन् । हविरिच्छन् । तदर्थमेवं करोति । तथान्यस्येत्यादित्यस्यैवैः कामैर्गमनैर्वा निमित्तैर्भूतैः पीपयन्ते । आप्याययन्ति हविर्भिर्यजमानाः । तुष्ट्येन तेन प्रेरिता वेषन्तीर्व्याप्नुवन्तीः ऊर्ध्वा उन्नता उत्तीरा नद्यो न नदनशीला यथा नोऽस्मदर्थमागुः आगच्छन्ति ॥

*(Sanskrit as read; several words doubtful [?]. Gist: one of the Aśvins is "autumnal" (Moon) who, like Indra, drives off foes and moves about for the offering; the other's horses the sacrificers feed with oblations, and blessings come flowing like swollen rivers.)*

**Pratipadārtha** — (*he aśvinau* — O Aśvin deities!) **śaradvān** — the one who makes clouds, trees, leaves etc. wither (or: the one endowed with the autumn season); **vṛṣabhaḥ na** — like Indra, the rain-giver of desires; **niṣṣāṭ** — the one who drives away foes; **vāṃ** — among you two (the one, the Moon); **pūrvīḥ** — manifold, or ancient; **iṣaḥ** — foods (as the object); **madhvaḥ** — the sweet-flavoured oblation; **iṣṇan** — desiring; **pra carati** — moves forth, wandering about (**tathā** — likewise); **anyasya** — of the other one, of the Āditya (Sun) of the upper world; **evaiḥ** — with desires, or with goings (with respect to them); **vājaiḥ pīpayanta** — they (the sacrificers) gladden him with oblations etc. (by him, thus gladdened, being impelled); **veṣantīḥ** — pervading ones (fruits); **ūrdhvāḥ** — overflowing the banks, running; **nadyaḥ (na)** — like rivers; **naḥ** — to us; **ā guḥ** — come.

**Bhāvārtha** — O Aśvin deities, one of you two is the Moon of the middle region, the one who makes clouds etc. wither (that is, who has the nature of autumn), who, like Indra, drives away foes, and who, longing for oblations and the like, moves about bestowing abundant food; the sacrificers please the other with oblations and the like, and through him the fruits of sacrifice come, like river waters overflowing the banks.

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"(One of you), the disperser (of the clouds), like Indra, the annihilator (of his foes), desirous of the oblation, proceeds, (bestowing) abundant food. (Devout worshippers) cherish with (sacrificial) viands, (the faculties) of the other, for the sake of favours, wich [sic] flow upon us like swelling rivers."  XIII 37

### Printed p. 578  (PDF 598)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 578.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

One of the Aśvin deities has the epithet **śaradvān**. Sāyaṇa has given two senses to this epithet. First: "*śaradvān śaraṇavān meghavṛkṣaparṇādīnāṃ viśaraṇavān*" — that is, one who, in due season, makes trees and leaves etc. wither completely. The Nirukta-author, explaining this sense, has given this derivation for the word:

> शरच्छीर्णा अस्यामोषधयो भवन्ति । शीर्णा आप इति वा ।

> *śaracchīrṇā asyāmoṣadhayo bhavanti | śīrṇā āpa iti vā |*

(Ni. 4-25 [?]) — in this season the herbs ripen, or the river-currents have subsided; therefore it is named *śarat* (autumn). As the Moon prompts both of these functions, the epithet **śaradvān** here is applied to the Aśvin deity in the form of the Moon. Or, in the second sense, "*bahusaṃvatsaraḥ pūrvatano nityaḥ*" — one who has many years, that is, who is eternal. To state this sense, the ṛk-sentences of the Saṃhitā themselves may be taken as basis. For example:

> तच्चक्षुर्देवहितं शुक्रमुच्चरत् ।
> पश्येम शरदः शतं जीवेम शरदः शतम् ॥

> *taccakṣurdevahitaṃ śukramuccarat |*
> *paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ śatam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-16)

> दीर्घायुरस्या यः पतिर्जीवाति शरदः शतम् ।

> *dīrghāyurasyā yaḥ patirjīvāti śaradaḥ śatam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-39 [?]) — in all such ṛks the word *śarad* means a year composed of autumns. Accordingly, in the ṛk at hand also the meaning "one who has many years", that is, "eternal", has been given by the commentator.

**Niṣṣāṭ** — (*śatrūṇāṃ niḥsārayitā*) one who drives enemies out, having made them flee. The Nirukta-author also, citing the ṛk in which this word is used:

> अभी३ दमेकमेको अस्मि निष्षाळभी द्वा किमु त्रयः करन्ति ।
> खले न पर्षान्प्रति हन्मि भूरि किं मा निन्दन्ति शत्रवोऽनिन्द्राः ॥

> *abhī3 damekameko asmi niṣṣāḷabhī dvā kimu trayaḥ karanti |*
> *khale na parṣānprati hanmi bhūri kiṃ mā nindanti śatravo 'nindrāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-48-7 [?]), has explained: "*niṣṣahamāṇaḥ śatrūn abhibhavāmi*" — "I overcome the enemies, crushing them", that is, "I make them yield". In the ṛk at hand also the meaning is: one fit to drive away enemies.

---

### Printed p. 579  (PDF 599)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 26"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 579.)*

**Evaiḥ** — "*kāmyair ayanair vā*" (Ni. 12-21 [?]) — showing independent, unobstructed motion (of the Maruts, who are friends of Indra), this word is in general used of one who ever has the nature of moving. But in the ṛk at hand it is an epithet of the Sun-formed deity (one of the Aśvins).

**Pīpayanta** — from the root *pyai* this word, formed in the sense of "cause to grow" or "make manifest", has both these senses; the special senses of both have been told in the preceding ṛk with examples.

**Veṣantīḥ** — formed from the root *viṣ* in the sense of pervading; in general in places where this is used both senses are chief:

> अव स्म यस्य वेषणे स्वेदं पथिषु जुह्वति ।
> अभीमह स्वजेन्यं भूमा पृष्ठेव रुरुहुः ॥

> *ava sma yasya veṣaṇe svedaṃ pathiṣu juhvati |*
> *abhīmaha svajenyaṃ bhūmā pṛṣṭheva ruruhuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-7-3 [?]) — in places such as this, in the sense of "*paricaryā* work", i.e. rites like worship; in the ṛk at hand, "pervade". But:

> नि यद्युवेथे नियुतः सुदानू उप स्वधाभिः सृजथः पुरंधिम् ।
> प्रेषद्वेषद्वातो न सूरिरा महे ददे सुव्रतो न वाजम् ॥

> *ni yadyuvethe niyutaḥ sudānū upa svadhābhiḥ sṛjathaḥ puraṃdhim |*
> *preṣadveṣadvāto na sūrirā mahe dade suvrato na vājam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-180-6) — here Sāyaṇa has explained that if it is formed from the root *viṣ* the meaning is "pervading", and if from the root *iṣ* it is "desiring". In the ṛk at hand it means only "pervading everywhere": that is, the fruits come in abundance to the sacrificers.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly): *śaradvān* — "*śaradaḥ asya santi*"; suffix *matup*; "*māduṣ-padhāyāś ca*" gives *va* for *ma*; the suffix, having *p*, is unaccented; *niṣṣāṭ* — root *saha marṣaṇe*, suffix *ṇvi* by "*chandasi sahaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-63 [?]); "*ata upadhāyāḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116 [?]) gives vṛddhi of the penultimate; "*sahes sāḍaḥ saḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-56 [?]) gives *ṣa* for the root's *sa*; the accent of the base of a word ending in a *kṛt* suffix; *madhvaḥ* — "*jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam*": no guṇa etc.; genitive in the sense of the object (*karmārtha*).

### Printed p. 580  (PDF 600)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 580.)*

*(Grammar page, continued, noted briefly):* *iṣṇan* — root *iṣu icchāyām*; *kryādi*; *laṭ* with *śatṛ*-substitution; *śnā* (*vikaraṇa*) by "*kryādibhyaḥ śnā*"; since the suffix has *ś*, *śnā-bhyas-tayor ātaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-112 [?]) elision of the *ā* of the *vikaraṇa*; since *ṭakāra* is the occasion, "*raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade*" gives *ṇa*; the suffix takes initial acute accent; *evaiḥ* — root *iṇ gatau*; "*iṇ-śībhyāṃ van*" (Un. Sū. 1-150 [?]) gives suffix *van*; "*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*" gives guṇa of the root; the suffix being *nit*, initial acute accent; *veṣantīḥ* — root *vī gatyādiṣu*; *laṭ* with *śatṛ*; "*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-34 [?]); the *bahula* gives *śap*; guṇa of the root's *i*; in the feminine, by "*ugitaś ca*" *ṅīp*; *nuṃ* augment; "*supāṃ sulug*" — *jas* following, lengthening of the earlier vowel by *pūrvasavarṇa*; *āguḥ* — root *iṇ gatau*; in Vedic usage *luṅ*; "*iṇo gā luṅi*" (Pā. Sū. 2-4-45 [?]) gives *gā* substitution; when *sic* comes after *laṅ*… by "*gātisthāghupābhū*…" (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77 [?]) its *luk*; "*ātaḥ*" gives *jus* for *jhi*; *pararūpa*; tiṅ-accent *nighāta*.  ‖ 6 ‖

### Sūkta 181, Ṛk 7  (printed p. 580; PDF 600)

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> असर्जि वां स्थविरा वेधसा गीर्बाळ्हे अश्विना त्रेधा क्षरन्ती ।
> उपस्तुताववतं नाधमानं यामन्नयामञ्छृणुतं हवं मे ॥ ७ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> असर्जि । वां । स्थविरा । वेधसा । गीः । बाळ्हे । अश्विना । त्रेधा । क्षरन्ती ।
> उपस्तुतौ । अवतं । नाधमानं । यामन् । अयामन् । शृणुतं । हवं । मे ॥ ७ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे वेधसा विधातारावश्विनौ वां युवयोर्बाळ्हे दृढे स्थैर्ये निमित्तभूते सति गीः स्तुतिरूपा वागसर्जि । सृज्यते । कीदृशी सा । स्थविरात्यन्तं स्थिरा नित्या

> *he vedhasā vidhātārāvaśvinau vāṃ yuvayorbāḷhe dṛḍhe sthairye nimittabhūte sati gīḥ stutirūpā vāgasarji | sṛjyate | kīdṛśī sā | sthavirātyantaṃ sthirā nityā*

### Printed p. 581  (PDF 601)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 26"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 581.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (continued)**

> वेदमयी त्रेधा मन्त्रादिभेदेन त्रिप्रकारा क्षरन्ती युवां गच्छन्ती । ईदृशी स्तुतिः कृतेत्यर्थः । तथोपस्तुतौ सन्तौ नाधमानमभिमतफलं याचमानमवतं । रक्षतं तर्पयतं वा । किंच यामन् गमने ऽयामन्नगमने च हवमाह्वानं शृणुतं ॥

*(Gist: a threefold Veda-made hymn has been offered to you; praised thus, protect and satisfy the suppliant, and hear his call whether travelling or at rest.)*

**Pratipadārtha** — **he vedhasā** — O creators (makers, *sraṣṭṛ*); **aśvinā** — O Aśvin deities; **vāṃ** — of you two; **bāḷhe** — with the aim of a steady (firm) favour; **sthavirā** — exceedingly steady (eternal, or Veda-formed); **tredhā** — threefold, by the divisions *mantra* etc.; **kṣarantī** — flowing, moving towards you; **gīḥ** — praise; **asarji** — has been created (by us); **upastutau** — (so) having been praised; **nādhamānam** — him who solicits the desired fruit; **avataṃ** — protect, or (by granting fruit) satisfy; (**kiṃca** — further); **yāman** — also at the time of going; **ayāman** — also at the time of not moving; **me** — my; **havaṃ** — invocation with praise; **śruṇutaṃ** — hear.

**Bhāvārtha** — O Aśvin deities, makers of creation: this praise of ours, Veda-formed, threefold by *mantra* etc., adhering to you and directed to the aim of your steady favour, — being pleased with it, grant me, the suppliant, the desired fruit and protect me; and hear our invocation with praise both at your times of motion and at your times of rest.

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"Ashwins, creators, the perpetual threefold hymn, addressed to you, has been uttered, (to seeure [sic]) your steady (favour): thus glorified, protect him who solicits (your bounty), and, whether moving or resting, hear his invocation."

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

**Vedhasā** — "*vidhātārau aśvinau*": in this ṛk the Aśvin deities are called the doers of creation. The word *vedhas* is read in the Nirukta among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19 [?]). In many places this word is an epithet of a wise sacrificer. Though in one place the meaning "producer" may be possible, still, in the sense "producer of the sacrificial fruit", the word is not seen used in the sense of the creator of the world. But:

### Printed p. 582  (PDF 602)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 582.)*

> यः पूर्व्याय वेधसे नवीयसे सुमज्जानये विष्णवे ददाशति ।
> यो जातमस्य महतो महि ब्रवत्सेदु श्रवोभिर्युज्यं चिदभ्यसत् ॥

> *yaḥ pūrvyāya vedhase navīyase sumajjānaye viṣṇave dadāśati |*
> *yo jātamasya mahato mahi bravatsedu śravobhiryujyaṃ cidabhyasat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-156-2) — only here, the form of the creator of the world is described; the word *vedhase* is explained as "to the creator of the world in many ways" (*vividha-jagatkartre*). In the ṛk at hand also, Sāyaṇa has said "*vidhātārau aśvinau*". What connection the Aśvin deities have with the creation of the world may be said to be this: on the basis of Śruti-sentences, there is a direct connection between creation and them. For:

> …… एतद्वै प्रजापतिरेतस्मिन्नात्मनः प्रतिहितेऽकामयत प्रजाः सृजेयेति प्रजायेयेति स ऋतुभिरद्भिः प्राणैः संवत्सरेणाश्विभ्यां सयुग्भूत्वैताः प्रजाः प्राजनयत्तथैवैतद्यजमान एताभिर्देवताभिः सयुग्भूत्वैताः प्रजाः प्रजनयति । …… अग्निर्वै वैश्वानरः संवत्सरेण वै सयुग्भूत्वा प्राजनयदश्विनावध्वर्यू सादयतामिह श्वेत्सश्विभ्यां वै सयुग्भूत्वा प्राजनयत् ॥

> *…… etadvai prajāpatiretasminnātmanaḥ pratihite 'kāmayata prajāḥ sṛjeyeti prajāyeyeti sa ṛtubhiradbhiḥ prāṇaiḥ saṃvatsareṇāśvibhyāṃ sayugbhūtvaitāḥ prajāḥ prājanayattathaivaitadyajamāna etābhirdevatābhiḥ sayugbhūtvaitāḥ prajāḥ prajanayati | …… agnirvai vaiśvānaraḥ saṃvatsareṇa vai sayugbhūtvā prājanayadaśvināvadhvaryū sādayatāmiha śvetsaśvibhyāṃ vai sayugbhūtvā prājanayat ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 8-2-2-2 to 9 [?]; Sanskrit as read, doubtful in several words [?]) — Prajāpati, desiring "let me create offspring, let me be born in them", created offspring in union with the seasons, with the waters, with the vital airs, with the year, and with the Aśvin deities. Since it is thus said that the creation of the world has a direct connection with these, in the ṛk at hand the word **vedhasā** may be taken as "*vidhātārau*", that is, those who are creators.

**Bāḷhe** — this word means firm, steady.

> स व्राधतो नहुषो दंसुजूतः शर्धस्तरो नरां गूर्तश्रवाः ।
> विसृष्टरातिर्याति बाळ्हसृत्वा विश्वासु पृत्सु सदमिच्छूरः ॥

> *sa vrādhato nahuṣo daṃsujūtaḥ śardhastaro narāṃ gūrtaśravāḥ |*
> *visṛṣṭarātiryāti bāḷhasṛtvā viśvāsu pṛtsu sadamicchūraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-10) — as here the meaning is "firm" or "steady", so in the ṛk at hand also the praise-sentence is steady.

**Tredhā gīḥ** — the speech is explained as "threefold by the divisions *mantra* etc." And the epithet *sthavirā* is also there. Here it may be three kinds: *ṛc*, *yajus* and *sāman*; or, since the epithets *śastra*, *stoma*, *stotra* are present, and since Sāyaṇa has explained the sense of this word as "*atyantaṃ sthirā nityā vedamayī*", here *ṛc*, *yajus* and *sāman* [the passage continues on the next page].

---

### Printed p. 583  (PDF 603)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 26"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 583.)*

*(Special Topics, continued.)* … these divisions may be pointed to. And when explaining the word *udgītha* in the Upaniṣad,

> वाग्गीर्वाचो ह गिर इत्याचक्षते ।

> *vāggīrvāco ha gira ityācakṣate |*

(Bhā. 1-3-6 [?]) — by sentences such as this the division is shown: the three divisions of *śastra* etc., and the three *mantras* *ṛc* etc.; these will be explained later.

**Yāman, ayāman** — Sāyaṇa has explained these words as "*gamane, agamane ca*". The word *yāman* is used in many places and not in one sense; its meaning must be told according to the context. In many places Skandasvāmin, explaining this word, says "*yāmanty asmin devatā dvijātayaś ca iti yāmano yajñaḥ*" — "the deities and the twice-born come here, hence *yāma* means sacrifice" [as read, [?]]. It is formed from the root *yā prāpaṇe*. In each context the commentators' tendency gives different meanings. For example:

> अजोहवीन्नासत्या करा वां महे यामन्पुरुभुजा पुरंधिः ।

> *ajohavīnnāsatyā karā vāṃ mahe yāmanpurubhujā puraṃdhiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-13 [?]) — for the word *yāman* in this ṛk Sāyaṇa explains "*yāti gacchatīti yāmaḥ stotram*" (praise), while Skandasvāmin explains "*yāmanti yoddhāro yasmin sa yāmaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ*" — "where warriors go, that is *yāma*, battle", the sense of war here; and

> इन्द्रं नमस्यन्नुपमेभिरर्कैर्यः स्तोत्रे भ्यो हव्यो अस्ति यामन् ।

> *indraṃ namasyannupamebhirarkairyaḥ stotre bhyo havyo asti yāman |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-33-2 [?]) — for the word *yāman* in this ṛk Sāyaṇa explains "battle", and Skandasvāmin "sacrifice". In the ṛk at hand also the words *yāman; ayāman* may mean "going" and "not going", or "at the time of the sacrifice" and "at a time without sacrifice", or "at the time of battle" and "at a time without battle". The meaning is: hear our praise and be satisfied at all these times.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly): *asarji* — root *sṛj visarge*; in Vedic usage *luṅ* in the passive; "*ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-66 [?]) gives *ciṇ*-substitution for *cli*; with that as occasion, guṇa of the root's short penultimate; "*ciṇo luk*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-104 [?]) elision of the *ta* suffix following; *āḍāgama* to the base; being in a *pādādi* position there is no *nighāta* accent; the augment having the acute, the first syllable becomes acute.

### Printed p. 584  (PDF 604)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 584.)*

*(Grammar page, continued, noted briefly):* *sthavirā* — root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; "*ajiraśiśira…*" (Un. Sū. 1-53 [?]) gives suffix *kirac* as an irregular formation ending in the suffix; the suffix's accent makes the middle syllable acute; in the feminine, as it ends in *a*, *ṭāp*; *vedhasā* — "*supāṃ sulug*" gives ā-substitution for the dual; vocative: *nighāta* accent; *tredhā* — "*dhā ca*" (Pā. Sū. 5-3-45 [?]): suffix *edhācc* added to *tri* in the sense of manner; "*yasyeti ca*" elides the *i*; "*citaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 [?]) gives acute on the last syllable; *kṣarantī* — root *kṣar sañcalane*; *laṭ* with *śatṛ*-substitution; "*ugitaś ca*" (Pā. Sū. 4-1-6 [?]) gives *ṅīp* in the feminine; the *sārvadhātuka l* being unaccented, the root's accent remains; *upastutau* — *upa* + *ṣṭuñ stutau*; "*striyāṃ ktin*" gives suffix *ktin*; "*tādau ca niti*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50 [?]) gives the *gati* (*upa*) its own accent; *nādhamānam* — root *nāthṛ yācñāyām*; *laṭ*, *śānac*-substitution; *śap*; "*āneṃuk*" gives *muk* augment; "*tāsyanudāttet…*" the *sārvadhātuka l* being unaccented, the root's accent remains; *yāman* — root *yā prāpaṇe*; suffix *manin*; "*supāṃ sulug*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) gives *luk* for the locative; so also in *ayāman*, *luk* has come; the *nañ* has the special accent of its own nature (*prakṛti-svara*); *śruṇutaṃ* — root *śru śravaṇe*; *loṭ* second-person dual; *nighāta* accent.  ‖ 7 ‖

### Sūkta 181, Ṛk 8  (printed p. 584; PDF 604)

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> उत स्या वां रुशतो वप्ससो गीः प्रि बर्हिषि सदसि पिन्वते नॄन् ।
> वृषा वां मेघो वृषणा पीपाय गोर्न सेके मनुषो दशस्यन् ॥ ८ ॥

> *uta syā vāṃ ruśato vapsaso gīḥ pri barhiṣi sadasi pinvate nṝn |*
> *vṛṣā vāṃ megho vṛṣaṇā pīpāya gorna seke manuṣo daśasyan ‖ 8 ‖*
