### Printed p. 585  (PDF 605)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 26"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 585.)*

*(Correction of the Saṃhitā of Ṛk 8 given on the previous page, now that the Pada is seen: the printed word-group is* **गीस्त्रिबर्हिषि** *(gīs-tribarhiṣi), i.e. "gīḥ" + "tribarhiṣi" — not "गीः प्रि बर्हिषि". Earlier lines are not altered.)*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> उत । स्या । वां । रुशतः । वप्ससः । गीः । त्रिऽबर्हिषि । सदसि । पिन्वते । नॄन् ।
> वृषा । वां । मेघः । वृषणा । पीपाय । गोः । न । सेके । मनुषः । दशस्यन् ॥ ८ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ वां युवयोः रुशतो दीप्तस्य वप्ससो रूपस्यैव वपुषो वा ख्यापयित्री गीः स्तुतिवाक् त्रिबर्हिषि त्रिधातास्तीर्णबर्हिष्के सदसि यागसदने नॄन् कर्मनेतॄनस्मान् पिन्वते । आप्याययतु वोचितहविःप्रदानादिना । केन प्रकारेण उच्यते । हे वृषणा वर्षितारौ कामानां वां युवयोः स्वभूतो मेघः सेक्ता जलदः प्रदानविशेषो वा वृषा वर्षकः सन् मनुषो मनुष्यान् प्रति दशस्यन् प्रयच्छन् पीपाय । आप्यायते । गोर्न सेके उदकसेक इव शान्तेनात्मैक उदकस्येव तद्यथाप्याययति तद्वदित्यर्थः । यद्वा । नेति संप्रत्यर्थे । गोरुदकस्य सेके निमित्तभूते सति पीपायेति संबन्धः ॥

*(Sanskrit as read; the middle of the passage is doubtful [?]. Gist: this praise of your radiant form gladdens us, the leaders of the rite, in the sacred hall; and your rain-cloud rains on men, as a sprinkling of water refreshes.)*

**Pratipadārtha** — **he aśvinau** — O Aśvin deities; **vāṃ** — of you two; **ruśataḥ** — brilliant; **vapsasaḥ** — of form (of the body, which gives its accomplishment); **gīḥ** — the word in the form of praise; **tribarhiṣi** — with three layers (of sacred grass) strewn; **sadasi** — in the sacrificial hall; **nṝn** — us, the leaders of rites; **pinvate** — gladdens with proper gifts etc., or may it gladden; **uta** — and; **he vṛṣaṇā** — O Aśvin deities, who rain down desires; **vāṃ** — your own; **vṛṣā** — rain-giving; **meghaḥ** — the cloud; **manuṣaḥ** — with reference to men; **daśasyan** — bestowing rain; **goḥ sekena** *(as printed "goḥ seke na")* — as is the joy produced by a sprinkling of water; [or **goḥ seke** — when the sprinkling of water is the occasion; **na** — now; **manuṣaḥ** — with reference to men; **daśasyan** — giving rain]; **pīpāya** — gladdens.

**Bhāvārtha** — O Aśvin deities, this praise in the form of speech of ours, who praise your resplendent bodies, gladdens us, who perform the rite in this sacrificial hall strewn threefold with sacred grass. And, O Aśvin deities, who rain desires, your cloud, the cause of rain, raining for your own men when water is needed, satisfies them.

### Printed p. 586  (PDF 606)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 181"; page 586.)*

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"May the praise of your resplendent forms, (uttered) in the hall of sacrifice, thrice strewn with sacred grass, bring prosperity to the conductors (of the sacrifice). Showerers (of benefits), may the raining-cloud, proceeding to man, nourish him like a sprinkling of water."

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk the two words **ruśataḥ**, **vapsasaḥ** are epithets of **gīḥ**; and they suggest the special qualities of the speech in the form of praise.

**Ruśataḥ** — "*ruśad iti varṇanāma ǀ rocater jvalatikarmaṇaḥ ǀ*" (Ni. 2-20 [?]) — the Nirukta-author explains that *ruśat* is formed from the root *ruc*, which gives the sense "to shine", and means "of bright colour" (white).

**Vapsasaḥ** — the use of this word is very rare; though it is almost all in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, it cannot be missed that it occurs in only a few places. Sāyaṇa explains the word as "a body of beautiful form". That is, as in the ṛk at hand a beautiful body shows forth its beauty, so the praise too shows forth the skill of its beautiful composition.

**Tribarhiṣi** — for this word Sāyaṇa has explained "*tridhā tv āstīrṇabarhiṣke*". Why does it mean "threefold"? The reason why that sense comes here will be told in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-182-1.

From the sentence **vāṃ vṛṣā meghaḥ daśasyan** the relation of cause and effect between rain and the favour of the Aśvin deities is shown. As the Maruts are prayed to, so the Aśvin deities too are in many places prayed to for rain. But in these prayers, and in the epithets used in these contexts, the other special senses must be noted. For example:

> आ न ऊर्जं वहतमश्विना युवं मधुमत्या नः कशया मिमिक्षतम् ।
> प्रायुस्तारिष्टं नी रपांसि मृक्षतं सेधतं द्वेषो भवतं सचाभुवा ॥

> *ā na ūrjaṃ vahatamaśvinā yuvaṃ madhumatyā naḥ kaśayā mimikṣatam |*
> *prāyustāriṣṭaṃ nī rapāṃsi mṛkṣataṃ sedhataṃ dveṣo bhavataṃ sacābhuvā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-157-4) — here the prayer is: "O Aśvin deities, since you two also pour out rain, sprinkle us with the whip (*kaśā*) that has a sweet sound, make us full of vigour" — and likewise …  [the passage continues on the next page].

> *savane ahan triravadyagohanā triradya yajñaṃ madhunā mimikṣatam |*

> त्रिषधस्थे बर्हिषि विश्ववेदसा मध्वा यज्ञं मिमिक्षतम् ॥

> *triṣadhasthe barhiṣi viśvavedasā madhvā yajñaṃ mimikṣatam ‖*

(Ṛ. Sū. 7-1-58 [?]) gives *num* augment; *laṭ* third person singular form; being after a *tiṅ*-final, *nighāta* accent; *vṛṣaṇā* — root *vṛṣu secane*, suffix *kanin* by "*kanin yuvṛṣi…*"; "*supāṃ sulug*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) gives ā for the dual; "*vā ṣapūrvasya nigame*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-9 [?]) the lengthening of the penultimate does not occur; vocative: *nighāta* accent; *pīpāya* — root *ōpyāyī vṛddhau*; "*chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6 [?]) gives *liṭ* in the present sense; "*liṭy-abhyāsasyobhayeṣām*" … *pī* for the root; doubling; *ṇal*, *vṛddhi* of the *ī*; *āy*-substitution; *nighāta*; *seke* — root *ṣicir kṣaraṇe*; suffix *ghañ*; "*pugantalaghūpadhasya ca*" gives guṇa of the penultimate short vowel; "*cajoḥ kuḥ ghiṇṇyatoḥ*" (Pā. ### Sūkta 181, Ṛk 9  (printed p. 588; PDF 608)

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> युवां पूषेवाश्विना पुरंधिरग्निमुषां न जरते हविष्मान् ।
> हुवे यद्वां वरिवस्या गृणानो विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ ९ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> युवां । पूषाऽइव । अश्विना । पुरंऽधिः । अग्निं । उषां । न । जरते । हविष्मान् ।
> हुवे । यत् । वां । वरिवस्या । गृणानः । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरऽदानुम् ॥ ९ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ युवां पुरंधिर्बहुप्रज्ञः पूषेव पोषक इव हविष्मान् हविर्युक्तो जरते । स्तौति । यद्वा । पुरंधिर्बहूनां धारयित्री पूषेव पृथिवीव ॥ द्वितीयार्थे प्रथमा ॥ तां यथा स्तौति तद्वत् । किमिव । अग्निमुषां न । अग्निमुषसं च यथा तथा युवामपि । प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोराश्विनक्रतुवदाग्नेयोषस्योरपि सद्भावादिति भावः । कदेति आह । यद्वा वरिवस्या परिचर्ययायो युक्तो गृणानः स्तोता स्तौति तदा यजमानोऽपि जरते इत्यर्थः । विद्याम । इत्यादि गतम् ॥

*(Sanskrit as read; several words doubtful [?]. Gist: the sacrificer, rich in offerings, praises you two as one praises Agni and Uṣas; and "when I, serving, call you" he asks to gain food, strength and long life — the rest "as already explained".)*

**Pratipadārtha** — **yat** — whenever; **varivasyā** — joined with service; **gṛṇānaḥ** — praising (I); **huve** — (with praise) I invoke; (**tat** — then); (**he**) **aśvinā** — O Aśvin deities; **puraṃdhiḥ** — the highly wise; **pūṣā iva** — like the nourisher; **haviṣmān** — the sacrificer provided with oblations etc.; [or **puraṃdhiḥ** — the supporter of many people; **pūṣā iva** — as one praises Earth]; **agniṃ uṣāṃ na** — as Agni and the goddess Uṣas ([sacrificers] praise at dawn); **jarate** — praises; (**vayaṃ** — we); **iṣaṃ** — food; **vṛjanaṃ** — strength; **jīradānuṃ** — long life; **vidyāma** — may we obtain (through your favour).

**Bhāvārtha** — O Aśvin deities, with devotion I serve you by praise; at the same time the highly wise sacrificer, provided with oblations etc., praises the earth, the supporter of many, … [the passage continues on the next page].

### Printed p. 589  (PDF 609)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 26"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 589.)*

**Bhāvārtha (continued)** — … as one praises the supporter of many, so he praises you two, and also Agni and the goddess Uṣas. Thereafter may we obtain food, strength and long life.

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"The wise offerer of oblations, like Pushan, praises you, Ashwins, as (he would praise) Agni and Ushas, (at the season) at which I invoke you, praising with devotion. that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life."

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Sāyaṇa has shown that two kinds of purport are to be told for this ṛk. First: the words **puraṃdhiḥ**, **pūṣā iva** are epithets of the sacrificer who has oblations. Here **puraṃdhi** is explained as "of much wisdom" and **pūṣā** as "nourisher"; that is, the sacrificer, wise and possessed of oblations, praises you, like a nourisher, with oblations, for your growth. Second: if **puraṃdhiḥ** is an epithet of **pūṣā**, then **puraṃdhi** means "the supporter of many", and **pūṣā** means "the all-nourishing Earth".

For the word *puraṃdhi* the senses *prabhūta*, *pauṣkalya* (plenty) and *samṛddha* are in use. If it is an epithet of the sacrificer, it means one who has various kinds of actions, or one of many kinds of wisdom; or *puraṃdhi* may be a separate deity. All the special senses of this word have been told in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-180-6. And the word **pūṣā** too means "nourisher": either the Sun-form (Agni-form) that nourishes the world by rays, or Earth that nourishes the world with food etc.; the use of this word in this sense has been told in many places. This word is in many contexts used of the Aśvin deities. Since in the ṛk at hand the sense must be told according to context, Sāyaṇa has given another meaning. Through this very explanation, the quality of the deity Pūṣan, one of the twelve Ādityas, is also described.

> पूषा — यद्रश्मिभिः पोषं पुष्यति तत्पूषा भवति ।

> *pūṣā — yadraśmibhiḥ poṣaṃ puṣyati tatpūṣā bhavati |*

(Ni. 12-16 [?]) — the Nirukta-author explains that he is named *Pūṣan* because he nourishes with rays. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also:

### Printed p. 590  (PDF 610)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 25 Sū. 181"; page 590.)*

> इयं वै पूषा पूषेयं हीदं सर्वं पुष्यति यदिदं किंच ।

> *iyaṃ vai pūṣā pūṣeyaṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ puṣyati yadidaṃ kiṃca |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-4-2-? [?]) — it is said that this deity is called *Pūṣan* because it nourishes everything. This sense may refer to the Āditya, or, since the Fire (Agni), being the bearer of oblations, is the cause of the nourishment of all the devas and men, it may refer to Agni. Explaining this same derivation:

> पुष्यन्क्षितिं पोषयति प्रणुदन् रश्मिभिस्तमः ।
> तेनैनमस्तौत्पूषेति भरद्वाजस्तु पञ्चभिः ॥

> *puṣyankṣitiṃ poṣayati praṇudan raśmibhistamaḥ |*
> *tenainamastautpūṣeti bharadvājastu pañcabhiḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-63 [?]) — "destroying darkness, the Earth gains growth, and since he nourishes it he is named *Pūṣan*": the Bṛhaddevatā sentence also suggests the same purport. Thus, since the chief meaning is "nourisher of the world", and since in the ṛk at hand the intention is that the sacrificer, with oblations, increases the sacrifice and helps in the nourishing of the world, here it may mean the sacrificer. Or it may mean Earth.

**Agniṃ uṣāṃ na** — in the Āśvina-śastra, Agni and Uṣas have the chief place among these deities; the fact that the *nareveretas* [?] hymns of praise there refer to Agni and Uṣas will be told later when the subject of the Āśvina-śastra is explained.

> तदाहुर्यच्चस्कृत आग्नेयं कस्यैत उषस्यं कस्यैत ऐन्द्रमथ तस्मादेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षत इत्यश्विनौ हि तदुदजयतामुश्विनावाश्नुवाथां यदश्विनावुदजयतामश्विनावाश्नुवाथां तस्मादेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षते ॥

> *tadāhuryaccaskṛta āgneyaṃ kasyaita uṣasyaṃ kasyaita aindramatha tasmādetadāśvinamityācakṣata ityaśvinau hi tadudajayatāmuśvināvāśnuvāthāṃ yadaśvināvudajayatāmaśvināvāśnuvāthāṃ tasmādetadāśvinamityācakṣate ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 12-3 [?]; Sanskrit as read, garbled in print; several words doubtful [?]) — in this context, since mantras are to be recited aiming at Agni, Indra and Uṣas, an objection arises: how did the name "Āśvina" come to all these? The reply, that this is mainly connected with the victory of the Aśvin deities and therefore the name is given to these mantras, is told here, showing the greatness of the Aśvin deities. In the ṛk at hand also, the sentence **agniṃ, uṣāṃ na jarate** suggests the same item.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly): *pūṣā iva* — root *puṣ vṛddhau*; "*śnasnaksan pūṣan*" (Un. Sū. 1-158 [?]) — a *kani*-ending form (*pūṣan*) is formed irregularly; in Vedic usage the first (case) occurs in the sense of the second.

### Sūkta 182  (printed p. 591; PDF 611)

**The hundred and eighty-second Sūkta**

*(Anukramaṇikā and use, three layers)*

> अभूदिदमित्यृष्टर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तमाश्विनं जागतं । अवविद्धमिति षष्ठी तद्वां नरा नासत्यावित्यष्टमी चोभे त्रिष्टुभौ । अभूदिदमुष्वो षष्ट्यन्ते त्रिष्टुभावित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्जागते छन्दस्यस्य विनियोगः । तथा च सूत्रितं । अभूदिदं यो वां परिज्मेति तिस्र इति । आ. ४-१५ । इति ॥

*(Sanskrit as read; the "ṣaṣṭyante" phrase is as printed [?]; Āśvalāyana reference "4-15" [?].)*

**Anuvāda** — The Sūkta beginning *abhūdidam* is the third Sūkta in the twenty-fourth Anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. The ṛṣi of this Sūkta is Agastya; the deity is the Aśvin deities themselves; the metre is *Jagatī*. But the sixth ṛk (*avaviddhaṃ*) and the eighth ṛk (*tadvāṃ narā nāsatyā*) are in the *Triṣṭubh* metre. The Anukramaṇikā says: "*abhūdidam uṣvo ṣaṣṭyante triṣṭubhau*". At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka-mantras, this Sūkta is used for the *Jagatī* ṛks of the Āśvina-śastra, as the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra explains with the sūtra "*abhūdidaṃ yo vāṃ parijmeti trīṇi*" (Ā. 4-15 [?]).

### Sūkta 182, Ṛk 1  (printed p. 592; PDF 612)

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> अभूदिदं वयुनमो षु भूषता रथो वृषण्वान्मदता मनीषिणः ।
> धियंजिन्वा धिष्ण्या विश्पलावसू दिवो नपाता सुकृते शुचिव्रता ॥ १ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> अभूत् । इदं । वयुनं । ओ इति । सु । भूषत । रथः । वृषण्ऽवान् । मदत । मनीषिणः ।
> धियंऽजिन्वा । धिष्ण्या । विश्पलावसू इति । दिवः । नपाता । सुऽकृते । शुचिऽव्रता ॥ १ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे मनीषिणो मनस्विनो मेधाविन ऋत्विजः अस्माकमिदं वयुनं प्रज्ञानमभूत् । उत्पन्नं । कीदृशं तदिति उच्यते । वृषण्वानभिमतवर्षणवान्रथोऽश्विनोः संबन्धी गमनसाधनो रथ आगत इति शेषः । तत्पाद्वश्विनावो षु भूषत । ओ इति निपातद्वयसमुदायात्मक एको निपातः । सुष्ठु भूषत । अभिमुखा भवत स्तोतुं । तौ द्वौ शौ महानुभावावश्विनौ मदत । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थोऽयं । मदयत । संभावयत । अश्विनौ विशेष्यते । सुकृते सुष्ठु कृतवते मह्यं धियंजिन्वा कर्मणो बुद्धेर्वा प्रीणयितारौ धिष्ण्या धिषणार्हौ स्तुत्यौ विश्पलावसू विशां प्रजानामस्माकं पालयित्र्यधनौ विश्पलाख्यायाश्विन्नजङ्घायो हिरण्मयजङ्घाप्रदानेन तथाभूतौ । सद्यो जङ्घामायसीं विश्पलायै । ऋ. १-११६-१५ । इत्यादिनिगमः । दिव आदित्यस्य नपाता नप्तारौ नपातयितारौ वा शुचिव्रता दीप्तकर्माणौ । ईदृशावश्विनौ मदत ॥

*(Sanskrit as read; several words doubtful [?] — e.g. "tatpādvaśvināvo", "viśpalākhyā…", "…jaṅghā…". The quoted nigama is Ṛ. 1-116-15 as printed. Gist: O wise priests, our insight has arisen and the Aśvins' showering chariot has come; adorn yourselves for them and gladden the Aśvins, the radiant grandsons of Heaven, helpers of Viśpalā.)*

### Printed p. 593  (PDF 613)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 593.)*

**Pratipadārtha** — (*he*) **manīṣiṇaḥ** — O wise (intelligent) priests; **vṛṣaṇvān** — showering desired things; **rathaḥ** — (of the Aśvin deities) the chariot; (**āgataḥ** — has come, is implied); **idaṃ** — this; **vayunaṃ** — knowledge; **abhūt** — (to us) has arisen; **o ṣu bhūṣata** — (the Aśvin deities in that chariot) adorn well (praise); **sukṛte** — to (me) who has well done the rites; **dhiyaṃjinvā** — impellers of rite (knowledge); **dhiṣṇyā** — worthy of knowledge (praise); **viśpalāvasū** — those whose wealth protects the people (or: those who gave a golden leg to Viśpalā, whose leg was cut); **divaḥ** — of the Āditya; **napātā** — the grandsons; **śucivratā** — those of radiant works (who do pure works) — **madata** — gladden (the Aśvin deities with worship etc.).

**Bhāvārtha** — O priests, men of knowledge, it has come to us to know that the chariot of the Aśvin deities, who fulfil desires, has arrived; therefore, ready to worship them, gladden with worship etc. those who are the impellers of me, the performer of rites, who are worthy of praise, whose wealth protects the people, the grandsons of the Āditya, who ever do pure works.

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"The information, sage (priests), has been received : be ready with your praises, for the (benefit) showering car (of the Ashwins has arrived) : propitiate (the divinities) for they show favour to the doer of good works : they are entitled to praise, rich in benevolence to mankind, the grandsons of heaven, and observers of holy rites."  XIII 38

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

**Vayunaṃ** — the word *vayuna* is read among the names of knowledge (Ni. 3-13 [?]); "*vayunaṃ vetheḥ kāntir vā prajñā vā*" (Ni. 5-13 [?]): formed from the root *vī*, which gives the sense of "to go, to wish", it gives the sense of desire or knowledge. The Nirukta-author, citing the ṛk

> स इत्तमोऽवयुनं ततन्वत्सूर्येण वयुनवच्चकार ।
> कदा ते मर्ता अमृतस्य धामेयक्षन्तो न मिनन्ति स्वधावः ॥

> *sa ittamo 'vayunaṃ tatanvatsūryeṇa vayunavaccakāra |*
> *kadā te martā amṛtasya dhāmeyakṣanto na minanti svadhāvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-21-3 [?]; first line as read [?]), explains "*sa tenoऽprajñānaṃ tatanvat stotaṃ sūryeṇa prajñānavac cakāra*" (Ni. 5-13 [?]) — that it gives the sense that he spread the darkness-of-ignorance, and by the Sun made it knowledge-bearing, i.e. made what was in the form of darkness and beyond the reach of the senses an object of knowledge.

### Printed p. 594  (PDF 614)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 594.)*

> अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान्विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् ।
> युयोध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नम उक्तिं विधेम ॥

> *agne naya supathā rāye asmānviśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān |*
> *yuyodhyasmajjuhurāṇameno bhūyiṣṭhāṃ te nama uktiṃ vidhema ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-189-1) — in this ṛk, Śaṅkarācārya [as printed] has explained *vayunāni* as "*karmāṇi, prajñānāni vā*" — "works, or knowledges". Thus both senses are possible for this word. In the ṛk at hand it is understood that the chariot of the Aśvin deities, hidden till now, is now an object of our knowledge.

**Dhiyaṃjinvā** — "*karmaṇo buddher vā prīṇayitārau*" — impellers of rite, or impellers of intellect, is the meaning given. The word *dhī* is used in both senses, "intellect" and "rite".

> यज्ञं वष्टु धियावसुरिति वाग्वै धियावसुः ।

> *yajñaṃ vaṣṭu dhiyāvasuriti vāgvai dhiyāvasuḥ |*

(Ai. Ā. 1-1-4 [?]) — by this sentence, in the Aitareya-Āraṇyaka the word *dhī* is explained as "praise". The word *dhī* is read in the Nirukta among the names of rite (Ni. 3-1 [?]) and among the names of knowledge (Ni. 3-13 [?]); and

> महो अर्णः सरस्वती प्रचेतयति केतुना । धियो विश्वा वि राजति ॥

> *maho arṇaḥ sarasvatī pracetayati ketunā | dhiyo viśvā vi rājati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-12) — for the word in this ṛk it is explained as "*sarvāṇi prajñānāni*" (Ni. 11-26 [?]): "all our speech endowed with wisdom, that is, meditation". And:

> पथस्पृथः परिपतिं वचस्या कामेन कृतो अभ्यानळर्कम् ।
> स नो रासच्छुरुधश्चन्द्राग्रा धियंधियं सीषधाति प्र पूषा ॥

> *pathaspṛthaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā kāmena kṛto abhyānaḷarkam |*
> *sa no rāsacchurudhaścandrāgrā dhiyaṃdhiyaṃ sīṣadhāti pra pūṣā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-49-8 [?]; as read, first words doubtful [?]) — in places such as these the word *dhī* means rites like sacrifice. Hence in the ṛk at hand it may be said that they are gladdeners of rite or of intellect.

**Jinvati** — though the word *jinvati* is read among the names of motion (Ni. 2-6 [?]), in general this word shows delight in work. "*Jinvatiḥ prītikarmā*" (Ni. 6-22 [?]) — the Nirukta-author says, to show the delight suggested by this word, citing

> भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वन्ति दिवं जिन्वन्त्यग्नयः ॥

> *bhūmiṃ parjanyā jinvanti divaṃ jinvantyagnayaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-51) — and explains its sense. In the ṛk at hand it may be "impellers of rites like sacrifice", or "those who attain satisfaction from rites like sacrifice". The word is an epithet of the Aśvin deities.

### Printed p. 595  (PDF 615)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 595.)*

**Dhiṣṇyā** — those worthy of meditation, or worthy of praise. The special senses of this word have been told before.

**Viśpalāvasū** — for this word also two kinds of meaning are given. First, "*viśāṃ prajānām asmākaṃ pālayitṛdhanau*" — those whose wealth protects the people, that is, they who can protect us, the people. Second, "*viśpalākhyā-aśvinnajaṅghāyā hiraṇmayajaṅghā-pradānena tathābhūtau*" — they who gave a golden leg to the cut leg of Viśpalā. The story of Viśpalā has been hinted at earlier too. Its substance is this:

> अगस्त्यपुरोहितः खेलो नाम राजा बभूव । तस्य सेनायां योद्ध्री विश्पला नाम स्त्री । तस्या अन्नार्थं धनार्थं च युध्यमानायाः शत्रवो जङ्घां चिच्छिदुः । तस्याश्विन्नां जङ्घां ज्ञात्वा पुरोहितोऽगस्त्योऽश्विनौ तुष्टाव । तौ विश्पलां प्रति जग्मतुः । आगत्य च सद्यो लोहमयीं जङ्घां विश्पलायै चक्रतुः । तदेवेहाप्युच्यते ।

> *agastyapurohitaḥ khelo nāma rājā babhūva | tasya senāyāṃ yoddhrī viśpalā nāma strī | tasyā annārthaṃ dhanārthaṃ ca yudhyamānāyāḥ śatravo jaṅghāṃ cicchiduḥ | tasyāśvinnāṃ jaṅghāṃ jñātvā purohito 'gastyo 'śvinau tuṣṭāva | tau viśpalāṃ prati jagmatuḥ | āgatya ca sadyo lohamayīṃ jaṅghāṃ viśpalāyai cakratuḥ | tadevehāpyucyate |*

(Sā. Bhā. Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-15) — "There was a king named Khela, whose priest was Agastya. In his army was a woman warrior named Viśpalā. While she was fighting for food and for wealth, the enemies cut off her leg. Knowing that her leg was cut, the priest Agastya praised the Aśvin deities. They went to Viśpalā, and at once made her an iron leg. This same is said here too." — this is the old story: that the Aśvin deities made her an iron (*lohamayī*) leg and caused her to walk (in the ṛk at hand Sāyaṇa says "by giving a golden leg"). The same story was told by Sāyaṇa in the Sūkta of Kakṣīvān [as printed; "kakṣīvatkṛta sūkta"] also, citing the ṛk:

> चरित्रं हि वेरिवाच्छेदि पर्णमाजा खेलस्य परितक्म्यायाम् ।
> सद्यो जङ्घामायसीं विश्पलायै धने हिते सर्तवे प्रत्यधत्तम् ॥

> *caritraṃ hi verivācchedi parṇamājā khelasya paritakmyāyām |*
> *sadyo jaṅghāmāyasīṃ viśpalāyai dhane hite sartave pratyadhattam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-15).

**Divaḥ napātā** — the word *napāt* means "son" and also "grandson". The Nirukta-author says: "*napād ity antarāyoḥ prajāyāḥ nāmadheyam*" [as read; Ni. 8-5 [?]] — that it is not a direct son; the word means grandsons etc. In the ṛk at hand, for *divaḥ napātā* Sāyaṇa explains "*ādityasya napātayitārau*". On the origin of the Aśvin deities, it has been told fully before in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-181-4. To these the epithet *divaḥ napātā* comes in many places. Sāyaṇa does not give one meaning everywhere. In Ṛk 1-184-1 he explains *dyulokasya naptṛsthānīyau* ("in the position of grandsons of the heavenly world"), and:

### Printed p. 596  (PDF 616)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 596.)*

> कृष्णा यद्गोष्वरुणीषु सीदद्दिवो नपाताश्विना हुवे वाम् ।
> वीतं मे यज्ञमा गतं मे अन्नं ववन्वांसा नेषमस्मृतध्रू ॥

> *kṛṣṇā yadgoṣvaruṇīṣu sīdaddivo napātāśvinā huve vām |*
> *vītaṃ me yajñamā gataṃ me annaṃ vavanvāṃsā neṣamasmṛtadhrū ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-61-4) — here he explains "*dīpyamānasya svargasya prātaśātmakasya yāgasya vā napātayitārau*". Since the nature of the Aśvin deities is described in many ways, all these meanings are suitably reconciled.

**Śucivratā** — the word *śuci* means "purity" and also "shining". Here it is "those whose *vrata* (rite or deed of strength) is exceedingly extensive and shining".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly): *abhūt* — in the beginning of a *pāda* there is no *nighāta* accent; the *āḍāgama* being acute, the first syllable is acute; *vayunam* — root *aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ*; "*ajiyamiśī…*" (Un. Sū. 3-143 [?]) gives suffix *unan*; "*ajer vy-aghañapoḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 2-4-56 [?]) gives *vī* for the root; guṇa, *ay* substitution; by *vyatyaya* the suffix's initial acute accent; *bhūṣata* — root *bhūṣa alaṅkāre*, *bhvādi*; *loṭ* second person plural form; *nighāta* accent (as following a *tiṅ*); in Vedic usage lengthening in the Saṃhitā; *vṛṣaṇvān* — suffix *matup* after the word *vṛṣan*; "*ano nuṭ*" (Pā. Sū. 8-2-16 [?]) gives *nuḍāgama*; "*hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-176 [?]) — *matup* acute; *madata* — root *mada tṛptiyoge*; as the causative action is shown, it is *antarbhāvita-ṇyartha*; *loṭ* second person plural; by *vyatyaya* initial acute; *manīṣiṇaḥ* — "*manīṣā eṣām asti*"; "*ata iniṭhanau*": suffix *ini*; vocative plural; *nighāta* accent; *dhiyaṃjinvā* — root *jivi prīṇane*; "*kṛtyaluṭo bahulam*": from the *bahula* rule the suffix *khac* (accent by the sound of the rule); "*idito num dhātoḥ*" gives *num*; "*ici ekāco 'm pratyayavac ca*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-68 [?]) gives *am* augment to the former; the accent of the *kṛdutta* last member gives final acute; "*supāṃ sulug*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) — ā-substitution for the dual (*au*); so also in *dhiṣṇyā*; *napātā* — "*na pātayitārau*; *nabhrāṇ napāt…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-75 [?]): the non-elision of *na* is irregularly established in the compound; ā-substitution of the dual as before; *nañ* — the former member keeps its own accent.

### Printed p. 597  (PDF 617)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 597.)*

*(Grammar page of Ṛk 1, continued, noted briefly):* *sukṛte* — "*śobhanaṃ karoti iti sukṛt*"; to it, root *kṛ*, *kvip*; *tuk* augment to the root; the accent of the *kṛdutta* last member is the *prakṛti* accent; fourth case singular form; *śucivratā* — "*śuci vrataṃ yayoḥ*"; "*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) gives the former member's own accent; second (case), ā-substitution for the dual.  ‖ 1 ‖

### Sūkta 182, Ṛk 2  (printed p. 597; PDF 617)

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> इन्द्रतमा हि धिष्ण्या मरुत्तमा दस्रा दंसिष्ठा रथ्या रथीतमा ।
> पूर्णं रथं वहेथे मध्व आचितं तेन दाश्वांसमुप याथो अश्विना ॥ २ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> इन्द्रऽतमा । हि । धिष्ण्या । मरुत्ऽतमा । दस्रा । दंसिष्ठा । रथ्या । रथिऽतमा ।
> पूर्णं । रथं । वहेथे इति । मध्वः । आऽचितं । तेन । दाश्वांसं । उप । याथः । अश्विना ॥ २ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ युवामिन्द्रतमा हीश्वरतमौ खलु । एवं प्रतिविशेषणं हिः संबन्धः । तथा धिष्ण्या स्तुत्यर्हौ मरुत्तमा मरुद्भ्योऽतिशयेन वेगगामिनौ मितरागिणौ मितरावणौ वा दस्रोपक्षयितारौ शत्रूणां दंसिष्ठातिशययुक्तकर्माणौ रथ्या रथार्हौ रथवन्तौ रथितमा । रथिनो नेतारः । तेषां श्रेष्ठौ । रथीरध्वराणां । ऋ. ८-१०-२ । इति नेतृत्वपरतया व्याख्यातत्वात् । ईदृशौ युवां मध्वो मधुसदृशस्य उदकस्यामृतस्य वा पूर्णं पूरितमाचितं सर्वतः संनद्धं रथं वहेथे । नयथः । तेनोक्तगुणविशिष्टेन रथेन हे अश्विनावश्विनौ उक्तगुणविशिष्टौ सन्तावुप याथः । यज्ञमभिप्राप्नुथः ॥

*(Sanskrit as read; doubtful in several words [?], and the reference "Ṛ. 8-10-2" is as read [?]. Gist: the Aśvins are most lordly, swift, best chariot-leaders; come in your chariot full of sweetness to the sacrificer.)*

**Pratipadārtha** — (*he aśvinau* — O Aśvin deities!) (you two) **indratamā** — endowed with the highest splendour; **dhiṣṇyā** — worthy of praise; **marutvatamā** *(printed "marut-tamā")* — swifter than the Maruts (of measured passion, or of measured sound); **dasrā** — destroyers of foes; **daṃsiṣṭhā** — performers of exceedingly great deeds; **rathyā** — worthy of the chariot; (and) **rathītamā** — the highest of charioteers (chiefs of chariot-owners); **hi** — verily; (such) you two; **madhvaḥ** — resembling honey (with water or with ambrosia); **pūrṇaṃ** — full; (and) **ācitaṃ** — on all sides made ready; **rathaṃ** — the chariot; **vahethe** — you bring; **tena** — with that chariot; (*he*) **aśvinā** — O Aśvin deities (possessed of the said qualities); **dāśvāṃsaṃ** — the sacrificer who offers oblations; **upa yāthaḥ** — approach.

### Printed p. 598  (PDF 618)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 598.)*

*(The page opens in the middle of the Pratipadārtha, continuing from p. 597:)* … **daṃsiṣṭhā** — doers of exceedingly great works; **rathyā** — worthy of the chariot; (and) **rathītamā** — the most distinguished charioteers (chiefs of chariot-owners); **hi** — verily; (such) you two; **madhvaḥ** — resembling honey (with water or with ambrosia); **pūrṇaṃ** — full; (and) **ācitaṃ** — on all sides made ready; **rathaṃ** — the chariot; **vahethe** — you bring; **tena** — with that chariot; (*he*) **aśvinā** — O Aśvin deities (possessed of the said qualities); **dāśvāṃsaṃ** — the sacrificer who gives oblations; **upa yāthaḥ** — approach.

**Bhāvārtha** — O Aśvin deities, you two are truly very mighty, worthy of praise, swifter than the wind, destroyers of foes, who especially perform works of strength, who move in the chariot, and are the best of charioteers; come to the sacrificer, sitting in that chariot of yours, full of ambrosia and ready in all ways.

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"Dasras, in truth most imperial, adorable, swifter than the winds, and eminent in good works, riders in a car, and most distinguished charioteers, bring hither your car, full heaped up with ambrosia, and with it come, Ashwins, to the donor (of the offering)."

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

**Indratamā** — for the word *indratamā* Sāyaṇa has explained "*īśvaratamau khalu*" — "most mighty". Earlier, the Nirukta-author's sentences giving derivations of the word *indra*, and the senses of *alaṅkāra* [as printed], have been cited as examples. Therefore, as the Nirukta-author has given a few derivations suited to the epithets applied to the Aśvin deities in the ṛk at hand, the purport of these derivations must be understood as describing their greatness in whatever way (Ni. 10-8 [?]).

> इन्द्र इरां दृणातीति वा ।

> *indra irāṃ dṛṇātīti vā |*

(Ni. 10-8 [?]) — the root *dṛ* gives the sense of "to divide"; from it, *irām annaṃ vrīhyādi dṛṇāti vidārayati* [as read; doubtful [?]]: he splits the seed-sprout moistened by rain; that is, he is called Indra because, by causing the seeds of grain etc. to burst from the rain, he makes the tree grow. And:

> इरां ददातीति वा । वर्षद्वारेणासौ इरां ददाति ।

> *irāṃ dadātīti vā | varṣadvāreṇāsau irāṃ dadāti |*

(as read [?]) — from the root *dā*, "to give", the word is formed: "he gives food through rain-giving" — thus considering the meanings of the two derivations, and seeing that it applies to the Aśvin deities,

---

### Printed p. 599  (PDF 619)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 599.)*

> वृषा वां मेघो वृषणा पीपाय गोर्न सेके मनुषो दशस्यन् ।

> *vṛṣā vāṃ megho vṛṣaṇā pīpāya gorna seke manuṣo daśasyan |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-8) — from the descriptions in ṛks such as these it is well known that the qualities mentioned above are fully present in them. In the same way:

> इन्दवे द्रवतीति वा ।

> *indave dravatīti vā |*

— from the root *dru*, "to run", from running with eagerness to the Soma-juice; hence this name, if so:

> हंसाविव पतथो अध्वगाविव सोमं सुतं महिषेवाव गच्छथः ।
> सजोषसा उषसा सूर्येण च त्रिर्वर्तिर्यातमश्विना ॥
> श्येनाविव पतथो हव्यदातये सोमं सुतं महिषेवाव गच्छथः ।
> सजोषसा उषसा सूर्येण च त्रिर्वर्तिर्यातमश्विना ॥

> *haṃsāviva patatho adhvagāviva somaṃ sutaṃ mahiṣevāva gacchathaḥ |*
> *sajoṣasā uṣasā sūryeṇa ca trirvartiryātamaśvinā ‖*
> *śyenāviva patatho havyadātaye somaṃ sutaṃ mahiṣevāva gacchathaḥ |*
> *sajoṣasā uṣasā sūryeṇa ca trirvartiryātamaśvinā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-35-8 to 9 [?]; as read) — in ṛks such as these, the Aśvin deities, like Indra, are described as coming in haste for drinking Soma; so the derivation above is suitable. Therefore, the epithet *indratamā* can be applied to them. And:

> इन्दौ रमते इति वा ।

> *indau ramate iti vā |*

— from the root *ram*, which gives the sense "to be delighted": one who is satisfied by drinking the Soma-juice; for the name too the above example is the basis. Or:

> इन्धे भूतानीति वा ।

> *indhe bhūtānīti vā |*

— from the root *indh*, meaning "to shine": one who makes beings shine; or the name Indra is famous in this sense; by this derivation the epithet becomes:

> वि चेदुच्छन्त्यश्विना उषासः प्र वां ब्रह्माणि कारवो भरन्ते ।
> ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सविता देवो अश्रेद्बृहदग्नयः समिधा जरन्ते ॥

> *vi ceducchantyaśvinā uṣāsaḥ pra vāṃ brahmāṇi kāravo bharante |*
> *ūrdhvaṃ bhānuṃ savitā devo aśredbṛhadagnayaḥ samidhā jarante ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-72-4 [?]; Sanskrit as read, last words doubtful [?]) — in ṛks such as these, along with the rising of the Aśvin deities there is the destruction of darkness, and the world receives the rays of the Ādityas; so they are praised as the illuminators of the world. Hence this epithet suits them.

> इदं करणादित्याग्रयणः ।

> *idaṃ karaṇādityāgrayaṇaḥ |*

(Ni. 10-8 [?]; as read) — "Since in the creation of the world he did everything (*idam asau sarvam akarot*)": if the word Indra is [taken to be] so formed, it is in agreement with "*asarji vāṃ sthavirā vedhasā…*"

### Printed p. 600  (PDF 620)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 600.)*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-7) — in the Special Topics of this ṛk it has been told how the Aśvin deities are the cause of the creation of the world. By that same greatness they can be praised with this epithet.

**Indratevaiśvaryakarmaṇaḥ** *(as printed; the intended sense: "all-lordship")* — if the derivation is given that this name may be borne because of lordship over everything: since the Aśvin deities are in the forms of the Sun, Moon and Earth [?], and in the forms of day and night, and in the form of Heaven and Earth the producers of the world, and are pervaders of the universe, and are presidents over all the activities, this sense also fits when praising their greatness. Thus, since all great qualities are in the Aśvin deities, the epithet *indratamā* is very suitable. Likewise:

> अभूदुषा इन्द्रतमा मघोन्यजीजनत्सुविताय श्रवांसि ।
> वि दिवो देवी दुहिता दधात्यङ्गिरस्तमा सुकृते वसूनि ॥

> *abhūduṣā indratamā maghonyajījanatsuvitāya śravāṃsi |*
> *vi divo devī duhitā dadhātyaṅgirastamā sukṛte vasūni ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-79-3 [?]) — here also the epithet *indratamā* is applied to Uṣas, and her greatness is described by this epithet.

**Marutvatamā** *(printed "marut-tamā")* — "*marudvegagāminau mitarāgiṇau mitarāviṇau vā*": swift-moving like the Maruts; or of measured passion; or in the matter of measured splendour or sound. Sāyaṇa has so explained the epithet. All these qualities are described in the Aśvin deities.

**Daṃsiṣṭhā** — "*atiśayakarmāṇau*": *daṃsa* is read among the names of work; the meaning is "those who have exceedingly great works".

**Rathītamā (rathinaḥ)** — for this word the meaning "*netāraḥ*" is given. If the question comes: how does this meaning fit this word? then, as the basis for it,

> त्वमसि प्रशस्यो विदथेषु सहन्त्य ।
> अग्ने रथीरध्वराणाम् ।

> *tvamasi praśasyo vidatheṣu sahantya |*
> *agne rathīradhvarāṇām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-11-2 [?]) — taking this ṛk as example: as there the word *rathīḥ* gives the sense *netā*, so in the ṛk at hand also it is to be understood as meaning that.

**Madhvaḥ** — "*madhu sadṛśasya udakasya vā (pūritaṃ rathaṃ)*": the chariot filled with water like honey, or with ambrosia — the special quality of the chariot of the Aśvin deities is praised. In general the chariots of the Aśvin deities have the epithets *madhumān*, *madhuvāhanaḥ* etc. by their very nature; and not only to their chariot, but to them also, it is famous that they are bearers of honey (*madhuvāhaka*).

### Printed p. 601  (PDF 621)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 601.)*

> इदं वै तन्मधु दध्यङ्ङाथर्वणोऽश्विभ्यामुवाच । तदेतदृषिः पश्यन्नवोचत् ।

> *idaṃ vai tanmadhu dadhyaṅṅātharvaṇo 'śvibhyāmuvāca | tadetadṛṣiḥ paśyannavocat |*

(Bṛ. U. 2-5-16 [?]) — thus the story is well known that Dadhīci, the son of Atharvan, taught the *madhu-vidyā* to the Aśvin deities. Since the Aśvin deities were the teachers of this *madhuvidyā*, which is the basis of spiritual knowledge, there is a figurative description that they come filling their chariot with this knowledge. This very point is:

> त्रयः पवयो मधुवाहने रथे सोमस्य वेनामनु विश्व इद्विदुः ।

> *trayaḥ pavayo madhuvāhane rathe somasya venāmanu viśva idviduḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-2 [?])

> अधि वां स्थामु वन्धुरे रथे दस्रा हिरण्यये ।
> पथेव यन्तावनुशासता रजोऽञ्जसा शासता रजः ॥

> *adhi vāṃ sthāmu vandhure rathe dasrā hiraṇyaye |*
> *patheva yantāvanuśāsatā rajo 'ñjasā śāsatā rajaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-119-4 [?]) — in many ṛks, such as these, it is shown by the epithets "*madhuvāhane rathe*" and "*hiraṇyaye rathe*". "*Hiraṇyaye rathe*" too, as before, means "in the chariot filled with honey (*madhu*)". Therefore, for the epithet **madhvaḥ** here, a special meaning must be told. How this *madhuvidyā* came to the Aśvin deities:

> दध्यङ् ह यन्मध्वाथर्वणो वामश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा प्र यदीमुवाच ॥

> *dadhyaṅ ha yanmadhvātharvaṇo vāmaśvasya śīrṣṇā pra yadīmuvāca ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-12) — Sāyaṇa, explaining this ṛk, has told it with the story context. Its substance was told earlier. The same story, repeated here, is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, and the very form of this *madhuvidyā* is described in the Upaniṣads etc.; this is to be understood here. This context in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-18 to 25 [?]) runs thus:

> दध्यङ् ह वा आथर्वणः । एकं शुक्रमेतं यज्ञं विदांचकार । यथा यथैतद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिधीयते यथैष कृत्स्नो यज्ञो भवति । सहेन्द्रेणोक्त आस । एतं चेदन्यस्मा अनुब्रूयास्ते एव ते शिरश्छिन्द्यामिति ।

> *dadhyaṅ ha vā ātharvaṇaḥ | ekaṃ śukrametaṃ yajñaṃ vidāṃcakāra | yathā yathaitadyajñasya śiraḥ pratidhīyate yathaiṣa kṛtsno yajño bhavati | sahendreṇokta āsa | etaṃ cedanyasmā anubrūyāste eva te śiraśchindyāmiti |*

(Sanskrit as read; doubtful in places [?]) — Dadhīci Ātharvaṇa, son of Atharvan, knew this pure sacrificial doctrine: how the head of the sacrifice is set back again, and how the sacrifice becomes complete. Indra told him: "If you tell this to anyone else, I shall cut off your head."

### Printed p. 602  (PDF 622)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 602.)*

> तदु हाश्विनोरनुश्रुतमास । दध्यङ् ह वा आथर्वण एतं शुक्रमेतं यज्ञं वेद यथैतद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिधीयते यथैष कृत्स्नो यज्ञो भवति ।

*(Sanskrit as read [?]).* Then the Aśvin deities, hearing of this prohibition of Indra, still wished to obtain from Dadhīci the sacrificial doctrine he knew:

> तौ हेत्योचतुः । उप त्वायाव एति किमनुवक्ष्यमाणावित्येतं शुक्रमेतं यज्ञं यथा …… कृत्स्नो यज्ञो भवतीति ।

> *tau hetyocatuḥ | upa tvāyāva eti kimanuvakṣyamāṇāvityetaṃ śukrametaṃ yajñaṃ yathā …… kṛtsno yajño bhavatīti |*

(print has a row of dots in the middle) — then they went to Dadhīci, and asked that they themselves be made his pupils, so that they too might learn that doctrine and he might teach them.

> स होवाच । इन्द्रेण वा उक्तोऽस्म्येतं चेदन्यस्मा अनुब्रूयास्ते एव ते शिरश्छिन्द्यामिति तस्माद्वै बिभेमि यद्वै मे स शिरो न विन्द्यान्न वामुपनेष्य इति ।

> *sa hovāca | indreṇa vā ukto 'smyetaṃ cedanyasmā anubrūyāste eva te śiraśchindyāmiti tasmādvai bibhemi yadvai me sa śiro na vindyānna vāmupaneṣya iti |*

(as read [?]) — knowing the command Indra had given him, he said that he could not accept them as pupils.

> तौ होचतुः । आवां त्वा तस्मात्त्रायस्यावह इति कथं मा त्रास्येथे इति यदा नौ उपनेष्यसेऽथ शिरश्छित्वान्यत्रापनिधास्यावोऽथाश्वस्य शिर आहृत्य तत्ते प्रतिधास्यावस्तेन नावनुवक्ष्यसि स यदा नावनुवक्ष्यस्यथ ते तदिन्द्रः शिरश्छेत्स्यत्यथ ते स्वं शिर आहृत्य तत्ते प्रतिधास्याव इति तथेति ।

> *tau hocatuḥ | āvāṃ tvā tasmāttrāyasyāvaha iti kathaṃ mā trāsyethe iti yadā nau upaneṣyase 'tha śiraśchitvānyatrāpanidhāsyāvo 'thāśvasya śira āhṛtya tatte pratidhāsyāvastena nāvanuvakṣyasi sa yadā nāvanuvakṣyasyatha te tadindraḥ śiraśchetsyatyatha te svaṃ śira āhṛtya tatte pratidhāsyāva iti tatheti |*

(as read [?]) — to this they replied: "We shall protect you from that." "How will you protect me?" he asked. "When you accept us as pupils, we shall cut off your head and put it elsewhere, and bring a horse's head and set it on you; with it you will teach us. When you have taught us, Indra will cut off that head of yours; then we shall bring your own head and set it back on you." He agreed, saying "So be it."

> तौ होपनिन्येते । तौ यदोपनिन्येऽथास्य शिरश्छित्वान्यत्रापनिदधतुरथाश्वस्य शिर आहृत्य तदस्य प्रतिदधतुस्तेन हाभ्यामनूवाच स यदाभ्यामनूवाचाथास्य तदिन्द्रः शिरश्चिच्छेदाथास्य स्वं शिर आहृत्य तदस्य प्रतिदधतुः ।

> *tau hopaninyete | tau yadopaninye 'thāsya śiraśchitvānyatrāpanidadhaturathāśvasya śira āhṛtya tadasya pratidadhatustena hābhyāmanūvāca sa yadābhyāmanūvācāthāsya tadindraḥ śiraścicchedāthāsya svaṃ śira āhṛtya tadasya pratidadhatuḥ |*

(as read [?]; several words doubtful) — Straightway the two accepted the pupilhood and he gave the instruction; then Indra came and cut off that horse's head; at once the Aśvin deities set Dadhīci's own head back again.

### Printed p. 603  (PDF 623)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 603.)*

> तस्मादेतदृषीणामभ्यनूक्तं । दध्यङ् ह यन्मध्वाथर्वणो वामश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा प्र यदीमुवाचेत्यायतं तदुवाचेति हैतदेवैतदुक्तम् ।

> *tasmādetadṛṣīṇāmabhyanūktaṃ | dadhyaṅ ha yanmadhvātharvaṇo vāmaśvasya śīrṣṇā pra yadīmuvācetyāyataṃ taduvāceti haitadevaitaduktam |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-18 to 25 [?]; as read, doubtful in places [?]) — therefore the seers say in the ṛk: "when Dadhīci Ātharvaṇa spoke the *madhu* to you with a horse's head". Hence it is well known that it was through the horse's head that the Atharvan-born Dadhīci taught this *madhuvidyā*. The story is told also in the Bṛhaddevatā:

> प्रादाद्ब्रह्माऽपि सुप्रीतः सुताय तदथर्वणः ।
> स चाभवदृषिस्तेन ब्रह्मणा दीप्तिमत्तरः ॥
> तमृषिं निषिषेधेन्द्रो मैवं वोचः क्वचिन्मधु ।
> न हि प्रोक्ते मधुन्यस्मिञ्जीवन्तं त्वोजाम्यहम् ॥
> तमृषिं त्वश्विनौ देवौ विविक्ते मध्वयाचताम् ।
> स चेताभ्यां तदाचख्यौ यदुवाच शचीपतिः ॥
> तमब्रूतां तु नासत्यावाश्व्येन शिरसा भवान् ।
> मथ्नाशु ग्राहयेत्वावां मेन्द्रश्च त्वा वधीत्ततः ॥
> आश्व्येन शिरसा तौ तु दध्यञ्चाह यदश्विनौ ।
> तदस्येन्द्रोऽहरत्क्षिप्रं तन्न्यधत्तानुस्य यज्ञिरः ॥
> दधीचश्च शिरश्चाश्व्यं कृत्तं वज्रेण वज्रिणा ।
> पपात सरसो मध्ये पर्वते शर्यणावति ॥
> तदद्भ्यस्तु समुत्थाय भूतेभ्यो विविधान्वरान् ।
> प्रादायु युगपर्यन्तं तास्वेवाप्सु निमज्जति ॥

> *prādādbrahmā 'pi suprītaḥ sutāya tadatharvaṇaḥ |*
> *sa cābhavadṛṣistena brahmaṇā dīptimattaraḥ ‖*
> *tamṛṣiṃ niṣiṣedhendro maivaṃ vocaḥ kvacinmadhu |*
> *na hi prokte madhunyasmiñjīvantaṃ tvojāmyaham ‖*
> *tamṛṣiṃ tvaśvinau devau vivikte madhvayācatām |*
> *sa cetābhyāṃ tadācakhyau yaduvāca śacīpatiḥ ‖*
> *tamabrūtāṃ tu nāsatyāvāśvyena śirasā bhavān |*
> *mathnāśu grāhayetvāvāṃ mendraśca tvā vadhīttataḥ ‖*
> *āśvyena śirasā tau tu dadhyañcāha yadaśvinau |*
> *tadasyendro 'haratkṣipraṃ tannyadhattānusya yajñiraḥ ‖*
> *dadhīcaśca śiraścāśvyaṃ kṛttaṃ vajreṇa vajriṇā |*
> *papāta saraso madhye parvate śaryaṇāvati ‖*
> *tadadbhyastu samutthāya bhūtebhyo vividhānvarān |*
> *prādāyu yugaparyantaṃ tāsvevāpsu nimajjati ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-18 to 21 [?]; Sanskrit as read, many words doubtful [?]) — the same story is told in these sentences. There is no difference in the telling of the story, except that at the end it is added that the horse's head, cut off by Indra's weapon, the *vajra*, fell in the lake on the mountain *Śaryaṇāvat*; rising from there, it gave in abundance to all beings suitable boons, and remains in those waters to the end of the *yuga*.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly): *indratamā* — "*atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau*" (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55 [?]) gives suffix *tamap*; having *p*, it is unaccented; "*supāṃ sulug*" gives ā-substitution for the first (case) dual; so too the changes in *marutvatamā*. *daṃsiṣṭhā* — by the above sūtra, suffix *iṣṭhan* in the sense of excess; "*ṭeḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-155 [?]) elides the final part (*as*) of the base; "*ñit-ādir-nityam*" gives initial acute; ā-substitution for the dual as before.

### Printed p. 604  (PDF 624)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 604.)*

*(Grammar page, continued, noted briefly):* *rathyā* — "*rathaṃ arhataḥ iti rathyā*": "*rathād yat*" (Pā. Sū. 4-4-121 [?]) gives suffix *yat* in the sense of "worthy"; "*yasyeti ca*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-148 [?]) elides *a*; "*tit svaritam*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-185 [?]) gives svarita accent; ā-substitution for the dual. *rathītamā* — as before the suffix *tamap* in the sense of excess; "*anyeṣām api dṛśyate*" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 [?]) gives lengthening of the former member in the Saṃhitā; ā-substitution for the case ending. *pūrṇam* — root *pyai pālanapūraṇayoḥ*; "*niṣṭhā*" gives suffix *kta*; "*udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-102 [?]) gives *u*; "*uraṇ raparaḥ*" gives *r* following; "*halī ca*" lengthens; "*radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 8-2-42 [?]) gives *na* when *kta* follows *r*; "*raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ*" gives *ṇa*; by the suffix accent final acute. *vahethe* — root *vaha prāpaṇe*; *laṭ* second person dual form; *nighāta* accent. *ācitam* — root *ciñ cayane*; *niṣṭhā*, suffix *kta*; as it has *k*, no guṇa; "*gatiranantaraḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49 [?]) the *gati* (*ā*) has *nighāta* accent. *dāśvāṃsam* — root *dāś dāne*; "*dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-12 [?]) — the suffix *kvasu* comes as irregular; second case singular: *num* augment because it has *u*; the suffix's accent. *yāthaḥ* — root *yā prāpaṇe*; *laṭ* second person dual form; *nighāta* accent.  ‖ 2 ‖

### Sūkta 182, Ṛk 3  (printed p. 604; PDF 624)

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> किमत्र दस्रा कृणुथः किमासाथे जनो यः कश्चिदहविर्महीयते ।
> अति क्रमिष्टं जुरतं पणेरसुं ज्योतिर्विप्राय कृणुतं वचस्यवे ॥ ३ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> किं । अत्र । दस्रा । कृणुथः । किं । आसाथे इति । जनः । यः । कः । चित् । अहविः । महीयते ।
> अति । क्रमिष्टं । जुरतं । पणेः । असुं । ज्योतिः । विप्राय । कृणुतं । वचस्यवे ॥ ३ ॥

> *kiṃ | atra | dasrā | kṛṇuthaḥ | kiṃ | āsāthe iti | janaḥ | yaḥ | kaḥ | cit | ahaviḥ | mahīyate |*
> *ati | kramiṣṭaṃ | jurataṃ | paṇeḥ | asuṃ | jyotiḥ | viprāya | kṛṇutaṃ | vacasyave ‖ 3 ‖*

---

### Printed p. 605  (PDF 625)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 605.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे दस्रोपक्षपयितारौ युवामत्रास्मिन्मनुष्ये किं कृणुथः । कुरुथः । हविषोऽभावादिति भावः । तत्रैव किमासाथे । किं तिष्ठथः । अत्रेत्युक्तं कुत्रेत्याह । यः कश्चिज्जनो जन्मनानहविर्यज्ञार्थहविरहितो महीयते पूज्यते स्वयं न युष्मान् पूजयति । तं जनमति क्रमिष्टं । पराभूयात् तिष्ठतं । न केवलमतिक्रममात्रं किंतु पणेर्वणिग्भूतस्य लुब्धकस्यायुष्यस्तस्यासुं प्राणं जुरतं । अहिंसिष्टं । अनीनशतं । विप्राय मेधाविने वचस्यवे वचसः स्तोत्ररूपस्य युवाभ्यामिच्छते मह्यं ज्योतिः कृणुतं । युष्मद्यजनविषयज्ञानं कुरुतम् ॥

*(Sanskrit as read; doubtful in several words [?]. Gist: why do you linger where a man, giving no oblation, is honoured? Overcome him, destroy the life of the niggardly trader, and give me, a wise praiser, the light of knowledge.)*

**Pratipadārtha** — *he dasrā* — O Aśvin deities, destroyers of foes; **yaḥ kaḥ cit janaḥ** — whichever man; **ahaviḥ** — devoid of oblations for sacrifice; **mahīyate** — (himself, without worshipping you) is honoured, becomes worshipped; **atra** — in the matter of such a man; **kiṃ kṛṇuthaḥ** — what do you do; **kiṃ āsāthe** — why do you sit there; **ati kramiṣṭaṃ** — overcome (such a man); **paṇeḥ** — of the miser, the trader; **asuṃ** — the life; **jurataṃ** — afflict (destroy); **viprāya** — for the wise one; **vacasyave** — who desires praise in the form of words; **jyotiḥ** — the light of knowledge (that you should be worshipped); **kṛṇutaṃ** — make.

**Bhāvārtha** — O Aśvin deities, destroyers of foes, why do you go near a man who, himself honoured, gives no oblation for sacrifice? What do you do with such a man? Overcome that man; destroy the miser, the niggard; and grant to me, a wise man who desires to praise you, the light of knowledge to worship you.

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"What make you here, Ashwins : why do you tarry, (where) any man who makes no oblation is respected : humble him ; take away the life of the niggard ; grant light to the pious man striving to speak your praise,"

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

**Dasrā** — the senses of this word — "those with attractive forms" in one sense, and "destroyers of enemies" in another — were told earlier. In the present context it is explained as "destroyers of enemies" (*upakṣayakāraka*).

### Printed p. 606  (PDF 626)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 606.)*

There is a reason for telling this meaning. The sacrificer who is destitute, not having oblations in full to give and unfit to give, shows his fear. And solely from poverty, saying "*haviṣaḥ abhāvāt*" ("from lack of oblation"), he prays that he has not been able to offer oblations to them for their sake, that his devotion and faith are boundless nonetheless, and therefore that no calamity may come to him; and, though possessing full wealth, he who without faith and devotion does not offer oblations — he prays that the *paṇi*s, the other kind, be wholly destroyed.

For the word **paṇi**, the Nirukta-author's derivation, and the meaning given by Sāyaṇa, were told before in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-180-2 [?]. In **lubdhakāḥ**, **abudhyamānāḥ**, **yāgā dīnakurvāṇāḥ**, **adānaśīlāḥ**, **asmacchatravaḥ** and the like, Sāyaṇa has shown the nature of the *paṇi*s.

Thus, since they are harmful to the sacrificers, the sacrificer there prays to the Aśvin deities to destroy them.

**Juratam** — for this word the meaning is "afflict, or destroy". In general this word is used of enemies who are harmful. For example:

> चित्रं तद्वो मरुतो याम चेकिते पृश्न्या यदूधरप्सा यो दुदुहुः ।
> यद्वा निदे नवमानस्य रुद्रियास्त्रितं जराय जरतामदाभ्याः ॥

> *citraṃ tadvo maruto yāma cekite pṛśnyā yadūdharapsā yo duduhuḥ |*
> *yadvā nide navamānasya rudriyāstritaṃ jarāya jaratāmadābhyāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-10 [?]; as read) — in ṛks such as these, *jaratām* is explained as "of the afflicters, of the enemies". In the ṛk at hand, "afflict the enemies".

**Jyotiḥ** — for this word the meaning is not merely physical light or radiance. "*Yuṣmadyajana-viṣayajñānaṃ*" — "the light in the form of the knowledge to worship you" is the meaning given.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly): *kṛṇuthaḥ* — root *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*; *laṭ* second person dual form; being after a *tiṅ*-final, *nighāta* accent. *āsāthe* — root *āsa upaveśane*; *laṭ* second person dual form; *tiṅ*, *nighāta* accent. *ahaviḥ* — "*na vidyate haviḥ yasya saḥ*", by *vyatyaya* the *nañ* … gives no *nimitta*-accent; *bahuvrīhau* — "…" gives initial acute; or, since the word *haviḥ* has the suffix with the sense of possession dropped, being a *tatpuruṣa* compound, "*tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2 [?]) gives the *prakṛti* accent of the former member that is an indeclinable.

### Printed p. 607  (PDF 627)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 607.)*

*(Grammar page of Ṛk 3, continued, noted briefly):* *mahīyate* — root *maha pūjāyām*; *yak* in the passive; *laṭ* third-person form; "*niṣāt-tairyadyadi*" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30 [?]) — because *ci(t)* is connected, no *nighāta* accent comes; the accent of *yak* remains. *kramiṣṭam* — root *kramu pādavikṣepe*; "*chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭaḥ*": *luṅ* in the sense of the imperative; *tam*-substitution for the second person dual; *iṭ* augment for *siṭ*; "*hmyantakṣaṇaśvasa…*" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-5 [?]) prohibits *vṛddhi*; "*bahulaṃ chandasy-māṅyoge 'pi*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-75 [?]) — no *āḍāgama*; *tiṅ*, *nighāta* accent. *juratam* — root *jṝ vayohānau*; *loṭ* second person dual, *tam*-substitution; by *vyatyaya*, *śa* as *vikaraṇa*; "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" (Pā. Sū. 2-4-73 [?]) gives *u* … *r* follows; *nighāta* is not applied, since a *tiṅ* is not following; the *vikaraṇa* accent makes the middle syllable acute. *vacasyave* — "*vacaḥ ātmanaḥ icchati vacasyati*"; "*supa ātmanaḥ kyac*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 [?]) gives *kyac*; "*kyāc chandasi*" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-170 [?]) gives suffix *u* after the *kyac*-ending; "*ato lopaḥ*" elides *a*; the suffix accent comes; fourth case singular form.  ‖ 3 ‖

### Sūkta 182, Ṛk 4  (printed p. 607; PDF 627)

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> जम्भयतमभितो रायतः शुनो हतं मृधो विदथुस्तान्यश्विना ।
> वाचंवाचं जरितू रत्निनीं कृतमुभा शंसं नासत्यावतं मम ॥ ४ ॥

> *jambhayatamabhito rāyataḥ śuno hataṃ mṛdho vidathustānyaśvinā |*
> *vācaṃvācaṃ jaritū ratninīṃ kṛtamubhā śaṃsaṃ nāsatyāvataṃ mama ‖ 4 ‖*

*(The last word is printed "ममु" in the Saṃhitā and Pada — as printed, evidently "मम" [sic].)*

**Pada-pāṭha**

> जम्भयतं । अभितः । रायतः । शुनः । हतं । मृधः । विदथुः । तानि । अश्विना ।
> वाचंऽवाचं । जरितुः । रत्निनीं । कृतं । उभा । शंसं । नासत्या । अवतं । मम ॥ ४ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ रायतो निन्दितं शब्दयतोऽस्मान्हन्तुमागच्छतो वा शुनः श्वसदृशानभितो जम्भयतं । नाशयतं । तथा मृधस्तेषां संग्रामान् संग्रामं कुर्वतो वा हतं । मारयतं । तानि हननोपायान्विदथुः । जानीथः । किंच

> *he aśvinau rāyato ninditaṃ śabdayato 'smānhantumāgacchato vā śunaḥ śvasadṛśānabhito jambhayataṃ | nāśayataṃ | tathā mṛdhasteṣāṃ saṃgrāmān saṃgrāmaṃ kurvato vā hataṃ | mārayataṃ | tāni hananopāyānvidathuḥ | jānīthaḥ | kiṃca*

### Printed p. 608  (PDF 628)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 608.)*

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (continued)**

> जरितुः स्तोतुर्मह्यं वाचंवाचं तां तां स्तुतिलक्षणां वाचं रत्निनीं कृतं । सर्वामसि स्तुतिं रमणीयफलवतीं कुरुतं । हे नासत्या सत्यभूतौ युवामुभौ मम मदीयां शंसं स्तुतिमवतं । रक्षतं ॥

*(Sanskrit as read; doubtful in "sarvāmasi" [?]. Gist: destroy the barking dogs and the foes who fight us; you know the means; make every word of praise of mine fruitful and accept my praise.)*

**Pratipadārtha** — (*he*) **aśvinā** — O Aśvin deities; **rāyataḥ** — those who make abusive sounds (barking) or who come to kill us; **śunaḥ** — men like dogs; **abhitaḥ jambhayataṃ** — destroy them utterly; **mṛdhaḥ** — those who fight against us; **hataṃ** — kill; **tāni** — the means of killing them, or the means of harm they use; **vidathuḥ** — you know; **kiṃca** — and; **jarituḥ** — of the one who praises you; **vācaṃ-vācaṃ** — every word of praise; **ratninīṃ** — endowed with delightful fruit; **kṛtaṃ** — make; **he nāsatyā** — O Aśvin deities, who are truth-formed; **ubhā** — you two; **mama** — my; **śaṃsaṃ** — praise; **avataṃ** — protect (accept).

**Bhāvārtha** — O Aśvin deities, destroy those who revile you, or who come to kill us; destroy those who come to fight us; you know the means of killing them; and, pleased with the praise of me who praise you, make every word of praise bear excellent fruit.

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"Annihilate, Ashwins, the dogs who bark at us : slay them warring (against us) : you know their (means of harm) : render every word of him who praises you affluent in precious (rewards) : accept, Nasatyas, both of you, my praise."

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

**Rāyataḥ** — "*ninditaṃ śabdayataḥ asmān hantum āgacchato vā*" — those who revile us, or who come to harm us, that is, enemies.

**Mṛdhaḥ** — "*teṣāṃ saṃgrāmān saṃgrāmaṃ kurvato vā*": for this word the meaning is either "war" or "enemies who make war". The Nirukta-author has read this word among the names of *saṃgrāma* (Ni. 3-9 [?]): it means war. In some places it means the enemy who is the cause of war.

---

### Printed p. 609  (PDF 629)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 609.)*

> वि न इन्द्र मृधो जहि नीचा यच्छ पृतन्यतः ।

> *vi na indra mṛdho jahi nīcā yaccha pṛtanyataḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-152-4) — citing this ṛk, it is shown that there it has the meaning "*saṃgrāmakāriṇaḥ śatrūn*" ("the foes who make war") (Ni. 7-2 [?]). Both senses are taken in the ṛk at hand.

**Jambhayataṃ** — "*nāśayataṃ*" (destroy the enemies): this is the meaning given for this word. The word *jambha* means "tooth"; it is current especially for the canine teeth. Though the word *jambha* is used, the purport is the same. For example:

> न यो वराय मरुतामिव स्वनः सेनेव सृष्टा दिव्या यथाशनिः ।
> अग्निर्जम्भैस्तिगितैरत्ति भर्वति योधो न शत्रून्स वना न्यृञ्जते ॥

> *na yo varāya marutāmiva svanaḥ seneva sṛṣṭā divyā yathāśaniḥ |*
> *agnirjambhaistigitairatti bharvati yodho na śatrūnsa vanā nyṛñjate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-143-5 [?]) — in ṛks such as these, the word *jambhaiḥ* is used as a synonym for the flames of Agni. "*jambhair dantair daṃṣṭrāsthānīyābhir jvālābhiḥ atti*" — he devours with the flames which stand for the teeth: the fierce fangs are compared to the flames of Agni. In like manner, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-144-4 [?] etc. such descriptions occur.

> असौ य एषि वीरको गृहंगृहं विचाकशत् ।
> इमं जम्भसुतं पिब धानावन्तं करम्भिणमपूपवन्तमुक्थिनम् ॥

> *asau ya eṣi vīrako gṛhaṃgṛhaṃ vicākaśat |*
> *imaṃ jambhasutaṃ piba dhānāvantaṃ karambhiṇamapūpavantamukthinam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-91-2) — here *jambhasutam* means "*dantair abhiṣutam*", "pressed with the teeth, i.e. held and crushed with the teeth": as in the ṛk at hand *jambhayatam* is the verbal word, and as lions and others destroy other creatures with their teeth, so you do the crushing of enemies — this is the meaning.

**Śunaḥ** — by the comparison "*śvā sadṛśān*" it is understood that people like the Paṇis are seen by them with every contempt and with a spirit of enmity.

**Ratninīṃ** — "*ramaṇīyaphalavatīṃ*" (our praises) — they pray: make them bear delightful fruit. The word *ratna* is told in many places to mean "delightful". The Nirukta-author also, in the sentence "*hotāraṃ ratnadhātamam*", gives this very meaning for the word *ratna* (Ni. 7-15 [?]). In describing a rare (*amūlya*) thing, this word is used in describing its excellence and beauty. For example:

> यस्ते स्तनः शशयो यो मयोभूर्येन विश्वा पुष्यसि वार्याणि ।
> यो रत्नधा वसुविद्यः सुदत्रः सरस्वति तमिह धातवे कः ॥

> *yaste stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūryena viśvā puṣyasi vāryāṇi |*
> *yo ratnadhā vasuvidyaḥ sudatraḥ sarasvati tamiha dhātave kaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-49)

### Printed p. 610  (PDF 630)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 610.)*

— here the "juice" (*rasa*) in the form of bliss is indicated. As it has the epithet *ratnadhā*, it has been explained as "the bearer of many kinds of delightful juices". Likewise in the ṛk at hand also the fruit, excellent and delightful, is indicated.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly): *jambhayatam* — root *jabhi nāśane*, *curādi*; "*satyāpapāśa…*" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-25 [?]) gives *ṇic* in the root's own sense; since it has *i*, *num* augment; *loṭ* second person dual form; in the beginning of a *pāda* there is no *nighāta* accent; the accent of *ṇic* remains. *rāyataḥ* — root *rai śabde*, *bhvādi*; *laṭ* with *śatṛ*-substitution; *śap* as *vikaraṇa*; *āy*-substitution; "*tāsyanudāttet…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 [?]) — the *sārvadhātuka l* being unaccented, the root's accent remains; second (case) plural form. *hatam* — root *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *loṭ* second person dual; since *lakṣaṇa*-no-*dyāva* applies, *tam*-substitution; "*adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ*" (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72 [?]) gives *luk* of *śap*; "*anudāttopadeśa-vanati…*" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37 [?]) elides the root's *n*; being at the beginning of a *pāda* no *nighāta* accent; by the suffix accent, final acute. *vidathuḥ* — root *vida jñāne*; *laṭ* second person dual; "*vido laṭo vā*" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-83 [?]) gives *athus*-substitution; since the suffix has *ñ* [as read] there is no guṇa; by *vyatyaya* the suffix's initial acute. *vācaṃ-vācam* — "*nityavīpsayoḥ*" gives doubling; "*anudāttaṃ ca*" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-3 [?]) — the later repeated word is wholly unaccented. *kṛtam* — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *loṭ* second person dual, *tam*-substitution; "*bahulaṃ chandasi*" gives *luk* of the *vikaraṇa*; since the suffix has *ñ*, no guṇa; following a *tiṅ*-final, *nighāta* accent. *ubhā* — "*supāṃ sulug*" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 [?]) gives ā-substitution for the dual. *avatam* — root *ava rakṣaṇe*; *loṭ* second person dual form; *tiṅ*, *nighāta* accent.  ‖ 4 ‖

### Sūkta 182, Ṛk 5  (printed p. 611; PDF 631)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 4 Va. 27"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page 611.)*

**Saṃhitā-pāṭha**

> युवमेतं चक्रथुः सिन्धुषु प्लवमात्मन्वन्तं पक्षिणं तौग्र्याय कम् ।
> येन देवत्रा मनसा निरूहथुः सुपप्तनी पेतथुः क्षोदसो महः ॥ ५ ॥

**Pada-pāṭha**

> युवं । एतं । चक्रथुः । सिन्धुषु । प्लवं । आत्मन्ऽवन्तं । पक्षिणं । तौग्र्याय । कं ।
> येन । देवऽत्रा । मनसा । निःऽऊहथुः । सुऽपप्तनी । पेतथुः । क्षोदसः । महः ॥ ५ ॥

**Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya**

> हे अश्विनौ युवं युवामेतं सिन्धुषु समुद्रोदकेष्वेतं प्लवं प्रसिद्धं प्लुतिसाधनं प्लवं नावमात्मन्वन्तं दाढ्यवन्तं पक्षिणं पक्षवद्गतिसाधनरथवन्तं तौग्र्याय तुग्रनाम्नो राज्ञः पुत्राय भुज्युनाम्ने राज्ञे कं सुखकरं चक्रथुः । तौग्र्यो भुज्युः राजा समुद्रवर्ती ससेनः परचक्रं प्रमथितुं प्रस्थितः । तं प्रतीपबलान्यागत्याघातयन् । स च प्रसादफलकरावश्विनौ स्तुत्वा स्वात्मानं ररक्षेत्ययमितिहासो बहुधा पूर्वं प्रपञ्चितः । यद्वा । कमिति पूरणः । तस्य जलसंचारिरथस्य सहायभूतानप्ताहून्रथादीनकुरुतमित्यर्थः । अयमर्धर्चः । तमूहथुर्नौभिः । ऋ. १-११६-३ । चतस्रो नावः । ऋ. १-११६-५ । त्रिभी रथैः । ऋ. १-११६-४ । इत्यादिमन्त्रान्तरेषु प्रसिद्धः । येन युष्मद्दत्तेन प्लवेन देवत्रा देवेषु मध्ये मनसानुग्रहयुक्तया बुद्ध्या । येन मनसेति वा योज्यं । निरूहथुः निर्गमनं कुरुथः । तथा सुपप्तनी शोभनपतनं यथा भवति सुपतनौ वा युवां महो महतः क्षोदसः । उदकनाम्नैतत् । उदकात्पेतथुः । तद्धः पतेथ उत्तरीतुं ॥

*(Sanskrit as read; the passage is dense and several words are doubtful [?]; the Ṛg references 1-116-3, 1-116-5, 1-116-4 are as read [?]. Gist: you made a winged, sturdy vessel on the ocean-waters for Bhujyu, son of Tugra; by it, with minds favourably set towards the gods, you bore him out and sped from the great flood.)*

**Pratipadārtha** — (*he*) **aśvinā** — O Aśvin deities; **yena** — by which float; **devatrā** — among the gods; (you two alone) **manasā** — with a mind of grace; **nirūhathuḥ** — (you bore Bhujyu out of) the sea; **etaṃ** — such a famous; **ātmanvantaṃ** — endowed with firmness; **pakṣiṇaṃ** — wing-like, endowed with a chariot that is the means of motion; **plavaṃ** — the boat; **sindhuṣu** — in the ocean-waters; **tauġryāya** — for Bhujyu, the son of Tugra [text continues on the next page].

### Printed p. 612  (PDF 632)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 182"; page 612.)*

*(Pratipadārtha, continued)* … for Bhujyu, the son of one named Tugra; **kaṃ** — so that it may be pleasant; **yuvaṃ** — you two; **cakrathuḥ** — made; (**tathā** — and so); **supaptanī** — as a pleasant descent into the ocean (or: you two who are accustomed to falling into the ocean); **mahaḥ kṣodasaḥ** — from the immeasurable water of the ocean (to lift up that Bhujyu); **petathuḥ** — you plunged (into the water).

**Bhāvārtha** — O Aśvin deities, of all the gods, you two alone, with a mind of grace towards Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, made for him in the ocean-waters that boat, firm and wing-like, a chariot-vessel that helps one go over the earth; and, so as to give him ease in the waters, joined him to it, and, plunging into the sea, you two, accustomed to such daring acts, lifted him out of the immeasurable waters of the ocean.

**English Translation.** *(printed)*

"You constructed a pleasant, substantial, winged bark, borne on the ocean waters for the son of Tugra, by which, with mind devoted to the gods, you bore him up, and, quickly descending (from the sky), you made a path for him across the great waters."

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this ṛk also, the matter of the protection of Bhujyu told earlier is itself told. "*Pūrvaṃ prapañcitaḥ*" ("already elaborated"), says Sāyaṇa, and tells again that same story in this way:

> तौग्र्यो भुज्युः राजा समुद्रवर्ती ससेनः परचक्रं प्रमथितुं प्रस्थितः । तं प्रतीपबलानि आगत्याघातयन् । स च प्रसादफलकरावश्विनौ स्तुत्वा स्वात्मानं ररक्षेत्ययमितिहासः ।

*(Sanskrit as read, "pratīpabalāni āgatyāghātayan" doubtful [?].)* — King Bhujyu, the son of Tugra, who was in the ocean, set out with his army to crush an enemy host; the enemy forces, coming, struck him; and he, praising the Aśvin deities, who give the fruit of favour, protected himself: this is the story. The enemy armies cast Bhujyu, who had gone into the sea to destroy the enemy armies, into the sea. Then, when he prayed to the Aśvin deities as protectors, they protected him with the help of a boat: this subject is told in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-3 and 1-116-4 [?] and in many other places. The subject of Bhujyu was told earlier; and it was told earlier that he was troubled by the dust-storm [?, "birugāḷi"] — in the account at hand it is told that he was caught by enemies. The difference is that.

**Sindhuṣu** — for this word is given the sense "*samudrodakeṣu*": in the waters of the ocean. The word *sindhu* is read among the names of rivers (Ni. 1-24 [?]); "*sindhuḥ sravaṇāt*" (Ni. 2-25 [?]) — since it flows, *sindhu* is the name for a river. As it is in the form of a current, in some places the meaning "rays" is also possible; in that sense also this word is used. For example —
